Out of the total population, one . three % of those under the age of one eight and one three . five % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Government 
 Local government 
The Borough's Mayor and Council constitute the governing body of the Borough. The Borough form of government, was established in one eight seven eight allowing any part of a Township to set itself of as an independent municipality providing that the new entity was not more then four square miles and a population not exceeding five , zero zero zero persons. Over the years the Borough Act of one eight seven eight was amended several times.

The Borough form of government consists of six elected council members two of which each year are elected (or re-elected) to three year terms. Council members are elected at large meaning that each member represents the entire Borough, instead of representing a portion of the Borough in a ward or district. The Borough Council is considered the legislative body of municipality and can override the Mayor's veto of an ordinance by a two three majority of all members. The Borough Council also confirms the Mayor's appointments.

The Mayor is considered the head of the municipal government and as chief executive is responsible to see that all state laws and borough ordinances are faithfully executed. The Mayor, who is elected to a four year term, presides over Borough Council meetings and only votes in order to break a tie. The Mayor can veto ordinances and appoint subordinate officials, ad hoc committees and certain other officials to boards, committees and commissions. 

The Mayor of Mendham Borough is Richard Kraft. Members of the Borough Council as of the two zero zero six reorganization are Council President Neil J. Henry, Jr., Brad Badal, Louis S. Garubo, David H. Murphy, Barbara Stanton and Stanley Witczak, III. 

 Federal, state and county representation 
Mendham Borough is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's one six th Legislative District.

 

 



 Education 
Students in grades K- eight attend the Mendham Borough Schools. Schools in the district (with two zero zero three - zero four enrollment data from the National Center for Education Statistics) are Hilltop Elementary School with four six zero students in grades K - four and Mountain View Middle School with four zero nine students in grades five - eight .

Students in grades nine - one two attend West Morris Mendham High School, which is located in Mendham Borough and is part of the West Morris Regional High School District. Students in the district come from the surrounding Morris County school districts of Chester Borough, Chester Township, Mendham Borough, Mendham Township and from Washington Township.

 '''Mine Hill Township''' is a Township located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of three , six seven nine . 

Mine Hill Township is a residential community located in the northwest corner of Morris County. The Township and is easy to reach via the MidTOWN DIRECT line of New Jersey Transit, which is available in nearby Dover, Interstate eight zero , U.S. Route four six , and Route one zero .

Mine Hill was once a thriving mining center, with the first mining occurring in the early one seven zero zero s. The Dickerson Mine was owned and operated by Mahlon Dickerson  New Jersey's one two th Governor ( one eight one five - one eight one seven ) and Secretary of the Navy ( one eight three four - one eight three eight )  and his family and was the largest ore mine in the area. The mine supplied much of the iron ore used during the American Revolutionary War period. The township had some of the richest iron ore mines in the country, until the last mine closed during the late one nine six zero s.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of seven . eight km ( three . zero mi ).  seven . seven km ( three . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . three three % is water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are three , six seven nine people, one , three six five households, and one , zero four one families residing in the township. The population density is four seven five . one km ( one , two two eight . six mi ). There are one , three eight eight housing units at an average density of one seven nine . two km ( four six three . five mi ). The racial makeup of the township is nine zero . four one % White, three . four two % African American, zero . one one % Native American, two . five zero % Asian, zero . zero eight % Pacific Islander, one . seven nine % from other races, and one . six nine % from two or more races.  eight . six seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , three six five households out of which three three . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six one . two % are married couples living together, one zero . six % have a female householder with no husband present, and two three . seven % are non-families. one nine . three % of all households are made up of individuals and six . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . seven zero and the average family size is three . zero eight .

In the township the population is spread out with two four . five % under the age of one eight , four . nine % from one eight to two four , three four . three % from two five to four four , two three . one % from four five to six four , and one three . two % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are nine four . five males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine four . three males.

The median income for a household in the township is $ six four , six four three , and the median income for a family is $ six seven , four six seven . Males have a median income of $ four seven , eight one three versus $ three seven , two five zero for females. The per capita income for the township is $ two seven , one one nine .  five . six % of the population and four . seven % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, eight . seven % of those under the age of one eight and seven . one % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Government 
 Local government 
Mine Hill Township is governed under the Faulkner Act (Mayor-Council) system of municipal government.

The Mayor of Mine Hill Township is Richard Leary.

The Mine Hill Township Council consists of five elected members, each chosen by the voters of Mine Hill for a four -year term. At the Councils organizational meeting each January, one member is elected to serve as President for a twelve-month term and another is chosen to serve as Vice President. The current members are Marc Sovelove (Council President), Gary Colucci )Council Vice President), Steven Cicchetti, Cynthia Collins and Michael Warholak.
 Federal, state and county representation 
Mine Hill Township is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's two five th Legislative District.

 





 Education 
Mine Hill Township has an excellent K- six school system. The Canfield Avenue School has been recognized by the Blue Ribbon Schools Program and has been declared a National School of Excellence.

 '''Montville Township''' is a Township located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of two zero , eight three nine .

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of four nine . five km ( one nine . one mi ).  four eight . nine km ( one eight . nine mi ) of it is land and zero . seven km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . three six % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two zero , eight three nine people, seven , three eight zero households, and five , eight six seven families residing in the township. The population density is four two six . four km ( one , one zero four . three mi ). There are seven , five four one housing units at an average density of one five four . three km ( three nine nine . six mi ). The racial makeup of the township is eight four . nine five % White, zero . nine three % African American, zero . zero four % Native American, one two . five seven % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . three six % from other races, and one . one four % from two or more races.  two . five five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are seven , three eight zero households out of which three seven . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven one . zero % are married couples living together, six . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two zero . five % are non-families. one six . six % of all households are made up of individuals and five . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight zero and the average family size is three . one seven .

In the township the population is spread out with two five . two % under the age of one eight , five . five % from one eight to two four , three zero . six % from two five to four four , two eight . zero % from four five to six four , and one zero . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are nine four . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine one . nine males.

The median income for a household in the township is $ nine four , five five seven , and the median income for a family is $ one zero five , three nine four . Males have a median income of $ seven one , three five six versus $ four five , four two seven for females. The per capita income for the township is $ four three , three four one .  three . eight % of the population and two . six % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, four . four % of those under the age of one eight and six . three % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. 

 Government 
 Local government 
The Township of Montville is headed by five elected officials who constitute the Township Committee (also referred to as the governing body ) which establishes laws and policies for the Township. The Mayor is a member of the Township Committee and is elected annually by the Committee.

The Township Administrator serves as the chief administrative and executive officer for the organization and is responsible for the day-to-day operations of all municipal departments. 

Montville's Township Council consists of Mayor Steve Moscone (Term Expires December three one , two zero zero seven ), Deputy Mayor Art Daughtry (Term Expires December three one , two zero zero seven ), Jean Bader (Term Expires December three one , two zero zero six ), Deb Nielson (Term Expires December three one , two zero zero eight ) and Jim Sandham (Term Expires December three one , two zero zero eight ).
 Federal, state and county representation 
Montville Township is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's two six th Legislative District.

 

 



 History 
The area now known as Montville Township was first settled by Dutch farmers who migrated from a similarly named town in Connecticut. The region, originally called Uyle-Kill (the Dutch pronunciation of Owl-Kill), was the name given to the creek and valley which run through the region. By the one seven four zero s, the settlement had grown in size and construction of the first road was begun. The early road, now know as U.S. Highway two zero two , connected various farms with Montvilles first gristmill.

During the American Revolutionary War, Montville was one of the major military routes from Morristown to the Hudson River. General George Washingtons troops often took this route and Washington stayed in Montville in June one seven eight zero . The French troops also passed through Montville on their way to the Wars final victory at Jamestown, Virginia.

The construction of the Morris Canal in this area was completed in one eight two eight , bringing commercial navigation to the Montville area. It was about this same time that the area adopted the more recognizable English name of Montville. The mid- one nine th century saw the development of two smaller village centers set apart from Montville: Pine Brook, a fertile agricultural area in the Townships southern end and Whitehall (later called Towaco), situated on the Morris Canal. In one eight six seven , the Township of Montville was formally chartered from one nine square miles of territory set off from what had been part of Pequannock Township.

 Education 
The Montville Township School District is comprised of the following schools (with two zero zero three - zero four enrollment data from the National Center for Education Statistics).

The district includes five Kindergarten to fifth grade elementary schools  Cedar Hill Elementary School with four zero four students, Hilldale Elementary School with three five seven students, Valley View Elementary School with four three three students, William Mason Elementary School with three eight three students and Woodmont Elementary School serving three six two students  Robert R. Lazar Middle School with about one , zero three nine students in grades six - eight (as of the beginning of the two zero zero five - two zero zero six school year), and Montville High School with an enrollment of one , zero nine eight students in grades nine - one two . MTHS's mascot is the Mustang and thanks to Dr. Steven Kramer the school's new motto is You can't hide from Mustang Pride! 

Private Schools include St. Pius X Grammar School and Trinity Christian School.

 Transportation 
As part of its MidTOWN DIRECT expansion program, New Jersey Transit, with supplemental funding from the Township of Montville, renovated the Towaco Train Station using a design harkening back to the early one nine zero zero s. Commuters may now go from Towaco to Penn Station in midtown Manhattan via a transfer in Montclair rather than transferring to the PATH in Newark.

'''Morris Township''' is a township located in Morris County, New Jersey, USA. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of two one , seven nine six . It is known as the doughnut around Morristown since it completely encapsulates it, and has at least five times the area. Though, near Morris Plains the width of Morris Township is less than a mile.

 '''Morris Plains''', billing itself the Community of Caring , is a Borough located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the borough had a total population of five , two three six .

Morris Plains serves as a bedroom community for workers in New York City. The Morristown Line of New Jersey Transit provide commuters with access to New York Penn Station (via the Secaucus Junction) and to Hoboken Terminal. 

Morris Plains is also a major base of operations for Pfizer, previously the headquarters for Warner-Lambert. Pfizer also sponsors the Health and Medical Science Academy at Morristown High School and has an annual five k race around Morris Plains.

A major attraction in Morris Plains is Arthur's, a popular restaurant known for its steaks. 

 Geography

The population density is seven eight zero . six km ( two , zero one eight . seven mi ). There are one , nine nine four housing units at an average density of two nine seven . three km ( seven six eight . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the borough is nine two . nine one % White, one . three four % African American, zero . zero six % Native American, four . three two % Asian, zero . one zero % Pacific Islander, zero . four zero % from other races, and zero . eight eight % from two or more races.  two . six nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

 Elvis Presley - Heartbreak Hotel
 '''Heartbreak Hotel''' is a rock and roll song by Elvis Presley, with Bill Black (bass), Scotty Moore (guitar), and D.J Fontana on the drums as the main supporting musicians. Recorded in January one nine five six , the song introduced Presley to the US' national music consciousness. It was released as a single with the b-side song I Was The One on January two seven , one nine five six .

 Heartbreak Hotel 's lyrical matter deals with the singer's sadness, implicitly that following the end of a romantic relationship. It uses the metaphor of a hotel to represent this emotional state.

It was written by Thomas Durden and Mae Boren Axton, the mother of singersongwriteractor Hoyt Axton.

The song achieved high chart success with pop ( one ), R more echo on his voice. The song is an example of simple verse form.

There is now a real hotel named after the song, and located across from Graceland, in Memphis, Tennessee.  


A movie by the same title, based on a mythical incident involving the kidnapping of Elvis Presley, was released theatrically in one nine eight eight . It starred David Keith, and Tuesday Weld and was directed by Chris Columbus.

There are numerous cover versions of the song, including one by avant garde musician John Cale, although the mood of the song was significantly more unsettling than Elvis's version.

Three other different songs, also entitled Heartbreak Hotel  were released as singles, one by the Jacksons, (later renamed This Place Hotel ), one by Whithney Houston, whose mother, gospel singer Cissy Houston appears in several Elvis recordings, both in the studio,  and live, as a member of the Sweet Inspirations. The third song, called 'Heartbreak Hotel' was perfomed by C.C.Catch. This song has nothing to do with the Elvis' song.

'''''Jailhouse Rock''''' is a one nine five seven film starring Elvis Presley, as Vince Everett, an ex-convict working in the music industry. 

Deemed culturally significant, the film has been selected for preservation in the United States National Film Registry.

The film co-starred actress Judy Tyler, who was killed in an automobile accident a few weeks after the film was completed.

The single was followed in October by an extended play record titled Jailhouse Rock that featured the four other songs from the motion picture.

'''Dokken''' is an American metal band which was formed in one nine seven eight . The group became one of the classic metal bands from that era, joining contemporaries like Twisted Sister, Judas Priest, Quiet Riot and Iron Maiden. Dokken's music consists of traditional metal characterized by extravagant use of lead guitars and soaring vocals backed by a heavy thumping bass. Although their image was somewhat glam, their music was traditionally heavy with technical expertise. 

Dokken was comprised of founder Don Dokken on vocals, George Lynch on lead guitars, Jeff Pilson on bass and Mick Brown on drums. Currently the band consists of Don Dokken on vocals, Jon Levin on guitar, Barry Sparks on bass and Mick Brown on drums.

Short album history
Their early albums like ''Tooth And Nail'', ''Under Lock And Key'', ''Back For The Attack'' and ''Beast From The East'' were highly successful, but after that, intra-band rifts and spats ensured that the band would eventually break up. Don Dokken went on to a successful solo career, while George Lynch formed the Lynch Mob and recorded several albums. Jeff Pilson too released his acclaimed ''War And Peace'' album. The band released a few albums in the late nine zero s and then ''Long Way Home'' in two zero zero zero , which met with some success due to attention from fans starved for traditional heavy metal. Recently, Dokken has released their latest album, ''Hell To Pay'', which has gotten rave reviews in metal circles.

Biography
Dokken was born in the late one nine seven zero s when guitarist George Lynch and drummer Mick Brown from the group Xciter teamed up with Don Dokken on vocals and Peter Baltes as a temporary bassist to record ''Back in the Streets'' with Carerre Records. 

In one nine seven eight Juan Croucier replaced Peter Baltes as another temporary bassist; that same year the band released the singles Hard Rock Woman, and Paris is Burning. In one nine eight one the band released the album ''Breaking the Chains'' in Europe, which was re-mastered and re-released by Elektra Records in the US in one nine eight three . While the band was very popular in Europe by then, they had not yet made the charts in the US.

Juan Croucier left Dokken in one nine eight two to join the band Ratt and was replaced by Jeff Pilson who became their first official bassist. one nine eight four was Dokken's breakout year in the US with the release of the album ''Tooth and Nail'', which contained several hit songs: Into the Fire ( eight ), Just Got Lucky ( two seven ) and Dokken's first one hit Alone Again . The album sold over one million copies in the US alone and peaked at one three . In one nine eight five the album ''Under Lock and Key'' also sold over a million copies with hits like In My Dreams ( two four ), The Hunter ( two five ) and It's Not Love. 

Following a successful tour with the Scorpions, Dokken returned to the studio in one nine eight seven to record ''Back for the Attack''. The record, which spawned the hits Burning Like A Flame ( two zero ) and Heaven Sent became the band's most popular release, reaching eight on U.S. charts. It included the single Dream Warriors ( two two ), written for the third Nightmare on Elm Street film. The accompanying music video, which featured band members interacting with the film's characters, was the band's most popular video. ''Back for the Attack'' became Dokken's third record to reach platinum status. Sculptor Steve Fiorilla's customized writhing skeleton guitar was the highlight of another Dokken video.

Recordings from their tour in Japan led to one nine eight eight 's release of ''Beast from the East'' just before the band broke up due to creative differences between Don and George. The band reunited in one nine nine two , but didn't release an album until ''Dysfunctional'' in one nine nine five with Columbia Records. ''One Live Night'' (a live acoustical album) was released in one nine nine six by CMC, along with ''Shadowlife'' in one nine nine seven . 

In one nine nine eight Lynch left the band and was replaced by Reb Beach of the band Winger. They released ''Erase the Slate'' in one nine nine nine and ''Live from the Sun'' in two zero zero zero . In two zero zero one , Beach was replaced by John Norum (formerly with the band Europe), and Jeff Pilson was replaced by Barry Sparks on bass.  two zero zero two also saw the release of the album ''Long Way Home.'' In two zero zero four John Norum was replaced by Jon Levin (formerly he plays guitar on Doro's Force Majeure), and they released thealbum Hell to Pay .

Guest appearances
Members and ex-members of the band have appeared on various tribute albums. Don Dokken appeared on a tribute album to Rush, while George Lynch and Jeff Pilson have appeared on tribute albums to Iron Maiden. Jeff Pilson also appeared as a bassist in the movie Rock Star (starring Mark Wahlberg and Jennifer Aniston), which was loosely based on Judas Priest

'''Dover''' is a Town located in Morris County, New Jersey, three nine miles ( six three km) west by north of New York City on the Rockaway River. In one nine zero zero , five , nine three eight people lived in Dover; in one nine one zero , seven , four six eight ; and in one nine four zero , one zero , four nine one . As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the town had a total population of one eight , one eight eight . 

History 
Dover was incorporated as a village in one eight two six and in one eight six nine as a town. The town charter was amended in one eight seven five . In its past, Dover had extensive ironworks, machine shops, stove, furnace, and range works, boiler and bridge works, rolling mills, drill works, knitting and silk mills, a large hosiery factory, and an overall factory.

Today, Dover has a large Hispanic population with the largest concentrations being of Puerto Rican, Colombian and Mexican ancestry. Hispanics have been a demographic majority since one nine eight zero , and are growing quickly. As of the two zero zero zero Census, Dover's population was five seven . nine % Hispanic, making it the municipality with the fifth highest Hispanic population percentage in New Jersey and one of eight New Jersey municipalities with a Hispanic majority. It is often referred to as Doverico by residents of surrounding townships to mock the Hispanic dominance of the downtown, as these surrounding regions are wealthier and predominantly non-Hispanic. While Dover is not currently financially disadvantaged in comparison to average towns nationwide, it is considerably less affluent than those that surround it, thus giving the township a reputation of being poor.

 Life in Dover 
The community of Dover is centered around a developed downtown area that is filled with many eateries. A vast percentage of these are owned and run by Hispanics of different countries, and feature their ethnic food.

The population of Dover is very friendly. One can always find residents passing time day and night outside of the filled eateries and residences that exist over them. This is most common on Blackwell Street, the town's main road.

Residential areas of Dover are known for their city-like lots, with portions of town having rows of houses with little space in-between lining the streets. Other sections appear typical of suburban New Jersey, excluding the southwest corner of town that features larger yards and homes.

One can best witness the community spirit of Dover when the weather turns warm. Every week, there is a flea market downtown. 

Hamilton Field is Dover's recreation center, featuring a football field with bleachers, soccer fields, and a historic cinder track that is used by walkers and joggers. Townspeople and students gather on select Friday nights to watch Dover High School's football team, the Dover Tigers, play under the lights of Hamilton Field. The Dover Grill is a popular eatery among students, who often cross bordering US four six during and after games to eat and talk to friends.

In sum, Dover is extremely safe and is a great place to live.

 Geography 
Dover is located at four zero  five three ' nine  North, seven four  three three ' three zero  West ( four zero . eight eight five eight nine nine , - seven four . five five eight two four one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of seven . zero km ( two . seven mi ).  six . nine km ( two . seven mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . one one % water.

 '''Morristown''' is a Town located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the town had a total population of one eight , five four four . Its estimated population in two zero zero four was one eight , eight four two . It is the county seat of Morris County. Morristown is not to be confused with Moorestown, a township further south in New Jersey, in the Philadelphia metropolitan area.


 History 
 one eight th Century
Morristown was settled around one seven one five by English Presbyterians from Southold, Long Island and New Haven, Connecticut as the village of New Hanover. The town became the seat of the new Morris County shortly after its separation from Hunterdon County on March one five , one seven three nine . The village and county were named for Lewis Morris, the first and then sitting royal governor of a united colony of New Jersey.

By the mid-century the two five zero people shared the village with two churches, a courthouse, two taverns, two schools, several stores, and numerous mills nearby.

George Washington, the Marquis de Lafayette, and the Continental Army was encamped near Morristown from January to May one seven seven seven and from December one seven seven nine to June one seven eight zero at Jockey Hollow. Washington had his headquarters during the first encampment at Arnold's Tavern located on the Morristown Green. During the second encampment Washington's Headquarters was located at the Ford Mansion, a large mansion near the edge of town. Arnold's Tavern was lost to fire in the one nine th century, but the Ford Mansion, Jockey Hollow, and Fort Nonsense are all preserved as part of Morristown National Historical Park managed by the National Park Service.

During Washington's stay, Benedict Arnold was court-martialed in Morristown, not for treason, but on minor charges. Alexander Hamilton courted and wed Betsy Schuyler at the residence used by Washington's personal physician. The home is owned and operated by the Daughters of the American Revolution as the Schuyler-Hamilton House.

 one nine th Century
The Marquis de Lafayette returned to Morristown in July one eight two five on his return tour of the United States, where a ball was held in his honor at the one eight zero seven Sansay House on DeHart Street, which still stands.

Antoine le Blanc, a French immigrant laborer murdered the Sayre family and their servant (or possibly slave) Phoebe. He was tried and convicted of murder of the Sayres (but not Phoebe) on August one three , one eight three three . On September six , one eight three three Le Blanc became the last person hanged on the Morristown Green. The house where the murders were committed is today known as Jimmy's Haunt which is purported to be haunted by Phoebe's ghost since her murder never saw justice.

Samuel Morse and Alfred Vail built the first telegraph at the Speedwell Iron Works on January six , one eight three eight . The first telegraph message was A patient waiter is no loser. The first public demonstration occurred eleven days later as the first step towards the information age we enjoy today.

 Education 
The Morris School District is a regional school district that serves the communities of Morristown and Morris Township (for grades K- one two ), along with students Morris Plains for grades nine - one two only, as part of a sending receiving relationship. The district provides a supportive and challenging educational environment for a total student population of approximately four , seven zero zero . Within the District there are three primary schools (K- two ), three intermediate schools ( three - five ), one multiage magnet school (K- five ), one middle school ( six - eight ), and one high school, Morristown High School.

 Interesting facts
The largest statue of Thomas Paine is located in Morristown.
Morristown was the home of Thomas Nast for more than two zero years.
Morristown & Erie Railway, a local short-line freight railway, has its main office, yard and shop here.
The Seeing Eye, founded in one nine two nine by Morris Frank, trains dogs in town and are a common site on the streets.
Morristown is home to one of the largest Chabad Lubavitch Chasidic yeshivas in the world. The Rabbinical College of America in Morristown has trained hundreds of young Lubavitch rabbis. Many other Jewish families have moved into the area to be near the yeshiva and surrounding synagogues.
Many prominent Chabad Rabbis and Emissaries attended the Rabbinical College of America.
The Rabbinical College of America also has a Baal Teshuva yeshiva for students of diverse Jewish backgrounds, named Yeshiva Tiferes Bachurim.
On Campus for the Rabbinical College of America is the New Jersey Regional Headquarters for the world-wide Chabad Lubavitch movement.

 '''Mount Arlington''' is a Township located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the borough had a total population of four , six six three . It is located on the southeast shore of Lake Hopatcong, New Jersey's largest natural lake and a major recreational resource. 

 History 
While Mount Arlington is now mostly a suburban residential community, it was once a thriving resort town. In the era before the world wars and the advent of air travel, it was a welcome respite for the residents of nearby New York City and Newark.

Every summer thousands would arrive by train at Landing Station, and then travel by water taxi across Lake Hopatcong to the areas many large resort hotels to escape the city heat and enjoy the famous Mount Arlington breeze which always cooled the summer evenings. 

There was also a major amusement park, Bertrand Island, which featured a world famous carousel and roller coaster.

 '''Mount Olive Township''' is a Township located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of two four , one nine three . Mount Olive Township is governed under the Faulkner Act (Mayor-Council) system of municipal government.

The Township of Mount Olive was formed by an act of the New Jersey Legislature on March two two , one eight seven one .

Budd Lake ( two zero zero zero Census population of eight , one zero zero ) is a census-designated place and unincorporated area located within Mount Olive Township. Flanders is an unincorporated area within the Township.

The racial makeup of the township is eight six . six nine % White, three . seven nine % African American, zero . one seven % Native American, six . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, one . five three % from other races, and one . eight one % from two or more races.  five . nine seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are nine , zero six eight households out of which three nine . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five nine . six % are married couples living together, seven . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two nine . seven % are non-families. two three . seven % of all households are made up of individuals and five . one % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six six and the average family size is three . two two .

In the township the population is spread out with two seven . six % under the age of one eight , six . eight % from one eight to two four , three seven . six % from two five to four four , two one . seven % from four five to six four , and six . four % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, three . one % of those under the age of one eight and three . five % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Government
Local government
Mount Olive Township is governed under the Optional Municipal Charter Law's (Faulkner Act) Mayor-Council Form of government, a Strong Mayor Form of government, providing for a separately elected mayor and council, who serve for four-year terms of office. The mayor, who is elected directly by the people, is the Chief Executive Officer of the Township. The Mayor is responsible for carrying out all Council decisions and for the day to day operation of all functions of the municipality. 

The Township Council consists of seven members elected at large with staggered terms. The Township Council is the legislative branch of the government charged with approving the municipal budget and enacting the ordinances (laws) of the municipality. The Township Council President presides over all meetings of the governing body. The Council elects the Council President from amongst its members each year at a reorganization meeting. 

The Mayor of Mount Olive Township is Richard DeLaRoche. Members of the Township Council are Rob Greenbaum (Council President), Ray Perkins (Council Vice President), Jim Buell, Bernie Guenther, Colleen Labow, Lisa Lashway, Lee Mund and Steven Rattner.
Federal, state and county representation
Mount Olive Township is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's two four th Legislative District.

 History 
Netcong, formerly South Stanhope was incorporated as a Borough on October two two , one eight nine four . Parts of Mount Olive and Roxbury Townships were added to South Stanhope to form the Borough, which is about one mile square. Netcong received its name from the Musconetcong River, which the Lenape Native Americans called grass creek or swamp stream. The proximity of the old Morris and Sussex Turnpike, which passed through the region shortly after one eight zero one , and the coming of the Morris Canal, in one eight three one , also made the site a favorable one for development.

After becoming a Borough, the residents had to elect the first Governing Body. The first Mayor was Abraham J. Drake, elected November one four , one eight nine four . A census of Netcong taken July of one eight nine five showed a population of eight seven seven people. 

Netcong derived much of its business from the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, which had its last stop in Morris County in the heart of the Borough. The big railroad roundhouse in Port Morris also supplied many jobs for the town residents.

 Education 
Netcong is home to its own Pre-K to grade eight school district, serving two nine one students at Netcong Elementary School. Netcong's school offers small class sizes that allow teachers to offer personalized attention not possible in larger schools. 

For grades nine - one two , the borough shares Lenape Valley Regional High School with the Sussex County communities of Stanhope and Byram Township, part of the Lenape Valley Regional High School District.

 Government 
 Local government 
Parsippany-Troy Hill Township is governed under a Faulkner Act (Mayor-Council) system of municipal government under the Faulkner Act (also known as The Optional Municipal Charter Law). This Mayor-Council form of government is similar to that of the federal and state governments. One can liken this form of government to a presidential system.

Under the Faulkner Act Mayor-Council form of government, the Mayor and Council are separately elected, with the Mayor, serving as the chief executive officer, and the Council serving in the capacity of a legislative body.

Some responsibilities of the Mayor include preparation of the budget, enforcement of the ordinances, supervision of municipal departments and property, execution of Council decisions, and oversight of other functions of the municipality. Some of the responsibilities of the Council include adopting ordinances, approval of contracts presented by the Mayor, scheduling times and places for council meetings and designation of the official newspapers of the municipality.

The Mayor of Parsippany-Troy Hills is Michael Luther. Mayor Luther, while officially a Democrat, won a narrow election, with support from certain pro-development Republicans, over Township Council member Rosemarie Agostini, who favored a moratorium on development in the township. Green Party candidate Michael Spector and independent Roy Messmer also ran in the two zero zero five election. 

Parsippany-Troy Hills's Township Council consists of Council President Rosemarie C. Agostini, John Cesaro, Ann Grossi, James J. Vigilante, and Michael J. dePierro.

 Federal, state and county representation 
Parsippany-Troy Hills Township is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's two six th Legislative District.

'''Randolph Township''' is a Township located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of two four , eight four seven .

The main campus of the County College of Morris is located in Randolph Township.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of five four . six km ( two one . one mi).  five four . three km ( two one . zero mi) of it is land and zero . three km ( zero . one mi) of it is water. The total area is zero . five seven % water.

New York City is approximately five six km ( three five mi) or a four five minute commute from Randolph. Atlantic City is two zero nine km ( one three zero mi) or two hours away (Source: Google Maps)

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two four , eight four seven people, eight , six seven nine households, and six , eight zero four families residing in the township. The population density is four five seven . seven km ( one , one eight five . two mi). There are eight , nine zero three housing units at an average density of one six four . zero km ( four two four . seven mi). The racial makeup of the township is eight five . seven zero % White, two . three zero % African American, zero . zero six % Native American, nine . one four % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, one . three one % from other races, and one . four six % from two or more races.  four . eight six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are eight , six seven nine households out of which four four . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven zero . two % are married couples living together, six . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and two one . six % are non-families. one eight . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and four . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight six and the average family size is three . two eight .

In the township the population is spread out with two nine . seven % under the age of one eight , five . two % from one eight to two four , three two . two % from two five to four four , two five . seven % from four five to six four , and seven . three % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are nine eight . three males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine five . eight males.

The median income for a household in the township is $ nine seven , five eight nine , and the median income for a family is $ one one five , seven two two . Males have a median income of $ eight zero , one two zero versus $ four five , four five five for females. The per capita income for the township is $ four three , zero seven two .  one . four % of the population and one . zero % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one . zero % of those under the age of one eight and three . four % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Background 
Randolph's beginnings predate the creation of Morris County, New Jersey. Hartshorne Fitz-Randolph bought one , zero zero zero acres ( four km) of what would become the township in the Mine Hill area in one seven five three .
In one eight zero five , the township was formed from the larger Mendham Township. Dover separated from Randolph in one eight nine six , and Mine Hill Township gained independent status in one nine two three .

There are several sections of Randolph, including Mount Freedom, Center Grove, Fernbrook, Ironia, and Shongum. (Source: Daily Record)

Randolph Township's two two square miles in western Morris County have been designated half rural, half suburban by the New Jersey State Planning Commission. 

The town was inhabited by the Lenni Lenape Native Americans, settled by Quakers, and served as a supply point for George Washington's army during their winter in nearby Jockey Hollow. Randolph Historical Society has preserved this heritage in the Museum of Old Randolph. One of Randolph's oldest streets, Gristmill Road, is on the National Register of Historic Places. 

Randolph became a vacation haven in the early part of the two zero th century, known for its woods, ponds, lakes and invigorating air. Through the one nine five zero s, farms, large hotels and bungalow colonies dotted the community. Performers like Phil Silvers, Frank Sinatra and Jan Pierce appeared at the hotels. Boxers Max Baer, Floyd Patterson, James J. Braddock and Rocky Marciano trained or fought at Sain's Hotel on Brookside Road. The Sain Hotel later turned into a vacant building used by drug addicts, and burned down in the late eighties. 

Randolph's two four township historical landmarks range from the two seven six year old Liberty Tree through the one eight six nine Bryant Distillery (famed for its apple jack) to the one nine two four Millbrook School, now rehabilitated and in use as offices.

Randolph is located within the New Jersey Highlands, one of New Jersey's four major physiographic provinces. Part of the Appalachian Mountains, the Highlands are characterized by alternating flat-topped ridges and deep-striking valleys. 

Land in Randolph runs from five five one to one one two zero feet above sea level. While a major state road bisects the town, country roads wind through woods, along streams, up and down hills. Open land is preserved by both municipal and county parkland within the town boundaries. 

Temperatures range, in an average year, from the low two zero s in February to the mid- nine zero s fahrenheit in August. With Route one zero , Route two four Interstate two eight seven , Interstate eight zero , Interstate seven eight , Interstate two eight zero nearby the average commute to work is two seven minutes, which means many of Randolph's citizens have time to be involved in community recreation and government. (Source: Randolph Township Website)

 Government 
 Local government 
The Township Council is the legislative body of Randolph. Randolphs Council-Manager form of government calls for the partisan, at-large election of seven Township Council members, from whom the elected body selects one of its members to serve as mayor each year.

The council represents the public and develops and adopts policies, resolves public issues, formulates township policy through motions, resolutions and ordinances which reflect the needs of the public, and maintains a working knowledge of intergovernmental issues and how they will affect the Township of Randolph. Thirteen separate advisory boards and committees assist policy formulation of the council.

The Township Council is similar to a corporate board of directors and is assisted by the Township Attorney, who prepares ordinances and advises on legal issues, the Township Clerk, who prepares resolutions, and the Township Manager, who functions much like the CEO of a corporation.

Members of the Randolph Township Council for two zero zero five are Mayor Al Napoliello (term ends two zero zero six ), Deputy Mayor Gary Algeier (term ends two zero zero seven ), Jon Huston (term ends two zero zero six ), Andrew J. Manning (term ends two zero zero six ), Trina Mitsch (term ends two zero zero seven ), Michael Obremski (term ends two zero zero seven ) and Arlene Price (term ends two zero zero six ).
 Federal, state and county representation 
Randolph Township is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's two five th Legislative District.

 

 



Life in Randolph

The community of Randolph Township is quite close-knit, so many are involved in the different functions of the town. There is a public library, with regularly scheduled reading groups and other programs. Many citizens are involved in Randolph's Senior Citizen Center, where games, get-togethers and other exciting activities are hosted. The Brundage Park Playhouse shows plays with youth and adult performers alike.

Randolph is also popular for athletics. In the schools, there are pre-high school track, football and soccer teams, among others. Randolph is represented in regional athletic conferences, such as the Iron Hills Conference. In terms of recreation, there are many programs available for children, teenagers and adults.

'''Washington Township''' is a Township located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of one seven , five nine two .

Washington Township has the distinction of occupying the largest area of any municipality in Morris County. The township borders Somerset, Warren, and Hunterdon Counties and is approximately fifteen miles from Pennsylvania and the Delaware River. U.S. Highway four six , and County Route five one three and County Route five one seven pass through town. Interstate eight zero is only minutes away in the neighboring community of Mount Olive.

Long Valley is a census-designated place and unincorporated area located within Washington Township. The Long Valley section  the heart of the township  was called German Valley when it was first settled in the one seven zero zero s by people from Saxony, a region of Germany near the Polish border.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of one one six . two km ( four four . nine mi ).  one one six . two km ( four four . nine mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

There are five , seven five five households out of which four seven . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven six . one % are married couples living together, six . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and one five . three % are non-families. one two . two % of all households are made up of individuals and five . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, two . zero % of those under the age of one eight and four . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Government 
 Local government 
The New Jersey Legislature enacted the Township Act of one seven nine eight , in an effort to bring more efficient government to a young state. The act incorporated one zero four Townships, and authorized an elected group, referred to as the freeholders to form a committee to oversee the expenditure of township funds between town meetings.

The Township Act was modified over one five zero times between one eight four six and one eight nine nine , when in one eight nine nine the Act abolished the town meeting form of government and empowered the three elected members with legislative powers. Later revisions to the act increased the number of committee members to five, with elections scheduled so the three year terms were staggered.

In one nine eight nine the Township Act and its many amendments and revisions were replaced with a much clearer and concise statute through the coordinated efforts of the State Legislature and Governor overseen by the State Commission on County and Municipal Government. The Township Act of one nine eight nine retained the basic structure of the township form of government and provided for a mayor elected by the committee from among its members for a one-year term of office. The Act provides for an annual partisan election, with primaries in June and the general election in November. 

The Elected Officials of the Washington Township Committee are Mayor Tracy Tobin (R) (term expires in two zero zero six ), Vice Mayor Kevin Walsh (R) ( two zero zero seven ), Walter J. Cullen (R) ( two zero zero seven ), Kevin M. Nedd (I) ( two zero zero eight ) and Kenneth Short ( two zero zero six ).

 Federal, state and county representation 
Washington Township is in the Eleventh Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's two four th Legislative District.

 

 



 Education 
The Washington Township Schools include five schools and a central office. There are approximately two nine five zero students currently enrolled in the schools served by two three zero teaching staff. 

The Old Farmers Road School serves the southern section of the district and houses approximately five five zero students in grades K- four . The Walter J. Kossmann School and the Flocktown Road School form a two building complex serving the northern section of the district. Kossmann houses approximately five six zero students in grades K- two . Flocktown houses approximately four five zero students in grades three - four . The Long Valley Middle School is centrally located in the valley and serves the entire district.  Long Valley Middle School houses approximately one four zero zero students in grades five - eight . The new Benedict A. Cucinella Elementary School housing grades K- four is scheduled to open in September, two zero zero six . Then, all elementary schools will house grades K- five and the middle school will house grades six - eight .

Students in grades nine - one two attend West Morris Central High School, which is located in Washington Township and is part of the West Morris Regional High School District. Students in the district come from the surrounding Morris County school districts of Chester Borough, Chester Township, Mendham Borough, Mendham Township and from Washington Township.

 '''Wharton''' is a Borough located in Morris County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the borough had a total population of six , two nine eight .

 Geography 
Wharton is located at four zero  five three ' five three  North, seven four  three four ' four nine  West ( four zero . eight nine eight zero nine eight , - seven four . five eight zero one five one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of five . seven km ( two . two mi ).  five . seven km ( two . two mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . three six % water.

 History 
On June two eight , one eight nine five , voters from the settlements of Port Oram, Irondale, Luxemburg, Maryville and Mount Pleasant voted one four three to five one to incorporate as a town under the name of Port Oram, the largest member of the group. These localities, covering an area of two and a quarter square miles west of Dover, New Jersey, were basically mine camps or housing for blast furnace and silk mill workers. A mayor, six councilmen, an assessor and a collector were elected to govern this new borough which had started life as an ore shipping port on the Morris Canal. These elected officials -- mine superintendents, store owners, a railroad superintendent and a school teacher -- represented the leaders of these settlements where iron ore was mined, smelted and shipped.

In one eight three one the Morris Canal was completed from Newark to Phillipsburg, New Jersey across the Delaware River from the terminus of the Lehigh Canal. On the way, it passed through Boonton, Dover and Port Oram all connected with iron. On this route it tapped the Morris County ore fields and became a carrier for both ore and pig iron. Its main purpose, however, was as an extension of the Lehigh Canal to furnish a route for anthracite coal from the Pennsylvania mines to seaboard. Any local traffic was a gain to supplement the through anthracite freight and iron ore and its products soon became important sources of revenue. Sites on the canal were selected for docks and industry, including iron works 

Born in one eight two six in Philadelphia to an old Quaker family, he first studied at a local Friend's school but being sickly did not attend college, rather he was sent to a farm to regain his health and during the winter studied chemistry at the laboratory of Martin Boye in Philadelphia. Joseph Wharton died in January one nine zero nine .

The average household size is two . seven zero and the average family size is three . two eight .

 ''Sister Carrie'' book cover

'''''Sister Carrie''''' ( one nine zero zero ) is a novel by Theodore Dreiser about a young country girl who moves to the big city where she starts realizing her own American Dream by embarking on a life of sin rather than by hard work and perseverance.

At the time of its first publication, the novel caused a minor scandal and Dreiser had difficulty finding a publisher for it. This was due to the blurred division line between good and bad in the plot and the fact that, at the end, Carrie is rewarded rather than punished for her immoral life. Although Dreiser's moralising narrator does assert that, despite the fame and the money she has amassed, Carrie will not be able to achieve peace of mind in her life, the apparent lack of poetic justice -- the notion that immorality should pay in the end, even if only up to a point -- was a concept the reading public were altogether unused to at the time.

Plot

Leaving her rural Wisconsin home, one eight year-old Caroline Meeber heads for Chicago, Illinois, where she wants to live with her older sister's family. Soon, however, Carrie finds out that working in a sweatshop and living in a squalid and overcrowded apartment is not what she wants. When she meets a man named Drouet, a travelling salesman whose acquaintance she already made on the train to Chicago, she readily leaves behind her family they never see Sister Carrie again when he offers to look after her.
Drouet installs her in a much larger apartment in return for her favours. Through Drouet, Carrie meets Hurstwood, the manager of a respectable bar. From the moment he sets eyes on her, Hurstwood is infatuated with the young girl, whereas for Carrie, Hurstwood is just a wealthy man past the prime of his life. Before long they start an affair, communicating and meeting secretly in the expanding, anonymous city. Although Hurstwood has a family and Carrie might conclude that he does, the lovers never talk about it and it never seems to occur to Carrie to ask.

One night, at his job, Hurstwood is presented with the opportunity to embezzle a large sum of money. He succumbs to the temptation and decides, on the spur of the moment, to leave everything behind and start a new life with Carrie. Under a pretext, he lures Carrie onto a northbound train and escapes with her to Canada. After a while, his guilty conscience makes him pay back most of the money, but there is no way he could return to his former life so the couple eventually decide to move to the East coast.

The second part of the book is set in New York City. Hurstwood and Carrie rent a flat where they live as man and wife under an assumed name. Gradually, Hurstwood realizes that finding a new job is not easy at all. As his money is slowly running out, the couple have to start economizing, which Carrie does not like at all. She starts looking for a job herself and finds employment at one of the many theatres. Her rise to stardom is sharply contrasted with Hurstwood's downfall: she leaves him, and the rapidly ageing Hurstwood, overwhelmed by apathy, is left all alone, without a job and without any money. At one point, during a strike, he even works as a scab driving a Brooklyn streetcar. He joins the homeless of New York and finally, in a cheap hotel, puts an end to his life.

In his Nobel Prize Lecture of one nine three zero , Sinclair Lewis said that Dreiser's great first novel, ''Sister Carrie'', which he dared to publish thirty long years ago and which I read twenty-five years ago, came to housebound and airless America like a great free Western wind, and to our stuffy domesticity gave us the first fresh air since Mark Twain and Whitman .

Movie version
''Sister Carrie'' was filmed in one nine five two as ''Carrie'' by William Wyler starring Jennifer Jones in the title role and Laurence Olivier as Hurstwood. The movie should not be confused with Stephen King's novel and Brian De Palma's one nine seven six film version ''Carrie'', which is not a remake of Wyler's movie.

'''Brick Township''' is a Township located in Ocean County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of seven six , one one nine . Brick Township is governed under the Faulkner Act (Mayor-Council) system of municipal government.

Since the year two zero zero zero , Brick Township has been the safest city (population over seven five , zero zero zero ) in New Jersey. In two zero zero three and two zero zero four , Brick Township held the title of being the second safest city in the United States after Newton, Massachusetts . In two zero zero five , Brick Township dropped down to the fourth safest city (population over seven five , zero zero zero ) in the United States. (Source: ISBN zero - seven four zero one - zero seven three nine - nine )

Brick Township has also been in the news for its autism epidemic in which four zero children out of over six zero zero zero surveyed were found to be autistic. There is no proof, however, that this is linked to any specific environmental factor in Brick, since many of the children were born in Northern New Jersey and other parts of the country. In addition, Brick's autism rate is statistically not far removed from national average.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of eight three . six km ( three two . three mi ).  six seven . nine km ( two six . two mi ) of it is land and one five . six km ( six . zero mi ) of it is water. The total area is one eight . six nine % water. Brick Township is bordered to the north by Howell Township and Wall Township, both of Monmouth County; to the west by Lakewood Township, to the east by Point Pleasant, and to the south by Toms River. Brick Beach, which is detached from the Township, is bordered to the north by Mantoloking and to the south by Toms River.

As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are seven six , one one nine people, two nine , five one one households, and two zero , seven seven five families residing in the township. The population density is one , one two zero . five km ( two , nine zero one . five mi ). There are three two , six eight nine housing units at an average density of four eight one . two km ( one , two four six . zero mi ). The racial makeup of the township is nine five . eight one % White, zero . nine nine % African American, zero . one zero % Native American, one . one nine % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . eight five % from other races, and one . zero four % from two or more races.  three . eight five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race. 

Current projections, as of June two zero zero five , estimate the population of Brick Township to be around eight three , five zero zero with a trend moving towards a more non-white population. This is influenced by a large emigration of residents from Northern New Jersey and New York City, whom make up the majority of the township's population.  

There are two nine , five one one households out of which three one . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five six . eight % are married couples living together, one zero . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and two nine . six % are non-families. two five . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. Laurelton Circle
The '''Laurelton Circle''' was located near the center of Brick Township. The traffic circle was at the junction of Route seven zero , Route eight eight , and Princeton Avenue. It was converted to a traffic light regulated intersection in one nine eight six , due to an increase in traffic and accidents. To reduce the need for left turns, a short portion of eastbound Route eight eight was re-routed onto Princeton Avenue. Some other movements are controlled by jughandles and a two-way connection in the northwest corner.

;See also
List of traffic circles in New Jersey

 Government 
 Local government 
The Township operates under a Faulkner Act (Mayor-Council) form of government. The Mayor is elected for a four year term without limitation as to the number of terms. In November one nine eight eight , the voters approved a referendum which returned the Township to the partisan system of government. As a result, Township elections, which had been held in May, are now held in November.

The Mayor is the chief executive and administrative officer in the Township and, as such, is responsible for administering local laws and policy development. The specific powers of the Mayor include various appointments, preparation of the Township's budget, and approval or veto (which may be overridden by a two three vote of the Township Council) of the ordinances adopted by the Township Council. The Mayor appoints, with the advice and consent of the Township Council, the Business Administrator, the Township Attorney, and the Directors of the Departments of Public Safety, Engineering and Public Works.

The current Mayor of Brick Township is Joseph C. Scarpelli (D). Members of the current Township Council are President Anthony Matthews (R), Vice President Stephen C. Acropolis (R), Ruthanne Scaturro (R), Michael A. Thulen, Sr. (R), Dan Toth (R), Kathy M. Russell (D) and Joseph Sangiovanni (R).

 Federal, state and county representation 
Brick Township is in the Fourth Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's one zero th Legislative District.

 

 



Noted residents
Major League Baseball All-Star pitcher Hank Borowy who played for the New York Yankees, Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies, Pittsburgh Pirates and Detroit Tigers. He lived the majority of his life in Brick Township and died there at age eight eight . 
Mike Bucci, a professional wrestler who wrestled for ECW and WWE under the names '''Simon Dean''' and Nova
National Hockey League Player Jim Dowd who grew up playing in the Ocean Ice Palace (which was featured in the motion picture Chasing Amy starring Ben Affleck)
Actress Kirsten Dunst, who also lived in Point Pleasant

 Map of Lacey Township in Ocean County
'''Lacey Township''' is a Township located in Ocean County, New Jersey and is considered part of the Jersey Shore region. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of two five , three four six . It was named for Continental Army General John Lacey.

Forked River is a census-designated place and unincorporated area located within Lacey Township. The township also contains the unincorporated area of Lanoka Harbor. 

The Oyster Creek Nuclear Generating Station is located in the southern part of the township.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of two five five . two km ( nine eight . five mi ).  two one seven . six km ( eight four . zero mi ) of it is land and three seven . six km ( one four . five mi ) of it is water. The total area is one four . seven four % water. The township is bordered by the Barnegat Bay to the East, Berkeley Township on the North, Ocean Township to the South, and Woodland Township to the West. 

In Lacey Township, the north-south track of the Garden State Parkway serves as an informal use divider under the one nine seven nine Pinelands Act and the subsequent Comprehensive Management Plan. To the east of the Parkway are more than nine five % of Lacey's residential dwellings, located in the unincorporated areas of Lanoka Harbor and Forked River. To the Parkway's west is a mostly undisturbed pine and cedar forest, part of New Jersey's vast Pine Barrens. The forest is interspersed with a scattered few farms, houses ranches, the tiny village of Bamber Lake and open pit gravel quarries - all of which predate passage of the Pinelands Act or were developed under its tight zoning rules. The conditions of grandfathering vary - the mines' exceptions are to expire upon the deaths of their owners whereas the farms' exceptions are indefinite. Development west of the parkway is strictly controlled by the New Jersey Pinelands Commission.

'''Lakehurst''' is a Borough located in Ocean County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the borough had a total population of two , five two two .

Lakehurst is located at four zero  zero ' four seven  North, seven four  one nine ' one three  West ( four zero . zero one three zero six six , - seven four . three two zero three nine zero ).

As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , five two two people, eight seven zero households, and six six two families residing in the borough. There are eight seven zero households out of which four one . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five seven . five % are married couples living together, one three . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two three . nine % are non-families. one nine . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and six . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . nine zero and the average family size is three . three three .

In the borough the population is spread out with three zero . six % under the age of one eight , eight . zero % from one eight to two four , three four . one % from two five to four four , one nine . four % from four five to six four , and eight . zero % who are six five years of age or older. Males have a median income of $ three five , four zero three versus $ two six , six six seven for females. Out of the total population, seven . six % of those under the age of one eight and two . five % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

History
The town of Lakehurst first reached international fame as a winter resort around the turn of the two zero th century, following the opening of the Pine Street Inn in one eight nine eight . In one nine one one , the rope factory in the town burned down, prompting the formation of a volunteer fire department.

Lakehurst is frequently cited as the site of the Hindenburg disaster, when on May six , one nine three seven the German Zeppelin Hindenburg caught fire at the Lakehurst Naval Air Station. In fact, the Hindenburg exploded over portions of Manchester Township, not the more famous Lakehurst. None of the Lakehurst Naval Air Station lies within the Borough of Lakehurst.

 Government 
 Local government 
The Borough of Lakehurst's governing body consists of a Mayor and six Council Members elected at large. Members of the Council are elected for three-year terms with two Council Members being elected each year while the Mayor is elected every four years.

The Borough form of government, which dates back to one eight seven eight , is the single most popular form of local government in New Jersey. The Mayor retains all general law authority, presides over council meetings, and can vote in case of a tie. With the advice and consent of the council, the Mayor appoints all subordinate officers of the Municipality. The Council is the legislative body of the Borough and is responsible for formulating all local ordinances. There are currently two one eight New Jersey municipalities using the borough form of government.

The Mayor of Lakewood Borough is Stephen F. Childers. Members of the Lakewood Borough Council are Council President Harry Robbins, Tim Borsetti, James Davis, Pat Ford, Steven Oglesby and Edward Smith.
 Federal, state and county representation 
Lakehurst is in the Fourth Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's nine th Legislative District.

 

 



 Education 
The Manchester Township School District is the receiving district for approximately one six zero high school students from Lakehurst Borough at Manchester Township High School in Manchester Township.

'''Lakewood Township''' is a Township located in Ocean County, New Jersey. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the township had a total population of six zero , three five two . Lakewood is an urban center in Northern Ocean and Southern Monmouth Counties. 

Lakewood is one of the hubs of Orthodox Judaism, home to one of the largest yeshivas in the world. The large Orthodox population wields considerable political clout in Lakewood Township, commanding a block of about one zero , zero zero zero votes for candidates supported by the Orthodox leadership.

Lakewood CDP ( two zero zero zero Census population of three six , zero six five ), Leisure Village ( one , seven eight five ) and Leisure Village East ( one , five nine four ) are census-designated places and unincorporated areas located within Lakewood Township.

 Government 
 Local government 
Lakewood's Township Committee is a five-member committee elected in staggered three-year terms. The township committee exercises all legislative power of the township, except in matters of health, which are done at the Board of Health. In addition, the Committee appoints members to many boards, commissions, and committees. Each member of the township committee serves as a liaison to different divisions, departments, and committees.

The mayor, elected from among the members of the committee, presides at meetings and performs other such duties as the Township Committee may prescribe. The mayor has the power to appoint subcommittees with the consent of the committee. When authorized, he or she executes documents on behalf of the township, makes proclamations concerning holidays and events of interest, and exercises ceremonial power of the Township and other powers conferred upon him by law.

The Mayor of Lakewood Township is Meir Lichtenstein. Other township committee members are Raymond G. Coles (Deputy Mayor), Charles Cunliffe, Menashe Miller and Sen. Robert Singer.

 Federal, state and county representation 
Lakewood Township is in the Fourth Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's three zero th Legislative District.

 

 



Education
The Lakewood School District is broken up into three different stages of schooling. ( two zero zero three - zero four enrollment data is from the National Center for Education Statistics). Students from K- six attend one of the district's four Elementary Schools: Oak Street School, with nine six eight students; Spruce Street School, with six one four students; Clifton Avenue School, with seven eight one students; and Ella G. Clarke School, with nine three nine students (including pre-K). In grades seven and eight children attend Lakewood Middle School, which has seven six eight students. For grades nine - one two students attend Lakewood High School, with an enrollment of one , three eight nine students.

Georgian Court University is a private university located on the shores of Lake Carasaljo.

Trivia 
In the universe of DC Comics, the actual towns and geography in and surrounding the Mystic Island section of Little Egg Harbor Township are replaced by Gotham City, home of Batman.

 Government 
 Local government 
Little Egg Harbor operates under the Township form of government. The Township Committee cocnsists of five members elected to serve three-year terms on a staggered basis. Each year, the Township Committee selects one of its members to serve as Mayor, and another as Deputy mayor, both serving one-year terms. The members of the Township Committee are Mayor Ray Gormley (term ends one two three one zero five ), 
Deputy Mayor Barbara Jo Crea ( one two three one zero seven ), Brian E. Rumpf ( one two three one zero five ), Scott Stites ( one two three one zero six ) and Arthur Midgley ( one two three one zero six ).

Students in grades seven - one two attend the schools of the Pinelands Regional School District, which serves students from Bass River Township, Eagleswood Township, Little Egg Harbor Township and Tuckerton Borough. The district is comprised of the Pinelands Regional Junior High School ( one , zero eight two students in grades seven - nine ) and Pinelands Regional High School ( eight eight eight students in grades one zero - one two ). The current combined enrollment is nearly two , zero zero zero students. The student to teacher ratio is two five : one in the high school, and two two : one in the middle school.

Out of the total population, three . zero % of those under the age of one eight and five . two % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Government 
 Local government 
Voters elect a Mayor and six Borough Council members in partisan elections on an at-large basis. The Mayor serves a four-year term. The Borough Council members serve staggered three-year terms, with two seats coming up to vote each year. 

The Mayor is the head of municipal government; sees that state laws and borough ordinances are faithfully executed; presides over the Council. votes only to break ties; can veto ordinances subject to override by two three majority of Council; and appoints subordinate officers with Council approval. After thirty days or upon Council disapproval, Council fills posts.

The Borough Council is the legislative body of municipality. The Council overrides a mayor's veto by two three majority of all members, confirms mayor's appointments. The Council gains appointment power upon failure to confirm mayor's appointee or after office vacant for thirty days. The Council has all executive responsibility not placed in office of mayor.

The Mayor of Point Pleasant is Martin Konkus who, this November will run for a second term.The members of the Borough Council are Brian W. McAlindin (Council President), Timothy Ferrie, Shawn McCarthy, Shaun O'Rourke, Roger Pyrtko and Lee Birdsall Sharpe.

 Federal, state and county representation 
Point Pleasant is in the Fourth Congressional District and is part of New Jersey's one zero th Legislative District.

 

 



 Trivia

A fictionalized version of the town was the setting of a short-lived two zero zero five television show, ''Point Pleasant.''

 Government 
Local government
The Borough of Seaside Heights' governing body consists of a Mayor and six Council Members elected at large. Members of the Council are elected for three-year terms with two Council Members being elected each year, while the Mayor is elected to serve a four-year term.

In the borough form of government, the Mayor retains all general law authority, presides over council meetings, and can vote in case of a tie. With the advice and consent of the council, the Mayor appoints all subordinate officers of the Municipality. The Council is the legislative body of the Borough and is responsible for formulating all local ordinances.

The Mayor of Seaside Heights is P. Kenneth Hershey. Borough Council members are William Akers, Joyce Camera, Joann Duszczak, Arleen Ottorson, Richard Tompkins, Tom Yannacone
