 '''Portales''' is a municipality located in Roosevelt County, New Mexico, USA, with a total population of one one , one three one ( two zero zero zero census). It is the county seat of Roosevelt County and is also the home of Eastern New Mexico University. It is located near the larger city of Clovis as well as Cannon Air Force Base, a major contributor to the economy of the region.

Eastern New Mexico University opened in one nine three four and has grown to become the third largest university in the state. Peanuts and sweet potatoes were formerly the largest crops in the area. Although Portales is one of the largest producers of Valencia Peanuts in the United States, it is now best known for its successful, growing dairy industry.

City
The city's downtown area is centered around a traditional square, descending from Spanish urban design, with a county courthouse and various commercial venues. The university, Eastern New Mexico University (ENMU), forms a sizable district with its campus and surrounding residential stock catering to students. Portales has thirty-four churches, which are predominantly Baptist.

 Geography 
Location of Portales, New Mexico
Portales is located at three four  one zero ' five six  North, one zero three  two zero ' one nine  West ( three four . one eight two one eight four , - one zero three . three three eight seven three seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one seven . seven km ( six . eight mi ).  one seven . seven km ( six . eight mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

History
The town takes its name (Spanish for gates ), from a nearby rock formation thought by the first Western visitors to resemble gates or porches.
The settlement was founded in the late one eight zero zero s and the city was formally established in one nine zero nine . Its first mayor was Washington Ellsworth Lyndsey, later a state governor of New Mexico. 

Economy
The town and surrounding communities are heavily dependent on agriculture, including cattle ranching and dairy farming, peanuts, and grain, as well as the service industry. Retailers include Wal-Mart, many dollar stores and Allsups convenience stores. There are two bars in Portales.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one one , one three one people, four , one eight eight households, and two , six five nine families residing in the city. The racial makeup of the city is six eight . eight zero % White, two . two eight % African American, one . one two % Native American, zero . nine six % Asian, zero . zero nine % Pacific Islander, two three . three nine % from other races, and three . three five % from two or more races.  three eight . one three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four , one eight eight households out of which three three . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four five . three % are married couples living together, one four . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and three six . five % are non-families. two seven . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and one zero . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four nine and the average family size is three . zero nine .

In the city the population is spread out with two six . three % under the age of one eight , two zero . one % from one eight to two four , two five . four % from two five to four four , one five . nine % from four five to six four , and one two . two % who are six five years of age or older. Airport










'''Four Corners Regional Airport''' is a public airport located one mile northwest of Farmington, New Mexico. The airport has three runways: two paved with asphalt and one that is dirt.

 '''Shiprock''' (Navajo: '''Naat anii Nz''') is a census-designated place (population eight , one five six , according to the two zero zero zero census) located in San Juan County, New Mexico on the Navajo reservation. 

Shiprock is named after the nearby Shiprock rock formation. It is home to the annual Northern Navajo Fair, held every October. It is also home to a campus of Din College (formerly Navajo Community College), a tribally controlled community college with seven other campuses across the Navajo Nation. It is the site of a Chapter House for the Navajo and a BIA Agency, as well as being a key road junction for truck traffic and tourists visiting the Four Corners, Mesa Verde, and the Grand Canyon'

 The Plaza Hotel, built in one eight eight one , on the Plaza of West Las Vegas.

'''Las Vegas''' is a city located in San Miguel County, New Mexico. Once two separate towns, West Las Vegas ( old town ) and East Las Vegas ( new town ), divided by the Gallinas River, retain distinct characters and separate, rival, school districts. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one four , five six five . It is the county seat of San Miguel County.

Las Vegas is the home of New Mexico Highlands University. It is often used in the media as a mistaken location, referring to Las Vegas, Nevada. Las Vegas is also a venue used by the IBNA for teacher training, perhaps due to the proximity of the Armand Hammer United World College of the American West. 

Teddy Roosevelt's Rough Riders held their first reunion at the Plaza Hotel in Las Vegas in one eight nine nine .

 Movies filmed in Las Vegas
Parts of ''The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez'' ( one nine eight three ) were filmed in and around Las Vegas.

Early silent film star Tom Mix made a number of Western films here. 

Las Vegas was the real-world town used to represent the fictional setting of Calumet, Colorado in John Milius' one nine eight four film ''Red Dawn''. As of two zero zero five , many of the buildings and structures seen in the film remain.

The town was the filming location for parts of the one nine seven eight movie ''Convoy'', a film about truck drivers inspired by the one nine seven five song of the same name by C.W. McCall.

In the one nine six nine movie ''Easy Rider'', Las Vegas, NM is the town where the two bikers ride behind a parade, are arrested for parading without a permit, and meet Jack Nicholson's character in jail. The town name can be seen in the background in one scene during this part of the movie.

Several scenes in the one nine nine eight John Carpenter's Vampires were filmed in the plaza.

In the two zero zero one documentary Freedom Downtime, a cross-country road trip to Las Vegas, Nevada ends up in Las Vegas, New Mexico by mistake.

 '''Pecos''' is a village located in San Miguel County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of five , four four one . The easternmost suburb of Santa Fe, traffic congestion is becoming heavier along the freeway from downtown. A fast growing area, Pecos has become a colony for a large Gay and Lesbian population, who admire the towns climate, attitude, and proximity in metro Santa Fe. Problems for the area include traffic, sky-rocketing property values, and the need for greater integration with Santa Fe.

 '''Here is the temporary format of what an article about a battle would look like. This is not the final format. Only the finalized format which all has agreed upon will be placed on Wikiproject Battles'''


(Links, can either be placed at the top or bottom of the page)

History -- Military history -- List of battles -- Thirty Years' War
 The Box 
The box summarizes crucial informations and should be able to tell what happened on the battlefield without reading the text. Lists of battles will be sorted on the criteria listed in the box.

Sortable criteria that can be listed in the box:

 one ) dates of the battle. (sorted chronologically on List of battles, eg. September five 

 two ) year of the battle (eg. one six three four )

 three ) venue of the battle. (sorted alphabetically on first letter of the place, eg Nordlingen)

 four ) country of the battle (sorted bny names of coutry, eg Germany)

 five A) side A of combatants (eg. Saxony, Sweden)

 six A) forces of side A ( and types of troops etc)

 seven A) links of important personnels of side A, eg Horn, Duke Bernhard

 five B) side B of combatants (eg. Holy Roman Empire)

 six B) troops of side B ( and types of troops)

 seven B) links of important personnels, eg. 

 five C), six C, seven C) side C of combatants

 eight ) result

 nine ) stats (eg. casualties: one zero zero zero soldiers, two zero zero zero wounded, two zero zero missing. Marshall Horn and five zero zero soldiers as POWs. etc.)

 The Text 
'''Overview'''
A paragraph on short description of the battle; some disambuguations if needed.
eg. This article is the Battle of Nordlingen in one six three four . See also Battle of Nordlingen ( one six four five )

'''Historical significance''' 
talks about how the battle affect the whole picture of the war. Can be merged with Aftermath if they described more or less the same scenario.

'''Prelude''' 
e.g.
After the Protestant victory at Lutzen, two years before, the Swedes failed to follow up their victory due to the death of their King Gustavus Adolphus. As a result, the Imperial forces regained the initiative. In one six three four they occupied the town of Regensburg. Threatening to advance further into Saxony, they started to besiege Nordlingen. The 
Protestants realized they had to make some attempt to relieve the town, and planned a night attack.

'''Geography'''
e.g.
Geography of the Nordlingen city should be here. Emphasis is on how the landscape relates to the tactics employed on the battleflied. eg. one ) Hill A is two miles away from the city, making artillery bombardment more feasible. two ) Highway one zero is the only road connecting the city to ammunition supply depot at station B. Defenders thus constantly patrols the highway or invaders thus try to control the highway before lauching full scale attack.

'''Notable Figures from both sides'''
links to the generals and their posts.


'''Troops information and deployment'''
how the troops of all sides enter the battlefield, detailed description on troops composition.

'''Description of the Battle''' or '''Strategic appraisal''' or some other relevant titles
eg.
The Protestant's intended assault went wrong when their forces got cluttred up with artillery and supply wagons in front of the infantry. This gave the imperial forces time to prepare. Swedish infantry ended up in an unsupported attack on the Imperial positions.
Nevertheless they pushed on and succeeded in driving back one Imperial flank. The Imperial commander responded by a coordinated attack on the Saxon lines, which broke and collapsed.
Horn was captured, and the Protestant allies lost one two - one four zero zero zero men.

'''Aftermath'''
This battle marked the end of Swedish interference in the Thirty Years War. With Imperial forces threatening dominance in Germany, France stepped in.

'''Casualties Assessment'''
stats (eg. casualties: one zero zero zero soldiers, two zero zero zero wounded, two zero zero missing. Marshall Horn and five zero zero soldiers as POWs. etc.)

'''San Ysidro''' is a village located in Sandoval County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two three eight . The village is near the junction of U.S. Highway five five zero and NM Highway four , at the south end of the Jemez Valley. It is also on the Jemez River, just north of were the Rio Salado joins the Jemez. 

This has been a farming community since one six nine nine when Juan Trujillo established a settlement named for San Ysidro, or Saint Isidore the Farmer. The Village was incorporated in one nine six seven . An annual San Ysidro Fiesta Day is held each year in mid-May.

'''''Uncle Jam Wants You''''' is an album by Funkadelic.

Significance
In some ways, Uncle Jam Wants You (a reference to the Uncle Sam wants you! US Army recruitment posters) is a more militant sequel to the previous album, One Nation Under a Groove. Whereas that album described an ideal country ruled by Funk, Uncle Jam actually attempts to provoke the conversion into Funkadelia. Its purpose is also (as the cover claims) to rescue dance music from the blahs.  The cover art depicts George Clinton in a Huey Newton-Black Panthers pose, reflecting the more martial lyrical themes of the album.

Track listing

 (Not Just) Knee Deep (George Clinton Junior)
 Uncle Jam (Clinton Sr, Bootsy Collins, Bernie Worrell)
 Field Maneuvers (D. Clinton???, D Clinton???)
 Holly Wants to Go to California (Clinton Sr., Bernie Worrell)
 Foot Soldiers (Star Spangled Funky) (Clinton Sr., Jim Vitti)

Keyboards ( Keyboard Battlecruisers ): Bernie (U.S.S. Woo!) Worrell, J.S. Theracon
Drums ( Uncle Jam's Drum and Wiggle Corps ): Tyrone Speedfeet Lampkin, Larry Fratangelo
Bass ( Bass Anti-Flam Units ): Rodney Skeet Curtis, Cordell Boogie Mosson
Vocals ( Vocal Assault ): Uncle Jam Clinton, Gary DooWop Shider, Larry Sir Nose Heckstall, Sheila Horn, Ron Prophet Ford, Jeanette McGruder, Dawn Silva, Michael Clip Payne, Greg Thomas, Stingray Davis

Critical Response
 Uncle Jam Wants You takes not merely a more daring musical approach but a more forthright political stance  The All Music Guide

 '''Lamy''' is a census-designated place located in Santa Fe County, New Mexico to the south of the city of Santa Fe. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of one three seven . The former Atchison, Topeka, and Santa Fe Railroad (ATSF) passes through Lamy. This railroad, usually called just the Santa Fe , was originally planned to run from Atchison, Kansas, on the Missouri River, to Santa Fe, the capital city of New Mexico, and then points west. However, as the tracks progressed west into New Mexico, the civil engineers in charge realized that the hills surrounding Santa Fe made this impractical. Hence, they built the railway line though Lamy, instead. Later on, a spur line was built from Lamy to Santa Fe, bringing the railroad to Santa Fe at last. Thus Lamy became an important railroad junction.

 '''Los Cerrillos''' is a census-designated place located in Santa Fe County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of two two nine . Accessible from State Highway one four , Los Cerrillos is on the road from Santa Fe to Albuquerque, closer to Santa Fe. Visitors to the town may stop at the Rock ShopPetting ZooMuseum where they can buy samples of various rocks, minerals, and other naturally occurring curiosities, feed chickens, peacocks, goats, and llamas, and tour the Museum of Northern New Mexican History, which contains artifacts from the old west days, and cardboard cutouts of characters from the film ''Young Guns'', which was filmed in and around Los Cerrillos.

 '''San Ildefonso Pueblo''' is a census-designated place located in Santa Fe County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of four five eight .

 Geography 
Location of San Ildefonso Pueblo, New Mexico

San Ildefonso Pueblo is located at three five  five three ' five two  North, one zero six  seven ' one nine  West ( three five . eight nine seven nine zero two , - one zero six . one two one eight three four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one zero . seven km ( four . two mi ).  one zero . two km ( three . nine mi ) of it is land and zero . six km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is five . five four % water.

San Ildefonso Pueblo is located at the foot of the Pajarito Mountains just one two . eight seven km ( eight miles) east from Los Alamos New Mexico, three eight . six km ( two four miles) NW of Santa Fe, New Mexico. A large volcanic outcroping lies directly north of San Ildefonso Pueblo, it is called the Black Mesa.  The Rio Grande runs through San Ildefonso Pueblo and the lowest elevation is approximately one six seven six meters ( five five zero zero feet).

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are four five eight people, one five zero households, and one one eight families residing in the CDP. The population density is four five . one km ( one one six . seven mi ). There are one seven eight housing units at an average density of one seven . five km ( four five . four mi ). The racial makeup of the CDP is one six . one six % White, zero . zero zero % African American, seven nine . four eight % Native American, zero . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, two . eight four % from other races, and one . five three % from two or more races.  one zero . four eight % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one five zero households out of which three eight . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four eight . zero % are married couples living together, two four . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and two zero . seven % are non-families. one five . three % of all households are made up of individuals and six . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is three . zero five and the average family size is three . four three .

In the CDP the population is spread out with three one . four % under the age of one eight , one zero . zero % from one eight to two four , two six . four % from two five to four four , two two . five % from four five to six four , and nine . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three two years. For every one zero zero females there are nine zero . eight males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine eight . seven males.

Out of the total population, zero . zero % of those under the age of one eight and five zero . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 History 
The pueblo (Spanish for town) was founded when people came from the Mesa Verde complex in Southern Colorado. These people had first moved to Bandelier just south of Los Alamos New Mexico (birthplace of the atomic bomb). There these people thrived due to the rainfall (elevation about seven zero zero zero feet) and the ease of constructing living structures from the surrounding soft volcanic rock. But after a prolonged drought the people moved down into the valleys of the Rio Grande around one three zero zero AD. The Rio Grande and other arroyos provided the water for irrigation. 

The Spanish conquistadors tried to subdue the native people and force their religion on the native people during the early one six zero zero s, which lead to the Great Pueblo Revolt of one six eight zero . The people withstood the Spaniards by climbing to the top of the Black Mesa. The siege ended with the surrender of the native people but the Spanish gave the native people freedom of religion and other self-governing rights.
Black-on-Black pottery of the pueblo. Artifact at the Field Museum, Chicago
The pueblo natives continued to lead an agricultural based economy until the early one nine zero zero s when Maria Martinez and her husband Julian Martinez rediscovered how to make the Black-on Black pottery for which San Ildefonso Pueblo would soon become famous. From that time the pueblo has become more tourist minded with numerous tourist shops existing in the Pueblo. Because of the nearness of the State of New Mexico Capital (Santa Fe) and the presence of the Los Alamos National Laboratory a large portion of those employed in the pueblo have government jobs.

Cities in New Mexico
Sierra County, New Mexico
 
   
 :''For the game show, see Truth or Consequences.''

'''Truth or Consequences''' is a city located in Sierra County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, it had a total population of seven , two eight nine . It is commonly known within New Mexico as '''T or C'''.

Originally called '''Hot Springs''', it took the name of a popular radio program in one nine five zero , when ''Truth or Consequences'' host Ralph Edwards announced that he would do the program from the first town that renamed itself after the show. Ralph Edwards came to the town during the first weekend of May for the next fifty years. This event was called the Fiesta and included a beauty contest, parade, and a stage show. The town was also the fictional hometown of Cactus Jack, one of the many professional wrestling personas of Mick Foley.

It is the county seat of Sierra County.

Virgin Galactic, the first company to develop commercial flights into space, has decided to put its world headquarters and mission control two five miles south of Truth or Consequences, New Mexico.

 '''Magdalena''' is a village in Socorro County, New Mexico, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , nine one three . Magdalena has recently been trying to transform the town into an art center and culture destination. The opening of at least a dozen art galleries, several rock and mineral shops, a woolery, the renovation of the Bank West Building and the Magdalena Hall Hotel have all made their mark on this mountain village. The ghost town of Kimberly, and two important festivals-the Lady Magdalen Art Walk, and the Old Timers Reunion and Rodeo bring toruists to the area. Newly paved roads, additions to the large school, and a pulic water, trash disposal service and the opening of a new Mini-Mart and Gas Station have improved the quality of life for its citizens. The town was founded at the base of a mountain, which has the silhouette of Lady Magdalen on the hillside, giving the town its name.

 '''Socorro''' is a city located in Socorro County, New Mexico in the Rio Grande Valley, at an elevation of four five seven nine feet. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of eight , eight seven seven . It is the county seat of Socorro County.

The City of Socorro bills itself as having been established in one five nine eight , but it would be more accurate to say that the area was named in that year by Spanish explorers who had crossed the Jornada del Muerto and were much in need of the aid and hospitality they received upon reaching the area which is Socorro today. The name means aid , help , or refuge .

Modern Socorro offers many diversions for travelers and tourists, but is easily missed by drivers on Interstate two five . Those travelers who explore the area beyond California Street (the main through road) can easily get lost as the pattern of roads in Socorro follows several patterns which come together at atypical intersections. Additionally, some streets in town are oddly named: Central and Center street are parallel, two blocks apart; Neel and Neal have nothing to do with each other; there is a Cassity St. on one end of town and a Cassady Ln. on the other; and Long Street is one block long while Short Street is three blocks long.

Socorro is home to the New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology, the Energetic Materials Research and Testing Center, as well as the New Mexico State Fire Academy. Also on the campus at Tech is the NRAO (National Radio Astronomy Observatory) Array Operations Center, the headquarters for the Very Large Array radiotelescope which is west of Socorro between Magdalena and Datil, and which was where various parts of the movie Contact was set.

UFO incidents
Socorro has been the site of a number of important incidents in UFO history. The most famous and best-documented of these involved a Socorro policeman by the name of Lonnie Zamora on April two four , one nine six four . An unknown object landed and took off just south of town. Zamora was able to approach the craft within five zero feet and also reported seeing two small humanoid crew members from a distance. Much physical trace evidence was left behind. The incident was considered one of the most puzzling cases investigated by the Air Force's Project Blue Book.

On July two four , one nine four nine , a green fireball was observed falling close to Socorro, one of a large number of these mysterious green fireball incidents over northern New Mexico that began in late one nine four eight . Dust samples were collected at the School of Mines and were found to contain large particles of copper. This was considered an important possible clue to the composition of the fireballs, since copper would burn with the same anomalous yellow-green color associated with the fireballs.

There have also been several stories of UFO crashes taking place near Socorro, including one purportedly associated with the Roswell UFO incident in one nine four seven . There is still no convincing evidence to support any of these rumored Socorro area crashes.

Located on the northwest side of the beautiful Enchanted Circle highway, Questa is the poorest and least developed town on the route. '''Red River''' is a town located in Taos County, New Mexico, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of four eight four .

History
The town of Red River began in earnest in the one eight seven zero s, when miners were drawn in by gold strikes in the area. By one eight nine five , Red River was a booming mining camp and had a population estimated at three , zero zero zero . The mines shut down a few years later and the population waned, but the town lived on, and by the one nine three zero s the remaining residents turned to tourism to sustain the town.

 Geography 
Location of Red River, New Mexico
Red River is located at three six  four two ' two three  North, one zero five  two four ' one nine  West ( three six . seven zero six three one one , - one zero five . four zero five two seven one ). Red River is located in the southern Rocky Mountains, part of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and is completely surrounded by the Carson National Forest.

The main industry in Red River is tourism. Red River sits at the base of the Red River Ski Area, located eight seven five zero feet above sea level in the southern Rocky Mountains.  '''Taos Ski Valley''' is a village located in Taos County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of five six . The town is one of the major ski areas in the state. It is one of the last U.S. resorts not to allow snowboarding. Very alpine in climate, culture and geography, the area is almost indistinguishable from a community in Switzerland. The village has an elected council.

 '''Folsom''' is a village located in Union County, New Mexico. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of seven five .

 Geography 
Location of Folsom, New Mexico
Folsom is located at three six  five zero ' five three  North, one zero three  five five ' five  West ( three six . eight four eight one five two , - one zero three . nine one eight one seven six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one . four km ( zero . five mi ).  one . four km ( zero . five mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

History
Folsom is the type site for the Folsom Tradition, a Paleo-Indian cultural sequence dating to between nine zero zero zero BC and eight zero zero zero BC. The Folsom site was excavated in one nine two six and found to have been a marsh-side kill site or camp where two three bison had been killed using distinctive tools, known as Folsom points.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are seven five people, three one households, and one nine families residing in the village.  '''Altamont''' is a village located in the Town of Guilderland in Albany County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , seven three seven . The name means high mountain. 

The '''Village of Altamont''' is in the western part of the town. 

(NOTE: The former Town of Altamont in Franklin County, New York is now know as the Town of Tupper Lake )

 History 
The village was formerly called Knowersville.  A village fair has been held since one eight nine three .

 Geography 
Altamont is located at four two  four two ' one nine  North, seven four  two ' one  West ( four two . seven zero five three two six , - seven four . zero three three four eight seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of three . one km ( one . two mi ).  three . one km ( one . two mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. However, there are two major streams that run through the town center.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , seven three seven people, six four six households, and four seven four families residing in the village. The population density is five five eight . nine km ( one , four five one . five mi ). There are six seven four housing units at an average density of two one six . nine km ( five six three . two mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine seven . six four % White, one . zero nine % African American, zero . zero zero % Native American, zero . one two % Asian, zero . zero six % Pacific Islander, zero . one seven % from other races, and zero . nine two % from two or more races.  one . zero four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six four six households out of which four two . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six zero . one % are married couples living together, one one . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and two six . five % are non-families. two two . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six six and the average family size is three . one four .

In the village the population is spread out with three zero . one % under the age of one eight , five . one % from one eight to two four , three zero . two % from two five to four four , two two . three % from four five to six four , and one two . four % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, three . five % of those under the age of one eight and five . nine % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Points of Interest 
In colonial times, this area was part of the Manor of Rensselaerwyck, granted by the Dutch West India Company to Killian Van Rensselaer in one six three zero . The area was known as Hellerburgh in the early one seven zero zero s. In the early one eight zero zero 's Knowersville was established in the rural part of Albany county just below the Helderberg Mountains. This settlement eventually became known as Altamont.

Altamont was a summer vacation spot that was reached by train. The train station which once served this once busy whistle stop is currently a law office. The old hotel in the town center burned down nearly a century ago. Altamont still hosts a fairground that operates a week long country fair in mid-August. The fairground is also the site of other festivals.

There is an elementary school, post office, drugstore, funeral home, feed store and a weekly newspaper, the ''Altamont Enterprise''. There are three churches in the town center: St Lucy Roman Catholic Church, St John Lutheran Church, and the Altamont Reformed Church.

 '''Bethlehem''' is a town located in Albany County, New York, USA in the USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of three one , three zero four .

The '''Town of Bethlehem''' is south of the City of Albany. Bethlehem is comprised of five hamlets: Delmar, Elsmere, Slingerlands, Glenmont, and Normanskill. Route nine W passes through the town. The town is named after the biblical Bethlehem. 

 History 
When Henry Hudson saild up the river that would eventually bear his name, he is thought to have landed at what is now the town of Bethlehem. The spot where he is presumed to have landed is comemorated at the town's Henry Hudson Park. The town was established in one seven nine three from the Town of Watervliet. In one eight three two , part of the town was used to form the Town of New Scotland. 


The Town's earliest growth took place in Normanskill, named for its location along the Normanskill, a creek, which forms town's border with Albany, NY. In the mid one eight zero zero 's the Delaware and Hudson railroad initiated service into the hamlet then called Adamsville, renaming the hamlet Delmar. Delmar has become the most populated hamlet and its Delaware Avenue is the site of the present day town hall, police station, justice court, public library, as well as numerous businesses. The railroad discontinued passenger service in the one nine six zero 's and its tracks started being removed in the year two zero zero zero with the last of the track removed in two zero zero five . The Town has continued to grow, and is today considered to be an affluent suburb of the city of Albany, NY.

 Politics 
The town, controlled for over one hundred years by the republican party, is now controlled by the Democrats. In a two zero zero three election, Teresa Egan was elected the first Democratic town supervisor in over a century. The Democrat takeover was solidified by the two zero zero five election of two more Democrat board members and the reelection of Egan. 

During the two zero zero five supervisor election, two zero year old Victor Rodriguez ran as a write-in candidate for the position after being taken off the ballot by the Conservative party. Recently, the Voter rights party, founded by Rodriguez, has started growing within the town and within Albany County. After the loss by the Republicans in two zero zero five , the local committee has loss a lot of support within the town, and many expect that the Voter rights party may take over as a major party in town.

 Education 
Most Town residents live within the Bethlehem Central School District. The town has five public elementary schools -- Hamagrael, Elsmere, Slingerlands, Glenmont and Clarksville. Elementary schools include students up to grade five . The Bethlehem Central Middle School educates children in grades six , seven and eight , while the Bethlehem Central High School includes grades nine - one two . The High School also features a Lab School, a school-within-a-school created to experiment with new methods of teaching and learning. The employees of the high school are wholly unfriendly.

The Town also includes the School of Saint Thomas the Apostle, a Catholic school for grades K- eight located across from the Catholic church.

The school district offers Continuing Education classes in a variety of topics for adult learners of all ages. 

The Town also provides busing and most textbooks for families who choose to educate their children in private schools. The nearby City of Albany includes several noted private schools and academies, including the Albany Academy for Boys, the Albany Academy for Girls, the Doane Stuart School, the Christian Brothers Academy, and Bishop Maginn High School.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one two eight . four km ( four nine . six mi ).  one two six . four km ( four eight . eight mi ) of it is land and two . zero km ( zero . eight mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . five five % water. 

 Location and adjacent areas 
The town is located in Albany County, New York. The east town line, defined by the Hudson River, is the border of Rensselaer County, New York. To the north, the town shares a border with Albany, the capital of New York State. To the west is the Town of New Scotland, and to the south is the Town of Coeymans. 

The New York State Thruway ( Interstate nine zero  passes through the town.

 '''Cohoes''' is a city located in Albany County, New York, USA. At the time of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one five , five two one . The name is believed to arise from a native expression, meaning below the falls. 

The '''City of Cohoes''' is at the northeast corner of the County. It is called the Spindle City because of the importance of textile production to its growth. 

 History 
The city is on land purchased from the local natives in one six three zero . The land was once part of the Rensselaerwyck manor. 

In one eight three zero , a dam was constructed. This provided power to make the community a leading textile center with the establishment of the Harmony Manufacturing Company, later famous as Harmony Mills, in one eight three six . In one eight six six , during excavation work for construction of one of the mills, the bones of a mastadon were unearthed. During the one eight seven zero s the mills were enormously profitable, a result of the Erie Canal that flows past them. Mill three , at over one zero zero zero feet long, has been considered the longest continuous textile mill in the country at the time, although some dispute that Lowell, Massachusettes was in fact home to the longest mill. In one eight four eight , Cohoes was incorporated as a village, and in one eight six nine chartered as a city.

The one nine th century saw an influx of immigrants to Cohoes to work in the mills, particularly French Canadians from Quebec, and Irish. 

 Past residents of note 
It is the birthplace of baseball player George Davis. 

 Geography 
Cohoes is located at four two  four six ' two four  North, seven three  four two ' one one  West ( four two . seven seven three two five zero , - seven three . seven zero three one one zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one one . zero km ( four . two mi).  nine . seven km ( three . seven mi) of it is land and one . three km ( zero . five mi) of it is water. The total area is one one . seven nine % water. 

The City of Cohoes is at the confluence of the Mohawk River and the Hudson River. The city includes '''Van Schaick Island''', where the historic Van Schaick Mansion is located, and '''Simmons Island'''. 

The city borders Saratoga County, New York. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one five , five two one people, six , nine three two households, and three , eight six one families residing in the city. The population density is one , six zero two . three km ( four , one four five . eight mi). The racial makeup of the city is nine five . one four % White, two . one six % African American, zero . one six % Native American, zero . six eight % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander, zero . five nine % from other races, and one . two three % from two or more races.  two . zero three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six , nine three two households out of which two five . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three six . four % are married couples living together, one five . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and four four . three % are non-families. three eight . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two zero and the average family size is two . nine one .

In the city the population is spread out with two two . four % under the age of one eight , eight . five % from one eight to two four , two nine . three % from two five to four four , two two . five % from four five to six four , and one seven . three % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are eight six . one males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight one . six males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three two , eight five six , and the median income for a family is $ four two , zero five four .  Additional Cohoes facts 
Large knitting mills took advantage of the power of the Cohoes Falls in the one nine th Century.

In several of Kurt Vonnegut's novels the character Kilgore Trout is a longtime resident of Cohoes, N.Y.

 '''Knox''' is a town located in Albany County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , six four seven . 

The '''Town of Knox''' is in the northwest part of Albany County and is west of Albany, New York. The town calls itself the pillbox capital of the world. 

 History 
The Town of Knox was established in one eight two two from part of the Town of Berne. During the American Revolution loyalties of the inhabitants was split, but the issue was resolved when Tories moved away. The fire house serves pancakes in the spring for a syrup festival.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one zero eight . six km ( four one . nine mi ).  one zero eight . two km ( four one . eight mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . three three % water. 

The west town line is the border of Schoharie County, and the north town line is the border of Schenectady County.

 Demographics

 The '''Abraham Lincoln Brigade''' was an organization of United States volunteers supporting or fighting for the anti-fascist Spanish Republican forces in the Spanish Civil War as part of the International Brigade.

The name brigade is something of a misnomer, as there were several American battalions organized under the Fifteenth International Brigade of the Spanish Republican army. This brigade was loosely organized by the Comintern and was made up of volunteers from nations around the globe. The George Washington Battalion, Abraham Lincoln Battalion, John Brown Anti-Aircraft Battery were part of the American contingent. Other U.S. volunteers served with the MacKenzie-Papineau battalion (Canadian), the Regiment de Tren (transport) and in various medical groups. The name Abraham Lincoln Brigade was used to include all the U.S. volunteers, regardless of which unit they served with.

Most of the people making up the Abraham Lincoln Brigade were official members of the Communist Party USA or affiliated with other socialist organizations. The IWW, or Wobblies , were lightly represented. However, the brigade was made up of volunteers from all walks of American life, and from all socio-economic classes. It was the first unit of soldiers made up of Americans to have an African-American officer, Oliver Law, lead white soldiers.

American volunteers began organizing and arriving in Spain in one nine three six . Centered in the town of Figueras, near the French border, the brigade was organized in one nine three seven and trained by Robert Merriman. By early one nine three seven , its numbers had swelled from an initial nine six volunteers to around four five zero members. In February one nine three seven the League of Nations Non-Intervention Committee banned foreign national volunteers.

The International Brigade was used by the Loyalist army for several battles in Spain. They unsuccessfully defended the supply road between Valencia and Madrid in the Jarama Valley from February one nine three seven until June one nine three seven . They were also present at the battles of Brunete, Zaragoza, Belchite, and Teruel. 

The Brigade was a ''cause celebre'' in the United States, however. Liberal and socialist groups organized fund-raising activities and supply drives to keep the Brigade afloat. News of the Brigade's high casualty rate and bravery in battle made them romantic figures to an America concerned about the rise of Fascism around the world.

The war dragged on and the Fascist forces gained victory after victory over the Spanish Republic. The International Brigade was withdrawn from battle by the Spanish prime minister in spring of one nine three eight . Most of the surviving Lincolns were repatriated promptly afterwards, and were welcomed home as heroes.

The legacy of the Lincoln Brigade has been a romantic vision of idealistic volunteers fighting for justice and freedom in a nation far from their own.

In the aftermath of the Spanish Civil War, however, members of the Brigade were castigated as supporters of the Soviet Union. Following World War II, at the height of the Red Scare , former members of the Brigade were considered security risks, and branded premature anti-fascists .

The US volunteers of the International Brigades adopted a song named The Red River Valley. This song was translated into Catalan and is nowadays a folk song for young boy and girl scouts during summer camps and sung by youth at music festivals. The lyrics have changed under the perhaps confused perception that it was an African spiritual song brought to the US mainland by enslaved people. However, the song is said by others to be an English or a Canadian, not
a Texan song, that became popularized among US soldiers. Whichever the case, the tune is a combat song chanted by those who fought against the empire, fascisms of various sorts, and in favor of the underdog. The first Catalan line says: trobarem a faltar el teu somriure (we will miss your smile).

'''Elizabeth Bthory''' (married ''Elizabeth Ndasdy'', ''Albeta Btoriov-Ndady'' in Slovak, ''Bthory Erzsbet'' in Hungarian, August seven ?, one five six zero - August two one , one six one four ), the '''Bloody Lady of achtice''', was a Slovak countess. She lived in achtice (''Csejte'' in Hungarian) castle near Trenn, in present-day Slovakia. She is considered the most famous serial killer in Slovak and Hungarian history. She spent most of her life at the achtice Castle. She and her alleged four collaborators were accused of torturing and killing numerous girls and young women ( two zero - two zero zero zero victims, depending on the source. It is rumoured that she documented each death in her diary, totalling to six one two entries). In one six one zero , she was imprisoned in solitary confinement, where she stayed until her death four years later. Her nobility permitted her to avoid an immediate execution. However, her alleged collaborators were executed.

Various legends about her life, including the idea that she bathed in or drank the blood of servant girls, are thought by some to have been the origin of numerous vampire myths, the Dracula story, and the trope of the sexually sadistic vampiress in particular. She has a few historical nicknames, The Blood Countess and Countess Dracula because she was a possible model for Bram Stoker's vampire character.
framed

The Bthory lineage
The ancestors of Elizabeth (the Gutkeled clan) came to the Hungarian Kingdom in the mid- one one th century. They held power in what is now Poland, Hungary, Slovakia, and Romania. The Gutkeled clan emerged to assume a role of relative eminence by the early one three th century and the name Bthory (according to one of their estates Bthor today Nyrbtor meaning '' valiant '') was assumed by that sub-family in one two seven nine . Their power peaked during the mid- one six th century, and was virtually gone by one six five eight . With the death of the wife of George Rkczi II (Zsfia Bthory), they died out in one six eight zero . Elizabeth's parents were from the two branches of the Bthory family (Bthory of Ecsed and Bthory of Somly) and the brother of Elizabeths mother was the Polish king Stephen Bthory.

Life
She was born in Nyrbtor in present-day Hungary on August seven one five six zero and died on August two one  one six one four in achtice in present-day Slovakia.

She spent her childhood at the Ecsed Castle; details from this period are unknown. At the age of one one she was forced to become engaged with the noble and successful warrior Francis Ndasdy and moved to the Srvr Castle. In one five seven five , she married Ndasdy in Vranov nad Topou, who in one five seven eight became the chief commander of Hungarian troops in their war against the Turks. He was considered a very brave, but also very cruel person. The Turks feared him and called him the Black Beg. 

Ndasdys wedding gift to Elizabeth was his home, the achtice Castle (situated in the Carpathians in present-day western Slovakia near Trenn, then part of the Kingdom of Hungary) together with the achtice country-house and seventeen adjacent villages. The castle itself was surrounded by a peasant village and rolling agricultural lands, interspersed with outcroppings of the Carpathian Mountains. In one six zero two , Elizabeths husband definitively bought the castle from the emperor Rudolf II, so that it became a property of the Ndasdys. Since battles with the Turks occupied her husband, Elizabeth became the lady of the castle. At this time she was able to read and write in four languages. 

Elizabeth had six children though two of them died at an early age:

Anastasia Bthory, illegitimate daughter (born one five seven four ).
Anna Ndasdy (born c. one five eight five ).
Katalin (Katherina) Ndasdy (born c. one five nine four ).
Miklos.
Orsolia (Orsika) Ndasdy.
Paul Ndasdy ( one five nine eight - one six five zero ).

Her husband died in either one six zero two or one six zero four .

It is unknown when Elizabeth started to kill young women, if she did; however, it is speculated that she did so sometime between the years one five eight five and one six one zero . Both her husband and her relatives knew about her sadistic inclination, but they did not directly intervene. She was constantly improving her torturing methods and her brutality was increasing. While her husband lived, she apparently kept her activities to a moderate level, but upon his death any restraints he may have imposed on her (or she on herself) were completely removed. It is said that people living around her castle hated her so much that she only left the castle under an armed escort. (Note: politicians and other famous figures often use armed escorts, whether hated or not.) However, she did torture some girls at her properties in Srvr and Keresztr. Her victims were initially local female peasants, many lured to Cachtice by offers of well-paid work, but when word spread of the countess's inclinations, the supply of new maids began to dwindle. It was then she began to kill daughters of lower gentry, who were sent to her castle by their parents to learn noble manners. In the early one seven th century, parents of substantial position often wished their daughters to be educated in the social graces and etiquette. When it became known in the surroundings what she was (probably) doing, she had to send assistants to bring young women from more distant regions. As rumours spread throughout the Hungarian Kingdom, she had to have girls kidnapped in order to get them. 

It was only after the parish priest of achtice and monks in (relatively) nearby Vienna had lodged several complaints with the ruling class in Vienna about cries from the castle that the (new) emperor Matthias II assigned Gyrgy Thurz, the palatine of Hungary, to investigate the complaints. Thurz and his men invaded achtice in the morning of December two nine  one six one zero and caught Elizabeth in the act in the achtice country-house; she was torturing several girls - one of them had only just died. She and four collaborators were charged with sadistic torture, as well as mass murder. Despite the overwhelming evidence found by investigators, Elizabeth herself was not brought to trial. Her son Paul and his tutor Megyery, raised valid concerns that apart from the public scandal and family disgrace, under the law the family inheritance would go to the crown. While she was investigated in absentia, Elizabeth was kept under tight house arrest and waged a spirited defence by a furious stream of letters. But the outcome was inevitable. The bloody countess was bricked up in her own private chamber of her castle, kept alive only by food poked through a slit in the door, and died there on August two one  one six one four . For the fates of her collaborators see below.

 Guilt or innocence 
More than three zero zero people were interrogated before her death between one six one one and one six one four . Despite several interventions by the Hungarian king, a regular trial never took place and the case remained open. The reason for this might have been that the palatine Thurz did not want a trial against a member of the high gentry (with which he was reproached at the time). Moreover, Elizabeths nephew Gabriel Bthory was the ruler of Transylvania and Thurz did not want to get into troubles with Transylvania. And finally, Thurzs properties were adjacent to those of Elizabeth and Thurz was interested in her properties. 

Some sources mention the possibility that she was falsely convicted by the political opponents of the family, mainly because the Bthory family owned large areas of land and were wealthy. The existing historical documents show lack of investigation, omitted evidence and decisions kept in tight local political circles. Some of the most dramatic charges against her, that of Satanism and vampirism, are thought to have been either deliberate falsehoods or folklore that grew up around a disliked figure. Some people claim that the vampire legends could have been exaggerations of actual medical help provided for peasants; at that age it was very unusual that a noble cared about the health of her servants, and bloodletting was practiced by medical authorities for many years. Modern supporters of the vampire legends attached to her life are either unaware of or choose to ignore historical documents and letters that would possibly ruin the otherwise dramatic tales.

Irma Szdeczky-Kardoss, a Hungarian researcher published a very interesting article in Hungarian scientific magazine  let s Tudomny (December two zero zero five ) where she presented the results of many years of research on the life of Erzsbet Bthory. She strongly believes that the countess was the victim of a frame-up trial conducted by palatine Gyrgy Thurz from Western Hungary (man of Mtys II, King of Hungary). The goal of all this feigned action was to defame Prince Gabriel Bthori of Transylvania (brother of Elizabeth), who did not want to recognize the supremacy of Catholic Habsburgs over his small, mainly Protestant country.
Three hundred witnesses were summoned during the trial, but no injured, or tortured people, and no eyewitnesses were found. Not having enough proofs, the palatine postponed the passing of a sentence, and finally was urged by the emperor himself to do something and make an end to the proceedings.
 Ms. Szdeczky-Kardoss writes that actually not Erzsbet in person, but her servants treated a number of people, including young girls, of different diseases, with surgical tweezes, hoes and protractors specific to the period (lancing of abscesses and dirty wounds with hot iron; alternating hot and cold baths, phlebotomy etc.)

 Motives 
Her deviation might have had genetic reasons, because many of both her fathers and her mothers ancestors were very brutal individuals (e. g. the Transylvanian ruler Sigismund Bthory who liked to have his retainers killed). Alternatively, it is believed that the Bthory family was inbred and that this may have helped cause various psychotic disorders that the family was known to have.

Only later legends say that she was killing the girls in order to bathe in their blood and, thus, stay forever young or improve her complexion. 

It should be noted, however, that brutality was relatively widespread at the time. People arrested under suspicion of crimes and sometimes even witnesses were tortured for their confessions, and punishment of the poor or of political enemies was often death.

Collaborators
A shadowy figure named Anna Darvulia, a suspected local witch that dabbled in black magic and satanic ritual, is rumoured to have influenced much of Elizabeth's early sadistic career, but apparently died before the major events of Elizabeth's reign of terror commenced.

Elizabeth's main collaborators after Anna's death were her maids 
 Dorottya Szentes, Dorota Sentov, or Dorko; 
 Helena Jo Ilona J
 and Katarna Benick or Katalin Benick
: as well as the dwarf Jnos Ujvry, Jn Ujvri, or Fick. 

Except for Katarna, they were all executed at Byta on January seven  one six one one .

Katarna's guilt could not be proven, and according to McNally's sources from recorded testimony by all witnesses, she seems to have been dominated and bullied by the other executed women. Two of the women had their extremities hacked off before being thrown onto a blazing fire, while Fick, whose guilt was deemed the lesser, had the mercy of being beheaded before being consigned to the flames. A public scaffold was erected near the castle to show the public that justice had been done.

The confessions and testimony against Bthory were taken under torture by Thurzo.

 Legends 
The following lists some of the best known legends about Elizabeth Bthory. Although some are partly based on statements made by those interrogated after one six one zero , their truthfulness cannot be verified. 

Torture
While interrogating Turks, her husband employed a device of torture: articulated claw-like pincers of silver; which, when fastened to a whip, would tear and rip the flesh to such an obscene degree that he abandoned the apparatus in disgust and left it at the castle.

Aware of Bthory's preoccupations, her aunt had introduced her to the flagellation of others, a taste she quickly acquired. Equipped with her husband's silver claws, she generously indulged herself, whiling away many lonely hours at the expense of forlorn Slavic debtors. She preferred to whip her subjects on the front of their nude bodies rather than their backs, so that she could watch their faces contort in horror at their fate.

Bthory, being a sadist, had many ways of brutally torturing her victims, most of which were young girls. This gave the impression that she was bisexual. She usually had drastic punishments for servants who disobeyed the rules of her household. Elizabeth would stick pins under the fingernails of a servant who broke a rule. A technique her husband taught her before he died was something he liked to call the 'Honey Torture'. This was constructed by stripping a girl naked and covering her in honey. She was then left to be swarmed by bees. Her husband did not torture to kill, unlike The Countess. She liked to see their faces as she tortured them til death. During the harshest parts of winter, she would strip girls naked and force them outside. She would then pour water over them until they froze solid. She would then gaze among her 'beautiful' sculptures. She often enjoyed stripping girls in her room and made them lie flat on their backs as she tortured them. It is said they bled so profusely, pools of blood were left on her floor, which could be scooped up by bucketfulls. Elizabeth killed with such graceful glee, it was hard to believe she was human herself. She often viewed her servants as something other than human and cherished the contorted agony on their faces.

Witchcraft
Under torture, alleged conspirators of Bthory confessed to being witches.

Bloodbath
Elizabeth was a beauty back in her age. She had a very pale face contrasted with dark hair. Her face youthful and beautiful and her body voluptuous. She was intent on keeping her beauty and tried to force it to last. Once the concequences of time started taking a toll on her body, Elizabeth tried to cover it up with makeups and extravagant clothing, the most expensive around. It is said that the Countess bathed in the blood of peasant virgin girls usually young in age. This came about in an accidental discovery. One day, one of the Countess' servant girls was tending to Elizabeth's hair. She had either pulled it, or said her headdress was in some way not attractive. Elizabeth became engraged with her and slapped her so hard, her nose bled. Droplets of blood hit the Countess in the face and as she wiped it away, she claimed the wrinkles on her face had disappeared. She had a personal and close friend who happened to be a witch who told the Countess that the blood, indeed, would make her young and beautiful again. She had taken the young girl and slit her wrists and drained her of her blood. She then bathed in it, giving her the name ''The Blood Countess''. She began using her servants as 'blood donors'. When she began to run out of servants, she had people go out and kidnap virgin peasant girls. She became known as evil and hated, so when she left her castle, she had to have body guards to protect her, mainly from enraged peasants.

Lesbianism
Many works of fiction portray the countess as bisexual or lesbian. This speculation is tied directly to the belief that she exclusively murdered women.

In music
The black metal band Bathory, although taking its name from the blood countess, had few songs about her. The black metal band Cradle of Filth has many songs about the countess, and its one nine nine eight album, ''Cruelty and the Beast'', is completely dedicated to Elizabeth. Progressive power metal band Kamelot have a three part song on their Karma album about Bathory called Elizabeth.

In fiction
Bathory is a major character in the alternative historyfantasy novel ''This Rough Magic'' by Eric Flint, Dave Freer and Mercedes Lackey. In the book she is of undetermined age and uses the blood of the slain young girls to retain her youth and power, in the eventual goal of attaining immortality without giving up her soul to Shaitan.

''The Blood Countess'' is a novel by Andrei Codrescu, a Romanian native and descendent of Elizabeth Bathory, currently a professor of writing at Louisiana State University and columnist with NPR.

 '''Kling Klang''' is the private music studio of the band Kraftwerk. Its name is taken from track on their ''Kraftwerk two '' album. The studio, or at least an office, is located at Mintropstrae one six , in the middle of the red light district of Dsseldorf, Germany. 

Kraftwerk founders Ralf Htter and Florian Schneider first rented a room to use as a rehearsal space in one nine seven zero , and Htter has cited this as the beginning of their group. Their facilities there developed steadily, however it was not until one nine seven five that they were sufficient to record an entire album there (''Radio-Activity''). The studio does not appear to have been christened ''Kling Klang'' until one nine seven six .

The group have at times referred to the studio as their mother ship , and as a musical instrument in its own right, which they play interactively. (The latter concept is similar to ideas put forward by Brian Eno in the early one nine seven zero s.) For Kraftwerk's one nine eight one ''Computer World'' tour, the band literally packed up their entire studio and took it around the world with them.

It is nearly impossible for anyone to come into contact with the studios, as all mail is returned unopened and any outsiders are not welcome. The group is extremely secluded, and it is said that even though there is a phone installed, the number is not even known by the record company, and the telephone doesn't have a ring tone, as the group doesn't want any unwanted noise to interfere with their recording sessions. There is an anecdote about Johnny Marr, of The Smiths fame; Marr wanted to hold a recording session in the studios, and after several fruitless attempts to call the studio directly and mailing to them, he was told by the record company to call at a precise time on a precise date. The phone was answered immediately by a member of Kraftwerk, without showing any sign of ringing.

 Barr, Tim. Kraftwerk : From Dusseldorf to the Future (with Love). Ebury Press one nine nine eight ; ISBN zero zero nine one eight six four nine zero nine

 History

In one eight six four two railroads were built through the Town of New Scotland, headed west from the Hudson River, both trying to find a way around the Helderbergs. The Albany and Susquehanna line and the New York, West Shore and Buffalo railroads crossed one another in a farm field. Subsequently a village grew up around the crossroad and in one eight nine nine the Village of Voorheesville (named for a railroad attorney) was incorporated.

 '''Watervliet''' is a city located in Albany County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one zero , two zero seven .

The '''City of Watervliet''' is north of Albany, New York and is at the east border of the Town of Colonie. The city calls itself the Arsenal City. 

 History 
The explorer Henry Hudson arrived in the area of Watervliet around one six zero nine . The area was first settled in one six four three as part of the Rensselaerwyck Patroonship (see: Kiliaen Van Rensselaer). 

In one seven seven six , the Shakers settled in the Watervliet region. The Town of Watervliet was founded in one seven eight eight and included all of the county except Albany. This location of the future city was incorporated as the Village of Gibbonsville , along with the unincorporated Village of Port Schuyler and Village of West Troy in one eight three six . The City of Watervliet was incorporated in one eight nine six after the rest of the town became the Town of Colonie in one eight nine five . Because so many towns had been created from the Town of Watervliet, it is regarded as the mother of towns in the county. 

The Watervliet Arsenal, founded in one eight one three , is the oldest Federal arsenal in the country; it was the sole manufacturing facility for large caliber cannons. 

The junction of the main route of the Erie Canal to Buffalo and the Lake Champlain branch was in Watervliet, and a weigh station and a center for paying canal boat operators was located there; as a result, it was once famous for gambling, saloons, and prostitution.

 Past residents of note 
Watervliet was the birthplace in one eight two four of Leland Stanford, Governor of California and founder of Stanford University.

 Geography 
Watervliet is located at four two  four three ' two nine  North, seven three  four two ' two two  West ( four two . seven two four six two eight , - seven three . seven zero six one six two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three . nine km ( one . five mi ).  three . five km ( one . three mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is one zero . zero seven % water. 

Watervliet is on the west bank of the Hudson River. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one zero , two zero seven people, four , six six five households, and two , five four seven families residing in the city. The population density is two , nine four one . zero km ( seven , six zero eight . zero mi ). There are five , one one six housing units at an average density of one , four seven four . one km ( three , eight one three . three mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine two . zero zero % White, three . eight seven % African American, zero . one eight % Native American, one . three four % Asian, zero . zero eight % Pacific Islander, one . two one % from other races, and one . three three % from two or more races.  three . six two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four , six six five households out of which two six . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three two . nine % are married couples living together, one six . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and four five . four % are non-families. three eight . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one eight and the average family size is two . nine one .

In the city the population is spread out with two three . seven % under the age of one eight , nine . six % from one eight to two four , three one . zero % from two five to four four , one nine . seven % from four five to six four , and one six . zero % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Caneadea''' is a town located in Allegany County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , six nine four . The name is from the natives and means where the heavens rest on earth.

Houghton College, a private, Christian college, is located by the community of Houghton. 

 History 
The region was first settled around one eight zero zero . The Town of Caneadea was founded in one eight zero eight from part of the Town of Angelica.  Demographics

The population density is two nine . three km ( seven five . eight mi ). There are one , zero nine eight housing units at an average density of one one . nine km ( three zero . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine six . three three % White, one . zero zero % African American, zero . one five % Native American, zero . nine seven % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . five six % from other races, and one . zero zero % from two or more races.  two . two six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six five zero households out of which three three . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five six . five % are married couples living together, seven . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and three two . nine % are non-families. two five . two % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . seven two and the average family size is three . two zero .

 History 
The Town of Grove was established in one eight two seven as Church Tract from the Town of Nunda in Livingston County. The town assumed its current name in one eight two eight , possibly based on the number of trees in the town.

'''''K- two seven eight Komsomolets''''' was the only Project six eight five '''' (''Plavnik'', meaning fin , also known by its NATO reporting name of Mike -class) nuclear-powered attack submarine of the Soviet Navy.

Project six eight five was tasked with developing an advanced submarine that could carry a mix of torpedoes and cruise missiles with conventional or nuclear warheads. The first designs were developed in the one nine six zero s, but construction did not start until the first (and only) keel was laid down on two two April one nine seven eight at Severodvinsk. ''K- two seven eight '' was launched on nine May one nine eight three and commissioned in late one nine eight four .

''K- two seven eight '' had a double hull, the inner one being composed of titanium, which gave her an operating depth far below that of the best American submarines. An escape capsule was fitted in the sail to enable the crew to abandon ship in the event of an underwater emergency. Initial Western intelligence estimates of ''K- two seven eight ''s speed were based on the assumption that she was powered by a pair of liquid-metal lead-bismuth reactors. When the Soviet Union revealed that the submarine used a single conventional pressurized-water reactor, these estimates were lowered.

In October one nine eight eight , ''K- two seven eight '' was honored by becoming one of the few Soviet submarines to be given an actual name: '''' (''Komsomolets'', meaning a member of the Young Communist League ), and her commanding officer, Evgeniy Demitrievich Chernov, was made a Hero of the Soviet Union for diving to a depth of more than one three zero zero meters ( four two six five feet).

On seven April one nine eight nine , while still under Chernov's command and running submerged about one eight zero kilometres ( one zero zero nautical miles) southeast of Bjrnya, fire broke out in the aft compartment, and even though watertight doors were shut, the resulting fire spread through bulkhead cable penetrations. The reactor scrammed and propulsion was lost. Electrical problems spread as cables burned through, and control of the boat was threatened. An emergency ballast tank blow was performed and the submarine surfaced eleven minutes after the fire began. Distress calls were made, and most of the crew abandoned ship.

The fire continued to burn, fed by the compressed air system. and several hours after the boat surfaced, she sank again in one five zero zero - one seven zero zero meters ( five zero zero zero - five six zero zero feet) of water. The commanding officer and four others who were still on board entered the escape capsule and ejected it, but it was partially flooded and filled with toxic gasses. Only one of the five survived to reach the surface.

Rescue aircraft arrived quickly and dropped small rafts, but many men had already died from hypothermia in the two C ( three six F) water of the Barents Sea. The ship ''Aleksandr Khlobystsov'' arrived eight one minutes after ''K- two seven eight '' sank, and took aboard two five survivors and five fatalities. In total, four two men died in the accident.

In addition to her eight standard torpedoes, ''K- two seven eight '' was carrying two torpedoes armed with nuclear warheads. The site of the accident is one of the richest fishing areas in the world, and the possible leakage of plutonium from the torpedoes' warheads or enriched uranium and fission products from the reactor could destroy the local fisheries, costing billions of dollars annually. Under pressure from Norway, the Soviet Union used submersibles operated from the oceanographic rescue ship ''Akademik Mstislav Keldysh'' to search for ''K- two seven eight ''. In June one nine eight nine , two months after the sinking, the wreck was located. Soviet officials stated that any possible leaks were insignificant and no threat to the environment.

Examination of the wreck in May one nine nine two revealed cracks along the entire length of the titanium hull, some of which were of three zero - four zero centimetres ( one two - one six inches) wide, as well as possible breaches in the reactor coolant pipes. An oceanographic survey of the area in August one nine nine three survey did suggest that waters at the site were not mixing vertically, and thus the sea life in the area was not being rapidly contaminated. However, that survey also revealed a hole over six metres ( two zero feet) wide in the forward torpedo compartment.

An expedition during the summer of one nine nine four revealed some plutonium leakage from one of the two nuclear torpedoes. That expedition was successful in sealing some of the holes in the submarine's hull. On two four June one nine nine five yet another mission set out to seal the hull fractures, and declared success at the end of July one nine nine six . The Russian government has declared the risk of radioactive contamination of the environment negligible until two zero one five or two zero two five .

In one nine nine three , Vice Admiral (ret.) Chernov founded the ''Komsomolets'' Nuclear Submarine Memorial Society, a charity to support the widows and orphans of his former command. Since then, the Society's charter has expanded to provide assistance to the families of all Soviet and Russian submariners lost at sea.
