 '''Endicott''' is a village located in Broome County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one three , zero three eight . The village is named after Henry B. Endicott, a shoe manufacturer, who founded the community as the Home of the square deal. 

The '''Village of Endicott''' in the Town of Union and is west of Binghamton, New York. The town is served by the Greater Binghamton AirportEdwin A Link Field. It is part of the Triple Cities , along with Binghamton and Johnson City.

 History 
Part of Endicott was originally incorporated as Union Village in one eight nine two , but Endicott Village was consolidated with Union and named Endicott in one nine two one . Endicott is part of the Triple Cities, along with Johnson City and Binghamton. 

Endicott was the former site of Tri-Cities College of Syracuse University, which later became '''Harpur College''' and then Binghamton University. The location of Binghamton University is in the Town of Vestal on Union's south border. 

 Geography 
The village is on the north side of the Susquehanna River and the Southern Tier Expressway. 

Endicott is located at four two  six ' one one  North, seven six  three ' one seven  West ( four two . one zero three zero seven four ,  seven six . zero five four six eight seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of eight . one km ( three . one mi ).  eight . one km ( three . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one three , zero three eight people, five , nine nine six households, and three , zero one five families residing in the village. The population density is one , six zero three . two km ( four , one five six . one mi ). There are six , six eight six housing units at an average density of eight two two . one km ( two , one three one . three mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine one . six five % White, three . seven five % African American, zero . two five % Native American, one . nine six % Asian, zero . zero seven % Pacific Islander, zero . six seven % from other races, and one . six six % from two or more races.  one . six seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are five , nine nine six households out of which two four . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three two . four % are married couples living together, one three . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and four nine . seven % are non-families. four one . six % of all households are made up of individuals and one four . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . zero nine and the average family size is two . eight eight .

In the village the population is spread out with two one . eight % under the age of one eight , nine . five % from one eight to two four , three zero . six % from two five to four four , one nine . three % from four five to six four , and one eight . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are eight nine . three males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight six . four males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ two six , zero three two , and the median income for a family is $ three five , eight five eight . Males have a median income of $ two seven , seven eight zero versus $ two one , three two zero for females. The per capita income for the village is $ one seven , two seven four .  one eight . seven % of the population and one five . four % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two six . zero % of those under the age of one eight and one zero . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. 

 Additional facts about Endicott, New York 
Endicott is known as the birthplace of computers, because the company that became IBM was established there in one nine zero six . Endicott also was the former home of the Endicott Johnson Corporation. Until two zero zero six , the PGA TOUR's B.C. Open was played each July at En-Joie Golf Course on the west side of the village. The stop was dropped from the tour in January two zero zero six . Endicott also is the birthplace of baseball's four-time All-Star, Johnny Logan.
Endicott, along with the surrounding cities, is known as the Carousel capital of the world. This is because George F. Johnson wanted carousels to be free of admission, so he built six of them around the area, and all of them are free of charge.

 '''Port Dickinson''' is a village located in Broome County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , six nine seven . 

The '''Village of Port Dickinson''' lies within the Town of Dickinson.

 History 
The Village of Port Dickinson was incorporated in one eight seven six . The village was a port on the now-defunct Chenango Canal. It is now a suburb of Binghamton, New York. 

 Geography 
Port Dickinson is located at four two  eight ' one four  North, seven five  five three ' four zero  West ( four two . one three seven one seven five , - seven five . eight nine four three two one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one . eight km ( zero . seven mi ).  one . six km ( zero . six mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is seven . three five % water.

The Town of Fenton borders Port Dickinson on the North, while the City of Binghamton borders it on the South. It is bordered on the West by the Chenango River, and on the East by the Town of Kirkwood.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , six nine seven people, seven three four households, and four three eight families residing in the village. The population density is one , zero four zero . zero km ( two , six eight seven . zero mi ). There are seven nine nine housing units at an average density of four eight nine . seven km ( one , two six five . one mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine six . seven zero % White, one . two four % African American, zero . one two % Native American, zero . three five % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . four one % from other races, and one . one eight % from two or more races.  zero . five three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are seven three four households out of which three two . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four two . eight % are married couples living together, one four . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and four zero . two % are non-families. three four . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three one and the average family size is three . zero zero .

In the village the population is spread out with two six . five % under the age of one eight , seven . three % from one eight to two four , two seven . nine % from two five to four four , two two . three % from four five to six four , and one six . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are eight six . nine males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are seven six . nine males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ three eight , three nine three , and the median income for a family is $ four four , seven seven nine . Males have a median income of $ three five , eight seven zero versus $ two five , seven two six for females. The per capita income for the village is $ one nine , six six seven .  five . seven % of the population and three . four % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, five . eight % of those under the age of one eight and six . two % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Flooding
Several major floods have occurred in the area. An earth levee along the Chenango River and Phelps Creek and the channel excavation of Phelps Creek in one nine four three by the US Army Corps of Engineers helped reduce the devastation that was brought on by earlier floods of the Susquehanna River basin. These floods included ones in one eight one zero , one eight six five , one eight eight nine , one eight nine four , one nine three five , and one nine three six . In one nine four nine , the US Army Corps of Engineers excavated a one , three zero zero foot pilot channel and removed foundation pilings along the Chenango River. Minor floods have occurred since then about once every one zero years, although the average length between floods is two zero years for the Chenango River in general.

Recreation
There are a few recreational facilities in the Village. The Jeanne and John D. Wilfley Community Park is a reclaimed flood plain adjacent to the Chenango River. It was named, at first, the Port Dickinson Community Park. However, in two zero zero zero , with the news of Mayor Wilfley retiring, the Village renamed the park to remember him in our everyday lives. The Park is accessible from Chenango Street, which is above the filled-in Chenango Canal. I- eight eight passes over the park. There is a . seven five -mile walking trail along the perimeter of the park. The Park also has an extension at the intersection of Chenango Street and Beacon Ave. The King Ave park is not officially recognized, as is the same with Wayne Ave Field, by the Village, but the residents of the Village treat them with the same due respect as is necessary for all parks. The Jeanne and John D. Wilfley Community Park has . seven five miles of walking trails, a pavilion with picnic tables and several charcoal grills, two tennis courts, a basketball court, two squash courts, two baseball fields, a soccer field and restroom facilities. The Beacon Ave extension features several picnic tables. The Wayne Ave park has a baseball field. The King Ave park features the Port Dickinson Community Association's headquarters, restroom facilities, two baseball fields, and a softball field.

'''Vestal''' is a town located in Broome County, New York between the Susquehanna River and the Pennsylvania border in the Southern Tier of New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two six , five three five , estimated to have grown to two seven , zero five five by two zero zero four .

The '''Town of Vestal''' is on the south border of the county and is south and southwest of Binghamton, New York. New York Route one seven passes across the north part of the town. 

 History 
The first settlement occurred around one seven eight five . 
The Town of Vestal was formed from the Town of Union in one eight two three .  

In the one nine nine zero s, Vestal became the major retail center of the area, with many large shopping centers such as the Town Square Mall, Parkway Plaza, Shoppes at Vestal, Campus Plaza, and Vestal Park (mixed residentialcommerceretail) along the Vestal Parkway (also known as NY Route four three four ), one of the busiest roads in the area.  Transportation 
Retail along the Vestal Parkway
Vestal is linked from the west primarily by New York State Highway one seven , which is under development to become Interstate eight six . It is also very close to Interstate eight one and Interstate eight eight . Two major bridges and one minor bridge of New York State Highway two six , New York State Highway two zero one , and Bridge Road link Vestal to the villages of Endicott and Johnson City. New York State Highway four three four , The Vestal Parkway is the main artery through Vestal. It provides a direct link to Binghamton in the east.

Broome County Transit provides Vestal with bus service around the town and to surrounding municipalities. Greater Binghamton Airport is located about seven miles away in Maine, New York and provides direct connections to Cincinnati-Northern Kentucky International Airport, Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport, Philadelphia International Airport, Pittsburgh International Airport, and Washington Dulles International Airport.

 '''South Valley''' is a town located in Cattaraugus County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of three zero two . The name is from the town's geographical attributes. 

The '''Town of South Valley''' is in the southwest corner of the county. 

 History 
The town was first settled in one seven nine eight by Quaker missionaries, who attempted to teach the local indians agriculture and civilization.  The Quakers started a school in one eight zero three and erected a sawmill in one eight one two , but the mill caused dissention in the tribe and was pulled down. In one eight three eight the Quakers helped the Indians from losing their property to a land company. The Town of South Valley was formed in one eight four seven from the south part of the Town of Randolph.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of nine six . one km ( three seven . one mi ).  nine five . six km ( three six . nine mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . four six % water. 

The south town line is the border of Pennsylvania and the west town line is the border of Chautauqua County, New York. 

The Allegheny River forms a reservoir in the town. 

 Adjacent towns and areas 
The south town line is the border of Warren County, Pennsylvania, and the west town line is the border of the Town of Carroll in Chautauqua County, New York. To the east is Allegany Reservation and the Town of Cold Spring. North of South Valley is the Town of Randolph.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are three zero two people, one two six households, and eight nine families residing in the town.  '''Auburn''' is a city located in Cayuga County, New York, United States of America. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a population of two eight , five seven four . It is the county seat of Cayuga County and home to the Auburn Doubledays minor league baseball team.

 History 
The city of Auburn was founded in one seven nine three . 

In one eight one six , Auburn Prison (now Auburn state correctional facility) was founded as a model for the contemporary ideas about treating prisoners, known now as the Auburn System.  Visitors were charged a fee for viewing the facility and its inmates. On August six , one eight nine zero , the first execution by the electric chair was carried out at Auburn Prison. Although the ideas of the Auburn System have been abandoned, the prison continues to serve as a maximum security facility.
 Famous residents 
Auburn was the home of William Seward, who as U.S. Secretary of State arranged the purchase of Alaska (known at the time as Seward's Folly ). Auburn was also the birthplace of Birdsill Holly, supposed inventor of the fire hydrant. Auburn also was the home of Theodore Case, who developed the first commercially successful system of recording sound on film. 

Harriet Tubman, an African American freedom-fighter and escaped slave, who brought many people to the North to escape slavery, formed a friendship with William Seward and spent the last years of her life in Auburn. She and Seward (including much of his family) are buried in Fort Hill Cemetery. Martha Coffin Wright, an early feminist and participant in the Seneca Falls convention was also an Auburn resident.

Auburn is the home of Manowar, a heavy metal band.

 Geography 
Auburn is located at four two  five five ' five four  North, seven six  three three ' five three  West ( four two . nine three one six six zero , - seven six . five six four seven seven zero ). The city is located north of Owasco Lake, one of the Finger Lakes. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two one . eight km ( eight . four mi ).  two one . seven km ( eight . four mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . four seven % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two eight , five seven four people, one one , four one one households, and six , five three eight families residing in the city. The population density is one , three one five . zero km ( three , four zero five . three mi ). There are one two , six three seven housing units at an average density of five eight one . five km ( one , five zero six . zero mi ). The racial makeup of the city is eight eight . five seven % White, seven . five nine % African American, zero . two nine % Native American, zero . five seven % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, one . four one % from other races, and one . five five % from two or more races.  two . eight two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one one , four one one households out of which two eight . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three seven . three % are married couples living together, one four . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and four two . seven % are non-families. three six . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two seven and the average family size is two . nine eight .

In the city the population is spread out with two two . eight % under the age of one eight , nine . three % from one eight to two four , three zero . three % from two five to four four , one nine . eight % from four five to six four , and one seven . eight % who are six five years of age or older.  ''Another Aurora is a town in Erie County, New York.'' 

'''Aurora''' is a village located in Cayuga County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of seven two zero . 

Prior to American settlement, a major Cayuga village, Chonodote, stood very near to the present-day site of Aurora village. Chonodote was destroyed by the Sullivan Expedition in one seven seven nine .

The '''Village of Aurora''' is in the Town of Ledyard on the shore of Cayuga Lake. An institution of higher education for women founded in one eight six eight , Wells College, is in this village. The college became coeducational in two zero zero five , amid strong protest from alumnae and students. 

The village is currently in the middle of a controversy related to the destruction of buildings within its National Register Historic District and control of the village's commercial center by developer Pleasant Rowland.

The village struggles to retain its autonomy as Rowland, a Wells alumna and the billionaire creator of the American Girl Doll Company, attempts to change Aurora into her ideal of a picture perfect village.

Aurora was home to Henry Wells, founder of Wells-Fargo and the American Express Company, as well as Congressman Edwin B. Morgan, a founder of the New York Times. 

 Geography

 '''Fair Haven''' is a village located in Cayuga County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of eight eight four . 

The '''Village of Fairhaven''' is in the Town of Sterling. It is also a harbor on Lake Ontario. Route one zero four A passes through the village. Fair Haven State Park is located northeast of the village. 

 Geography 
Fair Haven is located at the south end of '''Little Sodus Bay'''. 

Fair Haven is located at four three  one nine ' two seven  North, seven six  four two ' one nine  West ( four three . three two four one seven five , - seven six . seven zero five one five four ).

Fair Haven is quite the recreational fishing neighborhood. Plenty of opportunities to try fishing. When the Fair Haven Bay freezes there are huts and rental huts available for ice fishing. When you're not wanting to fish, the Fair Haven Beach State Park is open year round. The park has tenting sites wo electric hook-up and sites w electric. The beach is open during the summer supervised by trained waterfront lifeguards. And the pier is a great place to take walk. It has been measured to be a quarter of a mile all the way out.
If you really get tired of the water and the outdoors, drive about one zero miles north on Route one zero four A and follow the signs to the Sterling Renaissance Festival. Great place to find out what different eras were like and what culture was like back in the day!

On Sunday Morning, the church to attend is the little white church across the street from the State Park called Calvary Baptist Church. The services held are Sunday School at one zero am and the morning Worship service at one one am. Also other services are: Sunday Evening at six pm and Wednesday night fellowship and prayer meeting at seven pm.  :''For other uses of the term One Nation, see One Nation (disambiguation)''

'''One Nation,''' '''One Nation Conservatism,''' or '''Tory Democracy''' is a term used in political debate in the United Kingdom and sometimes Canada to refer to the moderate wing of the Conservative Party, and the Red Tory wing of the original Progressive Conservative Party in Canada who describe themselves as One Nation Conservatives. 

The term is used to denote a nation characterised by social solidarity and harmony between classes, rather than a nation polarised into two nations along class lines. Harold Macmillan, British prime minister from one nine five seven to one nine six three , and his rival Rab Butler, who served successively in several important posts without ever becoming prime minister, are usually seen as leading modern exponents of One Nation Conservatism. John Diefenbaker, Prime Minister of Canada from one nine five seven to one nine six three , is generally seen as a representative of the Canadian strain, via his New Vision Speech of one nine five eight , although in Canada, the two nations referred to the English- and French-speaking peoples. 

The term derives indirectly from one of Benjamin Disraeli's political novels, ''Sybil, or the Two Nations'', in which he described Britain as Two nations between whom there is no intercourse and no sympathy; who are as ignorant of each other's habits, thoughts, and feelings, as if they were dwellers in different zones, or inhabitants of different planets: the rich and the poor. 

Lord Randolph Churchill would also use the term Tory Democracy in this Disraelian sense in the late-Victorian era.

In his two zero zero zero Macmillan Lecture, the Conservative front-bencher Damian Green MP asked Who Needs One Nation Conservatism? He answered: My answer to the question posed tonight, 'Who needs One Nation Conservatism?' is first the Conservative Party, and secondly the British people. The current public debate on this topic is most peculiar. Many of those who for years have led the forces of One Nation Conservatism are now excoriated as dinosaurs by certain commentators. At the same time the One Nation label has never been so much in demand. Tony Blair wastes no opportunity to try on, at least in his rhetoric, this comfortable old Tory garment. Rather more convincing is the Conservative Party's former leader William Hague, who on two six January two zero zero one said, 'The Conservative Party I feel at home in is the party of One Nation reflecting the whole nation'. 
 
As this quotation illustrates, many Conservatives have tried since the party went into opposition in one nine nine seven to reclaim the One Nation ideal for their party, but (like William Hague) have found their way blocked by Tony Blair and his New Labour agenda espousing the Third Way in British politics.

One Nation Conservatives were referred to as wets by former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher. One Nation Conservatives were often the most vociferous opponents of Thatcherism within the British Conservative Party. In Canada, One Nation Conservatives and the Red Tories were the most active and vocal opponents of the merger between the Progressive Conservative Party and the Canadian Alliance party which they viewed as a disavowal of the Conservative - or Tory - tradition in Canada.

The '''Battle of Ltzen''' was the first major engagement of the War of the Sixth Coalition of the Napoleonic Wars. Following the disaster of Napoleon's invasion of Russia in one eight one two , a new Coalition formed against Napoleon I of France. In response to this, he hastily assembled an army of just over two zero zero , zero zero zero comprised largely of inexperienced, barely trained recruits and severely short of horses (A consequence of the Russian fiasco, where most of his veteran troops and horses had perished). He crossed the Rhine into Germany to link up with remnants of his old Grande Arme, and quickly defeat this new alliance before it became too strong.
On May two , one eight one three , the Russian commander, Prince Peter Wittgenstein, attacked Napoleon's advanced column near Ltzen, Germany, in an attempt to undo Napoleon's capture of Leipzig. After a day of heavy fighting, the combined Prussian and Russian force retreated, but without cavalry the French were unable to follow their defeated enemy.

Prelude 
On April three zero Napoleon crossed the river Saale, advancing on Leipzig in three columns led by an advanced guard. His intention was to work his way into the Coalition's interior lines, dividing their forces and defeating them in detail before they could combine. But due to inexperienced cavalrymen and faulty reconnaissance, he was unaware of seven three , zero zero zero allied troops under Wittgenstein and Graf (Count) von Blcher concentrating on his right flank to the south. Marshal Ney's corps was surprised and attacked on the road from Ltzen to Leipzig.

 The Battle 
Napoleon was visiting the one six three two battlefield, playing tour guide with his staff by pointing to the sites and describing the events of one six three two , in detail from memory, when he heard the sound of cannons. He immediately cut the tour short and rode off toward the direction of the artillery fire. Arriving on the scene, he quickly sized up the situation and decided to set a trap using Ney's corps as bait. He ordered the Marshal to make a fighting withdrawal toward Ltzen, meanwhile he would send Ney reinforcements which would take up strong, defensive positions in and around two villages south of the city. Once these divisions were ready, the rest of the corps would withdraw towards them, luring the allies to attack, while Napoleon, leading the main one one zero , zero zero zero strong French force, would come around the allied flank and counter attack.

Wittgenstein and Blcher took the bait, continuing to press Ney until they ran into the hook Napoleon had prepared. Once their advance had halted, with the perfect timing of old, he struck. While he had been reinforcing Ney, he had also concentrated a great mass of artillery (''Grande Batterie'') opposite Wittgenstein's center. With a thunderous roar they unleashed a withering barrage. Then Napoleon himself, along with his Imperial Guard, led the massive counter assault into the allied flank. Wittgenstein and Blcher were in danger of suffering another defeat on the scale of Austerlitz, but the green and exausted French troops, who had been marching and fighting all day long, could not follow through. In addition, darkness was closing in as night approached. This allowed the allied force to retreat in good order. The lack of French cavalry meant there would be no pursuit. Both sides lost around two zero , zero zero zero men, with some debate about which side lost slightly more. But casualties aside, by nightfall Wittgenstein and Blcher were in retreat while Napoleon controlled Ltzen and the field.

 Aftermath 
The Coalition had been very fortunate. Had the battle started earlier that day when Napoleon had fresher troops and more time, Ltzen could well have become a second Austerlitz. But what was almost a decisive defeat turned into only a marginal, tactical one. Wittgenstein and Blcher withdrew towards Dresden. Ltzen had shown the allies Napoleon was still very dangerous. They decided on a new strategy of avoiding direct battle with him while seeking out and attacking his subordinates instead, thus weakening his army. Meantime they would assemble an overwhelming force against which The Emperor, for all his abilities, could not stand (See the Trachenburg Plan ). 

Also during the battle of Ltzen, Gerhard von Scharnhorst, one of the brightest and most able Prussian generals, serving as Wittgenstein's Chief of Staff, was wounded. Although the wound was minor, due to the hasty retreat it could not be tended to soon enough. Infection set in and he died as a result. A tragic but all too common occurrence in warfare of the period.

 ''For other uses of Chautauqua, see Chautauqua.''
----
'''Chautauqua''' is a town located in Chautauqua County, New York, USA . As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of four , six six six . The town is named after a lake and means Place where fish are taken. 

The '''Town of Chautauqua''' is in the northwest part of the county. It is northwest of Jamestown, New York. 

 History 
The Town of Chautauqua was formed in one eight zero three from the Town of Batavia, while still part of Genesee County. The first settler arrived the same year near the current Village of Mayville. This town is the mother of towns in Chautauqua County because many later towns were set up from its territory. 

 Geography

 '''Fredonia''' is a village located in Chautauqua County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one zero , seven zero six . 

The '''Village of Fredonia''' is in the Town of Pomfret, New York south of Lake Erie. The village borders the City of Dunkirk and is the home of the State University of New York Fredonia. 

 History 
The community was first settled around one eight zero four .

In one eight two one William Hart dug the first successful gas well in what is now the Village of Fredonia. It supplied enough natural gas for lights in two stores, two shops and a grist mill by one eight two five . Expanding on Hart's work, the Fredonia Gas Light Company was eventually formed in one eight five eight , becoming the first American natural gas company.
 
The Village of Fredonia was incorporated in one eight two nine . SUNY Fredonia originally opened as Fredonia Academy in one eight two six . That building is now the village hall. The original name for the area was Canadaway (from the Indian word ''Ganadawao'', meaning ''Among the hemlocks''). 

In the mid one nine th century Fredonia became the home of the first dues-paying Grange of the Grange movement. The United States' first Grange Hall was erected in Fredonia during the late one eight six zero s (the Fredonia Grange was established on April one six , one eight six eight ), and the original building (Grange Hall one ) still stands on Main Street. Fredonia was also host to the first meeting of the Women's Christian Temperance Union, which was held at the Fredonia Baptist Church in one eight seven three .

:Fredonia, Wisconsin was named for Fredonia, New York.

 Geography 
Fredonia is located at four two  two six ' two seven  North, seven nine  two zero ' two  West ( four two . four four zero eight four five , - seven nine . three three three eight one three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one three . four km ( five . two mi ).  one three . four km ( five . two mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water, though it does have a small stream flowing northward through the village toward Lake Erie called Canadaway Creek.

 '''Frewsburg, New York''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in the Town of Carroll in Chautauqua County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the hamlet had a total population of one , nine six five . The postal code is one four seven three eight . 

Frewsburg is located on US Route six two , which forms the main street in the village. In spite of its small population, Frewsburg is a signicant community in the area, dwarfed only by the City of Jamestown several miles to the northwest. 

 Geography 
Frewsburg is located at four two  three ' two six  North, seven nine  nine ' three nine  West ( four two . zero five seven two two zero , - seven nine . one six zero eight nine eight ). 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the community has a total area of eight . seven km ( three . four mi ).  eight . seven km ( three . four mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. 

The '''Conewango Creek''' flows past the west side of the village. 

The community is on the west side of the town at the junction of several trunk roads, including Routes three four , three six , five three , and five five . 

 History 
Frewsburg is named after the Frews - Hugh and Mary Frew, who were supposedly the first European family to settle in this area in one eight zero seven . The location of their first house is commemorated by a historic marker on Main Street in Frewsburg. 

 Past residents of note 
Robert H. Jackson, United States Supreme Court Justice ( one nine four one - one nine five four ) and chief United States prosecutor at the Nuremberg Trials, was raised in Frewsburg. The community's elementary school is named in his honor. He later moved to Jamestown.

'''Jamestown''' is a city located in Chautauqua County, New York in the USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of three one , seven three zero . 

The '''City of Jamestown''' is within the Town of Ellicott and is at the southern tip of Chautauqua Lake. To the west of the city is an area (Census Enumeration District) known as Jamestown West.

 History 
The City of Jamestown was incorporated in one eight eight six . The city has been a center for manufacture of wood products such as furniture. The town was once the Furniture Capital of the World.  Although much of this industry has migrated away from the area in recent times, Jamestown still retains a few large factories for companies such as MRC, a bearings manufacturer, Cummins, makers of diesel engines, and Bush Industries, which produces ready-to-assemble office furniture.

 Geography 
Jamestown is located at four two  five ' four four  North, seven nine  one four ' one nine  West ( four two . zero nine five four five seven , - seven nine . two three eight six one nine ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two three . five km ( nine . one mi ).  two three . three km ( nine . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . eight eight % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are three one , seven three zero people, one three , five five eight households, and seven , nine zero four families residing in the city. The population density is one , three six four . three km ( three , five three four . six mi ). There are one five , zero two seven housing units at an average density of six four six . one km ( one , six seven three . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine one . five two % White, three . three nine % African American, zero . six four % Native American, zero . four four % Asian, zero . zero five % Pacific Islander, one . eight zero % from other races, and two . one six % from two or more races.  four . nine four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one three , five five eight households out of which two nine . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three nine . one % are married couples living together, one four . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and four one . seven % are non-families. three five . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two nine and the average family size is two . nine four .

In the city the population is spread out with two five . eight % under the age of one eight , nine . one % from one eight to two four , two eight . one % from two five to four four , two zero . nine % from four five to six four , and one six . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are nine one . zero males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight seven . three males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two five , eight three seven , and the median income for a family is $ three three , six seven five . Males have a median income of $ three zero , zero zero three versus $ two zero , zero three nine for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one five , three one six .  one nine . five % of the population and one five . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two nine . one % of those under the age of one eight and one zero . two % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. 

 Additional information about Jamestown 

The Chautauqua County-Jamestown Airport (JHW) is north of the city and provides scheduled and charter air service. 

Jamestown has one campus of Jamestown Community College. Jamestown Business College provides two-year degrees and certificates in the business field. 

This is the home city for the Jamestown Jammers baseball team.

Jamestown is also the hometown and birthplace of Television legend Lucille Ball.

Musician Natalie Merchant and the rock band one zero , zero zero zero Maniacs also call Jamestown home.

Naturalist, artist, educator, and photographer Roger Tory Peterson was also born in Jamestown and is remembered through the Roger Tory Peterson Institute of Natural History. 

The Fenton Museum of History is named after former resident Reuben Fenton, the twenty-fifth governor of New York.

The Red Raider Marching Band is also from Jamestown, and is one of the most traveled high school marching bands in the country, having been as far as Hawaii, and appearing on such shows as David Letterman's.

 '''Mayville''' is a village located in Chautauqua County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , seven five six . 

The '''Village of Mayville''' is in the Town of Chautauqua, and is the county seat of Chautauqua County. The Village and Town offices
share a building on Main Street, directly across from the Chautauqua County courthouse.

 History 
The first settlement in the county was at this location in one eight zero four , and 
the Village of Mayville was incorporated in one eight three zero . 
A noted incident in the community's early history came
in one eight three six when local residents rioted against the Holland Land Company and broke into its office, destroying furniture and papers. 

 Geography  
Mayville is located at four two  one five ' five  North, seven nine  three zero ' zero  West ( four two . two five one four zero two , - seven nine . five zero zero zero one five ).  

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of five . two km ( two . zero mi ).  five . two km ( two . zero mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. However, the village borders on
the north end of the picturesque Chautauqua Lake. Mayville is at the junction of Routes three nine four and four three zero ,
a few minutes' drive south of the New York State Throughway (Interstate nine zero ).

Mayville is the nearest village to the Chautauqua Institution, which draws thousands of
visitors during the summer months. Businesses in the village do a brisk tourist business both
with Chautauquans and with visitors to
cottages and resorts on the east and west sides of the lake.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , seven five six people, six eight six households, and three nine nine families residing in the village. Growing and shipping tobacco was a popular endeavor after one eight five eight .

 '''The Quarry Men''' (sometimes '''Quarrymen''') were a little-known skiffle group formed around Liverpool, England in March one nine five seven by John Lennon. They are most famous as the band that eventually evolved into The Beatles. 

History
When John Lennon decided that he wanted to play music, he first recruited his best friend, Pete Shotton to his embryonic group. Lennon was to be the singer and guitarist. Shotton was relegated to washboard, a common skiffle instrument. After just one week as the Black Jacks, they renamed themselves the Quarry Men, after a line in their school song at Quarry Bank Grammar School and a week later they recruited a friend from that school, Bill Smith to play tea chest bass, despite Shotton's protestations as he had recently been involved in a fight with Smith.

Smith was of a similar calibre to Shotton, and soon began to be sidelined when first Rod Davis (banjo) and Eric Griffiths (guitar) joined the band, as these two could play instruments reasonably well. He was eventually replaced by Len Garry and The Quarry Men performed at parties and skiffle contests around Liverpool, with the addition of Colin Hanton on drums. When Hanton joined the band he owned a drum set bought with his earnings as an apprentice upholsterer and then had the name The Quarry Men painted on the drum head.

With the recruitment of Len Garry as a more permanent bassist, the Quarrymen entered the ''Carroll Levis Discoveries Show'' talent contest on nine June one nine five seven but they failed to qualify for the preliminary audition.

Two weeks later (on two two June) the Quarry Men played twice at an outdoor party in Rosebery Street to celebrate the seven five zero th anniversary of the granting of Liverpool s charter by King John.

On six July one nine five seven the band played at St. Peter's Church garden f te. In the afternoon they played on a temporary stage in a field behind the church. After the set, Ivan Vaughan, an occasional tea chest bass player with the band, introduced Paul McCartney to John Lennon while the band was setting up in the church hall for the second set. McCartney showed the band how to tune a guitar and sang ''Twenty Flight Rock'' and ''Be-Bop-A-Lula'' to his own guitar accompaniment. The evening show started at eight pm and cost two shillings admission. Audience member Bob Molyneux recorded part of the evening performance on a Grundig portable reel-to-reel tape recorder. Two weeks later, meeting McCartney while cycling through Woolton, Pete Shotton, on behalf of John and the group, invited McCartney to join them.

Nigel Whalley, the ex-tea chest bass player who was currently managing the band, got the Quarry Men a booking at Lee Park Golf Club in Liverpool. Alan Sytner, owner of the Cavern club, was a member of the golf club. The band subsequently appeared several times in what were billed as Skiffle Sessions and in August one nine five seven , their name was first mentioned in the Cavern's advertisement in the Liverpool ''Echo'', by which time Pete Shotton had left the band, due to his lack of any real musical talent. Rod Davis followed a short time later as school commitments prevented him from contributing as fully as he would have liked.

McCartney made his debut with the band at The New Clubmoor Hall on Back Broadway on Friday, one eight October when he returned from his summer holidays. The band had been booked by local promoter Charlie McBain and they wore matching outfits with long-sleeved cowboy shirts, black string ties and black trousers. John and Paul wore white sports-coats. Paul played lead guitar but botched a solo, embarrassing himself and the group. To save face with John, during a break he played him I've Lost My Little Girl his recently-finished first song, which inspired John to also start writing. The other members of the band that night were Hanton on drums, Garry on tea-chest bass and Griffiths on guitar.

On Thursday, seven November, McBain booked The Quarry Men to appear at Wilson Hall, Garston. They also played Stanley Abattoir Social Club on one six November, New Clubmoor Hall on two three November and Wilson Hall on seven December.

The Quarry Men played The New Clubmoor Hall on one zero January one nine five eight and at The Cavern on two four January. Because John was losing interest in skiffle and playing more rock n roll, Rod Davis left the band in February one nine five eight . Paul McCartney's friend and school mate, George Harrison first saw them on six February at playing at Wilson Hall for Charlie McBain and he joined the band two weeks later. 

In March, Len Garry contracted tuberculosis (from which he later recovered) and was thus sidelined from the band. To fill the gap that his loss created, Eric Griffiths was invited to step down from his position of guitarist and take over the bass duties. He refused, and was sacked from the band.

Not long after this, John Charles Lowe, nicknamed Duff , joined the band, playing piano with them through the Summer of one nine five eight . On two three March the band performed at the opening night of Alan Caldwell s cellar club, The Morgue in Broadgreen.

In the summer of one nine five eight the band (comprising Lennon, McCartney, Harrison, Hanton and Lowe) recorded a seven eight rpm acetate demo of two songs at Percy Phillips s studio at five eight Kensington; the first was an original McCartneyHarrison tune called In Spite of All the Danger ; the other was a cover of Buddy Holly's That'll Be the Day .

Lowe left the band in the autumn of one nine five eight and the band continued to play regularly including the wedding reception of Harrison's brother Harry in Speke, on two zero December. After just two more performances (on one January at a Speke Bus Depot social club party at Wilson Hall organized by Harrison s father, and on two four January at a party at Woolton Village Club) Colin Hanton quit the band after a drunken argument. He was not replaced, and the band slowly disintegrated.

Lennon and McCartney continued to write songs together and Harrison joined The Les Stewart Quartet with Les Stewart and Ken Brown. When Mrs Mona Best opened the Casbah coffee club on two nine August one nine five nine , Ken Brown arranged for the quartet to be its resident band. When Brown missed rehearsals to help decorate The Casbah, Les Stewart refused to play with the band. Brown and Harrison recruited Lennon and McCartney at short notice to help them fill the residency, and the new band used the old name The Quarrymen . On one zero October there was an argument between the band and Mrs Best, and The Quarrymen walked out of The Casbah, ending their residency. 

The band next appeared as Johnny And The Moondogs at The Carroll Lewis Auditions at The Empire Theatre, Liverpool. By May one nine six zero , Lennon, McCartney and Harrison had been joined by Stuart Sutcliffe, and drummer Pete Best. They tried several other names, including the Silver Beetles, before shortening that to The Beatles for their performances in Hamburg in August one nine six zero .

 Recent history 
Len Garry, John Duff Lowe and Rod Davis reformed as a band for a short time in the one nine nine zero s and an album ''Open For Engagements'' was released in one nine nine four .

In one nine nine four , Bob Molyneux, then a retired policeman, rediscovered the recordings that he had made of the Quarry Men concert in one nine five seven . The scratchy recordings included covers of Lonnie Donegan's Puttin' On The Style and Elvis Presley's Baby, Let's Play House . On one five September one nine nine four Molyneux put his tape up for auction at Sotheby's. The tape sold to EMI for  seven eight , five zero zero , making it the most expensive recording ever sold at auction, but the recording quality was too poor to issue and the tape remains in the EMI archives.

In January one nine nine seven the Cavern Mecca invited all the bands who had played at the Cavern in the one nine five zero s to the unveiling of the Cavern Wall of Fame in Mathew Street to celebrate the club's four zero th birthday. All five of the surviving original Quarrymen and John Duff Lowe attended, and that evening they gave an impromptu performance on stage with Gary Gibson standing in for John Lennon, and Lawrence Gilmour for Paul McCartney.

That evening they were asked to help recreate the occasion of the Lennon - McCartney meeting at Woolton f te. Initially reluctant, the band were persuaded to help the Church Hall Restoration Fund, and the concert took place at the f te on six July one nine nine seven , exactly forty years after the original gig. The band toured the village in the f te procession, playing on the back of a lorry with their original one nine five seven driver. At the evening concert in the Church Hall the band played Putting On The Style which Bob Molyneux had recorded four zero years earlier. They also played the number that had persuaded Lennon to invite McCartney to join the band: Twenty Flight Rock . The set ended with Pete Shotton's first public solo performance: as a tribute to his friend John Lennon he sang Imagine .

On the back of this success ''The Original Quarrymen'' (Shotton, Griffiths, Davis, Garry and Hanton) recorded an album ''Get Back - Together'', which was released in September one nine nine seven and launched at the Beatlefans Convention at the Playhouse, Derby on Sunday, nine November one nine nine seven .

The band subsequently toured Europe, Canada, Cuba, the USA and Japan. Their album ''Songs We Remember'' was released in Japan in two zero zero three and released in the UK in January two zero zero five , by which time Pete Shotton had long since quit. With the death of Eric Griffiths in early two zero zero five , the band was forced to reassess itself, and eventually settled for recruiting John Duff Lowe to the pianist's seat and continuing the act in that form.

 '''Rouses Point''' is a village located in Clinton County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two , two seven seven . The village is named after Jacques Rouse, an early settler. 

The '''Village of Rouses Point''' is in northeast part of the Town of Champlain. The village is located on US Route two and US Route one one

Rouses Point is a port of entry from Canada and is close to the border with Quebec. The village is on the west shore of Lake Champlain. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , two seven seven people, nine seven eight households, and six zero four families residing in the village. The population density is four nine three . nine km ( one , two eight one . eight mi ). There are one , zero six two housing units at an average density of two three zero . four km ( five nine seven . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine seven . one nine % White, zero . seven zero % African American, zero . four zero % Native American, zero . four four % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander, zero . one eight % from other races, and one . zero five % from two or more races.  one . three six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are nine seven eight households out of which two eight . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four six . two % are married couples living together, one two . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three eight . two % are non-families. three three . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two six and the average family size is two . eight eight .

In the village the population is spread out with two three . eight % under the age of one eight , six . nine % from one eight to two four , two seven . six % from two five to four four , two five . eight % from four five to six four , and one five . eight % who are six five years of age or older. There is one elementary school in Rouses Point housing grades K- five . Students from grades six - one two attend Northeastern Clinton Central MiddleHigh School in the Town of Champlain.  '''Saranac''' is a town located in Clinton County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of four , one six five . The name is that of the river flowing past the town.

The town is west of the City of Plattsburgh and is within the Adirondack State Park.

Saranac was established from part of the Town of Plattsburgh in one eight two four .

The west town line is the border of Franklin County, New York. 

The Saranac River is the principal waterway in the town, flowing along the south border toward Lake Champlain. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are four , one six five people, one , five one nine households, and one , one three four families residing in the town. The population density is one three . nine km ( three six . zero mi ). There are one , six four two housing units at an average density of five . five km ( one four . two mi ). There are one , five one nine households out of which three nine . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six one . one % are married couples living together, nine . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two five . three % are non-families. one nine . four % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  '''Austerlitz''' is a town located in Columbia County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , four five three . The town is named after a Napoleonic battle. 

The '''Town of Austerlitz''' is in the east part of Columbia County. 

 History 
The first settlers arrived around one seven four five . The town was formed in one eight one eight from parts of the Towns of Canaan, Chatham, and Hillsdale. 
The town was named Austerlitz by Martin Van Buren; the original intention was to name it Waterloo, but Van Buren insisted on using a Napoleonic victory rather than a defeat.

 Past residents of note 
Edna St. Vincent Millay, poet, lived at Steepletop farm. The farm is now occupied by a writer's colony.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one two six . five km ( four eight . eight mi ).  one two six . two km ( four eight . seven mi ) of it is land and zero . three km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two zero % water. 

The east town line is the border of Massachusetts. 

The Taconic State Parkway crosses the northwest corner of the town. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one , four five three people, six two zero households, and four two seven families residing in the town. The population density is one one . five km ( two nine . eight mi ). There are nine zero six housing units at an average density of seven . two km ( one eight . six mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine seven . four five % White, zero . eight three % African American, zero . zero seven % Native American, zero . five five % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . seven six % from other races, and zero . three four % from two or more races.  zero . eight three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six two zero households out of which two five . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five nine . zero % are married couples living together, six . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three one . one % are non-families. two four . two % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three four and the average family size is two . eight one .

In the town the population is spread out with two zero . four % under the age of one eight , four . four % from one eight to two four , two three . seven % from two five to four four , three four . zero % from four five to six four , and one seven . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four six years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero four . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero one . two males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ five one , three six nine , and the median income for a family is $ five six , seven seven one . Males have a median income of $ four four , five three one versus $ three seven , one eight eight for females. The per capita income for the town is $ three eight , zero five four .  five . six % of the population and four . seven % of families are below the poverty line.  '''Claverack''' is a town located in Columbia County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of six , four zero one . The town name is a corruption for the Dutch word for Clover fields. 

The '''Town of Claverack''' is centrally located in the county, east of the City of Hudson. 

 History 
The town was formed in one seven seven eight from the older District of Claverack.  In one seven eight two , the town lost some of its land to the new Town of Hillsdale. The town was reduced again in one seven eight five to form the City of Hudson. 

 Past residents of note 
Aaron Burr and Alexander Hamilton tried cases in the local courthouse. 
Martin Van Buren was admitted to the bar here. 
Margaret Sanger attended the former Claverack College (closed one nine zero two ) for two years. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one two four . two km ( four eight . zero mi ).  one two three . four km ( four seven . seven mi ) of it is land and zero . eight km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . six three % water. 

The Taconic State Parkway passes through the town. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are six , four zero one people, two , four eight five households, and one , six six nine families residing in the town. The population density is five one . nine km ( one three four . three mi ). There are two , eight three nine housing units at an average density of two three . zero km ( five nine . six mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine three . nine five % White, three . three one % African American, zero . two zero % Native American, zero . three six % Asian, zero . zero six % Pacific Islander, zero . seven eight % from other races, and one . three three % from two or more races.  two . four seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , four eight five households out of which two nine . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five three . four % are married couples living together, nine . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and three two . eight % are non-families. two six . four % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four four and the average family size is two . nine six .

In the town the population is spread out with two four . four % under the age of one eight , six . five % from one eight to two four , two five . three % from two five to four four , two four . six % from four five to six four , and one nine . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four one years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero zero . eight males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine four . seven males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ four one , six four seven , and the median income for a family is $ five zero , one seven five . Males have a median income of $ three two , eight nine six versus $ two three , nine two five for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one nine , eight four eight .  six . seven % of the population and three . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, six . eight % of those under the age of one eight and seven . one % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 '''Clermont''' is a town located in Columbia County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , seven two six . The name of the town is French for Clear Mountain, referring to the mountain views in the town. 

The '''Town of Clermont''' is in the southwest part of the county, south of the City of Hudson. 

History
Built in one seven three zero , Clermont is the oldest of the great estates of the mid-Hudson valley; it was home to seven generations of the Livingston family until one nine six two . 

The Clermont Manor was established by in one seven two eight in what is now the Town of Clermont. The manor was originally part of the one six zero , zero zero zero acre ( six five zero km ) Livingston Manor; Clermont was a one three , zero zero zero acre ( five three km ) section in the southwest corner that was bequeathed to Robert Livingston ( one six eight eight - one seven seven five ), a younger son. His descendants would come to own more than five zero zero , zero zero zero acres ( two , zero zero zero km ) in the Catskill Mountains and more than one zero zero , zero zero zero acres ( four zero zero km ) in Dutchess County. 

Clermont marked the northernmost penetration by British troops up the Hudson River during the American Revolution; Livingstons home was burned because of his prominent role in the Revolution. It was rebuilt between one seven seven nine and one seven eight two . The house is now a five zero zero acre ( two km ) historic New York State Historic Site and a United States National Historic Landmark. 

In one seven eight eight , Clermont Manor was organized as the Town of Clermont. 

Clermont was the port of registry of Robert Fulton's first steamboat, co-owned by Livingston, which was called the North River . Today it is known as the Clermont.  The ruins of its dock can still be found at the historic site. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of four nine . seven km ( one nine . two mi ).  four six . six km ( one eight . zero mi ) of it is land and three . one km ( one . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is six . three zero % water. 

The south town line is the border of Dutchess County, and the west town line, marked by the Hudson River, is the border of Ulster County.

 Demographics

 The '''City of Hudson''', the first chartered city of the entire United States, is located along the west border of Columbia County and the east bank of the Hudson River in Columbia County, New York, USA. 

As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of seven , five two four . It is the county seat of Columbia County. The city is named after the adjacent river and ultimately after the explorer Henry Hudson. 

 History 
The land was purchased from the natives by Dutch settlers in one six six two and was originally part of the Town of Claverack. Settled by New England whalers and merchants hailing primarily from Nantucket, Martha's Vineyard, and Providence, Rhode Island, Hudson was chartered as a city in one seven eight five . The self-described Proprietors laid out a city grid, and Hudson grew rapidly as an active port, and came within one vote of being named the capital of New York State. Hudson obtained a new charter in one eight nine five . 

Hudson became notorious as a center of gambling and prostitution in the late one nine th and first half of the two zero th century, as described in some detail in Bruce Edward Hall's book, Diamond Street. These rackets were broken up in one nine five one after surprise raids of Hudson whorehouses by then-Attorney General Thomas Dewey netted, among other catches, several local policemen.

With hundreds of properties on the State and National Registers of historic places, Hudson is a catalogue of American vernacular architecture. After a steep decline in the six zero s and seven zero s, the City has undergone a significant revival, and is now known for its active arts scene, antiques shoppers, restaurants, and nightlife.

Between one nine nine eight and two zero zero five , the City was also the center of a fiercely-contested land use battle between private citizens and a subsidiary of what was then the largest cement company on earth, Holderbank (since renamed Holcim). The company proposed a massive, coal-fired cement manufacturing project sprawling over one , eight zero zero acres in the City of Hudson and Town of Greenport, New York, which eventually was blocked through citizen opposition led by local activists Peter Jung and Sam Pratt. Some three dozen organizations joined in the opposition.

 Geography 
Hudson is located at four two  one five ' four  North, seven three  four seven ' six  West ( four two . two five one two three zero , - seven three . seven eight five zero six six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of six . zero km ( two . three mi ).  five . six km ( two . two mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is six . four seven % water. 

Hudson is located on what began as a spit of land jutting into the Hudson River between the South Bay and North Bay, now both largely filled and degraded (but not without hope of restoration).

Across the Hudson River lies the Town of Athens and Greene County, New York; a ferry connected the two municipalities during much of the one nine th century. Between them lies Middle Ground Flats, a former sandbar that grew due to both natural silting and also from dumping the spoils of dredging; today it is inhabited by deer and a few occupants of quasi-legal summer shanties.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are seven , five two four people, two , nine five one households, and one , five nine zero families residing in the city. The population density is one , three three eight . seven km ( three , four six eight . two mi ). There are three , three four seven housing units at an average density of five nine five . five km ( one , five four two . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the city is six four . two nine % White, two four . zero two % African American, zero . two eight % Native American, two . eight four % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, four . one five % from other races, and four . four one % from two or more races.  eight . four one % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , nine five one households out of which two eight . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, two nine . four % are married couples living together, one nine . six % have a female householder with no husband present, and four six . one % are non-families. three nine . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two six and the average family size is three . zero zero .

In the city the population is spread out with two three . seven % under the age of one eight , nine . four % from one eight to two four , three zero . zero % from two five to four four , two one . zero % from four five to six four , and one six . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero six . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero five . six males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two four , two seven nine , and the median income for a family is $ two seven , five nine four . The '''Town of Livingston''' is in the southwest part of Columbia County. US Route nine passes through the town. 

 History 
The land grant for Livingston Manor was made in one six eight six to Robert Livingston. The region was made a district in one seven seven two and the Town of Livingston was founded in one seven eight eight , being one of the original towns of the county. 

In one seven one zero , the area was used to settle Palatine Germans. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one zero zero . nine km ( three nine . zero mi ).  nine nine . zero km ( three eight . two mi ) of it is land and one . nine km ( zero . seven mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . eight five % water. 

The west town line, at the Hudson River is the border of Greene County, New York. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are three , four two four people, one , three three two households, and eight eight nine families residing in the town. The population density is three four . six km ( eight nine . six mi ). There are one , six five one housing units at an average density of one six . seven km ( four three . two mi ). There are one , three three two households out of which two seven . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five four . three % are married couples living together, eight . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and three three . two % are non-families. two six . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four one and the average family size is two . nine five .

In the town the population is spread out with two one . five % under the age of one eight , six . zero % from one eight to two four , two six . one % from two five to four four , two five . three % from four five to six four , and two one . one % who are six five years of age or older.  '''New Lebanon''' is a town located in Columbia County, New York, USA, two four miles ( three nine km) southeast of Albany. In one nine one zero , one , three seven eight people lived in New Lebanon, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , four five four . 

The '''Town of New Lebanon''' is in the northwest part of Columbia County. US Route two zero crosses the town. 

 History 
New Lebanon was formed from the Town of Canaan in one eight one eight . 

New Lebanon was home to an early settlement of Shakers. Some of the surviving buildings are home to the Darrow School. Others have been converted into a Sufi retreat center called the '''Abode of the Message'''. The latter is the residence of Pir Vilayat Inayat Khan. 

 Past residents of note 
Samuel Jones Tilden, New York politician and vice-presidential candidate. 
George H. Williams, attorney and judge. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of nine three . two km ( three six . zero mi ).  nine three . zero km ( three five . nine mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two two % water. 

The north town line is the border of Rensselaer County, New York, and the east town line is the border of Berkshire County, Massachusetts. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two , four five four people, nine eight three households, and six five one families residing in the town. The population density is two six . four km ( six eight . four mi ). There are one , two zero one housing units at an average density of one two . nine km ( three three . five mi ).  '''Cortland''' is a city in Cortland County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a population of one eight , seven four zero . It is the county seat of Cortland County. 

The '''City of Cortland''' is surrounded by the Town of Cortlandville. Interstate eight one and US Route one one pass through the city. 

The State University of New York at Cortland is on the west side of the city. 

 History 
The City of Cortland, settled in one seven nine one , was made a village in one eight five three , and was incorporated in one nine zero zero as the four one st city in the State of New York. When the county was formed in one eight zero eight , Cortland vied with other villages for the status of becoming the county seat. The City of Cortland is the county seat of Cortland County. Cortland contains the campus of SUNY Cortland (formerly a teachers' Normal College) within its limits. 

Known as the Crown City because of its location on a plain formed by the convergence of seven valleys, Cortland is situated about one , one three zero feet ( three four four m) above sea level, making it the uppermost city to crown the state. 
 four zero stars, representing the four zero cities incorporated before Cortland, circle the State of New York and Crown on the Official City Seal. The seven points of the Crown create seven valleys depicting Cortland's seven surrounding valleys. The four one st star in the center of the Crown illustrates Cortland as the closest incorporated City to the geographic center of New York.

 Geography 
The Tioughnioga River flows past the city, and Interstate highway eight one passes through the northeast side of the community. 

Cortland is located at four two  three six ' two  North, seven six  one zero ' five three  West ( four two . six zero zero six five eight , - seven six . one eight one two eight four ). Cortland lies between Syracuse, New York and Binghamton, New York. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one zero . two km ( three . nine mi ).  one zero . two km ( three . nine mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . five one % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one eight , seven four zero people, six , nine two two households, and three , four five four families residing in the city. The population density is one , eight four five . eight km ( four , seven seven eight . six mi ). There are seven , five five zero housing units at an average density of seven four three . six km ( one , nine two five . two mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine five . seven two % White, one . five six % African American, zero . two five % Native American, zero . five seven % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . five six % from other races, and one . three three % from two or more races.  one . seven two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six , nine two two households out of which two four . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three four . seven % are married couples living together, one one . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and five zero . one % are non-families. three six . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two eight and the average family size is two . nine five .

In the city the population is spread out with one eight . three % under the age of one eight , two eight . four % from one eight to two four , two three . six % from two five to four four , one six . eight % from four five to six four , and one two . nine % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is two eight years. For every one zero zero females there are eight eight . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight four . five males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two six , four seven eight , and the median income for a family is $ three nine , one six seven . Males have a median income of $ two nine , eight five seven versus $ two one , six one four for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one four , two six seven .  two four . seven % of the population and one three . nine % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two four . eight % of those under the age of one eight and one five . two % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Trivia 

Famed heavy metal vocalist Ronnie James Dio (born Ronald Padavona), who sang with (among others) Rainbow and Black Sabbath and now fronts his own band, grew up in Cortland, though he was born in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. A street in Cortland is named for him.

 '''Maracas''' are simple percussion instruments (idiophones), usually played in pairs, consisting of a dried gourd shell (cuia - 'kOO-ya') filled with seeds or dried beans. They may also be made of leather, wood, or plastic. Often one maraca is pitched high and the other low.

The instrument is of prehistoric American origin. The word ''maraca'' is thought to have come from the Tupi language of Brazil, where it is pronounced 'ma-ra-KAH'.

Maracas are heard in many forms of Latin American music and are also used in pop and classical music. They are considered characteristic of the music of Colombia, Venezuela, and Brazil. In rock and roll, they are probably most identified with Bo Diddley.

Although a simple instrument, the method of playing the maracas is not obvious. The seeds must travel some distance before they hit the leather, wood, or plastic.
