 '''East Aurora''' is a village located in Erie County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of six , six seven three . 

The '''Village of East Aurora''' lies in the eastern half of the Town of Aurora. It is southeast of Buffalo, New York. 

 History 
The village was founded in one eight zero four , and incorporated in one eight seven four .

Former President of the United States Millard Fillmore lived in East Aurora with his wife Abigail from one eight two six to one eight three zero . The house he built there while practicing law in the beginning of his political career is currently maintained by the Aurora Historical Society.

The founder of the Roycroft Movement, Elbert Hubbard, also lived there during the turn of the nineteenth century. The Roycroft Inn was granted National Landmark Status in one nine eight six and re-opened in June one nine nine five through the support of the Margaret L. Wendt Foundation. 

It is also the birthplace of and home to the Corporate Headquarters for Fisher-Price.

Christ the King Seminary is located west of the village.

 Geography 
East Aurora is located at four two  four six ' one  North, seven eight  three seven ' two  West ( four two . seven six six eight zero nine , - seven eight . six one seven one two one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of six . five km ( two . five mi ).  six . five km ( two . five mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. 

Main Street in the village is US Route two zero A.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are six , six seven three people, two , five nine six households, and one , seven two eight families residing in the village. The population density is one , zero two six . five km ( two , six five three . eight mi ). There are two , seven two nine housing units at an average density of four one nine . eight km ( one , zero eight five . three mi ). The average household size is two . four four and the average family size is three . zero five .

In the village the population is spread out with two five . six % under the age of one eight , five . three % from one eight to two four , two seven . six % from two five to four four , two two . six % from four five to six four , and one eight . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The '''Elma''' is a town located in Erie County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one one , three zero four . 

The '''Town of Elma''' is located in the north-central part of the county, east of Buffalo, New York. Because of its location, Elma likes to refer to itself as the heart of Erie County. 

 History

 Communities and locations in Elma 
Billington Heights -- A location in the south part of the town. 
'''Blossom''' -- A hamlet in the northwest corner of the town. It was the principal location of the Ebenezer Society.

 '''Evans''' is a town located in Erie County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one seven , five nine four . The town derives its name from David E. Evans, an agent of the Holland Land Company and nephew of Joseph Ellicott. 

The '''Town of Evans''' is in the southwest corner of the county and borders Lake Erie. 

 History  
The Town of Evans was established in one eight two one from part of the Town of Eden. The first settler arrived around one eight zero four , but there was no permanent settlement until one eight zero eight . David Evans was named the local agent of the Holland Land Company in one eight two seven . He was known for his humane management of the company business in relation to the impovrished settlers. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one zero eight . four km ( four one . eight mi ).  one zero eight . four km ( four one . eight mi ) of it is land and zero . zero two % is water. 

The New York State Thruway (Interstate nine zero ) ,US Route two zero , and New York State Route five pass through the town. 

 Bordering areas 
The Town of Brant is to the south, and the Town of Hamburg is to the north. The Town of Eden is on the east side.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one seven , five nine four people, six , six three nine households, and four , seven seven three families residing in the town. The population density is one six two . three km ( four two zero . five mi ).  '''Grand Island''' is a town and an island located in Erie County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one eight , six two one . 

The '''Town of Grand Island''' is located at the northwestern corner of the county. 

 History 
In the early historical period of the island, the one six th Century, French explorers found the Neutral indians living on the island. By one six five one the Senecas had destroyed this tribe and absorbed some of the survivors. The Seneca used the island for hunting and fishing. 

After the French and Indian War the island became part of the British colonies in North America. 

In the one eight two zero s, journalist and utopian Mordecai Manuel Noah tried to found a city to be called Ararat on the island as a refuge for persecuted Jews from around the world.

The Town of Grand Island was organized in one eight five two from part of the Town of Tonawanda.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of eight six . two km ( three three . three mi ).  seven three . eight km ( two eight . five mi ) of it is land and one two . four km ( four . eight mi ) of it is water. The total area is one four . three five % water. 

The town is located entirely on the island of '''Grand Island''' in the Niagara River. The river splits into two parts at the south end of the island and rejoins at the northwest end.

It lies adjacent to the international border between Ontario in Canada and the United States. Paired bridges connect the south end of the island to the Town of Tonawanda, and another pair of bridges connect the northern end to the City of Niagara Falls, New York in Niagara County. The two sets of bridges are connected by Interstate one nine zero , a branch of the New York State Thruway.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one eight , six two one people, six , eight nine eight households, and five , two two one families residing in the town. The population density is two five two . two km ( six five three . one mi ). There are seven , three five five housing units at an average density of nine nine . six km ( two five seven . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine five . eight zero % White, one . six five % African American, zero . two five % Native American, one . one seven % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, zero . two five % from other races, and zero . eight eight % from two or more races.  one . zero nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six , eight nine eight households out of which three five . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six four . eight % are married couples living together, seven . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and two four . three % are non-families. two zero . two % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six eight and the average family size is three . one three .

In the town the population is spread out with two six . seven % under the age of one eight , six . five % from one eight to two four , two seven . seven % from two five to four four , two seven . seven % from four five to six four , and one one . three % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are nine seven . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine four . four males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ six zero , four three two , and the median income for a family is $ seven zero , five two one . Males have a median income of $ four eight , four five seven versus $ three zero , one five seven for females. The per capita income for the town is $ two five , eight one six .  three . zero % of the population and two . four % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, three . three % of those under the age of one eight and five . one % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 '''Harris Hill''' is a hamlet (and a census-designated place) located in the Town of Clarence in Erie County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the community had a total population of four , eight eight one . The region is named after Asa Harris, a former officer in the American Colonial Army, who established a tavern near the top of a low hill northeast of Buffalo, New York. 

 Geography 
Harris Hill is in the southwest corner of the town and is centered on the intersection of Main Street (Route five ) and Harris Hill Road. 

Harris Hill is located at four two  five eight ' one  North, seven eight  four zero ' four zero  West ( four two . nine six seven zero five eight , - seven eight . six seven seven eight two eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the region has a total area of one zero . five km ( four . zero mi ).  one zero . five km ( four . zero mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

To the south east of Harris Hill is a large crushed stone Quarry that plunges some three zero meters in to the bedrock. The quarry now owned by Buffalo Crushed Stone was opened in one nine zero four 

 History 

Asa Harris's Tavern was a stop on the Underground railroad. Freed slaves would sneak under Main Street (Route five ) through livestone caves and exit north at the bottom of the Onondaga (geological formation) in to a swampy forest. The tavern has since been repurposed as the Home Town Cleaners.

'''Lackawanna''' is a city located in Erie County, New York, located just south of Buffalo in the western part of New York state. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one nine , zero six four . The name derives from the Lackawanna River. 

The '''City of Lackawanna''' is in the western part of the county. 

 History 
The City of Lackawanna was incorporated in one nine zero one . Located along Lake Erie, Lackawanna was a center of iron and steel manufacture throughout most of the two zero th Century until a decline in that industry reduced and finally closed the immense facilities located in this city. With the two zero th century growth of the steel plant, at one time the fourth largest in the world, came the continued growth of the city and its institutions. It attracted people from many lands to settle here and make their homes. In the diversity of national origin of its people, it is second to no city in the nation. It is one of the great melting pots of America. 

In recent years, efforts have been made to convert the former steel plant brownfields to other uses. 


Lackawanna is home to '''Our Lady of Victory Basilica''', a National Shrine. Father Nelson Baker is buried here. Father Baker, who fought in the Civil War at Gettysburg as part of the seven four th Regiment of the New York State militia, was responsible for the building of working boy's home in Buffalo in one eight nine eight , an infants home in one nine zero seven , a maternity home in one nine one five , Our Lady of Victory Hospital in one nine one nine and the Basilica of Our Lady of Victory in one nine two six . Father Baker named the Basilica after the famous shrine to Our Lady of Victories in Paris, France, which he had visited as a seminarian in one eight seven four . Father Baker was in charge of the Basicilica and the various institutions of charity until his death at the age of nine four , on July two nine , one nine three six . Father Baker's legacy continues to this day in many ways. His social programs have evolved into Baker Victory Services, which provide care to more than two , five zero zero children each and every day, his Hospital continues to offer services to the area, his Homes of Charity provide the critical funds necessary to continue his social programs through donations, and his wonderful Basilica enjoyed its seven five th Anniversary in two zero zero one . In addition, the Catholic Church named Father Baker Servant of God in one nine eight seven , the first step towards declaring him a saint. Currently, his cause for canonization, overseen by his third successor, Msgr. Robert C. Wurtz, is under review by Vatican officials in the hopes of beatifying the humble priest in the very near future.



The City of Lackawanna was the defendant in the one nine seven one decision ''Kennedy-Park Homes Association v. City of Lackawanna'', which forbade the municipal government from interfering with the construction of a low-income housing development in a predominantly white section of the city, because such action would amount to racial discrimination. , NY ( one nine seven one ) ( four three six F two d one zero eight )

The Buffalo six (also known as the Lackawanna six ) is a group of alleged Al-Qaida terrorists and were convicted of material support to Al-Qaida. They travelled to Afghanistan in the spring of two zero zero one . They were arrested in Lackawanna in mid-September two zero zero two .

 Geography 
Lackawanna is located at four two  four nine ' one zero  North, seven eight  four nine ' three two  West ( four two . eight one nine three nine one , - seven eight . eight two five six three seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one five . nine km ( six . one mi ).  one five . nine km ( six . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one nine , zero six four people, eight , one nine two households, and four , seven seven five families residing in the city. The population density is one , two zero two . seven km ( three , one one four . zero mi ). There are eight , nine five one housing units at an average density of five six four . seven km ( one , four six two . one mi ). The racial makeup of the city is eight three . nine nine % White, nine . five zero % African American, zero . four zero % Native American, zero . three one % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, two . three zero % from other races, and three . four nine % from two or more races.  five . zero eight % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are eight , one nine two households out of which two six . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three seven . two % are married couples living together, one six . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and four one . seven % are non-families. three seven . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three zero and the average family size is three . zero six .

In the city the population is spread out with two four . five % under the age of one eight , eight . five % from one eight to two four , two eight . zero % from two five to four four , two zero . four % from four five to six four , and one eight . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are nine two . three males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight seven . five males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two nine , three five four , and the median income for a family is $ three nine , two three seven . Males have a median income of $ three two , zero six three versus $ two two , seven nine four for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one six , seven two seven .  one six . seven % of the population and one three . one % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two seven . four % of those under the age of one eight and nine . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Adjacent towns and other areas 
The City of Buffalo is to the north. The east border is shared by the Town of West Seneca, and the south border is shared by the Town of Hamburg and the Village of Blasdell. The western border is defined by Lake Erie. 

 Education 
Children in Lackawanna attend school in the Lackawanna City School District.

Children in grades Pre-K to two attend Truman Elementary. Grades three - six are in Martin Road Elementary. Grades seven through eight are in Lackawanna Middle School. Grades nine through one two are in Lackawanna High School.

 Additional facts about Lackawanna 

Ron Jaworski, former quarterback for the Philadelphia Eagles, was born and raised in Lackawanna.

Ruben Santiago-Hudson, a Lackawanna native, set his musical play ''Lackawanna Blues'' in one nine five six Lackawanna.

Connie Porter's novel ''All-bright Court'' is set in Lackawanna.

Dick Shawn, actorcomedian (born Richard Schulefand), was raised in Lackawanna, where his parents owned a store.

 '''Newstead''' is the most northeastern town in Erie County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of eight , four zero four . 

The '''Town of Newstead''' is northeast of Buffalo, New York, and its principal community is the Village of Akron. 

 History 
The town was first settled around one eight zero one . 
The Town of Newstead was established in one eight two three as the Town of Erie from the eastern part of Town of Clarence. In one eight three one the name was changed to Newstead. 

The discovery of Gypsum and the related cement industry helped promote the area. 
 
 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one three two . three km ( five one . one mi ).  one three two . zero km ( five one . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two seven % water. 

The Tonawanda Creek defines the northern boundary. 

The Town of Newstead is in the northeast corner of the county. The north town line is the border of Niagara County (Town of Royalton) and the east town line is the border of Genesee County (Town of Pembroke).

The New York State Thruway (Interstate nine zero ) and New York State Highway five cross the south part of the town. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are eight , four zero four people, three , three seven one households, and two , three three two families residing in the town. The population density is six three . seven km ( one six four . nine mi ). There are three , six two three housing units at an average density of two seven . four km ( seven one . one mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine eight . two zero % White, zero . four zero % African American, zero . seven seven % Native American, zero . one two % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . one zero % from other races, and zero . four zero % from two or more races.  zero . five two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , three seven one households out of which three zero . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five seven . two % are married couples living together, eight . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and three zero . eight % are non-families. two six . one % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four nine and the average family size is three . zero two .

In the town the population is spread out with two four . zero % under the age of one eight , six . nine % from one eight to two four , two eight . five % from two five to four four , two three . eight % from four five to six four , and one six . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are nine five . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine two . three males.

 Communities and locations in Newstead 
Akron -- The village of Akron is located on Route nine three . 
'''Akron Airport ( nine G three )''' -- A general aviation airport on the hilltop east of Akron village. 
'''Akron Falls County Park''' -- A park located within the village of Akron, built along the banks of Murder Creek. The park provides picnicking, walking trails, and some sports fields. 
'''Falkirk''' -- A previous community in Newstead, now absorbed into Akron village. 
'''Hawkins Corners''' -- A location now of historical interest only, south of the Village of Akron. 
'''Leisurewood Recreational Community''' -- A large seasonal community composed of trailers and recreational vehicles, occupied primarily during the summer months. It is southwest of Akron. 
'''Murder Creek''' -- A tributary of Tonawanda Creek that flows through the town. The name stems from the first white person having been killed there. 
'''Sand Hill''' -- A small hamlet in the northwest part of the town, consisting of a few residences and a church. The hamlet at the intersection of Rapids and Crego Roads. 
'''South Newstead''' -- A location near the border with the Town of Alden at the junction of South Newstead and Buckwheat Roads. Residences and farms are scattered through the area. Formerly, a post office was located in this area. 
'''Swifts Mills''' -- A location of historical interest in the north part of the town, located on Murder Creek. 
Tonawanda Reservation -- A small inhabited part of this Indian reservation is in the eastern part of the town. Several retail establishments sell discount cigarettes and untaxed gasoline.

 Additional information about Newstead 
Newstead and the Town of Clarence have constructed several miles of biking and jogging trails that link the towns. The Octagon House in the village of Akron is open to visitors who wish to examine this architectural style.

 History 



 Secession: Last of the Rebels 

In one eight six one in the small hamlet of Town Line in Upstate New York,  one two five voters met and voted eight five to four zero to seceed from the Union and join the Confederate States of America.  The reasons are unclear and a article in the Buffalo New York Newspapers cite discontent with President Lincoln, treatment of confederate soldiers at a POW camp in Elmira, the interest of self rule or perhaps an incident by some runaway slaves at a local underground railroad stop. It was also reported that Town Line sent five men to fight for the Confederate States under General Robert E. Lee.

During the American Civil War, as casualties on both side increased and the nature of the Civil War changed, the secession was slowly forgotten by members of the community but never revoked.

During World War II, it was discovered that Town Line didn't officially had not rejoint the Union and in one nine four five , Town Line voted to officially rejoin the Union. Even today, the local volunteer fire company has the words ''''Last of the Rebels'''' on their shoulder patch.

'''Wales''' is a town located in Erie County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , nine six zero .

The '''Town of Wales''' is one of the Southtowns of Erie County by virtue of its position in the southeast part of the county. 

 History 
The first known settlers arrived around one eight zero six . The town was formed in one eight one eight from the (now defunct) '''Town of Willinck'''. 

The Bleak House (named after the Dickens novel) was used in the filming of the original Tuck Everlasting. Was also the home of the Carpenter family who raised State Fair winning cows.

Originally a farming community, the town of Wales is documented through profiles of its churches, civic organizations, businesses, and individual citizens. Established in one eight one eight , the town of three , zero zero zero residents is located in a scenic area of Erie County amid woodlands and streams. Town boards over the years have been respectful of the residents' desire to maintain a small-town atmosphere and quality of life, and the transition to modern life has emphasized small, family-oriented businesses. Personal commitment and a spirit of volunteerism have prevailed in the community, as evidenced by its many interactive organizations. 

 Historical extract 
 TOWN OF WALES.
The town of Wales was formed from the territory of Willink on April one five , one eight one eight , comprising township nine , range five , of the Holland Company survey, with nominal jurisdiction over the Indian lands opposite that township to the center of the Buffalo Creek Reservation. The town has an area of thirty-six square miles, or two two , six zero zero acres. It is situated on the east line of Erie county, with Aurora on the west, Holland on the south and Marilla on the north. The central branch of the Buffalo Creek (commonly called Big Buffalo Creek) flows northwesterly across the town. Hunter's Creek flows northerly nearly across the town and empties into Buffalo Creek. Cazenove Creek flows across the southwest corner. The Big Buffalo Creek is bordered by a broad and fertile valley, while a narrower one extends along Hunter's Creek. The greater part of the remainder of the town is high land with gravelly and clayey soil.

The territory of Wales received its first settlers in one eight zero six in the persons of William and Ethan Allen, Amos Clark and William Hoyt. In one eight zero seven Jacob Turner, Nathan Moon and Charles and Alexander McKay came in. In one eight zero eight Ebenezer and John Holmes, brothers, settled on Holmes Hill, where their descendants are still found. Silas Hunter also settled in the town in that year. In one eight zero nine Peleg Havens, Welcome Moore and Isaac Reed were among the newcomers. James Wood settled in Wood's Hollow (or Wales Hollow, now Wales village), and Samuel Searls settled where the widow of Thomas Hill now resides.

In one eight one zero Jacob Turner built the first frame house. Alvin Burt, William A. Burt (his son) and Benjamin Eariwere in the town as early as one eight one zero . Isaac Hall settled in one eight one one at Hall's Hollow, and with his brother Eli built mills that year, and in the next year built a tavern. Varnum Kenyon, William Carpenter, Nathan M. Mann, Lyman Blackmar and Eli Weed, jr., came in about the same time, the latter locating on Weed's Hill, where his descendants still live.

Dr. Ira G. Watson settled in one eight one two a little north of South Wales and in the same year William Burt opened the first store. John Russell bought a large tract of land in one eight one three in the southwest part, on the site of South Wales. In one eight one five he sold a part to Aaron Warner; Henry Monroe was another purchaser from him. In one eight one six Mr. Warner built the Osborn House, which is still standing but not in use as a public house. In one eight one five John Cole settled where Lyman Wood lives, and in one eight one seven Isaac Wightman became a resident. Ira Hall settled in the town in one eight one eight and established a tannery and shoe shop near his brother's mills. Stephen Patch and his three sons also settled that year. Jacob Turner built a grist mill before one eight one eight at Wood's Hollow. Distilleries were numerous in early years, seven being at one time in operation on Buffalo Creek within this town. Other early and prominent settlers were John Cadugan, Frank N. Smith, Thomas Hill, Harry A. Stevens, Chandler Barber, Charles N. Brayton, Orlo Grover, Joseph Charles, James Chalmers, Elias Dimond, Harding W. Hall, Martin J. and George Keem, S. R. Hall, Samuel Gail, J. W. Waters, Welcome Moore, B. D. Norton, Thomas Stokes, Dennis Sullivan and John Weaver.

The first post-office in this town was opened in one eight two one with the name Wales; it was in the store of William A. Burt at Hall's Hollow (now Wales Center). A few years later when James Wood was made postmaster, he took the office to Wood's Hollow (now Wales). Another office was established in one eight two six at South Wales.

A hotel was built in one eight three five a mile west of Hall's Hollow. This has been known as the old Pochel tavern and is still kept open. Mortimer Stevens had a small store near the hotel and in one eight four three obtained a postoffice there called Wales Center, in which he was the first postmaster; it was removed to Hall's Hollow in one eight five zero .

Numerous saw mills were built in early years along the streams, but most of them have disappeared with the forest. There is one in operation at South Wales, and one at Wales Center, with a few portable mills. The character of the agricultural products has changed in comparatively recent years. Grain growing has largely given place to cheese and butter making. A cheese factory is in operation at Wales and one at South Wales. There is also a butter factory at Wales Center and the dairy products of the town have an excellent reputation. 

 Geography 
The east town line is the border of Wyoming County, New York. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of nine two . three km ( three five . six mi ).  nine two . two km ( three five . six mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . one one % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two , nine six zero people, one , one one six households, and eight four one families residing in the town. The population density is three two . one km ( eight three . one mi ). There are one , one six five housing units at an average density of one two . six km ( three two . seven mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine eight . five eight % White, zero . one zero % African American, zero . three seven % Native American, zero . three seven % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . two zero % from other races, and zero . three seven % from two or more races.  zero . seven four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , one one six households out of which three four . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six four . three % are married couples living together, seven . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and two four . six % are non-families. one nine . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six five and the average family size is three . zero seven .

In the town the population is spread out with two four . nine % under the age of one eight , six . four % from one eight to two four , two nine . three % from two five to four four , two seven . eight % from four five to six four , and one one . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are nine eight . one males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine seven . nine males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ five one , four eight six , and the median income for a family is $ five nine , three five zero .  '''Crown Point''' is a town located in Essex County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , one one nine . 

The '''Town of Crown Point''' is on the eastern edge of the county. 
A south view of Crown Point one seven six zero by Thomas Davies. 

History
During colonial times and the American Revolutionary War, its strategic location often made Crown Point an important location. Situated on the west shore of Lake Champlain about one five miles north of Fort Ticonderoga it provided a fortified position about a day's travel north of that site. Two forts were built near the current location of the town, Fort St. Frdric by the French and later Fort Crown Point by the British.

After the failure of the American Invasion of Canada in one seven seven six it represented the northernmost point of American control. During the British Saratoga Campaign in one seven seven seven , General Burgoyne organized a supply magazine here to support his attack of Ticonderoga.

The Town of Crown Point is an original town of the county, established in one seven eight six . 

 Geography 
The east town line, defined by Lake Champlain, is the border of Vermont (Addison County). A bridge (Route one seven ) connects Crown Point to Vermont. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of two one two . one km ( eight one . nine mi ).  one nine seven . five km ( seven six . three mi ) of it is land and one four . six km ( five . six mi ) of it is water. The total area is six . eight nine % water.

Crown Point lies entirely within the Adirondack State Park.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two , one one nine people, seven nine seven households, and five seven eight families residing in the town. The population density is one zero . seven km ( two seven . eight mi ). There are one , zero six three housing units at an average density of five . four km ( one three . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine seven . five zero % White, zero . zero nine % African American, zero . two four % Native American, zero . three eight % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . one four % from other races, and one . six five % from two or more races.  zero . one four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are seven nine seven households out of which three three . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five eight . two % are married couples living together, eight . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and two seven . four % are non-families. two one . three % of all households are made up of individuals and nine . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  '''Lake Placid''' is a village of two , six three eight in the Adirondack Mountains in Essex County, New York, near the center of the Town of North Elba and named after an adjacent lake. 

While the village is a year-round resort, it's likely most known as the site of the one nine eight zero Winter Olympics, and particularly the USA-USSR hockey game, the Miracle on Ice, when a group of American college students and amateurs upset the heavily-favored Soviet national team four - three and two days later won the Gold Medal. The victory is usually ranked as one of the greatest in American sports' history. 

Lake Placid also hosted the Winter Olympics in one nine three two . Along with St. Moritz, Switzerland and Innsbruck, Austria, it is one of the three places to have twice hosted the Winter Olympic Games.
 

 History 
Lake Placid began developing as a tourist location in the latter part of the one nine th Century. 
The one nine three two and the one nine eight zero Winter Olympics were held here. American singer Kate Smith had a summer home here for many years.

 Geography 
The village is located near the south end of a lake called Lake Placid. More immediate to the village is Mirror Lake, which lies between the village and Lake Placid. 

Lake Placid is located at four four  one seven ' eight  North, seven three  five nine ' seven  West ( four four . two eight five six nine one , - seven three . nine eight five four zero four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of three . nine km ( one . five mi ).  three . six km ( one . four mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is nine . eight seven % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , six three eight people, one , three zero three households, and six zero four families residing in the village. The population density is seven three eight . one km ( one , nine one three . two mi ). There are one , seven six five housing units at an average density of four nine three . eight km ( one , two eight zero . one mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine five . seven five % White, zero . six eight % African American, zero . four five % Native American, zero . nine one % Asian, zero . five seven % Pacific Islander, zero . one nine % from other races, and one . four four % from two or more races.  zero . nine one % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , three zero three households out of which two two . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three four . one % are married couples living together, eight . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and five three . six % are non-families. four five . seven % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . zero two and the average family size is two . nine three .

In the village the population is spread out with two two . four % under the age of one eight , eight . five % from one eight to two four , three three . two % from two five to four four , one nine . three % from four five to six four , and one six . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are nine two . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight eight . three males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ two eight , two three nine , and the median income for a family is $ four three , zero four two . Males have a median income of $ two six , five eight five versus $ two one , seven five zero for females. The per capita income for the village is $ one eight , five zero seven .  one three . two % of the population and eight . five % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one three . three % of those under the age of one eight and one seven . eight % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Lake Placid facts 
The Olympic Bobsleigh run from the air

Lake Placid was the first location in North America to host two Olympic games. Los Angeles became the other when it hosted the Summer Olympic Games for the second time in one nine eight four .

The village has been host to other events besides the Olympic Games, and is also the location of sports training facilties, especially those for winter events. Jack Shea, a resident of the village, became the first person to win two gold medals when he doubled in speed skating at the one nine three two Winter Olympics.

Lake Placid Airport (LKP) is south of the village. Lake Placid is also home to the Lake Placid Sinfonietta, a professional summer chamber orchestra that has existed since one nine one seven .

 '''Willsboro''' is a town located in Essex County, New York, in the United States. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , nine zero three . 

The '''Town of Willsboro''' is in the eastern part of the county. 

 History 
The region was first settled in one seven six five by William Gilliland. Originally called Milltown by its founder, shortly after the Revolutionary War the town was renamed Willsborough (and subsequently shortened to Willsboro ) in his honor.

While the town has always had a thriving farming tradition, through most of its history Willsboro's main employer was a paper mill (which produced the wood pulp used in the making of paper). With the closing of this pulp mill in the one nine six zero s, the town faced hard economic times and relied heavily on tourist dollars. Recently, new industries have moved to the town, most notably: a wallastonite mine, curtain and funiture manufacturers, and numerous web-based service companies. It is also becoming a bedroom community for the city of Plattsburg, to the north.

 Geography 
The east town line, marked by Lake Champlain, is the border of Vermont. The Bouquet River enters Lake Champlain in the town. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one nine zero . one km ( seven three . four mi ).  one one zero . six km ( four two . seven mi ) of it is land and seven nine . five km ( three zero . seven mi ) of it is water. The total area is four one . eight one % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one , nine zero three people, eight zero three households, and five four nine families residing in the town. The population density is one seven . two km ( four four . six mi ). There are one , four six eight housing units at an average density of one three . three km ( three four . four mi ). The ''' one nine nine eight Football World Cup''' was held in France, by the FIFA decision in July one nine nine two . The tournament was won by France, who beat Brazil three - zero in the final. 

Intro
This was the first World Cup title for France, who joined Brazil and five others (Uruguay, Italy, Germany, England, and Argentina) to be world champion by winning all its matches.

The format of the competition changed from one nine nine four : it was expanded from two four (six groups of four teams) to three two teams, divided into eight groups of four. Sixteen teams: eight group winners and eight second place finishers would qualify for the knockout competition.

Davor uker of surprise third-place finisher Croatia won the Golden Boot after scoring six goals.

Michael Owen made his World Cup debut in ' nine eight by scoring one of his most amazing solo goals ever. Taking the ball from the halfway line, he dribbled past three Argentine defenders before slotting the ball past the goalkeeper.

This World Cup tournament was the first one for the countries of Croatia, Jamaica, Japan, and South Africa.

For details of the competition, see Football World Cup one nine nine eight (match reports) article.

Qualification
See Football World Cup one nine nine eight (qualification).

Trivia

A change in the rules came into effect at the one nine nine eight World Cup, stating that as regulation time was about to expire in any period of play the fourth official would use a handheld electronic display to show how many minutes of stoppage time were to be played. This practice has continued since then, after being well received by media and spectators alike.

An attempt to revive ancient ballgame of La Soule to celebrate the Football World Cup ( one nine nine eight ), fell through.

 '''Harrietstown''' is a town located in Franklin County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of five , five seven five .

 '''Gloversville''' is a city located in Fulton County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one five , four one three . 

The '''City of Gloversville''' is located in the northern part of the Town of Johnstown. With the City of Johnstown, Gloversville is one of the Twin Cities. 

 History 
The location became a settlement for Puritans from New England at the end of the one eight th Century. 
It earned its name for being the centre of the U.S. glove making industry for many years. Upon the establishment of a United States post office in one eight two eight , Gloversville became the official name of the city. The manufacture of gloves is still its main industry. At one time during the heyday of glove production in the middle two zero th century, Gloversville factories and shops made one out of every three gloves in the world. 

The current mayor of Gloversville is Timothy Hughes (D) who began his first four-year term on January one , two zero zero six . 

Gloversville High School and neighboring Johnstown High School have the oldest continuous high school football rivalry in the state of New York.

Legendary film producer Samuel Goldwyn's first place of residence in the United States when he emigrated from Poland via Canada was Gloversville. Pulitzer Prize winning author Richard Russo (''Empire Falls, The Risk Pool'') was raised in Gloversville and the city and its residents were the inspiration for many of his characters and locations in his novels, especially his novel ''Mohawk''.

 Geography 
Gloversville is located at four three  three ' nine  North, seven four  two zero ' three four  West ( four three . zero five two four seven six , - seven four . three four two seven nine eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one three . two km ( five . one mi).  one three . two km ( five . one mi) of it is land and zero . two zero % is water.

 In linear algebra, a '''symmetric matrix''' is a matrix that is its own transpose. Thus ''A'' is symmetric if

:A^\textrm A

which implies that ''A'' is a square matrix. The entries of a symmetric matrix are symmetric with respect to the main diagonal (top left to bottom right). So if the entries are written as ''A'' (''a''''ij''), then
:a_ a_
for all indices ''i'' and ''j''.

The following three -by- three matrix is symmetric:

:\begin
 one  looks like 
:q(x_ one ,\ldots,x_n)\sum_^n \lambda_i x_i^ two 
with real numbers ''i''. This considerably simplifies the study of quadratic forms, as well as the study of the level sets which are generalizations of conic sections.

This is important partly because the second-order behavior of every smooth multi-variable function is described by the quadratic form belonging to the function's Hessian; this is a consequence of Taylor's theorem.

Other types of symmetry or pattern in square matrices have special names; see for example:

circulant matrix
Hankel matrix
Toeplitz matrix.

See also symmetry in mathematics.

 '''Alabama''' is a town located in Genesee County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , eight eight one . The village is named after the State of Alabama. 

The '''Town of Alabama''' is in the northwest part of the county. 

 History 
The town was first settled around one eight zero six . 
The Town of Alabama was established in one eight two six from a part of the Town of Shelby. The town was originally called the Town of Gerrysville after Vice-President Elbridge Gerry. In one eight two eight the town assumed its current name. 

Some of the water from local sour springs, eight in total, was once bottled for medicinal use. 
A three seven room hotel was erected on the property and named Spring House . The building burned in one nine one four . The land is now part of the Iroquois National Wildlife Refuge.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one one zero . seven km ( four two . eight mi ).  one one zero . two km ( four two . five mi ) of it is land and zero . five km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . four nine % water.

The Tonawanda Creek flows through south part of the town, and Oak Orchard Creek flows through the north part. 

The north town line is the border of Orleans County and the west town line is the border of Erie County and Niagara County. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one , eight eight one people, six six three households, and four eight three families residing in the town. The population density is one seven . one km ( four four . two mi ). There are seven zero zero housing units at an average density of six . four km ( one six . five mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine five . one six % White, zero . eight five % African American, two . two three % Native American, zero . two one % Asian, zero . one one % Pacific Islander, zero . zero zero % from other races, and one . four four % from two or more races.  zero . eight five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six six three households out of which three seven . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six three . seven % are married couples living together, five . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and two seven . one % are non-families. two two . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight four and the average family size is three . three six .

In the town the population is spread out with three zero . zero % under the age of one eight , seven . three % from one eight to two four , two nine . eight % from two five to four four , two zero . nine % from four five to six four , and one two . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three five years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero one . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero zero . eight males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ four zero , two two three , and the median income for a family is $ four five , nine four seven . Males have a median income of $ three two , four five four versus $ two three , four five six for females.  Communities and locations in Alabama 

'''Alabama''' (or '''Alabama Center''') -- The hamlet of Alabama is centered on the crossroad of Routes six three and seven seven , where there is a restaurant on one corner and a small market on another. 
'''Basom''' -- This hamlet is on Route seven seven where Bloomingdale Road runs off to the west. This community had a railroad station at one time. 
'''Indian Falls''' -- A hamlet at the south town line on Route seven seven . Tonawanda Creek flows through the community and has a spectacular waterfall. Above the falls are rapids which were a source of water power in the early days of the community. 
Iroquois National Wildlife Refuge -- A federal refuge in the northern part of the town.
'''Oak Orchard State Wildlife Management Area''' - Partially in the northern part of the town. 
'''South Alabama''' -- A hamlet on Route six three , near the Oakfield border and south of Wheatville. The community was formerly called Smithville. 
Tonawanda Reservation of the Seneca tribe - A part of the reservation is inside the west border of the town. Bloomingdale Road passes through the reservation, connecting Basom and Akron. 
'''Tonawanda State Wildlife Management Area''' - A conservation area, partially in the northern part of the town. 
'''West Alabama''' -- A former hamlet, now a location in the northwest corner of the town on Route seven seven . 
'''Wheatville''' -- A hamlet east of Alabama village by the intersection of Knowlesville and Lockport Roads. 
'''Wheatville Station''' -- A location south of South Alabama.

 '''Byron''' is a town and township located in Genesee County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , four nine three . It was named in honor of Lord Byron. 

The '''Town of Byron''' is on the northern border of Genesee County. The town is northeast of Batavia, New York. 

 History 
Byron was first settled around one eight zero seven . 
The '''Town of Byron''' was incorporated in one eight two zero from part of the Town of Bergen.  

Byron was traditionally a rural area of dairy and vegetable farms, but is increasingly becoming a bedroom community for Rochester and Batavia.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of eight three . five km ( three two . two mi ).  eight three . four km ( three two . two mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . one nine % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two , four nine three people, eight seven eight households, and six six three families residing in the town. The population density is two nine . nine km ( seven seven . four mi ). There are nine two two housing units at an average density of one one . one km ( two eight . six mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine five . seven five % White, zero . two eight % African American, zero . six four % Native American, zero . three six % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander, one . eight nine % from other races, and one . zero four % from two or more races.  three . seven seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are eight seven eight households out of which four zero . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six four . two % are married couples living together, seven . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two four . four % are non-families. one eight . six % of all households are made up of individuals and five . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight four and the average family size is three . two four .

In the town the population is spread out with two nine . three % under the age of one eight , eight . two % from one eight to two four , three one . four % from two five to four four , two two . nine % from four five to six four , and eight . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero zero . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero one . one males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ four nine , seven two two , and the median income for a family is $ five six , nine two seven . Males have a median income of $ three eight , eight two eight versus $ two four , eight seven seven for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one nine , eight two five .  five . zero % of the population and three . seven % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, six . two % of those under the age of one eight and six . four % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Communities and locations in Byron 
'''Byron''' (previously Byron Center ) -- The hamlet of Byron, located at the junction of Routes two three seven and two six two . 
'''Lidke's Hill''' -- A location in the northern part of the town. 
'''Mosquito Point''' -- A location in the northwest part of the town. 
'''Pumpkin Hill''' -- A hamlet north of Byron village on Route two three seven . It is also called North Byron.  The name Pumpkin Hill comes from a sign with a pumpkin shape at a former hotel.
'''South Byron''' (originally Brusselville ) -- A community south of The Byron village on Route two three seven , it lies along the main branch of the New York Central rail line.

 '''Pembroke''' is a town located in Genesee County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of four , five three zero . The name is that of a town in west Wales. 

The '''Town of Pembroke''' lies on the west border of Genesee County.

The town was first settled in one eight zero four . Pembroke was established from part of the Town of Batavia in one eight one two .

The New York State Thruway (Interstate nine zero ) and the Tonawanda Creek pass through the town. 

The west town line is the border of Erie County, New York. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are four , five three zero people, one , six six zero households, and one , two two eight families residing in the town. The population density is four one . nine km ( one zero eight . six mi ). There are one , seven seven six housing units at an average density of one six . four km ( four two . six mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine eight . one two % White, zero . three eight % African American, zero . three five % Native American, zero . one five % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . one three % from other races, and zero . eight six % from two or more races.  zero . six eight % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , six six zero households out of which three six . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six one . three % are married couples living together, eight . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and two six . zero % are non-families. one nine . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . seven three and the average family size is three . one six .

In the town the population is spread out with two seven . nine % under the age of one eight , six . seven % from one eight to two four , three zero . two % from two five to four four , two two . eight % from four five to six four , and one two . five % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, four . five % of those under the age of one eight and four . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Communities and locations in Pembroke 
'''Brick House Corners''' -- A hamlet at the intersection of Main Street (Route five ) and Allegany Road (Route seven seven ). Toll plaza four eight A of the Thruway is located north of the intersection.
'''Cookville''' -- A location now marked by the Pembroke service area on the New York State Thruway in the east part of the town. 
Corfu -- The Village of Corfu, on the south border of the town. 
'''East Pembroke''' -- A hamlet on Main Street (Route five ) at the east town line of Pembroke and the Town of Batavia. 
Indian Falls -- This hamlet, located by a waterfall on the Tonawanda Creek, is the birthplace of Ely S. Parker. Route seven seven passes through the community. 
'''Murder Creek''' -- A stream that flows past Pembroke village and is a tributary of the Tonawanda Creek. 
'''North Pembroke''' -- A hamlet on the Tonawanda Creek in the northeast corner of the town. 
'''Pembroke''' -- A hamlet on Main Street (Route five ) near the border with Erie County. The hamlet is composed of houses and commercial buildings (some closed) scattered along Main Street. The only intersection is where Lake Road crosses. Two small factories on the east end of the village are dairy-related. 
'''Pembroke Center''' -- A location on Main Street between Pembroke and East Pembroke. 
'''Richville''' -- A formler community in the west part of the town.

 Adjacent Towns and areas 
The east border is shared with the Town of Batavia and the west border with the Town of Newstead in Erie County, New York. The north border is the Town of Alabama and the south is the Town of Darien.

 '''Stafford''' is a town located in Genesee County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , four zero nine . The town was named after a location in England.

 History 
The town was first settled in one seven nine eight , one of the first of the towns in the Holland Purchase to be occupied. Stafford was formed in one eight two zero from parts of the Town of Batavia and the Town of Le Roy. Part of Stafford was taken to form the Town of Pavilion in one eight four two .

The New York State Thruway (Interstate nine zero ) and Oatka Creek cross the town. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two , four zero nine people, nine zero nine households, and six nine five families residing in the town. The population density is two nine . nine km ( seven seven . four mi ). There are nine nine seven housing units at an average density of one two . four km ( three two . zero mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine seven . seven two % White, one . zero eight % African American, zero . three three % Native American, zero . one seven % Asian, zero . zero eight % Pacific Islander, zero . one two % from other races, and zero . five zero % from two or more races.  zero . two five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are nine zero nine households out of which three one . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six six . three % are married couples living together, six . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two three . five % are non-families. one eight . seven % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six five and the average family size is three . zero three .

In the town the population is spread out with two four . zero % under the age of one eight , seven . one % from one eight to two four , two seven . one % from two five to four four , two seven . four % from four five to six four , and one four . four % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four zero years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero one . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero one . eight males.

Males have a median income of $ three five , five four eight versus $ two four , three seven five for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one nine , seven seven five .  three . seven % of the population and three . zero % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two . one % of those under the age of one eight and three . four % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 '''Durham''' is a town located in Greene County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , five nine two . The town was named after Durham, Connecticut. 

The '''Town of Durham''' is in the northwest corner of the county. 

 History 
The town was first settled around one seven eight two . The town was established from part of the Town of Coxsackie in one seven nine zero as the Town of Freehold.  In one eight zero five , the name was changed to Durham, the town having been called informally New Durham by the many settlers from Connecticut. 

Part of the town was lost to form, in one eight zero three , the new Towns of Cairo, Greenville, and Windham. In one eight three six , the western part of Durham became the Town of Conesville in Schoharie County.

 Demographics

The population density is two zero . three km ( five two . six mi ). There are one , six four two housing units at an average density of one two . nine km ( three three . three mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine eight . three eight % White, zero . zero eight % African American, zero . three one % Native American, zero . four two % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . zero eight % from other races, and zero . seven three % from two or more races.  one . three five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , zero four six households out of which two eight . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five six . one % are married couples living together, eight . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three one . three % are non-families. two five . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four four and the average family size is two . nine one .

In the town the population is spread out with two three . zero % under the age of one eight , six . three % from one eight to two four , two five . zero % from two five to four four , two eight . two % from four five to six four , and one seven . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four two years. For every one zero zero females there are nine nine . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine seven . eight males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ three four , two eight two , and the median income for a family is $ four one , eight seven five . Males have a median income of $ three four , eight two one versus $ two two , two nine two for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one eight , seven zero five .  one one . five % of the population and nine . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, nine . zero % of those under the age of one eight and seven . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 '''Halcott''' is a town located in Greene County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one nine three . 

The '''Town of Halcott''' is located in the southwestern corner of the county. 

 History 
The first recorded settlers, the Valkenburg family, arrived around one eight one three , although some non-permanent settlers had attempted to live in the area about one seven nine zero . The town was established in one eight five one from the Town of Lexington. 

In one nine zero zero , the town population was two seven two . 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of five nine . seven km ( two three . zero mi ).  five nine . seven km ( two three . zero mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. 

Halcott is in the Catskill Mountains. The west and south town lines are the border of Delaware County. The northern and eastern borders are the range of mountains from Bearpen Mountain to Halcott Mountain, beyond which lies the neighboring Town of Lexington. The town is basically the valley of Vly Creek, and ringed by mountains on three sides. Most access to the town is from the south, via the Delaware County village of Fleischmanns.

The pass between Bearpen and neighboring Vly Mountain is traversed by Halcott Mountain Road, an unimproved county highway which reaches two , eight zero zero ft ( eight five three . four m) at the col, making it the highest elevation free public through road in New York State. It is also the only route between Halcott and the rest of Greene County. Like Hardenburgh in neighboring Ulster, to reach the rest of the county via a paved road one must leave and go through a portion of either Ulster or Delaware counties.

This geographic isolation also means that Halcott is the only place in Greene County whose telephones are in the eight four five area code.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one nine three people, eight four households, and five four families residing in the town. The population density is three . two km ( eight . four mi ). There are two eight eight housing units at an average density of four . eight km ( one two . five mi ). There are eight four households out of which two zero . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five two . four % are married couples living together, seven . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and three five . seven % are non-families. two eight . six % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  Communities and locations in Halcott 
'''Halcott Center''' -- A hamlet near the south town line. This is the only named community in the town, and how most mail is addressed (the town relies on, and shares the ZIP code of, Fleischmanns as it is too small to rate its own post office).  '''Palenville''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Greene County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of one , one two zero .

Palenville is in the southwest part of the Town of Catskill, located at the junction of Routes two three A and three two A. It lies at the foot of Kaaterskill Clove, nestled against the base of the Catskill Mountains. Kaaterskill Creek runs through the town, and is spanned by a locally famous swinging footbridge.

 History 
Palenville was an important center of the Hudson River school of art in the Nineteenth Century. Thomas Cole, Frederic Church, and other notable painters stayed and worked in Palenville during the height of the movement. The famous painting ''Kindred Spirits'' depicts Cole and William Cullen Bryant in the background can be seen Kaaterskill Falls, just uphill from the town. The famous Catskill Mountain House was also located just outside Palenville. Palenville is also the fictional home of Rip van Winkle.

Palenville historically is considered the 'First Art Colony in America'(as noted by Dr. Roland Van Zandt, author of ''The Catskill Mountain House''). It is located at the base of the Catskill Mountains at the entrance of the Kaaterskill Clove. There you will find countless waterfalls and many of the motifs of the most famous of one nine th century American artists. In fact, it was called the Village of Falling Waters.
As noted above, Palenville sits at the entrance to the Kaaterskill Clove. This remains today, a popular motif for painters. In the later part of the two zero th century the arts were revived in Palenville. Theatre, Opera and the Circus-arts flurished; and the Terrance Gallery exhibited more than one two zero zero artists from all over the country, in a call to revisit the historic gathering place of the one nine th century painters.

Other noted artists who frequented Palenville and the Clove were: Winslow Homer, Asher B. Durand, Thomas Addison Richards, Frederick Kensett and Sanford R. Gifford. Landscape painters of the two zero th century, to name a few, included: Albert Handel, Barry Hopkins, Athena Billias and Patti Ferrara. George H. Hall who was a 'gendre' painter, took up residence in Palenville towards the end of the one nine th century; and Terrance J. DePietro an abstract painter, who was early on influenced by the Hudson River School, maintained residence and a studio from the later part of the two zero th century into the two one st.(He brought artists from Quebec, Canada, i.e. Nicole Lemelin shadow of the mountain .)

 Geography 
Palenville is located at ( four two . one six nine eight five eight , - seven four . zero one nine one one zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of eight . six km ( three . three mi). eight . six km ( three . three mi) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , one two zero people, four three three households, and two eight seven families residing in the CDP. The population density is one three zero . three km ( three three seven . two mi). There are five five one housing units at an average density of six four . one km ( one six five . nine mi). The racial makeup of the CDP is nine six . one six % White, zero . four five % African American, zero . two seven % Native American, one . zero seven % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . two seven % from other races, and one . seven nine % from two or more races. two . two three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four three three households out of which three zero . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five two . zero % are married couples living together, one zero . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three three . five % are non-families. two five . nine % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four five and the average family size is two . nine four .

In the CDP the population is spread out with two five . five % under the age of one eight , six . one % from one eight to two four , three two . zero % from two five to four four , two four . five % from four five to six four , and one two . zero % who are six five years of age or older.  History 
The local natives called it the Onteora hunting grounds. 
The town was first settled around one seven six three , and the region was then called Schoharie Kill.  An attempt during the American Revolution by the British and their Tory allies to drive the settlers out was thwarted when they were defeated by the settlers. 

Prattsville was established in one eight two four from the Town of Windham. Some of the town was lost to form the Town of Ashland in one eight four eight . 

The one eight three zero population of the town was eight three zero .

The town is in the Catskill Mountains. The north town line is the borderof Schoharie County, New York, and the west town line is the border of Delaware County, New York.

 '''Wells''' is a town located in Hamilton County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of seven three seven . The town is named after Joshua Wells, a land agent, who built the first mills in the area.

 Communities and locations in Wells 

'''Blackbridge''' -- A location on West River Road southwest of Wells and on the north bank of the West Branch Sacandaga River.

'''Windfall''' -- A location northeast of Wells on Windfall Road.

The south border of Wells is formed by the Towns of Benson and Hope. The Town of Arietta is at the west border, and the Town of Lake Pleasant is the northwest border. The Town of Indian Lake is the north border. The Towns of Stony Creek, Thurman, and Johnsburg in Warren County are to the east.

 '''Webb''' is a town located in Herkimer County, New York, United States.  The town is named after William Seward Webb. 

The '''Town of Webb''' is the northernmost town in the county.  The Adirondack Scenic Railroad traverses the town. 

 History 
Attempts were made to settle Webb around one eight zero zero and one eight one one , but both efforts failed. The first permanent settlers arrived around one eight three seven . 

In one eight three six , the Town of Wilmurt was formed from parts of the Towns of Ohio and Russia. Only the south part of Wilmurt was heavily settled. 

Webb was formed from the northern part of the (now defunct) Town of Wilmurt in one eight nine six . Part of Wilmurt was returned to the Town of Ohio. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one , two five zero . eight km ( four eight two . nine mi ), making it the largest town geographically in the state of New York..  one , one six eight . one km ( four five one . zero mi ) of it is land and eight two . seven km ( three one . nine mi ) of it is water. The total area is six . six one % water. 

Webb has the most land area of any town in New York State, making it the largest town in the state, a title it shares with the Town of Hempstead, which is the largest based on population. The Town of Green Island claims to be the smallest based on area. 

Webb is in the Adirondack State Park. One end of the Fulton Chain Lakes is located in the town.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one , nine one two people, eight four five households, and five three four families residing in the town. The population density is one . six km ( four . two mi ). There are three , eight three three housing units at an average density of three . three km ( eight . five mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine seven . nine six % White, zero . six eight % African American, zero . two six % Native American, zero . two six % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . one six % from other races, and zero . six eight % from two or more races.  zero . eight nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are eight four five households out of which two four . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five four . three % are married couples living together, five . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three six . seven % are non-families. two nine . nine % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two one and the average family size is two . seven two .

In the town the population is spread out with two zero . two % under the age of one eight , seven . five % from one eight to two four , two five . six % from two five to four four , two nine . zero % from four five to six four , and one seven . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four three years. For every one zero zero females there are nine six . nine males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine eight . four males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ three five , five four one , and the median income for a family is $ four three , five one six . Males have a median income of $ three zero , nine zero six versus $ two zero , three nine eight for females. Barisan Nasional Logo
'''Barisan Nasional''' ('''National Front''' or '''BN''') is a political coalition in Malaysia. Formed in one nine seven three as the successor of the Alliance ('''Parti Perikatan'''), it has ruled Malaysia uninterrupted (its term as the Alliance included) since independence.

As of December two zero zero three , Barisan Nasional's member parties are:

 United Malays National Organization (UMNO)
 Malaysian Chinese Association (MCA)
 Malaysian Indian Congress (MIC)
 Gerakan Rakyat Malaysia (Malaysian People's Movement)
 People's Progressive Party
 Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu
 Sarawak United People's Party
 Sabah Progressive Party(SAPP)
 Parti Bersatu Sabah
 Liberal Democratic Party
 Parti Bersatu Rakyat Sabah
 United Pasokmomogun Kadazandusun Murut Organisation
 Sarawak Progressive Democratic Party

Party loyalty in Parliament
In two zero zero five , the issue of voting on party lines was brought up when two BN Members of Parliament (MPs), Bung Moktar Radin and Mohamed Aziz, supported a motion by Opposition leader Lim Kit Siang of the Democratic Action Party (DAP) to refer International Trade and Industry Ministry secretary Sidek Hassan to the Committee of Privileges. Deputy Prime Minister Najib Razak, who is also the BN whip in the Dewan Rakyat (lower house of Parliament) had the two MPs referred to the Cabinet for breaking the BN policy of never voting for motions proposed by the opposition.

According to Najib, the two MPs apologised for their actions once informed of their mistake. Eventually, the Cabinet decided to merely reprimand them and not mete out any punishment.
