Geography
East Meadow is located within the Town of Hempstead in Nassau County on Long Island in New York State in the United States. It is located at four zero  four two ' four nine  North, seven three  three three ' two one  West ( four zero . seven one three seven three nine , - seven three . five five five eight two three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one six . three km ( six . three mi ).  one six . three km ( six . three mi ) of it is land and zero . one six % is water. 

East Meadow is generally flat, and the elevation ranges from three two feet near its southwestern edge, to eight two feet along Hempstead Turnpike to the north.

Landmarks
The most prominent features are the town's water tower and hospital, the Nassau University Medical Center (formerly known as the Nassau County Medical Center) which dominate the skyline.  The Nassau County Jail, East Meadow Public Library, Mitchel Manor military housing complex (closed in two zero zero three ), and Eisenhower Park, which includes the attraction, Safety Town are also located in East Meadow.

Education
East Meadow's nine public schools are operated by the East Meadow Union Free School District. The district was organized in one eight one four under the name Brushy Plains and eventually became the third largest school district in New York State. The first school building was on Front Street (where the East Meadow Public Library building stands today). The district is still highly regarded for its educational programs. East Meadow High School's Baseball, Wrestling, and Bowling teams are perennial powerhouses in Nassau County and New York State athletics. The East Meadow Jets Baseball team won a dramatic New York State Championship in one nine nine seven in come-from-behind fashion.

 '''Elmont''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Long Island Nassau County, New York, in the Town of Hempstead. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of three two , six five seven . 

Elmont is famous as the home of Belmont Park Race Track, which has the world's largest dirt thoroughbred racecourse and is the site of the Belmont Stakes.

Elmont is served by two Nationally Recognized Schools of Excellence, Elmont Memorial High School and Sewanhaka High School. Elmont Memorial High School recently was recognized as having the largest percentage of African-American high school students receive a  three  or higher on Advanced Placement tests nationally. 

The Elmont Union Free School District provides outstanding primary school education for Elmont residents. In two zero zero five , the Elmont Union Free School District was recognized by the New York State Comptroller as one of five out of five two districts cited as well managed .

Residents are served by the Belmont Park stop on the Long Island Rail Road(though not always open due to Park events), as well as close proximity to the Floral Park and Valley Stream stops on the LIRR, allowing quick access to New York City and the rest of the Island.

Tree-lined streets, parks, old churches and temples, cultural festivals and parades, restaurants, low-crime rates(In two zero zero five , Forbes magazine listed Long Island as having two , zero four two crimes per one zero zero , zero zero zero residents; the lowest crime rate and less than half the US average) , outstanding schools, a diverse neighborhood, and proximity to New York City make Elmont a unique part of the Town of Hempstead and Long Island.


 Geography

 '''Floral Park''' is a village located in Nassau County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one five , nine six seven . 

The '''Village of Floral Park''' is at the western border of the county. Floral Park is in both the Town of Hempstead and the Town of North Hempstead. 

Government

The village has a mayor-council form of government. The current mayor is Phil Guarnieri; the four-member village board is comprised of trustees Thomas J. Tweedy, Gerry M. Bambrick, Kevin J. Greene, and James E. Rhatigan.

Floral Park has its own police force, which is currently comprised of two lieutenants, six sergeants, two detectives and twenty-five police officers, and is commanded by police commissioner Michael Reid. Floral Park also has a volunteer fire department, lead by Chief Peter Billardello and sanitation department.

Floral Park Police officers earn starting salaries of approximately $ seven zero , zero zero zero .

Quality of life

Floral Park is considered to have a high standard of living. The violent crime rate in two zero zero three was zero . eight per one , zero zero zero and there were zero homicides. This figure is particularly impressive considering that Floral Park borders New York City proper. 

Along with the low crime, the local government ensures that the village is kept visually pleasing as well. Some relevant ordinances include:
 No fences over six feet high may be erected, and no wire fences of any sort are allowed.
 No driveway may be enlarged in any way without a permit.
 No car may be parked anywhere but a specified driveway or garage, or the street.
 No in ground pools are allowed.
 Cars are not allowed to be parked on the street at night (from three AM to five AM) so that the street sweeper can move unobstructed.
 Any unhealthy trees visible from the street must be removed at owner's expense.
 Snow must be removed from walkways within one two hours of snowfall.
 Public loitering is prohibited anywhere in the village.

The town currentally own and maintains three three variously-sized parks. The range is around one zero square feet, to a full town park with three baseball fields (two regular sized, one pee-wee sized), one football field, an ice rink, two handball courts, a pool, and a kiddie pool. Membership is required to use these facilities, and member identification must be produced upon request.

The western village boundary is the border of New York City.

 History 
Franklin Square was the home of the Franklin National Bank, once the nation's two zero th largest bank. Under the leadership of Arthur T. Roth, the Franklin National Bank introduced many banking innovations, such as
 The bank credit card
 The drive up teller window ( one nine five zero )
 Junior savings accounts ( one nine four seven )
 A no-smoking policy on banking floors ( one nine five eight )

On eight October one nine seven four , the Franklin National Bank was declared insolvent due to mismanagement and fraud, involving losses in foreign currency speculation and poor loan policies. This caused massive losses for its stockholders, resulted in jail and disgrace for its management; Italian financier and CEO Michele Sindona, (member of Propaganda Due, an Italian renegade freemasonry lodge), was poisoned in his cell in one nine eight two while serving a life-sentence for his part in this affair. It was at the time the largest bank failure in the history of the country, and forced US banking policymakers to reexamine and reassess regulation of international banking.

'''Freeport''' is a village located in Nassau County, New York, USA, on the south shore on Long Island. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of four three , seven eight three .

The '''Village of Freeport''' is in the southern part of the county, lying within the Town of Hempstead. 

 History and Culture 
The Village of Freeport was incorporated in one eight nine two . The south part of the village is penetrated by several canals that allow access to the Atlantic Ocean by means of passage through salt marshes. Freeport has extensive small boat facilities and a resident fishing fleet, as well as charter and open fishing boats. In the early years Freeport was a tourist and sportsman's destination due to the boating and fishing, but after WWII it became a bedroom community for New York City. The separation between the two eras was marked by the fire that destroyed the Freeport Hotel in the late one nine five zero 's.

A very popular place for people to flock to during the summer is the Nautical Mile. A faved festival occurs there each June which attracts many people from across Long Island and NYC which features their well-known seafood, bars and eclectic little boutiques. 

Freeport has a sizable African-American population, particularly in the northern section of the village. There is also a significant Hispanic community, made up of immigrants that hail from Colombia, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic and many other Latin American nations. One can go through Freeport and experience the wares, groceries of Latin American cuisine at Compare Foods Warehouse, a Latin American themed supermarket (there are three in the village) and, on top of that, there are many Latin American themed grocery stores, restaurants dotting Merrick Road and Main Street that display Caribbean food, Central American food, and South American food. The differences in these ethnic fares are substantial.

Freeport is also the gateway to Jones Beach, one of the largest state beaches in the State of New York.

 The '''Village of Garden City''', New York is located in Nassau County, New York in the USA. The village is located one eight . five miles to the east of New York City, on Long Island. Garden City is on the border of the Town of Hempstead and the Town of North Hempstead. 

As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two one , six seven two . The village is an upper middle-class, predominantly white, Catholic and Protestant community. Many families can trace their heritage to Italian and Irish immigrants to New York City. 


 History 
Thousands of years before tree-lined streets stretched past graceful, formal homes, the place that would become Garden City sat in the heart of the Hempstead Plains, the only prairie east of the Mississippi River.

It was a flat, barren meadow -- as clean a sheet of paper as any developer could hope for. No hills. No forest to clear or swamps to fill. In pre-colonial times, Indians lived on the shores, using the plains only for hunting. Then, for more than a century before Garden City was developed in the mid- one eight zero zero s, the plains were public land in the Town of Hempstead, used as pastures available to all. Some of Long Island's first horse-racing tracks were laid out on the plains. Every so often in the years after one eight five zero , town officials would try to put the seven , zero zero zero acres they controlled up for sale, but voters routinely vetoed the attempts.

Finally, in one eight six seven , the sale narrowly won voters' approval, and two years later Charles Harvey agreed to buy the plains for $ four two an acre. Harvey, one of the backers of New York City's elevated railways, was secretive about his plans for the Nassau land. Rumors spread that he would make the plains into an enormous cemetery, or build a jail. Enter wealthy New York merchant Alexander T. Stewart. He offered to pay an astounding $ five five an acre - and promised to invest millions of dollars to build homes, roads and neighborhoods. It would be one of the nation's first planned communities.

In the one eight six zero 's, Scottish-born multi-millionaire Alexander Turney Stewart bought the then relatively unpopulated Hempstead Plains, and in one eight six eight founded the Village of Garden City. The village was created as an upscale community for those seeking respite from New York City. The main attraction of the community was its McKim, Mead and White-designed The Garden City Hotel (which exists to this day as Long Island's most exclusive hotel, albeit in a more modern form) as well as its many fine Victorian homes, which still exist in the village's Central Section.

Stewart and his architect, John Kellum, got to work laying out their new village, which Stewart named Garden City, after Chicago's informal nickname. Stewart liked the sound of it. 

Much of one eight seven zero was spent clearing and grading land and building an occasional house. The first one, a two-story cottage at four First St., was the headquarters for the enterprise. Workers erected two eight miles of white picket fence around the empty blocks, and Kellum had six , five zero zero sugar maple trees transplanted from Flushing. (The first house was razed in the one nine six zero s, but the fence in front remains.)

In one eight seven one , builder James L'Hommedieu of Great Neck won the first contract to build two zero ``fine villa residences'' in Garden City, priced between $ two , zero zero zero and $ two zero , zero zero zero . Construction began the following year on the original Garden City Hotel. Despite the trappings of a fine village, residents were slow to arrive. They may have been put off by Stewart's insistence on retaining ownership of the entire village. He leased every house and every business to occupants. By the end of one eight seven four , only four zero families had moved to Garden City. But Stewart persevered. He built a railroad to serve Garden City. He built a waterworks and the first sewage system in what was then Queens County. He built more stately houses.

And then he died, in April, one eight seven six . His village was still a shell, with empty roads, saplings and empty houses. Residents began referring to the picket fences around empty lots as Stewart's ribs. Stewart's widow, Cornelia, continued to improve the village and began work on a massive memorial to him. She founded the St. Paul's Schoolfor boys, St. Mary's School for girls, a Bishop's Residance and the gothic Cathedral of the Incarnation, which is to today the center of the Episcopal Diocese of Long Island, as well as the final resting place of Alexander Turney and Cornelia Stewart. St. Mary's school was demolished in the late one nine nine zero 's, the land being sold to private developers. Six luxury homes now stand where St. Mary's used to be. St. Paul's is a constant debate point for Village residents, as they are unsure of what to do with the building. A recient village Board of Trustees vote had designated the site as park-land, under New York State Law. The Cathedral of the Incarnation is currently undergoing a multi-million dollar renevation, which should be completed by two zero one two . This elaborate memorial was completed in one eight eight five . Mrs. Stewart died the following year. There were no heirs.

Control of the village passed to the newly formed Garden City Corp., and in the one eight nine zero s, the village came to life. The company cleared away Stewart's ribs, encouraged renters to buy their homes and hired famed New York architect Stanford White to remodel the Garden City Hotel. It was an instant success. The hotel attracted the Astors, the Vanderbilts, the Pierpont Morgans -- the richest citizens of the day. A golf course was similarly successful.

At the same time, the inability to attract land buyers prompted the Garden City Corp. in one nine one zero to sell four zero acres on Franklin Avenue to Doubleday, Page main line, has concerned many Village residents. The reason for the high concentration of train stations in Garden City, can be accredited to Alexander T. Stewart's vision of a village public transportation network, known as: Stewart's Central Railroad of Long Island.

The early village did well due to its proximity to Hempstead, at that time the commercial center of Long Island. In time, thanks both to the railroad and automobiles, Garden City finally began to fill up. It incorporated as a village in one nine one nine , and its exclusive reputation led nearby communities to spring up and associate themselves with it, particularly Stewart Manor and Garden City Park. 

In one nine one five , the Village of Garden City merged with the Village of Garden City Estates to its west, to form the Incorporated Village of Garden City.

In the one nine two zero 's, the community continued to grow, with housing constructing mainly in the Colonial and Tudor styles occurring largely in Garden City Estates as well as the Eastern Section of Garden City (including the Mott Section, developed by the heirs to the Mott Apple Juice fortune), spurred by the relocation of Doubleday park land. Although still a controversial topic among Village politics, hopefully this new designation will help find a use for the classic Gothic-style building.

In the late one nine eight zero 's, one nine nine zero 's and early two zero zero zero 's, the village's downtown area on Seventh Street, New Hyde Park Road and Franklin Avenue benefitted from a renewal campaign and some new construction. Formerly known as the Fifth Avenue of Long Island, many upscale department stores such as Saks Fifth Avenue, Bloomingdale's and A Wall Street of Long Island, being the home to many banks and investment firms. In addition to this, several luxury restaurants have opened in recent years along this majestic avenue.



 Geography 
Garden City is located at four zero  four three ' three seven  North, seven three  three eight ' five nine  West ( four zero . seven two six eight eight five , - seven three . six four nine seven two zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one three . eight km ( five . three mi ).  one three . eight km ( five . three mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two one , six seven two people, seven , three eight six households, and five , eight five seven families residing in the village. The population density is one , five six seven . zero km ( four , zero five nine . five mi ). There are seven , three eight six households out of which three six . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six nine . eight % are married couples living together, seven . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and two zero . seven % are non-families. one nine . two % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. In the village the population is spread out with two six . five % under the age of one eight , seven . seven % from one eight to two four , two three . one % from two five to four four , two five . eight % from four five to six four , and one six . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four one years. For every one zero zero females there are nine zero . five males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight four . one males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ one zero four , one seven six , and the median income for a family is $ one two zero , three zero five . Males have a median income of $ nine three , one four four versus $ four nine , nine five four for females. The per capita income for the village is $ five three , one nine six .  two . three % of the population and one . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two . three % of those under the age of one eight and two . six % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 A Bernal Sphere viewed from outside.
The inside of the sphere as viewed from the sunlight portal .
A '''Bernal sphere''' is a type of space habitat intended as a long-term home for permanent residents, first proposed in one nine two nine by Dr. John Desmond Bernal.

Dr. Bernal's original proposal described a hollow spherical shell one six km in diameter, with a target population of two zero , zero zero zero to three zero , zero zero zero people. The Bernal sphere would be filled with air.

In a series of studies held at Stanford University in one nine seven five and one nine seven six with the purpose of speculating on designs for future space colonies, Dr. Gerard Kitchen O'Neill proposed a modified Bernal sphere with a diameter of only five zero zero m rotating at one . nine RPM to produce a full Earth gravity at the sphere's equator. The result would be an interior landscape that would resemble a large valley running all the way around the equator of the sphere. Sunlight was to be provided to the interior of the sphere using external mirrors to direct it in through large windows near the poles. The form of a sphere was chosen for its optimum ability to contain air pressure and its optimum mass-efficiency at providing radiation shielding.

This version of the Bernal sphere was dubbed the Island One design, and was sized for a population of one zero , zero zero zero . For comparison, Island Two would house one four zero , zero zero zero , and Island Three (O'Neill cylinder) would support a population of one zero , zero zero zero , zero zero zero .

 :''For the William Gibson novel, see:'' Pattern Recognition (novel).

'''Pattern recognition''' is a field within the area of machine learning. Alternatively, it can be defined as the act of taking in raw data and taking an action based on the category of the data  one . As such, it is a collection of methods for supervised learning.

Pattern recognition aims to classify data (patterns) based on either ''a priori'' knowledge or on statistical information extracted from the patterns. The patterns to be classified are usually groups of measurements or observations, defining points in an appropriate multidimensional space. 

A complete pattern recognition system consists of a sensor that gathers the observations to be classified or described; a feature extraction mechanism that computes numeric or symbolic information from the observations; and a classification or description scheme that does the actual job of classifying or describing observations, relying on the extracted features. 

The classification or description scheme is usually based on the availability of a set of patterns that have already been classified or described. This set of patterns is termed the training set and the resulting learning strategy is characterised as supervised learning. Learning can also be unsupervised, in the sense that the system is not given an ''a priori'' labelling of patterns, instead it establishes the classes itself based on the statistical regularities of the patterns. 

The classification or description scheme usually uses one of the following approaches: statistical (or decision theoretic), syntactic (or structural). Statistical pattern recognition is based on statistical characterisations of patterns, assuming that the patterns are generated by a probabilistic system. Structural pattern recognition is based on the structural interrelationships of features. 

Typical applications are automatic speech recognition, classification of text into several categories (e.g. spamnon-spam email messages), the automatic recognition of handwritten postal codes on postal envelopes, or the automatic recognition of images of human faces. The last two examples form the subtopic image analysis of pattern recognition that deals with digital images as input to pattern recognition systems.

Pattern recognition is more complex when templates are used to generate variants. For example, in English, sentences often follow the N-VP (noun - verb phrase) pattern, but some knowledge of the English language is required to detect the pattern. Pattern recognition is studied in many fields, including psychology, ethology, and computer science.

 '''Great Neck''' is a village located in Nassau County, New York in the USA, on the North Shore of Long Island. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the village had a total population of nine , five three eight . 

The '''Village of Great Neck''' is in the Town of North Hempstead. 
The term '''Great Neck''' is also commonly applied to the entire peninsula on the north shore, comprising a residential community of some four zero , zero zero zero people made up of nine villages as well as unincorporated portions of North Hempstead (and a few hamlets). There is no governing entity which encompasses this larger Great Neck, but it is unified as a postal zone, a water district or two, a school district, and a park district.

Great Neck is within easy commuting distance of Manhattan's Penn Station on the Port Washington Branch of the Long Island Rail Road.

 History 

Great Neck, originally called Madnan's Neck , was settled in the late one seven th century, not long after settlers landed on Plymouth Rock. The area had previously been inhabited by the Mattinecock Native Americans, who were pushed back by the colonists' expansion.

In more recent days, Great Neck -- in particular the incorporated village of Kings Point -- provided a backdrop to F. Scott Fitzgerald's book ''The Great Gatsby''. Thinly disguised as West Egg, in counterpoint to Port Washington's more posh East Egg, the next peninsula over on Long Island Sound, Great Neck symbolized the decadence of the Roaring Twenties as it extended out from New York City into the then-remote suburbs. ''The Great Gatsby's'' themes and characters reflected the real-world transformation that Great Neck was experiencing at the time, as show-business personalities like Sid Caesar and the Marx Brothers bought homes in the hamlet and eventually established it as a haven for newly rich Jews, formerly of Brooklyn and the Bronx.

The end of World War II saw a tremendous migration of Ashkenazi Jews from the cramped quarters and frequent discrimination of the city to the burgeoning suburb. They founded many synagogues and community groups and pushed for stringent educational policies in the town's public schools. Jay Cantor's novel, ''Great Neck,'' portrays the eponymous town of this era, with recently installed residents of various stripes all trying to secure the brightest futures for their children.

During the one nine six zero s, many residents frequented the local pool and ice skating complex, Parkwood, but in the past fifteen years attendance has declined as homeowners built their own inground pools. (After the events of September one one , two zero zero one , the ice skating rink was renamed in honor of Andrew Stergiopoulos, a local resident who was killed in the attack).

Things have changed in Great Neck since the Baby Boomer era. In the one nine eight zero s, an influx of affluent Iranian Jews who were expelled from their country following the one nine seven nine Islamic Revolution settled in Great Neck. Though the majority of their children attended Great Neck schools, they did not integrate into the existing Ashkenazi temples, instead starting their own Iranian synagogues, where they could follow Sephardic traditions. The Persian community also established their own grocery shops. 

From the late one nine nine zero s, the Great Neck peninsula has been home to another Jewish shift. During this time, more observant, Orthodox Jews have moved to the area. This is a similar trend to what has happened in the Five Towns area on the south shore of Long Island. The Orthodox also use their own synagogues. 

It should also be noted that the general trend is that the North part of Great Neck (those students who are sent to Great Neck North Middle and High) is home to more Iranian families, while the South part has a larger East Asian population.

 Culture and tourism 
Currently, Great Neck, connected to New York City by the Long Island Rail Road, serves primarily as a bedroom community for New York City. As such, it contains few touristy attractions. Notable exceptions include:

 Saddle Rock Grist Mill, a historical grain-mill; known to have been in operation as early as the one seven zero zero s.
 United States Merchant Marine Academy in Kings Point
 Steppingstone Park
 Temple Beth-El (Great Neck, New York)

''' Great Neck School District''' is the school district of Great Neck, New York. About six , zero zero zero students, grades K- one two , attend the Great Neck Public Schools. There are three high schools (grades nine - one two ): North High School, with an alternative program, Community School; South High School; and The Village School, a small alternative high school. There are also two middle schools (grades six - eight ) and four elementary schools (grades K- five ).

 '''Laurel Hollow''' is an village in the Town of Oyster Bay in Nassau County, New York in the USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , nine three zero . 

The '''Village of Laurel Hollow''' is in the Town of Oyster Bay. 

 History 
The settlement began around one six five three with purchase of land from the local natives. The village was incorporated in one nine two six as Lauralton, but the name was changed to Laurel Hollow in one nine three five to avoid confusion with a location in Queens County, New York.

 : ''Another Lawrence is a town in St. Lawrence County, New York''. 
----
'''Lawrence''' is a village located in Nassau County, New York in the USA. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the village had a total population of six , five two two . 

The '''Village of Lawrence''' is within the Town of Hempstead. Lawrence is one of the Five Towns, which consists of the villages of Lawrence and Cedarhurst, the hamlets (unincorporated areas) of Woodmere and Inwood, and The Hewletts , which is made up of the hamlet of Hewlett together with the villages of Hewlett Bay Park, Hewlett Harbor and Hewlett Neck. 

 Back LawrenceOld Lawrence 
'''Old Lawrence''' or '''Back Lawrence''' is a part of the Village of Lawrence, comprised of many enormous mansions, beachside luxury villas and former plantations with very large property, some dating back to the time of the American Revolution. Huge golf courses, vast wetlands and nature preserves with historic battlefields enrich this beautiful area making it one of the most exclusive areas in all of Long Island.

Old Lawrence is commonly referred to by historians as the First Hamptons. During the second half of the one nine th century, it was a main vacation spot for the rich families of the highest social scale until the one eight nine zero s. At that time, it became more like a modern village with schools, public facilities, better roads and a large town area that expanded into what is now today. 

Lawrence, or most notably Old Lawrence, was formerly home to a large dominant upper class of White Anglo-Saxon Protestant families that lived there since the time of the American Revolution.  While some blue-blood families still reside there, it has since become home to many upper class Modern Orthodox , Reform, and Conservative Jewish families who have established a number of growing synagogues, particularly since the one nine eight zero s.
 

The Orthodox Jewish communities are close to the more Haredi nearby center of Far Rockaway which has more yeshivas for the children and younger members as well as a variety of kosher restaurants and communal organizations. Central Avenue in Lawrence (and its continuation in Cedarhurst) has a large and growing number of kosher restaurants and other business catering to the Orthodox community.

 Geography 
Lawrence is located at four zero  three six ' three four  North, seven three  four three ' three six  West ( four zero . six zero nine five six six , - seven three . seven two six five four three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one two . one km ( four . seven mi ).  one zero . zero km ( three . eight mi ) of it is land and two . two km ( zero . eight mi ) of it is water. The total area is one seven . nine one % water.

 Demographics

'''Long Beach''' is a city located in Nassau County, New York on the South Shore of Long Island. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the city had a total population of three five , four six two . It was incorporated in one nine two two , and is nicknamed ''The City By the Sea'' (as seen, in Latin, on its official seal). 

The '''City of Long Beach''' is surrounded by the Town of Hempstead.

History 
The community became an incorporated village in one nine one eight and a city in one nine two two . 

Early history
Long Beach's first inhabitants were the Rockaway Indians, who sold the area to colonists in one six four three . While the barrier island was used by baymen and farmers for fishing and harvesting salt hay, no one lived there year-round for more than two centuries, until Congress established a lifesaving station in one eight four nine . A dozen years before, six two people died when the barque ''Mexico'' carrying Irish immigrants to New York ran ashore on New Year's Day.

The first attempt to develop the island as a resort was organized by Austin Corbin, a builder from Brooklyn. He formed a partnership with the Long Island Rail Road to finance the New York and Long Beach Railroad Co which laid track from Lynbrook to Long Beach in one eight eight zero . The company also opened the one , one zero zero -foot-long Long Beach Hotel, at the time the largest in the world. The railroad brought three zero zero , zero zero zero visitors the first season. By the next spring, tracks had been laid the length of the island, but after repeated winter washouts they were removed in one eight nine four .

 The Riviera of the East 
Long Beach boardwalk, c. one nine one one Corbin's development scheme ultimately failed, as did two successive efforts. In one nine zero six , William Reynolds, a three nine -year-old former state senator and real estate developer, entered the picture. Reynolds had already developed four Brooklyn neighborhoods (Bedford-Stuyvesant, Borough Park, Bensonhurst and South Brownsville) and Coney Island's Dreamland, the world's largest amusement park. Reynolds, who also owned a theater and produced plays, gathered investors and acquired the oceanfront from its private owners and the rest of the island from the Town of Hempstead in one nine zero seven so he could build a boardwalk, homes and hotels.

Reynolds had a herd of elephants march in from Dreamland, ostensibly to help build the boardwalk, but in reality it was just a publicity stunt. Dredges created a channel one , zero zero zero feet wide on the north side of the island so Reynolds could bring in large steamboats and even seaplanes to carry more visitors. The new waterway was named, naturally, Reynolds Channel.

Crowded beach, c. one nine two three 

To ensure that Long Beach lived up to Reynolds' billing as 'The Riviera of the East', he required every building to be constructed in an eclectic Mediterranean style with white stucco walls and red tile roofs. And they could be occupied only by white Anglo-Saxon Protestants. After Reynolds' corporation went bankrupt in one nine one eight , these restrictions were lifted and Long Beach became a melting pot filled by immigrants from overseas.

The new town attracted wealthy businessmen and entertainers. Before Reynolds' bankruptcy, he built a theater called Castles by the Sea with the largest dance floor in the world for dancers Vernon and Irene Castle. In the one nine four zero s, Jose Ferrer, Zero Mostel, Mae West, and other famous actors performed at local theaters. And Jack Dempsey, Cab Calloway, Humphrey Bogart, Lillian Roth, Rudolph Valentino, Florenz Zigfield, James Cagney and John Barrymore lived in Long Beach decades before anyone heard of Long Beach's most famous modern-day native, Billy Crystal. More recently, singer Joan Jett, and New York Yankees shortstop Derek Jeter have lived in the city.

Corruption and scandal
In one nine two three , the world-famous Prohibition agents known simply as Izzy and Moe raided the Nassau Hotel and arrested three men for bootlegging. In one nine three zero , five city police officers were charged with offering a bribe to a United States Coast Guard officer to allow liquor to be landed. The police had another problem a year later: a mystery that captivated the nation in the summer of one nine three one . A beachcomber found the body of a beautiful young woman named Starr Faithfull. She had left behind a suicide note, but others believed she had been murdered.

Official corruption had become almost a regular feature of life in Long Beach. In one nine two two , the state Legislature designated Long Beach a city and Reynolds was elected the first mayor. He was promptly indicted on charges of misappropriating funds. When he was found guilty, the clock in the tower at city hall was stopped in protest. When a judge released Reynolds from jail later that year on appeal, almost the entire population turned out to greet him. And the clock was turned back on.

In one nine three nine , Mayor Louis F. Edwards was fatally shot by a police officer on the front steps of his home. Officer Alvin Dooley, a member of the police motorcycle squad and the mayor's own security detail, killed the mayor after losing his bid for PBA president to a candidate the mayor supported. Jackson Boulevard was later renamed Edwards Boulevard in honor of the late mayor.

After the murder, the city turned to a mayorless city manager system, which still exists to this day.

Urban decay and renewal
By the one nine four zero s and one nine five zero s, with the advent of cheap air travel and air-conditioning, Long Beach had become a primarily bedroom community for New York City, although there was a significant summer population increase into the one nine seven zero s. The rundown boardwalk hotels became old-age homes, until a scandal around one nine seven zero led to many of the homes losing licenses. At that time, patients released from mental hospitals were warehoused in the hotels.

The boardwalk had a small amusement park until the mid one nine seven zero s. In the late one nine six zero s, the boardwalk and amusement park area were a magnet for youth from around Long Island, until a police crack down on drug trafficking ended that. Today, while there are few businesses left, the boardwalk is full of bikers, joggers, walkers and people-watchers.

Beginning in the one nine eight zero s and accelerating in the one nine nine zero s, Long Beach has begun an urban renewal, with new housing, new businesses and other improvements. Today, the city is again a popular bedroom community for people working in New York, attracted by the quiet beach atmosphere and the easy, four zero -minute train commute.

Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of five . two km ( two . zero mi ).

The city is located on a barrier island off the south shore of Long Island. The city fronts on the Atlantic Ocean.

Cultural and literary references
''The Godfather'' takes place partly in Long Beach and nearby Atlantic Beach, where Sonny lives. He is murdered at the toll booths on the highway leaving Atlantic Beach. (Mafia members were widely known to live in Long Beach and neighboring Atlantic Beach throughout the mid- two zero th century.)
John Dos Passos' ''The Big Money'' mentions weekends spent in Long Beach in the one nine two zero s.
The two zero zero two movie ''City by the Sea'' starring Robert De Niro, James Franco, and Frances McDormand was inspired by a true story about a murderer from Long Beach. This lad in his two zero s killed someone over the alleged theft of a few bagels. Ironically, the murderer's grandfather had committed a kidnapping in one nine five nine that led to an accidental death while his dad was a highly decorated police detective. The film was based on a fictional interpretation of Long Beach and was filmed in Asbury Park, New Jersey.

'''Deathrock''' (also spelt '''death rock''') can refer to either one . the name given to an offshoot of punk rock which incorporates the imagery and themes of horror movies and first appeared in and around Los Angeles, United States during the late one nine seven zero s and early one nine eight zero s, two . a synonym for first generation gothic rock; three . the label applied to modern (post- one nine nine zero ) Deathrock bands which have a stronger post-punk influence than the earlier Deathrock bands; or four . the subculture surrounding the modern Deathrock music scene.

Origins of Deathrock
Etymology of Deathrock
The origin of the term 'deathrock' can be traced back to the one nine five zero s when it was used to describe a genre of rock and roll called death rock . This death rock genre began in one nine five eight with Jody Reynold's Endless Sleep  and ended in one nine six four with J. Frank Wilson's ''The Last Kiss'' . In these songs, teenagers sang about the tragic deaths of their boyfriends or girlfriends from accidents, suicides, illnesses, etc. The Shangri-Las' ''Leader Of The Pack'' is arguably the best known example of one nine five zero s style death rock , but other well known songs from this era would include Mark Dinning's ''Teen Angel'' and Ray Peterson's ''Tell Laura I Love Her'' . These early death rock songs were generally more serious, introspective and romantic in nature than the novelty songs of this era which humorously dealt with encounters with vampires, monsters, werewolves, etc.

Exactly when the term deathrock re-emerged is unclear; it was being used as early as one nine seven nine to describe the sound of various bands which would later become associated with the deathrock scene. Mark Splatter of deathrock.com attributes it to Rozz Williams , although some attribute it to the lyrics from the one nine seven nine Misfit's song All Hell Breaks Loose ( And broken bodies in a death rock dance hall ) , while still others attribute the term to a label applied by the media to describe Los Angeles based Punk bands obsessed with spooky imagery and death, in much the same manner as positive punk was used by the media to describe the early Batcave sound in the U.K. In any event, the term deathrock appears to have first caught hold in the West Coast of the United States then spread outward from there. 

The term deathrock was used interchangeably with gothic rock until sometime during the mid one nine nine zero s when eventually deathrock as a label fell out of vogue and was seldom used except in reference to the Los Angeles bands four five Grave and Christian Death.

Earliest influences on Deathrock
While the aforementioned death rock songs of the Shangri-Las, Mark Dinning, Ray Peterson, etc. helped to initially establish some of the themes (death, grief, loss, tragedy, etc.) which would become associated with Deathrock, both the sound and visuals of Deathrock were perhaps more influenced by the less serious late one nine five zero searly one nine six zero s novelty music acts such as Bobby Boris Pickett with the ''Monster Mash'' and Screamin' Jay Hawkins with ''I Put a Spell on You'' in the United States, and Screaming Lord Sutch  they were simply considered a darker flavor of PunkHardcore or maybe even Horror Punk. These bands would play at the same venues as other Punk, Hardcore and New Wave bands and were not considered part of a separate music scene .

A one nine eight one review of the Veil, a Los Angeles club catering to a gothic clientele, indicates that downtown art types may have also been an indirect influence on the deathrock scene by supporting clubs where Deathrock and Gothic Rock were played . Unlike some of the sub-genres of Punk, many Deathrock songs have a strong strong dance beat. The lyrics of the Dead Milkmen's one nine eight seven satirical song Instant Club Hit (You'll Dance to Anything)  supports the notion that art school students continued to be some of the more enthusiastic supporters of the Deathrock and Gothic Rock club scenes through the one nine eight zero s.

A parallel development in the UK: The Batcave in London
Around the same time as deathrock was emerging as a distinctive subgenre of punk and early hardcore punk in the United States, another extremely similar subgenre of punk and post-punk was developing independently in the UK . The main focal point for this emerging UK scene was a London club called the Batcave .

Initially, the Batcave was envisioned as a club which would specialize in darker Glam and Post-Punk musical acts . However, several of the bands that debuted and frequently performed at the Batcave, Specimen, Alien Sex Fiend and Sex Gang Children , were also strongly influenced by horror in British pop culture and they developed their own campy horror sound which set them apart from the glam and post-punk scenes in Britain . Initially, this new Batcave inspired sound was referred to as positive punk, but this term positive punk quickly gave way to gothic rock .

The merger and formation of Gothic Rock
In early one nine eight three , the Batcave scene in the UK was had acquired the label positive punk , but in less than a year it had changed to goth and gothic . In one nine eight three , The Gun Club began touring in Europe as did Christian Death which meant the European and American deathrock scenes began to influence one another. Two years later in one nine eight five , deathrock band Kommunity FK began touring with the Batcave band Alien Sex Fiend which continued this trend. Around this point in time, deathrock and goth merged with one another and evolved into gothic rock . Eventually, the term 'gothic rock' replaced deathrock, which Rozz Williams attributes to the influence of the Sisters of Mercy . 

The mid one nine eight zero s also marked the second wave of Gothic Rock which is when the influence of Post-Punk began to wane and be replaced with a more serious and more rock oriented approach . The tempo of the Gothic Rock gradually slowed down and become more mechanical from the widespread use of drum machines instead of live drummers . Also, the growing influence of atonal lead vocals would replace the more Punk and Post-Punk styled vocals. This shift in sound was largely due to the influence of The Sisters of Mercy .

During the third wave of gothic rock in the mid one nine nine zero s, the music would begin to incorporate many elements of the harsher, factory inspired sound of industrial music and the more repetitive and electronic sounds of EBM and electro-industrial while losing some of the remaining introspection and romanticism inherent in first and second waves gothic rock. Some goth clubs even dropped gothic rock from their setlists and instead focused on alternative electronic music (EBM, futurepop, darkwave, power noise, etc.) to appeal to a crossover crowd . These changes alienated many in the goth scene who preferred the livelier, punkier deathrock and Batcave sound . Their growing dissatisfaction with the new direction of gothic rock and the club scene led some to seek out their earlier deathrockBatcave roots .

(For a more complete description of two nd and three rd generation Goth, see the gothic rock article.)

Influential Deathrock artists

Rozz Williams
Christian Death's one nine eight two debut album, ''Only Theatre Of Pain'' is widely held by many as the first purely deathrock album which could not be easily classified as either a darker flavor of punk (as with T.S.O.L or the Damned), horror punk (as with four five Grave or Voodoo Church), or post-punk (as with Bauhaus or Joy Division). As a result, Rozz Williams, the lead singer of Christian Death, Shadow Project and Premature Ejaculation, is considered by many as one of the single most influential musicians in the deathrock scene.

Dinah Cancer
In the one nine eight zero s, Dinah Cancer has been referred to as the Queen of Deathrock, the Goddess of Deathrock and the High Priestess of Deathrock for her role as the front woman for four five Grave during a time when female lead singers were still considered somewhat of a rarity. She eschewed the more pretty gothic look for one more horror inspired, and emphasized the more fun side of death as opposed to the more serious and sensual gothic side.  

Other artists
However, this is not to imply that Los Angeles were solely responsible for the formation of the deathrock sound; many bands in the United States released EPs and LPs prior to one nine eight two which would now be considered deathrock. Also British bands made major contributions to the sound by adding a strong post-punk influence, including Joy Division, Bauhaus, Siouxsie  experimentation with unusual sounds. Lyrics are normally introspective and angsty, and deal with the dark themes of isolation, irony, disillusionment, loss, death, etc. which are designed to strike an emotional cord with the listener, but his places greater demands on the lead vocalist to convey complex emotions. Lead singers have strong, distinctive or unusual voices in order to stand out from the heavily atmospheric and rhythmic music. While the songs have a four four beat to encourage dancing, the heavy emphasis on mood means that Deathrock DJs spin their music to match moods instead of matching beats as do techno musicTechno DJs do. Abrupt shifts in the mood of the songs caused by inexperienced DJs frequently leads to Deathrockers leaving the dancefloor.

Modern deathrock scene
The current deathrock scene is similar to the original deathrock scene in Los Angeles and the Batcave scene in London . In addition to clubs, the current scene is centered around concerts, special events, parties, and horror movie screenings. The internet is playing a major role in the Death Rock revival. There are websites devoted to the discussion deathrock music, bands and fashions as well as horror movies, such as deathrock.com and post-punk.com, plus mailing lists for deathrockers on Yahoo! and on-line virtual communities on LiveJournal and MySpace.

In contrast to the early deathrock scene, the current scene has four additional influences which didn't exist in the late one nine seven zero s or early one nine eight zero s.

First, there is the influence of post-punk and glam which came from Batcave bands such as Specimen, Sex Gang Children, Alien Sex Fiend, etc. Their influence on deathrock has caused a shift in sound away from away from early hardcore punk towards a more post-punk sound. Some of the darker songs from modern post-punk revival bands being occassionally played in deathrock clubs.

Second, there is the influence of psychobilly (another music fusion genre of horror and Punk) which is noted for being strongly apolitical. This influence has discouraged political debates which have the potential to fragment the scene. And the Drop Dead Festival, featuring several days of about six zero bands with psychobilly and deathrock bands is similar to psychobilly's Hootenanny.

Third, there is a more serious horror movie influence on deathrock, based in part on fewer unintentionaly campy horror movies being made, plus the increasing availability of horror movie film scores through CDs and legal online music download. Deathrockers also frequently participate on internet discussion forums and mailing lists for horror fans, and many deathrock discussion forums have separate sections specifically for horror movies.)

Fourth, and perhaps most importantly, there now exists the influence of older deathrockers still active in the scene on a new generation of deathrockers. A significant percentage of modern deathrockers were part of the deathrock scene in the one nine eight zero s and are now in their three zero s or four zero s. Members of the original deathrock scene did not have the benefit of a group of 'elders' to pass on the oral history of music and the traditions of the scene. 

As the modern goth scene continues to drift further away from its punk roots under the influences of alternative electronic music, gothic metal, shock rock, BDSM and fetishism, an increasing number of new deathrock bands and clubs are appearing as a reaction against this trend . Cinema Strange, Bloody Dead and Sexy, The Brides, The Vanishing, Bella Morte and Devilish Presley are popular modern deathrock bands, while Release the Bats in Long Beach, CA; Funeral in Pomona, CA; the Asylum in San Francisco, CA; Kiss Kiss Bang Bang in Melbourne, Australia; Dead and Buried in London, UK; Pagan Love Songs in Bochum, Germany; Onderstroom in Nijmegen, Netherlands and The Wake in Nottingham, UK remain popular deathrock clubs.

Deathrock compared to other subgenres

Deathrock synonyms
Deathrock probably has more synonyms than any of the other subgenres of punk, and they help illustrate it's similarities and differences to these other punk related subgenres. These synonyms include the one nine eight zero s terms death dunk, gothic punk, goth punk, horror rock, splatter rock, creepy rock and roll, spooky rock and roll, positive punk, Batcaver, PIB (Person in Black), and monochromatic punk; the one nine nine zero s terms punky-goth, gothic punk, old school goth, ' eight zero s goth and new grave; as well as the two zero zero zero s terms dark post-punk and dark dance punk.

Horror Punk is sometimes used as a synonym for Deathrock though in reality it is a different (though closely related) fusion sub-genre of Punk.

Deathrock or horror punk?
Deathrock and horror punk, because of the overlap which exists between these two subgenres' sense of fashion, musical preferences and bands, are sometimes so similar as to confuse members of both musical subcultures. Generally speaking, horror punk is considered louder, faster and closer to early Punk and early Hardcore Punk as well as less introspective and romantic than deathrock. Conversely, deathrock is considered more serious, moody and Post Punk influenced than horror punk. Keyboards are another differentiating point: deathrock bands frequently use keyboards (mainly for atmosphere) whereas Horror Punk band do not. 

(From a more humorous perspective, deathrock bands do not use whoas in their choruses, frequently use the word spooky to describe their music, and prefer Deathhawks over Devilocks .)

What deathrock is not
Despite the similar sounding names, deathrock has very little in common with the similarly named death metal, a subgenre of heavy metal.

Additionally, Deathrock should not be confused with shock rock. Deathrockers and Deathrock bands do not deliberately seek to shock others or cause controversy; their fashion choices are generally done in a playful, tongue in cheek manner. However, as it has been previously noted, Deathrock was influenced by earlier shock rockers such as Screamin' Jay Hawkins and Alice Cooper.

 '''New Hyde Park''' is a village located in Nassau County, New York, USA.
As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of nine , five two three . 

The '''Village of New Hyde Park''' is in both the Town of Hempstead and the Town of North Hempstead. 

 History 

The village was incorporated in one nine two seven .

'''The Origins of New Hyde Park'''

Hyde Park, as this area was formerly called, is one of the oldest and most historic settlements in the United States. The first settlers were Dutch and English. The Dutch came first to New York, then called New Amsterdam, shortly after one six two four . The English crossed Long Island Sound in one six four four to the Town of Hempstead of which this area was a part.
The original records kept by these settlers of their Town meeting are preserved in the office of the Town Clerk of The Town of North Hempstead. They are among the oldest records of local government in America.
Thomas Dongan, Royal Colonial Governor of New York in one six eight three , lived here on a large estate, Success Pond, now known as Lake Success and Lakeville Road. The Towns of Hempstead and Flushing granted the property to him. Governor Dongan is credited with devising the County system of governmental division for New York.
His estate, Dongan Manor, came into the ownership of George Clark, Secretary of the Province. Clark's wife, Anne Hyde, had grown up on her family estate in England called Hyde Hall, and Clark renamed Dongan Estate Hyde Park, perpetuating Mrs. Clark's family name.
More than three hundred years ago, shortly after the English gained dominion from the Dutch over a vast area including Long Island, Richard Nicolls, Governor of the Province of New York, chose the open grounds of the Salisbury Plain to establish a racecourse. A first in the colonies, the course was called Newmarket and was located just to the south of the present New Hyde Park Rail Road Station. Many of the participants and spectators may well have traveled the ancient road we call Jericho Turnpike.
Instituted originally as an annual event, with a silver cup awarded to the winner, the purpose of racing competition was ostensibly to improve the breed. (Later historians reflected that this lofty assertion continued to be used to justify the practice of horse racing.) A porringer, dated one six six eight , is reputed to have been the prize at one of these first contests at Newmarket, and is the earliest piece of dated silver still in existence, which was made in the colonies.
Waves of immigrants arrived in America and many came to labor on the farms of Long Island. They worked, saved, and raised families. Most were deeply religious.
The first New Hyde Park settlers were of English and Dutch descent, followed by the Germans, Irish, Polish and Italians. In the one nine zero zero 's Jewish families came to this area.
Thus, we have an amalgam of ethnic backgrounds in our community.
With improved farming methods, the plains became excellent farming territory. Jericho Turnpike opened as a plank toll road to New York City for carrying produce to the market. The Long Island Railroad came through New Hyde Park in one eight three seven , but for years there was nothing to justify a station there. In the mid-nineteenth century, Irish and German immigrants began to buy farms in the area. Anton Herkomer, a weaver, operated his looms at the northeast comer of Miller's Lane and the Long Island Railroad. This was within the limits of the Incorporated Village of New Hyde Park, as later constituted. At that time, the Village had only four houses on the Turnpike, plus a scattering of farms in the open fields.
At the end of the Civil War, two young immigrants from Seilsheim, Germany, John C. Christ and Philip J. Miller arrived in New York to make their fortunes. Miller was a coppersmith and Christ a machinist.
Anton Herkomer had to go to New York to have special parts made for his looms and he discovered that Christ could make them perfectly. Anton Herkomer convinced him to leave the shop where he worked and move to New Hyde Park. Christ  four three ' five six  North, seven three  four one ' five  West ( four zero . seven three two two four one , - seven three . six eight four five nine three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of two . two km ( zero . eight mi ).  two . two km ( zero . eight mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Government 
The Village of New Hyde Park is governed by a Mayor and four trustees, known collectively as the Board of Trustees. They are elected to serve a four year term. The current Mayor is Danial P. Petruccio. The curent board is Deputy Mayor Robert A. Lofaro, Trustee Richard A. Coppola Jr., Trustee Donald Barbieri, and Trustee Lawrence J. Montreuil.

 Education 
New Hyde Park has schools in the Sewanhaka Central High School District, Great Neck School District, and the New Hyde Park-Garden City Park Elementary School District.

 '''North Hempstead''' is a town located in Nassau County, New York, USA. 
As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two two two , six one one .

The '''Town of North Hempstead''' occupies the northwest part of the county. Its Supervisor is Jon Kaiman, a Democrat. 

 History 
The area was first settled around one six four three and became part of the Town of Hempstead. During the American Revolution the south part of the Town of Hempstead was primarily Tory while the north part supported the revolution. Following the war, the Town of North Hempstead was split off in one seven eight four . 

 Geography 
The west town line is the border of Queens County, New York, part of New York City. The north town line, delineated by the Long Island Sound is the border of Bronx County and Westchester County. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one seven nine . zero km ( six nine . one mi ).  one three eight . eight km ( five three . six mi ) of it is land and four zero . two km ( one five . five mi ) of it is water. The total area is two two . four seven % water.

Oceanside is a community in the south part of the Town of Hempstead.

 History 
Oceanside has many historical events. It was founded in one seven eight three and it was first named Christan Hook.  In one eight seven one , it was renamed to Oceanside. In one nine zero two , The Oceanside Fire Department was established. The last farm in the community was on Mann Place; it was destroyed in a fire. 

 Geography 
Oceanside is located at four zero  three eight ' one one  North, seven three  three eight ' one five  West ( four zero . six three six two eight six , - seven three . six three seven four zero four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the community has a total area of one four . zero km ( five . four mi ).  one three . zero km ( five . zero mi ) of it is land and one . zero km ( zero . four mi ) of it is water. The total area is seven . three eight % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are three two , seven three three people, one one , two two four households, and nine , one two five families residing in the area. The population density is two , five one seven . six km ( six , five two three . six mi ). There are one one , three nine six housing units at an average density of eight seven six . five km ( two , two seven one . two mi ). The racial makeup of the CDP is nine four . nine five % White, zero . five six % African American, zero . zero seven % Native American, one . eight three % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, one . five eight % from other races, and one . zero zero % from two or more races.  five . nine zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one one , two two four households out of which three six . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six nine . five % are married couples living together, eight . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and one eight . seven % are non-families. one six . one % of all households are made up of individuals and nine . one % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . nine zero and the average family size is three . two five .

In the community the population is spread out with two five . zero % under the age of one eight , six . one % from one eight to two four , two seven . six % from two five to four four , two five . seven % from four five to six four , and one five . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four zero years. For every one zero zero females there are nine three . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight nine . five males.

The median income for a household in the community is $ seven five , seven one nine , and the median income for a family is $ eight three , seven one one . Males have a median income of $ five five , six five two versus $ four zero , one six three for females. The per capita income for the CDP is $ three zero , two four five .  three . five % of the population and two . eight % of families are below the poverty line.  Education 
The Oceanside School District is made up of nine schools, including one kindergarten, six elementary schools, one middle school, one high school and an alternative high school. Herb Brown is the Superintendent of Schools and has held that position since one nine nine seven , where he replaced Eliot Garfinkel.

Nearby Colleges include: Adelphi, Nassau Community College, Molloy College, Hofstra University, New York Institute of Technology and C. W. Post College. 

 Politics 
Oceanside is part of the Fourth District of New York and is represented by Congresswoman Carolyn McCarthy.

 '''Old Bethpage''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in the town of Oyster Bay, Nassau County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of five , four zero zero . Its ZIP code is one one eight zero four . 

Old Bethpage and its neighboring hamlet, Plainview, share a school system, fire department and water district. Law enforcement for the community is provided by the Nassau County Police Department's Eighth Precinct.
 

 History 
Before one nine three six Old Bethpage was known simply as Bethpage, until a larger adjacent hamlet changed its name from Central Park to Bethpage.

Old Bethpage is home to the world famous Old Bethpage Village Restoration.

 Geography 
Old Bethpage is located at four zero  four five ' four three  North, seven three  two seven ' one six  West ( four zero . seven six one eight one nine , - seven three . four five four five four four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one zero . seven km ( four . one mi ).  one zero . seven km ( four . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

It's considered Mid-Island by locals due to it's location on Long Island.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are five , four zero zero people, one , eight three four households, and one , five five seven families residing in the CDP. The population density is five zero six . one km ( one , three one one . four mi ). There are one , eight four three housing units at an average density of one seven two . seven km ( four four seven . six mi ). The racial makeup of the CDP is nine four . five seven % White, one . one nine % African American, zero . zero four % Native American, two . nine four % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . three five % from other races, and zero . nine one % from two or more races.  one . nine three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , eight three four households out of which three eight . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven five . six % are married couples living together, seven . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and one five . one % are non-families. one three . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and one zero . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight eight and the average family size is three . one six .

In the CDP the population is spread out with two four . two % under the age of one eight , five . five % from one eight to two four , two seven . one % from two five to four four , two five . one % from four five to six four , and one eight . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four one years. For every one zero zero females there are nine one . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . five males.

 Trivia 
Actor John Savage was born in Old Bethpage.

Portions of the Long Island Motor Parkway ran through Old Bethpage. Street names such as Vanderbilt Lane , Motor Parkway and Toll Place serve as reminders. Segments of the old roadbed and some bridges can still be seen in some places. For example, in Battle Row Campground, Bethpage State Park, and the Old Bethpage Village Restoration.

 School System 
The Plainview- Old Bethpage Central school district contains one high school named Plainview-Old Bethpage John F. Kennedy High School, two middle schools named Howard B. Appearances in literature and motion pictures

F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel ''The Great Gatsby'' is set in the fictional East Egg and West Egg Villages, which are thinly-disguised versions of, respectively, Port Washington and Great Neck. The novel portrays East Egg (Port Washington) as a posh, wealthy place of old money. 

Parts of the two zero zero zero film ''Meet the Parents'' were filmed in this town, featuring a local restaurant, Louie's, located on Main Street in downtown Port Washington, and a local drugstore. Though the interior scenes were shot inside the drugstore, the exterior was that of the neighboring supermarket (now closed.)

 '''Rockville Centre''' is a village located in New York's Nassau County in the United States. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two four , five six eight . 

The '''Village of Rockville Centre''' is inside the southwest part of the Town of Hempstead. 

It is home to Molloy College and the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Rockville Centre. 

The village ( RVC to its residents) claims to have the highest ratio of restaurants per-capita in the United States. 

 History 
The village was settled in the one seven th Century as New Rockaway. 
The village was incorporated in one eight nine three . 

 Geography 
Rockville Centre is located at four zero  three nine ' four eight  North, seven three  three eight ' one three  West ( four zero . six six three three nine zero , - seven three . six three six eight three one ).

 '''Uniondale''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Nassau County, New York (Long Island), United States. It is part of the Town of Hempstead, one of three towns (along with North Hempstead and Oyster Bay) that make up Nassau County. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two three , zero one one .

Uniondale is one of the few African-American majority neighborhoods on Long Island, although it is a more middle class community than neighboring Hempstead.

The racial makeup Uniondale is two six . nine seven % White, five five . five three % African American, zero . three five % Native American, two . one zero % Asian, zero . zero eight % Pacific Islander, nine . nine five % from other races, and five . zero one % from two or more races.  two two . eight six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.  Landmarks, Attractions 
Uniondale is home to the NHL's New York Islanders and the New York Dragons of the AFL, both of whom play at the Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum. It is also home to the Mitchel Athletic Complex which hosts the Long Island Rough Riders, a pro soccer team, and the Major League Lacrosse's Long Island Lizards

 Music 
Uniondale is home to The Leaders of the New School, an early hip-hop group with ties to the infamous Public Enemy. Busta Rhymes, known most notably for his solo projects, was the only member of The Leaders of the New School to launch a successful solo career. Rapper Joey Batts, born and raised in Uniondale, currently residing in Hartford, Connecticut, is one of two frontmen (the other being Matt Zigs) that front the eight piece hip-hop band ZBC, The Zigs and Batts Circus.

 Cargolux Boeing seven four seven - four zero zero F
'''Cargolux''' (Cargolux Airlines International) is a cargo airline based in Luxembourg. It is one of the largest scheduled all-cargo airlines in Europe with a global network. Charter flights and third party maintenance are also operated. Its main base is Luxembourg-Findel Airport.

 Code Data 

IATA Code: '''CV'''
ICAO Code: '''CLX'''
Callsign: Cargolux

 History 

The airline was established in March one nine seven zero by Luxair, the Salen Shipping Group, Loftleidir Icelandic and various private interests in Luxembourg. It started operations in May one nine seven zero with one Canadair CL- four four freighter with services from Luxembourg to Hong Kong.

Over the next two years, the airline grew, as did their public visibility. In one nine seven three , Cargolux had five Canadair CL- four four 's and made the leap into the jet age by acquiring a Douglas DC- eight jet. This enabled the company to speed up their cargo deliveries. In one nine seven four , Loftleidir Icelandic and Cargolux joined their maintenance and engineering departments together, and by one nine seven five , Cargolux enjoyed the new facilities of new central offices and two plane hangars.

In one nine seven eight the airline began to take shape into the company it is today. The Canadair CL- four four 's began to be retired and the airline ordered its first Boeing seven four seven s. In that same year they also began flying to other places in Asia, as well as to the United States. In one nine seven nine , as the company concluded its first decade, their first Boeing seven four seven 's were delivered.

In one nine eight two , China Airlines became the first airline company to sign a strategic alliance with Cargolux. one nine eight three saw the introduction of ''CHAMPS'' ('''C'''argo '''H'''andling '''A'''nd '''M'''anagement '''P'''lanning) and the start of some charter passenger flights for the Hajj pilgrimage.

 one nine eight four saw the departure of the last Douglas DC- eight in the fleet and the addition of a third Boeing seven four seven . Lufthansa bought a two four . five % share of the airline in one nine eight seven and Luxair increased their share to two four . five three %. 

 one nine eight eight saw the birth of Lion Air, a passenger charter airline that was set up by both Cargolux and Luxair. The airline had two Boeing seven four seven jets but Cargolux's venture into the charter airline world prove unsuccessful and soon Lion Air folded. 

Despite that setback, Cargolux made it into the one nine nine zero 's in proper financial shape. They added two more Boeing seven four seven 's in one nine nine zero , as a way of celebrating their two zero th anniversary, and in one nine nine three , three Boeing seven four seven - four zero zero F's (F is for Freighter) arrived at Luxembourg. one nine nine five saw Cargolux have a year round celebration because of its two five th anniversary and Heiner Wilkens was named CEO and President. 

In one nine nine seven Luxair was able to increase their share to three four %, while in September one nine nine seven Lufthansa sold their two four . five % to Sair Logistics and Swiss Cargo made a cooperation agreement with the Luxembourg company. one nine nine eight saw Sair Logistics increase their share to three three %.

By one nine nine nine Cargolux's fleet had reached double figures, with ten Boeing seven four seven s. In two zero zero zero a route was opened to Seoul, South Korea, and in two zero zero one Wilkens decided to step down as President and CEO of the air company. 

The airline is owned by Luxair ( three four . nine %), SAirGroup ( three three . seven %), Luxembourg Financial Corporations ( three one . one %) and other shareholders ( zero . three %) (at January two zero zero five ).

 Incidents and accidents 
In January two zero zero six , the nose gear of a plane in park position was accidentally retracted. Nobody was injured. The incident occurred at Shanghai Pudong airport.

 Services 

Cargolux operates freight services to the following international destinations (at January two zero zero five ): Abidjan, Abu Dhabi, Accra, Auckland, Baku, Bangkok, Barbados, Barcelona, Beirut, Bogot, Budapest, Calgary, Chennai, Chicago, Curitiba, Damascus, Dubai, Glasgow, Guadalajara, Helsinki, Hong Kong, Houston, Huntsville, Istanbul, Johannesburg, Karachi, Kinshasa, Komatsu, Kuala Lumpur, Kuwait, Lagos, Latacunga, Los Angeles, Lusaka, Maastricht, Manila, Melbourne, Mexico City, Milan, Nairobi, New York, Panama City, Rio de Janeiro, San Francisco, Santiago, So Paulo, Seattle, Seoul, Shanghai, Sharjah, Singapore, Taipei, Tehran.

 Fleet 

The Cargolux fleet consists of one four Boeing seven four seven - four zero zero F aircraft (at November two zero zero five ).

November one six th, two zero zero five : Cargolux, based in Luxembourg, has ordered one zero  seven four seven - eight Freighters and will take delivery of the first seven four seven - eight F in third-quarter two zero zero nine . It also holds purchase rights for one zero additional airplanes.

 '''Upper Brookville''' is a village located in Nassau County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , eight zero one . 

The '''Village of Upper Brookville''' is inside the Town of Oyster Bay. 
The village was named for the brook that used to run along the main road, Wolver Hollow. Although the village is physically lower than the surrounding area, its wealthy residents did not want to live in Lower Brookville, and so named it Upper Brookville instead.

Westbury is a very diverse community, made up of Italian-Americans, African-Americans and Hispanics, mostly immigrants from El Salvador. 

 History 
The first settlers arrived in one six five eight in this region known as Hempstead Plains . Many of the early settlers were Quakers. The village was incorporated in one nine three three .

For example, the world-famous Westbury Music Fair performing venue (now known as the North Fork Theatre at Westbury), located in the Westbury postal zone, is part of the Jericho hamlet.

 '''Cambria''' is a town located in Niagara County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of five , three nine three . Cambria is an early name for Wales.

The '''Town of Cambria''' is in the center of Niagara County.

 History 
The Town of Cambria was established in one eight zero eight when Niagara county was formed. Cambria was the original town of Niagara County; all other towns were formed from its territory after one eight one two . 

When Genesee County, New York was formed in one eight zero two , all of Niagara County was included and was part of the Town of Batavia. Subsequently Erie County was created by removing the Towns of '''Willink''' and Clarence, both towns having been created from Cambria in Niagara County. 

 Geography

 '''Gasport''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in the Town of Royalton in Niagara County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the community had a total population of one , two four eight . The name is derived from observed natural gas and the historic Erie Canal port at that location. 

 History 

On May one eight , one eight two six , a geological expedition, led by Amos Eaton and physicist Joseph Henry of the Rensselaerian School (now Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute) through the western part of New York state aboard the canal boat LaFayette, encountered flammable coal gas rising from a spring. They named the local community Gasport. On the return voyage, May two six th, they passed through the settlement again, and saw that the name was already appearing on signboards.
