 '''Public Image Ltd.''' ('''PiL''') is a rock music band formed in one nine seven eight by John Lydon, also known as Johnny Rotten of the Sex Pistols. PiL is often cited as one of the most challenging and innovative bands of the post punk period. 

Early career
Following the Sex Pistols' breakup, Lydon took a three-week trip to Jamaica with Virgin Records head Richard Branson, in which Lydon helped scout for new reggae artists. 

After this vacation, Lydon approached Jah Wobble (n John Wardle) to start a new band. The pairing seemed natural: they had been friends since the early one nine seven zero s, and had casually played music together during the last days of the Sex Pistols. Furthermore, they were both avid fans of reggae, and of what would later be called world music. Lydon assumed, much as with his friend Sid Vicious - the Sex Pistols' mid-career replacement for original bassist Glen Matlock - that Wobble could learn to play bass guitar as he went. While that had proven a fatal assumption with Vicious (Lydon cites his inability to learn his instrument as a prime reason for the Pistols' breakup), Wobble would prove to be a natural talent. Lydon also launched an effort to locate guitarist Keith Levene (n Julian Levene), whom he had met on tour in mid- one nine seven six while Levene was a member of The Clash. Lydon and Levene had both considered themselves outsiders even within their own bands. After Levene heard of the invitation, he quickly signed on. The original drummer was Jim Walker (n Donat Walker) - a Canadian student newly arrived in the UK - who answered an ad in a weekly music magazine. 

PiL debuted with Public Image, a single not far from Sex Pistols territory. The single sold well enough to reach number nine in the UK charts, and surprisingly well as an import in the US, where the mainstream rock culture of the time was strongly resistant to edginess or innovation.

First album
In preparing the album, ''First Issue'', they ran through their recording budget well before finishing (drugs were a significant expense), and ended up with eight tracks of varying sound quality, half of which were written and recorded in a last-minute fire drill. Wobble had also beaten up producer Bill Price's assistant engineer (Price, with John Leckie, had secured the tight sound of the Public Image single), inciting Price to ban the group from their preferred Wessex Studios, and forcing them to scramble for another venue and soundman as deadlines loomed and passed. 

The album, however, was groundbreaking: scabrous and dirge-like, but lyrical by turn, 'Gothic' before the term was coined, and grounded in heavy dub reggae. Wobble's bass tone was called impossibly deep by contemporary reviews, and Levene's uniquely sharp guitar sound (Levene played an all-aluminum Veleno guitar, and a mostly-aluminum Travis Bean Wedge) was widely imitated, most notably by The Edge of the then-fledgling U two and Geordie of Killing Joke. Lydon's vocals were more tuneless and incantatory than in the Sex Pistols, gesturing toward the avant-garde territory of such artists as Yoko Ono. Despite being widely criticised in the UK press for being ''self indulgent'' and ''not rock'n'roll'', the first album did sell well in the UK and Europe reaching number two two in the UK charts.

Metal Box
 one nine seven nine 's ''Metal Box'' was a more focused effort, although created, like ''First Issue'', under notably unfocused circumstances. In addition to the drugs and disorganization that were the normal condition of the band, Jim Walker had quit from general disillusionment, making way for a series of exploding drummers -- in one case literally, when Wobble set fire to the aptly-named Karl Burns. Sessions took place in which a star-struck young drummer would show up for an 'audition' and be stunned to discover himself in the middle of a recording date with the tape rolling. 

''Metal Box'' was originally released as three untitled four five rpm one two -inch records packaged in a metal film canister (it was later reissued as a double LP set, ''Second Edition''), and features the band's trademark hypnotic dub reggae bass lines, glassy, arpeggiated guitar, and bleak, paranoid, stream of consciousness vocals. ''Metal Box'' is starker than ''First Issue'', more spread out and uncompromising, and scattered with bits of ambient synthesizer. It is now widely regarded as a classic record, both for its music and its sheer tonality (the four five rpm one two  format added depth and fidelity to what was already a highly tactile, spacious sound), and it sold quite well upon release, and for years afterward. But with ''Metal Box'', PiL was no longer operating as a standard rock band, but was entering a different territory altogether. 

One critic wrote, they sounded nothing like the Pistols or anyone else at the time. . In fact, although radically different from other British and American rock groups, PiL was heavily influenced by German experimental rock, or Krautrock, especially by Can, Neu!, and the sonic aesthetic of producer Conny Plank. Hallmarks of the genre include minimalism, classically-inspired ambient or atonal leanings, via Stockhausen, and an abandonment of traditional song form in favor of long, slowly-unfolding compositions. 

The teenage dance show ''American Bandstand'' was, circa one nine eight zero , entirely innocent of such things, with a history beginning with the likes of Frankie Avalon and extending to the mild end of ' seven zero s pop-rock. PiL's booking there revealed a latent fiendish streak in host Dick Clark. The band mimed to the bleak soundscapes of Poptones and Careering, from ''Metal Box'', with Lydon haranguing the cameramen and making no effort to conceal that he was lip-synching. The studio audience made a valiant, but futile attempt to dance and stay in character, ruined by Lydon's good-humored incitements to storm the stage. General chaos broke out, and the show ended with the audience dancing with band members, band members goofing on their instruments, and Lydon chatting with fans while Careering blared on. Clark, in later years, would refer to the appearance as One of the ten best American Bandstand episodes of all time.  

A U.S. tour led to several cancelled dates and (more of the usual) chaos, this time between the band and their U.S. label, Warner Brothers (PiL was on Virgin in the UK). 

Lydon had always been a difficult character to work with, but Levene had begun to challenge his crown, by many reports acting increasingly grandiose and delusional, and by all reports sinking ever-deeper into heroin. Levene was a very small, skinny person, of the sort that one thinks of as 'runty.' Jah Wobble, for his part, was among the rarest of sensitive art-musicians and world-music aficionados in that his habits included assault and battery, setting people on fire, and hurling televisions out of hotel windows. Something had to break, and it was clear that it couldn't be Lydon. Oddly, it was Wobble.  

PiL's elusiveness lent it a thick mystique, but to those behind the curtain it was known as the laziest band in the world -- never rehearsing, rarely gigging (the original band only played five UK shows), and recording only when forced to by frantic record execs. (One exec called PiL a well-oiled machine that burns money and generates pot smoke and excuses. ) When Jim Walker joined, he started hanging out at Lydon's apartment, and noticed that Levene would often call from wherever Levene lived -- presumably miles away, since he never saw him. One evening, moments after a phone exchange, he was astonished to see Levene walk in the door: The guitarist had been living the whole time in the apartment downstairs. He'd never bothered to come up before.  

With that as a ground aesthetic, it's easy to see how an ambitious musician could be frustrated. Wobble had been releasing solo singles since one nine seven eight , and had long been unhappy with the band's relaxed sense of time and lack of ambition. While working on his first solo album, he began using PiL basslines as backing tracks, on the premise that nobody else in the band seemed likely to mind. When Levene found out, it provided fuel for a grudge; and while claims differ as to whether Wobble quit or was fired, the split was decisive. Upon Wobble's departure, the band continued not-playing as a bassless trio.

A show at the Ritz, in New York, signaled a turning point. The band's musical core had by then been stripped down to Lydon and Levene (drummer Martin Atkins had recently exploded), and PiL had begun to relocate to New York, partly because the MI five was conducting a harassment campaign -- later admitted -- against the band's headquarters, the London apartment that Lydon bought with his Sex Pistols royalties. (A similar campaign would chase Throbbing Gristle and Psychic TV frontman Genesis P. Orridge out of Britain in the early ' nine zero s.) Levene had also begun to get big ideas about PiL's formerly-ironic claims to be a 'corporation' and an 'art collective': While friends of the band including filmmaker Jeanette Lee had long been 'full members' of PiL (original drummer Jim Walker was only 'voted off the board' in one nine eight zero ), no creative works besides the records had ever ensued. For the Ritz gig however, Levene decided that PiL would reorganize as an improvisational multimedia troupe -- working, as usual, without planning or rehearsals.  

The band appeared at the Ritz playing from behind a projection screen. (Drummer Sam Ulamo had been recruited for the gig from a bar -- the six zero -year-old jazz player had never heard the band before.) While something reminiscent of, but clearly different from PiL improvised behind the screen, PiL records were played simultaneously through the PA. Lydon taunted the audience, who expected to hear familiar material (or at least see the band), and a melee erupted in which the audience pelted the stage with bottles and pulled on a tarp spread under the band, toppling equipment. The promoters cleared the hall and cancelled the next night's show, and a local media furore ignited in New York. 

An appearance a short time later on NBC's Tom Snyder show had Lydon and Snyder insulting each other on-air. The band soon regrouped, after a fashion, back in London.

Flowers of Romance
Martin Atkins, who had initially joined at the tail end of the ''Metal Box'' sessions (most tracks on that album were played by Richard Dudanski), was re-recruited to drum on ''Flowers of Romance,'' an album considered much stranger and more difficult than the already strange ''Metal Box''. Levene had by then largely abandoned guitar in favor of synthesizer, picking up a technique that was nearly unique, although perhaps owing a debt to Allen Ravenstine of Pere Ubu. Atkins' propulsive marching band-style drumming and Lydon's increasing lyrical abstraction made this LP a difficult listen for rock fans: contemporary reviews expressed great confusion. The record consists mostly of drums, vocals, ''musique concrte'', and tape loops, with only gestures toward bass (played by Levene) and keyboards. Its drum sound was widely copied, notably by Phil Collins and Kate Bush. (Collins admits the deed; Bush went an extra step in buying some of Wobble's 'impossibly deep' ''Metal Box''-era bass equipment the secret is a one nine seven zero s or equivalent Fender Jazz Bass through all-tube Ampeg SVT amplifier, speakers faced toward a solid wall, with mikes arranged to pick up the ambient sound). 

An autographed copy of the one nine eight three ''This Is Not A Love Song'' one two  single

Atkins was, like Levene and Lydon, a control freak in ways, but Levene had the disadvantage of having repeatedly fired Atkins over apparent trifles, and of being zonked on junk much of the time -- so when conflict arose again, Levene was the one to go. An aborted fourth album, from one nine eight two , was later released by Levene as ''Commercial Zone'' which included contributions on bass from Pete Jones. Lydon and Atkins claim that he stole the tapes, while Levene's claim is, in effect, that possession is nine-tenths of the law. Recollections, as usual, differ widely on the particulars, and the album, while considered far superior to the official ''This Is What You Want, This Is What You Get'' that later appeared, has never been legally reissued. Atkins stayed on through a disatrous live album, ''Live in Tokyo'' -- in which PiL consisted of him, Lydon, and a band of New Jersey wedding musicians -- and left in one nine eight five , following the album, ''This Is What You Want, This Is What You Get.'' The band was moving, or perhaps hurtling, toward a more commercial pop music and dance music direction, and while many new fans had found PiL, little of their original audience (or sound) remained.

Compact DiscCassetteAlbum
PiL's one nine eight six release was simply entitled ''Compact Disc'', ''Cassette'', or ''Album'', depending on the format. The cover's blue typeface and spartan design parodied generic brands; promotional photos featured Lydon in a generic blue suit surrounded by generic foods and drinking generic beer. Produced by Bill Laswell (despite Lydon-fuelled faction and disunion) and with many of Laswell's usual rotating cast of musicians, it also featured guitar solos by Steve Vai, considered by Vai as some of his best work. Controversy reared its hoary glower again with claims that the album cover and title concept had been stolen from the San Francisco noisepunk band, Flipper, contemporaries of PiL, whose album, ''Album'', featured a similarly unadorned sleeve. Flipper retaliated by naming their next album, ''Public Flipper Limited''.

Late career
PiL released ''Happy?'' in one nine eight seven , and during the spring of one nine eight eight performed throughout the United States as part of INXS' ''Kick'' tour. In one nine eight nine , PiL toured with New Order and The Sugarcubes as The Monsters of Alternative Rock, an arrangement of disparate alternative bands that predated the Lollapalooza festival by two years. PiL kept going as a Lydon project until one nine nine three , when Lydon disbanded the group. Their final lineup consisted of Lydon, Ted Chau (guitar, keyboards), Mike Joyce of The Smiths (drums), John McGeoch (guitar), and Russel Webb (bass). Notable exploding members of the later PiL include world music multi-instrumentalist (and former Damned guitarist) Lu Edmunds (who left due to tinnitus), ex-Pop Group drummer Bruce Smith, and legendary Cream drummer Ginger Baker, who played on ''Album''. Lydon released a solo album, ''Psycho's Path'', in one nine nine seven . He considers PiL to be on hiatus, and plans a book on his years with the group.

 '''Walden''' is a village located in the Town of Montgomery in Orange County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of six , one six four .

 Geography 
Walden is located at four one  three three ' four one  North, seven four  one one ' two two  West ( four one . five six one two six eight , - seven four . one eight nine four four two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of five . three km ( two . zero mi ).  five . one km ( two . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is three . nine zero % water.
Great Falls and dam with power station, seen here from High Bridge after heavy rainfall in October two zero zero five 
The village is bisected by the Wallkill River. There are two waterfalls and dams on the river within the village limits, known as the Great and Little Falls; and two auto bridges, the High (Route five two ) and Low (Oak Street) bridges).

The average household size is two . seven nine and the average family size is three . two nine .

History
Statue of President McKinley in downtown Walden

The area around present-day Walden was purchased in one seven three six by Alexander Kidd, and settlers of Scots-Irish, English and German descent started arriving not long afterwards. It was the first settlement west of the Wallkill River, known at the time as Kidd's Town.

In the one eight two zero s, a successful New York shipper named Jacob Walden convinced some of his business partners to finance the construction of woolen mills on the river, attracted by the Great Falls as a source of power and the railroad connections at nearby Maybrook. He dammed the Wallkill above the falls, creating a power station that remains in use today, and his mill was a success.

Other wool-makers followed as the Industrial Revolution picked up steam and the growing population center became known instead as Walden's Mills. Most of them failed a few decades later, but their influence was such that the village incorporated in one eight five five as Walden.

The village fathers needed to replace the mills as a source of employment, and began encouraging knife manufacturers to relocate from nearby Dutchess County to the vacant buildings, where the New York Knife Company made much of the cutlery employed by the Union Army during the U.S. Civil War.

After the war, other knifemakers came to Walden, too, and the village became colloquially known as Knifetown. Other industrial concerns, making products as diverse as engines and women's underwear, also set up shop.

In the early one eight nine zero s, President Grover Cleveland lowered tariffs on many imported goods, including knives. Competitively priced German cutlery began to flood the American market, and together with the Panic of one eight nine three and the economic slowdown that followed for several years, the knife companies and their owners went heavily into debt and it looked for a while as if they might not survive.

But in one eight nine seven President William McKinley, a personal friend of Robert Bradley of the U.S. Knife Company, pushed through the Dingleby Tariff that restored the ''status quo ante''. The knifemakers returned to profitability and were able to pay off their debts; and in gratitude Bradley had a statue of McKinley erected that remains in Walden today.

In the one nine one zero s the facilities at the dam began to be primarily used for power and less for industry.

In the late one nine two zero s, one of the largest Ku Klux Klan gatherings outside the South in that era took place outside Walden.

Thruway Markets

The Depression was hard on many of the village's economic concerns, but the knifemakers persisted. However, after World War II they gradually became less prominent and moved as the rail connections they had depended on were replaced by trucking on the growing Interstates. The last company making knives in the village, Imperial Schrade, closed down its factory after a one nine five seven fire and moved to nearby Ellenville afterwards, where it lasted until two zero zero four . The ruins of the factory still stand behind Walden's most visible economic giant, the Thruway Markets retail complex.

Today, Walden retains some light industry and much of its working-class feel, enough for the village to have gotten into a spat with WPDH-FM disc jockey The Wolf in the late one nine nine zero s over his constant joking on- and off-air joking about Walden as a redneck town. However, that atmosphere is changing as new homebuyers take advantage of it being at the outer fringe of the New York metropolitan area and establish more of a bedroom-community commuter lifestyle.

Government

As a village of the Town of Montgomery, Walden residents are taxpayers and electors in both.

The village has seven elected officials, a village board comprised of the mayor and six nonpartisan trustees, as per the New York State Village Law. Most of the executive functions are handled by the village manager, who serves at the board's pleasure.

Walden has had this system of government since one nine six four . A one nine seven two referendum to return to a strong-mayor system was defeated.

The village has its own police force, which provides two four -hour protection for residents; a public works department which maintains roads, water and sewer lines; a recreation department which maintains several parks within the village, including one with a pond in which swimming is permitted; and a village court presided over by an elected justice. Fire protection is provided for the village and surrounding fire district by the Walden Volunteer Fire Department, which has its own elected board of commissioners.

'''West Point''' is a federal military base (and a census-designated place) located in the Town of Highlands in Orange County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the area had a total population of seven , one three eight . The United States Military Academy is located at West Point and is often itself called West Point .

 History 
West Point was a fortified site during the Revolutionary War. General Benedict Arnold attempted to turn over the site to the enemy in one seven eight zero for a bribe. 

On November two nine , one eight nine zero , the U.S. Naval Academy defeated the U.S. Military Academy two four  zero in the first Army-Navy football game.

Location of the United States Military Academy since one eight zero two .

In one nine three seven the West Point Bullion Depository was constructed, in one nine eight eight it became the West Point Mint, as a branch of the United States Mint.

 Geography

West Point and the contiguous village of Highland Falls, New York, are on the west bank of the Hudson River. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are seven , one three eight people, nine nine six households, and nine three nine families residing in the CDP. The population density is one one three . three km ( two nine three . four mi ). There are one , zero four four housing units at an average density of one six . six km ( four two . nine mi ). '''Woodbury''' is a town located in Orange County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of nine , four six zero . The origin of the town name is no longer known. 

The '''Town of Woodbury''' is in the eastern part of the county. 

 History 
The region was once called Woodbury Clove ( valley ). The Town of Woodbury was incorporated in one eight eight nine (the town was originally created in one eight six three , but was dissolved soon afterwards).

The Town of Woodbury, which is comprised of the hamlets of Central Valley and Highland Mills; and the area which was formerly known as the hamlet of Woodbury Falls, was officially created on December one nine , one eight eight nine by an act of the Orange County Board of Supervisors. The first town meeting was held the following year on March four th with John A. Patterson presiding as Supervisor. The second Supervisor was James Seaman. Eventhough the land is no longer used for farming, the Seaman family property can still be identified by a sign which reads Sweet Clover Farm along Route three two on the northern end of town. 

The Town of Woodbury was actually created twice - the first time in one eight six three when the Board of Supervisors approved the division of Monroe into the three communities of Monroe, Tuxedo and Woodbury. Objections to this arose and two years later the Legislature was asked to overrule the Board's decision which it did by recreating the old Town of Monroe. In one eight eight nine the Board of Supervisors reinstated the original separation and Woodbury was reborn. 

Woodbury had gone through numerous geographic and name changes prior to its incorporation in one eight eight nine . Until one seven six four , the area was part of an enlarged Goshen. In that year, Goshen was divided into two parts with Woodbury becoming part of Cornwall. During the American Revolution, the area was shown on maps as Woodbury Clove. By one seven nine nine , Cornwall was also divided with Woodbury joining the present day Monroe and Tuxedo to become the Town of Cheesekook. This name was changed to Smithfield or Southfield and in one eight zero eight became Monroe in honor of the newly elected United States President James Monroe. 

No one is quite sure of the derivation of the name Woodbury. Some say it may have come from the Dutch word WODE for wood and meaning a dwelling place in the woods. Others claim that the many English families who settled here bestowed the name of a famous English family named Woodbury upon the area. As for the hamlets, Central Valley and Highland Mills were once called Lower Smith's Clove (clove meaning valley). Highland Mills was also known as Orange Post Office, but the residents changed it in one eight two four with the present name most likely reflecting the mills, flour and tannery businesses in the area. A map dated about one seven nine zero shows Woodbury Falls as being called Smithfields. It may have later taken its name from the once lovely falls there. 

In addition to the flour and grist mills, the area's industry was dominated by a large tourism business as well as a famous fly rod (fishing rod) manufacturing business. Woodbury was the home to both the Payne Rod Company and the Leonard Rod Company.

 Geography 
The town is adjacent to West Point, the United States Military Academy. Interstate eight seven passes through the town. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of nine six . three km ( three seven . two mi ).  nine three . seven km ( three six . two mi ) of it is land and two . six km ( one . zero mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . seven two % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are nine , four six zero people, three , one one seven households, and two , five four six families residing in the town. The population density is one zero one . zero km ( two six one . six mi ). There are three , three five eight housing units at an average density of three five . nine km ( nine two . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine zero . one eight % White, three . zero three % African American, zero . two nine % Native American, two . six zero % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, two . two one % from other races, and one . six seven % from two or more races.  seven . nine four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , one one seven households out of which four six . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six nine . nine % are married couples living together, eight . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and one eight . three % are non-families. one five . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and four . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is three . zero three and the average family size is three . three nine .

In the town the population is spread out with three zero . nine % under the age of one eight , five . eight % from one eight to two four , three one . four % from two five to four four , two four . five % from four five to six four , and seven . four % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are nine six . five males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine two . seven males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ seven nine , zero eight seven , and the median income for a family is $ eight four , one five six . Males have a median income of $ five nine , seven four four versus $ three seven , six nine five for females. The per capita income for the town is $ two eight , five six six .  three . three % of the population and one . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, three . one % of those under the age of one eight and one . six % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 '''Fulton''' is a city located in Oswego County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one one , eight five five .  The city is named after Robert Fulton, inventor of the steamboat. 

The '''City of Fulton''' is located in the western part of the county. 

A branch of Cayuga County Community College is in the city. 

 History 
This area was known as Oswego Falls due to the rapids on the Oswego River and was one of the first regions settled in the Town of Granby. Settlement commenced in two locations, the Upper Landing and the Lower Landing. 

In one eight two six , construction of the Oswego Canal began, and it was completed in one eight two eight . 

The community was incorporated as a village in one eight three five .

When Nestl began production in the United States, Fulton was home to the first factory built by the company. However, in two zero zero one the company closed the factory citing that the costs to restore and update the century old location were too out of reach. Factory employees hung the Nestl company flag outside the factory upside down the day the closing was announced by company officials.

 Geography 
Fulton is located at four three  one nine ' one two  North, seven six  two four ' four eight  West ( four three . three one nine eight seven eight , - seven six . four one three two two four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one two . three km ( four . eight mi ).  nine . nine km ( three . eight mi ) of it is land and two . four km ( zero . nine mi ) of it is water. The total area is one nine . seven five % water. 

Fulton is located on the Oswego River, Erie Canal, and borders Lake Neatahwanta. The city straddles the border of the Town of Granby and the Town of Volney.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one one , eight five five people, four , nine two three households, and two , nine seven three families residing in the city. The population density is one , one nine eight . two km ( three , one zero two . nine mi ). There are five , five zero one housing units at an average density of five five six . zero km ( one , four three nine . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine six . eight zero % White, zero . seven four % African American, zero . three seven % Native American, zero . three three % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, zero . eight eight % from other races, and zero . eight five % from two or more races.  one . nine two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four , nine two three households out of which three one . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four zero . nine % are married couples living together, one five . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three nine . six % are non-families. three three . six % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three eight and the average family size is three . zero two .

In the city the population is spread out with two seven . two % under the age of one eight , eight . seven % from one eight to two four , two eight . zero % from two five to four four , two zero . one % from four five to six four , and one six . zero % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Pulaski''' is a village located in Oswego County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two , three nine eight . 

The '''Village of Pulaski''' is within the Town of Richland. The village is located on US Route one one and is adjacent to Interstate eight one . Pulaski was incorporated in one eight three three . Pulaski is pronounced with sky (rhymes with 'my') at the end instead of the traditional ski (rhymes with lee ).

 Geography 
Pulaski is located at four three  three three ' five four  North, seven six  seven ' three zero  West ( four three . five six five one zero eight , - seven six . one two five zero zero three ). It is on the Salmon River. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of eight . nine km ( three . four mi ).  eight . five km ( three . three mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is four . zero eight % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , three nine eight people, one , zero three four households, and five eight five families residing in the village. The population density is two eight one . four km ( seven two nine . four mi ). There are one , one five five housing units at an average density of one three five . five km ( three five one . three mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine eight . two one % White, zero . one seven % African American, zero . four six % Native American, zero . four two % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . zero zero % from other races, and zero . seven five % from two or more races.  zero . seven five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , zero three four households out of which two nine . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four zero . one % are married couples living together, one two . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and four three . four % are non-families. three seven . one % of all households are made up of individuals and two zero . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three zero and the average family size is three . zero five .

In the village the population is spread out with two five . three % under the age of one eight , eight . zero % from one eight to two four , two seven . one % from two five to four four , two one . four % from four five to six four , and one eight . one % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, one nine . eight % of those under the age of one eight and one eight . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. 

 Commerce 
Commerce in Pulaski revolves heavily around fishing tourism - located on one of the three Salmon Rivers off the east end of Lake Ontario, (which is named for the salmon which, each fall, return to the river during the salmon run) is a major draw for sportfishing, as is Lake Ontario, the shore of which is a few miles distant.

During the winter, there is also a large amount of snowmobile tourism.

The '''sarrusophone''' is a family of transposing musical instruments patented and placed into production by Pierre-Louis Gautrot in one eight five six . It was named after the French bandmaster Pierre Auguste Sarrus ( one eight one three - one eight seven six ) who is credited with the concept of the instrument (it is not clear if Sarrus benefitted financially from this association) and its intended use was to serve as a replacement for the oboe and bassoon in bands, the tones of which lack the carrying power needed for the outdoor band music of that era.

Sizes and ranges
Similar to the saxophone, the sarrusophone, was manufactured in the following sizes and had the following theoretical ranges:

 Eb Sopranino Bb-G  (Sounding Db-Bb) 
 Bb Soprano Bb-G    (Sounding Ab-F)
 Eb Alto Bb-G       (Sounding Db-Bb)
 Bb Tenor Bb-G      (Sounding Ab-F)
 Eb Baritone Bb-G   (Sounding Db-Bb)
 Bb Bass Bb-g       (Sounding Ab-F)
 EEb Contrabass Bb-G (Sounding Ab-F)
 CC Contrabass Bb-G (Sounding at pitch Bb-G)
 BBb Contrabass Bb-G (Sounding Db-Bb)


As can be seen, the non-transposed range of the sarrusophone is nearly identical to that of the saxophone. The traditional conventional range of the saxophone is written Bb-F. Initially, Gautrot advertised the range of the sarrusophone to high F as well, but later fingering charts indicated a range to high G. Sometime after one eight six eight , Gautrot also released a fingering chart indicating fingerings higher still up to a top Bb giving a range of three full octaves. The photo above is that of a EEb Contrabass.

Method of sounding
Like the oboe and bassoon, all sizes were originally designed to be played with a double reed. Later, single reed mouthpieces were developed which resemble alto or soprano saxophone mouthpieces, and attach to the bocal.

Use in classical music
The sarrusophone is rarely called for in orchestral music. However, around the turn of the two zero th century, the contrabass sarrusophones in EEb and CC, enjoyed a vogue, the latter as a substitute for the contrabassoon, (the French model patterned after the German Heckel model, having been introduced later around one nine zero six by Buffet et.al) so that it is called for in, for example, Maurice Ravel's L'heure espagnol ( one nine zero seven ) and Arrigo Boito's Nerone ( one nine two four ). Igor Stravinsky included a part for contrabass sarrusophone in Thereni. The composer Paul Dukas used the contrabass sarrusophone to great effect in one eight nine zero in his The Sorcerer's Apprentice where the instrument begins the bassoon's macabre dance motif (familiar to all who recall Disney's animated film Fantasia ). These parts are nowadays all played on the contrabassoon. In general when the term sarrusophone is used, it usually refers to the EEb contrabass which appears to have been made in larger numbers than any other size. It should be pointed out that although the CC contrabass was perhaps envisoned for these and other orchestral works, few instruments were made and those that did exist, were most likely the property of the orchestras that they were made for. The CC contrabass has a range that is identical to the contrabassoon, while the EEb contrabass, while having the same written range as the CC, due to its key, lacks the lowest three notes of the contrabassoon's range (C, B, Bb).

The EEb contrabass has also been used as an alternative to the EEb contrabass saxophone, which due to its large size is impractical in many musical situations, especially marching.

Until recently, the BBb contrabass had the distinguishing feature of being the lowest pitched reed instrument ever placed in production, since it is capable of producing Ab, one semitone lower than the standard piano and the extended range contra bassoon to low A. However, the German instrument maker Benedikct Eppelsheim has recently introduced a brand new instrument called the Tubax (a saxophone hybrid), one model of which, the BBb subcontrabass, also has Ab as its lowest pitch.

The French firm of G. Leblanc for many years ( one nine five zero 's- one nine eight zero 's?) featured photographs of its EEEb octocontra-alto and BBBb octocontrabass clarinets, instruments that could play lower still, in its advertising. However, despite their notoriety and frequent citing in books on musical instruments and in on-line discussion forums, these instruments were never placed in production and were, perhaps, more along the lines of engineering achievements and curiosities (despite the fact that the EEEb model could be a viable instrument, it is said that only three were made). Even then, it appears that few BBb contrabass sarrusophones were ever built, the EEb being much more portable and perhaps, practical.

In the concert band literature, Percy Grainger used the EEb contrabass in the original scoring of his children's march '' Over the Hills and Far Away ''. In early two zero th centuruy Italian band scores, parts for the Bb tenor, Eb baritone, and Bb bass sarrusophones as well as the contrabass are common. It appears that higher members of the sarusophone family were not as popular as the lower members. For the most part, the use of the sarrusophone was primarily in France, Italy and Spain. During or after World War one , US Military personnel noted the use of the contrabass sarrusophone in French military bands and thereafter, commissioned the US firm Conn to manufacture the EEb contrabass for use in US military bands beginning in approximately one nine two one , as per Conn's advertising of the time. The initial order was for one four eight instruments. The instrument was offered for sale to the general public as well, but production appears to have ceased in the late one nine two zero 's or early one nine three zero 's. Beginning in one nine two one , the John Philip Sousa band used the Conn sarrusophone for an unknown period of time. In Germany, the instrument was practically unknown (although curiously, Heckel stated in its one nine three zero catalog that sarrusophones could be made on demand) and in England, there may have been limited use, but it never caught on there. In one nine zero eight when Sir Thomas Beecham wished to perform the work Apollo and the Seaman by the British composer Josef Holbrooke (who had included parts for several sizes of sarrusophones), the sarrusophone parts had to be played by performers brought over from France. Paderewski included three Eb contrabass sarrusophones in his Symphony in B Minor ( Polonia ).

Use in jazz
A very unusual example of the sarrusophone in jazz is on the one nine two four recording by the Clarence Williams Blue five of Mandy, Make Up Your Mind , with the sarrusophone played by the jazz soprano saxophone and clarinet virtuoso Sidney Bechet. One can conjecture that the sarrusophone played was most likely a contrabass with a single reed mouthpiece, as Bechet was not a trained double reed player. It is interesting to note that Bechet later denied having ever played the sarrusophone!

In the one nine seven zero s and one nine eight zero s the late American jazz musician Gerald Oshita (based in Chicago and the San Francisco Bay Area and associated with Roscoe Mitchell) played avant garde jazz on an EEb contrabass manufactured by Conn. More recently ( one nine nine zero - two zero zero six ), recordings using sarrusophone have been released by saxophonists Scott Robinson, Lenny Pickett, James Carter, and Paul Winter.

Present status
The sarrusophone is now obsolete and only used as a novelty upon occasions. However, there appears to be a resurgance of interest in the instrument and there are amatueur players (mostly the EEb contrabass) now in several regional concert bands in the US. 

The tone of the sarrusophone is less clear but much more reedier than that of the saxophone. In humorous terms, the sarrusophone can be said to sound rather industrial or perhaps unrefined . New sarrusophones can still be bought by request from the Orsi Instrument Company, in Italy. Historically, Orsi, Rampone (later Rampone standard top four th of its range). From sopranino through bass, two octave keys. The contra basses (and perhaps some basses) have three 

No articulated G, bis Bb, F trill keys or one one and one two Bb as found on the saxophone. The top and bottom key stacks are not linked

The key for low Bb is activated by the left thumb as opposed to the left little finger as on the saxophone

A key for rapid alternation across the C-D break. This key can also be used to play high D as well (This may be taken to be an equivalent of the high D palm key of a saxophone)

No palm keys for playing the top range. Using the non-automatic register keys, three rd harmonics are easily available, rendering palm keys unnecessary.

The Rothphone
The rothphone, also known as the rothophone or saxarrusophone, is a sarrusophone hybrid that is rewrapped to look like a saxophone. It was manufactured by the Italian maker Roth of Milan and was introduced around one nine zero zero , but found no popular acceptance. They are, nowadays, even less common than the sarrusophone. They came in sizes from soprano to bass. It had a less conical bore than both the saxophone and the sarrusophone. As per advertising of the time, the well known American saxophone manufactuer, Buescher imported a number of these instruments into the USA during the late one nine two zero 's or early one nine three zero 's, perhaps as an answer to Conn's production of the contrabass sarrusophone.

Mistaken identity
Another obscure deep toned double reed instrument called the Reed Contrabass or contrabasso ad ancia is frequently mistaken for the contrabass sarrusophone. This instrument was developed by the Belgian maker Mahillion in the one eight six zero 's based on a slightly earlier design by the Czech maker Chervany, some time after the introduction of the sarrusophone. This instrument has a much wider bore than the contrabass sarrusophone and is acoustically unlike any other woodwind instrument in that the bore is so wide in fact, that only one key at a time needs to be open to produce a given note. Hence, for the most part, only one key is opened at a time to produce a note, save the two octave keys. All of the keys on this instrument, except for the very lowest (producing the lowest D on the piano), lie normally closed. This instrument seems to have found use only in Italy, where it is still manufactured by the Orsi firm. However, both this instrument and all of the sarrusophones are still considered special order items.

 Burlington, Otsego County, New York

'''Burlington''' is a town located in Otsego County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , zero eight five .

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one one six . six km ( four five . zero mi ).  one one six . five km ( four five . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . one three % water.

 History 
Town of Burlington, c. one seven nine two 
Burlington was formed from the Town of Otsego, April one zero , one seven nine two . It retained its original dimensions until one seven nine seven , when Pittsfield (and what would come to be New Lisbon) was set off.  Cooperstown facts 
Cooperstown is perhaps best known as the home of the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum. Folklore tells that Abner Doubleday invented baseball on a cow pasture within the Village in one eight three nine . (The actual origins of baseball are much less clear.) Part of the film ''A League of Their Own'' was filmed in Cooperstown. 

Also present in or around Cooperstown are a number of other attractions. These include the Farmers' Museum, the Fenimore Art Museum, The New York State Historical Association's (NYSHA) library, Brewery Ommegang, and the Clark Sports Center (a large fitness facility). All construction in the village is closely monitored by a village board, so the buildings have maintained a historical feel to a certain extent.

Cooperstown gets a large amount of monetary support from Jane Clark. The Clark family, who became wealthy off of the patent for the Singer Sewing Machine, has donated money for a variety of causes including decorating the village, scholarships, and village construction projects.

Also associated with Cooperstown is the Glimmerglass Opera, although the Alice Busch Opera House is actually located eight miles north of the village.

Cooperstown was home to Henry Nicols, the Eagle Scout who in one nine nine one revealed that he had contracted HIV through a blood transfusion, about whom the HBO documentary Eagle Scout: The Story of Henry Nicols was made.

 Edmeston, Otsego County
'''Edmeston''' is a town located in Otsego County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , eight two four . Edmeston is also the name of the largest hamlet in the town. Two other communities in the Town of Edmeston are West Edmeston and South Edmeston.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one one five . five km ( four four . six mi ).  one one five . four km ( four four . five mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . one one % water. The major water features are:
 the Unadilla River, which forms the entire western border of the town,
 Wharton Creek, which meanders to the south and west through the southeastern corner of the town,
 Mill Creek, which flows from north to south from the northern border of Edmeston to the Wharton Creek at the Edmeston hamlet.
 Summit Lake in the northeastern corner of the town.

The elevation of the town varies by about eight zero zero feet: from just under one one zero zero feet above sea level at the Unadilla River in the southwest corner of the town, to just over one nine zero zero feet at peaks near Taylor Hill and Summit Lake in the northeast corner.

 History 
:''For a documented history of the Town of Edmeston, see the Wikisource article: History of Edmeston, New York''

The town of Edmeston, in Otsego County, extends to the West as far as the Unadilla River, a line that was established by the one seven six eight Treaty of Fort Stanwix between the British and the Iroquois, signed by Sir William Johnson ). The town's name came from the brothers, Robert and William Edmeston, who had been granted one zero , zero zero zero acres ( four zero km ) of land in what is now the northwest corner of the town. The hamlets of West Edmeston and South Edmeston are situated in the Unadilla Valley, while the hamlet of Edmeston lies in the Wharton Valley. Earlier settlers came from New England; for most of the settlers, it was planned as a stopover on their way west. A strong Baptist influence came with the settlers. Universalists, Methodists and Roman Catholics soon arrived.

Dairy farming has historically been the main business of the area. Cheese factories, creameries, livery stables, blacksmith shops, and tanneries were created to support the dairy industry. One room schoolhouses were scattered throughout the town. By damming the creeks, power was created for foundries and mills. Hop growing and maple syrup production were seasonal ocupations. Each of the town's communities developed business districts and became self sufficient. By the late one eight zero zero s, and the beginning of the one nine zero zero s, trains were introduced. Then cars, busses and trucks arrived on the scene. Dams were washed out and electricity became available. The hamlets evolved into bedroom communities. The one room schoolhouses closed and the Central School was developed in the hamlet of Edmeston.

Today residents go in all four directions for employment. The New York Central Insurance Company (in Edmeston) not only provides positions for many of the locals, but also for hundreds that commute into the community each day. On the Eastern side of the town is the Pathfinder Village (home for Down Syndrome residents) that provides more employment.

The population of the town has not increased much through the years. It still remains largely rural. Organizations like the local Rotary Club, American Legion and Fire and Emergency Squads have active volunteers that provide community needs in lieu of governments in the hamlets. Edmeston Central School is the center of activities.

 '''Gilbertsville''' is a village located in Otsego County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of three seven five .

 History 

According to the article  Goliath Met David on the Banks of the Butternut Creek, by Leigh C. Eckmair, for much of the two zero th century, the Village of Gilbertsville had been living with the very real threat of destruction from a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers flood control project. One dam of the Upper Susquehanna Rivershed Project was to be built on the lower Butternut Creek at a spot called Copes Corners. This dam was to flood the valley behind it, including the village of Gilbertsville, to create a three-mile long lake. Residents had been watching in horror over the years as communities in the nearby Catskills had become victims of similar projects and had vowed not to let it happen to their small village.

The dam project, originally proposed prior to WWI, met with very strong local opposition every time it was reintroduced. Delayed due to WWI and The Great Depression, the project came about again in one nine three five following a flood which did millions of dollars of damage to communities in eight southern tier counties in upstate New York. Funding was appropriated but the project was delayed because of WWII.

In the early one nine five zero s, the Village of Gilbertsville was again endangered when the U.S. Congress reauthorized future funding for the project. A locally organized protest was begun to call attention to the negative aspects of the project on a state and federal level. The protest was very active from the one nine five zero s through the one nine seven zero s.

During this time, several important studies of Gilbertsville and Butternut Valley architecture had been compiled. These studies called attention to the fact that a number of well known architects of the late one nine th and early two zero th centurys had been responsible for the design, building and renovation of many attractive village structures. As a result, a number of architectural scholars became involved in protesting the dam project which would destroy this unique community. From that effort came the suggestion that several structures in the center of the village be nominated to the new Department of Interior's National Register of Historic Places. It was hoped that National Register recognition would afford some protection for the village, on the state and federal level, from the proposed dams.

The Committee for the Historic Preservation of Gilbertsville was formed to work with the N.Y. State Office of Parks and Recreation and to prepare nominations, documentation and photographs. Consultants came to inspect the nominated properties and saw that many other structures and sites in the village were equally worthy of nomination. The suggestion was made that the entire village be inventoried as a complete Historic District and that the recognition of the entire village as an Historic District would be even more powerful protection from the dams.

The committee called on the community for help with the expanded project and was not disappointed. It took a total of seven years but the full committee of one nine volunteer researchers, typists, gofers, and photographers prepared a total of one nine four individual structural inventory reports plus reports for each cemetery, park, bridge and five additional structures just outside the village incorporation.

A one six page pamphlet describing the importance of the Historic District, its setting and architecture, including photographs, was prepared for the congressional committee reconsidering funding of the project.

A detailed study was prepared for the same committee documenting weather history in the Upper Susquehanna Rivershed during times of flooding on the lower Susquehanna River. The author of the study used as her source one hundred years of state and federal government weather records dating back to the one nine th century when those agencies first started collecting that data. The study found that no significant rains or storms occurred in the areas drained by the Butternut Creek and the Unadilla River during times of damaging floods on the lower Susquehanna River.

The combination of all these efforts was rewarded when deauthorization of funding for the complete Upper Susquehanna River Shed Project was proposed to Congress in one nine seven nine . Within a year, the threat of the construction of the dams was removed.

The National Register of Historic Places recognition of the entire village of Gilbertsville as an Historic District was awarded in May one nine eight three .

 Architecture

Overlook Park - This one zero zero year old park sits next to a stone arch bridge surrounded by stone buildings.

 The '''Town of Richfield''' is located in northern Otsego County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a population of two , four two three .

 History 
From the ''Gazetteer of the State of New York'' by J. H. French, Published by R. Pearsall Smith, Syracuse, N. Y. one eight six zero :
:Richfield was formed from Otsego, New York on April one zero , one seven nine two . Exeter and Plainfield were taken off in one seven nine nine . It is the extreme northern town of the county. Its surface is rolling and moderately hilly, with a mean elevation of one five zero to two zero zero ft. above Schuyler Lake ''Canadarago Lake'', which lies in the southeast corner of the town and occupies a deep valley, into which flow several small streams from the north and west. The soil is of a diversified character, consisting of gravel, slate, clay, and sandy loam, well cultivated and productive. About five zero zero , zero zero zero pounds of cheese are made in the town annually,  being more than double that made in any other town in the county. Richfield Springs (p.v.), near the head of Schuyler Lake, in the northeast corner of the town, contains three churches, a flouring mill, and three six eight inhabitants.''' one ''' Monticello, (Richfield p.o.,) near the center, contains a church and one three nine inhabitants. Mayflower is a p.o. Brighton contains about one five houses. Settlements were made prior to the Revolution; but they were broken up during the war. The first settlers after the war were John Kimball, Richard and Wm. Pray, John Beardsley, Joseph Coats, and Seth Allen, in one seven eight seven .''' two ''' The first church (Prot. E.) was formed at Monticello, May two zero , one seven nine nine ; Rev. Daniel Nash was the first preacher.''' three '''

:''' one ''' Richfield Springs  from which the village derives its name  are celebrated for their medicinal properties in the cure of cutaneous disorders and large numbers of invalids are annually attracted here. Professor Reid has given the following as the result of an analysis of a wine gallon of the water of these springs:
:Grains. Bicarbonate of magnesia  two zero 
:Bicarbonate of lime  one zero 
:Chloride of sodium and magnesia  one . zero five 
:Sulphate of magnesia  three zero 
:Hydrosulphate of magnesia and lime  two 
:Sulphate of lime  two zero 
:Solid matter  one five three . zero five 
:Total Grains two three six . one zero 
:Sulphurated hydrogen gas, two six . nine inches. 

:''' two ''' Willam Tunnicliff, Dan'l Hawks, John Hatch, Ebenezor Eaton, and Jos. Rockwell settled at or near Richfield Springs in one seven eight nine ; Obadiah Beardsley and his son Obadiah, jr., the father and grandfather of the late Levi Beardsley, and Hon. Samuel Beardsley, of Utica settled near Schuylers Lake in one seven nine zero . The first birth was that of Jos. Beardsley; and the first marriage, that of Ebenezer Russell and Mrs. Moore. James S. Palmer taught the first school at Richfield Springs; Israel Rawson kept the first inn, and Cyrus Robinson the first store, at the Springs; William Tunnicliff erected the first mill, at the same place.

 Demographics

'''Kent''' is a town located in Putnam County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one four , zero zero nine . The name is that of an early settler family. 

The '''Town of Kent''' is the north-central part of the Putnam County. It is sometimes called Kent Lakes.  Many of the lakes are reservoirs for New York City. 

 History 
Kent was part of the Phillipse Patent of one six seven nine , when it was still populated by the Wappinger tribe. 
The town was first settled around one seven five zero . It became the Frederickstown district in one seven eight eight . 

The Town of Kent was established as the Town of Frederick in one seven nine five when the township boundaries were realigned. Its name was changed to Kent in one eight one seven . A small portion of the Town of Philipstown was transferred to Kent in one eight seven seven . 

The major population center of the township is Lake Carmel, a settlement around an artificial lake (also known as Lake Carmel ) developed in the one nine two zero s. Historically the population centers had been Farmer's Mills and Ludingtonville, little of which remain. The town is part of the Carmel Central School District and is served by the Carmel Post Office under the name Kent Lakes (because another community upstate has a post office called Kent).

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one one one . eight km ( four three . two mi ).  one zero five . two km ( four zero . six mi ) of it is land and six . six km ( two . five mi ) of it is water. The total area is five . eight eight % water. 

The north town line is the border of Dutchess County. 

Interstate eight four passes through the town.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one four , zero zero nine people, four , eight six eight households, and three , seven four eight families residing in the town. The population density is one three three . one km ( three four four . eight mi ). There are five , three five three housing units at an average density of five zero . nine km ( one three one . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine three . eight one % White, one . four one % African American, zero . one four % Native American, one . two four % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, one . eight one % from other races, and one . five seven % from two or more races.  five . seven seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four , eight six eight households out of which three eight . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six four . four % are married couples living together, nine . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and two three . zero % are non-families. one seven . five % of all households are made up of individuals and four . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight four and the average family size is three . two four .

In the town the population is spread out with two six . three % under the age of one eight , six . two % from one eight to two four , three two . one % from two five to four four , two five . seven % from four five to six four , and nine . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are nine eight . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine six . two males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ seven two , three four six , and the median income for a family is $ seven nine , seven one six . Males have a median income of $ five one , six three four versus $ three eight , five seven five for females. The per capita income for the town is $ two nine , nine eight four .  four . one % of the population and four . two % of families are below the poverty line.  '''Lake Carmel''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in the Town of Kent in Putnam County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, it had a total population of eight , six six three . 

The home of most of the Town of Kent's population, Lake Carmel is centered on the eponymous artificial lake, in the southeast corner of the township and just north of the Carmel. Lake Carmel was developed in the one nine two zero s and thereafter by the Smadbeck brothers, who excavated and dammed a swamp and sold lots through the now-defunct ''New York Daily Mirror''. Lake Carmel is the seat of a volunteer fire district covering the eastern half of the township, and of the Kent town government.

 Geography 
The community is west of Interstate eight four . 

Lake Carmel is located at four one  two seven ' three seven  North, seven three  three nine ' four two  West ( four one . four six zero two six eight , - seven three . six six one six six three ).

'''Patterson''' is a town located in Putnam County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one one , three zero six . The town is named after early farmer Matthew Patterson. 

The '''Town of Patterson''' is in the northeast part of the county. Interstate eight four passes through the southwest part of the town. 

 History 
The town was first settled around one seven three one . 
The Town of Patterson, known as the Town of Franklin when it was formed from parts of the Towns of Frederickstown and Southeast in one seven nine five , changed to its current name in one eight zero eight . 

It is also the site of the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead, the missionary school of Jehovah's Witnesses.

 Demographics

The population density is one three five . three km ( three five zero . four mi ). The '''Town of Philipstown''' is a town located in the western part of Putnam County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of nine , four two two . 

 History 
The town was first settled around one seven one five . 

Established in one seven eight eight as one of the three original towns in what is now Putnam County, the Town of Philipstown's main population centers are the Village of Cold Spring, Garrison, and the Village of Nelsonville. In one eight zero six , part of the town was used to form the Town of Fishkill. Putnam Valley was part of Philipstown until one eight three nine , and a small portion of the town north of Putnam Valley was transferred to Kent in one eight seven seven . 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one three three . four km ( five one . five mi ).  one two six . five km ( four eight . eight mi ) of it is land and seven . zero km ( two . seven mi ) of it is water. The total area is five . two two % water. 

The western border is the Hudson River with Orange County on the opposite shore. The north town line is Dutchess County, and the south town line is Westchester County. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are nine , four two two people, three , five nine nine households, and two , five four eight families residing in the town. The population density is seven four . five km ( one nine three . zero mi ). There are three , nine eight three housing units at an average density of three one . five km ( eight one . six mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine five . five seven % White, one . one three % African American, zero . one five % Native American, one . one four % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . nine two % from other races, and one . zero nine % from two or more races.  three . seven nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , five nine nine households out of which three two . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six zero . eight % are married couples living together, six . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and two nine . two % are non-families. two three . five % of all households are made up of individuals and nine . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . five six and the average family size is three . zero six .

In the town the population is spread out with two four . zero % under the age of one eight , four . nine % from one eight to two four , two eight . five % from two five to four four , two nine . six % from four five to six four , and one three . zero % who are six five years of age or older. '''Southeast''' is a town located in Putnam County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one seven , three one six . 

The '''Town of Southeast''' is in the southeast part of the county. Interstate eight four , Interstate six eight four , US Route two zero two , and US Route six pass through the town. 

Southeast is the second largest town in Putnam County. 

 History 
The first settler arrived around one seven three zero . The area first exlpoited was called The Oblong, and was outside of the land claimed by the Philiplse Patent. 

The Town of Southeast was founded in one seven eight eight , was then the southeast corner of Dutchess County, New York whose northeast corner was the township of North East, New York (now part of Dutchess County).  In one seven nine five , the land that had been Southeast and ''Frederickstown'' (Now Kent ) was divided into four townships, the present Southeast, Carmel, Kent, and Patterson, the latter two known at first as Frederick and Franklin.  Southeast lost its northern half, and expanded slightly to the west. Its most densely populated area in the town is the Village of Brewster, New York.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of nine zero . six km ( three five . zero mi ).  eight three . zero km ( three two . one mi ) of it is land and seven . six km ( two . nine mi ) of it is water. The total area is eight . three five % water. The town contains several reservoirs that supply New York City. 

The east town line is the border of Connecticut (Fairfield County), and the south town line is the border of Westchester County. 

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one seven , three one six people, six , one eight four households, and four , five six nine families residing in the town. The population density is two zero eight . five km ( five four zero . one mi ). There are six , four one two housing units at an average density of seven seven . two km ( two zero zero . zero mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine two . eight eight % White, one . eight seven % African American, zero . one four % Native American, one . six three % Asian, zero . zero nine % Pacific Islander, two . four zero % from other races, and zero . nine nine % from two or more races.  eight . zero four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six , one eight four households out of which three seven . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six one . nine % are married couples living together, eight . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and two six . one % are non-families. two zero . six % of all households are made up of individuals and six . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . seven seven and the average family size is three . two two .

In the town the population is spread out with two six . four % under the age of one eight , five . nine % from one eight to two four , three three . one % from two five to four four , two four . six % from four five to six four , and one zero . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero one . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine seven . two males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ six nine , two seven two , and the median income for a family is $ seven eight , five five three .  '''Castleton-on-Hudson''' is a village located in the Town of Schodack in Rensselaer County, New York, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , six one nine . The name is from a local indian village, known as Castle Hill. 

The '''Village of Castleton-on-Hudson''' is in the southwestern part of the town. The village is southeast of Albany, New York. 

Schodack Island State Park is located south of the village. 

 History 
Castleton gets its name from the exploration of the North (Hudson) River by Henry Hudson. While traveling up the river, he came upon a Mahikan Indian village noted for a large structure located on a rise above the river. This structure was a storehouse for foodstuffs, but was of such size that it was thought to be a castle , hence the name Castleton. 

When the small village was incorporated into Rensselaer County in one eight two seven , there were about one zero zero people living in the area, mostly along the banks of the river. Between one eight nine zero and one nine two zero , the village had a booming economy, with small industry, a hotel, and a small port to gain access to river traffic. However, a large flood destroyed much of the business district in one nine three six , and the industry took the opportunity to relocate. These days the town is a very residential suburb, with some light agriculture.

The name of the village was changed from Castleton to Castleton-on-Hudson in one nine two seven , possibly to help prevent inadvertent mail delivery to the community of Castleton, Vermont.

 Geography 
Castleton-on-Hudson is located at four two  three one ' five seven  North, seven three  four five ' one  West ( four two . five three two three seven seven , - seven three . seven five zero three four zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of two . one km ( zero . eight mi ).  two . one km ( zero . eight mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. 

The village is on the east bank of the Hudson River. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , six one nine people, six one five households, and three nine nine families residing in the village. The population density is seven eight one . four km ( two , zero two five . five mi ). There are six five four housing units at an average density of three one five . six km ( eight one eight . two mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine six . seven nine % White, one . three six % African American, zero . zero zero % Native American, zero . two five % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . nine three % from other races, and zero . six eight % from two or more races.  one . seven nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six one five households out of which three five . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four five . zero % are married couples living together, one five . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three five . one % are non-families. two nine . six % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four six and the average family size is three . zero six .

In the village the population is spread out with two seven . one % under the age of one eight , six . four % from one eight to two four , two eight . three % from two five to four four , one nine . one % from four five to six four , and one nine . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are eight three . one males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are seven three . zero males.

 '''Hoosick''' is a town located in Rensselaer County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of six , seven five nine . 

The '''Town of Hoosick''' is in the northeast corner of the county. 

 History 
The town is one of the original towns of the county and was created as a town in one seven eight eight , before the creation of Rensselaer County. The region was formerly the District of Hoosick ( one seven seven two ) and previously the Hoosick Patent ( one six eight eight ).

The Battle of Bennington of the American Revolution was fought in the town northeast of the community of Walloomsac. 

 Past residents of note 
Among the notable natives of Hoosick is John Palmer ( one seven eight five - one eight four zero ), who seved two non-consecutive terms in the United States Congress. 

Folk artist Grandma Moses is buried in Hoosick. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one six three . six km ( six three . two mi ).  one six three . two km ( six three . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . three km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two one % water. 

The north town line is the boundary of Washington County, New York, and the east town line is the border of Vermont. The Hoosick River is an important waterway in the town. 

 Demographics
