Out of the total population, two one . six % of those under the age of one eight and zero . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

The Land of No
There are a number funky laws to the uninitiated in effect in Ocean Beach. This is why regular visitors and residents have affectionatly dubbed OB the land of No. Here are a few examples that may catch you off guard:

 Bicycle Riding, while no longer banned outright, is restricted in the Summer Season to the hours of five am to eight pm Monday through Thursday and five am to seven pm on Fridays. Bicycle riding is illegal on Saturday and Sunday. 
 All bicycles must be equipped with a bell and a flash light after dark. Yes Biking after dark will get you a ticket, and not having a flash light will get you another one. In the law's defense, it does apply to the off-season too when bike riding is allowed at any time but the bell and light are still required. 
 Bike riding in the commercial district, better known as In Town , is not permitted at any time during the Summer Season. 
 Scooters, skateboards & roller blades are restricted to the same area and time frame but are additionally only allowed by those one two years old or younger. Helmets are required regardless of age, no joke.
 Remember that pedestrians always have the right of way and you are expected to stop and look before crossing Midway (The East West walk running the Width of the Village)
 The ban on Eating and Drinking on the walks has been reduced as well. At one time you could not eat or drink anything on the walks anywhere in Ocean Beach. Now it is permitted in the commercial district, the opposite of where biking is allowed. Glass drink containers and alcoholic beverages are not allowed though. Littering is a big no no too, and carries a hefty fine. Eating and Drinking is also disallowed on the beach overpasses (wooden steps over the dunes to the ocean) and on the beach itself.
 If you want to barbecue you need a permit. Propane only, flame proof base required, and the area must be inspected before you can receive your permit, which must renewed every summer. 
 Mind your noise pollution when you party. Ocean Beach's noise law states if sound can be heard beyond the property line you are in violation of the law and can be ticketed. I always found this amusing because it seems to indicate that if one stands in their front yard and whispers to someone in the street, they are breaking the law. It is really only enforced if you are being a nuisance though.
 Guys listen up! The topless laws apply to you too when you are off the beach and in town. No shirt, no service, and a summons. Shoes are still optional for the most part though.
 All trash put out for collection must be in bags which in turn must be in cans which in turn must have lids! Your cans also have to be removed from the walkway before one zero am the next day!
 Dogs must be on a leash in public at all times (You'll note the local's dogs which are on leashes but on their own). You also must have a pooper scooper with you at all times when walking your dog. A plastic bag in your back pocket will do, (pun hehe) but some fecal conveyance is required. 
 Dogs are not permitted on the beach between May one five and Sept. one five 
 Frisbees, Ball playing, kite flying, radios without headphones, disrobing, and unattended minors are not permitted on the beach. 

The police officers in Ocean Beach are generally polite and courteous and just want to promote a safe and fun environment for everyone. There are reasons for the laws and they understand they can be unwittingly violated. If you are ever stopped, just say you were unaware and that you will obey the rules in the future. You'll probably get off with just a warning. Making a fuss is a quick way to ruin your Saturday morning sitting in the court room. 

Lastly, a note on the theft of Bicycles. This is crime Numero Uno in Ocean Beach. Lock your bike whenever you aren't using it. Even if it is behind your house, in the bushes, which is behind a gate. Bicycle Theft is on the same level as grand theft auto or Horse Theft in the minds of many residents. Don't expect any leniency if you take someone's bike. It is taken quite seriously. Bikes also belong to Volunteer Fire Fighters and EMS workers who need them to respond to calls and emergencies. If you or your kid is hurt, or your house is burning you down, you don't want to hear the FD or EMS was late because someone stole a bike. Second only to Bike theft is Wagon Theft. What may just be a child's toy on the Mainland is a necessity on Fire Island. When you get off the ferry with one two bags of groceries for the weekend barbecue, you will know why.

These kinds of thefts may seem petty, but you could be charged with Larceny or Grand Larceny, a felony. It is also a big deal to those who need their bikes to get to work or do their work, like contractors doing emergency repairs, etc.

 '''Orient''' is a hamlet located in Suffolk County, New York. USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the community had a total population of seven zero nine . 

Orient is in the Town of Southold.

 History and Tourism 
Orient is the eastern-most town on Long Island's picturesque North Fork. It was originally named Poquatuck, after the name of the local native American tribe that resided along the inland waterways, then Oyster ponds. Legend has it that when Oyster Bay, New York became famous during the presidency of Teddy Roosevelt, the name was changed to ''Orient'' to match the name of its most prominent land feature, Orient Point. 

Its winter population swells to well over one zero zero zero in the summer. Other than a post office, a gas station, and a few small touristy stores, there is no commercial district, with its residents depend on nearby Greenport for every-day necessities.

The village of Orient has homes built during the last three centuries. Locals joke that a new house is anything built since World War II. It was originally settled by five families given a land grant by the King of England in the one six zero zero 's, and the names of King, Terry, and Latham are still present. Definitely New England in style and flavor, it was used a base by British commandoes and local Tories during the American Revolution to conduct raids on Yankee-held Connecticut. Benedict Arnold, after his infamous treason, was their commander.

Today it serves as quiet summer home for the well-heeled New York crowd who want to avoid the tony Hamptons, but still want sun and salt water. The year round residents make a living at the US Government Department of Agriculture lab on nearby Plum Island, a five zero minute boat ride across from Orient Point across Plum Gut, or at businesses further inland. Some truck farming and commercial fishing remain.

 '''Patchogue''' (rhymes with '''catch''' dog ) is a village located in Suffolk County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one one , nine one nine . 

The village is named after the Patchogue Indians, who once inhabited the area.

The '''Village of Patchogue''' is within the Town of Brookhaven. 
Patchogue is located on the south shore of Long Island on near the Great South Bay. 

:''The Patchogue area is not neatly divided into North, East, etc. For additional demographic and geographic information on the area also see North Patchogue and East Patchogue.''


 Overview 

Patchogue is just five zero miles east of from Manhattan. It was incorporated in one eight nine three . A riverfront and a natural harbor are spectacular natural resources that the town has used for the past one zero zero years to become a modern and largely self-contained community.

Patchogue has all the ingredients for a desirable residential area where children can study and grow in health and peace. The current mayor of Patchogue is Paul Pontieri, who was a vice-principal in the neighboring South Country School District's Bellport High School for many years and currently serves as a vice-principal in Ward Mellville High School in Three Village School District.

Patchogue and Medford share a School District and library. There are Primary, Middle and High Schools, plus continuing education programs for adults and a healthy emphasis on sports. The School District combines with the St. Joseph's and the Briarcliff Colleges to give the impressive commitment to education that makes a town attractive to families interested in providing the best for their children. 

The Patchogue Theatre for the Performing Arts takes forward and reinforces the village's image as a place of discerning taste and values. At one time a movie theatre, the Theatre has been fully renovated and seats more than a thousand. The lobby can hold Receptions and has a full service bar. This splendid institution is possible solely due to the concerted efforts of local people to conserve and promote the Performing Arts.

Patchogue has churches of all denominations. The Patchogue Chamber of Commerce with more than four zero zero members, Kiwanis, Rotarians and Lions join the religious institutions to provide support and voice to residents and business people in the town. The Patchogue Ambulance Company that provides the very best standards of emergency medical care, is an astonishing all volunteer effort. The Lighthouse Mission feeds more than a thousand poor people each week, provides spiritual support, provides school supplies and is perhaps the only organized body in all of Long Island to spare a thought for those who live below the poverty line.

The Brickhouse Brewery and Restaurant is a celebration of history. one five zero years of catering and hospitality permeate great food, quenching beer and entertainment that lift your spirits. 

 History 

Patchogue was nicknamed Milltown because of the many mills -- gristmills, sawmills, paper, wool, cotton mills -- that operated on Patchogue waterways from as early as one seven five zero . The village's permanent name may have derived from Pochaug or Paushag, which were the early settlers' interpretation of the name of Indians who lived in the vicinity.

Area residents once set their clocks by the noon whistle from the giant red-brick Patchogue-Plymouth Lace Mill, which closed in one nine five four and was demolished in the mid one nine nine zero 's. Most of the mills succumbed in the one nine four zero s and ' five zero s, as a result of foreign competition and the industry movement to the South and overseas for cheaper labor.

According to Marjorie Roe, president of the Greater Patchogue Historical Society, the Lace Mill was once known as the Patchogue College because so many Patchogue kids went there when they finished high school. Charles E. Merrill, a co-founder of brokerage firm Merrill Lynch They lasted forever and never had to be replaced - I still use a lace tablecloth my mother bought in the ' three zero s, says Roe, a sixth-generation descendant of Capt. Austin Roe, a chief spy for General George Washington during the American Revolutionary War.

Justus Roe, Capt. Roe's son, built Patchogue's first hotel in one eight zero eight , and the family continued building ever-larger hotels throughout the one nine th Century. Patchogue was then a bustling seaport with fishing, oyster and boat-building industries as well as mills on the Patchogue River and Great South Bay.

Patchogue's recorded history dates from one six six four , when John Winthrop, the Younger, Governor of Connecticut, purchased nine necks of land extending from Great South Bay to the middle of the Island. He sold some to Humphrey Avery of Boston, who, in need of cash, disposed of them by lottery. In one seven five nine , Leoffer d'Leofferda won the lot that ultimately became Patchogue.

Settlers and shipping entrepreneurs soon flocked to the area, attracted by waterpower. Schooners set out from Patchogue to do commerce up and down the East Coast and even to the Mediterranean.

In one eight nine zero , the Army Corps of Engineers dredged the Patchogue River, making it the only deep-water port on Long Island's South Shore. Until one nine two two , Patchogue was a U.S. port of entry with a customs house on South Ocean Avenue.

The port also attracted bootleggers during Prohibition in the one nine two zero 's. New York City gangster Dutch Schultz set up a headquarters in Patchogue, giving lucrative employment to farm boys, who helped unload and hide the kegs of illegal liquor.

The Long Island Rail Road came to Patchogue in one eight six nine . For awhile the South Shore line ended at Patchogue. It brought thousands of summer visitors from the city, seeking the cool southwest breezes. The village, which incorporated in one eight nine three , became a summer colony, with hotels accommodating as many as one , six zero zero guests. It was also the starting point for great bicycle races. The last of the Roe family's hotels, the elegant Eagle Hotel, burned down in one nine three four .

Tourism gradually declined after one nine two zero as the affordable motor car took tourists to farther destinations, notes village co-historian Hans Henke in a pictorial history of Patchogue in its boom years from one eight four zero to one nine one five .

 Community Reinvigoration Plans 
As of two zero zero five , Village co-historian Anne Swezey and the Greater Patchogue Historical Society hope to bring back the tourist industry, if not the mills. They have restored the one eight five eight one-room schoolhouse, and the village hopes to reopen the elegant Patchogue movie house of the ' two zero s as a community theater. The village plans to demolish the lace mill and replace it with a combination retail and housing development, according to Mayor Stephen E. Keegan.

Plans are also in the works to bring new life to the Patchogue River. The village, working with the Fire Island National Seashore, which has headquarters and a ferry terminal on the river, wants to develop a year-round commercial recreation area and visitors center. The historical society is also creating a showplace for an one eight nine zero catboat by Patchogue's best-known boat builder, Gil Smith. The river is where Patchogue began, Swezey says, and where it will come back.

 Geography 
Patchogue is located at four zero  four five ' four eight  North, seven three  one ' four  West ( four zero . seven six three three seven zero , - seven three . zero one seven eight six eight ).

 Miscellaneous 
Sadly, the best-known person from Patchogue is Army Captain Dr. Jeffrey MacDonald, who was convicted of murdering his wife and two children in a case that is still hotly debated.

 The '''Village of Port Jefferson''' is located in the Town of Brookhaven in Suffolk County, New York on the North Shore of Long Island. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the village had a total population of seven , eight three seven . 

 Geography 
Port Jefferson is located at four zero  five six ' four six  North, seven three  three ' four four  West ( four zero . nine four six one zero three , - seven three . zero six two two two four ).

It is situated on the North Shore of Long Island, about five six miles east of New York City. A ferry runs from Port Jefferson across Long Island Sound to Bridgeport, Connecticut.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of seven . nine km ( three . zero mi ).  seven . eight km ( three . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . nine eight % water.

 History 
Port Jefferson at one time was small ship building community, with the name ''Drowned Meadow''. The community leaders, knowing it to be a poor name for the ship building business eventually changed its name.

P.T. Barnum, the famous circus owner, owned a tract of land which ran through the village. His intention was to make Port Jefferson the home base for his circus. The townspeople put a stop to his plans, and he eventually sold his land. A road named Barnum Ave. now runs though the area that was once his land.

'''Remsenburg-Speonk''' is a census-designated place located in the Town of Southhampton, Suffolk County, New York. It consists of the hamlets of Remsenburg and Speonk. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of two , six seven five .

 History 
As early as one seven one two , meadows in Speonk were leased to cattle owners from Southampton. Most of the early residents came west from Southampton and Bridgehampton in the one seven four zero s, building farms and clearing the forests of wood. In the one eight eight zero s, duck farms thrived in Speonk, but few survived past the turn of the century. The name '''Speonk''' was inspired by a Native American word meaning ''high place''. A one eight nine seven Long Island Rail Road catalog listed Speonk, noting that that name certainly sounds like the call of a frog. 
Some residents pressed to change the name to '''Remsenburg''', after prominent resident ''Charles Remsen'' donated a new Presbyterian Church. Today, both names remain is use, each covering different areas of the community.

 Geography

 '''Sag Harbor''' is a village located in Suffolk County, New York, United States, shared by the towns of East Hampton and Southampton. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two , three one three . 

The '''Village of Sag Harbor''' is on the western town line of East Hampton, which is the eastern town line of Southampton.

 History 
Sag Harbor was founded in one seven zero seven . It is a town with a history of whaling, earning a mention in the book ''Moby Dick'' by Herman Melville. It was the first designated ''point of entry'' for customs in New York, and once a busier port than New York City. After the decline of whaling, Sag Harbor served as home to various industrial business, the last of which was the Bulova Watchcase Factory, which closed in one nine eight one .

Sag Harbor was also author John Steinbeck's residence from one nine five five until his death in one nine six eight . The Sag Harbor-North Haven Bridge is notable as the site of Pop artist Ray Johnson's presumed suicide in one nine nine five as well as two abortive suicide attempts by monologist Spalding Gray, in September two zero zero two and October two zero zero three .

 '''Thomas Cavendish''' ( one five five five - one five nine two ) was born in Trimley St. Martin near Ipswich, Suffolk, England. He was a descendant of Roger Cavendish, brother to Sir John Cavendish from whom the Dukes of Devonshire and the Dukes of Newcastle derive their family name of Cavendish.

Thomas Cavendish was known as the Navigator . He shared in Sir Richard Grenville's expedition to Virginia in one five eight five , and had circumnavigated the world not long after Francis Drake. 

In one five eight six he sailed with three ships for the Pacific where he burned three Spanish towns and thirteen ships. In one five eight seven he visited the ruins of the failed Spanish settlement of ''Rey Don Felipe'' and renamed it Port Famine. He seized the ''Santa Anna'' off Acapulco. He returned via the Cape of Good Hope to England with only one of his ships, the ''Desire'', in one five eight eight , after which Queen Elizabeth I knighted him.

A second expedition in one five nine one ended in disaster, and Thomas Cavendish died off Ascension Island.

 '''Sayville''' is the name of a hamlet (and a census-designated place) located in Suffolk County on Long Island. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of one six , seven three five . 

Sayville is a community in the southeast part of the Town of Islip.

 History 

The earliest Native American inhabitants of Sayville were the Secatogue tribe of the Algonquian Nation. 

Sayville was founded by John Edwards (b. one seven three eight , East Hampton, New York). He built his home, the first in Sayville, in one seven six one , located at what is now the northwest corner of Foster Ave. and Edwards St. The house was destroyed by fire in March, one nine one three . Another man, John Greene, settled what's now known as West Sayville in one seven six seven .

The community had no formal name until one eight three eight when residents gathered to choose a formal name. Until that time, Sayville was known informally as over south. The townspeople held a meeting to decide on a name, and after Edwardsville and Greensville tied in a vote, one resident suggested Seaville. According to historical accounts, the clerk at that particular meeting did not know how to spell and had to go home and look in an old Bible he had brought from England years before. In the Bible, the word Sea was spelled Say, and Sayville became the name he sent to Washington. After the error was discovered, the town sent a letter of protest to Washington; however, the Postmaster General responded that the town's name should stay Sayville, as there were many Seavilles in the world but no Sayvilles. As a result, the name stuck. Incidentally, in some very old Bibles, the town name is also spelled Saville. 

Sayville became important for its timber, oysters, and beginning in one eight six eight when the South Side Rail Road arrived, tourism. Sayville is the embarkation point for ferries to the Fire Island communities of Cherry Grove, Fire Island Pines and Sailors Haven, popular vacation communities for New Yorkers and Long Islanders. The Sayville station of the Long Island Rail Road connects with the ferries via taxi and van services, and also serves commuters to New York City.
In one nine one two a German Telefunken wireless transmitter was built in Sayville to broadcast to Germany. In one nine one five , the transmitter allegedly relayed a message from the German Embassy to get Lucy referring to the RMS Lusitania which was sunk on May one five . Whether the signals coming from the transmitter in Sayville authorized the attack or not, they caused concern for the US government which dispatched Marines to ensure encrypted messages were not sent. The station was seized by the government outright after war was declared in one nine one seven . President Woodrow Wilson sent a contingent of Marines to take the wireless station, thus the first hostile action taken by the United States against Germany during World War I was in Sayville.

From one nine one nine to May one nine three two Sayville was home to Father Divine, a controversial African American religious leader who claimed to be God. His religious movement, which came to be called the International Peace Mission movement, managed a commune-like house on seven two Macon Street which was the first black-owned residence in Sayville. At that time Sayville was predominantly a seasonal vacation community, and Father Divine's followers made good livings as native house sitters. Because followers turned over all of their profits to Father Divine, he was able to build several expansions on the house. He even bought an expensive Cadillac automobile when neighbors complained about his noisy Hudson.

Father Divine's apparent flaunting of wealth annoyed the middle class town. Street-clogging traffic that Father Divine attracted made him unpopular even to businesses he patronized with large cash purchases. Following a June, one nine three two trial and prison sentence for disturbing the peace, Father Divine moved to Harlem, New York claiming that Sayville was bigoted. However, the commune remained on Macon Street for many years. Father Divine occasionally preached in Sayville afterward, but the home was only an outpost of his movement, not its center stage.

In one nine five six the BBC, sponsored by Voice of America filmed here for two weeks for a program, Life in Sayville. 

Famous residents of Sayville past and present include Melissa Joan Hart, star of ''Clarissa Explains It All'' and ''Sabrina, the Teenage Witch''; author Robert Roosevelt; Tom Westman, a New York City fireman who won $ one , zero zero zero , zero zero zero on the reality show Survivor in two zero zero five ; and Marlon Brando, who was discovered for his first Broadway role shortly after having the starring role in a summer playhouse production. According to Cynthia Blair of Newsday Brando was expelled from an acting company, of the New School, in Sayville.

In one nine nine eight , media attention visited Sayville after a mother suffocated her one seven year-old daughter Charity Miranda in an effort to exorcise the demons supposedly afflicting her.

 Geography 
The community borders the Great South Bay. 

Sayville is located at four zero  four four ' four seven  North, seven three  four ' five two  West ( four zero . seven four six two eight two , - seven three . zero eight one one one two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one four . five km ( five . six mi ).  one four . three km ( five . five mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . zero seven % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one six , seven three five people, five , six zero three households, and four , three five three families residing in the CDP.  '''Setauket-East Setauket''' is a census-designated place located in Suffolk County, New York on the North Shore of Long Island. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the CDP had a total population of one five , nine three one .

The CDP encompasses the hamlets of Setauket and East Setauket in the Town of Brookhaven. 
 
 Geography 
Setauket-East Setauket is located at four zero  five five ' four eight  North, seven three  six ' seven  West ( four zero . nine three zero zero zero seven , - seven three . one zero two zero eight one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of two four . zero km ( nine . three mi ).  two one . nine km ( eight . five mi ) of it is land and two . one km ( zero . eight mi ) of it is water. The total area is eight . six four % water.

The village of Setauket is located on the North Shore of Long Island in central Suffolk County. Part of Brookhaven's Three Village area, Setauket varies considerably as one travels north to south. In Setauket's Old Field there are wealthy waterfront estates, many from earlier decades. There is a New England style village green with a mill pond and park, a quaint post office, and the Caroline Church, built in one seven two nine , and the Setauket Presbyterian Church established in one six six zero . The Emma S. Clark Library, also on the Village Green is often considered one of the best on Long Island. During the American Revolutionary War, a small skirmish was fought on the village green, with some of the bullets embedded into the walls of Caroline Chruch


The Setaukets historically referred to the area between Stony Brook and Port Jefferson Harbors, included what are now called Head of the Harbor and St James (now part of Smithtown and not usually included as part of the Three Villages), Stony Brook (Old Stony Brook and South Stony Brook, the latter is where Stony Brook University is located), South Setauket (not to be confused with parts of Centereach), Strong's Neck, East Setauket, and Port Jefferson (formerly known as Drowned Meadow, renamed at the behest one of its famous residents PT Barnum).

South of two five A, Setauket becomes more varied with quaint colonial style houses mixing with light industrial areas and Levitt-built houses near NY Route three four seven (Nesconsett Highway).

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one five , nine three one people, five , five two one households, and four , two eight nine families residing in the CDP. The population density is seven two seven . one km ( one , eight eight two . three mi ). There are five , six three two housing units at an average density of two five seven . zero km ( six six five . four mi ). There are five , five two one households out of which three nine . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six eight . six % are married couples living together, six . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and two two . three % are non-families. one seven . two % of all households are made up of individuals and four . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight eight and the average family size is three . two six .

In the CDP the population is spread out with two six . nine % under the age of one eight , seven . three % from one eight to two four , two nine . three % from two five to four four , two seven . two % from four five to six four , and nine . four % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are nine six . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine four . five males.

Local history
During the American Revolutionary War, the Culper Spy Ring headed by Benjamin Tallmadge passed information about British troop movements gathered in New York City to George Washington.

Education

The Three Village Central School district, which all Setauket children attend is considered to be a good performer, but is facing strains from enrollment growth and aging facilties.


 Ward Melville High School - Renowned nationwide for producing a disproportionate amount of Intel Semifinalists for the Intel Science Talent Search. Perhaps more noted in the region for their Lacrosse team. 

 Gelinas Junior High School - Named after Paul J. Gelinas, First district principal

 Murphy Junior High School - Named after Robert C. Murphy, a local naturalist.

 William Sydney Mount Elementary School - Named after a local one nine th century artist known for his renditions of local, everyday life. 

 Setauket School Elementary School

 Nassakeag Elementary School

 Minnesauke Elementary School - Setauket Indian word for Little Neck , the name for what is now known as Strong's Neck.

 Arrowhead Elementary School

 Christian Avenue School - Original buildings dating back from earlier part of the century. Used for Kindergarten and one st grade before closing in late one nine seven zero s. Demolished and redeveloped is McMansions.

 North Country School - Former elementary school, closed in one nine eight zero s. Some of the districts administrative offices are located there as well as rented to BOCES.

 Stony Brook School (Private) - local urban myth (which is most likely incorrect) is that this is the very school JD Salinger attended and wrote about in Catcher in the Rye.

 Emma S. Clark Library

 Stony Brook University

Food

Home to the Se-port Deli, most popular among a certain clique of Ward Melville High School students who live in the area, also know for its delicious Boone and Deathwish sandwiches. Although popular with HS Students, Se-ports revenue generation is mainly due to it's popularity amongst blue collar workers, who frequent the deli as well as the neighboring hardware store, Fox's. Also known for a strange concentration of chain restaurants on Route three four seven and a lack thereof along Route two five A.

Eastern Pavillion was formerly Little Mandarins, and The Curry Club was formerly the Dining Car one eight nine zero . Both restaurants were local institutions from the early one nine six zero until the early one nine nine zero s, when they were forced to close due to a dispute with the landowner.

 '''Stony Brook''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in the ''Town of Brookhaven'' on Long Island in Suffolk County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of one three , seven two seven .

 General Information 
Located on the picturesque North Shore of Long Island, New York, the area is home to, among other things, Stony Brook University, The Stony Brook School, and Stony Brook Village . The history of the town has been closely linked to that of Ward Melville, a local businessman who at one point owned most of what is now sometimes called the Three Villages (consisting of the areas of Stony Brook, Setauket, and Old Field).

Beginning in one nine three nine with the creation of the Community Fund (currently the Ward Melville Heritage Organization), Ward Melville began the transformation of the area into his idea of an idyllic New England village, with white clapboard and quaint stores. This effect has been largely achieved in the population center, which consists of a green and a crescent of stores. In further pursuit of this goal, Melville donated the land and funds for the creation of Stony Brook University to the state of New York, as well as for the local school district. 

The area has virtually no industrial or commercial base due to current zoning, and the rapid growth of residential development in the past decade has begun to place serious strain on schools as they try to cope with the added strain. However, the schools are generally considered to be above average.

Visitors to the area with children should plan to see, as well as the nearby Sand Street Beach, a duck pond, a historic grist mill (c. one seven five one ), as well as the newly created Avalon Park, which has a fabulous boardwalk, trails, landscaping, and a year-round groundskeeper. Additionally, the Carriage Museum is billed as one of the largest of its type in America.

 '''Wading River''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Suffolk County, New York on the North Shore of Long Island. As of the United States two zero zero zero Census, the CDP had a total population of six , six six eight .

The community of Wading River is on the town line between the Town of Brookhaven and the Town of Riverhead. 
The name of the hamlet comes from the original Native American name for the area, Pauquaconsuk, meaning the place where we wade for thick, round-shelled clams . Thankfully, the more simple translation of this descriptive native word, Wading in the River or Wading River was adopted by the first settlers. 

 one six seven one - the earliest records of a settlement known as Wading River was originally founded with eight families. The spot for the village was chosen with care. There was a stream adequate for water power and abounding in seafoodgood water for drinkingsoil rich enough to grow essential crops, woodland for fuel, building material and food, topography to offer protection from the elements, meadowland for it's grass. 

Until one nine four seven - the Hamlet of Wading River had a year round population of less than five zero zero . But during the summer months hundreds of visitors filled the town utilizing Wildwood State Park, the cottages on the cliffs and dunes and, of course, the beaches. 

 one nine four seven - was a landmark year of change for the sleepily little Hamlet, noteworthy accomplishments include returning service men from World War II began building homes in Wading River; the formation of Wading River's own volunteer Fire Department Wading River Fire Department; the Military Instillation known as Camp Upton was no longer necessary and became Brookhaven National Labs and last, but certainly not least, the Wading River Historical Society was formed.

'''Water Mill''' is the correct name as per local government and the United States Postal Service. Its ZIP Code is one one nine seven six .

 History 
In one six four four , England gave Edward Howell received four zero acres of land near the new settlement of Southampton to build a mill for settlers to grind their grain into meal. It became a landmark, and people began referring to other settlements that popped up as east or west of water mill. By the one eight zero zero s, the area was known as '''Water Mills''' and was later changed to '''Water Mill'''. Today, the hamlet boasts its status as the only settlement on the South Fork of Long Island with both a functioning watermill and windmill.

 '''Wyandanch''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Suffolk County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of one zero , five four six . 

Wyandanch is a community in the Town of Babylon. Located within the same exits of Lindenhurst , Amityville and Huntington.
 
History
This village is named after Chief Wyandanch, a leader of the Montauk tribe during the one seven th-century.
Wyandanch is also home of one of the best (according to many fans) rappers to ever grace the mic: Rakim. He was born and raised in Wyandanch.

 Geography 
Wyandanch is located at four zero  four four ' five zero  North, seven three  two two ' six  West ( four zero . seven four seven zero nine eight , - seven three . three six eight two seven five ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one one . three km ( four . four mi ).  one one . three km ( four . four mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

History-Originally known as Half Way Hollow Hills, West Deer Park ( one eight seven five ), Wyandance,( one eight nine three ),the area of scrub oak and pine barrens south of the southern slope of Half Hollow terminal moraine was named Wyandanch in one nine zero three by the Long Island Rail Road to honor Chief Wyandanch of the Montauk native American group, and end confusion between the Deer Park and West Deer Park railroad stations

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one zero , five four six people, two , five two five households, and two , one one three families residing in the CDP. The population density is nine three one . eight km ( two , four one zero . eight mi ). There are two , seven seven six housing units at an average density of two four five . three km ( six three four . six mi ). The racial makeup of the CDP is one zero . two one % White, seven seven . seven two % African American, zero . seven five % Native American, zero . five seven % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, six . two six % from other races, and four . four seven % from two or more races.  one six . three five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , five two five households out of which four six . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three nine . seven % are married couples living together, three five . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and one six . three % are non-families. one one . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and four . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is four . one four and the average family size is four . two five .

In the CDP the population is spread out with three five . six % under the age of one eight , one zero . five % from one eight to two four , two nine . three % from two five to four four , one eight . two % from four five to six four , and six . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is two eight years. For every one zero zero females there are eight nine . two males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight three . eight males.

 '''Yaphank''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Suffolk County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of five , zero two five . 

Yaphank is a community in the south part of the Town of Brookhaven. 

 History 
In the mid one eight th century, a man named John Homan built two mills along Carmen's River, which runs directly through the center of the town. These two mills inspired the first name for the town: Millville. In one eight four six a post office was opened in the town, but because there were thirteen other towns named Millville in New York State at the time, the town was renamed Yaphank , from the local Native American word '' Yamphanke '', meaning '' bank of a river ''.

In one eight four three the Long Island Rail Road built a railroad station in Yaphank (still named Millville at the time), and virtually overnight the small mill town became a major commercial center. By one eight seven five , Yaphank had two grist mills, two lumber mills, two blacksmith shops, a printing office, an upholstery shop, a stagecoach line, two physicians, a shoe shop, two wheelwright shops, a meat market, a dressmaker and a general store.

Yaphank was the home of Camp Upton, which was used as a boot camp in one nine one seven . In one nine four seven , the United States War Department transferred the Camp Upton site to the U.S. Atomic Energy Commission (AEC), and it now serves as the home of Brookhaven National Laboratory. Before the end of World War I, more than three zero , zero zero zero men were received their basic training there. Perhaps the most notable person to have trained at Camp Upton was the songwriter Irving Berlin. It was there he composed the musical comedy Yip Yip Yaphank, which had a brief run on Broadway.

 Geography 
Yaphank is located at four zero  five zero ' seven  North, seven two  five five ' four five  West ( four zero . eight three five two seven seven , - seven two . nine two nine one five nine ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of three six . five km ( one four . one mi ).  three six . two km ( one four . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . three km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . seven eight % water.

 Demographics

 Information about Bethel and Woodstock 
The Town of Bethel was the actual location of the Woodstock festival in one nine six nine . Because it was originally scheduled to take place in the Town of Woodstock in Ulster County, New York, that name persisted in spite of the change in venue.

 '''Cochecton''' is a town located in west-central Sullivan County, New York, USA.  As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , three two eight . The name is an aboriginal word for low land. 

The '''Town of Cochecton''' (its official name) is situated on the Delaware River, directly across from Damascus, Pennsylvania, to which a bridge over the river provides access. The village of Cochecton has a ZIP Code of one two seven two six ; the ZIP Codes for two other communities located within the town's boundaries  Cochecton Center and Lake Huntington  are one two seven two seven and one two seven five two respectively.

 History 
Cochecton was reportedly the home of Tammany, a Native American sage of the Lenape. 

In the original charter of one six six four , Cochecton marked the border between New York and New Jersey. After a long dispute - the New York-New Jersey Line War - the final border was set further South, near Port Jervis.

The town was formed from the Town of Bethel in one eight two eight . The Town of Delaware was formed from part of Cochecton in one eight six nine . 

The town once had a station on the Binghamton branch of the Erie-Lackawanna Railroad, but passenger service on this branch ceased in one nine seven one ; the branch has since been taken over by Conrail. More recently, various proposals were made to restore service on the line, but none have yet been adopted.

The correct pronunciation of the town's name is cuh-SHEK-ton, leading many to mistakenly believe the name is of French origin; the name is in fact derived from Cushektunk, a local Native American word meaning low land (alluding to the town's location in the upper Delaware Valley).

 Geography 
The west town line is the border of Pennsylvania. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of nine six . eight km ( three seven . four mi).  nine four . nine km ( three six . seven mi) of it is land and one . nine km ( zero . seven mi) of it is water. The total area is one . nine five % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one , three two eight people, five five five households, and three seven six families residing in the town. The population density is one four . zero km ( three six . two mi). There are nine five five housing units at an average density of one zero . one km ( two six . one mi). The racial makeup of the town is nine six . five four % White, zero . nine zero % African American, zero . zero eight % Native American, zero . six zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . nine eight % from other races, and zero . nine zero % from two or more races.  one . six six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are five five five households out of which two seven . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five six . zero % are married couples living together, seven . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three two . one % are non-families. two six . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . one % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  '''Fallsburg''' is a town located in Sullivan County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one two , two three four . The town takes its name from a waterfall on the Neversink River. 

The '''Town of Fallsburg''' is in the eastern part of the county. 

 History 
The town was created in one eight two six from parts of the Towns of Neversink and Thompson. During the period after World War II, the town was the center of resort hotel development.

On March nine , one eight two six , the New York State Legislature passed an act establishing the Town of Fallsburg. The town was created from portions of the already existing towns of Thompson and Neversink and derived its name from the falls located there in the Neversink River. One month later, on April four , the first town meeting was held in the schoolhouse where the hamlet of Fallsburg is today. The settlement was then known as Neversink Falls.

Little is known about the earliest white settlers of the town. Their names and the exact dates they located there have not been documented, but it is thought they arrived before the Revolutionary War. They were most likely Dutch and migrated from Ulster County. They probably reached the area by using an old Indian trail that crossed the Neversink River at Dennistons Ford near Glen Wild. Some of these settlers established a small settlement near the ford while others continued north, crossing the Sheldrake Creek, and settleing on a ridge east of Kiameshia Lake and Lake Anawana. This settlement was primarily in the Town of Thompson and was completely abandoned during the French and Indian War. A few of the settlers at Dennistons Ford, however, were thought to have braved it out or only left for a short period of time.

The Neversink River runs from north to south through the Town of Fallsburg and played an important part in its early development. In the late one seven eight zero s the valley above the falls in the Neversink, between what is now Fallsburg and Hasbrouck, became known as having fertile and cheap land. This brought another influx of settlers from Ulster County. They came south from Wawarsing by way of the Chestnut Creek through Grahamsville as well as traveling north by way of Dennistons Ford. By one eight zero zero , the upper flats along the river were pretty well settled.

During the first part of the one eight zero zero s, the region was primarily a farming community. Life at the time must have been a frugal. The long haul over the mountains to Kingston prevented a lot trade and it sometimes took as long as nine zero days for mail to reach Fallsburg from Kingston. When the D and H Canal was opened in one eight two eight it brought a change to the area. Now the nearest outlet for their products was in Ellenville. Up until this time Hasbrouck had been the major settlement in the area. The upper Neversink River between Woodbourne and Hasbrouck was the heaviest settled because of the rich flatlands there along the river. A number of sawmills and gristmills were built there in the one seven nine zero s further establishing the area. Hasbrouck was named in honor of Anthony Hasbrouck, a wealthy and prominent man who settled there in the early one eight zero zero s. Mr. Hasbrouck lived in the old stone house that is still standing today. The hamlet was a major business area for many years with a variety of shops and stores and had it own post office from one eight four six to one nine two three .

The closest settlement in the Town of Fallsburg to Ellenville and the D  ( seven nine . zero mi ).  two zero one . zero km ( seven seven . six mi ) of it is land and three . five km ( one . four mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . seven three % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one two , two three four people, three , seven six one households, and two , four seven eight families residing in the town. The population density is six zero . nine km ( one five seven . six mi ). There are six , six six one housing units at an average density of three three . one km ( eight five . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the town is seven five . one nine % White, one five . five six % African American, zero . four three % Native American, one . one seven % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, five . zero four % from other races, and two . five eight % from two or more races.  one four . five three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , seven six one households out of which three three . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four seven . zero % are married couples living together, one four . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three four . one % are non-families. two seven . six % of all households are made up of individuals and one zero . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six zero and the average family size is three . one six .

In the town the population is spread out with two three . three % under the age of one eight , eight . nine % from one eight to two four , three two . eight % from two five to four four , two four . zero % from four five to six four , and one one . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are one three three . eight males. The median income for a household in the town is $ three three , zero three six , and the median income for a family is $ three nine , two one six . Males have a median income of $ three one , nine four nine versus $ two four , five eight three for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one six , seven four four .  two zero . five % of the population and one five . nine % of families are below the poverty line.  '''Monticello''' is a village located in the Town of Thompson in Sullivan County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of six , five one two . It is the county seat of Sullivan County. The village was named after the residence of Thomas Jefferson. 

The '''Village of Monticello''' is in the central part of the town, adjacent to New York Route one seven . Monticello is the largest village in the county. 

 History 
The village was founded in one eight zero four , five years before one eight zero nine when Sullivan County, New York came into being, incorporated in one eight three zero . The founders, John P. Jones and Samuel F. Jones, admirers of Thomas Jefferson, named the village after his Virginia home, Monticello.

 Geography 
Monticello is located at four one  three nine ' one three  North, seven four  four one ' two six  West ( four one . six five three five two nine , - seven four . six nine zero four five four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one zero . five km ( four . one mi ).  one zero . five km ( four . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are six , five one two people, two , five five four households, and one , four six zero families residing in the village. The population density is six one seven . eight km ( one , six zero one . five mi ). There are three , seven five eight housing units at an average density of three five six . five km ( nine two four . two mi ). The racial makeup of the village is five five . five seven % White, two nine . three two % African American, zero . three one % Native American, two . one three % Asian, zero . zero five % Pacific Islander, eight . one four % from other races, and four . four eight % from two or more races.  two three . one six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , five five four households out of which three one . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, two nine . nine % are married couples living together, two one . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and four two . eight % are non-families. three six . one % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three nine and the average family size is three . one four .

In the village the population is spread out with two eight . three % under the age of one eight , eight . seven % from one eight to two four , two seven . five % from two five to four four , two two . eight % from four five to six four , and one two . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three five years. For every one zero zero females there are nine five . two males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . five males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ two two , six seven one , and the median income for a family is $ two nine , five five four . Males have a median income of $ three two , six two three versus $ two two , eight two seven for females. The per capita income for the village is $ one four , four three three .  three five . six % of the population and three zero . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, four nine . seven % of those under the age of one eight and two three . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Interesting Facts 
The town hosts one of the only Sullivan County-based radio stations. WSUL nine eight . three FM.

The local bus station is serviced by Greyhound Bus Lines, and Shortline acts like a main hub for the entire area.

The village of Monticello is the county seat and thus it has the county's court house, jail, and the county's only Wal-Mart.

Monticello is famous for its Monticello Raceway which attracted people from all over the northeast in its heydey. Now the Raceway has turned into a Racino , hosting electronic slot machines as well as horse racing.

Monticello is also home to the main station of Sullivan County's only Paid, private ambulance company. Mobilemedic EMS. Mobilemedic was sullivan county's first Paramedic service, running their first ALS call approx. one five years ago.

 '''Neversink''' is a town located in Sullivan County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of three , five five three . 

The '''Town of Neversink''' is in the northeast corner of the county. The Neversink River that flows through the town is claimed to be the birthplace of American fly fishing. 

 History 
The town was formed from the Town of Rochester in Ulster County, New York in one seven nine eight before Sullivan County was formed. The Town of Rockland was created from part of Neversink in one eight zero nine , and part of Neversink was used to make the newer Town of Fallsburg in one eight two six . When the Neversink and Rondout reservoirs were built, the communities of Old Neversink (Neversink Reservoir), Eureka , Montella , and Lackawack (Rondout Reservoir) were lost.

 Geography 
Part of the town is in the Catskill State Park. The nothern and eastern town lines are the border of Ulster County, New York.

 Facts about Apalachin 

An early resident was Benjamin F. Tracy, father of the modern navy. 

In November one seven , one nine five seven , the heads of the U.S. Mafia held the Apalachin Meeting at the home of Joseph Barbara, a conference of mobsters who had gathered to iron out various issues in the underworld. The gathering was quickly broken up when a curious state trooper turned up and sent some of the most powerful gangsters in the country fleeing through the surrounding countryside. In this context, Mafiosi and the FBI sometimes just refer to the meeting as ''Apalachin''. This meeting was humorously portrayed in the opening sequence of the one nine nine nine motion picture ''Analyze This'', which starred Robert DeNiro and Billy Crystal.

'''Waverly''' is a village located in Tioga County, New York, USA. '''Waverly''' is the largest Village in Tioga County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of four , six zero seven . The name is derived from the novel ''Waverley'' by Walter Scott. 

The '''Village of Waverly''' is in the southwest part of the Town of Barton, but it is so close to the state border that the village is part of a much larger community that runs into Bradford County, Pennsylvania, merging with Sayre, Pennsylvania. The village is adjacent to NY Route one seven , the Southern Tier Expressway. 

 History 
The Village of Waverly was incorporated in one eight five four .

 Current Events 
Efforts are ongoing to try and persuade the State to transform the Waverly Reservoir property into a State Park with river access and nearby golfing privileges. If successful, this would be a big boost for the local economy in the area.

 Geography 
Waverly is located at four two  zero ' one nine  North, seven six  three two ' one six  West ( four two . zero zero five two four seven , - seven six . five three seven eight nine two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of six . one km ( two . three mi ).  five . nine km ( two . three mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . one four % water. 

The village is on the east side of the Chemung River and is north of the confluence of the Chemung with the Susquehanna River. 

 Employment 
The Leprino Cheese factory is the largest employer in Waverly. The plant is located half in New York and half in Pennsylvania due to the mostly unnoticible border of it's neighboring state. It specializes in mozzarella cheese produced from milk from local dairy farms. It currently is the largest supplier of cheese for pizza chains in eastern United States. The plant is especially odoriferous at times and has long been a source of local controversy.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are four , six zero seven people, one , eight seven seven households, and one , one two eight families residing in the village. The population density is seven seven six . eight km ( two , zero one three . three mi ). There are two , zero five two housing units at an average density of three four six . zero km ( eight nine six . seven mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine seven . six three % White, zero . six three % African American, zero . two four % Native American, zero . five zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . three zero % from other races, and zero . six nine % from two or more races.  one . two four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , eight seven seven households out of which three zero . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four three . zero % are married couples living together, one three . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and three nine . nine % are non-families. three three . seven % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three two and the average family size is two . nine eight .

In the village the population is spread out with two four . zero % under the age of one eight , eight . one % from one eight to two four , two seven . two % from two five to four four , two zero . three % from four five to six four , and two zero . four % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are eight four . one males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are seven eight . eight males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ two eight , nine five eight , and the median income for a family is $ three nine , five two two . Males have a median income of $ three one , five four four versus $ two four , four nine two for females. Out of the total population, one eight . three % of those under the age of one eight and five . six % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Schools 
The Waverly Central School District provides a quality educational program for approximately two , two zero zero students from kindergarten through grade one two .

Elementary students receive their program in one of three uniquely sized and situated elementary schools. The Elm Street School, with six five zero students, and the Lincoln Street School, with four zero zero students, are located in the Village of Waverly. Chemung Elementary School, with one five zero students, is located in a rural setting in the Town of Chemung.

 Waverly Middle School is a school of approximately three five zero grade seven and eight students located on the High School campus.

 Waverly High School offers an outstanding program to approximately seven zero zero students in grades nine - one two .

The Waverly District takes great pride in offering a number of unique and challenging programs at both the elementary and secondary levels.

 '''Trumansburg''' is a village located in Tompkins County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , five eight one . The name is a misspelling of the name of an early settler. 

The '''Village of Trumansburg''' is in the Town of Ulysses. 

 History 
The village was originally named Tremaine's Village, after an early settler, Abner Treman, who was granted the land for his service in the American Revolutionary War. The village centers on a cascade on the creek in the center of the village that provided power for grain mills. Local lore has it that a mistake when building the post office, replacing the e in Treman with a u , led to the name Trumansburg .

Trumansburg in the one nine th century was dominated by Col. Hermon Camp, an officer in the War of one eight one two who settled in what was to become the village. For many years he was the local postmaster, and founded a bank, now the Tompkins Trust Company, the dominant bank in the county. His imposing and elegant Federal style house remains the largest in the village.

In the latter half of the two zero th century as the importance of agriculture in New York waned, the village became home to many faculty and staff at nearby Cornell University and Ithaca College as well as many musicans. Between one nine six one and one nine seven zero , Robert Moog built electronic music equipment including Theremins and his famous synthesizers in a downtown storefront. 

As of two zero zero five , its mayor is John R. Levine, the original author of Internet for Dummies .

The life of the village
Trumansburg has become a combination of a bedroom suburb for Ithaca and a modest tourist destination, with restaurants and antique stores.
Since one nine seven three the village's best known business has been the Rongovian Embassy to the USA, a diplomatic motif bar and restaurant that frequently features local, national and international musical talent. Since one nine nine three , the Finger Lakes GrassRoots Festival of Music and Dance has taken place each July at the village fairgrounds and is hosted by nationally popular Trumansburg-based band Donna the Buffalo. The village is also located along the Cayuga Wine Trail and is close to Taughannock Falls.

Other cultural resources include the Ulysses Philomathic Library, a member of the Finger Lakes Library System, and the Trumansburg Conservatory of the Arts, which offers concerts and music lessons.
First Presbyterian Church of Trumansburg, photographed in one nine three three 
Baptist, Catholic, Episcopalian, Methodist, and Presbyterian churches are located within the village, and Baptist and Mormon churches are located just outside the village limits.

The Trumansburg Central School District consists of the Elementary School, Russel I. Doig Middle School, and Charles O. Dickerson High School, all of which share a campus at one zero zero Whig Street.

 Geography 
Trumansburg is located at four two  three two ' two six  North, seven six  three nine ' three six  West ( four two . five four zero four four seven , - seven six . six six zero one two one ). The village is located on the Trumansburg Creek (also known as Frontenac Creek) which arises on the ridge west of the village and empties into Cayuga Lake at Frontenac Point.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of three . one km ( one . two mi ).  three . one km ( one . two mi ) of it is land and zero . eight three % is water.

Transportation
Trumansburg is bisected by NY Route nine six , a state highway constructed in one nine six one that runs north to Waterloo and south to Ithaca. Tompkins Consolidated Area Transit (TCAT) provides local bus service to Ithaca with connections to long distance bus and air service there.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , five eight one people, six eight two households, and four two four families residing in the village. There are seven one five housing units at an average density of two two eight . two km ( five nine two . two mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine six . five two % White, zero . seven six % African American, zero . zero six % Native American, zero . seven zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . five seven % from other races, and one . three nine % from two or more races.  two . zero nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six eight two households out of which three three . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four eight . five % are married couples living together, one zero . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and three seven . eight % are non-families. three three . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three two and the average family size is two . nine seven .

In the village the population is spread out with two six . nine % under the age of one eight , five . nine % from one eight to two four , two three . zero % from two five to four four , two eight . six % from four five to six four , and one five . six % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Ulysses''' is a town located in northwest Tompkins County, New York at four two . five one two North, seven six . six one eight West. The town was named after the hero of the ''Odyssey''. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of four , seven seven five . The Town of Ulysses is northwest of the City of Ithaca. Taughannock Falls, the highest waterfall in the state is in Taughannock Falls State Park in Ulysses; the falls drop two one five feet ( six six meters), one of the highest waterfalls east of the Rocky Mountains. Much of the town is devoted to dairy farms and fruit orchards.

 Geography 
The eastern town line is at Cayuga Lake, one of the Finger Lakes. The town's northern boundary line is the border of Seneca County, New York. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, Ulysses has a total area of nine five . four km ( three six . eight mi ).  eight five . four km ( three three . zero mi ) of it is land and one zero . zero km ( three . nine mi ) of it is water. The total area is one zero . four eight % water.

 History 
Ulysses is located in the Central New York Military Tract, which was used to pay soldiers of the American Revolution. It was named by Robert Harpur in one seven nine zero for the hero of Homer's Odyssey. The town once contained the towns of Dryden, Enfield and Ithaca (named for Ulysses' home in ancient Greece). Ulysses was organized in one seven nine four as part of Onondaga County and was incorporated in one eight seven two . The village of Trumansburg, the main settlement in Ulysses, was started by Abner Tremaine in one seven nine two .

'''Eternit''' is a brand of roofing and panelling material made of fibres and cement. 

Originally the fibres were asbestos, and the material was commonly used in housebuilding because of its low cost, fire-resistance, light weight and other properties. 

Now, after the discovery of its extremely high carcinogenic toxicity, its use is forbidden in many countries although it is still sold under the counter in some places, especially in coastal areas where Eternit stands the climate much better than other materials. Many ex-workers have sued the company. How the Eternit in use should be handled differs from country to country. In the USA most scientists advise removing it from houses and removal has to be done by specialized technicians. In other countries, like Sweden, the advice is to keep it as it is considered best not to disturb it and risk release of asbestos.

'''Cragsmoor''' is a hamlet (and census-designated place) located in Ulster County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of four seven four . 

Cragsmoor is located atop the Shawangunk Ridge, in the south part of the Town of Wawarsing. Sam's Point Preserve is near Cragsmoor. 

 Geography 
Cragsmoor is located at four one  four zero ' six  North, seven four  two three ' one seven  West ( four one . six six eight two nine eight , - seven four . three eight seven nine six two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one one . three km ( four . four mi ).  one one . three km ( four . four mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

The center of town is about one , eight zero zero feet ( five four eight . six m) above sea level, much higher than neighboring communities such as Ellenville and Walker Valley.

As a whole, the hamlet has a wooded, rustic ambience. Most homes are rather modest and old, but sit on large lots with many tall shade trees. There are also many large undeveloped woodlots, and thus property values in Cragsmoor are higher than in the rest of Wawarsing. Other than the post office, there is no business district to speak of.

The Long Path hiking trail passes through the center of town on its way to Sam's Point.

 Demographics

 '''Hardenburgh''' is a town located in Ulster County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two zero eight . 

The '''Town of Hardenburgh''' is located in the western part of Ulster County.  The town is inside the Catskill State Park. 

 History 
The first settlers arrived around one eight zero two . 
Hardenburgh was established in one eight five nine from the Towns of Denning and Shandaken. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of two one one . two km ( eight one . five mi ).  two one zero . six km ( eight one . three mi ) of it is land and zero . six km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two eight % water.

Hardenburgh sits in the western corner of the county, bordering Sullivan and Delaware counties, deep in the Catskill Mountains. Five of the Catskill High Peaks are within or along its borders.

Because of the mountains, the only direct route from Hardenburgh to the rest of the county are hiking trails over them. Any vehicular traffic must go through either Sullivan or Delaware counties.

One of those lesser mountains, Dry Brook Ridge, effectively divides the town as well. The portion north of it, in the Dry Brook valley, uses the ZIP code and telephone exchange of the nearby Delaware County hamlet of Arkville. The portion to the south, containing the headwaters of the famous Beaver Kill trout stream, is likewise oriented to the Sullivan County hamlet of Lew Beach to its south, although it contains a few of its own unique toponyms such as Turnwood, its only real road junction.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two zero eight people, nine five households, and five seven families residing in the town. The population density is one . zero km ( two . six mi ). There are two seven five housing units at an average density of one . three km ( three . four mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine six . one five % White, zero . four eight % African American, zero . zero zero % Native American, two . four zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . nine six % from other races, and zero . zero zero % from two or more races.  zero . nine six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are nine five households out of which two zero . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five one . six % are married couples living together, four . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and four zero . zero % are non-families. three five . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . zero nine and the average family size is two . seven zero .

In the town the population is spread out with one five . four % under the age of one eight , five . three % from one eight to two four , two six . four % from two five to four four , three three . two % from four five to six four , and one nine . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four seven years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero five . nine males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero nine . five males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ three five , two seven eight , and the median income for a family is $ four one , two five zero . Males have a median income of $ two seven , zero eight three versus $ two one , three eight nine for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one nine , one eight four .  one three . two % of the population and one two . three % of families are below the poverty line.  '''Rosendale''' is a town located in Ulster County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of six , three five two . 

The '''Town of Rosendale''' once had an incorporated village with the same name, until voters dissolved the incorporation. The town is centrally located in the county. 

 History 
The Town of Rosendale was formed in one eight four four from parts of other towns.

Rosendale was once famous for the cement it produced. The area is rich in limestone deposits. Rosendale Cement was used in the construction of many New York City landmarks and bridges. The industry fell into decline in the early one nine zero zero s. One old cement mine still exists as a museum, others are used by the records storage management company Iron Mountain for storing anything from microfiche to data backup tapes.

'''''Metal Machine Music''''' is a two-disc LP (now audio CD) by Lou Reed. It was released by RCA Records in one nine seven five . The album was re-released by BMG in one nine nine eight and again by Buddah Records in two zero zero zero . 

''Metal Machine Music'' is generally considered to be either a joke, a begrudging fulfillment of a contractual obligation, or an early example of noise music. According to Reed (despite the original liner notes), the album entirely consists of guitar feedback played at different speeds. He recorded the work on a four-track tape recorder in his New York apartment, mixing the four tracks for stereo.

In its original form, each track occupied one side of an LP record and lasted around one six minutes, though the fourth side was specifically cut to repeat the last few seconds endlessly. The rare eight -Track Tape version has no silence in between programs, so that it plays continuously without gaps on most players. 

In an interview with rock journalist Lester Bangs, Reed claimed that he had intentionally placed sonic allusions to classical works like Beethoven's ''Eroica'' and ''Pastoral'' in the distortion. It is not clear whether or not he was actually being serious.

The album was ranked number two in the one nine nine one book ''Slipped Discs: The Worst Rock 'n' Roll Records of All Time'' by Jimmy Guterman and Owen O'Donnell. The book gives sympathy to legendary record cutting engineer Bob Ludwig for having to listen to the album in its entirety.

Comedian Gilbert Gottfried sometimes used the record as audio backdrop, when he hosted USA Network's ''USA Up All Night'' in the one nine nine zero s.

 '''Shandaken''' is a town located in Ulster County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of three , two three five . The name is from a native phrase for land of rapid waters.
