 '''Shawangunk''' is a town in Ulster County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one two , zero two two . 

The '''Town of Shawangunk''' is in the southwestern part of the county. Like the neighboring mountain range, the name is sometimes pronounced Shongum.  

'''Name'''

The name is a Dutch transliteration of the indigenous Munsee Lenape Scha-WAN-gunk.  The Lenape linguist Raymond Whritenour reports that, Schawan is an inanimate intransitive verb meaning 'it is smoky air' or 'there is smoky air.'  Its noun-like participle is schawank, meaning that which is smoky air.'  Adding the locative suffix gives us schawangunk ('in that which is smoky air' or, more simply, 'in the smoky air').

Whritenour suggests the name derives from the burning of a Munsee fort by the Dutch in one six six three (the Second Esopus War) beside the creek later named the Shawangunk Kill, near the western terminus of what is now Old Fort Road.  European colonists truncated Shawangunk into SHONG-gum, a pronunciation frequently misrepresented as the original indigenous name.(Sources: Marc B. Fried, two zero zero five . Shawangunk Place-Names, pp three - one two .; Christopher Spatz, Smoke Signals, 
Spring two zero zero five , Shawangunk Watch: Friends of the Shawangunks  ( five six . five mi ).  one four five . six km ( five six . two mi ) of it is land and zero . eight km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . five five % water.

The Wallkill River flows through the eastern half of town and lends it its name, which it flows through, while the western (Walker Valley) half climbs the slopes of the eponymous mountains.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are one two , zero two two people, three , four three three households, and two , five five seven families residing in the town. The population density is eight two . six km ( two one three . nine mi ). There are three , seven five four housing units at an average density of two five . eight km ( six six . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the town is eight six . four nine % White, eight . one four % African American, zero . two six % Native American, zero . nine two % Asian, zero . zero one % Pacific Islander, two . eight six % from other races, and one . three two % from two or more races.  six . nine six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , four three three households out of which three nine . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six one . five % are married couples living together, eight . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two five . five % are non-families. two zero . two % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . seven eight and the average family size is three . two one .

In the town the population is spread out with two two . four % under the age of one eight , eight . five % from one eight to two four , three eight . three % from two five to four four , two two . two % from four five to six four , and eight . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are one three four . three males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one four four . three males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ five two , three six six , and the median income for a family is $ five nine , nine seven five .  '''Bolton''' is a town located in Warren County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two , one one seven . 

The '''Town of Bolton''' is on the east border of the county. 

 History 
The first settlements began around one seven nine two . 
The Town of Bolton was formed from part of the Town of Thurman in one seven nine nine . Bolton lost some of its territory as three new towns were created in the county. 

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of two three three . three km ( nine zero . one mi ).  one six four . two km ( six three . four mi ) of it is land and six nine . one km ( two six . seven mi ) of it is water. The total area is two nine . six two % water. 

The east town line, defined by Lake George is the border of Washington County. This town line includes the lake so that only the opposite shore is in Washington County. The town in within the Adirondack State Park. 

US Route nine N follows the lake along the west shore, connecting the major settlements. Interstate eight seven , the Northway, runs along the west town line.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two , one one seven people, nine four one households, and six two eight families residing in the town. The population density is one two . nine km ( three three . four mi ). There are two , one six four housing units at an average density of one three . two km ( three four . one mi ). There are nine four one households out of which two two . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five five . three % are married couples living together, eight . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and three three . two % are non-families. two seven . one % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two five and the average family size is two . seven zero .

In the town the population is spread out with one nine . four % under the age of one eight , four . four % from one eight to two four , two three . nine % from two five to four four , three two . nine % from four five to six four , and one nine . four % who are six five years of age or older.  Glens Falls, New York located in southern Warren County in eastern New York State.

'''Glens Falls''' is a city located in Warren County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one four , three five four . The name is derived from the large waterfall in the Hudson River at the southern base of the city. 

The '''City of Glens Falls''' is in the southern part of Warren County. The city has referred to itself as the Empire City.  Glens Falls is also known as Hometown U.S.A. , a title given to it by Look Magazine in one nine four four . The city is located in the southeast corner of the county, surrounded by the Town of Queensbury to the North, East, and West, and by the Hudson River and Saratoga County to the South. 

 History 
The area was originally called '''Chepontuc''', but was renamed '''The Corners'''. In one seven six six it was renamed Wings Falls for Abraham Wing, who established a permanent settlement. After title was granted to Colonel Johannes Glen, the name was changed to Glens Falls. 

Glens Falls became an incorporated village in one eight three seven , but was re-incorporated in one eight seven four and one eight eight seven . The city charter was granted in one nine zero seven at which time, the city became a separate entity from the Town of Queensbury into which it had formerly been incorporated as its largest village. 

 Historic and Noteworthy Sites in Glens Falls 
'''The Oldest Building in Glens Falls.''' 

The oldest building in Glens Falls, located in the downtown area, is one of the few buildings in the city that predates one eight six four . The stone and brick structure at the bottom of the hill was erected circa one eight one five and served as Calvin Robbin's Blacksmith Shop. In one eight six four there was a massive fire that destroyed most of buildings in the central business district.

'''The Feeder Canal'''
Across from this historic canal is a hydro-electric power-plant on Glens Falls. The canal was created circa one eight two zero to feed water into the Champlain Canal. During the Early one nine th Century the New York State Canal System served a crucial portion of the state's economy. In Glens Falls, Lime, Marble, Lumber, and agricultural products were shipped from the docks at the base of Canal Street.

'''Fort Amherst Road'''
Located near this road is the location where Fort Amherst once was. The fort is no longer extant, however portions of the wood foundations were known as late as one eight eight zero . The fort constituted a block house marking the half-way point on the road between Fort Ann and Fort William Henry at the head of Lake George. This Fort system, erected by the British, was built to secure the northern territories of the colony from incursions from the French during the French and Indian War.

'''Civil War Monument'''
Only solders from the Civil War are listed on the monument. Many battles of the war are listed.

'''Quaker Meeting House'''
The Quaker Meeting House, an Italianate edifice on Ridge St. was built in one eight seven five , and originally contained no heating system. 

'''DeLong House'''
Presently the home of the Glens FallsQueensbury Historical Association and the Chapman Historical Museum. A Greek Revival and Second Empire edifice on the corner of Glen and Bacon Streets. A Queen Anne style Carriage Barn also sits on the property.

'''Glens Falls Hospital'''
Founded in the summer of one eight nine seven , by a group of twelve local physicians, the Glens Falls Hospital was meant to serve the entire Upper Hudson River Valley. Solomon A. Parks generously donated his home in Glens Falls for the Hospital. The present structure has been modified and enlarged several times to better serve the needs of the community.

'''Charles R. Wood Theater'''
This theater opened in two zero zero three on Glen Street, in the heart of Glens Falls. A former Woolworth store for years, it is now the home of the Adirondack Theatre Festival during the summer months, and introduces culture and theatre into the surrounding community.

'''Hyde Museum'''
The center among a triplet of revival type residences constructed for the daughters of Samuel Pruyn, the Hyde is today a world class museum of european, american, and contemporary art. The principle collection is presented in it's original domestic context as a private collection.

'''First Presbyterian Church'''
The fifth house of worship of this Congregation chartered in one eight zero three was constructed in one nine two nine . A gothic revival design by Ralph Adams Cram, is among the most outstanding buildings in Glens Falls. Cram was also contracted subsequently by St. Mary's Parish to design the Academy building of the same name on Warren Street.

 Schools 
Glens Falls High School before renovations. From www.gfsd.org'''Glens Falls High School''' is located at one zero Quade Street near Sherman Avenue in Glens Falls, New York. The school has been recently renovated and modernized with a new three rd floor edition, new rooms, and new computers. It features a Spanish and French department, a science department (Biology, Chemistry, Forensics, Earth Science, Physics, etc.), a History and Social Sciences department (Global Studies, World War II, AP European History, etc.), Business (Keyboarding, Business Law, Accounting), and an Art and Music department. 

The Glens Falls City High School has a variety of athletic activities, most notable of which are the basketball team, lacrosse team, soccer team, football team, and field hockey team, and basketball team. In two zero zero four the Basketball team made it to the state championship, . However, more recently in two zero zero five , the lacrosse team won the NYS Class B Section II title, and the football team lost in the first sectional game, whilst the Varsity soccer team made it to the sectional finals for the first time since the ' seven zero 's. The girls field hockey team was able to clench the B title. 

All GFHS Athletic teams carry the name Indians.  (Glens Falls Indians)

'''Adirondack Community College'''

As part of the State University of New York, Adirondack Community College (ACC) is a two-year college accredited by the Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools. ACC offers extensive Associate degrees and Certificate programs and practices transfer agreements with numerous Colleges and Universities.

 Regional Events 
'''Glens Falls Snow Sculpture Contest'''
Crowds gathered in City Park late January two zero zero four to see the completion and judging of the New York State Snow Sculpting Championships. In this competition professional snow-sculpters were given a large block of snow and carved it into an incredible sculpture. The artists worked night and day in bitter cold conditions to complete their sculptures before January two four , two zero zero four when a panel of judges decided the first, second, and third place winners. The sculptures were judged based on intricacy and creativeness. Third Place and the People's Choice Award went to Spring , a sculpture featuring kittens and daffodils. Winning Second Place was Incepience . And the First Place Winner was Winding up Ahead of Evolution , a design featuring a human head with gears winding up in the back. There were many other great sculptures with everything from seahorses to dragons.

'''The Adirondack Balloon Festival'''
Each year, a balloon festival is held near Glens Falls at the Warren County Floyd Bennet Memorial Airport. The weather for the two zero zero four  balloon festival was great. Many balloons went up, including the Old Mcdonald's barn balloon, the Little Bees balloons, the American eagle balloon, the Chief Rocky balloon, the Octopus Garden balloon, and the Purple People Eater balloon. The MegaRay, the world's largest kite, was also scheduled to fly.

 Civic Facilities 

The ''' Glens Falls Civic Center''' opened in one nine seven nine and hosts sports and entertainment events in downtown Glens Falls. This versatile multi-purpose complex includes an arena for sporting events, concerts, family activities, dance, theater and trade shows as well as banquet facilities. The Civic Center includes four , eight zero six permanent arena seats focused on an ice hockeybasketball-type aren and the ability to accommodate an audience of up to seven , eight zero zero people for concerts and other events. The Civic Center is home to the Adirondack Frostbite, of the UHL, the Adirondack Wildcats of the USBL, the New York State Boys Public High School Basketball Tournament and the Federation Basketball Tournament of Champions as well as The Adirondack Stampede, a rodeo.

'''The Glens Falls YMCA''' features many different recreational activities for people of all ages. The YMCA is currently undergoing construction and renovations to make it better than ever. Plans have been made for the addition of an indoor running track, a new swimming pool for non-competitive swimmers, a youth fitness center, and more.
The expansion will be done in three phases. The first phase includes an arts and crafts room, youth fitness center, and group exercise and family activity rooms. Phase two is the construction of the indoor track, and phase three the new Lifetime Pool, which will have shallower, warmer water for the elderly and small children.
The YMCA has received about two five zero grants from individuals, foundations, and companies to cover the cost of the expansion.

 '''Queensbury''' is a town located in Warren County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two five , four four one . The town is named in honor of Princess Charlotte, the consort of George III. 

The '''Town of Queensbury''' is one of the oldest in the county. Queensbury is located in the southwestern part of the county, north of the City of Glens Falls, which it borders. 

 History 
Major efforts at settlement began with the Queensbury Patent in one seven six two , which enticed Quaker settlers to move into the area, the Township of Queensbury, the next year. The Quakers left during the Revolutionary War, but returned in one seven eight three when hostilities ended in the area. 

In one seven eight six , the town was re-established as the Town of Queensbury. It lost territory in one seven nine two upon the formation of the Town of Lake Luzerne and in one eight zero two to form part of the Town of Lake George. In one nine zero two , the then largest village within Queensbury, Glens Falls, incorporated as a city and became a separate municipality. Today Queensbury is the largest suburb of Glens Falls and now surpasses the city in population.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one six seven . nine km ( six four . eight mi ).  one six three . two km ( six three . zero mi ) of it is land and four . seven km ( one . eight mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . seven eight % water. 

The south town line is the border of Saratoga County, New York, and the east town line is the border of Washington County, New York. The south town line is partly defined by the Hudson River, parts of the northern town line border Lake George.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two five , four four one people, nine , nine four eight households, and seven , one six two families residing in the town. The population density is one five five . nine km ( four zero three . eight mi ). There are one one , two two three housing units at an average density of six eight . eight km ( one seven eight . one mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine seven . five four % White, zero . five five % African American, zero . two zero % Native American, zero . seven one % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . two two % from other races, and zero . seven six % from two or more races.  one . one two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are nine , nine four eight households out of which three four . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five nine . one % are married couples living together, nine . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two eight . zero % are non-families. two two . six % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . five two and the average family size is two . nine seven .

In the town the population is spread out with two five . three % under the age of one eight , six . one % from one eight to two four , two eight . three % from two five to four four , two five . one % from four five to six four , and one five . two % who are six five years of age or older. The median income for a household in the town is $ four seven , two two five , and the median income for a family is $ five four , eight eight zero .  Schools 

The Queensbury Union Free School District is located at four two nine Aviation Road. The over- two zero zero acre campus consists of the Queensbury High School, the Queensbury Middle School, the William H. Barton Intermediate School and the Queensbury Elementary School, with several large grass fields for play and sport, a running track, running trails, an indoor pool (located in the Elementary School) and several tennis and basketball courts. The school employs more than two six zero teachers for a student population of nearly four , zero zero zero in two zero zero five . 

Queensbury UFSD Mission Statement: To empower all students to be lifelong learners, inspired to pursue their dreams and contribute to the global community.

 In computer architecture and engineering, a '''sequencer''' or '''microsequencer''' is a part of the control unit of a CPU. It generates the addresses used to step through the microprogram of a control store. Usually the addresses are generated by some combination of a counter, a field from a microinstruction, and some subset of the instruction register.

A counter is used for the typical case, that the next microinstruction is the one to execute.

A field from the microinstruction is used for jumps, or other logic.

Since CPUs implement an instruction set, it's very useful to be able to decode the instruction's bits directly into the sequencer, to select a set of microinstructions to perform a CPU's instructions.

Most modern CPUs are considerably more complex than this description suggests. They tend to have multiple cooperating micromachines with specialized logic to detect and handle interference between the micromachines.



Microprocessors
 
   
 In the field of electronic music, a '''sequencer''' was originally any device that recorded and played back a sequence of control information for an electronic musical instrument. Nowadays, the term almost always refers to the feature of recording software which allows the user to record, play back and edit MIDI data. This is distinct from the software features which record audio data.

Early analog music sequencers used control voltagetrigger interface, but were replaced by digital hardware- or software-based MIDI sequencers, which play back MIDI events and MIDI control information at a specified number of beats per minute.

As computer speeds increased in the one nine nine zero s, audio recording, audio editing, and sample triggering features were added to the software. Software so enhanced is called a digital audio workstation (DAW). DAWs almost always include sequencing features but, strictly speaking, go beyond what a sequencer is.

Many sequencers have features for limited music notation, or are able to show music in a piano roll notation. (For software designed specifically for music notation, see the scorewriter article.)

Though the term 'sequencer' is today used primarily for software, some hardware synthesizers and almost all music workstations include a built-in MIDI sequencer. There are also standalone hardware MIDI sequencers.

Music can be sequenced in a sense using trackers such as ModPlug Tracker, and a drum machine can be viewed as a specialized music sequencer.

 '''Williamson''' is a town located in Wayne County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of six , seven seven seven . The town was named after Charles Williamson, a land agent.

 History 
The first settler, Daniel Russell, built a log cabin in Pultneyville in one seven nine four . This hamlet became the only port until the opening of the Erie Canal.

In one eight one four during the War of one eight one two , British troops landed in Pultneyville, and an agreement was made with the villagers allowing them to seize some stores without resistance, but a dispute broke out and firing began on both sides.

 '''Briarcliff Manor''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York. It is shared between the towns of Mount Pleasant and Ossining, and lies entirely within the zip code of one zero five one zero . As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of seven , six nine six , over nine one % of whom lived in the Town of Ossining. The town is known for its award-winning school district (ranked nine four th nationally as a public school system) and is also home to a campus of Pace University. It is the site of the Trump National Golf Course (formerly Briar Hall Country Club, originally Briarcliff Lodge early one nine zero zero 's), owned by real-estate mogul Donald Trump. 

 Geography 
Briarcliff Manor is located at four one  eight ' three nine  North, seven three  five zero ' two nine  West ( four one . one four four zero three three , - seven three . eight four one three four zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one seven . three km ( six . seven mi ).  one five . four km ( five . nine mi ) of it is land and one . nine km ( zero . eight mi ) of it is water. The total area is one one . two four % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are seven , six nine six people, two , four three five households, and one , nine nine six families residing in the village. The population density is five zero one . one km ( one , two nine eight . nine mi ). There are two , five zero one housing units at an average density of one six two . eight km ( four two two . one mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine zero . seven four % White, one . seven three % African American, zero . zero five % Native American, five . four four % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander, zero . nine five % from other races, and one . zero five % from two or more races.  three . one three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race. Though it has few minorities, Briarcliff has a decent-sized Jewish population, and a synagogue called Congregational Sons of Israel (CSI).

There are two , four three five households out of which four four . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven four . five % are married couples living together, six . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and one eight . zero % are non-families. one five . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and nine . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight four and the average family size is three . one six .

In the village the population is spread out with two six . eight % under the age of one eight , nine . zero % from one eight to two four , two four . seven % from two five to four four , two four . eight % from four five to six four , and one four . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four zero years. For every one zero zero females there are eight seven . three males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight one . three males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ one three three , two seven two , and the median income for a family is $ one five seven , six zero seven . Males have a median income of $ one zero zero , zero zero zero versus $ six one , two zero eight for females. The per capita income for the village is $ five eight , six four six .  two . five % of the population and zero . eight % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one . one % of those under the age of one eight and five . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. Briarcliff, like nearby Chappaqua or Scarsdale, is a very wealthy village.

 Neighborhoods 

'''The Tree Streets''' are a network of streets named after trees. They are popular trick or treating sites for the local youth.
'''North State Road''' is a street with apartment buildings, businesses, and small houses. This area incorporates streets such as Schrade Road, which also has apartment buildings and small houses. The Wyndcrest condominium development is also in this area.
'''Downtown''', commonly referred to as '''Town''', is the closest thing to a main street in Briarcliff Manor. Briarcliff's main street is Pleasantville Road. It is home to the Briarcliff Manor Fire Department as well as a number of commercial establishments. Farther along the road are the Briarcliff High School and Briarcliff Middle School. The elementary school, Todd School, is located on Ingham Road, which intersects with Pleasantville Road.
'''Long Hill Road''' stretches a long distance across Briarcliff. Many nice houses can be found on this road, as well as on the roads that branch off of it, such as Law Road, Holly Place, Cottonwood Lane, Hirst Road, and Cedar Drive East and West.
'''Rosecliff''' is a development of similar houses in the south-west corner of Briarcliff Manor.
'''Carleton Avenue and Washburn Road''' are streets in an area that falls under the postal and school systems of Briarcliff but is not governed under the village. It is governed under the Town of Mount Pleasant.

 Other Significant Areas 

'''Scarborough''' - an area of Briarcliff Manor along the Hudson River that has a train station on the Metro North Hudson Line. This is a less desirable area of Briarcliff because it is not incorporated in Briarcliff's School District.
'''Chilmark''' - Chilmark is a residential community along with a shopping center that is on the northern end of Briarcliff. The name of the area comes from the castle-like Chilmark Mansion. Like Scarborough, Chilmark is not incorporated in Briarcliff's School District. Children from this neighborhood fall under the Ossining School District's jurisdiction.
 Both Chilmark and Scarborough enjoy the priviledge of Briarcliff Manor Recreation.

 '''Croton-on-Hudson''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of seven , six zero six . As a village, it is located in the Town of Cortlandt. It should not confused with nearby Crotonville, which is actually part of Ossining, NY. The village was incorporated in one eight nine eight . It is named after Croton (modern Crotone), Italy.

It's the site of the New Croton Dam, Croton Point and the one eight th century Van Cortlandt Manor, a National Historic Landmark. It is the original home of the Hudson Institute. Near by is the Thomas J. Watson Research Center and the GE John F. Welch executive training center. The village's railroad station, Croton-Harmon, is served by Metro North and Amtrak. Metro North's main shops and yards are located here.

 Government Politics 
Mayor Dr. Gregory J. Schmidt, R-I
Trustee Thomas P. Brennan (Deputy Mayor), R-I 
Trustee Charles A. Kane, D-I
Trustee James M. Steinberg, R-I
Trustee Leo A. W. Wiegman, D-I

The Village Mayor, Dr. Gregory J. Schmidt, elected in March two zero zero five , has set forth an agenda to promote recreation in the village. Furthermore, the village has recognized the need for a community center, a gathering place for all residents of Croton.

The Republican Party currently holds a three - two majority on the Village Board of Trustees.

 '''Dobbs Ferry''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one zero , six two two . 

The '''Village of Dobbs Ferry''' is located in, and is a part of, the Town of Greenburgh. The village ZIP code is one zero five two two .

 History 
Named after a ferry service that traversed the Hudson River at this location, Dobbs Ferry may well have played a small but vital role in the American Revolutionary War. According to original manuscripts of General George Washington, Washington met at Dobbs Ferry with French allies the Comte de Rochambeau and the Comte de Grasse at this location to plan the Battle of Yorktown that ended the war with Great Britain. Although historians have long debated whether this meeting took place at present day Dobbs Ferry or at the ferry location directly opposite on the Hudson River, a monument has long stood in Dobbs Ferry at Livingston Manor, the site of the claimed one seven eight one meeting. 
 
 Geography 
Dobbs Ferry is located at four one  zero ' four six  North, seven three  five one ' five eight  West ( four one . zero one two seven two nine , - seven three . eight six six zero two six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of eight . two km ( three . two mi ).  six . three km ( two . four mi ) of it is land and one . nine km ( zero . seven mi ) of it is water. The total area is two three . zero three % water.

Commuter service to New York City is available via the Dobbs Ferry train station, served by Metro-North Railroad.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one zero , six two two people, three , seven nine two households, and two , five seven zero families residing in the village. The population density is one , six eight zero . eight km ( four , three five zero . zero mi ). There are three , nine four one housing units at an average density of six two three . six km ( one , six one four . zero mi ). The racial makeup of the village is eight zero . seven zero % White, seven . three eight % African American, zero . zero eight % Native American, seven . five six % Asian, zero . zero nine % Pacific Islander, one . nine three % from other races, and two . two six % from two or more races.  seven . zero zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , seven nine two households out of which three four . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five four . eight % are married couples living together, one zero . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three two . two % are non-families. two seven . six % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . five five and the average family size is three . one three .

In the village the population is spread out with two six . zero % under the age of one eight , seven . three % from one eight to two four , two seven . four % from two five to four four , two four . one % from four five to six four , and one five . two % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are nine five . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight four . five males.

Out of the total population, one . five % of those under the age of one eight and four . six % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Ferncliff Cemetery is located here, famous as the burial grounds for many celebrities including Malcolm X, Judy Garland, Joan Crawford, Ed Sullivan, Aaliyah, Jason 'Jam Master Jay' Mizell, Alan Freed, and others.

History
Hartsdale, a CDPhamletvillagepost-office in the town of Greenburgh, NY, lies on the Bronx River just two zero miles north of New York City. It is served by the Metro North Harlem River commuter rail line into Grand Central Station. Hartsdale is the home of America's first CaninePet Cemetery (started by veterinarian Samuel Johnson in one eight nine six ), and the world's first Carvel Ice Cream store ( one nine three four ). 

Hartsdale's earliest settlers were the Weekquaeskeeks, a sub-tribe of the Algonquin Indians. Weekquaeskeek is an Algonquin term believed to mean place of the bark kettle , and this kettle appears in the Greenburgh town seal today.

After the earliest British colonialists arrived, the area was developed under the Manor system when Frederick Philipse, a British Loyalist, was given the land by the British government. As Lord of his Philipse Manor, he leased his land to tenant farmers who, for a time, were believed to have lived alongside their Native American neighbors.

There is evidence to show that Hartsdale played quite a role ruring the Revolutionary War, some of which still stands today. On October two eight th, one seven seven six , a Revolutionary War battle was fought alongside the Bronx River, near the site of the current Hartsdale train station. The Odell House (on Ridge Road, built in one seven three two ) served as the headquarters for the French General the Comte de Rochambeau, and is where the Comte and George Washington are supposed to have formed an alliance in the Battle of Yorktown. The house was later named after John Odell, Washington's guide who bought the house in one seven eight five . In one nine six five , his descendents deeded the house to the Sons of the American Revolution, and today the house is a museum.

After the American colonialists won the Revolutionary War, Frederick Philipse fled, his land was confiscated and sold to the remaining farming tenants, many of whom were descendants of the Hart family. The intersection of Central Park Avenue and Hartsdale Avenue was named Hart's Corners after Robert Hart, one of these farmers, and in the mid one eight zero zero s the entire area became known as Hartsdale .

The area remained largely agrarian until one eight six five , when Eleazar Hart deeded land for the development of the New York and Harlem Railroad line into Manhattan, setting the stage for Hartsdale's change into a more cosmopolitan commuter village. Between one eight eight zero - one nine four zero , large tracts of farmland and estates were subdivided and converted into private houses and apartments at a furious pace. By the one nine six zero s, almost no remaining farmland was left for sale.

In one nine zero four , the successful German-Jewish banker Felix Warburg ( one eight seven one - one nine three seven ) purchased large tracts of land to build his five zero zero -acre Woodlands estate in Hartsdale, a summer home next to the country club where he and his wife Frieda Schiff Warburg ( one eight seven six - one nine five eight ) spent considerable time. The estate would later become an important site in the history of modern American ballet, when on June one zero th, one nine three four , their son Edward Warburg ( one nine zero eight - one nine nine two ) helped produce the first performance of Balanchine's masterpiece Serenade . In keeping with the family's philanthropic efforts, one five zero remaining acres were deeded on her death in one nine five eight by Frieda Schiff Warburg to the town to build a public school. These one five zero acres are now the home of the Greenburgh Central seven School District and Woodlands High School. The main Warburg mansion currently serves as the school district headquarters, but other remnants from the original estate grounds can still be seen standing in the surrounding woods and neighboring streets. The Warburg family's New York City home would later be donated to become the Jewish Museum of New York.

On February nine th, one nine two eight , Hartsdale became the birthplace of the American Couch Potato when the Scottish inventor John Logie Baird ( one eight eight eight - one nine four six ) transmitted the world's first inter-continental short-wave television signal from Coulsdon, Surrey (a suburb of London, England) to his colleague O.G. Hutchinson in the cellar of Robert Hart, an Amateur Radio Operator (call sign two CVJ) in Hartsdale, New York. 

In one nine three two , Henry Gaisman, the founder of the Gillette razor blade, purchased one three five acres of land from George Christiancy, the former U.S. minister to Peru. He later married a former Catholic nun, Catherine Gaisman. In one nine five seven , he and his wife Catherine passed the title for his land to the New York Archdiocese with the agreement that they could live there as long as they wished. Mr. Gaisman died in one nine seven four , and his wife remained on the estate until she moved to Connecticut in one nine nine five . In one nine nine nine , the estate was saved from sale and development when the Town of Greenburgh acquired the property and reopened it as the Hart's Brook Nature Preserve. Part of the agreement included the preservation of some portion of the estate as a home for retired Catholic nuns.

Hartsdale is one of the few communities immediately surrounding New York City that still has two working farms, both on Secor Road. It also has several parks including the two five -acre Secor Woods park, the one seven zero -acre Ridge Road park, and eight six -acre Rumbrook park. 

The town can generally be subdivided into several different areas including the Village or downtown part (East Hartsdale Avenue), Manor Park, Windsor Park, Poet's Corners, Ridge Road, Orchard Hill, College Corners, or more specifically one of the several condominium developments built since the one nine seven zero s. Over the years, the town has attracted many different ethnic groups, and the downtown village has a significant Japanese population with Japanese shops, restaurants, real-estate brokers, and even a supermarket all within walking distance of East Hartsdale Avenue.

The popular J-Pop RapR&B duo Heartsdales borrow their name from Hartsdale, as the two members spent considerable time here.

 '''Irvington''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of six , six three one . 

The '''Village of Irvington''' is located on the western side of the Town of Greenburgh.

 History 
Irvington was named after the American author Washington Irving, who had a residence there that still exists today, preserved as a museum. Sleepy Hollow (formerly North Tarrytown) is the nearby village after which Irving wrote his most famous work, ''The Legend of Sleepy Hollow''. 

Among Irvington's other famous residents was Madame C.J. Walker, America's first female millionaire. An African American woman, she made her fortune in creating the first ever hair-straightening method, which including a shampooing technique along with a chemical product that helped the process. In one nine one seven , Madame Walker had a $ two five zero , zero zero zero country home built on Broadway in Irvington. The neo-Palladian-style mansion still stands today; recently, however, several plots of the land have been sold to make room for newer homes. 

Jazz saxophonist Stan Getz also lived in Irvington. His estate Shadowbrook , as it is called, is less than a mile from both Washington Irving's home and the Walker mansion. 

Irvington is also home to one of the few surviving octagon houses. As with all river communities in Westchester County, Irvington is traversed by a stretch of the Croton Aqueduct (about three -miles of aqueduct run through village).

Today, Irvington is home to several important businesses, companies, and institutions and people including:
 Eileen Fisher, clothing design company
 the Internet portals iWon, Excite and MyWay
 The Nevis Laboratories of Columbia University
 AskJeeves, a division of Ask.com
 The Student Center, community site for teens by lots , as required by New York state law when a village election is tied ( eight four seven votes for each candidate).

The count that took place on election night gave Flood a one-vote lead. On March one eight , the Westchester County Board of Elections recounted the votes, giving Malloy a one-vote lead. Turning to two unopened absentee ballots, the board found that one was for Flood, resulting in a tie. The other absentee ballot was not opened as the name on the envelope did not match any names on the voter-registration list. Susan B. Morton, who had registered to vote as Susan Brenner Morton, stepped forward three days later and demanded that her vote for Malloy be counted. For several months afterward, various suits, motions, and appeals were filed in state courts. On October two zero , the Court of Appeals, New York State's highest court, denied requests by Malloy and Morton, leaving the election in a tie. To comply with state law, the village had to use random lots to decide the winner.

State law does not specify the method of drawing lots, so the village opted to draw quarters from a bag. Eight quarters were used. Four had a bald eagle on the back and represented Malloy. Flood was represented by four quarters with the Statue of Liberty on the back. Village TrusteeDeputy Mayor Richard Livingston, a Republican, drew a quarter from the bag. It was handed to Village Clerk Lawrence Schopfer, who declared Flood to be the winner. Flood was then sworn in for his sixth two-year term as mayor of Irvington.  

 Geography 
Irvington is adjacent to the Hudson River. 

Irvington is located at four one  two ' four  North, seven three  five one ' five six  West ( four one . zero three four three seven one , - seven three . eight six five four seven one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one zero . five km ( four . zero mi ).  seven . two km ( two . eight mi ) of it is land and three . two km ( one . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is three zero . nine four % water.

Commuter service to New York City is available via the Irvington and Ardsley-on-Hudson train stations, served by Metro-North Railroad.

For population by religious background, Irvington has a strong Jewish population totaling over three zero % of the total six , six three one residents. However, more current local estimates rate the Jewish population above three five %. (See note---)
The rest of the population is made up of a variety of Christian faiths as well as a myriad of other faiths which have not progressed as fast as the Jewish population, or the Christian majority.
NOTE: In the last decade, the Jewish population of Westchester experienced a boom of Jewish residents, with the total population growing by over four zero %. In Irvington, this change has reflected the society there. Current estimates show that on average, over a quarter of new sold houses are sold to Jewish families. The Jewish population is now the largest non-majority religious group in Irvington.

Irvington is also home to a large number of Unification Church members (often semi-pejoratively referred to as Moonies ), including several high-ranking families. This is due to the fact that there are several Church compounds and buildings located in Irvington, or in the neighboring village of Tarrytown. In fact, Reverend Sun Myung Moon himself, the leader of the Church internationally, has a large private residence located in East Irvington. His residence there probably led to the large influx of Church members.

'''Larchmont''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of six , four eight five . As a village, it is located within the Town of Mamaroneck. It is located on the shore of the Long Island Sound. 

Before the advent of the automobile, Larchmont was a resort community serving wealthy New York City residents. A few of the grand hotels remain to this day, though they have been converted to other uses such as private residences. The world-renowned Larchmont Yacht Club still hosts an annual Race Week competition. It is adjacent to Manor Park, which was designed by well-known landscape architect Frederick Law Olmsted. Famous residents have included: Lou Gehrig, New York Yankees baseball legend; Ang Lee, director of The Hulk  Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon and Brokeback Mountain ; Marcus Camby, basketball player for the Denver Nuggets; Matt Dillon; Joan Rivers; playwright Edward Albee; Moss Hart award winning playwright and author of Act One, his best selling biography; director D.W. Griffith; novelist Jean Kerr and her husband, the Pulitzer Prize winning theater critic Walter Kerr. Larchmont also contains three of the six schools in the Mamaroneck Schools District.

In July of two zero zero five , CNNMoney and Money magazine ranked Larchmont one one th on its list of the one zero zero Best Places to Live in the United States.

 History

 '''Mount Vernon''' is a city located in Westchester County, New York, immediately north of New York City's The Bronx. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of six eight , three eight one . A July one , two zero zero two Census estimate showed the population at six eight , six one five .

The city has three Metro North railroad stations: '''Mount Vernon West''', '''Mount Vernon East''' and '''Fleetwood'''.

Denzel Washington, Ken Singleton, Dick Clark, Art Carney, Heavy D, Al (B Sure) Brown, Betty Shabazz, Ben Gordon, Gus Williams, Michael Imperioli, Pete Rock and CL Smooth, Roz Kelly, and P. Diddy were born (or grew up) in Mount Vernon.

 Geography 
Mount Vernon is located at four zero  five four ' five one  North, seven three  four nine ' five zero  West ( four zero . nine one four zero six zero , - seven three . eight three zero five zero seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one one . three km ( four . four mi ).  one one . three km ( four . four mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . four six % water.

Neighborhoods
Residents usually define two distinct parts of Mount Vernon (North side and South side), whose dividing line is usually considered to be the tracks of the New Haven Line of Metro North commuter railroad. The North side of Mount Vernon contains Fleetwood, a neighborhood of shops, houses and apartments that seems to have a spiritual identity of its own. The South side of Mount Vernon contains many industries and is more densely populated than the North. The majority of the tax base for Mount Vernon is generated by the industrial section and retail shopping located on the South side.

Historically, the North side and South side had a racialethnic division as well, given that the South side is an almost exclusively African-American enclave (and has been since the one nine six zero 's) and the North side was mostly Italian, Jewish and Irish (in that order). However, since the late one nine eight zero 's the North sideSouth side distinction has become more of a zoning-related and socio-economic divide and less of a racialethnic one as every part of the North side is now very much integrated, with the eastern sections tending to be majority Black and the western sections (including Fleetwood) majority White, but no neighborhood being entirely one or the other. In general (though there are a few exceptions) the neighborhoods of the South side are less suburban than the North side. The city's website (see external links below) boasts that its residents come from nine eight different countries around the world.

In two zero zero four , a shopping mall opened on Sandford Blvd. to help economically revitalized the South side and bring in visitors who may not normally traverse the area. The mall contains Target, T.J. Maxx, PETCO, and Bed, Bath + Beyond. Across the street a Best Buy and Staples stores have opened as well.

 '''New Rochelle''' is a city located in Westchester County in the US state of New York, one six miles ( two six km) from Grand Central Terminal in New York City. The city is named after the city of La Rochelle in France, which was a stronghold of the Huguenots.

 History 

 one seven th century
New Rochelle's history begins with the purchase by Thomas Pell of the Pelham Manor tract, of which the city would become part, from the Siwanoy Indians in one six five four .

In one six eight seven a purchase agreement was made between John Pell, nephew of Thomas Pell, and Jacob Leisler, a wealthy merchant and acting Governor of New York who acted as agent for the Huguenots, for six , zero zero zero acres ( two four km ) of land and a donation of one zero zero acres ( zero . four km ) for a French church.

In one six eight nine , thousands of Huguenots - French Protestants who left France following the revocation by Louis XIV of the Edict of Nantes, which had protected them from religious persecution - began settling the area. Their new home was named after La Rochelle, the port from which they had departed France. There is a monument in Hudson Park which commemorates all the names of these Huguenot settlers. 

Also in one six eight nine , John and Rachell Pell officially deeded the six , one zero zero acres ( two five km ) of New Rochelle to Jacob Leisler. The Deed requires as an Acknowledgment to the Lord of the said Manor one Fatt Calfe on every fouer and twentieth day of June yearly and every Year Forever (if demanded). 

 one eight th century

In one seven seven five General George Washington stops in New Rochelle on his way to assume command of the Army of the United Colonies in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

In October of one seven seven six , the British Army occupies New Rochelle and Larchmont. General Sir William Howe establishes headquarters on the heights above North Avenue opposite Eastchester Road. The British support troops, four , zero zero zero Hessians and Waldeckers under Lieutenant-General Baron von Knyphausen, landed at Davenport Neck. The British left New Rochelle on October two five th, clogging available roads and leaving destruction behind. Two days later, the Battle of White Plains was fought, bringing victory to the British but allowing Washington to regroup his troops. New Rochelle became part of the Neutral Ground. 

Through the one eight th century, New Rochelle, with a one seven nine zero population of six nine two residents, remained a modest village. It retained an abundance of agricultural land, three zero zero acres ( one . two km ) of which was awarded in one seven eight four to the patriot Thomas Paine by New York State for his service to the cause of independence. He wrote his pamphlet Common Sense while residing there. Now located on a small street in New Rochelle, the Thomas Paine Cottage is a small museum where many Revolutionary re-enactments are played out.

 one nine th century

In one eight seven nine , Hohn H. Starin, former United States Congressman and New York transportation king, buys five islands, names them Glen Island and creates perhaps the first theme park open to the public. His one two steamboats transported millions of New York residents and others to the attractions which included a zoo, a natural history museum, a railway, a German beer garden (around the castle-like structure which still stands today), a bathing beach, and a Chinese pagoda. A chain ferry transported visitors from a mainland dock.

In one eight nine two , the New Rochelle Public Library is established and located in the Trinity School, on Trinity Place. Rose Hill Gardens, located on what is now Rose Hill Avenue, is one of the largest botanical gardens in the country during the one eight zero zero 's. The first orchid in the United States is cultivated here.

In one eight nine six , David's Island is re-named Fort Slocum after General Henry Warner Slocum, a Civil War officer. Fort Slocum becomes the largest recruiting depot east of the Mississippi River, with greatest use during World War I and World War II.

 two zero th century

In the early part of the twentieth century, the County's famous Glen Island Casino on Long Island Sound continued to draw such celebrities as Glenn Miller, the Dorsey Brothers and Ozzie Nelson.

In one nine three zero , New Rochelle population hits five four , zero zero zero , up from three six , two one three , in one nine two zero . In the early three zero 's, it is the wealthiest city per capita in New York State, the third wealthiest in the country.

New Rochelle had two of the first suburban branch department stores in America, with Arnold Constable opening on Main Street in the one nine four zero s and Bloomingdale's purchasing the locally owned Ware's Store in the late one nine four zero s.

New Rochelle was the scene of the first court-ordered school desegregation case in the north when the United States Supreme Court decided in one nine six two that New Rochelle's Lincoln School boundaries had been intentionally drawn to create segregated elementary school districts. Lincoln School was closed and demolished in one nine six five with students of that district allowed to attend any other city elementary school. Today the school district is known for its diversity, and the High School honors civil rights leader Whitney Young in the name of its auditorium and civil rights martyr Michael Schwerner in the name of its library.

Part of downtown New Rochelle near the Metro North train station was revitalized in the summer of one nine nine nine with the opening of the $ one nine zero million New Roc City, an entertainment complex featuring a one nine -screen movie theater, Westchester's first and only IMAX theater, mini-golf, go karts, an arcade, a health club, restaurants, a hotel, and a supermarket. New Roc City was built on the former Macy's and New Rochelle Mall sites.

 Geography 
The '''City of New Rochelle''' is on the Long Island Sound. It is the second largest city in Westchester County, after Yonkers.

New Rochelle is one of the largest suburbs of New York City. It is located a mere two miles from the New York City borough of The Bronx, and about one five miles northeast of Midtown Manhattan. 

New Rochelle is located at four zero  five five ' four three  North, seven three  four seven ' three  West ( four zero . nine two eight five eight four , - seven three . seven eight four two three zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three four . three km ( one three . two mi ).  two six . eight km ( one zero . four mi ) of it is land and seven . five km ( two . nine mi ) of it is water. The total area is two one . seven seven % water. The city has a rough triangle shape, approximately one zero miles ( one six km) from north to south and one . five miles ( two km) from east to west at its widest point.

 New Rochelle in Fiction, Film, Television and Theater 

In the early two zero th century New Rochelle was home to some of the first movie studios in the country.

Edwin Thanhouser establishes Thanhouser Film Corporation on the corner of Warren and Grove Street. Thanhouser's Million Dollar Mystery was one of the first serial motion pictures. After a devastating fire in one nine one three , the studio moved to Main Street near Echo Avenue.
Parts of the film ''Catch Me If You Can'' take place in New Rochelle.
 one nine four one - The cartoon charatcter Mighty Mouse was created at the Terrytoons Studio in New Rochelle. Terrytoons, which was created by Paul Terry in one nine two nine , produced cartoons for one zero , zero zero zero movie theatres across the country during the one nine four zero 's and one nine five zero 's.  
The early one nine six zero 's TV hit The Dick Van Dyke Show starring Dick Van Dyke and Mary Tyler Moore was set in New Rochelle.
 one nine seven six - Ragtime, a novel written by New Rochelle resident E. L. Doctorow was released and later became a major motion picture of the same name. Other celebrated works include Welcome to Hard Times, Loon Lake and Worlds Fair
 The Broadway show Ragtime is set in New Rochelle.
 The Broadway show (and George M. Cohan song)  four five Minutes from Broadway was about life in New Rochelle in the late one eight nine zero 's.

 Transportation

'''By Bus''': served by Greyhound Lines, and the Westchester County Bee-Line service.

'''By Car''': major highways include Interstate nine five and the Hutchinson River Parkway.

 Monroe College has a campus, with full dormitories in the downtown section of New Rochelle.

 Charles Moose

'''Charles Alexander Moose''' served as the one five th Montgomery County, Maryland, Police Chief from August two , one nine nine nine , to June one eight , two zero zero three , when he resigned to write a book. During October two zero zero two , he became known nationwide as the primary official in charge of the efforts to apprehend the Beltway snipers. Later analysis revealed that Moose's insistence on pursuing only white suspects delayed the solving of the crime spree.

Moose earned a PhD in urban studies and criminology from Portland State University.

In September two zero zero three , he released a book about the investigation titled ''Three Weeks in October: The Manhunt for the Serial Sniper'' (ISBN zero five two five nine four seven seven seven nine ). He resigned because he was barred by law from accepting a monetary advance for the book while still performing his job.

 '''North Castle''' is a town located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one zero , eight four nine . It has no villages.

 History 
'''Early Area History'''
It is believed that the last native inhabitants of North Castle were the Siwanoy people of the Algonquin group. The Siwanoy were taken by force in one six four four by Europeans. 
In the early one seven zero zero s King William gave his favorite courtiers the West Patent, of which the western portion of North Castle was a part, and the Middle Patent, the eastern part of North Castle. 

At one time North Castle included all the territory that became incorporated as New Castle in one seven nine one . The territory comprising both towns was once part of the Parish of Rye organized in one six nine three .

The area quickly became a refuge for people fleeing from religious persecution. People from Massachusetts and Connecticut settled the eastern part of North Castle, while Quakers from Rye and Long Island flocked to Armonk. By one seven three zero , North Castle was already an established settlement. 

The Rev. Mr. Wetmore of the Anglican Church, the Church of England, wrote in one seven two eight to the Venerable Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts that North Castle was: 

chiefly settled by people of no religion at all, very ignorant and barbarous being descendants of Long Island Quakers. 
The one seven nine eight Quaker Meeting House has been saved by The North Castle Historical Society and restored on its property at four four zero Bedford Road, Armonk. 

'''Early Town History'''
Incorporated as the town of North Castle on March seven , one seven eight eight . 
On March seven , one seven eight eight , New York State passed an act for dividing the counties of the state into towns: 

And that all that part of the said county of Westchester, bounded southerly by Mount Pleasant, the White Plains, the town of Harrison and Connecticut, easterly by Connecticut, Pound Ridge and Bedford, northerly by the Manor of Cortlandt and Bedford, and westerly by Bronx river and Mount Pleasant, shall be and hereby is erected into a town by the name of North Castle. 
North Castle's name is said to derive from a barrier built by the Mohican people to protect themselves from enemy attacks which stood on the hillside now occupied by the international headquarters of I.B.M. Corporation. 
They called the site North Fort and European settlers later gave it the more elegant name of North Castle. The name Armonk is derived from another Mohican word, 'Cohamoog', which means 'the wide, flat place where the water runs'. 

'''Revolutionary Times'''
During the Revolution, New and North Castle were officially considered neutral territory. However, the area was strongly patriotic. One significant Revolutionary War conflict did occur in North Castle - The Battle of White Plains. This battle of October two eight , one seven seven six was a series of short skirmishes between General Washington's small American army and General William Howe's much larger British cottage industries did exist. For example, some farmers supplemented their income by becoming shoemakers or shirtmakers. 
The coming of the railroad in the one eight four zero 's marked the beginning of the shift away from the region's agricultural way of life. Towns without the railroad, such as North Castle, suffered economically. 

Although the railroad by-passed North Castle, one so-called 'railroad' did run through the town. The Underground Railroad, which helped runaway slaves travel to freedom in Canada, operated a station between Armonk and North White Plains. 

North Castle was also hurt economically by the Industrial Revolution since new manufacturing techniques made the local cottage industries impractical. From one eight six zero to one nine zero zero , North Castle's population declined from two , two zero zero to one , four seven zero . 

'''Twentieth Century'''
By the early two zero th century, however, North Castle's economy improved dramatically due to the New York City purchase of reservoir land and the resulting building of the Kensico Dam in Valhalla ( one nine zero nine - one nine one five ) which used North Castle granite. Many of the European immigrant stone masons who built the dam later settled in the town's Quarry Heights section. 
Today, North Castle is a community that is ensuring an orderly rate of growth in order to preserve the quality of environment. Citizen participation in town affairs has been a long-standing tradition. It has had a major impact on the character of the community and will continue to make North Castle an exceptional town in which to live. 

'''Source: www.northcastleny.comhistory.html'''

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of six eight . six km ( two six . five mi ).  six two . four km ( two four . one mi ) of it is land and six . two km ( two . four mi ) of it is water. The total area is nine . zero six % water.

There are three , five eight three households out of which four four . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven four . six % are married couples living together, six . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and one six . two % are non-families. one three . one % of all households are made up of individuals and five . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. Population growth in the Town of North Castle reflects the pattern of rural to suburban development typical of the post World War II years. Like many other suburban communities in Westchester County and the nation, the Town experienced a surge of population growth between one nine four zero and one nine seven zero . The overall rate of growth was moderate between one nine seven zero and one nine nine zero because of national economic conditions, including the rising cost of land, construction and interest, which helped to bring about a general decline in housing construction. The median price of houses sold in North Castle in one nine nine eight was approximately $ six zero zero , zero zero zero .

 '''Peekskill''' is a city located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two two , four four one .

It is known as the site of the Peekskill Riots, although they technically occurred in the neighboring town of Cortlandt.

Peekskill is the birthplace of current New York Governor George Pataki as well as T.C. Boyle (born one nine four eight ), Paul Reubens (a.k.a. Pee-Wee Herman), Mel Gibson, Benjamin Civiletti, and basketball star Elton Brand. Gov. George Pataki was a Peekskill mayor and was the first upstate Governor since Franklin D. Roosevelt. However, some dispute that claim because Westchester County (even the northern portion) is usually not considered to be Upstate New York, nor is Garrison in Putnam County, where he lived when he became governor.

Peekskill is also the setting for the sitcom ''The Facts of Life''.

Transport
Peekskill train station provides commuter service to New York City via Metro-North Railroad. The Bear Mountain Bridge gives road access to Bear Mountain Park across the Hudson River, and to the United States Military Academy at West Point.

History
Peekskill was incorporated as a village within the town of Cortlandt in one eight one six . It became a city on July two nine  one nine four zero .

Peekskill was the site of a meteorite fall on Oct. nine , one nine nine two , just before midnight. The fall was recorded on film by at least one six different people. It is only the fourth meteorite in history for which an exact orbit is known. The meteorite had a mass of one two . four kg ( two seven . three lb) and punched through the trunk of Peekskill resident Michelle Knapp's red Malibu coupe as it struck.

 '''Pelham Manor''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of five , four six six . As a village, it is located in the Town of Pelham.

 History 
EARLY PELHAM MANOR.
On November one one , one six five four , Thomas Pell negotiated a treaty with Wampage, Chief of all the Siwanoy Indians and acquired title to about five zero , zero zero zero acres including all of today's Bronx and everything east of the Hutchinson River north to Mamaroneck. Pell took possession of his property and called it Pelham in honor his tutor Pelham Burton. 

Pell was challenged almost immediately by the Dutch who sent the Marshall of the Dutch Court in March one six five five with a court order stating that the English were trespassing on Dutch territory. Pell refused to accept the Dutch order and for the next several years they tried unsuccessfully to dislodge him. Finally, on September two one , one six six four English warships, supported by a militia unit called the Westchester Trained Band and led by Thomas Pell, sailed into the harbor of New Amsterdam and accepted the surrender of Governor Stuyvesant.

THE BATTLE OF PELHAM.
War came to Pelham Manor on October one eight , one seven seven six when Sir William Howe, Commander-in-Chief of the British army, landed four , zero zero zero English and Hessian troops near the stables on Pelham Parkway in an action which became the first permanent invasion of the American mainland in the American Revolution.

Howe's objective was to outflank the American army by marching west across today's Bronx along the Boston Post Road. This would also cut off Washington's vital supply route from New England and enable the British to surround Washington and quickly end the rebellion. However, six zero zero 
tough seaman from the Boston area, led by Colonel John Glover, and fighting from behind Pelham Manor's stone walls put an end to Howe's plan and saved Washington's army.
The main significance of the Battle of Pelham lay in the fact that it bought time for Washington to remove the American army from an extremely perilous position and to retreat to White Plains. It is for this reason that the Battle of Pelham has been called the battle that saved the American Revolution. 

INCORPORATION.
In response to resident's demands for improved fire and police protection, as well as water, gas and electricity, Pelham Manor was incorporated as a village. The election for incorporation was held at the Pelham Manor School House on Monday, June eight , one eight nine one . The official incorporation date for the Village is July six , one eight nine one .

 '''Erotomania''' is a rare disorder in which a person holds a delusional belief that another person, usually of a higher social status, is in love with them.

Erotomania is also called '''de Clerambault's syndrome''', after the French psychiatrist Gatan Gatian de Clerambault ( one eight seven two - one nine three four ) who published a comprehensive review paper on the subject (''Les Psychoses Passionelles'') in one nine two one .

History
Early references to the condition can be found in the work of Hippocrates, Erasistratus, Plutarch and Galen. In the psychiatric literature it was first referred to in one six two three in a treatise by Jacques Ferrand (''Maladie d'amour ou Mlancolie rotique'') and has been variously called old maid's psychosis , erotic paranoia and erotic self-referent delusions until the common usage of the terms erotomania and de Clerambault's syndrome.

Berrios and Kennedy (see references) have outlined several periods of history through which the concept of erotomania has changed considerably:

 ''Classical times  early eighteenth century'': General disease caused by unrequited love
 ''Early eighteenth  beginning nineteenth century'': Practice of excess physical love (akin to nymphomania or satyriasis)
 ''Early nineteenth century  beginning twentieth century'': Unrequited love as a form of mental disease
 ''Early twentieth century  present'': Delusional belief of being loved by someone else 

Contemporary syndrome
The core of the syndrome is that the affected person has a delusional belief that another person, usually of higher social status, is secretly in love with them. The sufferer may also believe that the subject of their delusion secretly communicates their love by subtle methods such as body posture, arrangement of household objects and other seemingly innocuous acts. The object of the delusion usually has little or no contact with the delusional person, who often believes that the object initiated the fictional relationship.

Occasionally the subject of the delusion may not actually exist, although more commonly subjects are media figures such as popular singers, actors and politicians. Erotomania has been cited as one cause for stalking or harassment campaigns. The assassination attempt of Ronald Reagan by John Hinckley, Jr. was reported to have been driven by an erotomanic delusion that the death of the president would cause actress Jodie Foster to publicly declare her love for Hinckley.

Late night comedian David Letterman was the target of delusional Margaret Mary Ray.

The term erotomania is sometimes used in a less specific clinical sense meaning excessive pursuit of or preoccupation with love or sex.

Erotomanic delusions are typically found as the primary symptom of delusional disorder, or in the context of schizophrenia.

 Erotomania in fiction 

The Booker Prize winning author Ian McEwan based the novel ''Enduring Love'' around the theme of a science writer who is harassed by an erotomanically deluded person.

In the book Diary of a Madman by Nikolai Gogol, the main character suffers from erotomania.

Erotomania was the cause of Ang lique's (Audrey Tautou) institutionalization in the two zero zero two film ''He Loves Me... He Loves Me Not'' ('' la folie... pas du tout'').

The episode ''Broken Mirror'' of the television show ''Criminal Minds'' deals with erotomania.

 Erotomania is the title of an instrumental on Progressive Metal band Dream Theater's second album, ''Awake'', released in one nine nine four .
