'''Van Halen''' is an International rock band formed in the early- one nine seven zero s. The band's first studio album, ''Van Halen'', released in one nine seven eight is widely regarded as a milestone in rock music. With this first release, the band established itself as a leader in the emerging and commercially successful U.S. heavy metal music genre of the one nine eight zero s. In particular, the band's guitarist, Eddie Van Halen, quickly gained widespread notoriety for his technical prowess and musical sensibility. Almost overnight, he was touted as one of the most innovative and influential American rock and roll guitarists.. The band has also established itself as one of the major live acts of that era, opening up for Journey, Montrose, and later Black Sabbath in one nine seven eight . According to Ozzy Osbourne, bringing Van Halen along on the tour was not the best idea because Van Halen simply outplayed them. It also became very popular for the antics, stage presence and larger-than-life persona of its lead singer, David Lee Roth, who was frequently called Van Halen by new fans. 

From one nine seven eight to one nine nine eight the band released one one studio albums (all of which broke the Top two zero spot of the Billboard two zero zero music charts). The band has sold more than seven five million albums worldwide and has received several Grammy nominations. Van Halen is listed in the Guinness Book of World Records with the most number one hits on the Billboard Mainstream Rock List. According to the Recording Industry Association of America Van Halen is one nine on the list of Top Selling Artists of all time (having sold more than five six million albums in the U.S.). Van Halen is one of five rock groups in the world that have had two albums sell more than one zero million albums in the U.S. (the others being: Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd, The Eagles and Def Leppard).

In addition to being recognized for their artistic contributions, commercial success and popularity, the band is known for drama surrounding the lead singer spot. Although the core instrumentalists and backing vocals have remained constant (Eddie Van Halen, Alex Van Halen and Michael Anthony), the band has recorded studio albums with three different lead vocalists: David Lee Roth, Sammy Hagar and Gary Cherone. Each vocalist has departed (at least once) under cloudy circumstances. Following their two zero zero four concert tour the band is currently on hiatus; once again they have a vacancy in the lead singer position and an uncertain future.

History
Origins
The Van Halen family immigrated from Nijmegen, Netherlands to Pasadena, California in the one nine six zero s. Eddie and Alex's father, Jan Van Halen, was an accomplished saxophonist and clarinetist (his work was featured on the song Big Bad Bill (Is Sweet William Now) from the album ''Diver Down'' ( one nine eight two )). Jan encouraged his sons' love of music. Alex (the older of the Van Halen brothers) and Eddie were both trained as classical pianists during their childhoods. As they grew older, Alex took flamenco guitar lessons and Eddie bought a drum set. According to folklore, while Eddie was out delivering papers to pay for his drums, Alex would practice on them. After hearing his brother play the drum solo from the song Wipe Out , Eddie abandoned the drums for guitar.  

 one nine seven seven Van Halen concert promotion poster by Dennis Loren 

During elementary and middle school, Eddie and Alex formed several different bands at different times, with names like The Trojan Rubber Company,  The Broken Combs, and The Space Brothers.  By the time the brothers were in their teens the band had evolved into a power trio named Mammoth (the original lineup included Eddie on guitar and lead vocals, Alex on drums, and Mark Stone on bass). In one nine seven four , Mark Stone was replaced by Michael Anthony, who was then fronting his own band called Snake. With no dedicated lead singer, Eddie and Michael took turns singing lead. 

David Lee Roth, a local entrepreneur, and lead singer of a rival Los Angeles band, had begun renting out his public address system to Mammoth in one nine seven three . Eddie and Alex grew tired of paying the PA Tax to Diamond Dave, and in one nine seven four brought him into the band as their lead singer. Upon discovering that another band in the L.A. area was also named Mammoth, at Roth's suggestion, they changed their name to '''Van Halen''' (passing on the name 'Rat Salad', named after a song by Black Sabbath). Roth stated in his autobiography, I felt that the name Van Halen was like the name Santana, it had power to it.  

The band became a staple act on California's Sunset Strip during the mid- one nine seven zero s, consistently playing at well known clubs such as the Whisky A Go-Go. In one nine seven six , Gene Simmons of the rock band KISS saw one of Van Halen's shows and subsequently financed their first demo tape (this bootlegged demo commonly circulates under the title ''Zero'' and features unfinished and alternative lyrics to many of Van Halen's early songs). Despite having a fairly polished demo tape, Van Halen was unable to secure a record deal, and Simmons subsequently released his rights to the band. The band continued to play club gigs, eventually connecting with Marshall Berle (nephew of the famous comedian Milton Berle). One night after playing to an empty house at the famed Starwood Club in Los Angeles, Berle, then the band's manager, introduced them to producer Ted Templeman and Warner Bros. executive Mo Ostin. Van Halen soon signed their first record contract. Templeman (who had previously produced hits for The Doobie Brothers) would go on to produce Van Halen's first six albums.

( one nine seven eight - one nine eight five ) with David Lee Roth
Cover from one nine seven eight debut album ''Van Halen'' (clockwise from upper left corner: Eddie Van Halen, David Lee Roth, Michael Anthony, Alex Van Halen)
With Ted Templeman at the helm, the band moved into the studio and quickly recorded their first album. Simply titled ''Van Halen'', the album was released to immediate commercial success, reaching one nine on the ''Billboard'' pop music charts. All of the tracks were laid down very quickly (about three weeks), with little over-dubbing or double tracking. Minor mistakes were left on the record and a very simple musical set-up was used to give the record an almost-live feel. After adding vocals, the album was essentially ready to be mixed. Despite the simple studio set-up, ''Van Halen'' featured innovations in musical technique, production, and arrangement. 

The first album, one of rock's most commercially successful debuts, is widely regarded as one of the most influential rock albums ever produced. While it included world famous pieces such as Ain't Talkin' 'Bout Love, Eruption, and Runnin' With the Devil, the album also portrayed a Kinks cover of You Really Got Me and a John Brim cover of Ice Cream Man. The band toured for nearly a year on the basis of ''Van Halen'', establishing their reputation as a talented and exciting live band. The early chemistry of the band was based upon the interplay of Eddie Van Halen's technical wizardry and David Lee Roth's flamboyant antics (a contrast that would later erupt into full-blown conflict). They returned to the studio in one nine seven nine for ''Van Halen II'', similar in style to their debut. This album yielded the band's first hit single, the poppy Dance the Night Away.  

Over the next four years, the band alternated album releases and touring to increasing commercial and critical acclaim. By one nine eight zero , Van Halen was perhaps the world's most successful and influential hard rock band (a legacy the band sustained throughout their career; in two zero zero zero , VH one cited Van Halen as seven on their list,  one zero zero Greatest Artists of Hard Rock ). Their third album Women and Children First was released in one nine eight zero , further cementing Van Halen's status as an elite rock group with such loud and popular songs as And the Cradle Will Rock and Everybody Wants Some!! . In one nine eight one , during the recording of their fourth album, ''Fair Warning'', tensions began to rise within the band. Eddie Van Halen's desire to experiment with more serious songs and complex structures was at odds with Roth's pop instincts and increasingly cartoonish, irony-laden persona. Although Roth (and producer Templeman) acquiesced to Eddie's wishes, ''Fair Warning'' was a relative sales disappointment, yielding no hit singles. The following album, ''Diver Down'', featured a hit cover of Roy Orbison's classic rock and roll song Oh, Pretty Woman . After a successful tour to support ''Diver Down'', Van Halen became the highest paid music group for a single appearance, earning a spot in the Guinness Book of World Records for their inebriated, $ one million, nine zero -minute set at the U.S. Festival in one nine eight three . (This record was eventually eclipsed in the one nine nine zero s.)

Cover art for the hit single Panama ( one nine eight four )
Van Halen's next album, '' one nine eight four '' (released on January nine , one nine eight four ) was their commercial, and many claim, artistic pinnacle. It was also a breaking point for the original line-up. Keyboards, previously heard only rarely, were now fully integrated into the band's sound. The album's lead single, Jump , featured a bouncy synthesizer hook and anthemic lyrics by Roth. Jump became the band's first and only one pop hit and resulted in the band's first Grammy nomination. The other huge hits off the album were Panama,  I'll Wait, and Hot For Teacher. The album '' one nine eight four '' was praised by critics and fans alike, peaking at two on the ''Billboard'' charts behind the popular ''Thriller'' by Michael Jackson (Eddie Van Halen played the guitar solo on the hit song Beat It, from that album). In the midst of their greatest commercial success and tour, the artistic and personal tensions between the musicians reached a breaking point. Roth exited the band on April one , one nine eight five .

( one nine eight five - one nine nine six ) with Sammy Hagar
Cover art for the hit single Love Walks In ( one nine eight six )
In search of a new lead singer, Eddie Van Halen first offered the position to Patty Smyth of Scandal, who turned down the offer. The band was then introduced to singerguitaristsong-writer Sammy Hagar. Hagar (who sang lead vocals for the band Montrose in the early ' seven zero s) was at that time a solo artist coming off a very successful year (his one nine eight four album ''VOA'' had yielded the hit single I Can't Drive five five ' that peaked at two six on the pop charts). Late in one nine eight five Hagar agreed to join the band and a new era began for Van Halen. 

The album five one five zero , released on March two four , one nine eight six , was an immediate smash hit. Driven by the keyboard-dominated singles Why Can't This Be Love,  Dreams, and Love Walks In, it became the band's first release to reach one on the Billboard album charts. Filled out with diverse songs ranging from the near thrash of Get Up, and party rock of Summer Nights and Good Enough, to the more introspective Best Of Both Worlds and an EVH guitar tour de force on the title track, five one five zero is generally considered the strongest album of the ''Hagar era''. 

The next ten years with Sammy Hagar were marked by two somewhat opposing trends: expansion of the band's commercial success amid increasing fan resentment over Roth's departure. Hagar's style enabled Van Halen to become accessible to a wider audience, with lyrics that were more conventional and refined. Eddie's keyboard work brought a wider variety of sonic textures within each song, and the production was altered toward the pop side. The result was markedly different from the hard charging, rollicking riffs of the group's earlier work, and Eddie's trademark guitar sound was now rarely heard without many digital effects. Die-hard old Van Halen fans referred derisively to the new Van Hagar sound as soft or fluffy compared with the raucous, raw sound of the Roth era.

During Hagar's tenure, the band established a musical formula that proved commercially successful in the United States. All four studio albums produced during this period reached one on the Billboard pop music charts. Also during this time, one seven singles breached the top one two of the mainstream rock tracks chart. In addition, Van Halen was nominated for two Grammy Awards, winning the one nine nine one Best Hard Rock Performance with Vocal award for the album ''For Unlawful Carnal Knowledge''. Van Halen continued to enjoy tremendous popular success throughout the mid- nine zero 's, while many of their hair metal contemporaries (such as Warrant and Poison) fell from favor, overtaken by anti-establishment Grunge Music. 

Van Halen with Sammy Hagar (circa one nine nine five )

During the recording of their contribution to the film ''Twister'', escalating tension between Hagar and the Van Halen brothers boiled over publicly as Hagar departed on Father's Day, one nine nine six . Hagar claimed that he was fired; Eddie Van Halen claimed that Hagar quit. The media storm surrounding the dramatic exit of Hagar helped him to immediately restart his solo career. However, the publicity wasn't helpful for Van Halen, only serving to shine a bright light on the vacant lead singer spot. The commercial success that Van Halen reached with Sammy Hagar set high expectations  and fans everywhere were watching and waiting for the band's next move.

( one nine nine seven - one nine nine nine ) with Gary Cherone
Image:vh three .jpg to Right: Alex Van Halen, Michael Anthony, Eddie Van Halen and Gary Cherone ( one nine nine eight )
Soon after Hagar's departure, David Lee Roth entered the studio with the Van Halen brothers, Michael Anthony, and producer Glen Ballard. Two songs from those sessions were added to the band's Greatest Hits album (with the Roth single Me Wise Magic reaching one on the mainstream rock chart; the album ''The Best of Van Halen, Vol. one '' was one on the pop charts). However, Eddie and Alex were still auditioning other singers  among them unknown singer Mitch Malloy. Malloy would reveal years later that, during this time, Eddie had hired him for the job. By September, however, David Lee Roth and the rest of the band were asked to present an award at the one nine nine six MTV Video Music Awards. On September four , one nine nine six , the four original members of Van Halen made their first public appearance together in over eleven years, presenting an award at the one nine nine six MTV Video Music Awards. This appearance was greeted with a standing ovation, and fueled hopeful speculation for a reunion tour. However, old wounds were reopened; while doing backstage interviews with the media, Roth told Eddie not to talk about personal issues such as Eddie's hip replacement. According to Eddie, Roth was very rude and self-centered, causing the relationship between them to sour once again. Mitch Malloy revealed several years later that immediately after the awards, he told Eddie that he did not want to be the lead singer of Van Halen because the public appearance with Dave made it impossible for any other singer to be successful with the group. Several weeks after the awards show, the public and media became aware that Roth would not be reuniting with the band. At this time, Roth released a media statement where he apologized to the media and the fans, stating that he was an unwitting participant in a publicity stunt perpetrated by the Van Halens and Ray Daniels (their manager) in order to sell more copies of the greatest hits album. The next day, Eddie and Alex Van Halen released their own statement, stressing that they were completely honest with Roth and never led him to believe that he was guaranteed to be the next lead singer.

Continuing their search, Van Halen recruited Gary Cherone, the frontman of the defunct Boston-based band Extreme. The result of their collaboration was the experimental ''Van Halen III''. Many songs were longer and more ethereal ( Once ), more thought-provoking ( How Many Say I, with Eddie on vocals), or were just plain different ( From Afar,  Josephina ). These changes alienated many existing Van Halen fans who were followers of Roth's and Hagar's hard rock sound while failing to attract a new audience. Sales were lackluster compared to those of previous albums  yet the ''VHIII'' album peaked at four on the charts (it was Gold certified), and produced a one Mainstream Rock Track hit, Without You . However, no tracks from the album ever appeared on the pop music charts. A left over track entitled That's Why I Love You found its way onto the internet, leaving fans to wonder why it didn't make the album. Van Halen also contributed a song to the Lethal Weapon four soundtrack with the title Fire In The Hole. 

In early one nine nine nine , the band started work on the follow up to ''III'' with Cherone on vocals. Working titles of demo tracks included Left for Dead,  River Wide,  Say Uncle,  You Wear it Well,  More Than Yesterday,  I Don't Miss You...Much,  Love Divine, and From Here, Where Do We Go.  However, the album was not completed and Cherone left the band amicably in November one nine nine nine .

( two zero zero zero - two zero zero four ) Four years of silence
From two zero zero zero to early two zero zero four , no albums were released and no official information was provided to fans about the future of the band. However, information about individual members, past and present, trickled in. Some highlights:

The Van Halen Logo
 During two zero zero zero , the band secretly started working with David Lee Roth, and six new tracks were worked on at five one five zero . However, Roth and the band fell out yet again and no new material was released.
 In one nine nine nine , Eddie Van Halen reluctantly had hip replacement surgery (when the pain became unbearable). He also underwent cancer treatment soon after (at the Mayo Clinic) and announced his complete recovery on the official website in May two zero zero two .
 On October one five , two zero zero one , Eddie and his wife of two one years, actress Valerie Bertinelli, separated. The couple filed for divorce on December eight , two zero zero five . Eddie keeps out of the public eye but appears at the LAPD charity golf tournament during May two zero zero one . His only live performances during this period were joining Mountain on stage for a rendition of Never in My Life in August two zero zero two , and a private audience jam at NAMM January two zero zero three . Eddie only gave one official interview, with Maximum Golf Magazine, in July two zero zero one .
 Alex Van Halen continued to work with his brother on new material at their '' five one five zero '' recording studio.
 In two zero zero two , Warner Bros. dropped Van Halen (still without a lead singer) from the label, after having released all of their albums since one nine seven eight .
 Since his departure in one nine nine six , David Lee Roth produced a number of albums and toured with his ''DLR band'' (his most recent release being an album of covers called ''Diamond Dave'' ( two zero zero three )). In two zero zero three , Roth brought a court action against Van Halen, their management, and record company claiming he was left out of one nine nine six royalty renegotiations. On July four , two zero zero four , Roth performed with the Boston Pops at Boston's annual ''Pops Goes the Fourth'' celebration. As of two zero zero five , he has become a certified EMT, and as of October two zero zero five , has agreed to become Howard Stern's future replacement on morning talk radio.
 Sammy Hagar has remained active musically. Since his departure from Van Halen, he has released five albums. He also created his own merchandising brand ''Cabo Wabo'', which lends its name to his popular line of tequila, as well as his franchise of cantinas located in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, and Lake Tahoe, Nevada. In addition, he reunited with the original members of his ' seven zero s band Montrose in two zero zero three and two zero zero five for a handful of performances. Hagar also maintains a good relationship with Michael Anthony and the two often play together.
 Michael Anthony stays busy outside of Van Halen with various product merchandising projects (such as his signature Yamaha bass) and has a website. He is involved with the annual music industry NAMM Show.
 Anthony has also released a statement on his official website denying rumors that he has been sacked by Van Halen.
 Since his departure from Van Halen, Gary Cherone recorded an album and performed locally with his new band Tribe of Judah.
 In the summer of two zero zero two , David Lee Roth and Sammy Hagar teamed up for the ''Song For Song, the Heavyweight Champs of Rock and Roll'' tour (known tongue-in-cheek as the 'Sans-Halen' or 'Sam He's the kind of guy you go out with to split a bottle with a friend. I'm the kind of guy you go out with if you want to split your friend with a bottle. During that tour, Michael Anthony guested with Hagar's solo band, ''The Waboritas'', but never played with Roth. Hagar released a live album (''Hallelujah''), which featured ''Mike (a few songs) and Gary (one song), and a documentary DVD, ''Long Road to Cabo'', chronicling his tour with David Lee Roth.
 During January two zero zero three , the VHND (Van Halen News Desk) website reported a rumour that Sammy Hagar was secretly working with the band.

( two zero zero four - two zero zero five ) Reunion with Sammy Hagar
The reunited Van Halen with Sammy Hagar ( two zero zero four )
In late March two zero zero four , Van Halen and Sammy Hagar announced that Hagar would reunite with the band for a Greatest Hits album release and a summer concert tour.

In July two zero zero four , Van Halen released their second Greatest Hits compilation, featuring three new songs with Hagar: It's About Time , Up For Breakfast , and Learning to See. Again, public reaction to the new songs was mixed. The track list had changed since its unveiling, and now Hagar and Roth songs alternated instead of one disc for each singer; a disappointing strategy for fans who prefer one singer over the other (often strongly). No VHIII songs made it onto the disc. Nevertheless, Van Halen's second Greatest Hits record would be certified platinum in August two zero zero four .  

Van Halen ( two zero zero four ), left to right: Alex Van Halen, Michael Anthony, Sammy Hagar, Eddie Van Halen
The summer tour grossed five five million dollars, and Pollstar listed Van Halen in the top one zero grossing tours of two zero zero four . Most of the concerts received positive feedback from professional reviewers. However, serious problems surfaced. Sammy Hagar and Michael Anthony would subsequently admit that Eddie Van Halen had problems with alcohol during the tour that affected everyone involved. Hagar stated that he was done with Van Halen and wished that everyone would have taken it more seriously. It was also revealed in Rolling Stone magazine that promoters had lost money on the tour. Many fans complained that tickets were overpriced (sometimes exceeding $ two zero zero ), and only a few shows were actually sold out. Reports of Eddie being drunk and playing sloppy circulated which is also evident on many of the bootlegs of the tour.

After the tour ended, Van Halen once again disappeared. Hagar returned to his solo band The Waboritas, and Anthony appeared with him on tour occasionally. Eddie's collaboration with Peavey ended (for his signature five one five zero guitar amplifier series, replaced with the six five zero five amp, and Eddie is now endorsing Charvel, which is reissuing the EVH classic guitar models). As for two zero zero five , no announcements had been made about the future of the band.

In August two zero zero five , Van Halen sued the Baltimore Orioles, claiming that the Orioles reneged on a deal to bring the band to Oriole Park at Camden Yards on September two , two zero zero four , which would have been the first concert at the otherwise baseball-only facility.

On October seven , two zero zero five , newsletter Popbitch reported that Van Halen would be seeking a new lead singer via a reality TV show similar to INXS's Rock Star: INXS. Several other news sources picked up this story but it turned out to be false.

He isnt asked any direct questions regarding the future of Van Halen but admits he was ''satisfied'' with the two zero zero four reunion tour. Asked if any problems occured with Sammy Hagar during the tour he answers ''Sammy is Sammy, and for the most part that's just fine with me.'' 

February one three , two zero zero six : Various news and music websites report that Van Halen is indeed the band to be featured in the new series out, called Rockstar: The Series. The band's publicist, Larry Solters, is quoted as saying ''I'm not denying it. I'm not going to answer any questions about it.'' 

February one five , two zero zero six : The New York Daily Times runs a story with several quotes from David Lee Roth regarding a Van Halen reunion. ''People want the reunion,'' said Roth. ''No one will pay respect to what any of us do musically until we get the reunion out of the way.'' .
 ''Once Eddie (Van Halen) does that, everything else he does can be seen with a fresh eye.'' 

 Influence on culture, music and business 
The David Lee Roth era remains Van Halen's most critically successful period, having influenced nearly all rock musicians who followed. The band's top selling albums to date are their one nine seven eight debut and '' one nine eight four ''. Both albums have reached diamond status, having sold over one zero million copies each, and are both regarded as milestones in rock and roll music, ushering in artistic innovations that were widely emulated throughout the one nine eight zero s (The ''Van Halen'' track Runnin' with the Devil and '' one nine eight four 's'' Jump are listed as two of the top five zero zero most influential songs in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame). The band's second and third productions, ''Van Halen II'' and ''Women and Children First'', each reached six on the charts. After this, every subsequent Van Halen album would breach the top five spot on the pop charts.

The ''Van Halen'' track Eruption introduced the rock and roll world to a new soloing technique called tapping, a technique utilizing both left and right hands on the guitar neck (tapping also exists and did for a long time in its more traditional one-handed form, involving just hammer-ons and pull-offs). Other musicians had developed two-hand playing techniques during the one nine five zero s, and Steve Hackett of Genesis used tapping extensively in the early one nine seven zero s, but Van Halen's technique was something else  a percussive, highly amplified barrage of notes and effects. Nothing like it had ever been heard on record. Eruption immediately propelled Eddie Van Halen to immense heights of popularity among guitar players worldwide (articles about Eddie Van Halen's style and technique remain a staple of guitar magazines). According to folklore, before the release of the first album, Eddie would hide his technique from imitators by playing his solos with his back to the audience. Eddie also introduced a never before seen technique in the instrumental Cathedral . This technique involved Eddie hammering notes on the fretboard with his left hand while simultaneously rolling the volume knob off and on with his right hand. He did two takes, and the volume knob froze completely at the end of the second take due to the heat generated from rolling it on and off at such a great speed. Many beginning hard rock and heavy metal bands of the era have testified that, when trying out new guitarists, being able to cover the song was often the audition criteria asked of the guitarist.

''Van Halen'' also introduced the guitar world to the band's signature Brown Sound, a nickname given to, among other things, the sonic result of Eddie's guitaramp combination and technique. With Templeman's warm production, Van Halen produced a distinctive tone sought by other musicians.

As the band began to make music videos for MTV, the telegenic Roth became the visual focus, often to the chagrin of the other band members. Music videos for the singles ''Jump'', ''Panama'', and ''Hot For Teacher'', were wildly popular and became part of the standard rotation on the then fledgling MTV. 

The second incarnation of Van Halen also saw broadened use of the Van Halen brand, as they expanded their reach into other media, with high-production films, live concert footage, and even their own cantina in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. If David Lee Roth's innovative, over-the-top style turned Van Halen from a member of the hard rock pack to its leader, Hagar's more conservative 'working man' persona turned Van Halen into a franchise and an icon. 

The hit single and award-winning video ''Present (time) Now'' (''F.U.C.K.'', one nine nine one ) was used to promote the ill-fated soft-drink Crystal Pepsi. The band's Roth-era remake of The Kinks song ''You Really Got Me'' was used in a Nissan commercial. 

Van Halen pioneered the way for the modern Rock and Roll Show with their extensive use of the concert technical contract rider. Although contract riders had existed before, Van Halen's use of them to specify the band's wish list (stage, production, transportation, personal requirements, etc.) was new and established a standard practice that is now used routinely throughout the music industry. As one of the first major bands with a full stage show to appear in many smaller cities, Van Halen had an extensive set of technical and logistical requirements including power availability and stage construction details that a venue had to comply with. Many venues in these markets had not previously dealt with such a large-scale show, and were not equipped to handle Van Halen's massive stage and light show, sometimes resulting in damage to the band's equipment and the venue, once nearly killing a roadie setting up the instruments. The band's demands were not limited to technical issues: their now infamous contract rider specified that, among other personal needs, a bowl of M Ain't Talkin' 'Bout Love for their landmark double album ''Double Nickels on the Dime'' (only the third verse, a guitar solo and the hey, hey, hey! outro were used) - an irony considering that, according to Roth, the song originated as an affectionate parody of punk rock when it was first written. 

Rapper Tone Loc used uncredited samples from Van Halen's Jamie's Cryin' extensively on his hit Wild Thing, but was not sued by the band; in Alex Van Halen's words, It was one nine eight seven , who knew?  two Live Crew later sampled the riff of Ain't Talkin' 'Bout Love for their song The Fuck Shop on their infamous one nine eight nine album ''As Nasty As They Wanna Be''; Van Halen sued the band for copyright infringement; the suit was settled out of court.

 '''Tarrytown''' is a village located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one one , zero nine zero . 

The '''Village of Tarrytown''' is located in the northwest part of the Town of Greenburgh, New York. 

Most of the village's population is white. About one-fifth of Tarrytown's population consists of Hispanics, many of whom are Ecuadorans and Dominicans. 

 Geography 
Tarrytown is adjacent to the Hudson River and the Tappan Zee Bridge. 

Tarrytown is located at four one  four ' nine  North, seven three  five one ' three five  West ( four one . zero six nine one zero eight , - seven three . eight five nine seven seven three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one four . seven km ( five . seven mi ).  seven . seven km ( three . zero mi ) of it is land and seven . zero km ( two . seven mi ) of it is water. The total area is four seven . five four % water.

Commuter service to New York City is available via the Tarrytown train station, served by Metro-North Railroad.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one one , zero nine zero people, four , five three three households, and two , seven six five families residing in the village. The population density is one , four three six . nine km ( three , seven two four . seven mi ). There are four , six eight eight housing units at an average density of six zero seven . four km ( one , five seven four . five mi ). The racial makeup of the village is seven seven . four four % White, seven . zero four % African American, zero . two two % Native American, six . four nine % Asian, zero . zero five % Pacific Islander, five . two nine % from other races, and three . four seven % from two or more races.  one six . one seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four , five three three households out of which two six . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four eight . five % are married couples living together, nine . six % have a female householder with no husband present, and three nine . zero % are non-families. three one . two % of all households are made up of individuals and nine . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three three and the average family size is two . nine five .

In the village the population is spread out with one nine . seven % under the age of one eight , eight . six % from one eight to two four , three four . eight % from two five to four four , two two . five % from four five to six four , and one four . four % who are six five years of age or older. The median income for a household in the village is $ six eight , seven six two , and the median income for a family is $ eight two , four four five . Males have a median income of $ six one , six nine nine versus $ four one , zero five four for females.  '''Valhalla''' is a hamlet and census-designated place (CDP) located in the town of Mount Pleasant in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the hamlet had a total population of five , three seven nine . Its name was inspired by a fan of Opera composer Richard Wagner, and its celebrity status comes from its relationship to the final burial places of famous people.

 History of Valhalla 
 Origin of name 
It gained its name when controversy arose over the naming of a post office in the one nine th Century. According to local historians and published work, the wife of a postmaster was a devoted fan of Richard Wagner and she shared the composer's interest in Norse mythology. Her preference led to the choice of name Valhalla, after the heavenly hall of slain warriors in that mythology. The area still maintains its association with death through its world famous cemetery area.

 Kensico Cemetery 
'''Kensico Cemetery''' is a cemetery founded in one eight eight nine in Valhalla at a time when many New York City cemeteries were becoming full and rural cemeteries were founded near the railroads which served the city. Initially two five zero acres ( one km), it was expanded to six zero zero acres ( two . four km) in one nine zero five , and reduced to four six one acres ( one . nine km) in one nine one two when a portion was sold to the neighboring Gate of Heaven Cemetery. 

This is where the remains are found of Herbert Howard Booth, son of Salvation Army founder William Booth and founder of the Salvation Army Musical Department. Billie Burke who played Glinda, the ''Good Witch of the North'' in the one nine three nine film classic The Wizard of Oz is also buried there and so is bandleader Tommy Dorsey; New Yorker cartoonist Peter Arno ;CBS-TV News President Fred Friendly; baseball star Lou Gehrig; film star Danny Kaye; pianist and conductor Sergei Rachmaninoff and author Ayn Rand and NBC founder David Sarnoff and many other famous personalities.

Area link to Norse mythology
Because of its association to Norse mythology and Viking legends, the area also became the focus of the novel ''Valhalla Rising'' written by Clive Cussler which was published in two zero zero one . Cussler's book featured a sci-fi story about Vikings which is set against the backdrop of nearby Tarrytown and other associated locations of the Hudson River Valley of Westchester County in New York.

Valhalla, New York also became a part of the strange obsession of Mark Guglielmo who grew up in Bedford, Westchester County. He was sentenced in Florida for the murder of his wife which had taken place in that state during one nine nine four . Guglielmo transported her remains in the trunk of his car to Westchester County where he disposed of her dismembered corpse at two different locations near Valhalla. Guglielmo then took a mock Viking sword and helmet which had been made at a Westchester County faire for burial at Peggys Cove in Nova Scotia, Canada. He did this because he believed that Lief Erickson's Vikings had once landed there. This same Viking association between Nova Scotia, Canada and Westchester County, New York was also made by Clive Cussler in his book several years later.

 Geography 
Valhalla is located at four one  five ' one four  North, seven three  four six ' two eight  West ( four one . zero eight seven one nine five , - seven three . seven seven four five one one ). According to the United States Census Bureau, the hamlet has a total area of nine . one km ( three . five mi ).  six . nine km ( two . seven mi ) of it is land and two . two km ( zero . nine mi ) of it is water.  '''White Plains''' is a city located in Westchester County, New York. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five three , zero seven seven , but a July one , two zero zero two Census estimate put the city's population at five five , three nine four . It is the county seat of Westchester County.

White Plains is perhaps the most significant of the edge cities that have developed outside of New York City. While the city itself dates to the colonial period, since the mid- one nine eight zero s it has experienced a tremendous commercial and residential boom. The construction of the White Plains Galleria Mall ushered in a period of new construction downtown and on the Westchester Avenue (NY Route one one nine ) corridor, including a series of skyscrapers, department stores and apartments. In the past ten years, development has continued as the city has become the leading retail and office center in Westchester County. A new courthouse for the Southern District of New York opened in one nine nine eight . An infusion of immigrants (largely from Mexico) and urban professionals drawn by the city's close commuting distance to midtown Manhattan ( three zero minutes by express train) has lent White Plains a cosmopolitan air in recent years.

The city's permanent population has experienced a growth spurt since two zero zero zero as a number of high-end apartment towers have been constructed. The new City Place development, opened in two zero zero four , features two skyscrapers with commanding views of the lower Hudson Valley. Two new towers are under development at present. In large part because of its close proximity to New York, the cost of living in White Plains has been ranked as second most expensive in the nation (to New York City).

White Plains is home to one of the campuses of Pace University, two Metro North commuter railroad stations, White Plains and North White Plains. White Plains is also the home of fast-growing Westchester County Airport, which offers regional travelers an alternative to New York's congested three major airports.

During the American Revolutionary War, the Battle of White Plains took place on Chatterton Hill, located just west of the downtown area on the Bronx River Parkway.

 Geography

 '''Yorktown''' is a town located in Westchester County, New York, about three eight miles north of Midtown Manhattan. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of three six , three one eight . The town is named after the Battle of Yorktown near Yorktown, Virginia. 

The '''Town of Yorktown''' is on the north border of the county. 

 History 
Town of Yorktown has a rich historical heritage beginning with the earliest known inhabitants -- Mohegan, Osceola, Amwalk, Kitchawan and Mohansic -- all familiar names of local places. The Mohegans of the Algonquin Nation had habitations within the boundary of Yorktown. 

In one six eight three , Stephanus Van Cortlandt, with a license issued by the Royal Governor of New York, made his first purchase of land from the Indians. By one six nine seven , when he confirmed his patent with the authorities, he had acquired roughly eight zero , zero zero zero acres ( three two zero km ). A patent for the Manor of Cortlandt was granted by the British King, William the Third, June one seven , one six nine seven . The Manor house was located north of the confluence of the Hudson and Croton Rivers. 

After the Revolutionary War and at the time of its incoporation in one seven eight eight , the township was officially designated as Yorktown in commemoration of the American's decisive victory at Yorktown, Virginia in October one nine , one seven eight one . 

During the town's bicentennial in one nine eight eight , Yorktowners took stock of their historic heritage including that of the one nine th and two zero th centuries and commemorated their community's participation in events that led up to the birth and growth of the United States. A Bicentennial Committee reviewed the Town's still remaining historic sites and determined which were to be preserved as a reminder of that past and a link betwee the Yorktown of yesterday and the Yorktown of tomorrow.

 Geography 
The north town line is the border of Putnam County, New York. Somers borders Yorktown on the east and Cortlandt Manor borders Yorktown on the west. New Castle borders Yorktown on the south.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one zero one . seven km ( three nine . three mi ).  nine five . one km ( three six . seven mi ) of it is land and six . seven km ( two . six mi ) of it is water. The total area is six . five seven % water.

There are one two , five five six households out of which four zero . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six nine . one % are married couples living together, seven . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and two one . seven % are non-families. one nine . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one zero . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight three and the average family size is three . two six .

In the town the population is spread out with two seven . six % under the age of one eight , five . four % from one eight to two four , two eight . five % from two five to four four , two five . two % from four five to six four , and one three . three % who are six five years of age or older.  Additional facts about Yorktown 

The Jefferson Valley Mall, in the hamlet of Jefferson Valley, is home to over five zero stores, including Sears, Macys, H Kitchawan, Croton Lake, Croton Heights, Yorktown Heights and Amawalk. The railroad failed, was purchased by the New York Central, and finally abandoned. The old right of way is now part of Westchester County Bike Path (see original  station.) There is currently no rail service in Yorktown, but the stations of Croton-Harmon, Mount Kisco or Cortlandt are one five - two zero minutes away.

 '''Wyoming''' is a village located in Wyoming County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village has a total population of five one three . 

The '''Village of Wyoming''' lies within the Town of Middlebury by the eastern town line. Wyoming is located on Route one nine . 
 
 History 
The Village of Wyoming was incorporated in one nine one six . 
It was one of the earliest locations where natural gas was developed. While the field never was a large producer it still provides gas for the village streetlights and some homes to this day. The downtown historic district is known as Gaslight Village. 

Middlebury Adademy: first high school in the Holland Purchase, now listed in the National Register of Historic Places

Middlebury Academy was founded as a high school level school in one eight one nine , and is believed to be the first high school west of the Genesee in New York. It still stands in downtown Wyoming, maintained as a museum by the Middlebury Historical Society. It is listed on the National Register of History Places as of one nine eight zero .

Another historic place is Hillside, a classic Greek revival mansion built by the Capwell family in one eight five one . It overlooks the village of Wyoming, and is a bed and breakfast inn today. It also has been a spa (with mineral springs) and has been host to many famous people including Susan B. Anthony, John Muir, and both President Roosevelts. 

 Geography 
Wyoming is located at four two  four nine ' three one  North, seven eight  five ' seven  West ( four two . eight two five two zero four , - seven eight . zero eight five two two seven ). 

Oatka Creek flows northward past the east side of the village.

'''Jane's Addiction''' was an American band, named in reference to Jane Bainter, a (now ex-) heroin addict who was a housemate of the band. The band formed in the late one nine eight zero s, dissolved in the early one nine nine zero s, and returned in the early two zero zero zero s. The band was influenced by punk, gothic rock, metal, funk, hard rock, progressive rock, and psychedelic styles; the lead singer once described the band as a cross between Duke Ellington and Bad Brains.
 
History
Formed out of the ashes of frontman Perry Farrell's previous band, Psi-com, Jane's Addiction are often compared to iconic ' seven zero s rockers Led Zeppelin. In the summer of one nine eight five , Farrell was searching for a new bass player for the faltering Psi-com when he was introduced to Eric Avery. Although Farrell and Avery worked well together, Psi-com disbanded before they managed to play live with their new bassist. Later, Eric's sister introduced the duo to Stephen Perkins. Following this fortuitous introduction, Perkins suggested his friend (and Dizastre bandmate) Dave Navarro might be a suitable guitar player for the new band, dubbed Jane's Addiction in honor of Farrell's housemate, Jane Bainter. With this lineup, the band released three albums: ''Jane's Addiction'', ''Nothing's Shocking'', and ''Ritual de lo Habitual''. 

Though the band had only released two studio albums and one live (''Jane's Addiction''), their effect on the rock and alternative music scenes was enormous. They became the poster children for a new wave of artful and thoughtful rockers who were eschewing the confinements of commercial rock music and stretching to express themselves both musically and theatrically. In their hey-day, Farrell created Lollapalooza, the alternative rock festival that revolutionized the North American concert promotion world by bringing together an ecclectic mix of musicians, exhibitors, and attractions for a high energy weekend of music and alternative lifestyles. 

The Ripple single that the band produced for the Grateful Dead tribute album ''Deadicated'' was the final studio track for this incarnation of the band. Internal strife and rampant drug usage lead the band to break up in one nine nine one after playing two nights at Hawaii's Aloha Tower; with Perkins and Farrell performing the final show completely naked, without incident. 

The band members pursued other projects in the one nine nine zero s. Farrell and Perkins formed another band Porno for Pyros which had some success. The band briefly reformed in one nine nine seven for the Jane's Relapse tour, with Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist Flea replacing Avery, after he declined an invitation to rejoin the band. 

Four years later, Jane's Addiction rose from the ashes again for a full blown tour. Again, Avery declined involvement. With Flea busy with the Chili Peppers, Porno for Pyros bassist Martyn LeNoble was brought in to fill the gap. Following the success of this tour, the band decided to record a follow-up album to one nine nine zero 's ''Ritual De Lo Habitual'' and brought in Chris Chaney to replace LeNoble on bass. They entered the studio with legendary producer Bob Ezrin in two zero zero one , recording as a band for the first time in over ten years. The result was their final album,''Strays''. 

The band spent two zero zero three on an extensive worldwide touring in support of ''Strays'', including, in a homecoming of sorts, a summer headliner slot in a reincarnated Lollapalooza US tour. Following the two zero zero three tour, Jane's Addiction broke up again, according to guitarist Dave Navarro's site in June two zero zero four . Although details surrounding the band's demise are sparse, Navarro claimed that the reasons for the breakup were essentially the same as they were in one nine nine one . ''''

Navarro, Perkins, and Chaney have since formed a new band, The Panic Channel, with singer Steve Isaacs. They are currently recording their debut album. Perry Farrell has also moved onto a new project entitled The Satellite Party and unveiled material at Lollapalooza two zero zero five .

In the future, there will be a release of a ''Best of Jane's Addiction'', tentatively scheduled for sometime around April-May, two zero zero six .

Announcement of the two zero zero four break-up
The following was posted on Navarro's site in June two zero zero four :

'''State of the Union'''

OK. We know we can't avoid this anymore so we will give it our best shot. What's the deal? The deal is that it simply didn't work out. Sometimes things just don't work out. In all honesty, we have broken up and rejoined roughly four times over the years. Perhaps that should shed some light as to where we are now. We really don't know. We do know that we really gave it everything we had this time and we actually made a really great record after so many years of silence. That was definitely a great thing and we are all proud of it. We were able to do a lot of shows and travel and see the world again. We had some amazing times. Why didn't it work out? So many reasons. Some of them over one five years old, some of them new and none of them worth mentioning. Maybe we are just a volatile combination. Maybe that is why we were so great. The bottom line is that we are all extremely creative and motivated people and I know we will all continue to create and work on many different projects.

After two zero years, just like in any relationship, you have your highs and lows and some amazing memories that can never be replaced. We were able to create great music together, and for that... We feel blessed. But sometimes relationships don't work, no matter how much time or energy you put into them... and at that point... you realize it is healthier to go your separate ways than to keep trying to recreate the magic of the early years. Sometimes people grow apart in the relationship, it is nobody's fault really... just a fact of life... an inevitable creative dissolution. Sometimes the best creative relationships are the most combustible and they aren't meant to last forever.

We know this doesn't answer all of your questions, but hopefully it answers some of them. We would personally like to say, thank you for all of the love and support you have shown us over the years, we greatly appreciate it and we love you.

Stephen, Dave  Jane's Addiction . ''All Music Guide''. Retrieved June one three , two zero zero five .

'''Penn Yan''' is a village located in Yates County, New York, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of five , two one nine . It is the county seat of Yates County. The name is an invention of the early settlers for their community. 

The '''Village of Penn Yan''' is primarily in the Town of Milo, but a small section is in the Town of Benton. 

'''Penn Yan Airport''' is south of the village. 

 Geography 
Penn Yan is located at four two  three nine ' three six  North, seven seven  three ' two zero  West ( four two . six six zero zero eight nine , - seven seven . zero five five four four seven ). Penn Yan is at the north end of the east branch of Keuka Lake, one of the Finger Lakes. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of six . zero km ( two . three mi ).  five . nine km ( two . three mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . five eight % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are five , two one nine people, two , one four one households, and one , two six one families residing in the village. The population density is eight eight seven . seven km ( two , two nine nine . seven mi ). There are two , two nine nine housing units at an average density of three nine one . zero km ( one , zero one three . one mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine seven . one five % White, zero . six seven % African American, zero . two seven % Native American, zero . three one % Asian, zero . zero six % Pacific Islander, zero . three three % from other races, and one . two three % from two or more races.  zero . nine four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , one four one households out of which two nine . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four one . two % are married couples living together, one two . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and four one . one % are non-families. three five . one % of all households are made up of individuals and one eight . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two eight and the average family size is two . nine zero .

In the village the population is spread out with two three . nine % under the age of one eight , seven . six % from one eight to two four , two six . four % from two five to four four , two zero . four % from four five to six four , and two one . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four zero years. For every one zero zero females there are eight seven . two males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight one . two males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ two nine , two seven eight , and the median income for a family is $ three nine , zero eight seven . Males have a median income of $ three zero , six nine two versus $ one nine , two six three for females. The per capita income for the village is $ one five , eight four eight .  one three . eight % of the population and nine . seven % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one seven . eight % of those under the age of one eight and one one . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. 

 History 
The first frame dwelling at Penn Yan was built in one seven nine nine . The village became the county seat in one eight two three , when Yates county was created, and was incorporated in one eight three three . 

The first settlers were chiefly followers of Jemima Wilkinson ( one seven five three - one eight one nine ), a religious enthusiast, born in Cumberland Township, Providence County, Rhode Island, who asserted that she had received a divine commission. Wilkinson preached in Rhode Island, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Pennsylvania. Obtaining a large tract (which was called Jerusalem in one seven eight nine ) in the present Yates county, she founded in one seven eight eight the village of Hopeton on the outlet of Keuka Lake about a mile from Seneca Lake. Many followers settled there, and she herself lived there after one seven nine zero . Some of her followers left her before one eight zero zero , and then the community gradually broke up. 

The name of the village is said to have been contrived from the first syllables of  Pennsylvania  and  Yankee, as most of the early settlers were Pennsylvanians and New Englanders. 

Many Amish and Mennonite families are recent arrivals to the area.

 '''Burlington''' is a city located in Alamance County in North Carolina, a state of the United States of America. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of four four , nine one seven . The town hosts the Burlington Indians baseball club of the Appalachian League.

 Geography 
Location of Burlington, North Carolina
Burlington is located at three six  five ' two three  North, seven nine  two six ' four four  West ( three six . zero eight nine six three six , - seven nine . four four five five seven eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of five five . three km ( two one . three mi ).  five five . one km ( two one . three mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two eight % water.

 Early History 
The need of the North Carolina Railroad Company in the one eight five zero s to locate land where they could build, repair and do maintenance on its track was the genesis of Burlington, North Carolina. The Company selected a piece of land slightly west of present day Graham, North Carolina. 

By the time the shops were completed in one eight five seven , the village had grown to twenty-seven buildings. Thirty-nine white men, twenty Negro slaves and two free Negroes were employed in or around the shops. 
The employees and their families needed to live within walking distance; hence, a town begin to develop. The town was called Company Shops. 

Sale of town lots soon started, but not surprisingly, the sale of lots was slow until after the Civil War. By one eight six four , Company Shops numbered about three zero zero persons.

In one eight eight six , the North Carolina Railroad Company transferred its operations to Manchester, Virginia. The railroad offices and shops at Company Shops were closed. With the railroad shops no longer operated there, the citizens of Company Shops decided a new name was needed. In February one eight eight seven a committee of the towns leading citizens selected Burlington.

The city of Burlington was incorporated and a charter was issued by the State Legislature on February one four , one eight nine three .

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are four four , nine one seven people, one eight , two eight zero households, and one one , seven five four families residing in the city. The population density is eight one five . zero km ( two , one one one . zero mi ). There are one nine , five six seven housing units at an average density of three five five . zero km ( nine one nine . six mi ). The racial makeup of the city is six six . two seven % White, two five . zero five % African American, zero . three four % Native American, one . seven one % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander, five . one six % from other races, and one . four four % from two or more races.  one zero . zero seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one eight , two eight zero households out of which two nine . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four five . one % are married couples living together, one four . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three five . seven % are non-families. three zero . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four zero and the average family size is two . nine six .

In the city the population is spread out with two three . seven % under the age of one eight , eight . nine % from one eight to two four , two nine . zero % from two five to four four , two one . four % from four five to six four , and one seven . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three seven years. For every one zero zero females there are eight eight . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight five . zero males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three five , three zero one , and the median income for a family is $ four five , four four one . Males have a median income of $ three one , six nine seven versus $ two two , four six six for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one nine , six four zero .  one three . seven % of the population and nine . seven % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one eight . one % of those under the age of one eight and one four . six % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Education 

Local public schools in Burlington include Hugh M. Cummings High School, Walter M. Williams High School, Sellars-Gunn Education Center, Broadview Middle School, Turrentine Middle School, R. Homer Andrews Elementary, Eastlawn Elementary, Grove Park Elementary, Hillcrest Elementary, E. M. Holt Elementary, Pleasant Grove Elementary and Marvin B. Smith Elementary. The local school system is known as the Alamance-Burlington School System, which was created by a merger between the Alamance County School System and the Burlington City School System in one nine nine six .

 Transportation 

Amtrak's Carolinian and Piedmont train connects Burlington with the cities of New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Washington, Richmond, Raleigh and Charlotte. The Amtrak station is situated at one zero one North Main Street.

 History and Legends 
Three subjects loom large in Bath's history. They are presented chronologically; an order which perhaps indicates their significance as well.
 Blackbeard the pirate, who figured prominently during the town's earliest days.
 The curse of Methodist evangelist George Whitefield.
 Edna Ferber's novel ''Show Boat'', and its subsequent film and Broadway adaptations. Ferber's inspiration came from her time aboard the showboat ''James Adams Floating Theatre'' when it visited Bath Creek during the spring of one nine two five .

 Mark Rothko's painting '' one nine five seven  two zero '' ( one nine five seven )
'''Mark Rothko''' (September two five , one nine zero three  February two five , one nine seven zero ) was a Latvian-born American Jewish painter who is often classified as an abstract expressionist, although he vociferously denied being an abstract painter.

History
He was born '''Marcus Rothkowitz''' in Daugavpils, Latvia (then part of the  Russian Empire) and emigrated to Portland, Oregon in one nine one three . He attended Lincoln High School in Portland, and then Yale University but only for a year.

Artwork
Among the founders of the New York School, his work concentrated on basic emotions, often filling the canvas with very few, but intense colours, using little immediately-apparent detail. In this respect, he can also be considered to presage the Color Field painters, such as Helen Frankenthaler. However, Rothko repeatedly protested, 'I'm not interested in color' and 'I'm not a colorist.' Color, he explained, was nothing more than an 'instrument' for expressing something larger: the all important 'subjects' of his pictures (Chave one nine eight nine ).

Although respected by other artists, Rothko remained in relative obscurity until one nine six zero , supporting himself by teaching art.

Rothko's ''Homage to Matisse'' ( one nine five three ) which sold for a record $ two two . five million

In one nine five eight , Rothko was commissioned by architect Philip Johnson to paint a series of murals for the Four Seasons restaurant in the Seagram Building in New York. This substantial project was completed in late one nine five nine . Ultimately, Rothko was not happy having his paintings as the backdrop to gourmet dining as he felt their intensity and contemplative qualities would not suit such surroundings. Having a high regard for the Tate Britain Gallery in London, he gave the set of nine of the maroon and black works to the gallery, where they were on permanent display in an intimate installation using subdued lighting designed by Rothko. The paintings arrived at the Tate Gallery on the same day as the news of Rothko's death. Since the building of the Tate Modern further along the river, they have been moved and featured in a similarly designed gallery set aside solely for Rothko. The subdued lighting and intensity of the paintings create a contemplative atmosphere, allowing visitors to view the works in the way Rothko would have wished. 

In one nine six seven , Rothko again collaborated with Johnson on a church in Houston, Texas, contributing one four related works in an installation setting. The church has subsequently become known as The Rothko Chapel . Numerous other works are scattered in museums throughout the world.

Rothko, along with other nonrepresentational painters, is alleged to have been favored by the CIA through arts institutions during the one nine five zero s. The support was part of a Cold War campaign to steer global intellectual culture of both left and right away from Communism, on the principle that it would stand little chance of becoming political Agitprop, in contrast to American representational fine art of the time which, descended from arts of the Great Depression, New Deal economic reconstruction, and World War II, frequently had overt social or political agendas. The allegations are controversial in hindsight, but for the implications the campaign has on global intellectual culture , rather than for the quality of the research.

Suicide and legacy

After a long struggle with depression, Rothko committed suicide by cutting his wrists in his New York studio on February two five , one nine seven zero . Additionally the settlement of his estate became the subject of the famous Rothko Case.

In early November, two zero zero five , Rothko's one nine five three oil on canvas painting, Homage to Matisse, broke the record selling price of any post-war painting at US $ two two . five million dollars.

A previously unpublished manuscript by Rothko about his philosophies on art, entitled ''The Artist's Reality'', has been edited by his son, Christopher Rothko, and is to be issued by Yale University Press in two zero zero six . 

 Quotations 
 I am not an abstract painter. I am not interested in the relationship between form and colour. The only thing I care about is the expression of man's basic emotions: tragedy, ecstacy, destiny. 

 Pictures must be miraculous. 

References
 Chave, Anne. ''Mark Rothko, one nine zero three - one nine seven zero : A Retrospective.'' New Haven: Yale University Press, one nine eight nine .

'''Hans Frank''' (May two three , one nine zero zero  October one six , one nine four six ) was a lawyer for the Nazi party during the one nine two zero s and a senior official in Nazi Germany. Because of his tenure as Governor-General of occupied Poland, he was prosecuted during the Nuremberg trials for his role in perpetrating the Holocaust, found guilty of complicity in the murder of millions of Poles and Polish Jews, and executed on October one six  one nine four six .
 
Frank was born in Karlsruhe and joined the German army in one nine one seven . He served in the ''Freikorps'' and joined the German Labour Party in one nine one nine , becoming a member of NSDAP proper in one nine two seven . He studied law, passing the final state examination in one nine two six , and rose to become the personal legal advisor to Hitler. He was elected to the ''Reichstag'' in one nine three zero , and in one nine three three he was made Minister of Justice for Bavaria. He was also the head of the National Socialist Jurists Association and President of the Academy of German Law from one nine three three . Frank objected to extra-judicial killings, both at Dachau and during the Night of the Long Knives. From one nine three four he was Reich Minister Without Portfolio.

In September one nine three nine Frank was assigned as Chief of Administration to Gerd von Rundstedt in the General Government. From October two six , one nine three nine , following the division of Poland, Frank was the Governor-General of the General Government for the occupied Polish territories (''Generalgouverneur fr die besetzten polnischen Gebiete''), that is head of the General Government controlling those areas of Poland that had not been directly incorporated into Germany (roughly nine zero , zero zero zero km out of the one seven zero , zero zero zero km Germany had gained). He was granted the SS rank of ''Obergruppenfhrer.''

Frank oversaw the segregation of the Jews into ghettos (Jewish quarters) and the use of Polish civilians as forced and compulsory labour. In one nine four two he lost his positions of authority outside of the General Government after annoying Hitler with a series of speeches in Berlin, Vienna, Heidelberg, and Munich and also as part of a power struggle with Friedrich Wilhelm Krger, the State Secretary for Security head of the SS and the police in the General Government. But it was Krger who was ultimately replaced, with Wilhelm Koppe. Frank later claimed that the extermination of Jews was entirely controlled by Heinrich Himmler and the SS and that he, Frank, was unaware of the extermination camps in the General Government until early in one nine four four . During his testimony at Nuremberg, Frank claimed he submitted resignation requests to Hitler on fourteen occasions but Hitler would not allow him to resign. Frank fled the General Government in January one nine four five , in advance of the Soviet Army.

Hans Frank (right) hosts Heinrich Himmler during a visit to Krakw in one nine four zero .

Capture and Trial

Frank was captured by American troops on May four , one nine four five , near Berchtesgaden and was one of the defendants in the Trial of the Major War Criminals Before the International Military Tribunal in Nuremberg from two zero November one nine four five to one October one nine four six . During the trial he renewed his childhood practice of Catholicism and, under the pressure of being on trial for his life, claimed to have a series of religious experiences. 

Frank voluntarily surrendered over forty volumes of his personal diaries to the Allies, which were then used against him as evidence of his guilt. Frank confessed to some of the charges put against him and viewed his own execution as a form of atonement for his sins. On the witness stand he uttered: a thousand years will pass and the guilt of Germany will still not have been erased .

He was found guilty of war crimes and crimes against humanity, and on October one , one nine four six , he was sentenced to death by hanging. Journalist Howard K. Smith wrote of his execution: 

:Hans Frank was next in the parade of death. He was the only one of the condemned to enter the chamber with a smile on his countenance.
:Although nervous and swallowing frequently, this man, who was converted to Roman Catholicism after his arrest, gave the appearance of being relieved at the prospect of atoning for his evil deeds.
:He answered to his name quietly and when asked for any last statement, he replied in a low voice that was almost a whisper, I am thankful for the kind treatment during my captivity and I ask God to accept me with mercy. 

Quote
About Polish partisans in Warsaw in one four XII one nine four three , Krakw:
''If not for Warsaw in the General Government, we wouldn't have four five of our current problems on that territory. Warsaw was and will be the center of chaos and a place from which opposition spreads throughout the rest of the country.''

 '''Washington''' is a city located in Beaufort County, North Carolina. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of nine , five eight three . In two zero zero four , it was estimated that the town had a total population of one zero , eight three one . It is the county seat of Beaufort County. The closest major city is Greenville six , approx. one nine mi to the west.

 Geography 
Location of Washington, North Carolina
Washington is located at three five  three three ' one three  North, seven seven  three ' seven  West ( three five . five five three four nine zero , - seven seven . zero five two zero five zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one seven . seven km ( six . eight mi ).  one six . eight km ( six . five mi ) of it is land and zero . nine km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is four . eight three % water.

Originally called The Fork of the Tar, for the way the Pamlico River splits into the Tar River and Chocowinity Bay, the city was renamed to Washington around the time of the American Revolution after George Washington. It is said that during the war, General Washington spent a night in this town.

 Features 
The town is rich in historical buildings and landmarks--many dating back to colonial times. The city was bombed during the American Revolution and there is even a downtown waterfront home that still contains a cannon ball shot from a Union ship in the Tar River. 

Locals enjoy fishing and boating on the Pamlico River, dining in the quaint downtown restaurants, watching the East Carolina University Pirates and Washington High School, Pam Pack football games, and a monthly downtown music and art festival called Music in the Streets. 

The town is also home to Fountain Powerboats, Inc., a company that specializes in luxury powerboats and powerboat racing. It is here, on the Pamlico sound, that Fountain has set its numerous high-speed world records.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are nine , five eight three people, three , nine six eight households, and two , four six eight families residing in the city. The population density is five six nine . two km ( one , four seven five . two mi ). There are four , three nine nine housing units at an average density of two six one . three km ( six seven seven . two mi ). The racial makeup of the city is five one . seven eight % White, four five . five zero % African American, zero . one seven % Native American, zero . four nine % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, one . zero four % from other races, and one . zero zero % from two or more races.  two . seven two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , nine six eight households out of which two eight . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three seven . three % are married couples living together, two one . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and three seven . eight % are non-families. three three . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one five . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three zero and the average family size is two . nine three .

In the city the population is spread out with two four . seven % under the age of one eight , eight . six % from one eight to two four , two four . five % from two five to four four , two two . six % from four five to six four , and one nine . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four zero years. For every one zero zero females there are seven seven . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are seven zero . eight males.

 '''Bald Head Island''' is a village located on the east side of Cape Fear in Brunswick County, North Carolina. Compared to the bustling city of Wilmington to the north, Bald Head Island is a small, somewhat remote village. It is only accessible by ferry from the nearby town of Southport. Cars are not allowed; instead residents drive modified electric golf carts. The village is revered for its picturesque nature and is a popular location for retirement. It was the primary filming location for the successful film Weekend at Bernie's in one nine eight nine , as well as being a major location in The Butcher's Wife in one nine nine one . Old Baldy, its out-of-service lighthouse, is the oldest still standing in the state, built in one eight one seven . As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one seven three .

History
Calabash was named after gourds that grew in the region, which were used for drinking.  '''Oak Island, North Carolina''' is a town located mostly on Oak Island (which also contains the town of Caswell Beach and the North Carolina Baptist Assembly at Fort Caswell) in Brunswick County, North Carolina; a small part of the town extends onto the mainland north of the island's bridge. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of six , five seven one . It was founded in one nine nine nine by the consolidation of the towns of Long Beach and Yaupon Beach. Its main industry is tourism; the town has an average summer population of three zero - four zero , zero zero zero . 

 History 
The island has been inhabited since the early one eight zero zero s; Fort Caswell was built on its eastern end in one eight three eight . The remainder of the island was developed beginning in the late one nine three zero s; a pavilion attracted people from nearby Southport and people hunted foxes in the northern area near the Intracoastal Waterway. The island was nearly wiped out by Hurricane Hazel in one nine five four ; only five buildings were left standing on Long Beach in the hurricane's wake. The island quickly recovered and towns of Long Beach and Yaupon Beach were incorporated in one nine five five . Other hurricanes, such as Diana in one nine eight four , Bertha and Fran in one nine nine six and Floyd in one nine nine nine , has caused damage to the island, though nowhere near as catastrophic as that of Hazel.
