 Culture 

Greenville serves as a regional entertainment hub for all of Eastern North Carolina. The area boasts a vast array of local and national-chain restaurants catering to a variety of tastes from down-home favorites to gourmet specialties. Several restaurants within the city have been recognized nationally for their barbecue and superior wine selection.

The retail sector has acquired a regional draw bringing shoppers to Greenville from all over Eastern North Carolina. Numerous options offer shoppers variety in price, selection, and style, and range from consignment shops to boutiques, malls to commercial strips, and galleries to showrooms. 

Culture permeates on and off the East Carolina University campus. On almost any given evening, East Carolina University offers world-class musical concerts, theatrical and dance productions, travel films, and lectures. Antique stores are scattered throughout the county and offer a number of unique treasures. Also, art galleries abound featuring major art collections, traveling exhibits, and the work of local and regional artists. County-wide festivals round out the calendar celebrating everything from collards to watermelons and offer something for all ages. 

Athletics predominate the area and the fans are avid. The city and all of Eastern North Carolina have a great passion for the East Carolina University Pirates. ECU Pirates offer sporting seasons sure to get everyone on their feet cheering. Certainly, Football dominates the ECU athletic scene(). Greenville is also home to the Eastern Regional High School Football and Basketball Tournament, NC Senior Games, and hosted the Babe Ruth World Series Girls Softball Tournament in the Summer of two zero zero two . 

Numerous trendy restaurants and nightclubs offer live entertainment in the evenings on the weekends and Uptown Greenville has a district that includes numerous venue options. Freeboot Friday in the fall and Sunday in the Park offer great opportunities to enjoy friends and family and the seasons. And, area coffee shops provide a chance to chat with an old friend or enjoy a good book. The downtown area is known on the national level for its annual large Halloween street party and live music bars.

 Educational Institutions 
 East Carolina University
 Pitt Community College

 Transportation 

Greenville is centrally situated within Eastern North Carolina. Several major U.S. and state highways converge in the area to provide easy access to the interstate highway system. A four two -mile beltway highway system around the city is expected to be completed by two zero one six . Two of the nation's most extensive and financially healthy railroads intersect in Greenville. 

Greenville is close to these destinations:

 one . five hours to Atlantic Beach, North Carolina
 one . five hours to Cape Hatteras National Seashore
 one hour to Raleigh, North Carolina
 two hours to Wilmington, North Carolina
 two hours to Virginia Beach, Virginia
 two . five hours to Richmond, Virginia
 two . five hours to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina
 four hours to Washington, DC
 four . five hours to Charlotte, North Carolina

Air service is available through Pitt-Greenville Airport with scheduled flights daily to Charlotte's Douglas International Airport and Philadelphia International Airport via USAirways.

The City of Greenville operates an efficient mass transit bus system, Greenville Area Rapid Transit or GREAT.

The City of Greenville has one of the largest greenway systems in the MidAtlantic. This network of sidwalks, gravel, and paved trails are used for walking, biking, and jogging. The greenway connects neighborhoods to recreational areas and parks within the city.

The North Carolina Global TransPark (GTP) is located approximately three zero minutes south of Greenville at the Kinston Regional Jetport (ISO) in Kinston. The TransPark is a combined airport-industrial complex developed by the State in Lenoir County. The runway has been extended to one one , five zero zero feet and a new one two zero , zero zero zero sf building is fully leased. Further construction is expected in the near future. 

Designed to attract industry and bring increased economic opportunities to the citizens of Eastern North Carolina and beyond, the GTP features more than two , four zero zero acres available for immediate development, an on-site Education & Training Center, and daily non-stop jet service to and from Atlanta with ASA Delta Connection.

In May of one nine nine six , the Global TransPark was designated as Foreign Trade Zone two one four . The designation means companies can export and import products through the TransPark without many of the usual customs restrictions and tariffs.

 '''Seagrove''' is a town located in Randolph County, North Carolina. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two four six . The name is derived from a railroad official. 

Seagrove is notable for its many potteries, and it is sometimes referred to as the pottery capital of North Carolina , or even of the world. In this usage, the name ''Seagrove'' not only refers to the town proper, but includes several other communities that are part of the pottery tradition. Nearly one zero zero potteries are located in Seagrove and the neighboring towns of Star, Whynot, Erect, Westmoore, and Robbins. Seagrove is also home to the North Carolina Pottery Center, which was established on November seven , one nine nine eight and has since received visitors from all five zero states and at least two zero foreign countries.

 History 
Seagrove was named for Edwin G. Seagroves, a railroad official who was responsible for routing a railroad through the area. According to local sources, after a unanimous decision to name the railroad station after Seagroves, the town name resulted from a sign painter running out of space and simply dropping the 's' from the end of the name. The railroad served Seagrove until December three one , one nine five one . The old train depot later became a pottery museum.

 Plank Road 
In one eight four nine , construction began of Plank Road, which was one two nine miles ( two zero eight km) long and made of planks eight feet ( two . four m) wide, eight feet ( two . four m) long, nine to one six inches ( two three zero to four one zero mm) wide, and three inches ( seven six mm) thick. The road carried horseback riders, wagons, and stagecoaches. A toll was charged of one cent per mile ( one . six km) for a wagon and four horses. Toll revenues later declined after construction of the railroad, and by one eight six two much of Plank Road was abandoned.

 Seagrove School 
A school funded by members of the community was established on April three , one nine one one . The school moved to a new site in one nine one eight  and again in one nine two six . The school burned on March two four , one nine three four , and was subsequently rebuilt. Seagrove accepted students from elementary to high school until the fall of one nine seven zero , when the high school students began attending the new Southwestern Randolph High School. In the fall of one nine nine zero , Seagrove students in the six th through eight th grades began attending Southwestern Randolph Middle School. Today, the school is known as Seagrove Elementary School and houses students only from Kindergarten until the five th grade.

 Pottery 
Seagrove's pottery tradition dates back to the one seven zero zero s, before the American Revolution. Many of the first Seagrove potters were English and German immigrants, and they primarily produced functional, glazed earthenware. Due to the high quality of the local clay, the Plank Road passing through the town, and, later, the railroad, Seagrove became known for its pottery.

The popularity of Seagrove pottery was severely reduced due to the Industrial Revolution and the advent of modern food preparation. For a time whisky jugs were a successful source of income, but the beverage was outlawed and potteries continued their decline in the early one nine zero zero s.

The potteries struggled until around one nine two zero , when they became popular with Northern tourists visiting nearby Pinehurst. The new tourist industry marked a general change from utilitarian pottery to more decorative ware.

After another decline from the one nine five zero 's through one nine seven zero 's a renewed interest in traditional pottery was beginning to sweep the area, and in one nine eight two a group of concerned individuals founded the North Carolina Museum of Traditional Pottery and organized the Seagrove Pottery Festival, an annual event held each year the weekend before Thanksgiving.
 
The Cole, King, Auman, Owen, McNeill, Teague, Luck and Albright families are eighth- and ninth-generation potters in Seagrove who continue this tradition.

 Pinto Beans 
While known for pottery Seagrove also has a traditon in food products and was home for many years to Luck's. Founded as Mountainview Cannery in the one nine five zero 's by Ivy B. Luck, Alfred Spencer  three two ' three two  North, seven nine  four six ' four one  West ( three five . five four two one six seven , - seven nine . seven seven eight one one four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one . nine km ( zero . seven mi ).  one . nine km ( zero . seven mi ) of it is land and one . three seven % is water.

 Economy 
Each year, tens of thousands of visitors come to Seagrove to see the area's potteries.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two four six people, one zero nine households, and six nine families residing in the town. The population density is one three zero . one km ( three three eight . eight mi ). There are one one nine housing units at an average density of six two . nine km ( one six three . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine five . one two % White, one . two two % African American, zero . eight one % Native American, zero . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, two . eight five % from other races, and zero . zero zero % from two or more races.  three . two five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one zero nine households out of which two three . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four nine . five % are married couples living together, nine . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and three five . eight % are non-families. three two . one % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two six and the average family size is two . eight three .

In the town the population is spread out with two zero . seven % under the age of one eight , one zero . six % from one eight to two four , two five . six % from two five to four four , two four . zero % from four five to six four , and one nine . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four one years. For every one zero zero females there are nine zero . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight seven . five males.

The '''Macintosh Classic''' was the first Apple Macintosh personal computer introduced at a price under US$ one zero zero zero . Demand for another all-in-one Mac, such as the popular Macintosh Plus and the SE, spurred the introduction of the Classic. Limitations of the form factor prohibited major innovations in this model, which had the same nine -inch display, five one two  three four two -pixel one-bit video, and four MB memory ceiling as its predecessors. (In fact, it ''was'' a Mac Plus, except that it used ADB for input like the SE.) Unlike other Macs, memory expansion was only possible with a special memory expansion card only available on the more expensive model, or as an option installed later.

One unique feature of the Classic was the ability to start from a ROM disk by holding down the XO (Command+Option+X+O) keys during the boot process. This would boot the Mac Classic into a special combination of the System and Finder that only the Mac Classic can run. The four zero MB hard disk drive model cost US$ one five zero zero .

Out of the total population, three three . nine % of those under the age of one eight and one eight . two % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Schools and other Education Facility

Hamlet is home to a Fairview Heights Elementary School (K- three ), Monroe Avenue Middle School ( four - six ), Hamlet Junior High School ( seven - nine ), and Richmond Community College.

Additional Information

Hamlet is a major junction of two major CSX railines heading north towards Raleigh, NC, Washington D.C., and New York and south towards Florida. The recently reopened Hamlet Passenger Station, served by AMTRAK, sits downtown at the junction of the lines. Hamlet yard resides to the north of downtown.

The National Railroad Museum and Hall of Fame is also located in Hamlet.

Hamlet was the largest city in Richmond County at one time, but it has been usurped by neighboring Rockingham since the decline of the railroad industry.

Birthplace of legendary Jazz innovator, saxophonist John Coltrane.

 '''Lumberton''' is a city located in Robeson County, North Carolina. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two zero , seven nine five . It is the county seat of Robeson County. Lumberton, located in southern North Carolina, is located on the Lumber River. Founded in one seven eight seven by John Willis, an officer in the American Revolution, Lumberton was originally a shipping point for lumber used by the navy, which was sent downriver to Georgetown, South Carolina. Most of the town's growth, however, began shortly after World War II.

David Lynch's one nine eight six film ''Blue Velvet'' was set in Lumberton, though it was actually filmed in nearby Wilmington. This situation raised some problems during filming, so Lynch filmed a small sequence in Lumberton and was subsequently allowed to use the name.

On July two three , one nine nine three , James Jordan, father of basketball legend Michael Jordan, was murdered at a rest stop off of Interstate nine five near Lumberton.

'''John Michael Hawthorn''' (April one zero , one nine two nine - January two two , one nine five nine ) was a race car driver, born in Mexborough, Yorkshire, England. 

He was the winner of the one nine five eight Formula One Championship. With only one win that year against four wins of Stirling Moss, he benefited from the gentlemanship of Moss at the Portuguese Grand Prix of Porto, after being disqualified for pushing his car, against the rules. Moss interceded and so Hawthorn could keep his second place in Porto, that contributed to his win in the championship only one point ahead of Moss. After winning the title, Hawthorn immediately announced his retirement from Formula One.

A matter of months later, on January two two , one nine five nine , Hawthorn died in an automobile accident on the A three Guildford by-pass.

In one nine five five , Hawthorn was the winner of the two four hours of Le Mans race, despite being involved in the horrible crash that killed eight zero spectators.

In Farnham, the town where he lived up to the time of his death, there is a street named after him, Mike Hawthorn Drive (off Dogflud Way).

'''Hans Fritzsche''' (April two one , one nine zero zero - September two seven , one nine five three ) was a senior Nazi official, ending the war as ''Ministerialdirektor'' at the Propagandaministerium.

Fritzsche was born in Bochum (a city in the Ruhr Area) and served in the German army from one nine one seven . Post-war he studied briefly at a number of universities before becoming a journalist for the Hugenberg Press and then involved in the new mass media of the radio, working for the German government. In September one nine three two he was made head of the ''Drahtloser Dienst'' (the wireless news service). On May one , one nine three three , he joined the NSDAP. Under Joseph Goebbels' Reich Ministry he continued to head the radio department before being promoted to the News Section at the Ministry. In mid- one nine three eight he became deputy to Alfred Berndt at the German Press Division. Responsible for controlling German news, the agency was also called the Home or Domestic Press Division. In December one nine three eight he was made chief of the Home Press Division. In May one nine four two Goebbels took personal control of the division, and Fritzsche returned to radio work for the Ministry as Plenipotentiary for the Political Organization of the Greater German Radio and head of the Radio Division of the Ministry.

Fritzsche was taken prisoner by Soviet soldiers in Berlin on May two , one nine four five . He was tried before the International Military Tribunal. In place of the deceased Goebbels, he was charged with conspiracy to commit crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity. He was one of only three Nazi figures to be acquitted at Nuremberg, but he was soon charged with other crimes and was eventually sentenced to nine years. He was released in September one nine five zero and died of cancer soon afterwards.

History
In one seven two eight , English planter and aristocrat Colonel William Byrd and his surveying party entered the Dan Valley. The Crown appointed Byrd as a commissioner, with responsibility for establishing a dividing line between Virginia and North Carolina. Awed by the physical beauty of the land, Byrd wrote this entry in his diary: This is a land rich even unto the fabled lands about Babylon. The air is wholesome, and the soil equal in fertility to any in the world. He further described it as the Wonderful Land of Eden.  In one seven three three he received his grant of twenty thousand acres, and named it, The Land of Eden, and said in his immortal book, it was the most beautiful section he had ever seen. All of Spray and Draper, and much of Leaksville were within the confines of Byrd's tract. When Leaksville's radio station, the first in Rockingham County, went on the air in December, one nine four six , the call letters, with perfect propriety, were WLOE, representing the  Wonderful Land of Eden. 

Leaksville, the oldest and largest of the communities came into being in one seven nine seven when the state legislature passed an act authorizing John Leak, a tanner, to lay off a town on a tract of his land on the north side of the Dan River. The town was officially incorporated in one eight seven four .

(From Eden: Past and Present one eight eight zero - one nine eight zero  by James E. Gardner, Friends of the Eden Public Library)

As early as one seven nine seven the General Assembly appointed Robert Coleman, Nathaniel Scales, Alexander Snead, Terry Hughes, and John Leak commissioners to build and improve the town of Leaksville in accordance with the plan drawn up by Abraham Philips; Leak, for whom the town was named, had already sold four five lots in one seven nine seven and a few houses had been erected.

A short commercial boom occurred in the period one eight one eight - one eight one nine when it appeared that Leaksville had won the prize as the designated navigational head of the Dan River for bateau traffic against the competition of Madison and Jackson, the town that was heavily promoted but never built, and Danville itself. The failure of the Jackson venture at Eagle Falls upstream of Leaksville led to quick growth here.

In one eight one eight , a great building boom had started, a large bank was established, a branch of the state bank, and lots were sold for almost fabulous prices. In one eight one nine , an academy was opened at Leaksville and later a school for girls was conducted. In later years, Nathan Henry, a son of America's great orator and patriot Patrick Henry, conducted the Academy for males. In one eight four six Patrick Henry III was head of the school. In that year he closed the school, formed a company, and as captain of it, went to Mexico with a North Carolina regiment. Other noted teachers conducted the school here, the best known being Professor N. S. Smith and B. W. Ray.

The bubble burst in the river port scheme and from one eight two one to one eight eight three , as noted by one commentator, the town was economically somnolent and ranged in population from two five zero to three zero zero . However, in this period a major development did occur, though outside the town of Leaksville, which presaged the economic future of the area, pointing it in a direction it would irreversibly take at the end of the century: the establishment in one eight three seven (variably cited as one eight three nine ) of the Leaksville Cotton Mill  Moreheads Factory, it was called  by John M. Morehead who was to be a two-term governor, serving from one eight four one to one eight four five . This mill operated steadily over the decades except perhaps for some lack periods associated with the Civil War.

An occasion, indeed the cause, for resurgence of economic growth in Leaksville was the completion of a narrow-gauge railroad branch (the Danville, Mocksville, and Southwestern Line; later the Danville and Western) from Leaksville junction near Cascade to Leaksville, connecting Leaksville with Danville, Virginia. The branch was built in one eight eight three , and the town has been improving ever since.

The Leaksville Woolen Mill began by Morehead as a modest adjunct to the cotton mill for the carding and spinning of wool from sheep raised on his own farm land. It later evolved into the weaving of blankets and cloth for commercial sale from toll wool received from farmers.

It was established in one eight eight one when the Morehead business interests were being managed by J. Turner Morehead and Company, but the major mill-building project in Spray was to come later, after the organization in one eight eight nine of the Spray Water Power and Land Company. Leaksville Woolen was incorporated in one nine zero three .

J. Turner Morehead described the one eight eight four scene of Leaksville as The town of Leaksville is a popular and growing tobacco market. It has three warehouses for the sale of leaf tobacco, and several flourishing tobacco factories. Auction houses had opened here soon after the War Between the States, and the market held up well in competition with other points. As late as one eight nine three , eight factories were making chewing tobacco here, and some of their brands were famous throughout the country.

The population of the town, including the cotton factory, aggregated eight zero zero . Five stores, in which all articles of general merchandise are sold, two others that sell groceries exclusively, and a millinery establishment, are among its business houses. It also contains four churches  Methodist, Baptist, Presbyterian, and Episcopalian. Since the completion of the D. M. 

Leaksville had also progressed politically. As Morehead proudly noted, the town had been incorporated by an act of the state General Assembly in one eight seven four .

(From A New Togetherness  by Alva W. Stewart, North Carolina correspondent for the National Civic Review)

In one nine four six the size of Leaksville was more than doubled by annexation. The citys corporate limits were expanded three more times in the fifties and twice in the sixties.

The consolidation of the three towns of Leaksville, Spray and Draper did not come easy. The first vote on the issue, on March three one , one nine five nine was defeated. Spray voted in favor, Leaksville and Draper against. In Leaksville the margin was almost three to one ( nine seven three - three seven four ) and in Spray it was not as lopsided ( three one seven - two eight eight ), but still a victory for foes for consolidation. The sentiment swung in favor of consolidation, according to a political leader, when an appeal was made to the Jaycees and younger voters. In the second vote (Sept. one two , one nine six seven ) the issue carried by a substantial majority in Spray and Draper, but by only three votes in Leaksville. The combined vote was two , two five nine to one , seven five three .

'''Greifswald''' (German ''Greif''griffin, ''Wald''forest) is a city in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Germany. Greifswald is located at the southern end of the Baltic Sea, between the islands of Rgen and Usedom, at the mouth of the river 'Ryck'. The population is roughly five five , zero zero zero . The city is officially known as ''Universitts- und Hansestadt Greifswald'', which means ''University and Hanseatic City of Greifswald''.

Historical notes

The first settlers were Danish Cistercian monks, who founded the Brick Gothic Eldena monastery in one one nine nine . The salt trade helped the monastery grow to a monumental religious centre. The earliest known document that refers to Greifswald was written in one two four eight . Enjoying a steady increase in population, Greifswald also became one of the earliest members of the Hanseatic League at the end of the one three th century, which further increased trade and wealth.

In one four five six , Greifswald's mayor Heinrich Rubenow laid the foundations of the second oldest university in Northern Europe, which is one of the oldest in Germany, and was, periodically, the oldest in Sweden and Prussia respectively.

As a result of the Thirty Years War Greifswald became part of the Kingdom of Sweden in one six three one and remained Swedish until one eight one five .

During the period of communist dictatorship that followed the Second World War, parts of the historic city saw little effort towards renovation. After the German reunification in one nine eight nine one nine nine zero this situation has changed substantially.

The largest nuclear powerplant in the former East Germany was located near Greifswald.
It had four reactors which were successively brought online starting in one nine seven four . The plant was promptly shut down after the reunification of Germany due to safety concerns, particularly in regard to the near-meltdown on November two four , one nine eight nine .

Education & science

 see traditional Ernst Moritz Arndt University of Greifswald
 The Max-Planck-Institut fr Plasmaphysik has its second site (after Munich) in Greifswald and is experimenting with a stellarator, Wendelstein seven -X.

 see also list of people associated with the local university here

 '''Lake Lure''' is a town located in Rutherford County, North Carolina. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , zero two seven . Some of the scenes from the film ''Dirty Dancing'' were filmed in Lake Lure, and it is the site of the two zero zero six HGTV Dream Home.

 Geography 
Location of Lake Lure, North Carolina
Lake Lure is located at three five  two six ' four one  North, eight two  one one ' two eight  West ( three five . four four four six six eight , - eight two . one nine one two four three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of three eight . three km ( one four . eight mi ).  three five . two km ( one three . six mi ) of it is land and three . one km ( one . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is eight . one one % water.

 History 
The town was incorporated in one nine two seven , following completion of a dam on the Broad River in one nine two six which created the one four -acre lake around which the town is situated. Dr. Lucius Morse is credited with creating the first plans for the town.

Poor health brought Dr. Morse to the gorge and it was from Chimney Rock in the early nineteen hundreds that the vision of a lake and a resort development was spawned. 

Soliciting the financial backing of his brothers Hiram and Asahel, Dr. Morse proceeded to purchase Chimney Rock ( four zero zero acres) from Jerome Freeman in one nine zero two for $ five , zero zero zero in the name of Chimney Rock Mountains, Inc. Subsequently the company acquired enough acreage in what is now the Lake Lure area to bring the total to eight , zero zero zero acres. 

Dr. Morse and his wife Betty occupied the Cliff Dwellers Inn at Chimney Rock and continued to formulate his plans for the property. He conceived the idea of building a dam on the Rocky Broad River to create a lake and the possibility of a year-round resort. A subsidiary Carolina Mountain Power Co. was formed and the construction of the dam began by it in one nine two five under the guidance of Mees  ( seven five . six mi ). There are one , nine five seven housing units at an average density of five five . six km ( one four four . one mi ). The racial makeup of the town is nine seven . two seven % White, one . four six % African American, zero . one nine % Native American, zero . two nine % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . zero zero % from other races, and zero . seven eight % from two or more races.  zero . one zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four nine five households out of which one zero . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six eight . one % are married couples living together, three . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and two seven . three % are non-families. two two . four % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . zero seven and the average family size is two . three eight .

In the town the population is spread out with one zero . four % under the age of one eight , three . two % from one eight to two four , one four . one % from two five to four four , three five . nine % from four five to six four , and three six . three % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is five nine years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero three . zero males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero two . six males.

The median income for a household in the town is $ three eight , four one seven , and the median income for a family is $ four five , eight three three .  Borlnge Municipality on Sweden's municipal map.
Coat of Arms
'''Borlnge Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden, with an area of five eight six . four km. The municipality has a population of four seven two zero six ; of these around four zero , zero zero zero live in the town '''Borlnge''', which is the seat of the municipality and located at . 

 Geography 
The city of Borlnge received its Royal charter in one nine four four after several smaller towns merged. With its four zero , eight eight zero inhabitants, Borlnge is the largest city in Dalecarlia (''Dalarna''), surpassing its northern neighbour Falun, two zero kilometres away. Together the two cities form a region with close to one zero zero , zero zero zero inhabitants. 

 Politics 
Currently ruling leader is Peter Hultqvist, from the Swedish Social Democratic Party.
Opposition leader is Ulla Olsson, from the Moderate Party. As in most of Dalarna, the Social Democrats hold a strong position. As a result of the Swedish municipal elections, two zero zero two they are currently in a majority in the city council with three one of six one mandates.

Youngest candidate to the Swedish municipal elections, two zero zero six is Carl-Oskar Bohlin, from the Moderate Party as the third candidate on their list. He is also the chairman of Moderate Youth League in Dalarna. The chairman of Moderate Youth League in Borlnge is Erik Hllman.

 Industry 
Borlnge has always been an industrial town surrounding the iron mill of Domnarvet (SSAB) and the paper mill of Kvarnsveden (Stora Enso). The city has two state authorities: the department of rails (''Banverket'') and the department of roads (''Vgverket''). Suitable for a city which structure is severely divided by rails and roads, with a modern city centre.

 Shopping 
Borlnge promotes itself as The Number One Shopping City in Dalarna. This is possible due to the Kupolen area, situated slightly west of the city centre. The Kupolen area includes Kupolen ('The Dome') Shopping Centre (Kupolen Kpcentrum in Swedish) and the surrounding region. Though the district was first built to catch the interest from bypassers it has withdrawn the focus from the nearby downtown area and has overtaken the role as the pulsating heart of Borlnge.

 Sport 
The city has a previously successful football team, although currently in a free fall through the series. IK Brage, named after the Norse god of poetry, has a history of one eight seasons in the Swedish Premier Division (Allsvenskan). Brage play in green and white and host their home games at Domnarvsvallen Stadium in Borlnge with a seating capacity of six , five zero zero .

 Notability 
Borlnge is notable for having a relatively high crime rate.
Borlnge is probably the municipality with the highest roundabout density in Sweden.

 Notable natives 
Jussi Bjrling, tenor
Lars Frlander, swimmer
Mando Diao, pop band
Sugarplum Fairy, pop band
Per Fosshaug, bandy player

 Education

 Yann Martel
'''Yann Martel''' (born June two five , one nine six three ) is a Canadian author.
As an adult, he continued to travel the globe, spending time in Iran, Turkey and India. After studying philosophy at Trent University in Peterborough, Ontario, at age two seven he embarked on a writing career. Living in or visiting many cultures influenced his writing, providing the rich cultural background mix in ''Life of Pi'' that garnered him the prestigious two zero zero two Booker Prize for fiction. To write ''Life of Pi'', Martel spent six months in India visiting mosques, temples, churches and zoos, and then an entire year reading religious texts and castoff stories. After the research, the actual writing required two more years.

''Life of Pi'' was chosen for Year two zero zero three edition of CBC Radio's ''Canada Reads'' competition, where it was championed by author Nancy Lee. In addition, its French translation, ''Histoire de Pi'', was included in the French version of the competition, ''Le combat des livres'', in two zero zero four , championed by singer Louise Forestier.

Martel spent a year in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan from September two zero zero three as the public library's writer-in-residence. He moved to Montreal, Quebec and has recently collaborated with Canadian composer Omar Daniel, composer-in-residence at the Royal Conservatory of Music in Toronto, on a piece for piano, string quartet and bass. The composition, ''You Are Where You Are'', is based on text written by Martel, which includes parts of cellphone conversations taken from moments in an ordinary day. 

In November two zero zero five , the University of Saskatchewan announced that Martel will spend a year in the university's English department as a scholar-in-residence. He plans to research his next book, a historical novel about the Holocaust, in Saskatoon, where he is currently living with his girlfriend.

Books
 ''The Facts Behind the Helsinki Roccamatios'' ( one nine nine three )
 ''Self'' ( one nine nine six )
 ''Life of Pi'' ( two zero zero one )
 ''We Ate the Children Last'' ( two zero zero four )

 Literary awards 
 Winner of the two zero zero two Booker Prize for Fiction 
 Winner of the two zero zero one Hugh MacLennan Prize for Fiction
 Shortlisted for the two zero zero one Governor General's Award for Fiction 
 Shortlisted for ChaptersBooks in Canada First Novel Award
 His short story The Facts behind the Helsinki Roccamatios was the winner of the one nine nine one Journey Prize

Pas-de-Calais

'''Boulogne-sur-Mer''' is a city in northern France, in the Pas-de-Calais ''dpartement'' of which it is a ''sous-prfecture''. It is located by the English Channel.

Population of the city (commune) at the one nine nine nine census was four four , eight five nine inhabitants, whereas the whole metropolitan area (''aire urbaine'') had one three five , one one six inhabitants.

Name
The name Boulogne was recorded for the first time during the Roman Empire as ''Bononia'', a derivative of the Celtic word ''bona'' (meaning foundation , settlement , citadel ). This derivation is also found in the name of the Italian city of Bologna.

History
The cathedral of Boulogne towers over the city.
Originally named ''Gesoriacum'', by the four th century Boulogne was known to the Romans as ''Bononia'' and served as the major port connecting the rest of the empire to Britain. The emperor Claudius used this town as his base for the Roman invasion of Britain, in AD four three , and until two nine six it was the base of the ''Classis britannica''.

In the Middle Ages it was the centre of a namesake county. The area was fought over by the French and the English. In one five five zero , The Peace of Boulogne ended the war of England with Scotland and France. France bought back Boulogne for four zero zero , zero zero zero crowns.

In the one nine th century the Cathedral of Notre Dame was reconstructed by the priest Benoit Haffreingue after he received a call from God to reconstruct the town's ruined basilica.

Miscellaneous

Open in one nine nine one , NAUSICA - The French National Sea Experience Centre is a Science Centre entirely dedicated to the relationship between Mankind and the Sea. Aquaria, exhibitions on the marine fauna, and the exploitation and management of marine resources (fisheries, aquaculture, coastal planning, maritime transport, exploitation of energies and mineral resources, tourism...). Its goal is to incite the general public to discover and to love the Sea, while raising its awareness on the need for a good management of marine resources.

In the year one nine zero five the First Esperanto Universal Congress was held in Boulogne-sur-Mer. L. L. Zamenhof, the creator of Esperanto, was among the attendees. In the year two zero zero five there was held a great anniversary meeting with more than five zero zero attendees.

Births

Boulogne-sur-Mer was the birthplace of:
Frdric Sauvage ( one seven eight six - one eight five seven ), engineer and inventor of the propeller.
 Pierre Claude Franois Daunou ( one seven six one - one eight four zero ), politician and historian 
 Charles Augustin Sainte-Beuve( one eight zero four - one eight six nine ), literary critic and one of the major figures of French literary history
 Guillaume Duchenne ( one eight zero six - one eight seven five ), neurologist
 Auguste Mariette ( one eight two one - one eight eight one ), scholar and archaeologist, one of the foremost Egyptologists of his generation, and the founder of the Egyptian Museum in Cairo
 Benot-Constant Coquelin ( one eight four one - one nine zero nine ), actor
 Ernest Alexandre Honor Coquelin, actor
 Georges Mathieu ( one nine two one ), painter,
 Sophie Daumier (born one nine three four ), actress,
 Jean-Pierre Papin (born one nine six three ), football player
 Franck Ribery (born one nine eight three ), football player

 Other famous people associated with Boulogne 
The Collonne de la Grande Arme marks the event that Napolean gather two zero zero zero zero zero soldiers near Boulogne for a proposed invasion of England

Centre of Malung
'''Malung Municipality''' is a municipality in Dalarna County in central Sweden. Its seat is in the town '''Malung''' with six , zero zero zero inhabitants.

Geography
The terrain in the area is largely submontane, with plenty of bog and forest. The Transtrandsfjllen in the north are the southernmost mountains in Sweden, marking the start of the Scandinavian mountain range. Rocks are mostly metamorphic and sedimentary, with occurrences of basalt. Most settlements are located in and around the valley of Vsterdallven.

Municipal towns 

The municipal population was around one three , zero zero zero in the one nine six zero s, but has decreased continually since then.

The villages in the municipality, with population figures from one nine nine three , are:
 Lima, Sweden ( seven zero zero )

 Transtrand ( five three zero )
 Yttermalung ( seven four zero )
 je ( two nine zero )

Zorn museum

'''Mora''' is a Municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden. Its seat is in Mora (pop. one one , zero zero zero ).

The town is located on the northern shore of lake Siljan. The northern part of the municipality marks the beginning of the Scandinavian mountain range.

The house where Swedish painter Anders Zorn was born in one eight six zero is in Mora and has been turned into a museum.

Mora is also known as the end of the Vasaloppet, an enduring nine zero kilometers long skiing event, with one zero , zero zero zero annual participants. This has been made in honour of the King Gustav Vasa in the one six th century, who was held to have skiid between Mora and the town Slen while escaping from Danes.

'''Orsa Municipality''' is a Municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden. The municipality covers an area of one seven four three . five km, and has a population of six  nine eight six , with a population density of four inhabitants per km. Its seat is in '''Orsa''' with five , two zero zero inhabitants, situated at .

 Geography 
The town Orsa is located on the north-eastern shore of the five three km large Lake Orsa (''Orsasjn''). Through a southern water passage, it is connected with one of Sweden's largest lakes: Siljan. 

View from the Grnklitt mountain.By the shores of Orsasjn the Orsa Camping was inaugurated in one nine three two . With a kilometer long sandy beach, it has several times one awards for its quality and beauty, and is by some referred to as the ''Dalecarlia Riviera''. 

Nature sights include the ''Grnklitt'' mountain, that houses a notable Bear park and skiing hill. The bear park is an enclosed area where not only bears but also wolves, lynx and wolverines reside.

'''Rttvik Municipality''' is a Municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden. Its main city is '''Rttvik''' with a population of four , four zero zero .

 Geography 
Rttvik municipality is situated in the middle of Sweden in the province of ''Dalecarlia'', in between the three Swedish cities Borlnge, Falun and Mora. 

It is located in a traditional forest and agriculture environment, which is how most of Sweden looked in the one nine th century and earlier. Nowadays, its culture also attracts a significant number of tourists.

The area near Rttvik municipality has the highest population of Brown Bears in Sweden. 

 Culture 
Rttvik is a worldwide-known small town because of its old tradition of folkmusic and the beauty of the surroundings close to Lake Siljan. Many tourists who are visiting Sweden go to Rttvik to experience a traditional Swedish and Scandinavian way of living. In the little village of Nusns, the original Dalecarlia Horses or ''Dalahstar''  a handsculpted wooden horse colored orange red and painted with a special pattern  are still being crafted and sold. 

Rttvik's churchIts culture and landscape are by some regarded as being as genuinely Swedish as it gets. For instance, Rttvik still has its picturesque old church located by the water, where it is surrounded by old log cabins where the woodcutters used to live.

Every year the folk music festival Music at Siljan is held in Rttvik, by the shores of Siljan.

 Nationalencyklopedin

'''Smedjebacken''' is a Municipality in Dalarna, in central Sweden. Its seat is in '''Smedjebacken''', with five , seven zero zero inhabitants, situated at . The second city is Sderbrke, with one , zero zero zero inhabitants. Smaller towns or villages include Hagge, Gubbo, Larsbo, Vad, Furbo, Lembo and Saxehammar. These locations have often been the seat of local industries (''bruk''), often as saw mills or iron works, and have century-old histories. Today several have been turned into tourism attractions.

The municipality covers an area of nine five three . three km. Of the total population of one one five nine eight , five eight five seven are male, and five seven four one are female, with a population density of one two inhabitants per km. The municipality borders to eight other municipalities.

Geographically, the town Smedjebacken is situated by the lake Barken, with an area of three four km, which in turn belongs to the Kolbcksn stream-system, which drains into lake Mlaren to the south-east.

The coat of arms depict a sailing ship and cogwheels. These are intended to depict the old and new industry sectors of the municipality. It was granted first time one nine four seven , but has undergone a few redesigns since.

'''Ster''' is a Municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden. Its seat is in Ster (pop. four , five zero zero ).

Ster is a picturesque small town.
 Geography 
Ster is known for the Ster Valley. It is abour five kilometers long and has a dense vegetaion and steeps. On its bottom the Ljuster River flows. The valley is popular for walking.

 Sub-divisioning 
The municipality consists of Ster, Stora Skedvi, Gustafs and SilvbergUlfshyttan.

 History 
At the location was a royal mansion named Ster's Royal Mansion. 

Sweden's first copper mint was built at the location in one six two four , influenced by its proximity to the copper mountain at Falun with its tannery that had been located to Ster a few years earlier. 

The town Ster was founded in one six three zero , and much of its old towm today has still kept wooden houses and street structure from that time, which few Swedish cities have. One of the oldest houses is the city hall.

On May eight , one six four two the town was chartered by Queen Christina of Sweden, making it one of the Cities in Sweden. The chosen coat of arms depicted a miner.

 Today 
The Ster hospital was opened in one nine one two and was at a time Sweden's largest mental hospital. Among others, the serial killer Thomas Quick was admitted there for a short while but renderring him the nickname ''the Ster killer''.

 Sights 
The Old Church of Stora Skedvi is one of Dalarna's oldest, with its oldest parts from the one three th century.

There are several remains from the province's mining history, such as the ''stra Silvberg's Mining Area'' with a silver mining history traced to the one four eight zero s with an adjecent cemetery and chapel. It was closed in the one nine th century and the mine itself is today a water filled hole.

''Bispbergs gruva'' was used for mining iron for over six zero zero years, until it was closed in one nine six seven .

'''Vansbro''' is a Municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden. Its seat is in Vansbro, pop two , one zero zero .

The town is situated by the end of the rivulet Vann (Van River), the main tributary of the Vsterdal River.

 Municipal towns 
 Vansbro, pop. two , one zero zero 
Dala-Jrna, pop. one , five zero zero 
Ns, Sweden, pop. four six five 
ppelbo

Dala-Jrna was formerly known as ''Jrna'' but added Dala not to be confued with that town in Sdertlje Municipality.
 History 
Many of the parishes and towns of today can be traced several centuries back. Around Jrna has been found ovens from the Viking Age or older, showing that the town had been used in the processing of iron for a long time, and probably leading to its name (''Jrn'' means iron in Swedish).

Ns parish was mentioned in one four seven nine , Jrna parish in one four one seven , ppelbo as ppelboda parish one four one seven . 

ppelbo (literally Apple Village ) was in the one six nine zero s the seat for the Vsterdal regiment, Western Dalarnas regimente. Swedish warlike kings Charles XII and Gustaf IV Adolf made use of the men when they fought around in Europe. 

Modern iron works were not established until the early one nine th century, and had a short history that ended before the end of the century. The industry then became dominated by wood industry. Around the year one nine zero zero , three large saw mills were built in the town, making it prosper. With the railroad located through the town Vansbro in one eight nine eight , it further enhanced communications for industries.

Vansbro Municipality with its current borders were created with the municipal reform of one nine seven one . Several small villages and parishes were united with the municipality. The largest town Vansbro, at the time been dominated by wood industry for some eight zero years, became the seat and gave it its name. The coat of arms show the sign of iron, an axe (symbolizing wood industries) and a sword.

 Sister cities 
Its sister city is Velk Mezi, in the Czech Republic.

 Notability 
In Dala-Jrna one of the distinct Dalacarlia dialects are spoken.

Vansbro is known in the annual Vanbro Swim . Inaugurated in one nine five zero , the competitors swim two , zero zero zero meters in Vann and one , zero zero zero meters in the Vsterdal River.

'''lvdalen Municipality''' is a Municipality in Dalarna County, in central Sweden. With an area of six nine one three km, it is Sweden's one two th largest. Its seat is in '''lvdalen''' with one , eight zero zero inhabitants. 

lvdalen literally means ''River Valley'', a name stemming from the area around the town lvdalen, situated along the sterdal River, in the municipals southern part.

The middle part of the coat of arms is ment to depict the landscape: streams and hills. 
 Geography 
Geographically, it is considered divided into three parts: From north to south: the fjeld part, the forest part, and the lv part. 

 North 
The northern part is located within the Scandinavian mountain range. It has cultural influences from the native sami people. 

The largest town is Idre, with about eight zero zero inhabitants, a notable skiing resort. 

This part has some high mountains including Storvtteshgna with one , two zero four meter and ''Stdjan'' with one , one three one . The Tfsingdalen National Park is also located in the northernmost parts.

 Central 
The forest part has forests, with the national park Fulufjllet also belonging to this part. Its influences come from it bordering to Norway, and its history has many examples and remains from its border conflicts. To symbolize this, the lower part of the coat of arms depict a crossbow.

The largest town is Srna, located along the sterdal River, with nine three zero inhabitants. Like Idre, its main industry is tourism. The town once belonged to Norway, but in one six four four it was occupied by two zero zero Swedish peasants, which in effect made it a Swedish town, although it was official granted first with new borders of one seven five one .

 Southern 
The southern area has given name for the dialectlanguage known as ''lvdalsml'', or Dalecarlian language in English. It is an ancient tongue that may be closest related to the Old Norse language. 

This area may be said to have the most interesting culture, with the town lvdalen and several notable villages such as Evertsberg, Blyberg, Klitten, Brunnsberg and sen.

'''County Down''', (''Contae An Din'' in Irish) is one of the six counties that form Northern Ireland (United Kingdom), covering an area of two , four four eight km ( nine four five square miles). It belongs to the province of Ulster. The estimated population in one nine nine two was four one six , six zero zero , a more recent figure puts it at four five four , zero zero zero . The county town is Downpatrick.

Down contains both the southernmost point in Northern Ireland (Cranfield Point) and the easternmost point on the island of Ireland (Burr Point).

The county borders County Antrim to the north, the Irish Sea to the east and County Armagh to the west.

The county colours, as used on flags at inter-county sporting events, are red and black.

 Places of Interest 
An area of County Down is known as Bront Country, after Patrick Bront (originally Prunty) -- father of Anne, Charlotte, and Emily Bront -- who was born in this region.

Down is also home to Exploris, the Northern Ireland Aquarium, located in Portaferry, on the shores of Strangford Lough, on the Ards Peninsula.

 Geography 
Mourne Mountains
County Down is where, in the words of the famous song by Percy French, the mountains of Mourne sweep down to the sea , and the granite Mourne mountains continue to be renowned for their beauty. Slieve Donard, at eight four eight m ( two , seven nine six feet), is the highest peak in the Mournes (and in Ulster). Another important peak is Slieve Croob, at five three two m ( one , seven seven five ft), this is the source of the River Lagan.

Down contains two prominent peninsulas: Ards Peninsula and Lecale peninsula.

The county has a coastline along Belfast Lough to the north and Carlingford Lough to the south (both of which have access to the sea). Strangford Lough lies between the Ards Peninsula and the mainland. Down also has a very short coast on Lough Neagh. Smaller loughs include Lough Island Reavy.

The River Lagan forms most of the border with County Antrim. The River Bann also flows through the southwestern areas of the county. The Clanrye River and River Quoile also flow through the county.

There are several islands off the Down coast: Mew Island, Light House Island and Copeland Island (together, the Copeland Islands), all of which lie to the north of the Ards Peninsula. Gun Island lies off the Lecale coast. In addition there are a large number of small islands in Strangford Lough.

 '''Mount Airy''' is a city located in Surry County, North Carolina, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of eight , four eight four . 

Mount Airy was the home of American actor Andy Griffith, and the inspiration for the fictional community Mayberry, the setting of ''The Andy Griffith Show''. Several locations mentioned in the show reflect real sites in or near Mount Airy, including Mount Pilot (nearby Pilot Mountain) and Snappy Lunch, a restaurant which still stands in the city's downtown. The community holds an annual Mayberry Days celebration which regularly attracts thousands of visitors from around the world. 

Mount Airy is also the home of the famous Siamese Twins, Chang and Eng Bunker ( one eight one one  one eight seven four ), Chinese brothers born in Siam, now Thailand. Chang and Eng were joined by a band of cartilage at the chest (xiphopagus). In modern times, they could be easily separated. For many years they traveled with the Barnum circus. In the one eight four zero s they married sisters Sarah and Adelaide Yates of North Carolina and purchased two adjoining farm properties just west of Mount Airy. Together they fathered between two zero and two three children (accounts vary, and in any case, many of the children passed away in early childhood). The twins would spend three days at one farm then three days at the second farm. They owned slaves and during the American Civil War many of the their descendants fought for the Confederacy. In January of one eight seven four , Chang, who was a heavy drinker and had fallen ill with pneumonia, died during the night. Eng also died within a few hours, surrounded by his and his brother's families. Many of their descendants still live in the Mount Airy area.

Even though Mayberry may be representative of Mount Airy, it is not to be confused with the fictional town. There are some similarities but the differences outnumber them. The City of Mount Airy markets and profits off of the idea of Mayberry, which draws tourists and money into the area.  Citizens of Mount Airy normally take pride in the Mayberry theme, but others are embarrassed by the association. These citizens would actually like to see Mount Airy showing off and marketing its own rich heritage.

In any case, downtown Mount Airy looks nothing like TV's Mayberry, as the show was filmed entirely in Hollywood, California, on the RKO Pictures backlot called Forty Acres .

Mount Airy's most notable feature is its granite quarry, the largest open-faced quarry in the United States.

Mount Airy is also the hometown of country singer Donna Fargo.

 Geography

Mount Airy is located at three six  three zero ' three  North, eight zero  three six ' three four  West ( three six . five zero zero seven five six , - eight zero . six zero nine three one one ).

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are eight , four eight four people, three , six six seven households, and two , one three zero families residing in the city. The population density is three nine zero . four km ( one , zero one zero . eight mi ). There are four , one two nine housing units at an average density of one nine zero . zero km ( four nine one . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the city is eight five . three four % White, seven . nine nine % African American, zero . three five % Native American, two . five five % Asian, zero . zero five % Pacific Islander, two . four nine % from other races, and one . two four % from two or more races.  five . eight seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

'''Avesta Municipality''' is a Municipality in Dalarna, in central Sweden. Its seat is in '''Avesta''' with a population of one five , zero zero zero .

The name is first found in one three zero three as Aghastadhum . ''Aghe'' (pronounced ave ) is of similar origin as the word , meaning stream, in this case the Avestadfors, a tributary of the Dalecarlia River. ''Stadhum'' is of similar origin as stead, or farm.

 History 
The Avestadfors settlement, cirka one seven zero zero , in Suecia antiqua et hodierna.
In the Scandinavian middle ages there was a blast furnace at the location. In one six three six the construction of a giant copper mine was initiated near the Avestadfors.

The town Avesta received partial privileges in one six four one as a town under the city of Falun, and in one six four four a copper mint was built. However, the privileges were withdrawn in one six eight eight due to complains of competition from its neighbour, mainly Falun. Copper coins were continued to be minted until one eight three one , and the copper works was in function until one eight six nine . 

Full city rights were regranted in one nine one nine . The designated coat of arms depict the signs for copper and iron.

 Geography 
The town is located by the Dalecarlia River (''Dallven'').

Avesta borders to the municipalities of:
 Hedemora in Dalarna,
 Hofors and Sandviken in Gvleborg County, 
 Norberg and Sala in Vstmanland County

 Municipal towns 
 Avesta 
 Krylbo - an important railway junction that has succesfully been incorporated with the town Avesta.
 Horndal 
 Fors

 Notability 
Near the town Avesta is a park of European bison.

The most successful sport team in Avesta is their speedway team Masarna, translating to the men of Dalecarlia , competing in the highest division in Sweden.

The city is today mostly notable for its steel mill owned by the finnish Outokumpu company.

 Sometimes confused with 
 Alvesta Municipality, Sweden.

 Avesta - Official site

 '''Brevard''' is a city located in Transylvania County, North Carolina. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of six , seven eight nine . It is the county seat of Transylvania County.

Brevard is located at the entrance to Pisgah National Forest and has become a noted tourism, retirement and cultural center in western North Carolina. A moderate climate, environmental beauty and cultural activities attract relocators to the area.

Brevard is the home of Brevard College, a four-year liberal arts institution with nationally-recognized programs in music and environmental studies. The town also is home to Brevard Music Center, one of the nation's preeminent summer music teaching and performance institutions. Brevard also boasts an extensive local music and arts community.

 Trivia 
Marshville is where the one nine eight five Oscar-nominated movie The Color Purple was filmed. The movie was directed by Steven Spielberg and its cast included Oprah Winfrey and Whoopi Goldberg.

Marshville is the birthplace of country singer Randy Travis.

Marshville is the site of the Boll Weevil Festival, an annual street fair and carnival that takes place every fall.

'''All Souls College''' (in full: '''The College of All Souls of the Faithful Departed, of Oxford''') is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom. 

All Souls is an oddity among Oxford colleges in that it has no students. Its members automatically become Fellows, i.e., full members of the College's governing body. 

Every year, the top finalists of the University are invited to sit the examination for fellowship of the College. About two are elected to fellowship each year. Fellowship of All Souls is thus regarded as one of the highest academic honours in the United Kingdom. These Fellows are known as Prize Fellows, their term of office is seven years and roughly a dozen are at the college at any one time. Other categories of fellowship include Senior Research Fellows, Post-Doctoral Research Fellows, Fifty-Pound Fellows (open only to former Fellows no longer holding posts in Oxford) and Distinguished Fellows. There are also many Professorial Fellows who hold their fellowships by reason of their University post.

It is one of the wealthiest colleges with an estimated financial endowment of  one four four m ( two zero zero three ).

 History 
The College was founded by Henry VI of England and Henry Chichele (fellow of New College and Archbishop of Canterbury), in one four three eight . The Statutes provided for the Warden and forty fellows - all to take Holy Orders; twenty-four to study arts, philosophy and theology; and sixteen to study civil or canon law. Today the College is primarily an academic research institution.


 Customs 
Every hundred years there is a commemorative feast after which the fellows parade around the College with flaming torches, singing the Mallard Song  and led by a Lord Mallard who is carried in a chair, in search of a fictional giant mallard that supposedly flew out of the foundations of the college when it was being built. The last mallard ceremony was in two zero zero one and the next will be held in two one zero one .

: Chorus: ''Hough the bloud of King Edward, By ye bloud of King Edward, It was a swapping, swapping mallard!'' (Compare with Terry Pratchett's cruel but accurate parody, the Hedgehog Song.)

 :''For other meanings of Balliol, see Balliol (disambiguation)''



'''Balliol College''', founded in one two six three , is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom. 

Traditionally, the undergraduates are amongst the most politically active in the university, and the college's alumni include several former prime ministers. Balliol also traditionally attracts more international students than the other undergraduate colleges.

During Benjamin Jowett's Mastership in the one nine th century, the College rose from its relative obscurity to occupy the first rank of colleges, and indeed continues to play a prominent role. Jowett is credited with having developed the tutorial system of education. Herbert Asquith once described Balliol men as possessing the tranquil consciousness of an effortless superiority .

 History 
The College was founded around one two six three by John de Balliol under the guidance of the Bishop of Durham. After his death in one two six nine , his widow, Dervorguilla of Galloway (Galloway, Scotland), made arrangements to ensure the permanence of the college. She provided capital, and in one two eight two , formulated the college statutes, documents that survive to this day.

 Student life 

The college provides its students with a broad range of facilities 
including accommodation, the great hall (refectory), a library, two bars, and separate common rooms for the fellows, the graduates and undergraduates. There are also garden quadrangles and a nearby sportsground and boat-house. The sportsground is mainly used for cricket, tennis, hockey and soccer and the recent new addition water polo. The majority of undergraduates are housed within the main college or in the modern annexes around the sportsground. Croquet may be played in the Master's Field, or garden quadrangles in the summer. The graduates are housed mainly within Holywell Manor which has its own bar, gardens, canteen, common room, laundry and computing facilities. Balliol is proud to have a long standing Music Society which organises four free Sunday evening concerts in the College Hall each term. Balliol is the only Oxford college to have its own bridge club; bridge is an integral part of Balliol and the club recently provided all four team in the cuppers semi-finals, a notable achievement.

Balliol also takes pride in its college tortoise, Rosa, named after the notable German Marxist Rosa Luxemburg. Each June, pet tortoises from various Oxford colleges are brought to Corpus Christi College, Oxford where they participate in a very slow race; Balliol's own Rosa has competed and won many times. Taking care of the resident tortoise is one of the many tasks assigned to Balliol students each year. Sadly, Rosa has been missing for over two years now raising the unanswered question of whether she exists any longer.

Balliol students are noted for their left-wing tendencies - the college ethos has been described as conservatively left-wing . The JCR has had requests for the Sun and News of the World newspapers several times, but each time a majority of students voted against the idea.

 Traditions and customs 
Image:Balliol_College_Feb_ two zero zero five .jpg
Along with many of the ancient colleges, Balliol has evolved its own traditions and customs over the centuries, many of which occupy a regular calendar slot. 

 The patron saint of the College is Saint Catherine of Alexandria. On her feast day ( two five th November), a formal dinner is held for all final year students within Balliol. This festival was well established by one five five zero (in which year college archives tell that a peacock was served up).

 Another important feast in the College calendar is the Snell Dinner (normally held on the Friday of the three rd week in March). This dinner is held in memory of John Snell, whose benefaction established exhibitions for students from Glasgow University to study at Balliol (the first exhibitioners were matriculated in one six nine nine ). The feast is attended by fellows of Balliol College, the current Snell Exhibitioners and representatives from Glasgow University and St. John's College, Cambridge.

 The two social highlights of the Balliol graduate community's year are the Burns Night dinner and ceilidh, held during Hilary term and the Holywell Manor Garden party, held in Trinity term. The former event celebrates the life of Scottish poet Robbie Burns, and the latter celebrates the beginning of summer and the end of examinations. 

 By far the most eccentric is 'The Nepotists' carol singing event organised by the College's Arnold and Brackenbury society. This event happens on the last Friday of Michaelmas term each year. On this occasion Balliol students congregate in the college hall to enjoy mulled wine and the singing of hymns. The evening ends with a rendition of The Gordouli on Broad Street, outside the gates of Trinity College. The Gordouli is an eccentric song written by Balliol students and inspired by the friendly rivalry between the students of Trinity and Balliol.

Another wonderful tradition comes in the form of 'The Betting Book'. After formal college meals, the fellows of the college retire to the senior common room. From time to time, the fellows discuss and place small amicable bets on a whole range of issues. Once made, bets are placed in the Book. The Book has existed since at least the one nine three zero s and gives wonderful insight into how famous historical events were perceived by learned people at the time.

 The College buildings 

Alfred Waterhouse built the main Broad Street frontage of Balliol College, with gateway and tower, known as the Brackenbury Buildings, in one eight six seven - six eight , as well as the adjoining Master's Lodgings. These replaced earlier structures. The Twentieth Century saw several further additions to the college's buildings.

Many undergraduates and some graduates live in buildings on Jowett Walk, five minutes' walking distance from the main buildings. The majority of graduates, and some fourth-year undergraduates, are housed in the Holywell Manor complex, on Manor Road. 'Holywell' or 'The Manor' is a self-contained graduate outpost, with its own dining facilities, bar, grounds, and an active social scene.

 Notable former students 
:''Main article: List of Balliol College people''

Balliol has produced an impressive range of graduates in the fields of economics, history, law, humanities, mathematics, science, technology, media, philosophy, poetry, politics and religion. A recent Nobel Prize winner in Physics, Anthony Leggatt, studied Ancient History with Latin and Greek. The notable biologist Richard Dawkins studied zoology. 

 Academics and visiting academics 

Balliol has a more or less permanent set of teaching staff, known as dons. There is a list of Balliol College academics past and present. These are supplemented by academics on short term contracts. In addition, there are visiting international academics who come to Oxford for a year or so in order to test their ideas in the intellectual milieu of Balliol. Postgraduate students also contribute to the life of the community. The official list of current senior members of the College can be found here.

 Fictional Balliol 

:''Main article: Balliol College in fiction''

Balliol has featured in fiction since the one nine th Century. This may be because it has historically been regarded as the college of the intellectual elite. Such a designation may no longer be assumed but novelists seek authentic symbols rather than statistical accuracy. The college has been regarded as typifying a whole range of attributes for good or ill. On the one hand it is positioned as the ultimate target for any educationally ambitious school boy (or girl - but only relatively recently). It is also selected as the typical college of a superior sort of person. Having placed the fictional character at the college the author may then endorse its academic excellence or alternatively take a swipe at its intellectual pretensions.

Institutes and centres
 Balliol, especially the Master, Andrew Graham, played a major role in two zero zero zero and two zero zero one in setting up the Oxford Internet Institute Oxford Internet Institute. This was the world's first multidisciplinary research and policy centre in a university devoted to examining the impact on society of the Internet. It is department of Oxford University, but is located in Balliol and its Director is a Professorial Fellow of Balliol.

'''Apex''' is a town located in Wake County, North Carolina, a suburb of Raleigh. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of two zero , two one two . 

 Geography 
Location of Apex, North Carolina

Apex is located at three five  four three ' five five  North, seven eight  five one ' one zero  West ( three five . seven three one nine five two , - seven eight . eight five two eight seven eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of two seven . five km ( one zero . six mi ).  two seven . three km ( one zero . five mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . five seven % water.

Neighboring towns include Cary to the north and northeast, Raleigh to the east, and Holly Springs to the south.

 History 

Apex Union Depot, built in one nine one two .

The town of Apex was incorporated in one eight seven three , named for its location as the highest point on the Chatham Rail Line between the state capitol of Raleigh and the coal fields of nearby Chatham County. Apex grew slowly through the succeeding decades, despite several devastating fires, including a one nine one two conflagration which destroyed most of the downtown business district. The town center was rebuilt and stands to this day, now one of the most intact railroad towns in the state. At the heart of town stands the Apex Union Depot, originally passenger station for the Seaboard Air Line Railroad and later home to the locally-supported Apex Community Library.

Apex suffered mild setbacks during the Depression-era, but growth began again in earnest in the one nine five zero 's. The town's position in proximity to North Carolina's Research Triangle Park spurred additional residential development; yet the town managed to preserve its small-town character, residents taking pride that they had stayed off the burgeoning growth of the neighboring town of Cary. Still, during the decade of the one nine nine zero 's, the town's population quadrupled to over two zero , zero zero zero , placing unprecedented demands upon Apex's infrastructure.

 Government 

Keith Weatherly is the current mayor of Apex, re-elected in November two zero zero three to his third consecutive term in office.

'''Fuquay-Varina''' (Few-Quay Vuh-ree-nah) is a town located in Wake County, North Carolina. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of seven , eight nine eight .  '''The English Dominican House of Blackfriars Hall in Oxford''', commonly known simply as Blackfriars, is one of the constituent educational institutions of the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom. It is not a typial college as its status is that of a permanent private hall , and it is located in St. Giles'. It is a centre for the study of Roman Catholic theology, and admits men and women of any faith.

 History 

Despite the fact that many of the dates and figures of Oxford's medieval and early life are imprecise, Blackfriars' history is unusually well documented, largely as a result of the hall being part of an international fraternity of scholarship, which was able to monitor and document its fortunes, even during times of the hall's collapse.

The Dominicans arrived in Oxford on one five August one two two one , at the instruction of St Dominic himself, in the final era of the friar's life. As such, the hall has some claim to be heir to the oldest tradition of teaching in Oxford, a tradition that precedes both the aularian houses that would characterise the next century and the collegiate houses that would characterise the rest of the University's history.

Like all the monastic houses in Oxford, Blackfriars came into rapid and repeated conflict with the University authorities, as the friars claimed all the rights and privileges of University membership but also claimed immunity from the University discipline or regulation. Relations with townspeople were also consistently difficult, but the reasons for this are difficult to assess dispassionately, as virtually all contemporary accounts are marked with deep bias on one side or the other.

With the Reformation, all monastic houses, including Blackfriars, were suppressed. The Dominicans did not return to Oxford for some four zero zero years, until one nine two one when Blackfriars was refounded, within six zero zero metres of the original site.

The hall was formally re-admitted into the University in one nine nine four as a permanent private hall.

'''Brasenose College''' (in full: '''The King's Hall and College of Brasenose''') is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom. It is one of the wealthiest colleges with an estimated financial endowment of  seven two m ( two zero zero three ).

 History 
The College was founded in one five zero nine by a lawyer, Sir Richard Sutton, and the Bishop of Lincoln, William Smyth. Smyth provided the money for the college's foundation, and Sutton acquired the property. It was built on the site of Brasenose Hall - one of the medieval Oxford institutions which originally existed just as a lodging house, but which had grown to become a seat of learning.

A copy of the original Brasenose Knocker is mounted on a door in Stamford
The name Brasenose is thought to originate from a brazen (bronze) door knocker in the shape of a nose.

The nose-shaped door knocker which hangs above the high table of the main hall of Brasenose College is thought to be the original door knocker belonging to Brasenose Hall. In the one three three zero s, a group of students left Oxford for Stamford in Lincolnshire led by a student from Brasenose Hall, and are thought to have taken the door knocker with them. In one eight nine zero , a house in Stamford named Brazenose bearing a one two th-century door knocker in the shape of a nose was put on sale. The house was purchased by the college for the sake of the door knocker, which was removed and placed in the hall, believed to have been returned to its rightful home.

Often referred to by the abbreviation, BNC , Brasenose stands near the Radcliffe Camera in the centre of Oxford.

Formal Hall is held three days a week, with the Latin grace read by the College Bible Clerk (current incumbent, Jennifer Ward) or a nominated substitute.

Brasenose College Boat Club (BNCBC) is popularly held to be the oldest boat club in the world; this is impossible to verify but BNCBC is certainly the oldest collegiate boat club and took part in the first ever head race, beating Jesus College Boat Club on that occasion.

'''Botkyrka Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Stockholm County, in east central Sweden, not far from the capital Stockholm. Its seat is in Tumba.

Botkyrka church
The municipality is named after Saint Botvid who was a christian missionary in the area in the one two th century. According to the legend, he was killed with an axe while fishing. Saint Botvid is shown on the seal and coat of arms, where he carries an axe and a fish. Another reminensce from Botkyrka's christian medieval history is the Botkyrka church, made of stone. 

Botkyrka, paricularly Northern Botkyrka, has one of the highest percentages of first and second generation immigrants in Sweden. Nearly half the population has at least one parent born in another country. In some areas, like Fittja, around nine five % belong to this group. This gives the municipality a multi-cultural atmosphere with for example a big Syriac Orthodox Church in Hallunda and the construction of a mosque in progress in Fittja. 

Politically the municipality is primarily Social Democratic. There is also a local party called Botkyrkapartiet (The Botkyrka Party) which was originally formed to prevent the exploitation of the small airfield, F one eight , in Tullinge to become a commercial airport in the one nine eight zero s.
 
The local weekly newspaper is called Mitt i Botkyrka and is delivered free of charge to all inhabitants.
