Radio
Grand Forks is home to one seven radio stations. Five of the stations are owned by Clear Channel Communications. Most music stations in Grand Forks play either rock or Country music. Popular news stations in Grand Forks include KNOX-AM and KCNN-AM, and popular music stations include KYCK  nine seven Kyck (Country music), KKXL XL nine three  (Top four zero ), and KJKJ KJ one zero eight  (rock music). The city is also served by both North Dakota Public Radio and Minnesota Public Radio stations.

Transportation
Grand Forks International Airport ('''GFK''', '''KGFK''') is served by Northwest Airlines with several daily round trips to Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport. The airport is a major distribution center for FedEx, which conducts flights daily with Boeing seven two seven and Cessna Caravan aircraft (the latter of which transport packages to outlying areas of the state). The airport is also one of the busiest airports in the country due mainly to the presence of the John D. Odegard School of Aerospace Sciences which is a part of the University of North Dakota.

The BNSF Railway runs track in several directions in and around the city. Amtrak passenger service on the Empire Builder line heads westbound daily at five : zero zero am and eastbound daily at midnight.

The city maintains a bus system called Cities Area Transit (or CAT). The system has operated since one nine two six when it was introduced to replace an earlier trolley system (in homage to which, the city now operates a bus that looks like a trolley). There are currently eleven bus routes including night service and service in the community of East Grand Forks. The Metro Area Transit Center is located downtown on Kittson Avenue. It is essentially the depot and main connecting point of the system. CAT is considered to be the best fixed-route public transit service in the state of North Dakota, and was used as a model when Bismarck-Mandan launched a Capital Area Transit service in two zero zero four . Grand Forks is served by two taxi companies: Grand Forks Taxi and Nodak Radio Cab Company.

Three federal highways pass through Grand Forks: U.S. Highway two , Interstate two nine , and U.S. Highway eight one . U.S. Highway two runs east to west through the northern part of town and is a four lane highway. In the city limits, the highway is called Gateway Drive. The highway is the primary connection between Grand Forks, East Grand Forks, the Grand Forks Air Force Base, Grand Forks International Airport, and nearby Crookston, Minnesota. Its business route, Demers Avenue, runs through the downtown areas of both Grand Forks and East Grand Forks. Interstate two nine runs north to south along the western part of the city, officially multiplexed with U.S. Highway eight one in the Grand Forks area. The U.S. Highway eight one business route, Washington Street, runs through many of the city's major commercial districts.

The older sections of Grand Forks are structured in the classic grid street system. In Grand Forks, road that run from north to south are traditionally called streets and roads that run from east to west are traditionally called avenues.  Streets are numbered in blocks west of the Red River. Avenues are numbered in blocks north or south of Demers Avenue (the city's historic dividing route adjacent to the rail yards).

 Air Mobility Command
'''Grand Forks Air Force Base''' ('''Grand Forks AFB''' or '''GFAFB''') is a base of the United States Air Force located in Grand Forks County, North Dakota one five miles ( two four km) west of the city of Grand Forks, North Dakota on U.S. Highway two . It is a part of the Greater Grand Forks metropolitan area. As of the two zero zero zero census, the base CDP had a total population of four , eight three two . 

It is the home of the three one nine th Air Refueling Wing, which consists of the KC- one three five Stratotanker. It is under the Air Mobility Command.
  
Base Realignment and Closure, two zero zero five 

In May of two zero zero five , The Pentagon recommended to the BRAC commision that GFAFB should be realigned. This would prevent the base from being closed, but would result in a significant loss in personnel levels as well as a loss of the tanker mission. To make up for these losses, the Air Force has proposed that a new family of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) missions be located at the base as well as emerging missions in homeland security. Also, there have been some signs that the tanker mission might be retained with a new fleet of planes replacing the older ones.

Geography
A missile on display at the entrance of GFAFB.
Grand Forks AFB is located at four seven  five six ' five zero  North, nine seven  two one ' three two  West ( four seven . nine four seven three four one , - nine seven . three five eight eight seven seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the base has a total area of two one . two km ( eight . two mi ).  two one . two km ( eight . two mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

There are one , two seven nine households out of which seven seven . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, eight eight . five % are married couples living together, four . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and three . eight % are non-families. three . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and zero . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is three . four one and the average family size is three . four eight .

On the base the population is spread out with three eight . four % under the age of one eight , two zero . four % from one eight to two four , three nine . four % from two five to four four , one . seven % from four five to six four , and zero . one % who are six five years of age or older. History
 one nine five four The Department of Defense chose Grand Forks as the site for a new installation.
 five Feb one nine five six Contractors begin construction of the base.
 eight Feb one nine five seven Air Defense Command (ADC) activated the four seven eight th Fighter Group at Grand Forks AFB as the host unit for the base.
 one Sep one nine five eight Strategic Air Command (SAC) activated the four one three three d Strategic Wing (Provisional) as a tenant unit at Grand Forks AFB.
 one five Dec one nine five nine The Grand Forks Air Defense Sector of the North American Air Defense Command became operational with the Semi Automatic Ground Environment (SAGE) System.
 one May one nine six zero The one eight th Fighter-Interceptor Squadron (FIS) was stationed at Grand Forks AFB with its F- one zero one B Voodoos.
 six May one nine six zero The nine zero five th Air Refueling Squadron (ARS) (Heavy), a unit assigned to the four one three three d Strategic Wing, received its first KC- one three five A Stratotanker.
 two eight Dec one nine six zero The four seven eight th Fighter Wing was activated under the ADC and became the host unit for the base.
 two nine Apr one nine six two The three zero th Bombardment Squadron, a unit assigned to the four one three three d Strategic Wing, received its first B- five two H Stratofortress.
 one Feb one nine six three Strategic Air Command organized the three one nine th Bombardment Wing (Heavy) at Grand Forks AFB. The three one nine BMW became the host wing as the four one three three d Strategic Wing inactivated and command of the base transferred from the ADC to SAC.
 one nine Aug one nine six four Strategic Air Command activated the eight zero four th Combat Support Group (CSG) as the host unit at Grand Forks AFB.
 one Sep one nine six four Strategic Air Command stationed the four th Air Division, later named four th Strategic Aerospace Division, at Grand Fork AFB.
 one Nov one nine six four The three two one st Strategic Missile Wing (SMW) was organized at Grand Forks AFB and construction began on its Minuteman II missile complex.
Dec one nine six six The three two one SMW became operational with the Minuteman II missile.
 one five Apr one nine seven one Air Defense Command inactivated one eight FIS.
 three zero Jun one nine seven one The four th Strategic Air Division transferred to Francis E. Warren AFB, Wyoming.
 one Jul one nine seven one The three two one SMW assumed host unit duties from the eight zero four CSG.
 three zero Jul one nine seven one Air Defense Command stationed the four six zero th Fighter-Interceptor Squadron, with F- one zero six Delta Darts, at Grand Forks AFB.
 eight Mar one nine seven three The three two one st Strategic Missile Wing completed an upgrade to Minuteman III missiles.
 one nine seven four The ADC inactivated the four six zero FIS.
 one nine eight six - one nine eight seven The three one nine th Bombardment Wing converted from the B- five two G Stratofortress and KC- one three five A Stratotanker to the B- one B Lancer and KC- one three five R Stratotanker.
 one six Jun one nine eight eight Strategic Air Command transferred the four two d Air Division (AD) to Grand Forks as the host support unit for the base.
 nine Jul one nine nine one Strategic Air Command inactivated the four two AD and appointed the three one nine th Bombardment Wing as the host unit for the base.
 one Sep one nine nine one The three one nine th Bombardment Wing was redesignated as the three one nine th Wing. The three two one st Strategic Missile Wing was redesignated as the three two one st Missile Wing (MW).
 one Jun one nine nine two The Air Force inactivated Strategic Air Command and reassigned Grand Forks AFB to Air Combat Command. The three one nine th Wing was redesignated as the three one nine th Bomb Wing. The nine zero five ARS was functionally reassigned to Grissom AFB, Indiana, although it continued to operate from Grand Forks AFB.
 one Jul one nine nine three The three two one MW was reassigned to Air Force Space Command.
 one Oct one nine nine three The Air Force redesignated the three one nine th Bomb Wing as the three one nine th Air Refueling Wing, reassigned it to Air Mobility Command, and reassigned the nine zero five th Air Refueling Squadron to the wing.
 one nine nine four As part of restructuring at Grand Forks the Air Force reassigned the nine zero six th, nine one one th, and nine one two th Air Refueling Squadrons to Grand Forks AFB.
 two six May one nine nine four The last B- one B Lancer departed from Grand Forks AFB, marking the end of over three zero years of bombers at Grand Forks.
 one Jul one nine nine four Air Force Space Command redesignated the three two one MW as the three two one st Missile Group (MG).
 one Oct one nine nine five The Clinton Administration approved the Base Realignment and Closure IV committee's recommendation to remove one five zero Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missiles from the Grand Forks Air Force Base missile complex and inactivate the three two one MG.
April one nine nine seven After a harsh winter, the Grand Forks area suffered a devastating flood. Members of the Grand Forks Air Force Base were called into action, first to help protect the town from the rising waters and later to house the victims of the disaster.
 two Jul one nine nine eight The three two one MG inactivated after three four years of service at Grand Forks AFB.
 six Oct one nine nine nine The first missile silo was imploded in accordance with the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START).
 two four Aug two zero zero one The last missile silo was imploded in accordance with the START Treaty.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one . five km ( zero . six mi ).  one . five km ( zero . six mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

On July six , one nine three six , the temperature in Steele soared to one two one F, the highest temperature ever recorded in the state of North Dakota. This event is even more remarkable in light of the fact that since one nine four eight , the temperature has not exceeded one zero nine F. Never has such extreme heat been recorded so far north on the North American continent. A prolonged period of extreme drought across the entire Great Plains contributed to the extreme heat. Record high temperatures for one five states fell that summer. In the United States, higher temperatures have been recorded in only four states: California, Arizona, Nevada, and New Mexico. (Kansas set its own one two one F record on July two four .)

There are four three six households out of which three one . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five zero . two % are married couples living together, eight . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and three six . nine % are non-families. three four . four % of all households are made up of individuals and two zero . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. In the city the population is spread out with two five . six % under the age of one eight , five . one % from one eight to two four , two three . six % from two five to four four , one nine . six % from four five to six four , and two six . zero % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, eight . five % of those under the age of one eight and one seven . three % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

History
Velva was officially founded in one eight eight three by August Peterson, a Swedish immigrant. Inheriting a tract of land from his brother, Peterson's property grew to become the town of Velva. Peterson sold four zero acres to the railroad, then sold additional acres to the city. From there, the town grew into what it is today.

Business
The city of Velva is a strong supporter of growth in its own local economy. Recent companies that have moved to the town, such as a software development firm, have maintained a quality of life in the city that many towns of comparable size can only aspire to attain. Velva is a city on the grow, housing many people who commute to nearby Minot.

To compensate this growth, as well as the influx of people from nearby cities, work has recently finished on the Sunset First Addition, a new residential development located near the school.

Education
All grades are contained in the same school. Velva Public School has approximately four seven five students enrolled in grades kindergarten through one two . Services offered by the Velva School District include special education, a counselor on sight and a highly-qualified teaching staff. Optional courses available to students in grades seven - one two include Spanish II, art, creative writing, physics, chemistry, technology and advanced math classes.

 :''This article details the region of northeastern North America. For other meanings of the term, see Acadia (disambiguation).''

The national flag of Acadia, adopted in one eight eight four .

'''Acadia''' (in French '''''Acadie''''') was the name given by the French to a territory in northeastern North America which includes parts of eastern Quebec, the Maritime provinces and modern-day New England stretching as far south as Philadelphia. The actual specification by the French government for the territory refers to lands bordering the Atlantic coast, roughly between the four zero th and four six th parallels. Later, the territory was divided into the British colonies which were to become American states and Canadian provinces.

The territory's first European colonists, who would later become known as '''Acadians''', were French subjects primarily from the Pleumartin to Poitiers in the Vienne ''dpartement'' of west-central France. The first French settlement was established by Pierre Dugua, Sieur de Monts, Governor of Acadia under the authority of King Henry IV, on Saint Croix Island in one six zero four . The following year, the settlement was moved across the Bay of Fundy to Port Royal after a difficult winter on the island and deaths due to scurvy. In one six zero eight , many of the settlers followed Samuel de Champlain north to found New France in modern day Quebec City. 

Map showing areas of Acadia settled by France, one eight th century

The French took control of the Abenaki First Nations territory. In one six five four , King Louis XIV of France appointed aristocrat Nicholas Denys as Governor of Acadia and granted him the confiscated lands and the right to all its minerals. 
British colonists captured Acadia in the course of King William's War but Britain returned it to France at the peace settlement. It was recaptured in the course of Queen Anne's War and its conquest confirmed in the Treaty of Utrecht of one seven one three . 

On two three June that year, the French residents of Acadia were given one year to declare allegiance to Britain or leave Nova Scotia. In the meantime, the French signalled their preparedness for future hostilities by building Fortress Louisbourg on Cape Breton Island. The British grew increasingly alarmed by the prospect of disloyalty in wartime of the Acadians now under their rule.

In one seven five five , the British burned Acadian homes at the outbreak of the French and Indian War between Britain and France, accusing Acadians of disloyalty (for not having taken the oath) and guerrilla action. Those who still refused to swear loyalty to the British crown then suffered what is referred to as the Great Upheaval, when some six , zero zero zero - seven , zero zero zero Acadians were expelled from Nova Scotia to France or the American colonies. Others fled deeper into Nova Scotia and other parts of the colony of Canada.

Many expelled Acadians eventually settled in Louisiana, which was then still under French rule. Acadians formed the nucleus of the Cajun population. The name ''Cajun'', a corruption of ''Acadian'', is used by both English- and French-speakers. After the end of the war, Britain allowed some Acadians to return to Acadia but these were a small minority.

The poem ''Evangeline'' by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow tells the story of an expelled Acadian struggling to reunite with her love.
 
Origin of the Name
The origin of the name Acadia is credited to the explorer Giovanni da Verrazzano ( one four eight zero  one five two seven ), who had the Greek term Arcadie , meaning land of plenty, written on the entire Atlantic coast north of Virginia on his sixteenth century map. Another theory is that Acadia is derived from the Mi'kmaq term for place , pronounced akatie (still found in place names like Tracadie) and the Malecite term quoddy , also meaning a fertile place .

Contemporary Acadia
Today, ''Acadia'' refers to regions of Atlantic Canada with French roots, language, and culture. In the abstract, ''Acadia'' refers to the existence of a French culture on Canadas east coast.

In one nine nine four , Acadians and Cajuns held the first Acadian World Congress in Moncton, New Brunswick. Clive Doucet's book ''Notes from Exile'' is about the one nine nine four Acadian World Congress. Subsequent world congresses were held in one nine nine nine and two zero zero four . 

The national anthem of Acadia is ''Ave Maris Stella''.

 '''Population density''' is a measurement of population per unit area or unit volume. It is frequently applied to living organisms, humans in particular.

 Biological population densities 
A street in Hong Kong, one of the most densely-populated places in the world.
Population density is a common biological measurement and is often used by conservationists as a more appropriate measure than absolute numbers. Low population densities may cause an extinction vortex, where low densities lead to further reduced fertility. This is referred to as the Allee effect, named after W. C. Allee, who first identified it. Examples of this may include:
 Increased problems with locating mates in areas of low density.
 Increased inbreeding in areas of low population density.
 Increased susceptibility to catastrophic events in low population densities.

Different species will have different expected densities. For example R-selected species commonly have high population densities, while K-selected species may have lower population densities. Low population densities may be associated with specialised mate location adaptations such as specialised pollinators; as found in the orchid family (''Orchidaceae'').

 Human population density 
 
For humans, population density is the number of persons per unit of area (which may include or exclude cultivated or potentially productive area). Commonly this may be calculated for a county, city, country, another territory, or the entire world.

For example, the world population is six . five billion humans, and Earth's area is five one zero million square kilometers ( two zero zero million square miles). Therefore the world-wide human population density is six five zero zero million  five one zero million  one three per km ( three three per mi), or four three per km ( one one two per mi) considering that humans live on land, which forms one five zero million km of the earth. This density rises with the population growth, and some people think there is a limit of what the Earth can support.

''Ed: In the country articles in Wikipedia, the density is typically based on land area. However, the list of countries by population density is based on total area, including inland water.''

World map of the population density in one nine nine four 

Several of the highest-density territories in the world are very small city-states, micronations or dependencies. These territories share a relatively small area and an exceptionally high urbanization level, with an economically specialized city population drawing also on rural resources outside the area, illustrating the difference between high population density and overpopulation. 

The most densely populated large state is Bangladesh, where one three four million people live in a highly agricultural area around the lower Ganges river, with a national population density in excess of one zero zero zero persons per square kilometer. The Indonesian island of Java has a similar density, with one one four million people, resulting in about eight five six people per square kilometer.
 
Cities with exceptionally high population densities are often considered to be overpopulated, though the extent to which this is the case depends on factors like quality of housing and infrastructure or access to resources. Most of the largest densely-populated cities are in southern and eastern Asia, though Cairo and Lagos in Africa also fall into the category. 
 
City population is however, heavily dependent on the definition used for the urban area: densities will be far higher for the central municipality than when more recently-developed and as yet administratively unincorporated suburbs are included, as in the concepts of agglomeration or metropolitan area, the latter including sometimes neighbouring cities.

 '''Watford City''' is a city located in McKenzie County, North Dakota. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , four three five . It is the county seat of McKenzie County. The local newspaper is the ''McKenzie County Farmer''.

History
Watford City's namesake is Watford, Ontario. The former was named after the latter by Dr. Vaughan G. Morris, a Watford, Ontario native who homesteaded near Schaefer, North Dakota (now a ghost town) before resettling in Watford City, North Dakota. Born in one eight seven nine , Morris graduated from Wayne State and was Watford City's first doctor. He eventually moved to Beach, North Dakota and is buried in a cemetary between Watford City and Schaefer.

 '''Zap''' is a town located in Mercer County, North Dakota. The two zero zero zero census lists the population as two three one , in two zero zero five , the town website listed the population as two nine zero .

The Zip to Zap 
Zap is probably most widely known for the ''Zip to Zap'' which happened on May one zero , one nine six nine . This event took place at the height of civil unrest over racial segregation and the Vietnam War, but was originally intended as a spring break diversion. Between two zero zero zero and three zero zero zero people descended upon the small town of Zap as a result of an article that originally appeared in the North Dakota State University's ''Spectrum'' newspaper and was later picked up by the Associated Press. 

As the resources of the small country town were depleted, the amiable revelry began to turn ugly, and the residents of Zap asked the visitors to leave. Some of them complied, but others stayed behind, and the event became a full-fledged riot. The National Guard was called in and the crowd was dispersed. 

The ''Zip to Zap'' occurred just three months before the famous Woodstock Festival, and the situation in Zap, North Dakota undoubtedly caught the attention of the organizers in Woodstock, New York.

Pierce County, North Dakota
 
   
 '''Rugby''' is a city located in Pierce County, North Dakota of which it is the County seat. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two , nine three nine . 

History

Rugby was founded in one eight eight six at a junction on the Great Northern Railway, where the spur to Bottineau met the main line. The railroad promoters initially named it '''Rugby Junction''' for the famous railroad junction in Rugby, England in the hope of attracting English settlers. In fact about eight zero per cent of the population is of North Germanic and Scandinavian anscestry. When the community became a city the ''Junction'' was dropped from the name.

North Dakota's first permanent settlers arrived in one eight one two from the Earl of Selkirk s colony in neighboring Manitoba, Canada. As farmers, they were more advanced than many of their contemporaries in the rest of the United States, having adopted sophisticated farming methods and machinery. Many of these implements, including an early McCormick Deering threshing machine, have found their way to the restored Pioneer Village at Rugby. 

In one nine three one , the town of Rugby erected a one five foot ( four . five metre) tall rock obelisk marking the geographic center of North America . This was moved to a slightly different location in or after one nine seven one . According to a listing by the United States Geological Survey, Rugby is actually approximately two five km from the geographic center of North America, and even this designation carries no official status.

 '''Sir Joseph Paxton''' ( one eight zero three  one eight six five ) was an English gardener and architect of The Crystal Palace. 

He was born on three August one eight zero three at Milton Bryant, Bedfordshire. 
(Some references, incorrectly, list his birth date as three August one eight zero one This is as a result of misinformation he provided in his teens which he admitted in later life, which enabled him to enrol at Chiswick Gardens)

He became a garden boy, and in one eight two three obtained a position at the Horticultural Society's Chiswick Gardens. These were close to the gardens of William Cavendish, six th Duke of Devonshire at Chiswick House. After a chance meeting, and on impulse, the Duke offered the two three year-old Joseph Paxton the position of Head Gardener at Chatsworth.

On his first morning at Chatsworth, Paxton met Sarah Bown, the housekeeper's niece. They later married. He enjoyed a very friendly relationship with his employer who recognised his diverse talents and facilitated his rise to prominence.

In one eight three seven , Paxton started the Great Conservatory or Stove, a huge cast iron heated glasshouse. At the time, the Conservatory was the largest glass building in the world. However, it was prohibitively expensive to maintain, and it was destroyed in one nine two three . It took five attempts to blow it up.

The Great Conservatory was the test-bed for the prefabricated glass and iron structural techniques which Paxton pioneered and would employ for his masterpiece  The Crystal Palace of the Great Exhibition of one eight five one . These techniques were made physically possible by recent technological advances in the manufacture of both glass and cast-iron, and financially possible by the dropping of a tax on glass.

In one eight five zero Paxton was commissioned by Baron Mayer de Rothschild to design Mentmore Towers in Buckinghamshire. This was to be one of the greatest country houses built during the Victorian Era. Following the completion of Mentmore, one of Baron de Rothschild's cousins commissioned Chteau de Ferrires at Ferrires-en-Brie near Paris to be Another Mentmore, but twice the size . Both buildings still stand today.

Paxton also designed another country house, a smaller version of Mentmore at Battlesden near Woburn in Bedfordshire. This house was bought by the Duke of Bedford thirty years after its completion, and wantonly demolished, because the Duke wanted no other mansion close to Woburn Abbey.

He also worked on several other large projects at Chatsworth, such as the Arboretum, the Great Fountain, the Rock Garden and the Lily House.

Between one eight three five and one eight three nine , he organised plant-hunting expeditions, one of which ended in tragedy. Tragedy also struck at home when his eldest son died.

Paxton was honoured by being a member of the Kew Commission which was to suggest improvements for Royal Botanic Gardens, and by being considered for the post of Head Gardener at Windsor Castle.

He became affluent, not so much through his Chatsworth job, but by successful speculation in the railway industry.

In October one eight four five he was invited to lay out one of the country's first municipal burial grounds in Coventry. This became the London Road Cemetery. He later became a Liberal Member of Parliament for Coventry from one eight five four until his death in one eight six five .

In one eight three one , Paxton published a monthly magazine, ''The Horticultural Register''. This was followed in one eight three four by the ''Magazine of Botany''. There followed in one eight four zero the ''Pocket Botanical Dictionary'', ''The Flower Garden'' in one eight five zero and the ''Calendar of Gardening Operations''. In addition to these titles he also, in one eight four one , co-founded perhaps the most famous horticultural periodical, ''The Gardeners' Chronicle'' along with John Lindley, Charles Wentworth Dilke and William Bradbury and later became its editor.

He died on eight June one eight six five .

Cities in North Dakota
Richland County, North Dakota
 
   
 '''Wahpeton''' is a city located in Richland County, North Dakota. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of eight , five eight six . It is the county seat of Richland County.

Wahpeton's twin city is Breckenridge, Minnesota. The Bois de Sioux River and the Otter Tail River join at Wahpeton and Breckenridge to form the Red River of the North.

The North Dakota State College of Science is located in Wahpeton. The local newspaper is the ''Wahpeton Daily News''.

Geography
Location of Wahpeton, North Dakota

Wahpeton is located at four six  one six ' one two  North, nine six  three six ' three eight  West ( four six . two six nine nine three one , - nine six . six one zero four six three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one two . nine km ( five . zero mi ).  one two . nine km ( five . zero mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

The Red River of the North forms one of the most fertile river valleys in the world. As it flows north to Canada it forms the state boundary between North Dakota and Minnesota. Near the river's head-waters on the bank of the Bois de Sioux is Wahpeton, North Dakota. 

This is the county seat of Richland County, one of the nations largest producers of oats. Richland County ranks first in the production of soybeans, corn and hogs in North Dakota. Other crops which add to the area's economy are wheat, barley, sugarbeets and sunflowers. While Wahpeton is basically an agricultural community, its eight , five eight six citizens are proud of its recent industrial growth. Making Wahpeton their home today are manufacturers of farm machinery, metal culverts, truck equipment, factory machinery, ceramics, knives, draperies, clothing, metal stampings and fabrications and canvas and vinyl products. 
 
But Wahpeton hasn't always been the southeast gateway to North Dakota. At one time it was merely the junction of the Bois de Sioux and Otter Tail rivers which met to flow into the Red River. It was the end of the Minnesota forests and the beginning of the western plains, a place where the buffalo grass began to grow in an unbroken sweep to the Rockies.
 
The first explorer in the area was Johathan Carver in one seven six seven . He explored and mapped the Northwest at the personal request of Major Robert Rogers. Rogers was commander of Fort Mackinac, the British fort on Mackinac Island which protected the passage between Lake Michigan and Lake Huron. Carver's mission was to find the Northwest passage, the imaginary waterway to the Orient which Rogers was convinced existed. While Carver failed in his search the passing years saw many fur traders and explorers pass through the area. More than one hundred years after the Carver expedition, a Government surveying party passed through the Wahpeton area. J. W. Blanding, a member of the expedition was so impressed by the fertile river valley that he returned to his Wisconsin home determined to move his family and belongings to the Dakota Territory. Blanding so influenced other Wisconsin settlers that many of them arrived and homesteaded in the Wahpeton area before Blanding could return.
 
The first settler was Morgan T. Rich. His plow turned the first furrow of rich black bottomland in one eight six nine . When other settlers arrived, they formed a tiny community and quite naturally named it Richville. An apt name considering its founder and the fertile quality of the soil. 
 
In one eight seven one , a Post Office was opened. At the same time, the town's name was changed to Chahinkapa an Indian name meaning the end of the woods. Two years later, the county was organized and called Chahinkapa County. Later that year the county was renamed Richland County and the town of Chahinkapa renamed Wahpeton. Credit for suggesting the name Wahpeton is given to an early settler named William Cooper. Wahpeton is a contraction of the Indian name Warpeotonwe meaning Leaf Village . 

Growth of the village of Wahpeton was quite slow during the first few years. But a flurry of activity was created in one eight seven two when the St. Paul and Pacific Railway (now the Great Northern) extended a line into Breckenridge, Minnesota, a tiny community just across the Bois de Sioux River. This created a booming business in flat boat building in both Breckenridge and Wahpeton. Flat boats could carry freight directly from the railroad down river to northern North Dakota and all the way to Winnipeg. 

At the same time, the railroad opened up the area to many more settlers. Germans, Bohemians, Scandinavians and native Americans moved to Richland County to file homesteads. Wahpeton was growing. And in one eight seven four , Jacob Morvin and Joseph Sittarich opened the first retail store in the county. By one eight seven six the traffic between Wahpeton and Breckenridge had grown to where the local ferry could not handle it and a bridge was built across the Bois de Sioux River connecting the two towns. 

Another flurry of growth was realized in one eight eight zero when the St. Paul, Minneapolis and Manitoba Railroad crossed the river and pushed its tracks on toward the north-west. A few years later, in one eight eight three , the population of Wahpeton was estimated to be as high as one , four zero zero people. 

As the county seat, Wahpeton was the center of all activity. Here was the courthouse, the bank and the first flour mills. In one eight eight nine the Red River Valley University was established later to become the North Dakota State School of Science. 

As the century came to a close, Wahpeton had settled down into a hard-working agricultural community. Its frontier had, years before, passed further west. 

In one nine zero four the United States Government established the Wahpeton Indian School for the Education of Indian Children from northern Minnesota, North Dakota and northern South Dakota. 

Through the Twenties and Thirties, Wahpeton continued to grow, develop and to keep pace with the rest of the nation. It has been through this half of the Twentieth Century that the Red River Valley has earned its reputation as one of the richest agricultural belts in the nation. 

But Wahpeton is more than just a community with a history. It is a community with a future. Here is a growing city with more than eight , zero zero zero people located in a county with many producing farms, a city that boasts the most modern medical center in the area, St. Francis Hospital. Wahpeton is a community with two railroads, a bus line, five truck lines and an airport. It is the home of the North Dakota State School of Science which includes a junior college, business college trade school and technical school.
 
Recreation too, is important to the citizens of Wahpeton. The area is a virtual paradise for the outdoorsman and hunter. Located in the midst of the Western flyway, the Wahpeton area provides some of the finest migratory waterfoul hunting in the nation. And in the spring and summer when the golfers take to the links, the Bois de Sioux Golf Course offers golfers the opportunity to literally hit their tee-shot into the next state . It is the only golf course in the nation where half the course is in one state and the other half in another. 

Near the golf course is Chahinkapa Park, one of the State's outstanding parks, which offers every facility for fun and entertainment. Here young people will find all imaginable playground equipment and be enthralled with the bears, buffalo, Ilama, elk and other zoo animals. The park also boasts baseball, softball, and football facilities, miniature golf, tennis and during the summer the large swimming pool bubbles with activity. 

There are many points of interest in Wahpeton, among them is the Richland County Historical Society Museum which is the most modern of its kind in the state and it provides hours of enjoyable browsing. Just a short drive from Wahpeton is famed Fort Abercrombie, where the restored fort and museum artifacts bring back the days of the covered wagon. Just outside the city is the Circus Monument erected in memory of circus workers killed by lightning here in one eight nine seven and where circus performers hold a memorial service whenever they play in the area. The Leach Public Library houses over one seven , zero zero zero volumes in an attractive library building. Worthy of the short drive is the view of the Carmelite Monastery nestled in the bend of the Wild Rice River a few miles from Wahpeton.

Source: www.wahpeton.com

Economy

Economic Development is a program, group of policies, or activity that seeks to improve the economic well being and quality of life for a community, by creating andor retaining jobs that facilitate growth, provide a stable tax base and create wealth.

On May one four , one nine nine one , City of Wahpeton voters approved a one % city sales and use tax, the proceeds of which are to be dedicated solely to economic development of the City of Wahpeton and Richland County, North Dakota by means of business and industrial expansion including job creation, job retention, business and industrial diversification, and the creation, fostering and maintenance of business and trade activities and facilities. The tax would become effective July one , one nine nine one and sunset in five years. On June one four , one nine nine four , voters approved to extend the sales tax one zero years to June three zero , two zero zero six . And again on October one four , two zero zero three , voters approved broadening the use and extending the one  one two % sales tax to June three zero , two zero two six ensuring planned economic growth for years to come.

In addition to strictly city sales tax funds, and the  
New Construction in jobs development levy direction and administration, the Economic Development operations budget enables, leverages and includes leadershipmanagement of andor support to a much broader range of related economic development activity. This activity includes but is not limited to the Community Development Corporation, revolving loan program, planning, other city departments, housing and community development, commercial and industrial base, work force training and development, chamber, tourism, county, regional, state and federal matters.

Wahpeton is the home of several large manufacturing plants, including Imation Corporation, Woodcraft Industries, Inc., WCCO Belting, Minn-Dak Farmers Cooperative, and Cargill. Wahpeton is also home to the North Dakota State College of Science.

'''Alingss Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is in '''Alingss'''. 

Geographically the city is situated by the estuary of a small rivulet into lake Mjrn. Communications is provided by the western main line railroad (''Vstra stambanan'') between Stockholm and Gothenburg, and by motorway through the European route E two zero .

Alingss was founded as inhabitants from the city Nya Ldse were made homeless as Danish troops burnt it down. Gustavus Adolphus granted Alingss its Royal Charter in one six one nine . 

Among its historical inhabitants is Jonas Alstrmer, who was born in Alingss in one six eight five . Almstrm is credited for introducing the potato plant to Sweden. He also established a large scale draper's industry there which before soon became Sweden's largest. However, some too optimistical calculations, devastating fires and political set backs finally forced its closure in one seven seven nine .

'''Bors''' bu'ro s is a city in Vstergtland in western Sweden, situated at . It has a population of six two , zero zero zero , and is the seat of Bors Municipality. 

Granted city privileges in one six two two , it soon became a center of textile industries.

 Geography 
Bors is located at the point of two crossing railroads, among them the railway between Gothenburg and Kalmar, and is often considered the Swedish city gaining the most from the nationwide railway system laid between one eight seven zero - one nine one zero .

 History 
The city of Bors received its privileges in one six two two . The reason was to give local pedlars a legal place for merchandise.

The city developed strongly from early on. After a century it had increased to over two , zero zero zero inhabitants. 

Krokshall square with Caroli church Bors has been struck by fires four times: in one six eight one , one seven two seven , one eight two two and one eight two seven . The Caroli church is the oldest of Bors's buildings, and has withstood all fires. 

Bors cirka one seven zero zero , in Suecia antiqua et hodierna.

Industry 
Bors is the leading textile city of Sweden, starting as a location spot for textile mills. It currently holds the Swedish record in number of established mail-order firms. The city arms depicts two sheep-shearing scissors as a tribute to this.

The company Swedac is based in Bors, and
Ericsson has a large manufacturing plant there also. Mini-Link microwave radios are manufactured here.

Sports
The most successful sports team is the football team IF Elfsborg, founded in one nine zero four but receiving its current name in one nine zero six . The teams home arena is since two zero zero five Bors Arena (formerly Ryavallen Stadium) in Bors, with a capacity of one five zero zero zero . Elfsborg play in black and yellow.
Another (but not that successful) team is BHC, Bors Hockey Club.

'''Dals-Ed municipality''' is a low populated Swedish municipality in Dalsland, in western Sweden, on the border to Norway. The municipal seat is located in Ed (pop. three , three zero zero ).

 Tourism 
Dals-Ed, located in the historical province Dalsland in Sweden, has a united tourism motto for Dalsland, saying that Dalsland, with its population of five zero , zero zero zero , is a place where one will not feel crowded. This is perhaps most fitting for Dals-Ed, as it is the scarsest populated municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, with seven inhabitants per km.

Dals-Ed promises a quiet environment. The nature hosts some four zero zero lakes for bathing, canoeing, fishing or boat tours. There are also several nature reserves, and the northernmost oak woods of Sweden grows in the municipality. In addition, the large Tresticklan National Park is contained within the municipality.

Historically Dals-Ed is rewarding for those interested in the ancient. Some six zero grave fields and burial places are situated here.

 Sister cities

Jgeva Municipality in Estonia since one nine nine three 
Cepoy in France since two zero zero zero .

'''Falkping Municipality''' is located in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden where the town of '''Falkping''' is the seat with about one five , zero zero zero inhabitants.

The city of Falkping most likely emerged during the one five th century but earlier the town was an important site of pilgrimage due to its one two th century church dedicated to Saint Olaf (''Sankt Olof''). The city was heading for a shut-down during the one six th century and was even burnt to the ground by the Danes during the Northern Seven Years' War. However the city survived as one of the smallest rural cities in the kingdom.

Today Falkping has a population of about one five , five zero zero . The city is located where the Western Railline (Vstra Stambanan) between Stockholm and Gothenburg meets the railline from Nssj via Jnkping to Falkping. The city has never been a major industrial town and has existed as a mere service centre for the surrounding rural landscape, known as Falbygden.

'''Grstorp municipality''' is a small Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden where the town '''Grstorp''' (pop. three , zero zero zero ) is seat. 

Grstorp is located right in the middle of Vstra Gtaland County, by the shores of lake Vnern.

Runestone by Sal church 
The area has been inhabited at least since the Viking Age as it contains several runestone. To the left a stone by the church at Sal. The incription reads Torgrd satte denna sten efter Toke, sin frnde , meaning Torgrd raised this stone for Toke, his friend .

Grstorp was none the less only a small rural community without any town until the second half of the one nine th century. Due to its population increase, it received rights as a ''kping'' (a merchancy city) on November four , one eight nine eight . 

It became a municipality in one nine seven one , with the municipal reform. From that time stems the coat of arms.

 Towns 
Only Grstorp (pop. three , zero zero zero ) has a population > one zero zero .

'''Hjo Municipality''' is a Municipality in far east Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is in '''Hjo''' town with about six , zero zero zero inhabitants. The town is renowned as one of few wooden towns in Sweden. 

 Geography 
Geographically it is situated by the western shore of lake Vttern. The large and fish rich waters have been the main influenced on the industry. the largest rivulet intersecting the municipality from Vttern in the Hjo River. Parts of it have been made a nature reserve. Partly this is due to the salmon (''Salmo trutta'') and the grayling (''Thymullus thymullus'') that occur natural in the rivulet, but have had hard times due to dams.

 History 
Hjo was known to have had a charter already in one four one three , and was an important site for merchandice eastward.

Many wooden towns have suffered fires, but Hjo has been relatively spared, apart from when the church and some adjecent houses burnt down in one seven nine four . The city structure is therefore almost exactly the same as in the medieval times.

It works together with the towns Eksj and Nora, to develop wooden towns as tourism attraction, under the joint name Three wooden towns (''Tre Trstder'').

'''Lidkping Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. It is neatly situated on the southern shore of Lake Vnern. Its seat is located in the town Lidkping with  two five , zero zero zero inhabitants. 

Lidkping sometimes refers to itself as Lidkping by Vnern , possibly to distinguish itself from the namewise (and historically) similar city Linkping. 

 Geography 
The municipality of Lidkping is together with its western neighbor Gtene located on the Lck-Kinnekulla peninsula. In association with several large local companies, they have a colloquial tourism company known as Gtene-Lidkping Vnern Turist AB .

Lck Castle

 Symbol

'''Lilla Edet''' is a Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. It was created in one nine seven one . Its seat is located in the town Lilla Edet (pop. four , five zero zero ), also the largest town. 

The town Lilla Edet is situated on the eastern side of the Gta lv, a main river on the west coast of Sweden. It became known as a halt there. A canal lock system was built there as early as one six zero seven , becoming the first of its kind in Sweden. The commons people had named Lilla Edet as a match for Stora Edet, situated north of Lilla Edet, and today known as Trollhttan. However, the official name for Lilla Edet was for a long time Bergastrm.

 Municipal towns 
 Lilla Edet (pop. four , five zero zero )
 Gta, Lilla Edet (pop. nine seven zero )
 Ldse (pop. one , two zero zero )
 Hjrtum (pop. four zero zero )

Of these towns, Ldse is nationally known for being the original location of the city Gothenburg. In the medieval age it was a busy city and hosted an important Swedish harbour, until it was moved to its present location in one four seven three , and little remained. Today it has an interesting museum with many interesting remainings.

 Industry 
The largest employer in Lilla Edet municipality apart from the government is the paper mill SCA Hygiene Products AB Edet Bruk , with some five zero zero employees. It has been in operation for some one two zero years, and are best known today for their manufacturing of the toilet paper brand Edet , available in every store in Sweden.

'''Lysekil municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is located in the town '''Lysekil''', wherein half of the municipal population live.

 Geography 
Munkedal borders to the municipalities of: Sotens (in north-west), Munkedal (north) and Uddevalla (east). The town Lysekil is located on the southern tip of the municipality. It lays by the Kattegatt strait.

The bay to the east, marking the border to Uddevalla, is called Gullmarsfjorden, or Gullmaren. It is one of Sweden's most distinctive fjords: two five kilometers long, between one - three wide, with a maximum depth of one one eight . five meters. The depth at the mouth is only two zero - four zero meters on average, leading to a distinctive marine life in the fjord. Gullmaren is currently Sweden's only marine nature preservation area.

Some of the municipal islets are considered part of the Gothenburg archipelago. Many islets are like small communities by themselves, with interesting histories of trading, fishing and stone quarrying in addition to their scenic nature. 

 Towns 
 Lysekil seven , three zero zero 
 Brastad one , eight zero zero 
 Lyse one , seven zero zero 
 Brodalen one , zero five zero 
 Fiskebckskil four three eight 


 History 
Due to its geographical location, the industry has always been dominated by fishing, which also shows on its coat of arms. Lysekil was mainly known as a bathing location in Sweden in the one nine th century, due to its popular bathing house dating from one eight four seven .

Postcard from Fiskebckskil around one nine zero zero .

Lysekil received its charter on April one , one nine zero three , making it one of the now defunct Cities of Sweden.

Today tourism plays an important part for the economy of Lysekil.

Mariestad Cathedral, two zero zero three 
'''Mariestad Municipality''' is a Municipality in western Sweden. Its seat is in '''Mariestad''' (coor ; pop. two zero , zero zero zero ; area one zero km ). Mariestad was once the seat for the Skaraborg County (deestablished with the new year one nine nine eight ). Instead it is now part of the giant cluster called Vstra Gtaland County.

The city was founded in one five eight three by Duke Charles, who later became King Charles IX of Sweden. His wife Marie of Pfalz gave the city her name. The coat of arms for Mariestad, an oxe stepping out of water, is said to be what Marie of Pfalz saw by the bay Tidan in Mariestad when she arrived there.

Mariestad is one of two swedish cities with a cathedral but no bishop's seat (the other being Kalmar). Mariestad only had a bishop in the one seven th century, but the diocese was later merged with Diocese of Skara.

 Notable natives 
 Torbern Bergman one seven three five - one seven eight four , chemist
 Rudolf Kjelln one eight six four - one nine two two , political scientist 
 Carl Fridolf Carlsson one eight seven zero - one nine two four industrial man 
: Carlsson was during World War I the owner of Germany's largest ship industry, Schichau.
 Charles Emil Lfwenskid one eight one zero - one eight eight eight , architect. 

 Industry 
The largest employers are Electrolux and ''Katrinefors bruk''.

 Geography 
Mariestad is located by lake Vnern and is visited by many tourists in the summer. The municipality has something comparable to a small archipelago, where Tors and Bromm are the largest islands.

Mariestad cirka one seven zero zero , in Suecia antiqua et hodierna.

'''Munkedal municipality''' is a Swedish Municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is located in the town '''Munkedal''' (pop. three , seven zero zero ). It borders to the municipalities of: Dals-Ed in the north, and then clock wise Frgelanda, Uddevalla , Lysekil, Sotens and Tanum.
__NOTOC__
Geography
Munkdal is located one one zero km north of Gothenburg. The geography is a varied terrain, covered with part forests, part mountains, part plains and part lakes and streams.

History
This area in western Sweden, by the Norwegian border, has been inhabited perhaps longer than any other in Sweden. Distinctives for Munkedal are some tools that have been dated to eight , zero zero zero BC, found around one nine zero zero at a farm named Herregrda. There is also a petroglyph area called Lkeberg p Tungenset, dated to the Nordic Bronze Age. 

In the medieval age, a monastery of Dragsmark was located within the current municipal borders. It subsequently led to the name Munkedal, and the names chosen for the municipality when it was established in one nine seven four with the reform. The coat of arms also portrait a medieval scroll and writing pen, characteristics for monks.

'''Orust Municipality''' is a municipality in western Sweden. It includes Sweden's third largest island '''Orust''' and some other small adjacent islets. The population of around one five , zero zero zero increases significantly in the summer due to all summer vacationers.

It is situated in the province of Bohusln, and administratively it belongs to Vstra Gtaland County. The municipal seat is in the town Henn, with an approximate population of one , eight zero zero . 

 History 
Historically, the area has been inhabited for thousands of years, as evident by ancient remains such as tombs, grave fields and rock carvings. From the Viking Age, runestones are plenty.

 Sights 
The geography offers several sights, with a couple of picturesque small towns. There is a nature reserve called ''Morlanda'' with a look out point offering a good view.

 Industry 
Industry wise, the area has always been dominated by fishing and boat production. Shipyard ''Hallberg Rassy'' is the largerst employer nowadays. Its ship yard is located in ''Ells'', in the north-west part of the island, and it has a significant export of sailing boats. The second largest employer is Najadvarvet, also a shipyard.

'''Partille Municipality''' is a municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is in the district Partille.

The municipality is one of the smallest by size in Sweden with an area of five seven . two km. 

 Towns 
The only independent urban area in the municipality is Jonsered (pop. nine six zero ). The municipal seat Partille has grown together with Gothenburg urban area (total population five zero zero , zero zero zero ).

 Geography
Its location is just west of the major city Gothenburg (with some five zero zero , zero zero zero inhabitants), and it has gradually been incorporated into Gothenburg urban area, effecting its industrial and economical life.

The municipality is subdivided into four geographical areas: Partille , Svedalen, Jonsered and jersj. 

The area is a traditional Swedish woodland. Much of its industries has therefore a connection to the forest industry. 

 History 
The area has been inhabited for several thousands years. There still remains one five ancient monuments from that time. 

Partille is located in a valley, between some mountains in a rocky terrain. Its name is believed to be derived from something similar to Part haella and mean Split rock . The small river Sven flows through the valley and intersects Partille. Sven is said to stem from a word for calm or quiet, as it is a very slowly flowing little river. 

It is also an excellent place for fishing. Records from the one six th century prove that it was performed by government officials already then; mostly desired were then, just as now, salmons and trouts.

Partille also has an old wooden church which basically still looks as it did when it was built in the one three th century. 

 Industry 
Industries which are based in Partille include: Olegruppen, Triumfglass (ice cream), Linjebuss (bus services).

'''Skvde''' is a Swedish city in Vstergtland in Sweden, located at . It has three two , five zero zero inhabitants, with five zero , zero zero zero in the municipal area. 

 Geography 
Skvde is situated between the two largest lakes in Sweden, Vnern and Vttern. The western main railway (''Vstra Stambanan'') was located through Skvde in the one eight nine zero s, which dramatically gave the town an industrial and population boost.

 History 
 Early history 

Skvde traces its history back to the medieval age. On its city arms is the image of Saint Helena who allegedly was a pious woman from Skvde. She was born about one one zero one , and was canonized in one one six five by the Pope Alexander III and Archbishop Stefan of Sweden.

 Later history 
Of the medieval houses there are no remains, as a fire in one seven five nine burnt down the entire city except for one house. After the fire, the city was rebuilt according to the check pattern. The city still only had a small population until the railroad between Stockholm and Gothenburg was laid through the city and leading to an industrial and population boost.

 Industry 
Volvo has a large industry in the city, with more than five , zero zero zero workers. 

The higher education is located at University of Skvde, that is mainly focused on interdisciplinary educations, blending natural sciences with engineering and the arts.

There is also the Skvde Garnison, one of the countires largest regiments.

 Military 
The armoured corps regiment Skaraborgs regemente (P four ) and the logistics corps regiment Gta trngregemente (T two ) are both located in Skvde.

 Education 
The University of Skvde has six , zero zero zero students and four faculties.

'''Sotens Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in eastern Sweden. It is located in the province of Bohusln, belonging to Vstra Gtaland County, and the municipal seat is located in Kungshamn with around three , five zero zero inhabitants.

 Population figures 
Approximate inhabitants of the larger population centres in the municipality. Source: SCB statistics from two zero zero two . They are here ordered after size.

 Bohus-Malmn four zero zero 
 Vjern nine zero zero 
 Bovallstrand one , one zero zero 
 Smgen one , four zero zero 
 Hovenset one , five zero zero 
 Hunnebostrand two , zero zero zero 
 Kungshamn three , zero zero zero 

municipal map

 History 
Vstergtland has been inhabited for several thousands of years. The province, Bohusln, is among the internationally most known because of its pre-historical remains. The oldest remains in Sotens are from around six zero zero zero BCE. From the younger Stone Age are several burial monuments (dolmens). From the Bronze Age and Iron Age are many rock carvings, which the province also otherwise is noted for (especially the northern municipality Tanum). 

The name Sotens is believed to have originated from around one zero zero zero AD, when also the first steps from the historical hundred, Sotens Hundred (or ''Hrad'' in Swedish), can be traced. 

With the Christianization of Sweden several churches were erected, starting in the one one th century. The first ones were the churches in ''Askum'' and ''Tossene''. 

Later, in the one six th century, the industry became dominated by fishing of herring. It dominated the industry for centuries; herring was used in large amounts in Bohusln -- as a basic food but also in the making of oil, wax candles, etc. 

In the one nine th century the island Malmn was started as a quarry. (Note that Malm means rock in Swedish). The quarry was kept alive and was of industrial significance until the one nine three zero s. 

Sotens hundred insignia anno one seven four six 
The coat of arms was granted in one nine seven seven and depicts a halibut. It is built on the insignia for Sotens Hundred and has been used for centuries.

'''Stenungsund Municipality''' is a Municipality in Bohus County in western Sweden; administratively belonging to Vstra Gtaland County. Its seat is in '''Stenungsund''' (pop. nine , six zero zero ). The municipality is often divided into six communities; Stenungsund, Stora Hga, Jrlanda, Spekerd, dsml and Svenshgen.

The municipality had Sweden's procentual largest expansion in the year two zero zero three .

The town is located right by the European route E six highway and the railway Bohusbanan. 

 History 
Stenungsund was once only an idyllic bathing and vacation location on the Swedish west coast. Since the one nine five zero s it has become the center for the petrochemical industry. Its distinguished silhouette is four giant chimneys, belonging to a large power plant. Another landmark is the Tjrn Bridge, a bridge to the island Tjrn.

'''Strmstad''' is a Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is in Strmstad.

Geography 
Strmstad is located on the Norwegian border and is known to attract large numbers of shoppers from Norway. 

The town is located at the estuary of the small Strmstad River.
 History 
Originally, the province Bohusln, where Strmstad is situated, belonged to Norway until one six five eight , when Sweden took it through warfare. At Strmstad, there was a small fishing village known as ''Strmmen''. The town got small privileges as a merchant town (''kping'') shortly thereafter, which seems to have made it expand, because it is documented to have gotten a charter in one six seven six by King Charles IX of Sweden, yet some documents show it was considered a city in one six seven two . As it was the seat for a merchant navy, the coat of arms was designed with such a ship, and has remained that way even after the sailing ships navy were discontinued in the one nine th century. 

The city became the seat for Sweden's warfare, and more than once it was conquered and reconquered throughout the centuries. The warlike King Charles XII of Sweden, for instance, used it as his outpost for his campaign against Norway in one seven one six - one seven one eight . 

At the time it had a population of three zero zero inhabitants. But soon the fishing blossomed, and it population increased to one , one zero zero by one eight zero five . The late one eight th century also saw the spa and bathing attract visitors, a position it kept throughout the one nine th century. By one nine one seven , its population was two , nine four nine inhabitants.

 Notability 
As the Norwegian alcohol taxes are higher than the Swedish ones, Norwegian shoppers have caused the Swedish alcohol retailing monopoly Systembolaget to open an extra store to cater the need.

The city is known for its yachting harbour.

 Tidaholm pedestrian area. '''Tidaholm''' is a Municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. The municipality covers an area of five two one . four km and is located on the banks of the river Tidan. Of the total population of one two six nine four , six three four two are male, and six three five two are female. The population density of the community is two four inhabitants per km.

Early Tidaholm was primarily an agricultural estate. An ironworks was established in one seven nine nine at the site of the Holmagarden forge. The ironworks were replaced in one eight six eight by a match factory. The Vulcan match factory eventually became the largest in the world. Today, the Lithographic Art Workshop in Tidaholm resides in the former factory and carries on the tradition of lithographic arts in Tidaholm that was begun by designers of matchbook labels.

Example of a medieval Swedish church in the Tidaholm area. Many well-preserved medieval churches stand in the municipality of Tidaholm. Some church sites also contain examples of early Scandinavian rune stones.

'''Tjrn Municipality''', ''Tjrns kommun'', is a Swedish municipality that covers the island of '''Tjrn''', in the province Bohusln in western Sweden; administratively Vstra Gtaland County. 

Tjrn is the fifth largest Swedish island. It is located on the Swedish West coast, in the province of Bohusln.

The municipality and island covers an area of one six seven . three km, has a total population of one four , seven three three , (as of two zero zero one  whereof seven , five four three male and seven , one nine zero female) and a population density of eight eight inhabitants per km. Its seat is located in Skrhamn.

The industry was for centuries dominated by fishing and boat production. The largest employers are still the shipyards B&N, Djupviks varv and Rnnviks varv.

Geography
Tjrn is connected in the east to the town of Stenungsund on the mainland by the Tjrn bridge, and to the island of Orust in the north by the Skpesund bridge. The largest town is Skrhamn, and it is also the municipal capital. Other communities, many of which are fishing communities, include Rnnng, Kldesholmen, and Kyrkesund. The peninsula of Mjrn has beautiful scenery, and large shell banks.

Waterfalls in Trollhttan 
'''Trollhttan Municipality''' is a Municipality in western Sweden where the City '''Trollhttan''' is the seat with a population of four four , zero zero zero inhabitants. 

History
Trollhttan was founded by the river Gta lv, at a location with several waterfalls. The site was first mentioned in literature from one four one three . For centuries, Trollhttan was an obstacle for the boats travelling the river, up until a lock system was completed in the nineteenth century. It has since been updated several times and the present locks were finished in one nine one six .

In the late nineteenth century, hydropower was developed in Trollhttan. The Swedish energy corporation Vattenfall ( waterfall ) took its name from the falls in Trollhttan. Today the city has two operational hydropower stations, Olidan and Hjum. The hydropower has helped the city in its industrial revolution.

The name Trollhttan comes from folkloristic tales. People believed that large trolls lived in the river Gta lv and that the islands in the river were the Trolls' hoods ( httor ). Other former names of the site is ''Eidar'' and ''Stora Edet''; the latter lives on in the name of the south-bordering municipality of Lilla Edet. The waterfall of Trollhttan has been theorized to be the Mimir's Well from the Norse mythology.

Trollhttan was granted city rights in one nine one six at which time it had about one five , zero zero zero inhabitants.
SAAB car sticker

Industries
Trollhttan houses a number of industries, foremost the main production sites for Saab Automobile and Volvo Aero. In the area, there is also a large number of suppliers to these two facilities. Historically Trollhttan housed the NOHAB industries who produced locomotives.
 
There is also a film production facility, known as Trollywood; movies shot there include ''Fucking ml'', ''Dancer in the Dark'' and ''Dogville''. The movie studio Film i Vst centered here produces about half of the Swedish full-length films.

'''Ulricehamn Municipality''' is located in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is in the town of '''Ulricehamn''' with nine , zero zero zero inhabitants. It is the largest municipality in Vstra Gtaland County with its one , zero five one km two .

Geography
The town is located on the slopes of a lakeside, where the river tran flows into lake sunden. The geography is signified by the scenic nature of trees and water, which offers popular activities such as bicycling, inlining and boat trips. 

In the winter, Ulricehamn has become something of the Ski centre of Western Sweden. For alpine skiing, there are seven lifts and six slopes; while for cross-country skiing there are some two one zero kilometers of prepared courses.
 
History
Ulricehamn, originally known as ''Bogesund'' has been populated at least since the middle ages. The town has had city privileges since at least the one five th century. There are still several old buildings from the one seven th and one eight th century and the picturesque main street ''Storgatan'' has existed in its present form for centuries. Among other historical structures, there is the city hall, located at the market square, a yellowish rococo building from one seven eight nine .

The town is situated on ''transtigen'' ( The tran path ), a trail following the river tran, stretching from the Kattegat strait in the west an inwards the country, connecting with other roads leading eventually to the eastern cities Sigtuna and Upsala. 

In one seven four one , it was renamed Ulricehamn in honour of Queen Ulrica Eleonora. Following a fire in one seven eight eight it encountered a recession, but several textile industries were established in the one nine th century. Together with its first railroad in one eight seven four the town's importance as a center of trade increased.

Ulricehamn (then Bogesund) around one seven zero zero , viewed from the south. Lake sunden on the left. From Suecia antiqua et hodierna.

'''Vnersborg Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is in the town '''Vnersborg''' with two one , zero zero zero inhabitants. 

The city is an important harbour for lake Vnern. It took its name when the inhabitants of the town Brtte to the south moved and founded it in one five four zero . The remains of Brtte is a popular attraction. 

Vnersborg received its charter in one six four four , becoming one of the defunct Cities of Sweden. Its coat of arms stems from that time, depicting a golden ship with two swedish flags.

Around one eight zero zero , Vnersborg and its one , five zero zero inhabitants were a decent city. After the inauguration of the canal at Trollhttan and the Gta lv -- making a waterway between Vnern and Gothenburg -- its importance further grew.

In one eight three four , most of the city with its wooden houses burnt down. Thereafter it was rebuilt according to a check pattern.

From one six nine three to one nine nine nine , Vnersborg was the capital of lvsborg County, until it was merged into Vstra Gtaland County.

Image:Birger Sjbergs Frida.jpgThe poet Birger Sjberg ( one eight eight five - one nine two nine ) was born in Vnersborg. He wrote appreciative about Vnersborg, most notably in ''Fridas bok'' ( one nine two two ), wherein the comparisment Vnersborg -- little Paris is found. The park in the northern part of Vnersborg, Skrckleparken, offers a picturesque view over Vners, and therein also stands this statue of mentioned Frida.

'''ml Municipality''' is located in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is located in the town '''ml''' with nine , three zero zero inhabitants.

 Geography 
The town ml is located in a bay of the lake Vnern, the largest lake in Sweden, at some five zero meter above sea level, and is considered a scenic location. The municipality has a small archipelago with some three zero islands located south of the town ml. It is called ''Tsse skrgrd'' and is nature reserve. Many of the islands are grown with woods, but a few are used for farming. They are inhabited by several different birds, including heron, osprey, mallard, goldeneye, goosander, the black-throated diver and hobby in the bays; on the cobs are colonies of herring gull, seagull and the common tern; while on the fir covered islands are capercaillie, woodpeckers and other birds.

In older times, fishing was an important industry, as apparent on the coat of arms that have been used at least since the one nine th century. Wood industry was also of importance.

 History 
On this engraving from Suecia Antiqua et Hodierna, from one seven zero eight , we see the location of ml by the lake, and the surrounding hills, and a church to the right.
ml was founded in the one seven th century, and became one of the now defunct Cities of Sweden already in one six four six , and the only city in the historical province of Dalsland. Its location close to the borders of the Denmark-Norway alliance made it suffer in the ensuing centuries. First in one six four five when it was almost completely demolished, furthermore in one six seven six and one six seven nine ; and the last time in one seven eight eight when it was conquered by the Danes who held it for a short while. 

After the last severe fire in one nine zero one , whereby one , zero zero zero people became homeless, it was rebuilt with wider streets and larger houses.

 Notability
The movie ''Fucking ml'' (released in English as ''Show Me Love'') is set there (but was actually shot in Trollhttan) and depicts it as a relatively boring and normal town.

'''cker Municipality''' is located in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. It consists of islands in the Gothenburg archipelago, just outside of Gothenburg. With a total area of two six km it is one of the smallest municipalities of Sweden.

 Specifics 
The municipality consists of ten islands. They are considered to strech from a renowned lighthouse called ''Vinga fyr'' up to the coastal town of Marstrand in the municipality of Kunglv. The ten islands are named 
 Bjrk (Gothenburg)
 Fot
 Grt
 Hyppeln
 Hls
 Hn
 Kalvsund
 Kll-Knippla
 Rr
 cker. 

NB that  means island in Swedish language.

Of these, Hn is the largest with some four , eight zero zero inhabitants, and cker is also fairly large with three , one zero zero . However, all ten are inhabited by people all year around. The connections are good and several islands are trafficated by ferries from Gothenburg.

 History 
During the Viking Age the islands of cker belonged to the Norwegian kings, and the part of the coast was known as ''lvsyssel''. In the one three th century the King Hkan Hkansson of Norway built himself a house on cker, because he was often around there with his navy. 

In one six five eight or thereabout, the area became Swedish together with Bohusln. 

In the midth one eight th century, the fishing of herring blossomed into a full scaled industry, and the islands fishing communities flourished for some five zero years.

In the one nine five zero s the coat of arms were designed. As the main industry has always been fishing, a boat and herring became symbols. The ten herrings correspond to the ten islands.

 References 
 The corresponding article on Swedish Wikipedia has been used as main reference.

'''Ale Municipality''' is a Municipality in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. The seat is located in Ndinge-Nol.

The town Ndinge-Nol was once three communities: Alafors, Nol and Ndinge. They have grown together into one urban area.

 Image:FIAV_ four eight .png Flag ratio: two : three -- Flag of Guernsey
Flag ratio: one : two -- St George's Cross
The Present flag of Guernsey was adopted in one nine eight five and consists of the red cross of St. George with an additional gold cross within it. The Gold cross represents Duke William of Normandy, who had such a cross on his flag in the Battle of Hastings.

The previous flag of Guernsey was just the St George's Cross. Guernsey was permitted to use it in one nine three six for its state flag.

'''Mark Municipality''' is located in Vstra Gtaland County, in western Sweden. Its seat is located in the largest town Kinna (pop. one four , zero zero zero ).

The municipality was created with the municipal reform (see: Municipalities of Sweden) in the early one nine seven zero s and took its name from an old name of the hundred.
__NOTOC__
 Coat of arms
The coat of arms was created and granted with the municipality in the one nine seven zero s. The ''circles'' in coat of arms come the one six th century insignia of the Mark hundred. The grain signifies the farming industry; and the thing at the right is a weaving tool; because the municipality had, and still has, a strong textile industry.

Sister cities 
Mark has three sister cities. They have been focusing on towns or municipalities that also had a significant textile industry.

 Szamotuly in Poland (since one nine eight eight ). Sparked because of the awakened awareness of Nuclear power in Szamotuly, who wanted contacts with Swedish cities because of Sweden's ongoing nuclear debates.
 Apolda in eastern Germany (cirka one nine nine four one nine nine five )
 Ontinyent (since two zero zero three )

See also
Mark Hundred
