 '''Jamestown''' is a city located in Stutsman County, North Dakota. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one five , five two seven . It is the county seat of Stutsman County.

The local paper is the ''Jamestown Sun''. Jamestown Regional Airport serves the city.

Geography
Location of Jamestown, North Dakota

Jamestown is located at four six  five four ' two zero  North, nine eight  four two ' one one  West ( four six . nine zero five six four one , - nine eight . seven zero two nine nine four ) at the confluence of the James River and Pipestem Creek.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three two . four km ( one two . five mi ).  three two . two km ( one two . four mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . four zero % water.

History
In one eight seven two , the US Army established Fort Seward, a small post garrisoned by three companies (about one two zero men) of the Twentieth Infantry Regiment, on a bluff overlooking the confluence of the James River and Pipestem Creek. The fort guarded the crossing of the James by the Northern Pacific Railroad. The fort only lasted five years, being decommissioned in one eight seven seven - but the railroad remained, establishing a repair yard that was among the city's main industries until the one nine six zero 's. In one eight eight three , the City of Jamestown was incorporated.

Demographics
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one five , five two seven people, six , five zero five households, and three , seven nine eight families residing in the city. The population density is four eight one . five km ( one , two four six . seven mi ). There are six , nine seven zero housing units at an average density of two one six . two km ( five five nine . six mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine six . eight four % White, zero . three six % African American, one . two one % Native American, zero . four nine % Asian, zero . zero five % Pacific Islander, zero . two seven % from other races, and zero . seven eight % from two or more races.  one . one nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

The top six ancestry groups in the city are German ( five four . zero %), Norwegian ( two two . four %), Irish ( nine . zero %), English ( six . six %), Swedish ( four . one %), Russian ( three . eight %). Many area families cite their heritage as Germans from Russia, in reference to a group of German emigrants who temporarily settled in Russia before coming to the United States.

There are six , five zero five households out of which two seven . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four six . eight % are married couples living together, eight . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and four one . six % are non-families. three seven . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one seven and the average family size is two . eight five .

In the city the population is spread out with two one . seven % under the age of one eight , one two . seven % from one eight to two four , two five . seven % from two five to four four , two one . eight % from four five to six four , and one eight . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three nine years. For every one zero zero females there are nine two . zero males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight eight . four males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three one , five zero zero , and the median income for a family is $ four two , two four five . Males have a median income of $ two eight , three one zero versus $ two zero , two two five for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one six , six eight six .  one zero . seven % of the population and six . five % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one two . four % of those under the age of one eight and one zero . eight % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Culture
Jamestown is the home of the World's Largest Buffalo.  This cement statue overlooks the city in a tourist attraction called The Frontier Village.  The pride of Jamestown is White Cloud , an albino buffalo housed in a fenced off area next to Frontier Village.  White Cloud lives with her daughter, Princess Winona , amongst a herd of fellow buffalo. 

Much of the city's cultural life centers around Jamestown College, a four-year liberal arts institution on the city's north side, and the Prairie Arts Center in downtown Jamestown, a home-grown art gallery and performance space that showcases regional visual arts and local performers. 

Famous natives of Jamestown include western author Louis L'Amour, pop singer Peggy Lee, disc jockey Shadoe Stevens, Cleveland Indians star Travis Hafner, and California Angels' star Darin Erstad.

 '''Ferdinand III, Grand Duke of Tuscany''', or, more fully, '''His Imperial and Royal Highness Ferdinando III Giuseppe Giovanni Baptista Grand Duke of Tuscany, Archduke of Austria, Prince of Hungary and Bohemia''', (May six , one seven six nine  June one eight , one eight two four ; born and died in Florence, Italy), was the son of Emperor Leopold II ( one seven four seven - one seven nine two ) and his wife Maria Luisa of Spain ( one seven four five - one seven nine two ).

He was married on August one five , one seven nine zero , at Naples, Italy, to Princess Luisa Maria Amelia Teresa of the Two Sicilies (July two seven , one seven seven three - September one nine , one eight zero two ), daughter of Fernando I of the Two Sicilies ( one seven five one - one eight two five ) and his wife Maria Carolina of Austria ( one seven five two - one eight one four ).

Their children were:
 Carolina Ferdinanda Theresia ( one seven nine three - one eight zero two )
 Franz Leopold ( one seven nine four - one eight zero zero )
 Leopold II ( one seven nine seven - one eight seven zero )
 Marie Louise Josephe Christine Rose ( one seven nine nine - one eight five seven )
 Maria Teresa ( one eight zero one - one eight five five )
 ? ( one eight zero two )

He was married again on May six , one eight two one at Florence, Italy to Maria of Saxony (or, more fully, Her Highness Maria Ferdinande Amalia Xaveria Theresia Josepha Anna Nepomucena Aloysia Johanna Vincentia Ignatia Dominica Franziska de Paula Franziska de Chantal, Duchess of Saxony) (April two seven , one seven nine six - January three , one eight six five ), daughter of Maximilian, Prince of Saxony, ( one seven five nine - one eight three eight ) and his wife Caroline of Bourbon-Parma ( one seven seven zero - one eight zero four ). There were no children born of this second marriage.

Ferdinand succeeded his father as Grand Duke of Tuscany in one seven nine zero , and ruled in Tuscany until one eight zero one , when he was forced by Bonaparte to give up Tuscany to the Bourbons of Parma, who turned it into the Kingdom of Etruria. Ferdinand was compensated by being given the secularized lands of the Archbishopric of Salzburg and several other ecclesiastical princes in Germany, and was made a Prince-elector of the Holy Roman Emperor. By the Treaty of Pressburg of one eight zero five , Ferdinand was made to give up Salzburg, which was annexed by his brother, the Emperor of Austria, and instead became Duke of Wrzburg, a new state created for him from the old Bishopric of Wrzburg. He remained in this role until Napoleon's fall in one eight one four , when he returned to Tuscany, which he ruled until his death.

The '''County of Avon''' was a short-lived non-metropolitan county and ceremonial county in the west of England, named after the River Avon which ran through it.


Creation
Avon was formed under the Local Government Act one nine seven two , on April one , one nine seven four . It took in the areas of the former county boroughs of Bristol and Bath, and areas from the administrative counties of Gloucestershire (Kingswood, Mangotsfield, and the rural districts of Warmley, Sodbury (most) and Thornbury (most)), and Somerset (Weston-super-Mare, Clevedon, Keynsham, Norton-Radstock, Portishead, and the rural districts of Bathavon, Long Ashton, Axbridge (much), and Clutton (much). Like most of the new counties created by the Act, its boundaries were substantially trimmed from its inception, with Frome and Bradford-on-Avon removed from the proposed area.

It had six districts. Bristol and Bath were taken in directly from the former county boroughs. In the north, the Gloucestershire side, the urban districts of Kingswood and Mangotsfield formed a single borough of Kingswood, with the rest becoming Northavon. In the south, there were two districts, Woodspring, on the coast, and Wansdyke, in the interior.

To the north it bordered Gloucestershire, to the east Wiltshire and to the south Somerset. In the west it had a coast on the Bristol Channel.

The area of Avon was one three four seven km two ( five two zero mi two ) and its population in one nine nine one was nine one nine , eight zero zero . Cities and towns in Avon included (in approximate order of population) Bristol, Bath, Weston-super-Mare, Yate, Clevedon, Portishead, Midsomer Norton county title from their city, and many people in parts of Gloucestershire and Somerset that were now included in Avon felt they had been cut off from their traditional counties. In particular there was a long-running campaign to return Weston-super-Mare to Somerset. The county did however have a fairly strong rational basis, being largely conterminous with the Bristol 'Travel to Work Area' defined since the five zero s six zero s for planning purposes.

Avon was one of the counties in the first tranche of reviews conducted by the Banham Commission in the one nine nine zero s. The Commission recommended that it and its districts be abolished and replaced with four unitary authorities. The Avon (Structural Change) Order one nine nine five was debated in the Commons on February two two , .
 
The Order came into effect on one April one nine nine six . The four authorities replacing Avon were The City and County of Bristol, South Gloucestershire (formerly Kingswood and Northavon), North Somerset (formerly Woodspring) and Bath and North East Somerset (formerly Bath and Wansdyke). For ceremonial purposes, the post of Lord Lieutenant of Avon has been abolished, Bristol has regained its own Lord Lieutenant and High Sheriff, while the other authorities were returned to their traditional counties.

Suggestions to alter Bristol's boundaries (either by drawing new boundaries or by merely incorporating the mostly urbanised borough of Kingswood into it) were rejected.

Legacy

The demise of the County of Avon was the focus of a documentary called The End of Avon by the BBC produced by Linda Orr and Michael Lund broadcast in one nine nine six . In two zero zero six Adam Thomas, a BBC Somerset Sound presenter, investigated, for Inside Out West on BBC One, why Avon refuses to die and continues to be included in the databases of large corporations as part of addresses in the area and in names such as Avon Wildlife Trust, the Avon and Somerset Constabulary, and Avon Fire and Rescue. Representatives from the organisations said they had no plans to change their names. However, the Royal Mail indicated that it was not necessary to include Avon as part of any address as it had abandoned the use of the former postal county in one nine nine six .

Some bodies still cover the whole area of the former county of Avon - for example the Avon Fire Brigade, the Avon Coroner's District and the West of England Strategic Partnership. Additionally the whole of the area is covered by Avon and Somerset Constabulary. 
Arms of '''Avon County Council'''

The term ''CUBA'', the Counties that Used to Be Avon , has been coined to refer to the Avon area post-abolition of the county. The term Severnside is sometimes used as a euphemism for 'Avon', although the term can also be used to refer to the stretch of shoreline from Avonmouth north to Aust, or from Newport to Chepstow. Many computer-generated address lists still give addresses in the area as being in the county of 'Avon', as it is a former postal county (see Postal counties of the United Kingdom).

Other relics of Avon's existence include the '''Avon Cycleway''', an eight five -mile circular route, which wends its way on quite roads and bridletracks around (or just beyond) the outer limits of the former county. Also, Avon County Council funded Sustrans' first cycleway, the Bristol and Bath railway path, which led to the creation of the National Cycle Network.

Traill County, North Dakota
 
   
 '''Hillsboro''' is a city in the U.S. state of North Dakota. It is the county seat of Traill County. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , five six three . 

Hillsboro sits in the fertile Red River Valley. Local agriculture has dominated the area's economy from the beginning. With its location on Interstate two nine , halfway between the two metropolitan centers of Greater Grand Forks and Fargo-Moorhead, Hillsboro has seen steady population growth in recent years and has become somewhat of a bedroom community. 

Hillsboro is known for having the oldest weekly newspaper in the state, the ''Hillsboro Banner''.

History
The area along the Goose River that is now Hillsboro was first settled by German and Norwegian settlers around one eight seven zero . 

Local folklore tells of the residents of nearby Caledonia, North Dakota turning away a shabby surveyor because of his appearance. This man was then offered hospitality by residents in a tiny settlement west of Caledonia. The man turned out to be railroad baron James J. Hill. Hill was impressed by the kindness showed to him by the residents of this small community and decided to place his Great Northern Railroad there instead of in Caledonia. This was a major blow to the future of Caledonia and a boon for the town that named itself after James J. Hill - Hillsboro.

Geography
Location of Hillsboro, North Dakota

Hillsboro is located at four seven  two four ' one four  North, nine seven  three ' three eight  West ( four seven . four zero three nine six zero , - nine seven . zero six zero five three one ).

Hillsboro sits on the banks of the Goose River in eastern North Dakota. It is in the center of the fertile Red River Valley. The area around Hillsboro is prime agricultural land. The land in and around the city is very flat.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two . eight km ( one . one mi ).  two . eight km ( one . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

Demographics
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , five six three people, six seven nine households, and four one four families residing in the city. The population density is five six four . zero km ( one , four six zero . six mi ). There are seven two seven housing units at an average density of two six two . three km ( six seven nine . four mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine four . eight two % White, zero . one nine % African American, two . zero five % Native American, zero . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, two . one one % from other races, and zero . eight three % from two or more races.  four . nine three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six seven nine households out of which three zero . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four nine . five % are married couples living together, six . six % have a female householder with no husband present, and three eight . nine % are non-families. three six . seven % of all households are made up of individuals and two zero . six % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two three and the average family size is two . nine two .

In the city the population is spread out with two five . two % under the age of one eight , five . eight % from one eight to two four , two five . seven % from two five to four four , two one . nine % from four five to six four , and two one . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four one years. For every one zero zero females there are nine four . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . one males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three three , five one six , and the median income for a family is $ four two , three five seven . Males have a median income of $ three zero , six zero seven versus $ one nine , seven six nine for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one seven , nine seven six .  nine . two % of the population and six . six % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, nine . four % of those under the age of one eight and one five . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Economy
The economy of Hillsboro, like so many other small, rural towns in North Dakota, is heavily dependent on agriculture. When local farmers have a bad harvest, the Hillsboro economy can also suffer. In turn, when the harvest is good, Hillsboro usually prospers. One of the more obvious effects the agricultural community has had on Hillsboro is found at the Crystal Sugar sugar beet plant directly north of town. The large plant, located on U.S. Highway eight one , has been responsible for both an increase in population and a steady stream of available jobs during the last few decades that it has been open.

In recent years, Hillsboro has become a bedroom community for the Greater Grand Forks and Fargo-Moorhead metropolitan areas. This has led to an increase in both population and home construction. However, the local business community has, for the most part, not reaped the benefits of the growth. Many Hillsboro residents pass up Hillsboro stores and restaurants in favor of the better selections available in the Grand Forks and Fargo areas. The once bustling downtown area (centered at the intersection of Caledonia Avenue and Main Street) has become filled with empty storefronts.

Education
The Hillsboro Public Schools system provides residents with an elementary school and a high school. 

Hillsboro High School's athletic teams are known as ''The Burros'', which makes their mascot the donkey. Recent budget cuts have forced the high school to discontinue its dining services, so high school students eat lunch at the elementary school down the street. The high school does not offer Advanced Placement classes, but has a dual credit program through Lake Region State College. These classes are worth college credit at most in-state colleges and universities.

In two zero zero three , four zero % of students met or exceeded grade-level standards in Math, and seven six % of students met or exceeded grade-level standards in English, above-average when compared to the state average of three nine % and six one %, respectively.

Culture
Recreation
The city of Hillsboro operates a large park on the north side of town. Woodland City Park sits on the banks of the Goose River. It offers a public swimming pool and scenic views of a dam on the river. For many years, there has also been a group of deer living in a penned in area of the park. The Goose River Golf Club sits directly north of town.

Media
The local paper is the weekly ''Hillsboro Banner''. The ''Banner'' has been published continuously since one eight seven nine , making it the oldest weekly newspaper in the state of North Dakota.
Hillsboro has no local radio stations or network television affiliates, but residents have access to radio stations and network affiliates from both Grand Forks and Fargo.

Sites of interest
'''The Plummer House''' - a historic one eight nine seven mansion that has been converted to a museum and restored to its turn of the century elegance
'''Pioneer Museum''' - museum complex featuring:
:'''Centennial Building''' - military, school, and pioneer collections
:'''Pioneer Building''' - agriculture collection
:'''St. Olaf Chapel''' - newly constructed church that resembles small, rural Churches that typify the Red River Valley
:'''Log Cabin''' - a log cabin built on the banks of the Red River of the North in the one eight seven zero s

Transportation
Residents of Hillsboro have easy access to major population centers via Interstate two nine . The Interstate runs on the western edge of the community and there is an interchange (Caledonia Avenue) that connects the Interstate to Hillsboro. U.S. Highway eight one runs through the community and also connects Hillsboro to Grand Forks and Fargo. 

Like so many towns in the American Midwest, Hillsboro's streets are aligned in the grid pattern. In Hillsboro, routes that run north to south are called ''streets'' and routes that run east to west are called ''avenues''.

Hillsboro is located on the railroad, but, unlike in the town's early years, it rarely stops and no longer plays a significant role in daily life. There is also a small airport south of town with a landing strip which provides an area for crop dusters or small private airplanes to stop. However, residents have to travel either to Grand Forks or Fargo in order to take regularly scheduled flights to major airports.

 '''Mayville''' is a city located in Traill County, North Dakota. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , nine five three which makes Mayville the largest community in Traill County. Mayville is often grouped with the neighboring city of Portland, North Dakota.  The two towns are sometimes given the name May-Port. Mayville State University is located in Mayville. 

Geography
Location of Mayville, North Dakota

Mayville is located at four seven  two nine ' five nine  North, nine seven  one nine ' three two  West ( four seven . four nine nine eight three zero , - nine seven . three two five five four five ).

Mayville sits in the fertile Red River Valley on the banks of the Goose River. The Valley was once a part of glacial Lake Agassiz. As the glacier receded, it left the land very flat, but also very rich. The area around Mayville is prime agricultural land.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of four . two km ( one . six mi ).  four . two km ( one . six mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

Mayville is also the home of Mayville State University.

Recreation
Mayville offers several parks with the largest being Island Park. The MayPort Community Center opened in two zero zero zero and offers space for hockey games and other community events. The Mayville Water Park opened in two zero zero two and features one of the larger water slides in the area. Mayville is also home to the nine -hole Mayville Golf Club.

 '''Bootleg''' was a term which originally referred to the shank or top part of a boot, the part which is around the leg instead of the foot. From the practice of hiding small items in a boot shaft to smuggle them past the authorities, the word became a verb, meaning to smuggle and an adjective, describing something that has been smuggled (or, more rarely, stolen). Those involved in the activity, bootlegging , are often known as bootleggers . 

The term bootleg can also refer to:
Bootleg recording, an otherwise unavailable audio or video recording distributed without the artist's consent 
Bootleg liquor, an alcoholic beverage sold without regard to legal regulations and taxes
Bootleg play, a tactic in American football 
Bootleg turn, a car maneuver
Bootleg pants, trousers which flare-out at the bottom of the legs and thus can cover the wearer's shoes.
''BOOTLEG'', an Australian television program

It may also refer to:
Pirate copy, an unauthorised duplicate of material already commercially available, sold illegally for significantly less than the standard retail price
Counterfeit merchandise
Bastard pop, music which contains unlicensed samples of other music

 Minot today, seen from North Hill

:''For other things named Minot see Minot (disambiguation).''

'''Minot''' (IPA , ) is a city located in north central North Dakota, USA. With three six , five six seven people, Minot is the fourth largest city in the state. The city is the county seat of Ward County and the trading center of a large portion of northern North Dakota, southwestern Manitoba, and southeastern Saskatchewan. Minot is also known as the Magic City.

Geography
Location of Minot, North Dakota

External
Minot is located in north central North Dakota, at ( four eight . two three three one nine zero , - one zero one . two nine two two two nine ). Minot is located about one seven zero km ( one zero zero mi) north of Bismarck, three zero zero km ( two zero zero mi) west of Grand Forks and four zero zero km ( two five zero mi) northwest of Fargo and southeast of Regina, Saskatchewan. 	 

The city is on the Souris River (also known as the Mouse River), some three zero km from its southernmost point near Velva. It eventually turns northwest and meets with the Assiniboine River .

Internal
According to the Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three seven . seven km ( one four . six mi ). It is almost entirely land; the Souris River, its oxbow lakes, and a few creeks take up just zero . one four % of the city's total landmass.

Grid and address system
The city is laid on a grid-based street system. Streets run North-South and Avenues run East-West. Streets are numbered by their block distance east or west of Main Street. Similarly, Avenues are numbered north and south of Central Avenue. There are four city quadrants (NW, SW, SE, NE) to describe the exact location of any given address. Main Street addresses are simply designated North and South. Central Avenue addresses are simply designated East and West.

Examples:

 five one five  two nd Avenue SW (City Hall) is located a little more than five blocks west of Main Street on two nd Avenue South.	 

 three five one five  one six th St SW (the Minot YMCA) is located three five blocks south of Central Avenue on one six th Street West.

City districts
The City of Minot has a number of distinct regions. Here's a partial listing.

:''Major divisions''
The Souris River, also known as the Mouse River, divides the city approximately in half, north and south. The valley rises to the plains both north and south of the river. Minot does not have particular names for these general topographic divisions of the city. The Valley is simply '''the Valley''' (or not called anything at all). The northern rise and the plateau north of it is referred to as '''North Hill''' and the southern rise and plateau south of it is referred to as '''South Hill'''.

:''Commercial Areas''
Minot has several commercial areas, the first of which is '''Broadway''' itself, the main north-south trunk route.

'''Downtown''' generally refers to the area bounded by Broadway, three rd Street East, Central Avenue, and Burdick Expressway, though the immediate vicinity is often also included.

There is a major shopping district along one six th Street SW south of the US two five two eight three bypass, including '''Dakota Square Mall''', Wal-Mart, and various other shops.

The '''Arrowhead Mall''' is located at Central Avenue and one six th Street West. '''Oak Park Center''' is nearby, along four th Avenue NW. There is also '''Town and Country Center''', located at Broadway and one one th Avenue SW.

:''Neighborhoods''
More specific named divisions tend to be upscale residential areas. These include '''Bel-Air''', which is the area north of four th Avenue NW and west of one six th Street NW and includes Bel-Air Elementary School, '''Eastwood Park''', which is southwest of Roosevelt Park and north of Burdick Expressway along seven th and eight th Streets SE, and '''Terracita Vallejo''' which is actually outside of the city, west of the US eight three bypass but north of US two five two .

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are three six , five six seven people, one five , five two zero households, and nine , two six five families residing in the city. The population density is nine seven zero . four km ( two , five one three . one mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine three . one eight % White, one . three four % African American, two . seven six % Native American, zero . six two % Asian, zero . zero seven % Pacific Islander, zero . four nine % from other races, and one . five four % from two or more races. one . four seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one five , five two zero households out of which two eight . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four six . six % are married couples living together, one zero . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and four zero . three % are non-families. three two . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two seven and the average family size is two . nine zero .

In the city the population is spread out with two three . two % under the age of one eight , one three . three % from one eight to two four , two seven . four % from two five to four four , two zero . seven % from four five to six four , and one five . four % who are six five years of age or older. History
Minot came into existence in one eight eight six , when Jim Hill's Great Northern Railroad ended its push through the state for the winter, after having trouble constructing a trestle across Gassman Coulee. A tent town sprung up over night, as if by magic, thus the city came to be known as the Magic City.

The townsite was chosen by the railroad to be placed on the land of then-homesteader Erik Ramstad. Mr. Ramstad was convinced to relinquish his claim, and became one of the city leaders.

The town was named after Henry Davis Minot, a railroad investor and friend of Jim Hill. The city was incorporated on two eight June one eight eight seven .

Later, the Soo Line was building a line from Valley City up to Canada. While initially their plan was to cross the Souris River some distance from Minot, local interests convinced them otherwise; landholders along the new route gladly donated the right-of-way. They reached Minot in one eight nine three .

Minot was a typical western boom town in its early years, with its share of vice and lawlessness. During Prohibition the city became known as Little Chicago , as it was a central hub of Al Capone's liquor smuggling operations. Smugglers used a network of underground tunnels (some of which were previously built for heating or deliveries) to transport and conceal the illicit cargo. Some of the tunnels can still be accessed.

The one nine five zero s saw the construction of the Minot Air Force Base, an Air Defense Command Base that later became a Strategic Air Command bomber  Westbound trains arrive about nine : zero zero am local time. Eastbound trains arrive about nine : zero zero pm.

Highways
Three US Highways run through the city: US two , US five two , and US eight three .

US two runs East-West. It is a four-lane highway from Minot east to Grand Forks and largely two lanes from Minot west to Williston. In February two zero zero four it was announced that Highway two would be expanded to four lanes between Minot and Williston by two zero zero eight .

US eight three runs North-South. It is a four-lane highway from Minot south to Bismarck and north to Minot Air Force Base. Past the Air Force Base the road reduces to two lanes. US eight three crosses the Canadian border at Westhope, ND, where it becomes Manitoba Highway eight three .

US five two runs Southeast-Northwest. Southeast from Minot, US five two follows a slightly circuitous route to Jamestown, where it meets up with Interstate nine four . Northwest from Minot, US five two crosses the Canadian border at Portal, NDNorth Portal, SK, where it becomes Saskatchewan Highway three nine .

Minot has a Bypass for these routes around the south and west sides of the city.

Airport
Minot International Airport is served by Northwest Airlines three times daily, four times daily in peak periods. Airport officials are constantly looking for additional service, both from Northwest and other airlines, but such efforts have proved fruitless so far.

Within the city
Automobiles dominate intracity and local area transport. There is limited fixed-route city transit service (Minot City Transit) on weekdays, and flexible-route rural transit service (Souris Basin Transportation) on an occasional basis. Local transit services for the elderly and disabled (Minot Commission on Aging Transit) meet federal guidelines but have two four -hour advance notice requirements.

Pedestrianism is the exception rather than the rule; though decent enough downtown, the sidewalk network is poor in many areas of the city, though improving. Automobile drivers take the right of way at all but the best-marked crosswalks, and major points are often separated by relatively large distances and hill slopes. Skateboarding is illegal in streets and on sidewalks (though there is a skating area in Roosevelt Park), and rollerblading is generally disallowed by downtown landowners.

Media
Minot has several media outlets but little local content. KXMC-TV and the Minot Daily News, and to a lesser extent, KMOT-TV, are somewhat active in collecting local news, while KCJB-AM, and KHRT-AM have some local news content, but do not actively collect it.

Aside from some local news programming, virtually no mass media content originates from Minot. The local media tends to rebroadcast Bismarck television stations and republish network and wire reports rather than maintain a strong local focus.

Radio
Minot has fifteen radio stations ( one two FM, three AM), of which six (including two of the AM stations) are owned by Clear Channel Communications. Bottineau-based Programmers Broadcasting owns two FM stations. North Dakota Public Radio operates a full power FM station, a community broadcaster operates a low-power FM station, and the remainder are nonprofit Christian stations, of which only KHRT is based locally.

Clear Channel has been blamed for placing its stations on autopilot and resulting failure to warn area residents not to go outside when an ammonia tanker derailed on one eight January two zero zero two . One man died and dozens were injured attempting to flee the area while Clear Channel continued to play its satellite feeds.

Print
The principal local newspaper is the ''Minot Daily News'', which publishes seven days a week. Morgan Printing produces the ''Lunch Letter'' three days a week on a double-sided leaflet. There are also two weekly classified-ad publications, the ''Trading Post'', printed by the ''Daily News'', and ''The Finder'', printed by the ''Bismarck Tribune''. The ''Bismarck Tribune'' is available at several outlets in the city, as is ''The Fargo Forum'' and the ''Grand Forks Herald'', to a lesser extent.

Politics
The mayor of Minot is Curt Zimbelman, a banker. As mayor he chairs the one four -member City Council, but only casts a vote to break a tie. The day-to-day affairs of the city are handled by the City Manager, currently David Waind.

While the city's leadership has been trending towards the conservative, Minot's liberal factions have been active in recent years and have had somewhat more success than in other areas of the state.

Government
Minot uses the Council-manager system of government. Fourteen councilmen are elected from seven city wards to four-year terms. Elections are arranged such that one councilman from each ward is elected in every even-numbered year. The mayor of Minot is elected to a four-year term as well; the last mayoral election was in two zero zero two . All city offices are nonpartisan.

City elections are held in June in North Dakota, along with the state primary election.

Policy
Minot's civic realm includes a number of debates over taxes, fiscal management, and economic development policy.

Major issues include:

Economic development
:''Main article:'' MAGIC Fund

In recent years, economic development has become a significant issue in the city of Minot. The city created the publicly-financed MAGIC Fund in one nine nine two to provide financial incentives for businesses, but a series of debacles made the operations of the fund a significant issue in the two zero zero two city elections.

Northwest Area Water Supply (NAWS)
:''Main article:'' Northwest Area Water Supply
The Northwest Area Water Supply is slightly less controversial among residents of Minot and area, however, it has attracted the ire of the Canadian government because the plan calls for water to be pumped from Lake Sakakawea, then to Minot for treatment, and then on to large stretches of Northwest North Dakota.

Minot voters decided in one nine nine eight to levy a one % sales tax to go towards the construction of NAWS; this tax fund was found in court to have been illegally diverted towards economic development purposes. A lawsuit was filed against the city and it was ordered to return the misappropriated funds to the NAWS fund. By that time, the money had already been spent, and the city instead voted to issue a special assessment on city water bills to raise the funds.

NAWS may be a moot point as water levels in Lake Sakakawea continue to fall; it is possible that not enough water will be available for use when the project is complete.

Economy
The city's economy is more robust than other cities of its size due to its large service area; however, it is beset by significant problems with enterprise capital and wage standards. About three zero % of Minot residents work two or more jobs, and two-thirds of households earn less than the national median household income.

A Coldwell Banker Home Price Comparison Index listed Minot as the most affordable area of three four eight markets in the US, Canada, and Puerto Rico for homebuyers.

Culture
Minot's midwestern setting and attitudes sometimes hides its sizable and sometimes flamboyant arts community. Minot has an art museum, a symphony orchestra and a city band, several dance and theatre troupes, a youthpunk concert organization, the AMP, and much more; over four zero organizations claim membership in the Minot Area Council on the Arts, and even more exist.

The attitudes of the people themselves run the gamut. Many are of the opinion that they do not wish to remain in the area any longer than they have to; while others are taken by what the city is today, or what it could be in the future if they applied themselves.

Nearly four zero % of the residents of Minot are of Scandinavian ancestry, and every October since one nine seven seven , Minot has been the host to the Norsk H stfest, North America's largest Scandinavian-American festival.

Sister cities
Minot maintains a sister city relationship with the Norwegian city of Skien. Some note the irony in that Skien is the center the of county of Telemark, while Minot has become a center for telemarketing.

Minot is also a sister city of Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan. In connection with the Little Chicago civic tourism initiative, there are plans to brand the road between the cities (US five two SK three nine ) as the ''Rum Runner Highway'', to emphasize its role in prohibition-era smuggling.

Sites of interest
The '''Scandinavian Heritage Park''' is home to the Minot Visitor's Center, as well as buildings based on the Scandinavian style of architecture.

'''Pioneer Village''', on the state fairgrounds, is a collection of various buildings from the pioneer era.

The '''North Dakota State Fair Center''', located on the state fairgrounds, is home to many of the city's largest events, including: The North Dakota State Fair, the Norsk Hstfest, the Big One craft show, and the Great Tomato Festival. It also hosts rodeos, and college hockey games.

Roosevelt Park Zoo

Recreation
The Minot Park District operates one seven parks with various facilities; Corbett Field, home to American Legion, high school and college baseball; Optimist soccer complex; MAYSA ice arena; the Sertoma Complex which has eight softball fields; Souris Valley Golf Course, and an indoor tennis complex.

The city's largest parks are Roosevelt Park and Oak Park. Roosevelt Park Zoo is one of the top zoos in the region. Dogs are not allowed in any of the city parks. A  bark park for dogs opened in the summer of two zero zero five .

The North Dakota State Fair is held annually in Minot.

Education
The Minot Public School District has one zero elementary schools located in the city; Bel Air, Edison, Lewis and Clark, Lincoln, Longfellow, McKinley, Roosevelt, Perkett, Sunnyside, and Washington. Jefferson Elementary was closed in two zero zero three . There are also two elementary schools on the Minot Air Force Base, Dakota and North Plains.

There are two middle schools in the city, Jim Hill and Erik Ramstad. Memorial Middle School is located on the Minot Air Force Base.

There is one high school on two campuses: Minot High School - Central Campus (for grades nine and one zero ) and Minot High School - Magic City Campus (for grades one one and one two ).

Minot Public Schools also operates an adult learning center and Souris River Campus, an alternative high school.

For private schools, Minot has a Catholic school system with two elementary schools, St. Leo's and Little Flower, and a combined middle and high school, Bishop Ryan. There is also a protestant K- one two school, Our Redeemer's.

Minot is also home to Minot State University.

 '''Minot Air Force Base''' ('''Minot AFB''') is an base of the United States Air Force located in Ward County, North Dakota, one five km ( eight mi) north of the city of Minot. In the two zero zero zero census, the base was counted as a CDP with a total population of seven , five nine nine .

History
Minot Air Force Base official opened in one nine five seven . The base started out as an Air Defense Command Base.

A Semi Automatic Ground Environment (SAGE) facility was built and activated in June one nine six one . SAGE was housed in a huge, windowless blast-resistant concrete building with a pair of two seven five -ton computers. The computers processed air surveillance information and sent the data to Air Defense Command units. While the SAGE network operated until one nine eight three , the Minot AFB website says the Minot SAGE facility was deactivated after less than two years of operation, in May one nine six three . 

Strategic Air Command had units assigned to Minot AFB in one nine five eight for air refueling support. In late January one nine six zero , fighters moved onto the base. The scope of operations grew as the Air Force assigned bombers to Minot in one nine six one . Also in one nine six one , the Air Force selected the land around Minot for a new Minuteman I complex. 

Command of Minot AFB passed from Air Defense Command to Strategic Air Command as the base's mission changed. During the one nine seven zero s the missile sites in the area were converted to Minuteman IIIs; a model of the older Minuteman I stands at the main gate. 

In June one nine nine two , the newly formed Air Combat Command took over the Eighth Air Force, and through it, the five th Bomb Wing and host command of the Minot Air Force Base.

Units
Minot Air Force Base is home to two major units:

The five th Bomb Wing
The five th Bomb Wing is the host unit at Minot AFB; its commander is the base commander, and the unit is responsible for all base services, such as housing, the library, the Officer's Club, etc. The primary mission of the five th Bomb Wing is to maintain and operate B- five two H Stratofortress bombers. Minot AFB is one of two bases with B- five two s; and the other is Barksdale Air Force Base in Louisiana.

The nine one st Space Wing
The nine one st Space Wing is responsible for maintaining the Minuteman III nuclear missiles located in three main fields across North Dakota. Operational squadrons attached to the nine one st SW are the seven four zero th Missile Squadron ( Vulgar Vultures ), seven four one st Missile Squadron ( Gravelhaulers ), and the seven four two nd Missile Squadron ( Wolf Pack ) The nine one st Security Police Group, attached to the nine one st SW, provide security to the surrounding missile fields.

 '''Grenora''' is a city located in Williams County, North Dakota. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two zero two .

The city's motto is, Friendliness lives here  you'll be a stranger only once. The city is home to a senior citizen's center, a golf club, bowling alley, restaurant, apartment buildings and community built low-income housing. There are also three churches, the St. Olaf Lutheran Church, St. Boniface Catholic Church, and a United Methodist Church. The town possesses only one bar.

The surrounding area is home to exceptional small game, pronghorn antelope, and deer hunting opportunities. Available in the nearby Missouri River are paddlefish, a prehistoric fish which can weigh more than one two zero pounds, and this is one of the only places the fish can be found on the North American continent. Grenora is located three zero miles ( five zero kilometers) from the Canadian border and only four miles ( six km) from North Dakota's border with Montana.

 Attractions 
Grenora is home to the Writing Rock State Historical Site. The Assiniboine, Lakota, and Plains Chippewa Indian tribes often returned to the Spirit Rock, or Hoi-waukon, located on a hilly prairie just outside of Grenora. The rock served to mark a spot where Native Americans felt they could foretell the future. The two granite rocks at this site are covered with petroglyphs presumably carved by ancient Plains Indians.

 '''Williston''' is a city in Williams County, North Dakota. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one two , five one two . It is the county seat of Williams County.

The local paper is the ''Williston Herald''. Sloulin Field International Airport serves the city. Williston State College is located here.

Geography
Location of Williston, North Dakota

Williston is located at four eight  nine ' two three  North, one zero three  three seven ' four one  West ( four eight . one five six four seven seven , - one zero three . six two eight zero six four ).

It is near the confluence of the Yellowstone River and the Missouri River, at the upper end of the Lake Sakakawea reservoir.

Notable people from Williston
Phil Jackson, basketball player and coach, was born in Montana, but spent the later part of his childhood, including his teenage years, in Williston.

Virgil Hill, a silver medalist in boxing at the one nine eight four Olympics and a four-time world champion boxer, spent his last year of high school at Williston High School.

 History 
West Union started as an Amish settlement. There are still many Amish communities in the area.

Nearby Seaman, Ohio is the birthplace of the sport of crockey. The first crockey championship was held in one nine nine seven in West Union.

West Union is a dry town.  No sales of alcoholic beverages are permitted, though they are available at nearby Manchester, Ohio, as well as other towns in and around Adams County.

 Downtown Lima.

'''Lima''' LIE-muh is a city in Allen County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of four zero , zero eight one . It is the county seat of Allen County. Lima is located in northwestern Ohio, north of Dayton along Interstate seven five ; it was founded in one eight three one .

''Note that the city's name is pronounced differently from that of Lima, Peru, which is pronounced LEE muh. ''
Lima, Ohio city flag.

Industry
At various times, Lima has manufactured railroad equipment, tanks, automotive engines, buses, various machinery, and electrical goods. A limestone quarry is nearby. The city once was an oil pipeline center and today has an oil refinery and a petrochemical plant. The city serves as a regional health care center. Its largest employers include St. Rita's Medical Center, which has experienced rapid growth in recent years.

Lima, Ohio, was the nations most affordable housing market, according to the revised National Association of Home BuildersWells Fargo Housing Opportunity Index (HOI) for the third quarter of two zero zero four .


 Geography 
Location of Lima, Ohio

Lima is located at four zero  four four ' two seven  North, eight four  six ' five four  West ( four zero . seven four zero seven zero zero , - eight four . one one four nine nine seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three three . four km ( one two . nine mi ).  three three . one km ( one two . eight mi ) of it is land and zero . three km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . seven eight % water.

The Ottawa River flows through the city. Locals sometimes refer to the river as Hawg Creek. This resembles a traditional local name used dating back to the Hog Creek Shawnee community that existed between Lima and present Ada, prior to the Shawnee removal of one eight three one . This removal made possible the official founding of Lima as a formal town in that year.

Allen County courthouse, downtown.

Business area in Lima.
Cultural relevance
The town was named after Lima, Peru, the source of the quinine bark used for the treatment of swamp fever or malaria in pioneer days prior to the draining of the Great Black Swamp.

Lima has sometimes been used as an example of a typical Midwestern American town. The town's opera house was a prominent spot on the Vaudeville circuit of the one nine two zero s and one nine three zero s. Reputedly, Lima audiences were so unreceptive to the humor that Lima became an inside joke among performers for an unpleasant or unproductive engagement. The joke first prize, one week in... second prize, two weeks in... was originally about Lima. Comedian Lenny Bruce had a routine called Lima, Ohio in his act, based on a booking he had there as a young comedian. He used Lima as a metaphor for small towns across America and his experiences in them.

A documentary titled ''Lost in Middle America (and What Happened Next)'' (PBS) was made about Lima, Ohio (making the title into the acronym LIMA ). The documentary attempted to reflect the crisis known as the Rust Belt by showing how Lima's industries fell one by one and how the crisis was a typical experience of small towns across the United States.

 '''Ashland''' is a city located in Ashland County, Ohio. It was formerly known as Uniontown, but because of another city named Uniontown in Ohio, the city was compelled to adopt a new name. Ashland was recommended as a name by congressman Henry Clay, after the name of his ranch in Kentucky. Later, Henry Clay High School was considered as a name for what is now known as Ashland High School. In the mid- one eight zero zero 's, Ashland pioneers traveled to Oregon and named the settlement there Ashland, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two one , two four nine . It is the county seat of Ashland County, and the center of the Ashland Micropolitan Statistical Area (as defined by the United States Census Bureau in two zero zero three ). It was incorporated in one nine one six . The city is governed by a mayor, William E. Strine, and a five-person city council.

 Location of Hayesville, Ohio
'''Hayesville''' is a village located in Ashland County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of three four eight .

 History 
The first settlers came to the Hayesville area in one eight one seven . A post office for the settlers was established in one eight two seven at Hayes Cross Roads. Hayesville was laid out in Vermillion Township and plots were recorded in Mansfield, Ohio on October two six , one eight three zero . Hayes Cross Roads was then renamed Hayesville. The village of Hayesville was incorporated in one eight four nine .

Source: ''Early History of Hayesville and Vermillion Township'' by Virginia Patterson (printed one nine seven five ).

 Geography 
Hayesville is located at four zero  four six ' two six  North, eight two  one five ' four two  West ( four zero . seven seven three eight five three , - eight two . two six one seven five three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one . nine km ( zero . seven mi ).  one . nine km ( zero . seven mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are three four eight people, one three six households, and nine five families residing in the village. The population density is one eight one . six km ( four six eight . nine mi ). There are one four one housing units at an average density of seven three . six km ( one nine zero . zero mi ). The racial makeup of the village is nine eight . two eight % White, one . one five % African American, zero . five seven % Native American, zero . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . zero zero % from other races, and zero . zero zero % from two or more races.  zero . zero zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one three six households out of which two seven . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six three . two % are married couples living together, four . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and three zero . one % are non-families. two seven . two % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four zero and the average family size is two . nine one .

In the village the population is spread out with two zero . one % under the age of one eight , seven . two % from one eight to two four , two five . three % from two five to four four , two nine . six % from four five to six four , and one seven . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four four years. For every one zero zero females there are nine five . five males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine one . seven males.

The median income for a household in the village is $ four one , four two nine , and the median income for a family is $ five two , five zero zero . Males have a median income of $ three four , three seven five versus $ two six , zero four two for females.  Timeline of the spread of the Christian Gospel

 '''c. three zero ''' - Pentecost and birth of the Christian church
 '''c. three four ''' - Church scattered by persecution; Philip, a deacon, baptizes a convert, an Ethiopian who had converted to Judaism in Gaza.

 ''' four two ''' - Mark goes to Egypt
 '''c. four eight ''' - Paul (formerly known as Saul of Tarsus) begins his first missionary journey to modern-day Turkey.

 '''c. five two ''' - Apostle Thomas arrives in India and founds church that subsequently becomes Indian Orthodox Church (and its various descendants).

The text, in both Chinese characters and Persian script, begins with the words, Let us praise the Lord that the Christian faith has been popular in China. The inscription had been written by Ching Ching (Adam), a Syrian monk in AD seven eight one . It told of the arrival of a missionary, A-lo-pen (Abraham), in AD six two five . He had arrived bearing the sacred books, braving difficulties and dangers. Christianity was described as The Illustrious Religion, and the text included a doctrinal overview and a list of Christian worship practices and ethics. It also mentioned a succession of Emperors who were greatly supportive of the Church, and the names of six seven priests in both Persian and Chinese.
