 ''' one six eight zero ''' - The Pueblo Revolt begins in New Mexico with the killing of twenty-one Franciscan missionaries 
 ''' one six eight one ''' - After arriving in New Spain, Italian Jesuit Eusebio Kino soon becomes what someone has described as the most picturesque missionary pioneer of all North America. A bundle of evangelistic zeal, Kino was also an explorer, astronomer, cartographer, mission builder, ranchman, cattle king, and defender of the frontier 
 ''' one six eight two ''' - one three missionaries go to remote cities in East Siberia 
 ''' one six eight three ''' - Missionary Louis Hennepin returns to France after exploring Minnesota and being held captive by the Dakota to write the first book about Minnesota, Description de la Louisiane 
 ''' one six eight four ''' - Louis XIV sends Jesuit missionaries to China bearing gifts from the collections of the Louvre and of the Versailles palace 
 ''' one six eight five ''' - Consecration of first Catholic bishop of Chinese origin 
 ''' one six eight six ''' - Russian Orthodox monks arrive in China as missionaries 
 ''' one six eight seven ''' - French activity begins in what is now Cte d'Ivoire when missionaries land at Assini 
 ''' one six eight eight ''' - New Testament translated into Malay (the first Bible translation into a language of southeast Asia) 
 ''' one six eight nine ''' - Calusa Indian chief from what is the state of Florida visits Cuba requesting missionaries 
 ''' one six nine zero ''' - First Franciscan missionaries arrive in Texas 
 ''' one six nine one ''' - Christian Faith Society for the West Indies organized 
 ''' one six nine two ''' - Chinese Emperor Kang Xi permits the Jesuits to freely preach the Christian message freely, converting whom they wish 
 ''' one six nine three ''' - Jesuit missionary John de Britto is publicly beheaded in India 
 ''' one six nine four ''' - Missionary and explorer Eusebio Francisco Kino becomes the first European to enter the Tucson basin in what is now Arizona and create a lasting settlement 
 ''' one six nine five ''' - China's first Russian Orthodox church building is consecrated 
 ''' one six nine six ''' - Jesuit missionary Francois Pinet founds the Mission of the Guardian Angel near what is today Chicago, Illinois. The mission was abandoned in one seven zero zero when missionary efforts seemed fruitless 
 ''' one six nine seven ''' - Thomas Bray, an English preacher who made several missionary trips to America, organizes a society for the propagation of the Gospel in the English Colonies 
 ''' one six nine eight ''' - Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge organized by Anglicans
 ''' one six nine nine ''' - Priests of the Seminary of Foreigh Missions establish a mission among the Tamoroa Indians at Cahokia in what is not the state of Illinois

 one seven zero zero to one seven nine nine 
 ''' one seven zero zero ''' - After a Swedish missionary's sermon to an Indian tribe in Pennsylvania, one Native American posed such searching questions that the episode was reported in a history of the Swedish church in America printed in one seven three one . The interchange later inspired Benjamin Franklin's Remarks Concerning the Savages of North America ( one seven eight four ), in which Franklin has an Indian reply to a sermon on original sin: What you have told us ... is all very good. It is indeed bad to eat apples. It is better to make them all into cyder. 
 ''' one seven zero one ''' - Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts
 ''' one seven zero two ''' - George Keith, Scotch Quaker, arrives in America as a missionary of the newly-organized Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts 
 ''' one seven zero three ''' - The Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts expands its work to the West Indies 
 ''' one seven zero four ''' - French missionary priests arrive to evangelize the Chetimaches Indians living along the Mississippi River in what is now the state of Louisiana 
 ''' one seven zero five ''' - Danish-Halle mission to India begins with Bartholomew Ziegenbalg and Henry Plutschau
 ''' one seven zero six ''' - Emperor Susenyos of Ethiopia becomes Catholic 
 ''' one seven zero seven ''' - Maillard de Tournon makes public, in Nanjing, the Vatican decisions on rites, including the stipulations against the veneration of ancestors and of Confucius. Clergy who do not conform are to be excommunicated. Emperor Kangxi is furious. To him, the Pope is a foreign sovereign who has no right to interfere in Chinese affairs; Italian Capuchin missionaries reach Kathmandu in Nepal 
 ''' one seven zero eight ''' - Jesuit missionary Giovanni Battista Sidotti is arrested in Japan. He is taken to Edo to be interrogated by Arai Kakuseki 
 ''' one seven zero nine ''' - Experience Mayhew, missionary to the Martha's Vineyard Indians, translates the Psalms and the Gospel of John into the Massachusett language. It will be a work considered second only to John Eliot's Indian Bible in terms of significant Indian-language translations in colonial New England 
 ''' one seven one zero ''' - German Bible Society founded by Count Canstein 
 ''' one seven one one ''' - Jesuit Eusebio Kino, missionary explorer in southern Arizona and northern Sonora, dies suddenly in northern Mexico. Kino, who has been called the cowboy missionary, had fought against the exploitation of Indians in Mexican silver mines. 
 ''' one seven one two ''' - Using a press sent by The Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, the Tranquebar Mission in India begins printing books in Portuguese 
 ''' one seven one three ''' - Jesuit Ippolito Desideri goes to Tibet as a missionary 
 ''' one seven one four ''' - New Testament translated into Tamil (India); a missionary training college is established in Copenhagen 
 ''' one seven one five ''' - Orthodox missionary outreach is renewed in Manchuria and Northern China 
 ''' one seven one six ''' - The establishment of the mission whose building became known as the Alamo (in modern day San Antonio, Texas) is authorized by the viceroy of Mexico. It was to be an educational center for Native Americans who converted to Christianity. 
 ''' one seven one seven ''' - Chen Mao writes to the Chinese Emperor about his concerns over Catholic missionaries and Western traders. He urgently requested an all-out prohibition of Catholic missionaries in the Qing provinces. 
 ''' one seven one eight ''' - Bartholomaeus Ziegenbalg constructs a church building in India that is still in use today 
 ''' one seven one nine ''' - Isaac Watts writes missionary hymn Jesus Shall Reign Where'er the Sun 
 ''' one seven two zero ''' - Missionary Johann Ernst Gruendler dies in India. He had arrived there in one seven zero nine with the sponsorship of the Danish Mission Society 
 ''' one seven two one ''' - Mission San Juan Bautista Malibat in Baja California is abandoned due to the hostility of the Cochimies Indians, as well as to the decimation of the local population by epidemics and a water shortage 
 ''' one seven two two ''' - Hans Egede goes to Greenland
 ''' one seven two three ''' - Robert Millar publishes ''A History of the Propagation of Christianity and the Overthrow of Paganism''
 ''' one seven two four ''' - The Yongzheng emperor bans missionary activities outside the Beijing area 
 ''' one seven two five ''' - Knud Leem arrives as a missionary to the Sami people of Finnmark (Norwegian Arctic) 
 ''' one seven two six ''' - John Wright, a Quaker missionary to the Native Americans, settles in southeastern Pennsylvania 
 ''' one seven two eight ''' - Institutum Judaicum founded in Halle by Francke as first Protestant mission center for Jewish evangelism 
 ''' one seven two nine ''' - Roman Catholic missionary Du Poisson becomes the first victim in the Natchez massacre. On his way to New Orleans, he had been asked to stop and say Mass at the Natchez post. He was killed in front of the altar 
 ''' one seven three zero ''' - Lombard, French missionary, founds a Christian village with over six zero zero Indians at the mouth of Kuru river in French Guiana. A Jesuit, Lombard has been called the most successful of all missionaries in converting the Indians of French Guiana 
 ''' one seven three one ''' - A missionary movement is born when Count Nicholas Ludwig von Zinzendorf attends the coronation of King Christian VI of Denmark. For the first time, he met people from outside of Europe who had never heard the name of Christ. By the following year, the movement with which he was associated, the Moravians, would launch missionary outreach in the Caribbean. 
 ''' one seven three two ''' - Alphonsus Liguori founds the Roman Catholic order known as the Redemptorist Fathers with the purpose of doing missionary work among rural people 
 ''' one seven three three ''' - Moravians go to Greenland
 ''' one seven three four ''' - A missionary convinces a Groton, Connecticut church to lend its building to the Mashantucket Pequot Indians for worship services. 
 ''' one seven three five ''' - John Wesley goes to Indians in Georgia as missionary with the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel
 ''' one seven three six ''' - Anti-Christian edicts in China; Moravian missionaries at work among Samoyeds of Archangelsk
 ''' one seven three seven ''' - Rev. Pugh, a missionary in Pennsylvania with The Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts, writes home to London to say that he had begun ministering to blacks. He noted that the slaves' masters were prejudiced against them becoming Christian. 
 ''' one seven three eight ''' - Moravian missionary Georg Schmidt settles in Baviaan Kloof (Kloof of the Baboons) in the Riviersonderend Valley of South Africa. He begins working with the Khoi people, who were practically on the threshold of extinction. 
 ''' one seven three nine ''' - The first missionary to the Mahican (Mohegan) Indians, John Sergeant, builds a home in Stockbridge, Massachusetts that is today a museum. 
 ''' one seven four zero ''' - Moravian David Zeisberger starts work among Creek Indians of Georgia 
 ''' one seven four one ''' - Dutch missionaries start building Christ Church building in Malacca, Malaysia. It will take one two years to complete. 
 ''' one seven four two ''' - Moravian Leader Count Zinzendorf visits Shekomeko, New York and baptizes six Indians 
 ''' one seven four three ''' - David Brainerd starts ministry to North American Indians
 ''' one seven four four ''' - Thomas Thompson resigns his position as dean at Cambridge University to become a missionary. He was sent by the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts to New Jersey. Taking a special interest in the slave population there, he would later request to begin mission work in Africa. In one seven five one Thompson became the first S.P.G. missionary to the Gold Coast (modern-day Ghana). 
 ''' one seven four five ''' - One day in late December, David Brainerd, missionary to Native American Indians, writes in his journal: After public worship was over, I went to my house, proposing to preach again after a short season of intermission. But they soon came in one after another; with tears in their eyes, to know, what they should do to be saved. . . . It was an amazing season of power among them, and seemed as if God had bowed the heavens and come down ... and that God was about to convert the whole world. 
 ''' one seven four six ''' - From Boston, a call is issued to the Christians of the New World to enter into a seven-year Concert of Prayer for missionary work
 ''' one seven four seven ''' - Jonathan Edwards appeals for prayer for world missions; birth of Thomas Coke, the Father of Methodist Missions 
 ''' one seven four eight ''' - Roman Catholic Petrus Sanz and the four other missionaries are executed, together with one four Chinese Christians. Prior to his death, Sanz reportedly converted some of his prison guards to Christianity. 
 ''' one seven four nine ''' - Spanish Franciscan priest Junipero Serra ( one seven one three - one seven eight four ) arrives in Mexico as a missionary. In one seven six seven he would go north to what is now California, zealously converting native Americans. 
 ''' one seven five zero ''' - Jonathan Edwards, preacher of the First Great Awakening, having been banished from his church at Northampton, Massachusetts goes as a missionary to the nearby Housatonic Indians. Christian Frederic Schwartz goes to India with Danish-Halle Mission
 ''' one seven five one ''' - Samuel Cooke arrives in New Jersey as a missionary for the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts 
 ''' one seven five two ''' - Thomas Thompson, first Anglican missionary to Africa, arrives in the Gold Coast (now Ghana) 
 ''' one seven five three ''' - Searchers in Labrador looking for Moravian Johann Christian Erhardt finds the body of one of his traveling companions. The disappearance a few months earlier of Erhardt and six companions had led to temporary abandonment of Moravian missionary initiatives in Labrador. 
 ''' one seven five four ''' - Moravian John Ettwein arrives in America from Germany in as a missionary. Preaching to Native American tribes and establishing missions, he will travel as far south as Georgia. Eventually Ettwein will become bishop and head of the Moravian church in the United States. 
 ''' one seven five five ''' - The Mahican Indian settlement at Gnadenhutten, Pa. is attacked and destroyed. Moravian missionary Johann Jacob Schmick who pastors a group of Indian converts will remain with the Mahicans through exile and captivity, though facing almost constant threats from white neighbors. Schmick will join his Indian congregation as they seek refuge in Bethlehem, follow them as captives to Philadelphia, and remain with them after they settle in Wyalusing (also called Friedenshutten), Pennsylvania. 
 ''' one seven five six ''' - Civil unrest forces Gideon Halley away from his missionary work among the Six Nations on the Susquehanna where he has been working for four years under the supervision of Jonathan Edwards with an appointment from the Society for Propagating the Gospel among the Indians. 
 ''' one seven five seven ''' - Lutherans reportedly begin ministering to Blacks in the Caribbean 
 ''' one seven five eight ''' - John Wesley baptizes two African-American slaves thus breaking the skin color barrier for Methodist societies 
 ''' one seven five nine ''' - Native American Samson Occom, direct descendant of the great Mohegan chief Uncas, is ordained by the Presbyterians. Despite poor eyesight, Occom became the first American Indian to publish works in English. These included sermons, hymns and a short autobiography. 
 ''' one seven six zero ''' - Adam Voelker and Christian Butler arrive in Tranquebar as the first Moravian missionaries to India 
 ''' one seven six one ''' - The first Moravian missionary in Ohio, Frederick Post, settles on the north side of the Muskingum in what is now Bethlehem township 
 ''' one seven six two ''' - Moravian Missionary John Heckewelder confers with Koquethagacton, White Eyes at the mouth of the Beaver River in Pennsylvania 
 ''' one seven six three ''' - The Presbyterian Synod of New York orders that a collection for missions be taken. In one seven six seven the Synod will ask that this collection be done annually. 
 ''' one seven six four ''' - The Moravians make a decision to expand and begin publicizing their missionary activity, particular in the British colonies; Moravian Jens Haven makes the fisrt of three exploratory missionary journeys to Greenland 
 ''' one seven six five ''' - Suriname Governor General Crommelin convinces three Moravian missionaries to work near the head waters of the Gran Rio. They settle among the Saramacca Indians near the Senthea Creek in Granman Abini's village where they are received with mixed feelings. 
 ''' one seven six six ''' - Philip Quaque, a Fetu youth who spent twelve years studying in England, returns to Africa. Supported as a missionary by the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts, Quaque is first non-European ordained priest in the Church of England 
 ''' one seven six seven ''' - Spain expels the Jesuits from Spanish colonies in the New World 
 ''' one seven six eight ''' - Five United Brethen missionaries from Germany, invited by the Danish Guinea Company, arrive in the Gold Coast (now Ghana), to teach in the Cape Coast Castle schools 
 ''' one seven six nine ''' - Father Junpero Serra founds Mission San Diego de Alcal, first of the two one Alta California missions.
 ''' one seven seven zero ''' - John Marrant, a free black from New York City, begins ministering cross-culturally, preaching to the American Indians. By one seven seven five he had carried the gospel to the Cherokee, Creek, Catawar, and Housaw Indians. 
 ''' one seven seven one ''' - Francis Asbury arrives in America; David Avery is ordained as missionary to the Oneida Indians 
 ''' one seven seven two ''' - After visiting Scilly Cove (now called Winterton) in Newfoundland, Cananda, missionary James Balfour describes it as a most Barbarous Lawless Place 
 ''' one seven seven three ''' - Pope Clement XIV dissolves the Jesuit Order; two Dominican missionaries beheaded in Vietnam 
 ''' one seven seven four ''' - Moravian missionaries Christoph Brasen and Gottfried Lehmann drown when their sloop sinks in a storm off Greenland 
 ''' one seven seven five ''' - John Crook is sent by Liverpool Methodists to the Isle of Man 
 ''' one seven seven six ''' - Cyril Vasilyevich Suchanov builds first church among Tungus people of Dauria (Siberia); The first baptism of an Eskimo by a Lutheran pastor takes place in Labrador. 
 ''' one seven seven seven ''' - Portuguese missionaries build a church at Hashnabad, Bangladesh 
 ''' one seven seven eight ''' - Theodore Sladich is martyred while doing missionary work to counter Islamic influence in the western Balkans 
 ''' one seven seven nine ''' - Charles Simeon is converted while a student at King's College, Cambridge. Twenty years later he helped found what became the Church Missionary Society. 
 ''' one seven eight zero ''' - August Gottlieb Spangenberg writes An Account of the Manner in Which the Protestant Church of the Unitas Fratrum, or United Brethren, Preach the Gospel, and Carry On Their Missions Among the Heathen. Originally written in German, the book will be translated into English in one seven eight eight . 
 ''' one seven eight one ''' - In the midst of the American Revolutionary War, the British so feared Moravian missionary David Zeisberger and his influence among the Delaware and other Native American Indians that they arrested him and his assistant, John Heckewelder, charging them with treason, 
 ''' one seven eight two ''' - Freed slave George Lisle goes to Jamaica as missionary
 ''' one seven eight three ''' - Moses Baker and George Gibbions, both former slaves, leave the U.S. to become missionaries in the West Indies 
 ''' one seven eight four ''' - Methodist Thomas Coke submits his Plan for the Society for the Establishment of Missions Among the Heathen. Methodist missions among the 'heathen' will begin in one seven eight six when Coke, destined for Nova Scotia, is driven off course by a storm and lands at Antigua in the British West Indies. 
 ''' one seven eight five ''' - Joseph White's sermon titled On the Duty of Attempting the Propagation of the Gospel among our Mahometan and Gentoo Subjects in India is published in the second edition of his book Sermons Containing a View of Christianity and Mahometanism, in their History, their Evidence, and their Effects. The sermon was first preached at the University of Oxford. 
 ''' one seven eight six ''' - John Marrant, a free black from New York City, preaches to a great number of Indians and white people at Green's Harbor, Newfoundland. Marrant's cross-cultural ministry led him to take the Christian gospel to the Cherokee, Creek, Catawar, and Housaw Indians. 
 ''' one seven eight seven ''' - William Carey is ordained in England by the Particular Baptists in one seven eight seven soon begins to urge that worldwide missions be undertaken 
 ''' one seven eight eight ''' - Dutch missionaries begin preaching the Gospel among fishermen in Bangladesh 
 ''' one seven eight nine ''' - The most missionary of Roman Catholic orders, the Jesuits, establish Georgetown University in present-day Washington, D.C., as the first US Catholic college 
 ''' one seven nine zero ''' - Prince Williams, a freed slave from South Carolina, goes to Nassau, Bahamas, where he will start Bethel Meeting House 
 ''' one seven nine one ''' - One hundred and twenty Korean Christians are tortured and killed for their faith. It began when Paul Yun Ji-Chung, a noble who had become a Christian, decided not to bury his mother according to traditional Confucian custom. When this was reported to the authorities, a ferocious persecution of Christians began. 
 ''' one seven nine two ''' - William Carey writes Enquiry into the Obligations of Christians to use means for the conversion of the heathen and forms the Baptist Missionary Society to support him in establishing missionary work in India.
 ''' one seven nine three ''' - Frontier missionary Stephen Badin became the first Catholic priest ordained in the United States 
 ''' one seven nine four ''' - Eight Orthodox Russian monks arrive in Alaska as missionaries 
 ''' one seven nine five ''' - The London Missionary Society is formed to send missionaries to Tahiti 
 ''' one seven nine six ''' - Scottish and Glasgow Missionary Societies established; In India, Johann Philipp Fabricius finishes translating entire Bible into Tamil 
 ''' one seven nine seven ''' - Netherlands Missionary Society formed; The Duff, carrying three seven lay and pastoral missionaries, drops anchor in Tahiti; Twenty-one-year-old William Pascoe Crook of the London Missionary Society is left alone at Vaitahu on the Pacific island of Tahuata. The first missionary to visit Hiva, he was not well received by the islanders. 
 ''' one seven nine eight ''' - The Missionary Society of Connecticut is organized by the Presbyterians. Its missionaries worked within the U.S., evangelizing both European settlers and Native Americans. 
 ''' one seven nine nine ''' - The Church Missionary Society (Church of England) is formed; John Vanderkemp, Dutch physician goes to Cape Colony, Africa; Religious Tract Society organized

 one eight zero zero to one eight nine nine 

 ''' one eight zero zero ''' - New York Missionary Society formed 
 ''' one eight zero one ''' - John Theodosius Van Der Kemp moves to Graaff Reinet to minister to the Khoikhoi (Hottentots) people. Earlier he had helped found the Netherlands Missionary Society. In one seven nine eight , he had gone to South Africa to work as a missionary among the Xhosa. 
 ''' one eight zero two ''' - Henry Martyn hears Charles Simeon speak of William Carey's work in India and resolves to become a missionary himself. He will sail for India in one eight zero five 
 ''' one eight zero three ''' - The Massachusetts Baptist Missionary Society votes to publish a missionary magazine now known as The American Baptist, the oldest surviving religious magazine in the U.S. 
 ''' one eight zero four ''' - British and Foreign Bible Society formed; Church Missionary Society enters Sierra Leone 
 ''' one eight zero five ''' - The first Christian missionaries arrive in Namibia, brothers Abraham and Christian Albrecht from the London Missionary Society 
 ''' one eight zero six ''' - Haystack prayer meeting at Williams College; Henry Martyn lands in Calcutta; Andover Seminary founded as a missionary training center; Protestant missionary work begins in earnest across southern Africa 
 ''' one eight zero seven ''' - First Protestant missionary to China, Robert Morrison, begins work in Canton
 ''' one eight zero eight ''' - London Society for Promoting Christianity Among the Jews founded 
 ''' one eight zero nine ''' - National Bible Society of Scotland organized
 ''' one eight one zero ''' - The American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions is formed.
 ''' one eight one one ''' - English Wesleyans enter Sierra Leone
 ''' one eight one two ''' - First American foreign missionary, Adoniram Judson, arrives in Serampore and soon goes to Burma
 ''' one eight one three ''' - The Methodists form the Wesleyan Missionary Society.
 ''' one eight one four ''' - First recorded baptism of a Chinese convert, Cai Gao; American Baptist Foreign Mission Society formed; Netherlands Bible Society founded; four Native Americans from beyond the Rocky Mountains come east to St. Louis seeking information on the palefaces' religion ; first missionaries arrive in New Zealand led by Samuel Marsden 
 ''' one eight one five ''' - American Board of Commissioners open work on Ceylon; Basel Missionary Society organized; Richmond African Missionary Society founded.
 ''' one eight one six ''' - Robert Moffat arrives in Africa; American Bible Society founded
 ''' one eight one seven ''' - James Thompson begins distributing Bibles throughout Latin America
 ''' one eight one eight ''' - Missionary work begins in Madagascar with the reluctant approval of the king 
 ''' one eight one nine ''' - John Scudder, the missionary physician, joins the Ceylon Mission; Wesleyan Methodists start work in Madras, India; Reginald Heber writes words to missionary classic From Greenland's Icy Mountains 
 ''' one eight two zero ''' - Hiram Bingham goes to Hawaii (Sandwich Islands)
 ''' one eight two one ''' - African-American Lott Carey, a Baptist missionary, sails with two eight colleagues from Norfolk, VA to Sierra Leone; Frotestant Episcopal Church mission board established.
 ''' one eight two two ''' - Paris Evangelical Missionary Society established
 ''' one eight two three ''' - Scottish Missionary Society workers arrive in Bombay, India; Liang Fa, first Chinese Protestant evangelist, is ordained by Robert Morrison; Colonial and Continental Church Society formed; African American Betsy Stockton is sent by the American Board of Missions to Hawaii. She thus becomes the first single woman missionary in the history of modern missions. 
 ''' one eight two four ''' - Berlin Mission Society formed 
 ''' one eight two five ''' - George Boardman goes to Burma
 ''' one eight two six ''' - American Bible Society sends first shipment of Bibles to Mexico
 ''' one eight two seven ''' - Missionary Lancelot Threlkeld reports in The Monitor that he was advancing rapidly in his efforts to disseminate the Scriptures among Australian aborigines of the Hunter and Shoalhaven Rivers. 
 ''' one eight two eight ''' - Basel Mission begins work at Christiansborg, Accra (Africa); Karl F. A. Gutzlaff of the Netherlands Missionary Society lands in Bangkok, Thailand; Rhenish Missionary Association formed
 ''' one eight two nine ''' - George Muller, a native of Prussia, goes to England as a missionary to the Jews 
 ''' one eight three zero ''' - Church of Scotland missionary Alexander Duff arrives in Calcutta; William Swan, missionary to Siberia, writes Letters on Missions, the first Protestant attempt at a comprehensive treatment of the theory and practice of missions; Baptism of Taufa'ahau Tupou, King of Tonga, by a western missionary
 ''' one eight three one ''' - American Congregational missionaries arrive in Thailand, withdrawing in one eight four nine without a single convert; Presbyterian Church mission board established; Trinitarian Bible Society formed
 ''' one eight three two ''' - Teava, former cannibal and pioneer Pacific Islander missionary, is commissioned by John Wiliams to work on the Samoan island of Manono 
 ''' one eight three three ''' - Baptist work in Thailand begins with John Taylor Jones; American Methodist missionary Melville Box arrives in Liberia; Free-Will Baptist Foreign Missionary Socity begins work in India
 ''' one eight three four ''' - American Presbyterian Mission opens work in India in the Punjab
 ''' one eight three five ''' - Rhenish Missionary Society begins work among the Dayaks on Borneo (Indonesia); Bishop Daniel Wilson calls India's caste system a cancer. 
 ''' one eight three six ''' - Plymouth Brethren begin work in Madras, India; George Mller begins his work with orphans in Bristol, England;Gossner Mission formed; Leipzig Mission Society established; Colonial Missionary Society formed; The Providence Missionary Baptist District Association is formed, one of at least six national organizations among African American Baptists whose sole objective was missionary work in Africa. 
 ''' one eight three seven ''' - Evangelical Lutheran Church mission board established; First translation of Bible into Japanese (actual translation work done in Singapore) 
 ''' one eight three eight ''' - Church of Scotland Mission of Inquiry to the Jews; four Scottish ministers including Robert Murray M'Cheyne and Andrew Bonar journey to Palestine.
 ''' one eight three nine ''' - Entire Bible is published in language of Tahiti; three French missionaries martyred in Korea; English Protestant missionaries murdered on Erromango (Vanuatu, South Pacific) 
 ''' one eight four zero ''' - David Livingstone is in present-day Malawi (Africa) with the London Missionary Society; American Presbyterians enter Thailand and labor for one eight years before seeing their first Thai convert; Irish Presbyterian Missionary Society formed; Welsh Calvinistic Methodist Missionary Society founded

 ''' one eight four one ''' - Edinburgh Medical Missionary Society formed; Welsh Methodists begin working among the Khasi people of India 
 ''' one eight four two ''' - Gossner Mission Society begun in Berlin 
 ''' one eight four three ''' - Baptist John Taylor Jones translates New Testament into Siamese; British Society for the Propagation of the Gospel among the Jews formed 
 ''' one eight four four ''' - Swiss Johann Krapf begins work on Zanzibar; first Young Men's Christian Association (YMCA) formed by George Williams; George Smith and Thomas McClatchie sail for China as the first two CMS missionaries to that country 
 ''' one eight four five ''' - Southern Baptist Convention mission organization founded 
 ''' one eight four six ''' - The London Missionary Society establishes work on Niue, a South Pacific island which westerners had named the savage island. 
 ''' one eight four seven ''' - Presbyterian William Burns goes to China, translates Pilgrim's Progress into Chinese; Moses White sails to China as a Methodist medical missionary 
 ''' one eight four eight ''' - Charles Forman goes to the Punjab; German missionaries Johannes Rebmann and Ludwig Krapf arrive at Kilimanjaro. Initially, their story of a snow-covered peak near the equator was scoffed at. 
 ''' one eight four nine ''' - Just weeks after arriving on the Melanesian island of Aneiteum, missionary John Geddie wrote in his journal: In the darkness, degradation, pollution and misery that surrounds me, I will look forward in the vision of faith to the time when some of these poor islanders will unite in the triumphant song of ransomed souls, 'Unto Him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in His own blood.' 
 ''' one eight five zero ''' - On the occasion of K.F.A. Gtzlaff's visit to Europe, the Berlin Ladies Association for China is established in conjunction with the Berlin Missionary Association for China. Work in China will commence in one eight five one with the arrival of Mrs. Hermandine Neumann in Hong Kong. 
 ''' one eight five one ''' - Allen Gardiner and six missionary colleagues die of exposure and starvation at Patagonia on the southern tip of South America when a re-supply ship from England arrives six months late 
 ''' one eight five two ''' - Zenana (women) and Medical Missionary Fellowship formed in England to send out single women missionaries
 ''' one eight five three '''- The Hermannsburg Missionary Society, founded in one eight four nine by Louis Harms, has finished training its first group of young missionaries. They are sent to Africa on a ship (the Kandaze) which had been built entirely from donations. 
 ''' one eight five four ''' - London Missionary Conference; New York Missionary Conference; Henry Venn, secretary of the Church Missionary Society, sets out ideal of self-governing, self-supporting and self-propagating churches; Hudson Taylor arrives in China 
 ''' one eight five five ''' - Henry Steinhauer is ordained as a Canadian Methodist missionary to North American Indians and posted to Lac La Biche, Alberta. Steinhauer's missionary work had actually begun one five years earlier in one eight four zero when he was assigned to Lac La Pluie to assist in translating, teaching and interpreting in the Ojibway and Cree languages. 
 ''' one eight five six ''' - Presbyterians start work in Colombia with the arrival of Henry Pratt
 ''' one eight five seven ''' - Bible translated into Tswana language; Board of Foreign Missions of (Dutch) Reformed Church set up
 ''' one eight five eight ''' - John G. Paton begins work in New Hebrides; Elizabeth Freeman martyred in India; Basel Evangelical Missionary Society begins work in western Sumatra (Indonesia);Publication of David Livingstone's book Missionary Travels and Researches in South Africa 
 ''' one eight five nine ''' - Protestant missionaries arrive in Japan
 ''' one eight six zero ''' - United Lutheran Church begins work in Liberia; Liverpool Missionary Conference; Cyrus Hamlin establishes Robert College in Constantinople
 ''' one eight six one ''' - (Protestant) Stundism arises amongst native population in Russian Empire in the village of Osnova, (modern-day) Ukraine; Sarah Doremus founds the Women's Union Missionary Society; Episcopal Church opens work in Haiti; Rhenish Mission goes to Indonesia under Ludwig Nommensen
 ''' one eight six two ''' - Paris Evangelical Missionary Society opens work in Senegal
 ''' one eight six three ''' - Robert Moffat, missionary to Africa with the London Missionary Society, publishes his book Rivers of Water in a Dry Place, Being an Account of the Introduction of Christianity into South Africa, and of Mr. Moffat's Missionary Labours 
 ''' one eight six four ''' - Baptists enter Argentina
 ''' one eight six five ''' - The China Inland Mission is founded by James Hudson Taylor; James Laidlaw Maxwell plants first viable church in Formosa (Taiwan).
 ''' one eight six six ''' - Theodore Jonas Meyer ( one eight one nine - one eight nine four ), a converted Jew serving as a Presbyterian missionary in Italy, nurses those dying in a cholera epidemic until he also falls prey to the disease. Barely surviving, he becomes a peacemaker between Catholics and Protestants; Robert Thomas, the first Protestant martyr in Korea, is beheaded giving a Bible to his executioner. 
 ''' one eight six seven ''' - Methodists start work in Argentina; Scripture Union established; Lars Skrefsrud and Hans Barreson begin working among the Santal people of India.
 ''' one eight six eight ''' - Robert Bruce goes to Iran, Caniadian Baptist missionary Americus Timpany begins work among the Telugus in India.
 ''' one eight six nine ''' - The first Methodist women's missionary magazine, The Heathen Women's Friend, begins publication
 ''' one eight seven zero ''' - Clara Swain, the very first female missionary medical doctor, arrives at Bareilly, India.
 ''' one eight seven one ''' - Henry Stanley finds David Livingstone in central Africa; George Leslie Mackay plants church in northern Formosa (now called Taiwan).
 ''' one eight seven two ''' - First All-India Missionary Conference with one three six participants
 ''' one eight seven three ''' - Regions Beyond Missionary Union founded in London in connection with the East London Training Institute for Home and Foreign Missions; first Scripture portion (Gospel of Luke) translated into a language of the Philippines (Pangasinan) 
 ''' one eight seven four ''' - Lord Radstock's first visit to St. Petersburg and the beginning of an evangelical awakening amongst the St. Petersburg nobility.; Albert Sturges initiates the Interior Micronesia Mission in the Mortlock Islands under the leadership of Micronesian students from Ohwa 
 ''' one eight seven five ''' - The Foreign Christian Missionary Society is organized with Isaac Errett as president. It served a network of churches within the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) and Church of Christ movements. 
 ''' one eight seven six ''' - In September, a rusty ocean steamer arrives at a port on the Calabar River in what is now Nigeria. That part of Africa was then known as the White Man's Grave. The only woman on board the steamer is two nine -year-old Mary Slessor, a missionary. 
 ''' one eight seven seven ''' - James Chalmers goes to New Guinea

 ''' one eight eight two ''' - James Gilmour, London Missionary Society missionary to Mongolia, goes home to England for a furlough. During that time he published his famous book, Among the Mongols. So interesting was the book that one critic wrote, Robinson Crusoe has turned missionary, lived years in Mongolia, and wrote a book about it. Concerning the author, the critic said, If ever on earth there lived a man who kept the law of Christ, and could give proof of it, and be absolutely unconscious that he was giving it to them, it is this man whom the Mongols called 'our Gilmour.' While at home Gilmour's main message was to pray more for the missionaries. Unprayed for, he said,  I feel very much as if a diver were sent down to the bottom of a river, with no air to breathe, or as if a fireman were sent up to a blazing building and held an empty hose; I feel very much like a soldier who is firing blank cartridges at an enemy.

 Railyard in the port of Ashtabula

'''Ashtabula''' is a city located in Ashtabula County, Ohio, and the center of the Ashtabula Micropolitan Statistical Area (as defined by the United States Census Bureau in two zero zero three ). A major location on the Underground Railroad in the middle one nine th century, the city today is major coal port on Lake Erie at the mouth of the Ashtabula River northeast of Cleveland. The name Ashtabula means river of many fish in the Iroquois language. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two zero , nine six two .

Trivially, the city was mentioned by Bob Dylan in his one nine seven five song You're Going to Make Me Lonesome When You Go in the line ''I'll look for you in old Honolulu, San Francisco, Ashtabula''. The poet Carl Sandburg wrote a poem titled Crossing Ohio when Poppies Bloom in Ashtabula. 

 History 
Bridge Street (Ohio route five three one )-Ashtabula Historic Harbor District-June, two zero zero five 
Ashtabula was founded in one eight zero three , later incorporated in one eight nine one . The city contains several former stops on the Underground Railroad which was used to convey African-American slaves to freedom in Canada in the years before the American Civil War. Among the stops is Hubbard House, one of the handful of termination points. Ex-slaves would reside in an basement of the house adjacent to the lake and then leave on the next safe boat to Canada, gaining their freedom once they arrived in Ontario. Its harbor has been a large ore and coal port since the end of the one nine th century and continues to be to some extent with a long coal ramp draping across the horizon in the current harbor.
Hubbard House
Many newcomers to Ashtabula in the late one eight th century and early one nine th century were immigrants from Finland, Sweden, and Italy. Ethnic rivalries among these groups were once a major influence on daily life in Ashtabula. A substantial percentage of the current residents are descended from those immigrants.

The one nine zero zero s saw great changes in Ashtabula. Its access to Lake Erie and nearly three zero miles of shoreline helped position Ashtabula as a major shipping and commercial center.

During the one nine five zero s, the area experienced growth with its expanding
chemical industry and increasing Harbor activity making Ashtabula one of the most important port cities of the Great Lakes. The population in the City of Ashtabula grew steadily until one nine seven zero , since when it has been declining just as steadily.

 Geography 
Location of Ashtabula, Ohio

Ashtabula is located at four one  five two ' three eight  North, eight zero  four seven ' four nine  West ( four one . eight seven seven one three eight , - eight zero . seven nine six nine seven six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two zero . zero km ( seven . seven mi ).  one nine . six km ( seven . six mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . two zero % water.

Ashtabula borders Lake Erie to the north and has a prominent harbor where the Ashtabula River flows into the lake. The Ashtabula Harbor was a primary coal harbor and still serves to ship . It has two public beaches: Walnut Beach, near the harbor and on the opposite side of the harbor Lake Shore Park, which was originally a Public Works Administration project.

The Ashtabula River and harbor are a significant superfund site due to past industrial abuse of the waterway.

Part of the city lies in Ashtabula Township, and part lies in Saybrook Township.

Ship in the port of Ashtabula

'''Geneva''' is a city located in Ashtabula County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of six , five nine five .

 Geography 
Geneva is located at four one  four eight ' zero  North, eight zero  five six ' four five  West ( four one . eight zero zero zero nine eight , - eight zero . nine four five seven eight four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one zero . four km ( four . zero mi ).  one zero . four km ( four . zero mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

History
'''The city of Geneva''' was formed from a part of Geneva Township, which was a part of Harpersfield Township until one eight one six . Geneva became its own township when a small group that lived just north of Harpersfield Village decided to withdraw from Harpersfield Township. At the suggestion of Levi Gaylord, they named their new community Geneva after Geneva, New York.
   
With the completion of the Erie Canal in one eight two zero , the introduction of steamboats, and an increase in shipping on Lake Erie, areas north of Harpersfield, especially near the lake, became more attractive for settlement. In Geneva's early years, the south ridge (today transversed by Ohio Route eight four ) served as its main road. Geneva's first frame school house was erected by its side in one eight two one . 

By one eight two nine , Geneva had spread from the south ridge to the north ridge (today U.S. Highway two zero ), so in one eight two nine a post office was established on the north ridge for Geneva residents, who originally had to go to Harpersfield for their mail.

In one eight six six , Geneva became an incorporated village, and Dennis Thorp served as its first mayor. In one eight nine six , the town had a population of three thousand. In one nine five eight , Geneva became a city with a new charter system of government, and the first city manager, Robert C. Salisbury, entered office. Geneva Township remains; it surrounds the incorporated area of the city of Geneva.

On April six th, one nine six six , in celebration of a century from the incorporation of the city of Geneva, Ohio (self-proclaimed the best location in the best location in the nation), three five representatives of its citizenry, in the presence of God, signed a Declaration of Lunar Ownership. According to Virgiliu Pop, the author of Unreal Estate: The Men who Sold the Moon , the Ohioans assumed full possession and complete responsibility of the Moon, bowing to no man or State in its sovereign right so to do. The Declaration of Lunar Ownership, unveiled on April one two th in the High School auditorium before over two zero zero persons, was in fact a stunt aimed at drawing attention to the citys centennial celebrations, capitalizing on the nations fascination with lunar exploration.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are six , five nine five people, two , five one five households, and one , six zero seven families residing in the city. The population density is six three six . six km ( one , six five zero . four mi ). There are two , six six zero housing units at an average density of two five six . eight km ( six six five . seven mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine four . eight four % White, one . one five % African American, zero . one five % Native American, zero . two four % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, one . eight zero % from other races, and one . seven seven % from two or more races.  five . nine four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , five one five households out of which three zero . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four seven . six % are married couples living together, one two . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and three six . one % are non-families. three zero . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four four and the average family size is three . zero four .

In the city the population is spread out with two three . nine % under the age of one eight , eight . nine % from one eight to two four , two seven . six % from two five to four four , two two . zero % from four five to six four , and one seven . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are nine two . six males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . two males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three five , zero four eight , and the median income for a family is $ four one , five one one . Males have a median income of $ three one , eight one seven versus $ two three , nine two seven for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one six , nine four zero .  nine . four % of the population and five . one % of families are below the poverty line.  '''Jefferson''' is a village located in Ashtabula County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of three , five seven two . It is the county seat of Ashtabula County. Modern-day Jefferson sports the world's only perambulator museum and a historical complex including several restored one eight th century buildings. Joshua Giddings' law office has also been restored as a museum. Annual village events include the Ashtabula County Fair, the Strawberry Festival, Jefferson Days, and the Covered Bridge Festival.

 History 

Jefferson was officially founded by Gideon Granger U.S. Postmaster General during Thomas Jefferson's administration in one eight zero three . He envisioned the new settlement as a Philadelphia of the West, and early plans for the village were based upon the layout of that city. A cabin was erected by Granger's agent in one eight zero four , but the settlement's first permanent residents arrived only in one eight zero five : the Samuel Wilson family. Wilson, misled by land agents, moved to Ohio in late autumn expecting to find a thriving city on Granger's land. Instead, he found a wilderness, broken only by trees emblazoned with Philadelphian street names, marking where future streets would be built. Wilson himself died after two weeks of herculean effort to prepare for the winter, but his family stayed on as the first citizens of Jefferson.

Jefferson's two most famous sons were Congressman Joshua Giddings and Senator Benjamin Wade, two prominent Republican abolitionists. In one eight three one the two men formed a law practice in Jefferson (which became the county seat of newly-formed Ashtabula County in one eight one one ) and worked together until Giddings was elected to Congress in one eight three eight . Wade successfully ran for the Ohio State Senate in one eight three seven , then won election to the US Senate in one eight five one . Both were instrumental in the foundation of the Republican Party and defied the Gag Rule barring discussion of slavery prior to the American Civil War. Jefferson itself was a hotbed of abolitionism. John Brown spoke in the village, and several of its houses acted as stations on the Underground Railway. During the American Civil War, it trained Union recruits at Fort Giddings, which stood in the village at the current site of the fairgrounds.

E.T. Fetch, the first American to drive an automobile from coast to coast, was also a Jefferson resident.

 Geography 
Location of Jefferson, Ohio

Jefferson is located at four one  four four ' one four  North, eight zero  four six ' one nine  West ( four one . seven three seven one one eight , - eight zero . seven seven two zero one nine ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of five . nine km ( two . three mi ).  five . nine km ( two . three mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

The village's principle watercourse is Mill Creek, an oft-insubstantial trickle which, nevertheless, was significant in the town's industrial development. A dam reigns in this liliputian flood menace, forming a now-redundant village reservoir.

Culture
Nelsonville owes its existence to the coal mining industry. In more recent years, its main industrial base was the Rocky Shoes factory, which has since closed, but is now employing several individual in their new Rocky Gear Store and the Rocky Brands company. One of its more important employers today is Hocking College. There is also the Tri-County Vocational School located just outside Nelsonville.

Nelsonville is organized around a public square, where, every month, a Final Friday celebration is held, with vendors, art show openings, and often shows at the recently-renovated Stuart's Opera House, an old theater from the one eight zero zero s. 

The Paul Bunyan Show is annually held, most often in the first weekend of October. And is a large and fun tourist draw. Lumberjacks, chain saw carving, pole climbing, log birling, crafts and logs skidded by horses - anything that has to do with wood or the wood products industry. Music, Paul Bunyan Queen, Bunyan Burgers, chain saws, heavy equipment demos and displays, and more; something for everyone of all ages. 

The Parade of the Hills Festival is held annually in the Month of August and boast the regions best community cultural event. With over six stages of entertainment, an Art Walk, Carnival, children's park (The First National Family Fun Park) and Library Junction. The Parade of the Hills is one of the premier events that you won't want to miss.

 The Parade of the Hills Festival

Nelsonville has two connections to Hollywood. It is the birthplace of actress Sarah Jessica Parker who is best known for her portrayal of Carrie Bradshaw on HBO's Sex and the City. Nelsonville is also the site of the one nine eight five film Mischief starring Kelly Preston.

The '''Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog''', also known as the '''Catahoula Cur''' and '''Catahoula Hog Dog''', is named after Catahoula Parish, Louisiana.
Of extant dog breeds, the Catahoula is thought to have been in North America the longest.


Litter of Catahoulas showing wide variety of coat colors

 Appearance 
As a working dog, Catahoulas have been bred more for temperament and ability than for appearance. As a result, the physical characteristics of the Catahoula are somewhat varied.
They typically range from five zero to nine five pounds in weight and have short to very short hair.
They come in a variety of colors: blue, red and yellow, in both merles and solids. The archetype, however, is the blue merle. They are known for having haunting light blue '' glass eyes '', or half-blue, half-brown '' cracked '' eyes, although all-brown is also an acceptable eye color. Some Catahoulas have a short tail.

 Temperament 
Catahoulas are highly intelligent, energetic and quick, yet are generally very loving and gentle with children. They are inquisitive and have an independent streak. However, the Catahoula temperament is NOT suited for everyone; these dogs tend to be very protective of their territory and family, and can also be aggressive towards other dogs, especially of the same sex. This, combined with their independent nature, their high energy levels, and physical strength, can make a Catahoula too much dog for inexperienced or meek owners, and can make it a liability in surburban neighborhoods. Ideally, a Catahoula should have proper obedience training, secure confinement on the owner's property, and an outlet for its energy.

 History 
Young red-and-white Catahoulas
One theory as to the breed's origins states that the Catahoula is thought to have descended from war dogs (Mastiffs and Greyhounds) brought to Louisiana by Hernando de Soto in the one six th century. Dogs left behind by the explorer's party were interbred by the local Indians with a semidomesticated Red Wolf. 
 four month old black-and-grey Catahoula
In the one seven th century, French settlers arrived in Louisiana. They brought with them the Beauceron and mixed it with the dogs that had been created by the cross of red wolves and the Spanish war dogs . 

The Catahoula is ''the'' working dog of the region. They are used for herding cattle and sheep, and for tracking and hunting feral pigs (as well as anything else huntable from squirrel to deer to bear...) In one nine seven nine , they were named the official state dog of Louisiana in recognition of their importance in the history of the region.

 Miscellaneous 
The breed is not fully recognized by the American Kennel Club but can be recorded under the foundation stock service program.

The Catahoula is the state dog of Louisiana.

 Louisiana Catahoula Leopard Dog - DogBreedInfo.com

'''Wapakoneta''' is a city located in Auglaize County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of nine , four seven four . It is the county seat of Auglaize County. It is the birthplace of Neil Armstrong, the first human to set foot on the Moon; the Armstrong Air and Space Museum is located in Wapakoneta. Oscar-winning screenwriter Dudley Nichols was also born in the city.

The current mayor is Donald Wittwer. The city is served by an eight member city council including a council president, four ward representatives, and three at large members.

 The '''Treaty of Stralsund''' (May two four , one three seven zero ) ended the war between the Hanseatic League and the kingdom of Denmark. The Hanseatic League reached the peak of its power by the conditions of that treaty.

The war began in one three six one with the capture of Visby, a Hanseatic town on the island of Gotland, today belonging to Sweden. King Valdemar IV of Denmark took the town and declared it to be Danish. The Hanseatic League, which used to be rather a trade league than a political union, raised a fleet and blockaded the harbour of Copenhagen ( one three six eight ). Denmark surrendered in one three six nine .

The treaty was negotiated for Danmark by drost Henning Podebusk and for the Hanseatic League by the burgomasters Jakob Pleskow of Lbeck and Bertram Wulflam of Stralsund.

In the treaty, the freedom of Visby was reestablished. Furthermore, Denmark had to assure the Hanseatic League of free trade in the entire Baltic Sea. This gave the Hanseatic League a monopoly on the Baltic fish trade. The league also gained the right of participation in deciding the future heirs to the Danish throne.

''See also: Stralsund''

----

There is another (less important) treaty known as Treaty of Stralsund: It was arranged on February one two , one three five four , and settled border disputes between the duchies of Mecklenburg and Pomerania.

 '''Martins Ferry''' is a city located in Belmont County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of seven , two two six .

The city, which is located on the Ohio River, is the largest in Belmont County and is part of the Wheeling, West Virginia Metropolitan Statistical Area of the U.S. Census Bureau.
 
 Geography 

Location of Martins Ferry, Ohio

Martins Ferry is located at four zero  five ' five seven  North, eight zero  four three ' three one  West ( four zero . zero nine nine one two two , - eight zero . seven two five one five four ). 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of five . six km ( two . two mi ).  five . six km ( two . two mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

The town is built on two basic plateaus situated between a hill and the Ohio River. The lower of the plateaus, along the river, is dominated by a large industrial park, the Martins Ferry Football Stadium and by Ohio Route seven , a four lane traffic artery that runs from north to south across Eastern Ohio. The higher plateau, which is the larger of the two, is predominantly residential and commercial and is home to most of the people. It gradually rises to a rather steep hillside in the west that forms a natural wall. 

Directly across the river lies the city of Wheeling, West Virginia, and just one one miles to the east is the Pennsylvania state line. The City of Columbus, Ohio is one two five miles to the west, and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania is only three eight miles northeast of the city. On the southern end of town, Martins Ferry is directly connected to the village of Bridgeport. 

 History 
Martins Ferry enjoys the honor of being the oldest permanent settlement in the state of Ohio, having been settled at least as early as one seven seven nine . The community was a westward extension of the city of Wheeling, Virginia (now West Virginia), but at that time settlement on the west bank of the Ohio River was not permitted. The town was disbanded a couple of times before finally permanently taking hold in one seven eight five . 

Unlike Marietta, Ohio's oldest city, Martins Ferry remained an unincorporated settlement for a relatively long time. It did not officially become a city until one eight six five , a full seven seven years after Marietta. Through the years it has been known as Hoglinstown, Mercertown, Norristown, Jefferson, Martinsville and Martin's Ferry (the apostrophe between Martin and s is no longer used).

In one eight three five , Ebenezer Martin, the son of Absalom Martin one of the cities earliest settlers, redesigned the town, with a grid system of streets, much of which survives to this day. It was from this family that Martins Ferry took its name. 

The city developed as an important industrial center during the late one eight zero zero 's and early one nine zero zero 's. It became an important rail hub and river port, from where products where shipped all over the United States and beyond. Over the past five zero years, the town's population has decreased significantly as industries have closed or moved elsewhere. Today the city's population is less than half of what it once was, and work is relatively scarce.

Economy
Today Martins Ferry's largest employers include East Ohio Regional Hospital, a two five zero bed hospital that is home to a level three trauma center, a popular birthing unit and a rapidly expanding surgical department. A new surgical building is scheduled for completion this year. Other major employers include Nickles Bakery, one of three modern bakeries in the Nickles family providing fresh baked goods to a seven state area; the United Dairy, a family owned dairy serving nine states; and the Wheeling Pittsburgh Steel Corporation, which operates their galvanizing plant in Martins Ferry, producing some seven zero zero , zero zero zero tons of SofTite Galvanized Steel each year. 

Martins Ferry is also home of the corporate headquarters of United Bancorp, a financial institution operating two banks, The Citizens Savings Bank of Martins Ferry and the Community Bank of Lancaster. These two banks have a total of one five locations across Eastern and Southern Ohio. The city is also home of the Times-Leader, one of East Central Ohios largest newspapers serving over five zero , zero zero zero people.

Educational Facilities
The children of Martins Ferry are educated by the Martins Ferry City School District which currently has an enrollment of one , four eight eight students in five separate buildings. The district is in the process of constructing brand new high school, middle school and grade school facilities. In addition to the public school system, Martins Ferry is also served by two religious schools, St Mary's Catholic School and the Martins Ferry Christian School. 

Community
There are one four churches providing places of worship for Catholics, Baptists, Methodists, Nazarenes, Pentecostals, Presbyterians, Lutherans, Greek Orthodox Christians, Episcopalians and non-denominational Christians. There are also a number of clubs and organizations for veterans, ethnic groups and senior citizens.

The city has three cemeteries, including Riverview Cemetery, St. Marys Catholic Cemetery and Walnut Grove Pioneer Cemetery, which is the burial place of local heroine, Betty Zane, who saved Fort Henry in Wheeling during one of the last battles of the Revolutionary War by hiding gunpowder inside her dress. Her brother, Ebenezer Zane, who cut the famous Zane Trace from Wheeling to Maysville, Kentucky opening the west for settlement, is also buried in the cemetery along with Absalom and Ebenezer Martin and other important early settlers. 

Martins Ferry Natives
Famous Martins Ferry natives include: Lou Groza (AKA The Toe ), Belmont County's only native to have been inducted in the Football Hall of Fame; and the Pulitzer Prize winning poet and author James Wright, who immortalized the blue collar city in his poem, Autumn Begins in Martins Ferry, Ohio. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are seven , two two six people, three , two zero two households, and one , nine five nine families residing in the city. The population density is one , two nine one . seven km ( three , three four five . one mi ). There are three , six eight zero housing units at an average density of six five seven . eight km ( one , seven zero three . six mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine three . one nine % White, five . one one % African American, zero . three zero % Native American, zero . zero four % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, zero . two two % from other races, and one . one one % from two or more races.  zero . six four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , two zero two households out of which two six . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four two . two % are married couples living together, one five . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and three eight . eight % are non-families. three five . two % of all households are made up of individuals and one nine . one % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two four and the average family size is two . eight six .

In the city the population is spread out with two two . four % under the age of one eight , seven . two % from one eight to two four , two five . nine % from two five to four four , two four . one % from four five to six four , and two zero . three % who are six five years of age or older.  Points of interest 
President Ulysses S. Grant attended grade school in Georgetown. The school house is still in the town, the locals refer to it as Grant's School House. Also, in Georgetown you will also find Grant's Childhood Home as well as the tannery that his father owned across the street. All three are stops on the Land of Grant tour.  Historic Georgetown also includes the headstone of general Hamer in the old cemetary located by the Brown County Fair Grounds. Internationally known wildlife artist John A. Ruthvennot only lives there but he has an art galleryshop next to the Grant Childhood Home and has helped restore some of the classic 'downtown row' back to its' original charm. Also from Georgetown is Brian Grant the basketball player formerly of Xavier University and now the NBA. Being the county seat, Georgetown host the large Brown County Fair and parade which brings in thousands of patrons from other towns. The historical Court House located on Main St. is the gathering place with officials come to town as well as other speakers including Sarah McLachlan.

 Main Street ends at the Ohio River in Ripley, Ohio
'''Ripley''' is a village located in Brown County, Ohio, five zero miles southeast of Cincinnati, along the Ohio River. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , seven four five .

History

Colonel James Poage, a veteran of the American Revolution, arrived in the free state of Ohio from Staunton, Virginia in one eight zero four to claim the one zero zero zero acres he had been granted in what was then the Virginia Military District. Poage was among a large group of veterans who received land grants beyond the Ohio for their service and freed their slaves when they settled there. Poage and his family laid out the town of Staunton in one eight one two ; it was renamed in one eight one six to honor an American officer in the War of one eight one two , General Eleazar Wheelock Ripley.


The proximity of the river and of the slave state of Kentucky on the opposite shore led to Ripley's role as an early stop on the Underground railroad, a network of citizens sympathetic to slaves escaping north to freedom. A number of prominent abolitionists lived in the town in the one eight zero zero s, mainly on Front Street near the river, including Reverend John Rankin, former slave John Parker, Thomas McCague, Thomas Collins and Dr. Alexander Campbell.

Rankin moved from Kentucky to Ripley in one eight two two and later built a house (now a National Historic Landmark) on Liberty Hill overlooking the town, the river and the Kentucky shore. There he was able to signal escaping slaves with a lantern on a flagpole and provide them shelter. A slave woman that crossed the frozen river to Ripley and stayed in his house in one eight three eight became the model for the character Eliza in Harriet Beecher Stowe's landmark book, ''Uncle Tom's Cabin''. Rankin was the minister at the Ripley Presbyterian Church for twenty-four years.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of two . eight km ( one . one mi ).  two . six km ( one . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is five . five six % water.

There are seven four five households out of which two eight . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four four . zero % are married couples living together, one six . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and three seven . two % are non-families. three two . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  '''Hamilton''' is a city located in Butler County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of six zero , six nine zero . It is the county seat of Butler County. two zero zero three estimates show slight population increase.

The city's mayor is Mr. Donald Ryan. Most of the city is in the Hamilton City School District, which has been named the number one urban school district in Ohio, and its superintendent, Janet Baker, has been named Ohio's superintendent of the year. 

History
Hamilton was laid out as Fairfield in one seven nine four , but took the name of Fort Hamilton, the army post established there by General Arthur St. Clair and named for Treasury Secretary Alexander Hamilton. From there, St. Clair and General Richard Butler, namesake of the county, marched north in one seven nine one to fight Indians. Butler was killed in the expedition. The 'father of Hamilton' and a leading statesman was James McBride.

Hamilton was first incorporated by act of the Ohio General Assembly in one eight one zero , but lost its status in one eight one five for failure to hold elections. It was reincorporated in one eight two seven with Rossville, the community across the Great Miami River in St. Clair Township but the two places severed their connection in one eight three one only to be rejoined in one eight five four . It became a city in one eight five seven . On March one four , one eight six seven , Hamilton withdrew from the townships of Fairfield and St. Clair to form a paper township. 

The paper industry, iron works, and manufacturing works thrived in Hamilton in the early to mid twentieth century due to the migration of skilled German immigrants and presence of a good water supply needed by industry; in the forms of the Great Miami River, Miami Aquafier and the old Miami Erie Canal system. Many military supplies needed for WWII were manufactured in Hamilton; including tank turrets, liberty ship and submarine engines, machined and stamped metal parts.

In the one nine two zero s, many Chicago gangsters had second homes in Hamilton. This gave Hamilton the nickname Little Chicago.  John Dillinger is documented to have been a visitor to Hamilton. During WWII, due to the large number of gambling and prostitution establishments such as Madame Freeze's and the long row of prostitution establishments along Wood Street (now called Pershing Ave), the entire city was declared off-limits to military personel. 

In the one nine eight zero s, in order to gain national recognition, Hamilton changed its name to ''Hamilton!'' (with an exclamation point).

The city is the birthplace of the late game-show host Ray Combs, and Joe Nuxhall, a star pitcher and longtime announcer for the Cincinnati Reds baseball team and also the youngest major leaguer ever. James Ruppert who murdered one one members of his entire family on Easter Sunday in one nine seven five including eight nieces and nephews, lived in Hamilton. Captain John Cleves Symmes (died one eight two nine ), constructed the Symmes Theory of Concentric Spheres and Polar Voids which contended that the earth was hollow and that the inside could be reached through the polar regions. Singer and movie star Doris Day broke her leg when riding in an automobile which was struck by a train in Hamilton.

 History 
Before the Miami canal was built, Jacksonburg, located in the northern part of Butler County, was the trading center of this region; it had a population of six zero zero to seven zero zero when Middletown had around three zero zero . The farmers for miles around went to Jacksonburg to buy the staples and clothing they needed. The canal changed all of this. The village of Middletown had promise of a great future; she had unexcelled transportation facilities. In one eight two seven the canal was opened as far north as Middletown.
