'''''The Godfather, Part III''''' ( one nine nine zero ) is the third film in the ''Godfather'' trilogy. It completes the story of Michael Corleone, a Mafia godfather who tries to legitimize his crime empire. The plot also weaves into its plot a fictionalized account of real life events--the mysterious one nine seven eight death of Pope John Paul I and the Papal banking scandal of one nine eight one - one nine eight two --and links them with each other and with the affairs of Michael Corleone. The film stars Al Pacino, Diane Keaton, Talia Shire, Andy Garcia, Eli Wallach, Joe Mantegna, George Hamilton, Bridget Fonda, and Sofia Coppola.

The movie was written by Mario Puzo and Francis Ford Coppola, and directed by Coppola.

Unlike its predecessors, ''Godfathers Part I'' and ''II'', ''Godfather Part III'' was not as widely critically acclaimed on release, and critics and fans remain divided on its legacy to this day.

Plot Synopsis


The final chapter of the Corleone saga begins in one nine seven nine . Michael Corleone is now in his sixties, his children are grown and he has not seen his ex-wife Kay (now remarried to a judge) in eight years. Tom Hagen is dead; his son Andrew (John Savage) has become a priest. Feeling that he may have made the wrong choices in life, Michael seeks to legitimize the family business. But these plans are upset by Vincent Mancini (Michael's illegitimate nephew) and his nemesis Joey Zaza. There is also a subplot regarding corruption in the Vatican.

Casting
Al Pacino, Diane Keaton, and Talia Shire reprised their roles from the first two movies, but Robert Duvall, who played Tom Hagen in the first two films, refused to take part. According to Coppola's commentary track for this film, found in ''The Godfather DVD Collection,'' Duvall refused to take part unless he was paid the same salary as Al Pacino. This did not happen and Duvall refused to participate, forcing Coppola to rewrite his screenplay to portray the Hagen character as having died before the story begins. Coppola created the character B.J. Harrison , played by George Hamilton, to replace the function of the Tom Hagen character in the story. (Coppola had gone through a very similar process in the making of ''The Godfather, Part II''. In that film, Richard Castellano, who had portrayed the ''capo regime'' or lieutenant Peter Clemenza in the first ''Godfather'' film, had refused to participate. Coppola responded by writing Clemenza out of the story as having died and replaced the character with a new character, Frank Pentangeli , played by the late actorplaywright Michael V. Gazzo in an Academy Award-nominated performance.) The director further states that, to him, the movie feels incomplete without Robert Duvall's participation.  According to Coppola, had Duvall agreed to take part in the film, the Hagen character would have been heavily involved in running the fictional Corleone charities. 

Coppola further comments that before he was even brought on board, Paramount had already had a script prepared, centering on the Vincent Mancini character, the illegitimate son of Sonny Corleone, with a plot revolving around the new kind of wiseguy (in Coppola's words) of the seven zero s and eight zero s and involving the drug cartels. The Vincent Mancini character was portrayed by Andy Garcia who was nominated for an Oscar for Best Supporting Actor. 

Coppola says that he felt the Godfather saga was essentially the story of Michael, how a good man becomes evil as the writerdirector puts it on the same commentary track referenced above. Coppola says he felt that Michael had not really paid for his sins in the second film and wanted this final chapter to demonstrate that. In keeping with this theme, Coppola wanted to subtitle the movie, The Death of Michael Corleone, but Paramount balked. Sofia Coppola, the director's daughter, was forced into the role of Michael Corleone's daughter at the last minute when Winona Ryder dropped out of the film. As an infant, Sofia had played Michael Corleone's infant nephew in ''The Godfather'', during the climactic baptismmurder montage at the end of that film, and her character's aunt is played by her real-life aunt, Talia Shire. Other Coppola relatives with cameos in the film included his mother, father and granddaughter, Gia. Michele Russo, who plays the son of the assassin Mosca, is also a distant Coppola relative, from the same town as Francis Coppola's great-grandmother. In addition, Coppola casted Catherine Scorsese, mother of Martin Scorsese, for a bit part. Sofia's much-criticized performance resulted in her father's being accused of nepotism, a charge Coppola bitterly refutes in the commentary track, asserting, in his opinion, that critics were using his daughter to attack him, something he finds ironic in light of the film's denouement when Sofia's character, Mary, pays the ultimate price for her father's sins.

Awards

''The Godfather Part III'' was nominated for Academy Awards for Best Actor in a Supporting Role (Andy Garcia), Best Art Direction-Set Decoration, Best Cinematography, Best Director, Best Film Editing, Best Music, Song (for Carmine Coppola and John Bettis for Promise Me You'll Remember ) and Best Picture.'

Historical background


Parts of the film are very loosely based on real historical events concerning the very short Papacy of John Paul I in one nine seven eight and the collapse of the Banco Ambrosiano in one nine eight two . Like the character Cardinal Lamberto, who becomes John Paul I, the historical John Paul I, Albino Luciani, reigned for only a very short time before being found dead in his bed. Journalist David Yallop argues that Luciani was planning a reform of Vatican finances and that he died by poisoning; these claims are reflected in the film. Yallop also names as a suspect ((fr:Archbishop Paul Marcinkus, who was the head of the Vatican bank, like the character Archbishop Gilday in the film. However, while Marcinkus was noted for his muscular physique and Chicago origins, Gilday is a mild Irishman. The character of Frederick Keinszig, the Swiss banker who is murdered and left hanging under a bridge, mirrors the fate (and physical appearance) of Roberto Calvi, the Italian head of the Banco Ambrosiano who was found hanging under Blackfriars Bridge in London in one nine eight two (although it has not yet been proven if Calvi was murdered). The character of Licio Lucchesi, who moves between the church, organised crime and Italian politics, recalls Licio Gelli, head of the Propaganda Due Masonic lodge.

Soundtrack
The soundtrack for the movie, The Godfather Part III (soundtrack), received one Oscar nomination, and two Golden Globe nominations, one for best score and two for best song, the film's love theme Promise Me You'll Remember . 

Trivia
 The character of Joey Zasa was one of the inspirations for Fat Tony, the resident mob boss on ''The Simpsons''. Both are portrayed by Joe Mantegna.
 After the adverse critical response to her performance, Sofia Coppola largely abandoned acting in favor of directing.
According to Francis Ford Coppola (see Director's Commentary track) Paramount Pictures was briefly controlled by Vatican Bank. He states that, on one occasion when he went to see Charles Bluhdorn, then chief of the Gulf Frederick Keinszig (played by Austrian-born actor, Helmut Berger) in this film.

 Government 

Moraine is served by a Council-Manager form of government, where a seven-member City Council appoints a professional City Manager, who serves as the administrative head of the City. 

The City Council of Moraine, Ohio consists of seven members. A Mayor and two Council Members-at-Large are elected by the entire city, while four additional members of Council are elected to represent each of four wards. The Mayor presides over meetings of the Council as Chairman, and may vote as a member of Council, but has no Veto.

Moraine has a municipal income tax of two %.

 '''Oakwood''' is a city located in Montgomery County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of nine , two one five . Oakwood is part of the Greater Dayton Area. It is a sister city with Le Vesinet, France and Outremont, Quebec and was incorporated in one nine zero eight .

 History 

Following the one nine one three Dayton Flood that decimated downtown Dayton, residents of Montgomery County searched for new land that was at a higher elevation. Oakwood is situated atop a large hill and thus was ideal for people fearful of another flood.

After this, the city's population boomed through the one nine three zero 's and became known for being a safe and pleasant place to live. The city's constant attention to aesthetic care and city services continue that reputation and has attracted many people moving to the Dayton area.

 Geography 
Location of Oakwood, Montgomery County, Ohio

Oakwood is located at three nine  four three ' six  North, eight four  one zero ' one zero  West ( three nine . seven one eight two zero nine , - eight four . one six nine five one eight ).
It is within the Miami valley region of Ohio, and borders on Dayton, Ohio to its North and East and Kettering, Ohio to its South and West.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of five . seven km ( two . two mi).  five . seven km ( two . two mi) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

The city is unofficially divided into two parts, east and west, by the city's major road, Ohio State Route four eight . SR four eight runs north to south and connects Kettering at its southern end to the city of Dayton to the north. The four lane highway, known as Far Hills, serves as a major route for commuters from the southern suburbs of Dayton into downtown, and as such is very busy during rush hour travel times.

West Side

The western side of Oakwood, colloquially known as The West Side, is a hilly region that is the older of the two sides. Because of its age, the West end features a great deal of oddly designed swirving and narrow roads that can be very confusing to people not familiar with the area. This aspect of the roads makes it very difficult for snow plows to clear snow and many times in the winter the roads of the West Side are the last plowed. Most roads also do not have sidewalks forcing many people to walk in the street.

Oakwood Avenue reflects these aspects of the West end as the road features many turns and changes in altitude. Roughly a quarter-mile section of the road is also made of red brick instead of asphalt or concrete, adding to the aged look of the area.

The hilly attributes of this section make an ideal swooping golf course and are likely one of the reasons that the bordering Dayton Country Club (DCC) is built adjacent to Oakwood's west border.

East Side
 
The eastern side of Far Hills Avenue (SR four eight ) is a great deal more level than its western counterpart and is a stark contrast to the geography of the West Side. Whereas the west end features older designed roads, the east is much more modern and thus the roads are designed in a common grid layout. It still features some slight changes in elevation, but they are much more subtle and span a longer distance. The roads are straight and wide and are many times well plowed in the winter before most workers commute to their jobs. The streets on the east are accompanied by well maintained sidewalks that are plowed in the wintertime along with the streets.

The flat geography makes it a perfect location for the city's main athletic venue, Mack Hummon Stadium, Oakwood High School's soccer, football, and track Beautification Awards to the judged most beautiful houses in order to maintain this high level of aesthetic awareness.

In a similar effort, the city has relatively strict zoning laws that restrict major changes to houses and require city approval for any planned structural additions. For example, the city requires all external utility units (such as air conditioning units) to be obstructed from the view from the street.

Some residents have chosen to resist this push and in a notable move to change from the norm, a resident on Far Hills Avenue chose to paint his or her house a bright hue of purple. The house, across from the high school, draws much attention due to its location. This action created a fair amount of controversey in the city but as of December two zero zero five it still remains the same color.

In addition to the well kept up houses, the city is adorned with a large amount of trees from border to border, most of them deciduous trees, giving the city a constantly changing look depending on the season.

Public architecture is a general source of pride for the Oakwood community. The city buildings were designed to encorporate the rich variation of traditional architectural styles found in the city's houses. Oakwood High School is often mistaken for a private, sprawling mansion, due to its elaborate external design. The elementary schools, Edwin D. Smith Elementary School and Harman Elementary School, echo this elaborate style. Smith Elementary is tudor styled like the High School while Harman Elementary is Colonial revival. The newest addition to the school system, The Julian and Marjorie Lange School, features Spanish revival architecture.

The public library offers similar aesthetics, and the policefire department is reminescient of a French chateau.

 Demographics 
Chart of the Oakwood Racial Makeup as of the two zero zero zero Census
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are nine , two one five people, three , six three three households, and two , five nine seven families residing in the city. The population density is one , six two four . six km ( four , two zero nine . zero mi). There are three , eight one five housing units at an average density of six seven two . six km ( one , seven four two . five mi). The racial makeup of the city is nine seven . four one % White, zero . four eight % African American, zero . zero seven % Native American, zero . nine eight % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, zero . two nine % from other races, and zero . seven five % from two or more races.  one . two zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race. The city of Oakwood is well known in the Dayton area for its low minority populations, which stand in stark contrast to those of the City of Dayton.

There are three , six three three households out of which three eight . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six one . eight % are married couples living together, eight . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and two eight . five % are non-families. two six . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . one % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . five three and the average family size is three . zero eight .

In the city the population is spread out with two nine . one % under the age of one eight , four . two % from one eight to two four , two seven . one % from two five to four four , two five . eight % from four five to six four , and one three . eight % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Vandalia''' is a suburb of Dayton located in Montgomery County, Ohio. It is the location of the James M. Cox Dayton International Airport. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one four , six zero three .

 Geography 
Location of Vandalia, Ohio

Vandalia is one zero miles north of Dayton on Dixie Drive. It is between the Great Miami River and the Stillwater River. The city has been called the Crossroads of America due to its location on the National Road and the Dixie Highway. These correspond to U.S. Highway four zero and the now decommissioned U.S. Highway two five .

Currently, Interstate seven zero and Interstate seven five are Vandalia's most important highways. The cloverleaf interchange is currently undergoing reconstruction until two zero zero eight . Three of the four left turns are being reconstructed as ramps or tunnels in place of right two seven zero  turns.

 Graham Greene
'''Graham Greene''' (born June two two , one nine five two ) is a Canadian actor. He is an Oneida Indian, born in Ohsweken on the Six Nations Reserve in Ontario.

Greene's first brushes with the entertainment industry came when he was an audio technician for rock bands. He graduated from The Centre for Indigenous Theatre's Native Theatre School program in one nine seven four , and began appearing in theater in Toronto and England.

His screen debut was in one nine eight three in ''Running Brave'', and appeared in such films as ''Revolution'' and ''Powwow Highway'', but it was his Academy Award nominated role as Kicking Bird in the one nine nine zero film ''Dances With Wolves'' that brought him stardom.

He followed that up with such films as ''Thunderheart'', ''Benefit of the Doubt'', and ''Maverick'', and on the television series ''Northern Exposure'' and ''The Red Green Show''. He also hosted a true crime documentary show called ''Exhibit A'' (called ''Secrets of Forensic Science'' in the United States) in one nine nine seven . 

In one nine nine four he began appearing as Mr. Crabby Tree in the children's series The Adventures of Dudley the Dragon for which he received his first and only Gemini Award.

In one nine nine seven , Greene suffered a major depressive attack, and had to be hospitalized after a police encounter. He survived the ordeal, making such movies as ''The Green Mile''. He starred in the short-run television series ''Wolf Lake'' in two zero zero one . 

In two zero zero four he accepted the Earle Grey Award for lifetime achievement at the Gemini Awards.

In two zero zero five he appeared as himself in a parody of the famous Lakota-brand pain reliever commercials, on CBC's ''Rick Mercer Report''. In two zero zero six , Greene was the presenter of the documentary series ''The War that Made America'' about the French and Indian War of the mid- one eight th century.

Selected filmography 

 ''Dances with Wolves'' ( one nine nine zero )
 ''Maverick'' ( one nine nine zero )
 ''The Education of Little Tree'' ( one nine nine seven )
 ''The Green Mile'' ( one nine nine nine )

'''Mount Gilead''' is a village in Morrow County, Ohio. The elevation is one , zero eight one feet above sea level. Shawnee people hunted in the surrounding forest before white settlers arrived in one eight two four . Mount Gilead was established in one eight three two . As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of three , two nine zero . It is the county seat of Morrow County.

Warren G. Harding, the two nine th President of the United States, was born near Blooming Grove, Ohio, northeast of Mount Gilead. As a college student, Harding began to seriously learn the newspaper and printing trade in Mount Gilead by working at the downtown ''Union Register.'' Satirical author Dawn Powell was born and raised in the village. Notable persons that resided in Mount Gilead were social reformer Victoria Woodhull, actor Tom Poston, and retired Major League Baseball pitcher Tim Belcher.  

Located in the center of the village is Morrow County's historic, World War I Victory Memorial Shaft, unique in the United States, and Mount Gilead State Park is nearby on State Route nine five . Other areas interesting to the tourist include Amish farms, shops, and stores east of Mount Gilead near Chesterville and Johnsville.

The Morrow County Hospital is located at six five one West Marion Road on the west side of the village. The Hospital offers a wide variety of outpatient services and a two four hour emergency department.

'''Dresden''' is a village located in Muskingum County, Ohio, along the Muskingum River. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , four two three .

Location of Dresden, Ohio

Dresden is located at four zero  seven ' one seven  North, eight two  zero ' four seven  West ( four zero . one two one two eight six , - eight two . zero one three zero nine four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of three . one km ( one . two mi ).  three . zero km ( one . two mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is three . three one % water.

 History 
Dresden is located on or near the site of the Delaware Indian village of Wakatomika, which gave its name to Wakatomika Creek, the creek that empties into the Muskingum River near the northern edge of the village.

In the one nine th century Dresden was an important trading town on the Ohio and Erie Canal. A side cut canal linked the Ohio and Erie Canal with the Muskingum River. A suspension bridge built by George Willison Adams and John Augustus Roebling once crossed the Muskingum River at Dresden. The Longaberger Basket Company was started in Dresden in the one nine eight zero s. --Source:  The G. W. Adams Educational Center, Inc.

There are six zero nine households out of which two nine . two % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four eight . four % are married couples living together, one zero . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and three seven . one % are non-families. three two . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. Dresden has the following historic structures of note:

 '''New Concord''' is a village located in Muskingum County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two , six five one .

Location of New Concord, Ohio

New Concord is located at three nine  five nine ' four zero  North, eight one  four four ' one one  West ( three nine . nine nine four three eight nine , - eight one . seven three six four one two ).

 Claims to fame 

John Glenn, a former United States Senator and the first American to orbit the Earth, was raised in New Concord and attended Muskingum College, a Presbyterian liberal arts college also located in the village. Incidentally, on May one , one eight six zero , a horse was struck by a meteorite near New Concord. (To stretch this theme a bit further, Muskingum graduate Agnes Moorehead played the role of an anonymous woman whose house is attacked by a miniature flying saucer in the one nine six one Twilight Zone episode The Invaders .)

New Concord's more down-to-Earth claims to fame include the local John Glenn High School's annual canned food drive, which set national records for five years up to and including two zero zero three .

On a more substanial note, New Concord is also the hometown of William Rainey Harper, founder and first president of the University of Chicago; it also claims as a native son the exceptional bluesrock guitarist Tom Nelson.

New Concord is also home to one of the rather unusual S-bridges found along sections of the old National Road.

 '''Zanesville''' is a city located in Muskingum County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two five , five eight six . It is the county seat of Muskingum County.

Zanesville was settled in one seven nine seven by Ebenezer Zane (who lent his name to the town) and his son in law, John McIntire. Novelist Zane Grey was a descendant of the Zane family and was born in Zanesville. The city was the state capital of Ohio from one eight one zero to one eight one two . 

 Geography 
Location of Zanesville, Ohio

Zanesville is located at three nine  five six ' four six  North, eight two  zero ' four four  West ( three nine . nine four six zero four nine , - eight two . zero one two one five zero ), along the Muskingum River at its confluence with the Licking River.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two nine . eight km ( one one . five mi ).  two nine . one km ( one one . two mi ) of it is land and zero . seven km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . two six % water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two five , five eight six people, one zero , five seven two households, and six , four three eight families residing in the city. The population density is eight seven eight . nine km ( two , two seven six . eight mi ). There are one one , six six two housing units at an average density of four zero zero . six km ( one , zero three seven . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the city is eight five . four eight % White, one zero . seven six % African American, zero . four zero % Native American, zero . two three % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . four two % from other races, and two . seven zero % from two or more races.  zero . seven nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one zero , five seven two households out of which three zero . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three eight . five % are married couples living together, one eight . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three nine . one % are non-families. three three . four % of all households are made up of individuals and one four . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three six and the average family size is two . nine nine .

In the city the population is spread out with two six . eight % under the age of one eight , nine . five % from one eight to two four , two seven . eight % from two five to four four , two zero . five % from four five to six four , and one five . five % who are six five years of age or older.  Claim to Fame 
A Y-shaped bridge (usually called the Y-Bridge ) spans the confluence of the Licking and Muskingum Rivers. It is currently the only bridge of its type in the world and has been built numerous times since the one eight five zero 's. When being given directions, visitors are often struck by the statement Drive to the middle of the bridge and turn right. 

It is also the only bridge in the United States that you can cross and still be on the same side of the river that you started on.

 '''Marblehead''' is a village located in Ottawa County, Ohio. It sits at the tip of the Marblehead Peninsula, which divides Lake Erie proper from Sandusky Bay. In the summer, it is a popular vacation area because of its lake frontage, ferry service to the Lake Erie Islands, quality sport fishery, the nearby chautauqua at Lakeside, and the Cedar Point amusement park. Marblehead is also commercially important as a major limestone producer. The limestone is mined in nearby quarries and transported by conveyor belt to the Marblehead port, where it is loaded on commercial lake freighters. Marblehead is also home to a US Coast Guard station, and to the Marblehead Lighthouse, the oldest continuously operating lighthouse on the Great Lakes.  Nearby, in Sandusky Bay, is Johnson's Island, a former confederate officer POW camp during the civil war.

 Put-in-Bay, Ohio, looking out towards Lake Erie

'''Put-in-Bay''' is an incorporated village located on South Bass Island, Ottawa County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one two eight . The village played a significant role in the War of one eight one two as the location of the squadron of U.S. naval commander Oliver Hazard Perry, who sailed from the port on September one zero , one eight one three to engage a British squadron just north of the island in the Battle of Lake Erie. The village is a popular summer resort and recreational destination. Ferry service connects it with Catawba Island, Kelleys Island, Port Clinton, and Sandusky, Ohio. 

 Geography 
Location of Put-in-Bay, Ohio

The island is located in Lake Erie, one five mi ( two five km) northwest of Sandusky Ohio at four one  three nine ' one one  North, eight two  four nine ' three  West ( four one . six five three zero zero six , - eight two . eight one seven six two zero ). 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one . seven km ( zero . six mi ).  one . two km ( zero . five mi ) of it is land and zero . five km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is two eight . one two % water. The island is three mi ( five km) long and one mi ( two km) wide. It has two sister islands, Middle Bass and North Bass located just north of South Bass Island.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one two eight people, six seven households, and three six families residing in the village. The population density is one zero seven . four km ( two seven nine . two mi ). There are one seven nine housing units at an average density of one five zero . two km ( three nine zero . five mi ). The population is nearly exclusively white.

The summer population is higher than the permanent population.

There are six seven households out of which one six . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four nine . three % are married couples living together, four . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and four four . eight % are non-families. four one . eight % of all households are made up of individuals and six . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is one . nine one and the average family size is two . five nine .

In the village the population is spread out with one five . six % under the age of one eight , four . seven % from one eight to two four , two five . eight % from two five to four four , three eight . three % from four five to six four , and one five . six % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four seven years. There are slightly more males than females both in the total and in the adult population.

The median income for a household in the village is $ five two , nine one seven , and the median income for a family is $ eight zero , zero zero zero . Males have a median income of $ four seven , zero eight three versus $ three eight , seven five zero for females. The per capita income for the village is $ three five , three zero one .  zero . zero % of the population and zero . zero % of families are below the poverty line.

 Tourism 

South Bass Island
The island's primary industry is tourism. The tourist season runs roughly between April and October. The most common methods of transportation to and from the island are via ferry boat, propeller driven aircraft and private boat.

Put-in-Bay is the site of Perry's Victory and International Peace Memorial commemorating Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry's September one zero , one eight one three naval victory over British ships in the War of one eight one two . Construction of the monument began in one nine one two and it opened to the public on June one three , one nine one five . It is three five two ft ( one zero seven m) tall and made up of seven eight layers of pink granite, topped with an eleven short ton ( one zero metric ton) bronze urn. The remains of six naval officers, three British and three Americans, were interred beneath the floor of the monument's rotunda.

Other Historical sites include: 

 Stonehenge Estate  An estate with one nine th century buildings that are listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
 Perry's Cave  Cave discovered by Commodore Perry during the War of one eight one two that has an underground stream from which Perry's men obtained drinking water.
 Lake Erie Islands Historical Society  six zero zero zero ft ( five six zero m ) museum that houses artifacts, memorabilia and genealogical data pertinent to the Lake Erie Islands.
 The Round House Bar  A one three zero year-old, circular building that houses a tavern offering live entertainment seven days a week.
 Beer Barrel Saloon  Houses the Guiness Book of World Records Worlds Longest Bar - four zero five ft one zero in. If you stood it on end it would be taller than the ( three five two ft high) Perry's Monument.

There are approximately six zero zero full-time (South Bass Island) residents, most of whom remain on the island over the winter. Supplies and perishables are flown to the island during the winter months along with the mail, parcels and bank employees who staff the island's only bank (for one day a week) until the spring. The island has a single school that is used for all classes  grades kindergarten through one two  and also serves the educational requirements of Middle Bass and North Bass islands. 

Put-in-Bay has one grocery store, one bank and two cemeteries. It has one corporate franchise restaurant, Dairy Queen, and no cinema. The island does not have a hospital, but does have an Emergency Medical Service that can use a Life Flight helicopter to transport critically ill patients to mainland medical facilities.

Villages in Ohio
Paulding County, Ohio
 
   
 The village of '''Paulding''' is the county seat of Paulding County, Ohio, in the United States. 

Paulding was a planned community, founded in one eight four eight at the center of the county, and named after the county by speculators who expected to profit by moving the county seat. In one eight five one , the county seat was moved from Charloe, which had been county seat for a decade; prior to that, court was held at Rochester. 

The town square is devoted to the courthouse, a rather attractive orange brick structure surrounded by majestic trees upon a spacious lawn. In the centennial year of one eight seven six , the county commissioners determined to build a new courthouse, and visited many courthouses, finally deciding to erect a duplicate of the courthouse in Jackson, Michigan at a cost of $ four zero , zero zero zero . The courthouse was finished in one eight eight six .

Tramsportation and Communications
Paulding is at the intersection of US Highway one two seven and Ohio Highway one one one and the terminus of Ohio Highway five zero zero . Formerly on the Cincinnati Northern Railroad, the tracks were removed in the one nine eight zero s. Paulding Airport, located two miles northeast of town, has one grass runway, three zero five six x eight zero ft

The dominant daily newspaper is the Defiance Crescent-News with some readers choosing the Fort Wayne Journal-Gazette, Toledo Blade, and Lima News, in that order. The local weekly is the Paulding County Progress, Paulding residents are part of the Fort Wayne, Indiana television market. 

Trivia
 Paulding has achieved an internet fame of sorts for supposedly having a law saying that a policeman may bite a rabid dog to bite him. No such law exists. However, a town councilman moved to disarm a town officer much as fictional deputy Barney Fife did not carry a loaded weapon in fictional Mayberry, another community where stolen bicycles were pretty much the extent of major crime. The officer, objecting to this indignity, pointed out that if a rabid dog were to threaten the community, he would need a gun to deal with the dog. The councilman directed the officer to proactively deal with rabid dogs by biting them first, to quiet them. 
 When the ''Paulding Democrat'' and the ''Paulding Republican'' merged, there was no obvious name for the new newspaper. Editorpublisher Ralph Reinhart held a contest to choose a new name, and selected ''Paulding Progress'' as the winner. 
 Miles Street is named for Paul Miles, one nine seven zero Paulding High School graduate, who was the first US college quarterback in nearly a half century to rush one zero zero zero yards per season for four seasons. 
 Sculptor David Smith, whose Cubi XXVIII became the most expensive work of contemporary art ever sold at auction, selling for $ two three . eight million at Sotheby's Manhattan auction house in two zero zero five , grew up in Paulding, where his father Harvey ran the Paulding Telephone Company and mother Golda taught school.

 '''Circleville''' is a city located in Pickaway County, Ohio, along the Scioto River. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one three , four eight five . It is the county seat of Pickaway County.

Circleville hosts the Circleville Pumpkin Show every October, which draws over four zero zero , zero zero zero visitors each year. The city's water tower has been painted to look like a giant pumpkin in honor of this festival.

History

Circleville was founded in one eight one zero . It derived its name from the circular portion of a large Hopewell culture earthwork upon which it was built. The original town plan integrated Circleville into the preexisting land with a street layout of concentric circles. An octagonal courthouse stood directly in the center.

Dissatisfaction rose with Circleville's layout, however, and in one eight three seven , the Ohio General Assembly authorized the Circleville Squaring Company to convert it into a conventional grid. By one eight five six , this had been completed in several phases. No remaining traces of the original earthworks remain, though a few old buildings retain curved walls that were part of the original circular layout.

 Geography 
Location of Circleville, Ohio

Circleville is located at three nine  three six ' one one  North, eight two  five six ' two one  West ( three nine . six zero two nine nine zero , - eight two . nine three nine two seven two ).

 Famous Residents 
Ted Lewis, a vaudeville performer, who was well known for his top hat, cane and clarinet and who sang, Me and My Shadow was born and raised in Circleville. There is a Ted Lewis Museum which exhibits his memorabilia.

Caleb Atwater, the Father of Ohios Public School System lived in Circleville for many years.

 Industry 

The initial operation of the lead cascade of The American Centrifuge Demonstration Facility in Piketon, Ohio in two zero zero five comprised the first publically visible component of next-generation uranium enrichment technology in the United States that employs a gas centrifuge process rather than gaseous diffusion to produce enriched uranium. Piketon is expected to exhibit a growth economy during the early two one st Century with the establishment of a USEC commercial uranium enrichment plant by two zero one zero .

'''Aurora''' is a city located in Portage County, Ohio, United States. It is co-extant with, and formed from, the former township of Aurora, which was formed from the Connecticut Western Reserve. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one three , five five six .

 Geography 
Aurora is located at four one  one nine ' nine  North, eight one  two one ' two one  West ( four one . three one nine two five four , - eight one . three five five eight five nine ). It borders or touches the following other townships and municipalities:

 The city of Streetsboro, on the south;
 The city of Hudson, on the southwest;
 Twinsburg Township, Summit County, on the west;
 The village of Reminderville, on the north-northwest;
 The city of Solon, on the northwest (touches, but does not border);
 Bainbridge Township, Geauga County, on the north;
 Auburn Township, Geauga County, on the northeast (touches, but does not border);
 Mantua Township, on the east;
 Shalersville Township, on the southeast (touches, but does not border)

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of six two . four km ( two four . one mi ).  six zero . one km ( two three . two mi ) of it is land and two . three km ( zero . nine mi ) of it is water. The total area is three . six one % water.

History
From its start as pioneer town to a thriving suburb, Aurora has seen many changes in its two zero zero years. Before one seven nine nine , Aurora was merely a spot on the map of the Connecticut Western Reserve, a parcel of land drawn in a lottery by members of the Big Beaver Land Co. comprised of citizens of Suffield, Connecticut.

The new landowners contracted Capt. Ebenezer Sheldon, a former Revolutionary War soldier, to settle their land and act as their agent. Having suffered business reversals, Sheldon at age four five looked to the Western Reserve for a fresh start.

Leaving his family behind, Sheldon traveled the south route to Ohio through Pittsburgh and had the distinction of being the first white man to enter the township for the purpose of settling.

The site of Sheldon's first log cabin, built with the help of Elias Harmon, lies east on Pioneer Trail near the edge of the township on prime property straddling the Chagrin River. After carving out a bit of civilization in the wilderness, Sheldon retrieved his family from Connecticut and they became the first family in Aurora.

For three years the Sheldon's nearest neighbors were in other townships. Eventually, more pioneers moved west, lured by stories that trickled east and told of rich soil, abundant game and powerful waterfalls to run mills.

They came by wagon and ox cart through Pittsburgh as Sheldon had done, or through New York and down rivers to Aurora, their dreams of a land of milk and honey packed with their precious few possessions.

Seventy-two people came in one eight zero seven alone, beginning the exodus that would carve roads from forests and sprout cabins throughout the township.

Much of the township's settlement edged the three main roads of Aurora, the first being the Cleveland-Warren Road (Pioneer Trail and Route four three north), constructed in one eight zero two by Ebenezer Sheldon.

The second was the Chillicothe Turnpike, which began at Lake Erie, splitting the small towns it passed through as it ran south until it reached Aurora, where it swerved southwest to Hudson and ended at the state capital of Chillicothe. The local segment is now called Aurora-Hudson Road.

The third was Bissell and David (Old Mill) roads. By opening up landlocked property for settlement through road construction, the Connecticut Land Co. encouraged purchasers of the land to actually settle and not just hold the property for speculation.

The Golden Age of Cheese between one eight five five and one nine one zero was responsible for developing Aurora into a well-established town. In one nine two nine , The village of Aurora was founded in the center of the former Aurora Township. By one nine seven one , Aurora took on city status after growing to more than six , zero zero zero residents in the one nine seven zero U.S. Census.

Many of the gracious buildings and century homes built during the time when cheese was king still stand today, giving Aurora its historic character and reflecting life as it was in the Western Reserve.

Aurora remained a Western Reserve farming community until the early one nine six zero s. About that time, interest grew in the potential for suburban residential development due to the community proximity to the major Cleveland and Akron, Ohio metropolitan areas. During the nine zero s, the population has increased by over six zero %, and it continues to experience substantial growth. Most housing development has been higher-priced, single-family homes and condominiums. Auroras desire to maintain its heritage has prompted community leaders to establish and maintain architectural standards to comply and be compatible with the Western Reserve architectural style.

 '''Kent''' is a located in Portage County, Ohio, United States. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two seven , nine zero six . Kent is home to the main campus of Kent State University. Nearby metropolitan areas include Akron, Cleveland, and Canton. Kent is included in the Akron metropolitan area for census purposes.

 History 
Although European settlers had begun settling in the area by the one seven zero zero s, Kent was founded in one eight zero five by John Haymaker, who moved west from Pittsburgh and settled on the banks of the Cuyahoga River. After Haymaker built a gristmill, two villages quickly sprung up. The upper village was named '''Carthage''' and the lower village was named '''Franklin Mills'''. The region was formerly inhabited by various tribes of American Indians, and around one seven eight zero the Indian fighter Captain Samuel Brady achieved notoriety for his activities in the area, including his famous leap over the Cuyahoga River to avoid capture.

When construction began on the Pennsylvania and Ohio Canal in the one eight three zero 's, land speculation was rampant in many areas of Northeast Ohio along the canal, including Franklin Mills and Carthage. As a result of this, an industrial and business region was established along the river in what is now downtown Kent.

The era of the canal would be relatively short-lived. In one eight six three a local businessman by the name of Marvin Kent was influential in bringing the Atlantic Tree City . Another of the city's oldest businesses, the Williams Brothers Mill, was also founded in the late one eight zero zero s; now operating under the name Star of the West, it is a flour mill specializing in the preparation of custom-ground wheat flours. In the mid-twentieth century, two factories produced buses, delivery trucks, and other similar vehicles, but these factories went out of business by the late two zero th century.

In one nine one zero , the Kent State Normal School was established as a college for training public school teachers. The school was later renamed Kent State University after it received authorization to issue bachelor of arts and bachelor of science degrees.

The one nine three zero 's brought the Great Depression and the closing of the railroads through Kent. By this time, however, Kent State University was firmly established and today nearly the entire Kent economy is in some way associated with the university.

On May four , one nine seven zero , four students were killed and nine were wounded by the National Guard at the Kent State shootings.

Today, Kent has a relatively diverse population, due in part to the university, as well as a downtown area which is slowly growing and recovering from a period of relative nondevelopment. Currently, a recently finished renovation of the old dam on the Cuyahoga River, new condominiums, a new library project, and a plan to new blocks of businesses to the downtown district are planned in and around the historical city center.

 Geography 
Location of Kent, Ohio

Kent is located at four one  nine ' two  North, eight one  two one ' four zero  West ( four one . one five zero four two three , - eight one . three six one one zero nine ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two two . six km ( eight . seven mi ).  two two . five km ( eight . seven mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two three % water.

As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two seven , nine zero six people, nine , seven seven two households, and four , seven nine eight families residing in the city. The population density is one , two three nine . nine km ( three , two one two . three mi ). Geographical features
The Tom S. Cooperrider-Kent Bog State Nature Preserve, located on the southern edge of Kent, is one of the most intact bogs in Ohio, with the largest stand of tamarack trees. As of two zero zero five , it is threatened by development of the forest just to its north.

 Interesting facts 
Kent was the first Tree City and is referred to as The Tree City on some signs seen upon entering the city. There are tree logos on Kent's street signs.

Kent is noted for its unusual local population of black squirrels, brought to the area in one nine six one by Larry Woodell from Canada while superintendent of grounds at Kent State ( source). Since this time, the black squirrels have multiplied rapidly and spread in and around Kent.

In one nine nine five , the city of Kent's municipal (tap) water won first place at the fifth annual Toast to the Tap International Water Tasting and Competition held in Berkeley Springs, West Virginia.

 Originally, before naming the city after Marvin Kent, city leaders were considering the name Rockton (hence the name of the Masonic lodge as Rockton Lodge) due to the rocky banks of the Cuyahoga River.

Kent has been a sister city to Dudince, Slovakia, since two zero zero three .

Education
Elementary and secondary schooling is provided by the Kent City School District, with five elementary schools: Holden, Longcoy, Franklin, Davey, and Walls; the recently completed Stanton Middle School, and Theodore Roosevelt High School. Theodore Roosevelt High School in Kent has been given the United States Department of Education Excellence in Education award. St. Patrick School is a parochial institution for grades K- eight . Kent State University is the major institution of post-secondary education in the area.

 Famous residents 
Anti-slavery crusader John Brown lived in Kent (then called Franklin Mills) c. one eight three five - three seven .
John Davey, founder of Davey Tree Expert Company and local philanthropist
Martin L. Davey, U.S. Representative and Governor of Ohio for two terms 
 Playwright and director Vincent J. Cardinal was raised in Kent and graduated from Kent State University.
The Egyptian-born composer Halim El-Dabh has made Kent his home since one nine six nine .
The Six Parts Seven (indie rock band)

Many now-famous or successful people have attended or graduated from Kent State University, among them Drew Carey, Arsenio Hall, Michael Keaton, and members of Devo. (See Kent State University Famous Alumni for a longer list).

 Sports 
The Kent State University Men's and Women's Basketball teams have been successful in the Mid-American Conference within the last decade, advancing to the NCAA championships several times. 

 Kent is home to the Kent Twisters, a member of the Pennsylvania-Ohio Women's Hockey Association (POWHA), an adult amateur women's ice hockey travel league. Kent has been consistent throughout their membership in the POWHA, but strong goaltending led them to finish second in the league in two zero zero four losing to the Cleveland Blues in the Championship game. Kent is also a member of the Northeast Ohio Women's Hockey Organization(NOWHO), a regional ice hockey league for women.

 Education 
Mantua hosts four public education facilities:   
 Crestwood High School, the ''Red Devils'' (grades nine to one two )
 Crestwood Middle School (grades six to eight )
 Crestwood Intermediate School (grades three to five )
 Crestwood Primary School (grades K to two )


The Crestwood Local School System provides education for the communities of Mantua, Hiram and Shalersville. The Hiram and Shalersville primary schools were recently consolidated into the Crestwood Primary and Intermediate schools.

Jack Lambert, a renowned football player with the NFL, was born in Mantua and was a graduate of Crestwood High School. The high school's football stadium is named ''Lambert Stadium'' in honor of his achievements.

Crestwood High School is part of the Portage Trail Conference, originally known as the Portage County League, which is a group of schools that compete in sporting events and intellectual competitions.

 Community events 
Mantua hosts the Potato Festival, a celebration that has occurred annually for over three zero years. The festival features live entertainment, food, rides, a parade, a one five k marathon (the Potato Stomp), and varying special attractions. Past special events included the world's largest serving of Mashed Potatoes and Gravy (they were mashed in a cement mixer), and Spud Wrestling (mud wrestling in a massive ring full of mashed potatoes).

The Ox Roast is another annual event that is a fund-raiser for the St. Joseph Church.

'''Streetsboro''' is a city located in Portage County, Ohio, United States. It is formed from the former township of Streetsboro, which was formed from the Connecticut Western Reserve. It is nearly co-extant with the former Streetsboro Township; the village of Sugar Bush Knolls, Ohio was also formed in part from a small portion of the former township. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one two , three one one .

 Geography 
Streetsboro is located at four one  one four ' three three  North, eight one  two zero ' five seven  West ( four one . two four two four five five , - eight one . three four nine one two four ). It borders or touches the following other townships and municipalities:

 Franklin Township, on the south;
 The village of Sugar Bush Knolls, also on the south;
 The city of Stow, on the southwest (touches, but does not border)
 The city of Hudson, on the west;
 Twinsburg Township, Summit County, on the northwest;
 The city of Aurora, on the north;
 Mantua Township, on the northeast (touches, but does not border);
 Shalersville Township, on the east;
 Ravenna Township, on the southeast (touches, but does not border)

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of six three . one km ( two four . four mi ).  six two . two km ( two four . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . nine km ( zero . four mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . four eight % water.

 History 
Long before settlers moved into the Western Reserve, Seneca Indians roamed this land known as Streetsboro. They used Old Portage Trail, which crosses the southwest corner of the city, to go from Lake Erie to the Ohio River basin. 

The founder of Streetsboro Township was Titus Street from Connecticut, in one seven nine eight . Streetsboro Township contained one five , two seven nine acres. The land was surveyed by Ralph Cowles and Lemuel Punderson in the summer of one eight two two and divided into lots of one zero zero acres. They were appointed agents by Titus Street.

In one eight two five , a turnpike from Cleveland to Wellsville, Ohio (better known as State Route one four ) was laid by Frederick Wadsworth, Samuel Cowles, John Strauyhen and Titus Street. Street agreed to give enough land to make it through the township. In one eight two seven , the turnpike was completed.

Major growth occurred in Streetsboro with the opening of the Ohio Turnpike on October one , one nine five five , with Exit one three (now known as Exit one eight seven ) initially being the only interchange in Portage County. By one nine five seven , with the growth of the automobile industry, Streetsboro experienced a population explosion. Proximity to the Akron and Cleveland areas, direct access to Interstate eight zero (Ohio Turnpike), Interstate four eight zero (Ohio) and State Routes three zero three , four three and one four have greatly contributed to the rapid growth of manufacturing, distribution, commercial and residential development in the past fifty years.

In one nine six eight , voters decided to merge the township and the village to become one city consisting of two five square miles. Streetsboro was primarily a farming community until one nine seven zero .

There are four , nine zero eight households out of which three one . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five five . three % are married couples living together, nine . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three one . one % are non-families. two five . one % of all households are made up of individuals and five . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four nine and the average family size is three . zero zero .

In the city the population is spread out with two four . three % under the age of one eight , eight . three % from one eight to two four , three five . eight % from two five to four four , two one . eight % from four five to six four , and nine . eight % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Windham''' is a village located in the United States; within Portage County in the state of Ohio. It is formed from portions of Windham Township, one of the original townships of the Connecticut Western Reserve. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of two , eight zero six . In one nine four two , the US government chose Windham as the site of an army camp for workers at the newly-built Ravenna Arsenal. As a result, Windham experienced the largest increase in population of any municipality in the United States between the one nine four zero and one nine five zero censuses: The population increased from three one six residents to three , nine four six . (Windham Exempted Village School District ( one nine nine eight ). History of the Windham Schools Retrieved July two nine  two zero zero four .)

History
In one eight one one , a group of sixteen men and an unknown number of women and children travelled from Becket, Massachusetts to the unoccupied survey township immediately south of Nelson Township in the Connecticut Western Reserve. This new township, known today as Windham Township, was survey town four in range six of the Western Reserve. The group of sixteen were known as the '''Becket Company''', after the town from which they departed for this land, although they originally came from Windham, Connecticut.

The township was originally named Strongsburg, after Caleb Strong, then Governor of Massachusetts. However, given Governor Strong's opposition to the War of one eight one two , which settlers in northern Ohio had strong reason to support, the name quickly fell into disfavor with the new settlers. The township was renamed Sharon, and in one eight two zero the township was renamed once again to Windham, after the Becket Company's town of origin.

The Village of Windham was incorporated in one eight nine two , and in one nine nine three the village officially withdrew from Windham Township.

 Geography 
Location of Windham, Ohio

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of five . five km ( two . one mi ).  five . five km ( two . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , eight zero six people, nine five nine households, and seven two nine families residing in the village. There are one , one four three housing units at an average density of two zero eight . two km ( five three eight . two mi ). The average household size is two . nine three and the average family size is three . three one .

In the village the population is spread out with three five . nine % under the age of one eight , one zero . two % from one eight to two four , two nine . two % from two five to four four , one seven . zero % from four five to six four , and seven . seven % who are six five years of age or older.  Schools 
Twin Valley South Elementary School, Lanier Township Middle School(closed), Twin Valley South Middle School, Twin Valley South High School

External Link: www.tvs.k one two .oh.us

 Local Events 

The village is home to several traditional events held annually, which includes the Oktoberfest.
Held at Peace Park on US three five , music, food and crafts are always main attractions at the event, which opens with classic German music performed from inside the gazebo at the park.
Also drawing a large crowd are the country cloggers and two-steppers. These local groups entertain the crowd on an outdoor stage as contemporary country music and classics are played while dancers perform.
The second day of the festival always brings out antique car lovers as the Antique Car Run begins its trek through the county on Sunday afternoon. Car lovers can also enjoy other classic vehicles on Saturday as cars throughout the area are lined up along the back of the park for spectators to enjoy.

Another favorite is the Santa's Villa, located on East Dayton Street. Santa's Villa is opened early in December and visitors can enjoy the sights and sounds of Christmas near the village's Peace Park.

 Historical Buildings 

Two buildings in the village are on the National Register the George Unger home and the old hotel.

Early History

Independence was laid out on the northwest quarter of Section two zero , January one two , one eight four eight , by Daniel Spohn. In the early days of its existence it was nicknamed Spohntown  and  Squeelgut, but was named Independence by Thomas B. Andrews, rather in a spirit of defiance at the attitude of Bellville, which was not a friendly one to the aspiring village. The name was changed to Butler in the one eight seven zero 's. Andrews was its first Postmaster, and, before the town was laid out, kept the office in his house near the site. After the town was laid out and a warehouse erected, he moved the office into the warehouse. The land upon which the town stands was entered on the one three th of May, one eight two zero : by William Simmons. The town plat was surveyed by Joseph Hastings. Mr. Andrews was instrumental in getting the town established and laying it out. taking a lot for pay.

The first store was started by William Lamley, who kept groceries and whisky. It may be remarked here that Independence is a temperance town, and will not allow (since the Bowersox affair mentioned in another chapter) any saloon to exist in the place. Lamley's store was a small frame building, near the rail road, in the north end of the town. He afterward erected a building, which is now occupied by Downing as a store, and started a. hotel. Joseph Geary kept this hotel. the first in the place. David Teeter erected a second hotel. John Diltz, a carpenter and present Postmaster, erected the next dwelling, and shortly after, Daniel Garber erected a shoe-shop on Main street. William Clapper erected the next building and kept boarders.

Gen. G. A. Jones came up from Mount Vernon, erected a warehouse, started a store and dealt in produce. In one eight five six , I. W. Pearce purchased the warehouse of Jones, conducted the business. and was also railroad agent. This gentleman at present keeps the principal store in the place, and does what banking business is necessary.

When the town was laid out, the schoolhouse a frame was a short distance south of town. 

In one eight six eight , the present building was erected. It is a two-story frame, and occupied by two teachers and about one hundred pupils.

In one eight seven seven , the village was incorporated, the first Mayor being J. M. McLaughlin; the second and present Mayor, George W. McBee.

There are four dry-goods and grocery stores, one hardware, one stove and tin, and several smaller establishments; two churches, one hotel, and a proper proportion of mechanics and professional men. The population is about four hundred. The place stands in a great land in the Baltimore The History of Richland County by A. A. Graham one eight eight zero

 Downtown Mansfield
'''Mansfield''' is the largest city and county seat of Richland County, Ohio. According to the two zero zero four United States Census, the city had a total population of five zero , five five seven .

Mansfield's twin cities are Mansfield, England and Funehiki, Japan. Mansfield's official nickname is The Heart of Ohio . Mansfield is also known as the Carrousel Capital of Ohio .

 Geography 
Location of Mansfield, Ohio
Mansfield is located at four zero  four five ' one seven  North, eight two  three one ' two two  West ( four zero . seven five four eight five six , - eight two . five two two eight five five ).

Aerial photo with points of interest
According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of seven seven . five km ( two nine . nine mi ). All of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.




 History 
The city was founded in one eight zero eight and named for Jared Mansfield, the U.S. surveyor-general who directed its planning. It was incorporated as a village in one eight two eight and as a city in one eight five seven . The area that is now Richland County, so named for the fertility of its soil, and the City of Mansfield were first settled in one eight zero zero . The city grew towards the north and the west. The first courthouse in the country was one of two blockhouses erected on the public square during the war of one eight one two .

Mansfield associates itself with many famous names such as John Chapman, better known as Johnny Appleseed; as well as Pulitzer Prize winning author, Louis Bromfield. Chapman found the fertile land of Ohio ideal for his nurseries. The heartland of Chapman's nurseries was located along the stream valleys between Mansfield and Loudonville, just east of Interstate seven one . Many of his orchards and nurseries are still found in Mansfield and the surrounding county. As a child, author Louis Bromfield played at his aunt's house, Oak Hill, in a neighborhood of Mansfield. The gothic house, built in one eight four seven , served as the inspiration for Shane's Castle in his one nine two four novel The Green Bay Tree.

The coming of the railroads in one eight four six , followed by the Lincoln Highway in one nine one three , ushered in Mansfield's greatest period of industrial expansion led by the city's nascent farm equipment and stove manufacturing industries, including the Tappan Company. By the late one nine two zero s, Westinghouse became the city's largest employer, specializing in electric lighting, industrial heating and engineering, and home appliances.

However, like many Rust Belt cities, Mansfield saw a precipitous decline in its manufacturing and retail sectors. Beginning with the Steel Recession of the one nine seven zero 's, the loss of jobs to overseas manufacturing, prolonged labor disputes, and deteriorating factory facilities all contributed to heavy industry leaving the area. Westinghouse, Tappan, and many other manufacturing plants were either bought-out, relocated or closed, leaving only the AK Steel Plant in Mansfield and the General Motors Fisher Body Stamping Plant in Ontario as the last two remaining heavy industry employers. The AK Steel Plant, formerly Armco Steel, was the location of a violent three -year United Steelworkers Union lock-out and strike from one nine nine nine to two zero zero two .

With the loss of the jobs, locally owned businesses in downtown Mansfield closed, as did much of the retail built in the one nine six zero 's along Park Avenue West (formerly known as The Miracle Mile ) and Lexington Avenue. New big-box retail and franchise restaurants have been built in the adjacent suburban city of Ontario, Ohio, which has replaced Mansfield as the major economic and retail center for Richland County and North-Central Ohio.

County library in Mansfield.

 Media 
 Mansfield's only daily newspaper is the Mansfield News Journal.
 Mansfield's first AM-radio station ( one nine two nine ) was WJW, now in Cleveland. Its studio and transmitter were on the ninth floor of the Richland Trust Building.
 Mansfield's notable radio stations are WYHT( one zero five . three FM) poprock (clear channel), WMAN ( one four zero zero AM) newstalk (clear channel), and WVNO( one zero six . one FM), Mansfield's light-rock station.
 Mansfield's only local television station is WMFD-digital television in Northern Ohio (most Mansfield residents watch Cleveland or Columbus stations for network programming.)

Colleges and Universities
 ''' Ohio State University''' has a regional campus at Mansfield, built in the early one nine six zero 's.
 ''' North Central State College''', a community college, shares the Mansfield campus with Ohio State.

Transportation
Three railroads eventually served Mansfield, and two serve it today. The Mansfield Ohio Market Route three .  This route was chosen in one nine one three to become part of the historical '''Lincoln Highway''' which was America's first transcontinental road, connecting New York City to San Francisco. The arrival of the Lincoln Highway to Mansfield was a major influence on the development of the city. Upon the advent of the federal numbered highway system in one nine two eight , the Lincoln Highway through Mansfield on Park Avenue East and Park Avenue West became U.S. Highway three zero .

On September one st, one nine two eight , the Lincoln Highway was marked coast-to-coast with approximately three zero zero zero concrete posts set by the Boy Scouts of America. Each post featured a medallion of Abraham Lincoln's profile. One of these concrete markers was erected at curbside in front of Central Methodist Episcopal Church, four three zero Park Avenue West. Today, a replica marker stands in downtown's Central Park, on Park Avenue's center divider. 

Today, Mansfield serves as a transportation hub and is connected by eight major highways:

 Interstate seven one , which connects Columbus to the southwest with Cleveland to the northeast.
 U.S. Highway three zero (the Lincoln Highway), which connects Wooster to the east with Ontario and Bucyrus to the west.
 U.S. Highway four two , which connects Lexington to the southwest with Ashland to the northeast.
 Ohio State Highway one three , which connects Bellville to the south with Norwalk to the north.
 Ohio State Highway three nine , which connects Shelby to the northwest with Lucas to the southeast.
 Ohio State Highway three zero nine , which connects Ontario and Galion to the west.
 Ohio State Highway four three zero , which connects Ontario to the west with Mifflin to the east.
 Ohio State Highway five four five , which connects Olivesburg and Savannah to the northeast.

Mansfield is served by Richland County Transit (RCT), a bus line that serves downtown and the Mansfield-Ontario area.

Mansfield is served by Mansfield Lahm Airport, a city-owned and operated, joint usage facility with global ties, located about four miles north of downtown.

 The Highway Safety Foundation 

From the one nine five zero s through the one nine seven zero s, Mansfield was the home of the infamous ''' Highway Safety Foundation''', the organization that created the controversial driver's education films that featured actual film photography taken at fatal automobile accidents in the Mansfield area. The films include '''''Signal three zero ''''', '''''Mechanized Death''''', '''''Wheels of Tragedy''''', '''''Highways of Agony''''' among many others. The Highway Safety Foundation also created other controversial education films, including '''''The Child Molestor''''', and '''''Camera Surveillance''''' (AKA ''Mansfield, Ohio Tearoom Busts'').

 '''Ontario''' is a city located in Richland County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five , three zero three . Ontario is a major regional retail center serving the entire North-Central Ohio area.

Location of Ontario, Ohio

Ontario is located at four zero  four six ' eight  North, eight two  three six ' one one  West ( four zero . seven six eight nine zero six , - eight two . six zero three zero six six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two eight . three km ( one zero . nine mi ).  two eight . three km ( one zero . nine mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

Males have a median income of $ four one , zero five three versus $ two six , two five zero for females. The per capita income for the village is $ two two , zero one six .  six . two % of the population and six . zero % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one one . six % of those under the age of one eight and three . five % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 History 
The original town of Ontario started as a settlement in Springfield Township between Mansfield and Bucyrus. In one eight three four , the settlement combined with another small settlement known as New Castle to became the village of Ontario.

Ontario is located on a major east-west transportation corridor that was originally known in the early one nine zero zero s as Ohio Market Route three .  This route was chosen in one nine one three to become part of the historical Lincoln Highway which was America's first transcontinental road, connecting New York City to San Francisco. The arrival of the Lincoln Highway to Ontario was a major influence on the development of the town. Upon the advent of the federal numbered highway system in one nine two eight , the Lincoln Highway through Ontario became U.S. Highway three zero .

In one nine five eight , General Motors built a large Fisher Body stamping plant in Ontario and the residents voted to incorporate the village.

In one nine six zero , the new Ontario High School was built, complete with an indoor swimming pool, a theatre, three shops, and numerous high-tech classrooms and labs for college-preparatory studies. New school construction and renovation has continued over the years, and today the Ontario School District enjoys a long and distinguished reputation for education excellence with state-of-the-art facilities.

In one nine six nine , North-Central Ohio's first modern enclosed mall was built in Ontario, the Richland Mall, which was anchored by the prestigious Lazarus Department Store (based in Columbus), by the O'Neils Department Store (based in Akron) and by Sears. The Lazarus store was the first Lazarus built outside of Columbus. The store's unique high-hat entrance tower remains visible for miles along U.S. Highway three zero . Today, the renamed Westfield Richland Shoppingtown Mall is home to almost seven zero stores and is anchored by Macy's (the old Lazarus store), Kaufmann's (the old O'Neils store), Sears, and JCPenney (a later addition to the mall). ''See Commerce below.'' 

The arrival of both General Motors and the Richland Mall to Ontario was the beginning of the eventual shift of commerce and industry from the adjacent rust belt city of Mansfield to the new suburbia of Ontario.

Several annexations have been made to Ontario since its incorporation and millions of dollars have been spent on public infrastructure including streets, water and sewer facilities, parks, schools, and new civic buildings for Administrative offices, Public Safety Departments and the Water Department. The city administration offices have been housed in several different locations including the Old Library which is now being used as a Senior Center. In one nine eight six , the city's offices were moved to the newly constructed Charles K. Hellinger Municipal Building.

As of two zero zero zero , with a population of five , three zero three , Ontario became a city.

Since the one nine six zero 's, Ontario has been a location of choice for residential development, with its progressive civic administration, an excellent school system, and a healthy tax base from significant commercial and industrial development.

 Transportation 
Ontario is connected by four major highways:

 U.S. Highway three zero (the Lincoln Highway), which connects Mansfield and Interstate seven one to the east with Bucyrus to the west. 
 Ohio State Highway three zero nine , which connects Mansfield to the east with Galion to the west.
 Ohio State Highway three one four , which connects Shelby to the north with Chesterville to the south.
 Ohio State Highway four three zero (Park Avenue West) connecting Ontario to downtown Mansfield.
Busy thoroughfares in Ontario are:
 Park Avenue West (east-west)
 West Fourth Street (east-west)
 Walker Lake Road (east-west)
 Millsboro Road (east-west)
 Home Road (north-south) along the eastern city limits at Mansfield
 Lexington-Springmill Road (north-south) connecting Springmill and Ohio State Highway three nine to the north with Lexington to the south.
Although Ontario only has a population of about five , three zero zero people, it has two four traffic lights within its city limits, including one four alone on Lexington-Springmill Road, the major thoroughfare through the city's popular retail and restaurant district.

 Commerce 
Ontario has developed into a major regional retail center serving the entire North-Central Ohio area. The Westfield Richland Shoppingtown Mall, built in one nine six nine as the Richland Mall with original anchor stores Lazarus, O'Neils and Sears, now has almost seven zero stores including the current anchors Macy's, Kaufmann's, Sears, and JCPenney. Other major retailers located in Ontario include Kohl's, Burlington Coat Factory, Old Navy, Circuit City, Best Buy, Target, Toys R Us, Tj Maxx, Wal-Mart, Meijer, Lowe's, Home Depot, Michaels, Office Max, Staples, Bed Bath & Beyond, PetSmart, Barnes & Noble Booksellers, and many others.

Franchise restaurants in Ontario include, Olive Garden, Red Lobster, Outback Steakhouse, Denny's, Bob,Evans, Applebee's, Cheddar's, Fire Mountain, TGI Friday's, O'Charley's, Ruby Tuesday, Brown Derby Road House, Fazoli's, Chipotle, McDonald's, Wendy's, Taco Bell, Arby's, Burger King, Steak n Shake, Skyline Chili, Dunkin Donuts, and many others.

Cinemas located in Ontario include the Cinemark one four , the Springfield Square Cinemas, and the historic Sunset Drive-In Theater on the old Lincoln Highway.
