 Shrine of Bah'u'llh

'''Mrz Husayn-'Al''' (Persian:   ) (b: one eight one seven - d: one eight nine two ), who later took the title of '''Bah'u'llh''' ( The Glory of God in Arabic) was the founder and prophet of the Bah' Faith. 

He claimed to fulfill the Bb prophecy of He whom God shall make manifest , but in a broader sense he also claimed to be the Messenger of God prophesied in all great religious traditions. He said that this day is the king of days, for which the soul of every Prophet of God, of every Divine Messenger, hath thirsted, and that In this most mighty Revelation, all the Dispensations of the past have attained their highest, their final consummation.

Bah'u'llh authored many religious works, most notably the ''Kitb-i-Aqdas'' and the ''Book of Certitude''. He died in Mansion of Bahj, Palestine, present day Israel, and is buried there.

''Note: A photograph of Bah'u'llh can be found at the end of this article.''

Early life
Background
Bah'u'llh was born on November one two , one eight one seven , in Tehran, Persia, the modern capital city of Iran. His father was Mrz Buzurg of Nur (in the province of Mazandaran), a distinguished nobleman from the court of Fath Ali Shah, the king of Persia.

As a young child, Bah'u'llh was privately tutored and was known for his intelligence. He was a devout Muslim, and by the age of one three or one four he discussed intricate religious matters with leading ulema.

Bah'u'llh's father, Mirza Buzurg served as vizier to Imam-Virdi Mirza, the twelfth son of Fath-'Ali Shah of the Qajar tribe. Mirza Buzurg was later appointed governor of Burujird and Lorestan. (Balyuzi) He was stripped of those positions during a government purge when Muhammad Shah came to power. After his father died, Bah'u'llh was asked to take a government post by the new vizier Haji Mirza Aqasi, but declined.

Marriage and family

Bah'u'llh had three concurrent wives by the names of Asiyih (Navvb), Fatimih (Mahd-i-'Ulya) and Gawhar. His third wife Gawhar was a maid of his first wife Asiyih, and some sources say he had only two wives. Bah'u'llh had fourteen children, only seven of whom lived to adulthood.

Bah'u'llh and his first wife Navvb were known as the Father of the Poor and the Mother of Consolation for their extraordinary generosity and regard for the impoverished. (Blomfield)

Bb movement
Acceptance of the Bb
At the age of two eight , Bah'u'llh received a messenger telling him of the Bb, which he accepted, becoming a Bb. Bah'u'llh began to spread the new cause, especially in his native province of Nur, becoming recognized as one of its most influential believers. (Dawnbreakers)

The accompanying government suppression of the Bb's religion resulted in Bah'u'llh's imprisonment twice and bastinado torture once.

Attempt on the life of the Shah
The Bb was martyred in one eight five zero by a firing squad in Tabriz, which instigated an assassination attempt of the King of Persia, Nasser-al-Din Shah, two years later by a handful of angry Bbs. Although the assassins claimed they were working alone, the entire Bb community was blamed, and a slaughter of several thousand Bbs followed. 

An Austrian officer, Captain von Goumoens, working in the court of the Shah at the time, gave the following account after signing his resignation:
: I saw ones who, with gouged-out eyes, must eat, on the scene of the deed, their own amputated ears; or whose teeth are torn out with inhuman violence by the hand of the executioner; or whose bare skulls are simply crushed by blows from a hammer... 
: As for the end itself, they hang the scorched and perforated bodies by their hands and feet to a tree head downwards, and now every Persian may try his marksmanship to his hearts content... When I read over again, what I have written, I am overcome by the thought that those who are with you in our dearly beloved Austria may doubt the full truth of the picture, and accuse me of exaggeration. Would to God that I had not lived to see it!... At present I never leave my house, in order not to meet with fresh scenes of horror... I will no longer maintain my connection with the scene of such crimes.
::quoted in ''God Passes By'' p. six five 
See also: ''Persecution of Bah's''

Revelation in the Syh-Chl
Many of the Bbs who were not killed, including Bah'u'llh, were imprisoned in the Syh-Chl (the Black Pit), an underground dungeon of Tehran.

According to Bah'u'llh, it was during his imprisonment in the Syh-Chl that he received a vision of a Maiden from God, through whom he received his mission as a Messenger of God and as the One whose coming the Bb had prophesized. After four months in the Syh-Chl, and after the person who tried to kill the Shah confessed and exonerated the Bbi leaders, the authorities banished Bah'u'llh from Persia. 

Bah'u'llh chose to go to Baghdad, then a city in the Ottoman Empire. Bah's believe that he was banished or exiled out of Persia whilst some sources believe that Bah'u'llh fled for fear of more persecution Maulana, one nine three three . Bah'u'llh's passport shows that he had permission to travel to the Shi'a holy shrines in Iraq.

Baghdad
Banishment from Iran
Bah'u'llh's passport dated January one eight five three 
In one eight five three , with limited supplies and food, and through the cold of winter, Bah'u'llh and his family travelled from Persia to Baghdad.

Mirza Yahya had been appointed by the Bb to lead the Bb community, and had been travelling around Persia in disguise. He decided to go to Baghdad and join the group using funds given to him by Bah'u'llh.

An increasing number of Bb's considered Baghdad the new center for leadership of the Bb Faith, and a flow of pilgrims started coming there from Persia. However, as time went on, people began to look to Mirza Yahya for leadership less and less, and instead saw Bah'u'llh as their leader.

Mirza Yahya, as the appointed leader of the Bbs, started to sow doubt about Bah'u'llh's intentions and further divided the community. The actions of Mirza Yahya drove many people away from the faith and gave its enemies confidence to continue their campaigns. The Bab's religion was declining.

Kurdistan
On April one zero  one eight five four Bah'u'llh, without telling anyone his purpose or destination, left to the mountains of Kurdistan, northeast of Baghdad, near the city Sulaymaniyah. He later wrote that he left so as to avoid becoming the source of disagreement within the Bb community.

For two years Bah'u'llh lived alone in the mountains of Kurdistan. At one point someone noticed his remarkable penmanship, which brought the curiosity of the instructors of the local Sufi orders. As he began to take guests, he became noted for his learning and wisdom. Shaykh 'Uthmn, Shaykh 'Abdu'r-Rahmn, and Shaykh Ism'l, undisputed leaders of the Naqshbandyyih, Qdiryyih, and Khlidyyih Orders respectively, began to seek his advice and admire him. It was to the second of these that the Four Valleys was written. Several other notable books were also written during this time.

News of a wise man living in the mountains under the name of Darvish Muhammad spread to neighbouring areas. When the news of such a man reached Baghdad, Bah'u'llh's family realized who the man was and pleaded with him to come back to Baghdad, which he did.

Return to Baghdad
When Bah'u'llh returned to Baghdad he saw that the Bb community had become disheartened and divided. According to `Abdu'l-Bah, two five people had claimed to be the One promised by the Bb during Bah'u'llh's absence and beforehand.

In the time of Bah'u'llh's absence, and in the coming years, Mirza Yahya had ordered the murder of some of his Bb opponents, including Dayyn, and a cousin of the Bb himself proceeded to marry the widowed wife of the Bb against the clear instructions left by him, and dispatched followers to the province of Nur with the mission of assassinating the Shah.

Bah'u'llh remained in Baghdd for seven more years. During this time, while keeping his perceived station as the Manifestation of God hidden, he taught the Bb's teachings. He published many books and verses, which he called revelations, including the Book of Certitude and the Hidden Words. 

Bah'u'llh's rising prestige in the city, and the revival of the Persian Bb community gained the attention of his enemies in Islamic clergy and the Persian government. They were eventually successful in having the Ottoman government exile Bah'u'llh from Baghdad to Constantinople.



Declaration in the Garden of Ridvan
On April two two  one eight six three , Bah'u'llh left Baghdad and entered the Garden of Ridvn near Baghdad. Bah'u'llh and those accompanying him would stay in the garden for twelve days before departing for Constantinople. It was during his time in the Garden of Ridvn that Bah'u'llh declared to his companions his perceived mission and station as a Messenger of God. Today Bah's celebrate the twelve days that Bah'u'llh in the Garden of Ridvn as the festival of Ridvn.

The eleven years of messianic secrecy that passed between when Bah'u'llh claimed to have seen the Maiden of Heaven in the Syh-Chl and this declaration are referred to by Bah' chroniclers and by Bah'u'llh himself as ''ayyam-i butun'' ( Days of Concealment ). Bah'u'llh stated that this period was a set time of concealment . It was during this period that Bah'u'llh wrote his primary eschatological work the Kitb-i-qn. (Buck, one nine nine eight )

Imprisonment

Constantinople (Istanbul)
As mentioned previously, Bah'u'llh was given an order to relocate to the Ottoman capital of Constantinople. Although not a formal prisoner yet, the forced exile from Baghdad was the beginning of a long process which would gradually move him into further exiles and eventually the penal colony of Akka.

Bah'u'llh and his family, along with a small group of Bbs, stayed in Constantinople for only four months. During this time the Persian Ambassador in the court of the Sultan mounted a systematic campaign against Bah'u'llh. He was thus exiled to Adrianople, but before leaving he wrote a Tablet to the Sultan, the contents of which are unknown, but Shamsi Big, who delivered the letter, gave the following report:
:I know not what that letter contained, for no sooner had the Grand Vizir perused it than he turned the color of a corpse, and remarked: It is as if the King of Kings were issuing his behest to his humblest vassal king and regulating his conduct.
::quoted in ''God Passes By'' p. one six zero 

Adrianople (Edirne)
During the month of December, Bah'u'llh and his family embarked on a twelve-day journey to Adrianople. Bah'u'llh stayed in Adrianople for four and a half years. Mirza Yahya, upon hearing Bah'u'llh's words in a Tablet read to him, challenging him to accept Bah'u'llh's Revelation, offered a counter-claim that he was the one whom the Bb had prophesized about. This caused a break within the Bb community, and the followers of Bah'u'llh became known as Bah's, while the followers of Mirza Yahha became known as Azals. See Bah'Bb split. At one point, Mirza Yahya tried to poison Bah'u'llh. While Bah'u'llh recovered, his hand was left shaking until the end of his life.

Also, while in Adrianople, Bah'u'llh proclaimed the Bah' Faith further by addressing Tablets to the kings and rulers of the world including: 

 Pope Pius IX
 Emperor Napoleon III of France
 Czar Alexander II of Russia
 King Wilhelm I of Prussia
 Queen Victoria of England
 Emperor Franz Joseph of Austria-Hungary
 Sultan Abd-ul-Aziz of the Ottoman Empire
 Nasser-al-Din Shah of the Persian Empire

Akka (Akko, Acre)
Prison Cell of Bah'u'llh, Akk

The disagreements between the Bah's and the Azals allowed the Ottoman and Persian authorities to exile Bah'u'llh once again. One morning, without any notice, soldiers surrounded Bah'u'llh's house and told everyone to get ready to depart to the prison-city of Akk, Palestine. Bah'u'llh and his family left Adrianople on August one two  one eight six eight and after a journey by land and sea arrived in Akk on August three one . The inhabitants of Akk were told that the new prisoners were enemies of the state, of God and his religion, and that association with them was strictly forbidden.

The first years in Akk had very harsh conditions for Bah'u'llh; Mirz Mihd, Bah'u'llh's son, was suddenly killed at the age of twenty-two when he fell through a skylight while pacing back and forth in prayer and meditation. After some time, the people and officials began to trust and respect Bah'u'llh's, and thus the conditions of the imprisonment were eased and eventually, after the Sultan Abd-ul-Aziz's death, he was allowed to leave the city and visit nearby places.

Final years

Bahji
The corner of the shrine where Bah'u'llh is buried.
The final years of Bah'u'llh's life were spent in the Mansion of Bahji, just outside Akk, even though he was still formally a prisoner of the Ottoman Empire. During his years in Akk and Bahji, Bah'u'llh produced many volumes of work including the Kitb-i-Aqdas. 

In one eight nine zero the Cambridge orientalist Edward Granville Browne had an interview with Bah'u'llh in this house. After this meeting he wrote his famous pen-portrait of Bah'u'llh:

: In the corner where the divan met the wall sat a wondrous and venerable figure, crowned with a felt head-dress of the kind called tj by dervishes (but of unusual height and make), round the base of which was wound a small white turban. The face of him on whom I gazed I can never forget, though I cannot describe it. Those piercing eyes seemed to read one's very soul; power and authority sat on that ample brow; while the deep lines on the forehead and face implied an age which the jet-black hair and beard flowing down in indistinguishable luxuriance almost to the waist seemed to belie. No need to ask in whose presence I stood, as I bowed myself before one who is the object of a devotion and love which kings might envy and emperors sigh for in vain! 
::(''A Travellers Narrative'', Introduction, p.XXXIX-XL)

On May nine  one eight nine two Bah'u'llh contracted a slight fever which grew steadily over the following days, abated, and then finally took his life on May two nine  one eight nine two .

Succession
When Bah'u'llh passed away, he left a Will and Testament, which stated the following in regard to succession:
: The Will of the divine Testator is this: It is incumbent upon the Aghsan, the Afnan and My Kindred to turn, one and all, their faces towards the Most Mighty Branch... Verily God hath ordained the station of the Greater Branch Muhammad Ali to be beneath that of the Most Great Branch Abdul-Bah. He is in truth the Ordainer, the All-Wise. We have chosen the Greater after the Most Great, as decreed by Him Who is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. 
::''Tablets of Bah'u'llh'', p. two two one 

The favor given to `Abdu'l-Bah was a cause of jealousy within Bah'u'llh's family. Muhammad Ali immediately began to claim that the Will was forged, and insisted that he should be the one to lead the Bah' community. This period is considered by Bah's as one of the most difficult tests of the early years of the Faith. 

Due to the conflict with his half brother, `Abdu'l-Bah ex-communicated him as a Covenant-breaker. The division was not long lived. After being alienated by the Bah' community, Muhammad Ali died in one nine three seven with only a handful of followers.

Bah'u'llh's works
Bah'u'llh wrote many books, tablets and prayers. Below are some that have been translated to English:

Photograph


Bah'u'llh
This photograph of Bah'u'llh's is a copy of one of two taken while he was in Adrianople (from William Miller's book on the Bah' Faith). Copies of both pictures are at the Bah' World Centre, and one is on display in the International Archives building, where the Bah's view it as part of an organized pilgrimage. Outside of this experience Bah's prefer to not view this photo in public, even in their private homes. .

Bah'u'llh's image is not offensive to Bah's, but rather treat the image of any Manifestation of God with due respect. For example, copies of the photographs are displayed on highly significant occasions, such as six conferences held in one nine six eight commemorating the centenary of Bah'u'llh's writing of the ''Suriy-i-Mulk'' (Tablet to the Kings), which Shoghi Effendi describes as the most momentous Tablet revealed by Bah'u'llh (''God Passes By'', pp. one seven one ). After a meeting in Edirne (Adrianople), Turkey, the Hands of the Cause travelled to the conferences, 'each bearing the precious trust of a photograph of the Blessed Beauty, which it will be the privilege of those attending the Conferences to view.' (Marks, Geoffry W. (Ed.) ( one nine eight six ). ''Messages of The Universal House of Justice one nine six three to one nine eight six '', p. one zero five .)

The official Bah' position on displaying the photograph of Bah'u'llh is:

: There is no objection that the believers look at the picture of Bah'u'llh, but they should do so with the utmost reverence, and should also not allow that it be exposed openly to the public, even in their private homes. 
::(From a letter written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi to an individual believer, December six , one nine three nine )
::(Compilations, ''Lights of Guidance'', p. five four zero )

While the above passage clarifies that it is considered disrespectful to display his photograph to the public, regarding postings on websites the Bah' World Centre has written:

: For Bah's, the photograph of Bah'u'llh is very precious and it should not only be viewed but also handled with due reverence and respect, which is not the case here. Thus, it is indeed disturbing to Bah's to have the image of Bah'u'llh treated in such a disrespectful way. However, as the creator of the site is not a Bah', there is little, if anything, that can be done to address this matter. We hope these comments have been of assistance. 
::(Office for Public Information, one nine nine nine Sept zero four , Photo of Bah'u'llh on Web Site)

 '''Vea''' is a Puerto Rican gossip magazine that has been published weekly since one nine six eight .

Vea is known for covering everything concerned with actors, actresses, singers, models, dancers, politicians and athletes. Lately, it has also been publishing articles of human interest. In one nine nine four , a discovery by a Vea employee caused a wide international controversy, when the employee ran across some papers that stated Puerto Rico as the birthplace of the famous singer, Luis Miguel, and not Mexico, as it had been widely believed before the discovery.

Vea has been involved in some controversies concerning the privacy of the famous people it writes about, because Vea writes about everything going on in famous people's private lives. But it could be said also, that when some of those famous people have seen their lights begin to turn off, they have gone to Vea for more exposure and fame.

Vea is one of the top gossip magazines in Puerto Rico, along with Artistas, Estrella, Estrellita and Teve Guia.

 '''Bainbridge''' is a village located in Ross County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the village had a total population of one , zero one two .

Location of Bainbridge, Ross County, Ohio

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one . three km ( zero . five mi ).  one . three km ( zero . five mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics

People and Culture
Fairs and Festivals
Chillicothe, rich in Indian history, hosts the annual '''Feast of the Flowering Moon Festival'''. Started in one nine eight four , the festival draws crowds of approximately eight five , zero zero zero . Yoctangee Park, in historic downtown, is the perfect setting for this family oriented three-day event featuring Native American music, dancing, traders and exhibits, a mountain men encampment rendezvous with working craftsmen and demonstrations, an extensive arts and crafts show with over eight zero crafters and commercial exhibits. Entertainment is continuous on the main stage with good food, fun, games and contests for familes to enjoy. This is an educational experience for the entire family. Handicap parking is available at the Feast from the alley of West Water to Walnut Street. Events are FREE to the public and typically include: the Laser Light Show (Friday, Saturday  Crossing near the present Ross County village of Bainbridge.

Massie and a party of three nine men laid out his town in the summer of one seven nine six . When it was completed, he called it Chillicothe, a name derived from the Shawnee word Chalagwatha, which means ''town'' or ''gathering place''. He then advertised his town lots and lands he had surveyed for sale in Virginia and Kentucky newspapers. Congress also authorized the sale of the government-owned lands on the east side of the river. In one seven nine seven , Zane's Trace, a federally funded road, was constructed through Chillicothe, providing an overland route to the east and southwest. The area grew rapidly and by the summer of one seven nine eight , the population was sufficient to warrant the formation of a new county. In August, Arthur St. Clair, governor of the Northwest Territory, created the county of Ross, naming it for his good friend from Pennsylvania, Senator James Ross.

Northwest Territory
Among the Virginians Massie attracted to his settlement were Thomas Worthington and Edward Tiffin. They played dominant roles in the political development of the Ohio Country and made Chillicothe the political center. They led the faction opposed to Governor St. Clair and his Federalist allies who believed in a strong central government which would regulate the development of the country s frontier. Those supporting Worthington and Tiffin thought the people should have a degree of self-determination. The two men knew this was possible only through statehood and concentrated their efforts towards that goal.

Worthington and Tiffin were successful in their efforts. A constitutional convention was held in November one eight zero two in Chillicothe. The town had been made the seat of government for the eastern division of the Northwest Territory when it was divided in one eight zero zero . Congress approved the constitution, and the government for the state of Ohio was organized at Chillicothe, the capital, on March one , one eight zero three . Edward Tiffin had been unanimously elected governor in January, and Worthington was selected by the general assembly to serve as one of Ohio s first two U. S. senators.

Chillicothe served as the capital of Ohio from the beginning of statehood in one eight zero three until one eight zero nine when Zanesville became the capital for three years. The capital moved to Zanesville as part of a deal to get a bill passed in the House of Representatives and the Senate. In one eight one two the capital moved back to Chillicothe until one eight one six when the capital moved to Columbus. Columbus became the capital because of the desire to have the capital in the middle of the state. (Ohio Historical Society)

Thomas Worthington, who has become known as the Father of Ohio Statehood, was elected as the state s sixth governor in one eight one four . Other Chillicotheans who served as Ohio s chief executive were Duncan McArthur, the eleventh governor, and William Allen who served from one eight seven four to one eight seven six . Chillicothe was the state capital until one eight one zero , at which time it was removed to Zanesville. It was returned in one eight one two to remain there until one eight one six , when the new permanent capital at Columbus would be occupied. The Great Seal of Ohio is a constant reminder of Chillicothe s place in the history of the state. As described by the legislative act creating the seal, its background is a representation of Mount Logan to the east of the city as viewed from Adena, Thomas Worthington s home.

Chillicothe was the seat of government during the War of one eight one two , a conflict that was fought on Ohio s borders. The city became an army town when the one nine th U. S. Regiment of Infantry was stationed there. Hundreds of soldiers were encamped in the vicinity. Chillicothe was on the line of march for those troops from the South and East going to and from the theater of war. Almost every family was affected by the war as thousands of Ross countians volunteered to fight the enemy threatening their state s frontier.

Following Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry s defeat of the British fleet on Lake Erie on September one zero , one eight one three , the three zero zero seamen he captured were marched to Chillicothe for confinement. A stockade, which was called Camp Bull, was erected north of town to house them. They spent ten months in the prison camp. A few days before the prisoners of war began the march back to the lake to be exchanged, they witnessed the execution by firing squad of six American soldiers who had been found guilty of desertion.

The town continued to grow and flourish after its years of political influence were over. Settlements in the county Bainbridge, Frankfort, Kingston, Clarksburg, Londonderry, Hallsville, Richmond Dale, Yellow Bud and others also prospered. The Ohio-Erie Canal in one eight three one and the railroad in one eight five one made economic growth possible, and the city and county exported a large variety of agricultural and manufactured goods.

During the Civil War, young men from the county enlisted in the many regiments organized in this part of the state. The seven three rd regiment was organized and trained at Chillicothe. Among its members was Ross County farmer George Nixon III, who was killed during the Battle of Gettysburg. He was the great-grandfather of President Richard M. Nixon.

The county had its share of heroes. Brigadier General Joshua W. Sill, a West Point graduate, was killed at the Battle of Stones River on December three one , one eight six two . His friend General Philip Sheridan named Fort Sill in Oklahoma in his honor. Henry Walke, a career Navy man who rose to the rank of rear admiral, was said to have seen more naval action during the war than any other officer in the navy. While commanding the riverboat Carondolet, he was successful in ending the Confederate s blockade of the Mississippi River. Five men from the county were awarded the Congressional Medal of Honor for heroic action.

On April six , one nine one seven , the United States declared war on Germany. As the country did not have a peacetime army large enough to fight the war, the draft was instituted to fill the ranks. Additional training facilities were needed to prepare the men. Word reached Chillicothe that the government was searching for sites for military camps. Recognizing the economic impact a military camp would have on Chillicothe and Ross County, John A. Poland, Chillicothe attorney and president of the Chamber of Commerce, aggressively sought the location of an army base in the area.

It was announced on June eight , one nine one seven , that Chillicothe had been chosen for a training camp. The site lay north of town, along the Scioto River. The government leased the land approximately two , zero zero zero acres from the farm owners, and on June two nine , construction began. Within two and a half months, the work force that ultimately numbered more than one four , zero zero zero , had erected a camp for four zero , zero zero zero men and one two , zero zero zero horses and mules. Upon completion, there were two , zero zero zero buildings; the cost of construction was $ four , zero zero zero , zero zero zero . The camp was named for Civil War general, William Tecumseh Sherman.

The first draftees and recruits from Ohio and surrounding states arrived at Camp Sherman on September five . By the time the war ended, one two three , five eight one men had received training there. The eight three rd Division was the first to complete its training and left for the front June one nine , one nine one eight . The eight four th Division was trained with that new military weapon the fighter airplane. Two planes were brought in for that purpose. The nine five th and nine six th were on their way to becoming fighting units, but the war ended before they could be deployed.
The influx of construction workers and military trainees and personnel had a tremendous impact on Chillicothe. The population was increased from one six , zero zero zero to six zero , zero zero zero . There was a flurry of housing construction and opening of new businesses. The community made the soldiers and their visiting families welcome.

Two hundred German sailors were confined as prisoners of war at Camp Sherman from July one nine one eight until September one nine one nine . There was quite a scare in the community when twenty-one of the prisoners escaped. Nineteen of them were captured almost immediately; the remaining two were soon found and returned to the camp.

The Spanish influenza epidemic of one nine one eight reached Camp Sherman in September of that year. More than eight , zero zero zero soldiers and personnel were infected and of those, nearly one one zero zero died. Almost two , zero zero zero cases were reported in the city, resulting in thirty-one deaths.

The Ross County economy continues to rely on industry and agriculture. Paper is the leading manufactured product, and the Mead Corporation has been a presence in the community for over a hundred years. Tourism is also important to the region, and there are many attractions for people wanting to know more about the birthplace of Ohio. These include Hopewell Culture National Historic Park, formerly known as Mound City; the Ross County Historical Society s museum, Franklin House, Knoles Log House and McKell Library; the Lucy Webb Hayes Heritage Center, the house in which the wife of President Rutherford B. Hayes was born; the Pump House Center for the Arts; and the Scioto Society s outdoor drama, Tecumseh!

Chillicothe in the Arts
In the novel ''Laughing Gas'' by P.G. Wodehouse, Chillicothe is mentioned several times as the home of child star Joey Cooley. Joey desires escape the constant scrutiny of life in Hollywood and return to his home in Chillicothe where he can eat whatever he likes.

 The Carl D. Perkins Bridge across the Ohio River at Portsmouth
'''Portsmouth''' is a city located in Scioto County, Ohio, at the confluence of the Ohio and Scioto Rivers. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two zero , nine zero nine . It is the county seat of Scioto County. From one nine three zero - one nine three three , it was the home of the Portsmouth Spartans, the NFL franchise that became the Detroit Lions in one nine three four . Shawnee State University is located in Portsmouth.

 Geography 
Location of Portsmouth, Ohio

Portsmouth is located at three eight  four four ' three five  North, eight two  five seven ' five six  West ( three eight . seven four three one eight six , - eight two . nine six five four three six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two eight . six km ( one one . one mi ).  two seven . nine km ( one zero . eight mi ) of it is land and zero . eight km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is two . six two % water.

 Industry 
Portsmouth was a city focused on industry and manufacturing until the one nine seven zero s when a number of companies closed down their factories over labor costs and foreign influence. Since the closure of these factories, Portsmouth has suffered a loss of jobs and revenue. The city is currently trying to promote service businesses. Things were made worse for the city and its government when Martings went out of business in two zero zero two . Then mayor Greg Bauer made a controvrsial deal in buying the building at a high price. Petitions were rounded up to have a recall on the mayor and other city council persons. Bauer was recalled in two zero zero four . 

In November of two zero zero two , the Portsmouth Uranium Enrichment Plant was recognized as an ANS Nuclear Historic Landmark by the American Nuclear Society. It had served a military function from one nine five two until the mid- one nine six zero s when the mission changed from enriching uranium for nuclear weapons to one focused on producing fuel for commercial nuclear power plants. Portsmouth ended enriching operations in two zero zero one and began to support operational and administrative functions and perform external contract work. 

All uranium enrichment in the area was taken over by Portsmouth's sister plant across the Ohio River in Paducah, Kentucky. Uranium enrichment functions had previously been shared by the two plants.  USEC interests in the area remain strong with the American Centrifuge Plant being built in Piketon, Ohio.

In January of two zero zero four , USEC announced the selection of Piketon as the expected site for its future American Centrifuge Plant. This commercial uranium enrichment facility is expected to employ up to five zero zero people and reach an initial annual production level of three . five million SWU by two zero one zero .

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two zero , nine zero nine people, nine , one two zero households, and five , two one six families residing in the city. The population density is seven four nine . six km ( one , nine four one . four mi ). There are one zero , two four eight housing units at an average density of three six seven . four km ( nine five one . five mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine one . five zero % White, five . zero zero % African American, zero . six three % Native American, zero . six one % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . three two % from other races, and one . nine two % from two or more races.  zero . nine three % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are nine , one two zero households out of which two five . nine % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three seven . nine % are married couples living together, one five . six % have a female householder with no husband present, and four two . eight % are non-families. three seven . three % of all households are made up of individuals and one seven . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one nine and the average family size is two . eight seven .

In the city the population is spread out with two two . zero % under the age of one eight , one one . three % from one eight to two four , two five . nine % from two five to four four , two one . two % from four five to six four , and one nine . six % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, two two . five % of those under the age of one eight and six . six % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Football 
In one nine eight nine , the Wheelersburg Pirates won the Division IV state championship in football by defeating the Warren John F. Kennedy Eagles.  The Pirates were led by head coach Ed Miller, who also won two Associated Press state championships at Portsmouth Notre Dame in one nine six seven and one nine seven zero .

The Pirates are members of the Southern Ohio Conference, Division II.  The Burg, as it is affectionately called, has won their conference twenty-six times. In fact, Wheelersburg has captured more conference titles than all other member schools (Lucasville Valley, Minford, Portsmouth West, Scioto Northwest and Waverly) combined.

Making the OHSAA playoffs eighteen times, the Pirates have captured five regional titles, reaching the state playoffs in one nine eight one , one nine eight nine , one nine nine one , one nine nine four and one nine nine eight .

 '''Canton''' is a city located in Stark County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of eight zero , eight zero six , but according to a July one , two zero zero four Census estimate, the population has declined to seven nine , nine zero five . It is the county seat of Stark County.

Canton is home to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. First Ladies National Historic Site is also in the city.

 Geography 
Location of Canton, Ohio

Canton is located at four zero  four eight ' one eight  North, eight one  two two ' three three  West ( four zero . eight zero four nine five eight , - eight one . three seven five seven nine two ).

Canton is bordered by Plain Township and North Canton to the north, Meyers Lake and Perry Township to the west, Canton Township to the South, and Nimishillen Township and Osnaburg Township to the east.


According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of five three . three km ( two zero . six mi).  five three . two km ( two zero . five mi) of it is land and zero . zero five % is water.

 History 

Canton officially became a village in one eight zero five and a city in one eight five four . Bezaleel Wells, the surveyor who divided the land of the town, named it after Canton (now Guangzhou), China. The name was a memorial to a trader named John O'Donnell, whom Wells admired. O'Donnell had named his Maryland plantation after the Chinese city, as he had been the first person to transport goods from there to Baltimore.

 Government
Canton works under a Mayor  Council government. It is the largest city in Ohio to operate without a charter. 

The current Mayor is Janet Weir Creighton(R). 

City council is divided among nine wards with three At- Large Seats and the Council President

 Economy 

The Canton area's economy is primarily industrial, with a significant agricultural segment. The city is home to the Timken Company, a major manufacturer of tapered roller bearings and specialty steel. Other companies that have significant operations are the Hoover Company (vacuums and floor cleaners), the Belden Brick Company (brick and masonry producer), and Diebold (ATMs, electronic voting devices, and bank vaults). LTV Steel (formerly Republic Steel) had historically been large employer, until its bankruptcy in two zero zero zero . Poultry production and dairy farming are also important segments of its economy.

However, like many industrial areas of the United States, employment in the manufacturing sector is in a state of long-term decline. The area is undergoing a transition to a retail- and service-based economy. In two zero zero four Timken Company proposed closing some of their factories in the Canton area, striking a blow to the economy and a bigger blow to city image and pride.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are eight zero , eight zero six people, three two , four eight nine households, and one nine , seven eight five families residing in the city. The population density is one , five one eight . two km ( three , nine three three . zero mi). There are three five , five zero two housing units at an average density of six six seven . zero km ( one , seven two eight . zero mi). The racial makeup of the city is seven four . four five % White, two one . zero four % African American, zero . four nine % Native American, zero . three two % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, zero . six one % from other races, and three . zero six % from two or more races.  one . two four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three two , four eight nine households out of which three zero . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three seven . one % are married couples living together, one nine . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and three nine . one % are non-families. three three . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and one two . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . three nine and the average family size is three . zero four .

In the city the population is spread out with two six . six % under the age of one eight , nine . eight % from one eight to two four , two nine . one % from two five to four four , two zero . two % from four five to six four , and one four . three % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three four years. For every one zero zero females there are eight seven . five males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight one . nine males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two eight , seven three zero , and the median income for a family is $ three five , six eight zero . Males have a median income of $ three zero , six two eight versus $ two one , five eight one for females. Out of the total population, two seven . four % of those under the age of one eight and one one . three % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

Due to Cantons diverse demographic, many pollsters used Canton as a microcosm of the country as a whole. President George W. Bush visited Canton on a number of occasions, as well as Democratic Presidential Nominee and Massachusetts Senator John Kerry in an effort to win Ohio, a vital state in the  two zero zero four Election.

Sports

There is an intense high school football rivalry between the Canton McKinley High School Bulldogs and the Massillon Washington High School Tigers.

The Pro Football Hall of Fame is located in Canton. The American Professional Football Association, the forerunner of the NFL, was founded in a Canton car dealership on September one seven , one nine two zero .

Every summer, Canton holds the Pro Football Hall of Fame Festival, which includes a (hot air) balloon festival, the Ribs Burn-off, fashion show, community parade, Sunday morning race, enshrinenee dinner, the Hoover Pro Football Hall of Fame Grande Parade, and culminates in the enshrinement of the new inductees and then the Hall of Fame Game on the following Monday night between the AFC and the NFC at Fawcett Stadium.

The Canton Invaders of the National Professional Soccer League and American Indoor Soccer Association played home games at the Canton Memorial Civic Center from one nine eight four until one nine nine six , winning five league championships.

Canton was home of the Canton Coyotes, a minor league baseball team which has since moved to Columbia, Missouri and has been renamed the Mid-Missouri Mavericks.
 
New to Canton in two zero zero six - two zero zero seven will be the Canton Firebirds, a women's ice hockey team that will likely compete in the Northest Ohio Women's Hockey Organization (NOWHO) and the Pennsylvania-Ohio Women's Hockey Association (POWHA). The team is now in the process of being formed.

 History 
Louisville was originally spelled Lewisville, which is the German spelling. The name had to be changed due to a conflict with the U.S. Post Office. It is still, however, pronounced the old way rather than like the French-named city Louisville, Kentucky.

 '''Massillon''' is a city located in Stark County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of three one , three two five .

The Friendly Association for Mutual Interests founded Massillon, then called Kendal, on a two , zero zero zero acre estate in response to Robert Owen's success in New Harmony, Indiana to create a utopian society. The group of approximately one five zero people, consisting of farmers, mill workers, and mechanics from the surrounding area, abandoned their communitarian lifestyle.

Football

In Ohio and elseswhere, the name Massillon is probably most associated with the Massillon Washington High School football team, the Tigers  as well as the fanatical sense of pride the town has for it. Distinguished Massillon alumni include Paul Brown and former Ohio State Buckeyes graduate and NFL veteran linebacker Chris Spielman. The Tigers are historically one of the winningest high school football teams in the United States, second only to the Valdosta High School Wildcats, in Valdosta, Georgia. Along with the Canton McKinley High School Bulldogs, the Tigers represent one half of what many consider to be the greatest high school football rivalry in the nation. The two teams meet each Fall in the only high school game in the nation to carry odds in Las Vegas. Both Massillon and their fierce rivalry with Canton are subjects of the documentary film ''Go Tigers!''.

Villages in Ohio
 
   
 
The city of '''Akron''' is the county seat of Summit County in the U.S. State of Ohio. The city is located between Cleveland to the north and Canton to the south. It is located in the Western Reserve in northeastern Ohio on the Cuyahoga River, approximately six zero miles ( one zero zero km) west of the Pennsylvania border. 

It was founded in one eight two five near the Ohio  in one eight nine zero , two seven , six zero one ; in one nine zero zero , four two , seven two eight ; in one nine one zero , six nine , zero six seven ; in one nine two zero (following the increase in the size of the city), two zero eight , four three five ; and in one nine four zero , two four four , seven nine one . As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two one seven , zero seven four . Akron is the eight two nd largest city in the United States and is the five th largest city in Ohio (U.S. Census Bureau, two zero zero one ). Akron has a metropolitan population of six nine four , nine six zero (U.S. Census Bureau, two zero zero zero ). Akron is also part of the larger Cleveland-Akron-Elyria Combined Statistical Area, which was the one four th largest in the country with a population of over two . nine million according to the two zero zero zero Census. 

Alcoholics Anonymous was founded in Akron in one nine three five . The city is home to The University of Akron, the Akron Aeros Double A affiliate of the Cleveland Indians, and the Firestone Country Club, at which the PGA TOUR's Firestone Invitational is annually played. The Akron Quakers, of the ibl( two zero zero five -) will begin play in the two zero zero seven season.

 History 
 Canal years 
Much of Akron's early growth was because of its location at the summit of the Ohio and Erie Canal (thus the name Summit County ) which at one time connected Lake Erie and the Ohio River.

Akron started as a small village on the divide between the St. Lawrence and the Mississippi. The village was a four three -block square with its main intersection at Exchange and Main Streets and a north limit one block beyond State Street. It was renamed South Akron when Cascade, an adjacent village north of State Street and centered on Market and Howard Streets, changed its name to North Akron. 

South Akron was built to serve people using the Ohio Canal. North Akron developed around a construction project originally intended to provide increased water power for industries. In one eight three six the villages joined. The completion of the Cross-cut Canal along Main Street in one eight three nine started Akron on its climb to industrial importantance. Coal, a major railroad, and manufacturing growth from the Civil War, gave the City its next boost with the population jumping from three , five zero zero to one zero , zero zero zero between one eight six zero and one eight seven zero .

Because of physical obstacles  The steep hill on West Market Street, the Little Cuyahoga Valley, and the swamp south of the City  Akron grew to the east. This encouraged the annexation of Spicertown, centered on Spicer and Exchange, and then Middlebury, with its center where the Arlington and Market Street commercial area is now located.

 The Rubber City 
Panorama of Akron, Ohio in one nine one one 
Akrons history and the history of the rubber industry are mutually bound. The rubber industry transformed Akron from a small canal town into a fledgling city. The birth of the rubber industry started in the eighteen hundreds, long before America fell in love with the automobile. Akron was incorporated as a village in one eight three five , and as a city in one eight six five . In one eight six nine , B.F. Goodrich began the first rubber company to settle in Akron. In one nine one five , the area increased from seven , two five four acres ( two nine . three eight km) to one six , one two zero acres ( six five . two nine km). The population rose approximately two zero zero % from six nine , zero six seven in one nine one zero to two zero eight , four three five in one nine two zero .  General Tire was founded in one nine one five , by the ONeils whose department store became an Akron landmark. 

The Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company became America's top tire manufacturer and Akron was granted the moniker of The Rubber Capital of the World. Goodyear's president, F.A. Seiberling, had been building homes costing around $ three , five zero zero for employees in what would become known as Goodyear Heights. Harvey Firestone, likewise, began building employee homes in what would be called Firestone Park. These leaders were responding to the housing crunch caused by the boom in the rubber business. 

Akron was, indeed, booming. For a time it was the fastest-growing city in the country, its population exploding from six nine , zero zero zero in one nine one zero to two zero eight , zero zero zero in one nine two zero . People came for the jobs in the rubber factories from many places, including Europe. Of those two zero eight , zero zero zero , almost one-third were immigrants and their children. 

In the fifties and sixties Akron continued to see a surge in industry as the automobile continued to take off. But while America was still using bias-ply tires, Europe had already seen the wave of the future in radial tires. The radials had almost three times the tread life of bias-ply, and Akrons rubber mills were not properly equipped to handle the manufacturing requirements. As a result many companies tried to produce hybrid tires, which were troublesome at best. Firestone manufactured the ill fated five zero zero series, which was recalled in the millions. B.F. Goodrich eventually bit the bullet and transformed all the old equipment with new machinery that would facilitate the manufacturing of the newer radial tires. 

In the seventies and eighties the rubber industry experienced a major decline as a number of strikes and factory shutdowns delivered the final blows to the industry. In ten years the number of people working within the rubber industry was slashed in half. By the early nineties all but Goodyear moved their headquarters out of Akron.

 Today 
Goodyear continues to manufacture racing and experimental tires, and Firestones technical centre remains in Akron. Because the rubber industry is still a major employer in the region, Akron has suffered less than other cities of similar size which have gone through Rust Belt decline, such as neighboring Youngstown.

 Geography and Climate 

Akron is located at four one  four ' two three  North, eight one  three one ' four  West ( four one . zero seven three one five five , - eight one . five one seven nine zero zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one six one . six km ( six two . four mi).  one six zero . eight km ( six two . one mi) of it is land and zero . nine km ( zero . three mi) of it is water. The total area is zero . five four % water.

Akron has a humid continental climate, with cold but changeable winters, wet, cool springs, warm (sometimes hot) and humid summers, and cool, rather dry autumns. Precipitation is fairly well-distributed through the year, but summer tends to have the most rainfall (and also, somewhat paradoxially, the most sunshine), and autumn the least.  The mid-autumn through early-spring months tend to be quite cloudy, with sometimes less than three zero % possible sunshine. The cloudiest month is December, and the sunniest month is usually July, which is also, somewhat ironically, the wettest month.

Winters tend to be cold, with average January high temperatures of three two F ( zero C), and average January lows of one seven F (- eight C), with considerable variation in temperatures. During a typical January, high temperatures of over five zero F ( one zero C) are just as common as low temperatures of below zero F (- one eight C). Snowfall is lighter than the snowbelt areas to the north, but is still somewhat influenced by Lake Erie, generally averaging about four seven . one inches ( one one eight . seven cm) per winter. During a typical winter, temperatures drop below zero F (- one eight C) on about six occurrences, generally only during the nighttime hours.

Summers are warm, sometimes hot, with average July high temperatures of eight three F ( two eight C), and average July lows of six two F ( one seven C). Summer weather is more stable, generally humid with thunderstorms fairly common. Temperatures reach or exceed nine zero F ( three two C) about seven times each summer, on average. In hot summers, such as one nine eight eight , however, as many as three zero days over nine zero F ( three two C) have been observed, and in cooler summers, such as the summer of two zero zero zero , the temperature may never reach nine zero F ( three two C). Temperatures over one zero zero F ( three eight C) are rare (about once per decade on average), most recently occurring on several occasions in the hot summer of one nine eight eight .

The all-time record high in Akron of one zero four F ( four zero C) was established on August six , one nine one eight , and the all-time record low of  two five F ( three two C) was set on January one nine , one nine nine four .

 Law and government 
The city adopted a new charter of the commissioner manager type in one nine two zero , but reverted to its old form in one nine two four . The current mayor of Akron is Don Plusquellic. Mayor Plusquellic is currently serving his fifth term, and was the President of the United States Conference of Mayors during two zero zero four .

The city is over $ one . one billion in debt, more then any other city of its size (in Ohio), and is likely to become an issue of contention during the next election. 

In one nine one five , a new municipal water system was established. It included a reservoir on the Cuyahoga River with storage capacity of two , three eight five , two zero zero , zero zero zero gallons ( nine , zero two seven , nine eight two , zero zero zero liters), a complete purification system, and a pumping station. 



 Economy 
Akron is home to two Fortune five zero zero companies: the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company and FirstEnergy. In addition, Akron is home to a number of smaller companies such as Gojo, makers of Purell, Advanced Elastomer Systems, FirstMerit Bank, and Roadway Express, a subsidiary of Yellow Roadway. The City of Akron created the first Joint Economic Development District to promote regional commerce with neighboring suburbs.

 Education 
The University of Akron is home to over two three , zero zero zero students, making it the fourth largest public university in the state, and is a world leader in polymer research. While Akron continues to predominantly serve commuter students, the university has worked hard to shake off its image as a commuter school. A $ three zero zero million dollar construction project saw the completion of nine new buildings, fourteen renovated facilities, and a freshly landscaped campus. The University also offers a combined B.S.M.D. program with the Northeastern Ohio Universities College of Medicine.

The Akron Public Schools are currently going through an $ eight zero zero million rebuilding process that will take one five years, remodeling some schools and entirely replacing others. Some schools will be closing permanently due to a drop in city population. The school board could not get a levy passed to pay for its portion of the construction expense so it worked out an arrangement with the city of Akron where the city will use the money from a new income tax to pay for Community Learning Centers, which will serve as schools but be owned by the city. Meanwhile the academic situation has improved recently as the citys schools have been moved from Academic Watch to Continuous Improvement by the Ohio Department of Education.

Akron also has many private, parochial and charter schools. Akron Public Schools made headlines in two zero zero four when a freshman student of Akron Digital Academy, the districts own online charter school, was not allowed to participate in extracurricular activities, an event later covered and satirized by ''The Daily Show''. St. Vincent - St. Mary High School, just west of Akrons downtown, also made headlines when basketball star LeBron James was recruited from the school by the Cleveland Cavaliers in two zero zero three .

 Culture and entertainment 
Akron has a diverse and colorful heritage of old restaurants and shopping centers. Quaker Square, located in the heart of Akrons downtown, is a mall made out of the old Quaker Oats factory, which originally operated there. The oat silos have been transformed into hotel rooms providing a unique experience to the patron. The Trackside Grille, themed with railroads which run parallel to the building, provides a narrative of Akrons history. 

There are two full-size shopping malls in the city limits of Akron: Chapel Hill Mall on Brittain Road to the northeast, and Rolling Acres Mall at Romig Road to the southwest. A third mall, Summit Mall, is in suburban Fairlawn. Chapel Hill, once a very low-key mall, has transformed itself into a very successful enterprise, with vacancies nearing zero %. Rolling Acres Mall is the largest mall in the region with one . three million square feet ( one two zero , zero zero zero m ) and was extremely popular in the one nine eight zero s and early one nine nine zero s when the other malls were not doing as well. As Chapel Hill Mall as well as Summit Mall in Fairlawn improved however, Rolling Acres began to fall apart. A reputation of violence surrounding the Rolling Acres area irrevocably hurt the mall. Today, the Romig Road Wooster Avenue (Vernon Odom Boulevard) area has vacancy rates surpassing five zero %.

Akron also supports independent retailers. West Point Market, a nationally-known specialty food and wine store, offers Akron residents exceptional imported and gourmet food items in addition to locally grown produce. 

Highland Square, located in West Akron and anchored by the historic Highland Theatre, is one of Akron's fastest-growing entertainment districts. 

Each summer Akron hosts the All American Soap Box Derby. Children from across the country race their homemade, gravity-powered race cars down the steep hill at Derby Downs in the shadow of the Lockheed Martin Airdock.

The city is also home to several museums, including:
 Akron Art Museum
 National Inventors Hall of Fame
 Stan Hywet Hall and Gardens
 American Marble and Toy Museum
 Goodyear World of Rubber Museum

Infrastructure
 Health 
Akron has an extensive and distinguished health sector, with a large number of hospitals for a city of its size. Akron has two large hospitals, Akron General Medical Center and Akron City Hospital (run by the larger Summa Health System). Akron City Hospital and Akron General have both been on the U.S. News and World Report Magazine's list of Best Hospitals many times. Akron is also home to Childrens hospital, a specialist in pediatric and burn care, and Saint Thomas Hospital, a smaller full service hospital located in the North Hill neighborhood.

 Transportation 
Akron's road network does not run on any grid system, and it can be confusing for out-of-town motorists. Roads frequently change name or direction without warning, or stop and continue elsewhere. In addition there are two sets of numbered roads, one in Kenmore ( one st - three one st Streets), and one along Arlington ( one st - nine th Avenues), the rest of the city has no numbering at all. This disparity between areas is due to Akron's many annexations over the years.
Akrons transportation needs are fulfilled by two major interstates, Interstate seven six and Interstate seven seven . I- seven six , I- seven seven , and Route eight meet at one central interchange, which is commonly known by the same name. The central interchange divides the city into four quadrants. The Interstate seven six Eastern Expressway weaves through much of Akrons warehouse sector and the Goodyear world headquarters is easily visible. I- seven six is paired with I- seven seven for about two miles ( three km) west of the central interchange, and then splits off again, with I- seven six later being paired with US- two two four and I- seven seven heading north towards Cleveland. The Western highway is a major route to Cleveland and Columbus, and is a near term destination to Fairlawn a major commercial area. Route eight has been overhauled numerous times and serves as a major entryway for the north-eastern suburbs, namely Cuyahoga Falls, Munroe Falls, Stow and Hudson. There are also two highways to the south, U.S. Highway two two four , and Interstate two seven seven . I- two seven seven connects I- seven seven directly with the southern portion of I- seven six providing a quick route between neighbouring Barberton and south Akron. The Martin Luther King Jr. Freeway, commonly known as the Innerbelt, includes part of the longer Route five nine . It serves the very center of the city, and was supposed to run from the I- seven six  I- seven seven to Route eight . However, due to poor planning, the Innerbelt was never completed and only runs to Main St. Route five nine also lacks direct I- seven six W I- seven seven N inbound and offbound ramps, furthering its problems. Mayor Don Plusquellic has brought up the idea of tearing up the northern end of the Innerbelt in order to free land for development.

Public transportation is available through the METRO RTA system, which has a fleet of over two hundred busses and trolleys. Amtrak closed its station near Quaker Square in two zero zero five . Airline passengers travelling to or from Akron use either the Akron-Canton Regional Airport in Green or Cleveland Hopkins International Airport. Two low-fare airlines, Frontier Airlines and AirTran Airways, have begun serving Akron-Canton in recent years, making that airport a fairly popular alternative for travellers to or from the Cleveland area. Akron Fulton Airport serves private planes and is the home of the Lockheed Martin Airdock, where the Goodyear blimps were formerly stored and maintained.

 Trivia 
O.C. Barber stables.Barberton was founded in one eight nine two by O.C. (Ohio Columbus) Barber. There are still several buildings in town that were built by Barber for his farms (although no farms remain in the city limits). Residents of Barberton are known as Barbertonians.

'''Cuyahoga Falls''' is a city located in Summit County, Ohio, in the United States. As of the two zero zero three census, the city had a total population of five zero , three seven five . It is currently the second largest city in Summit County, Ohio. It is considered a suburb of Akron, but is actually older than Akron. Founded in one eight one two by William Wetmore, the city was originally named Manchester. Cuyahoga Falls is named after the Cuyahoga River (which flows into Lake Erie) and the series of falls that run through the middle of the city.

Cuyahoga Falls borders Akron to the south and the Cuyahoga Valley National Park to the northwest.

 History 

Cuyahoga Falls was formed in one eight one two near the junction of what was then Northampton, Stow, Tallmadge, and Portage townships. The focus was the series of Cuyahoga River waterfalls that provided power for manufacturing. 

In one eight one two Kelsey and Wilcox built a dam on the Cuyahoga River at a place where a railroad bridge crossed it in one eight seven six . They then built a flour mill, an oil mill, and a saw mill. This led to the construction of a number of houses. This area was known as the old village. Development moved downstream, though, when it was discovered that the power was better there. The old village was eventually destroyed in one eight two six when a dam built by William Wetmore flooded the dam at the old village and its mills were torn down .

The earliest settler of Cuyahoga Falls included Joshua Stow and William Wetmore. In one eight one five a saw-mill was operating near Gaylord's Grove, using power generated by a dam on the Cuyahoga River there.

The town was initially called Manchester but was renamed Cuyahoga Falls at the request of the Post Office since there were already several other Manchesters in Ohio. 

The village proper was first laid out in one eight two six by Judge Richardson. 

The town was incorporated in one eight three six , occupying two four zero rods out of Stow and Tallmadge townships. In one eight five three , seeing that the village and township of Cuyahoga Falls occupied the same territory, the village council disbanded and the community was only a township until one eight six eight .

In one eight four one the Summit County Board of Commissioners named Cuyahoga Falls county seat. The state legislature then intervened and put the location of the county seat up to a popular vote. Akron won and has been the county seat ever since. In spite of being named the county seat Cuyahoga Falls never really functioned as such.

In March of one eight five one the township of Cuyahoga Falls was created out of the village limits. They covered the same territory so the village council voted to adjourn ''sine die'', letting the village be run under township jusidiction until June three , one eight six eight when the municipal government returned.

In one nine eight five Cuyahoga Falls merged with Northampton Township, the first merger of a city and township in Ohio.

Cuyahoga Falls had been founded as an industrial city, taking advantage of the river power. By the one nine seven zero s, though, it had become a residential community. This changed, though, when Don Robart became mayor. He had been in favor of the merger with Northampton Township because of the additional land that could be used for development. Parts of that area have since been used for industrial development. Commercial development has also picked up, especially on the Howe Avenue area at the southern border of the city.

Popular Culture

Cuyahoga Falls has a mention in a popular song, My City Was Gone , by the rock band The Pretenders (lead singer and songwriter Chrissie Hynde is an Akron, Ohio native). The verse's lyrics are: 

:I went back to Ohio
:But my pretty countryside
:Had been paved down the middle
:By a government that had no pride
:The farms of Ohio
:Had been replaced by shopping malls
:And muzak filled the air
:From Seneca to Cuyahoga Falls
:Said, a, o, oh way to go, Ohio

In the movie ''Tommy Boy'', starring the late Chris Farley, a plane ticket is bought by Farley's love interest in the film from Sandusky, Ohio, to Cuyahoga Falls. There are presently no commercial airports in Cuyahoga Falls or Sandusky.

In the movie ''My Fellow Americans'', we learn that Jack Lemmon's character, a former U.S. President, had his presidential library built in not in his hometown of Cleveland, Ohio, but in Cuyahoga Falls, because the latter city gave him a tax break.

Governmental History

Green was incorporated in one nine nine one as a municipality. Prior to incorporation, Green was a township with several unincorporated hamlets, most notably Greensburg. A section of the township became the village of Green and later merged with the rest of the township. Fred Ravagnani was the first Mayor of Green village. What is today Green was originally part of Stark County, although Green has been situated wholly within the County of Summit since one eight four zero .

The fairly recent incorporation of the city results in the city having no real postal service mailing address; it is served by its own Post Office, Green, OH four four two three two , but this is a P.O. Box only office. No street addresses in Green have this zip code. Green street addresses are served by five different post offices, covering different parts of the city:

 two Akron post offices (zip codes four four three one two , four four three one nine ), one Canton post office ( four four seven two zero ), the Clinton, OH ( four four two one six ) post office, and the Uniontown, OH post office ( four four six eight five ).

Politics of Incorporation (becoming a city)

The impetus for Green to become a city arose in part out of controversy generated by a letter supposedly written by former Akron City Schools superintendent Conrad Ott. The letter spoke of willingness by Akron to annex Green schools. Few voters realized that school districts are separate municipalities under Ohio law. Property annexation to a city does not change the school district. Nevertheless, the rally to save independent schools helped spur the drive to incorporate. 

Trivia

The AkronCanton Regional Airport is located mostly in the city of Green, although a small part extends into Jackson Township in Stark County.

Famous persons

Weatherman Dick Goddard of Fox eight Cleveland is a Green High School graduate.

 History 

The city's name is said to derive from a small joke among divinity students at Western Reserve College, which in the early one eight zero zero s was in Hudson, Ohio. The students, who were called upon to preach in the small hamlet six miles to the north, recalled Acts one six : one zero : ...we sought to go to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the gospel to them.

'''Munroe Falls''', formerly a section of Stow Township, is a city located in the northeast portion of Summit County, Ohio, near Kent and south of Stow. It is a suburb of Akron. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five , three one four .

Munroe Falls is located at four one  eight ' two zero  North, eight one  two six ' one six  West ( four one . one three eight eight zero six , - eight one . four three seven eight seven zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of seven . three km ( two . eight mi ).  seven . one km ( two . seven mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is three . one eight % water.

 History 

Munroe Falls's history is rooted in the Cuyahoga River, where many industrial plants were developed. In one eight one seven a log dam was built at the present dam location to provide power for both a saw and grist mill, which was constructed on either side of the dam. These industries flourished, and soon a carding factory and other small business found their home in the then village of Florence. In one eight three six the Munroe Brothers of Boston purchased two zero zero acres ( eight zero zero , zero zero zero m ) of land of Florence and renamed it Munroe Falls. They then started the Munroe Falls Manufacturing Company, which made things from wool to tools. Incorporation of the Village of Munroe Falls took place in one eight three eight as part of Portage County until one eight four zero when Summit County was formed. Completed in one eight four one , The Pennsylvania and Ohio Canal created great prosperity for the region. The grist mill was granted the tools needed to manufacture paper in one eight six six . The canal was disbanded shortly after its formation in one eight six eight . Railroad tracks took its place in the form of a single line owned by the Pittsburgh and Western Railroad. These tracks were doubled in one nine zero zero following the purchase of the railroad by Baltimore and Ohio Railroad. The growth of Munroe Falls continued when the Cleveland Paper Company purchased a mill in one eight six six . The Mill, today known as Sonoco Products, still operates and is an important part of the city's economy. 

Munroe Falls was not to become a large industrial center. It is a small residential community, with a rate of growth slow enough to preserve its rich history and quick enough to stay on course through the next century.

The city shares a school system with neighboring Stow, Ohio; six elementary schools, one intermediate, one middle and one high school. Their mascot is the bulldog and colors are maroon and gold.

The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) began a dam lowering project in August two zero zero five . It is slated to be completed sometime in two zero zero six .

 '''New Franklin Village''' is located at the southern edge of Summit County, Ohio, in Northeast Ohio. It is bounded to the north by Coventry Township, as well as the Cities of Barberton and Norton. Chippewa Township, in Wayne County, is to the west of New Franklin Village, with the Village of Clinton to the southwest. To the east, lies the City of Green. Franklin's southern neighbor is Lawrence Township, in Stark County. As of January one , two zero zero five , the village had a total population of one six , seven two one .

New Franklin Village was formed in November two zero zero three when the residents of Franklin Township and the Village of New Franklin voted to merge the two entities. This merger, which was precipitated by numerous annexation attempts by neighboring cities, took effect January one , two zero zero five . 

New Franklin Village, originally known as Franklin Township, was founded in one eight one seven . The Village of New Franklin was basically a part of Franklin Township; it's citizens were also citizens of Franklin Township.

The official website for the village is currently: www.franklintownship-oh.gov

 Description 
Pigeon Creek is not a real town, but rather a Census Designated Place in Copley Township. It is roughtly in the shape of a rectangle. surrounded by Medina Line Road, Ridgewood Road, Route two one , and a southern border that cuts through a wooded area. CDPs were created to recognize areas that are not formal government subdivisions but otherwise serve as communities. More obvious local CDPs include Montrose-Ghent and Portage Lakes. The curious thing about Pigeon Creek is that while some locals know of the creek itself, no one refers to the area by the name Pigeon Creek, or by any name at all. It is just an area with woods, fields, and residences, which makes it like most of the rest of 
Copley. (Akron Beacon Journal, two zero zero one )

Pigeon Creek became a CDP in one nine nine zero . The Census Bureau says it creates CDPs based on local input. No one locally seems to know why it was chosen, though. (Akron Beacon Journal, two zero zero one )

 '''Portage Lakes''' is a census-designated place located in Summit County, Ohio. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of nine , eight seven zero . It is not a municipality. The Portage Lakes CDP area encompasses portions of Franklin Township and Coventry Township which are wholly situated within Summit County. The city of Green is adjacent to the southeast and Akron on the north; the village of New Franklin is to the south. A much larger area surrounding the CDP is also commonly known as the Portage Lakes. The Portage Lakes of the area include but are not limited to Turkeyfoot Lake, Nimisila Reservoir, Mud Lake, and Long Lake. The lakes are connected by a series of channels . There is a Portage Lakes State Park with boat launching ramps and seasonal beach swimming.
