 :''See: United Torah Judaism and Degel HaTorah for the Haredi Israeli political parties''.

'''Torah Judaism''' is an English term, also a slogan, used by a number of Orthodox Jewish groups, mostly associated with Haredi Judaism, to describe a Judaism based on a strict adherence to the laws of the Torah's six one three mitzvot and the Halakha. Followers of ''Torah Judaism'' also follow the ''Daat Torah'' the guidelines of their rabbis who are usually their rebbes ( Hasidic rabbis), rosh yeshivas ( deans of yeshivas -- Talmudical schools ) or of a posek and expert in the Shulkhan Arukh ( Code of Jewish Law ).

Torah Judaism implies a belief and practice of Judaism that is based purely on the Torah (meaning the inclusion of the entire Torah, Tanakh, Talmud and more) and on the premise that the Torah emanated directly from God when he revealed himself to the Children of Israel (for Jews this is the Biblical name for their own people) at Mount Sinai and made an eternal covenant with them, which is further defined by the application and usage of such Hebrew phrases as: 

''Torah min hashamayim'' ( Torah from Heavensky )
''Torat Hashem'' ( Torah of God )
''Torah misinai'' ( Torah from Sinai )
''Kedushat HaTorah ( Holiness of Torah )
''Torat Hashem temimah'' ( Torah of God is purecomplete )
''Matan Torah'' ( giving the Torah )
''Kabbalat HaTorah'' ( receivingacceptance of Torah )
''Na'aseh venishmah'' ( we shall do and we shall learn )
 
The term Torah Judaism is a reaction to the perceived loss of meaning of other terms used to describe their beliefs. It is also a declaration that they perceive the liberalism of some Orthodox Jews, such as in some left-wing sectors of Modern Orthodox Judaism as leaving the bounds that they believe are mandated by the Torah.

On the other hand, Modern Orthodoxy has developed its own self-defining slogans such as Torah Umadda and Synthesis to define its world view of Judaism in modern times.

A separate article exists on Relationships between Jewish religious movements.

 The City of '''Guymon, Oklahoma''' serves as the seat of Texas County, Oklahoma. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one zero , four seven two . 

 Geography 
Location of Guymon, Oklahoma

Located on the High Plains of the central Oklahoma Panhandle Guymon sits one zero five miles ( one six nine kilometers) north of Amarillo, Texas and one zero zero miles ( one six one kilometers west-northwest of Woodward, Oklahoma. Optima National Wildlife Refuge and Optima Lake lie roughly one six miles to the east along the North Canadian River. 

Guymon is located at three six  four one ' seven  North, one zero one  two eight ' four six  West ( three six . six eight five three eight three , - one zero one . four seven nine five eight two ) and sits at an elevation of three , one two six feet ( nine five three meters).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one nine . zero km ( seven . three mi ).  one eight . nine km ( seven . three mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two seven % water.

 History 

In the one eight nine zero s, Edward T. E.T. Guymon purchased a section of land west of the Beaver River. The site grew very rapidly after the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railway began to pass through it after one nine zero one . The town, first named Sanford, was later renamed Guymon by railroad officials in order to avoid confusion with the town of Stratford, Texas, which was further down the line. Guymon incorporated in one nine zero five . 

The Pioneer Days Celebration and Rodeo has offered tributes to the communitys pioneer spirit every May since the one nine five zero s.

Guymon, Oklahoma is a small town but, is the county seat of Texas County. 

Guymon is a very busy little town. In one nine nine zero Seaboard Farms came to Guymon furthering the buissness in Guymon.

Guymon has a variety of elementary schools to choose from.
Guymon has one Jr. High School.
Guymon has one High School.

Guymon's team mascot is the Tiger.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one zero , four seven two people, three , six five one households, and two , six three two families residing in the city. The population density is five five three . one km ( one , four three three . two mi ). There are three , nine four one housing units at an average density of two zero eight . two km ( five three nine . four mi ). The racial makeup of the city is seven zero . four four % White, zero . eight four % African American, one . three two % Native American, zero . eight five % Asian, zero . one seven % Pacific Islander, two three . four six % from other races, and two . nine two % from two or more races.  three eight . three seven % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , six five one households out of which three nine . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five nine . zero % are married couples living together, eight . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and two seven . nine % are non-families. two one . five % of all households are made up of individuals and eight . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight two and the average family size is three . two six .

In the city the population is spread out with two nine . one % under the age of one eight , one two . zero % from one eight to two four , three zero . six % from two five to four four , one eight . three % from four five to six four , and one zero . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three zero years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero six . one males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero seven . nine males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three seven , three three three , and the median income for a family is $ four four , eight four one .  Economy 
Guymon serves as a trade center for a wide wheat, livestock, and dairy area. A United States soil conservation station sits nearby. The city has oil and gas wells. Manufactures include agricultural tillage tools, pressure tanks, printing, and formula feeds. The hamlet of Goodwell, Oklahoma, home of Oklahoma Panhandle State University, lies one one miles to the southwest. The city once had scheduled air service.

 '''Glenpool''' is a city located in Tulsa County, Oklahoma. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of eight , one two three .

 History 
On November two two , one nine zero five , wildcatters, Robert Galbreath and Frank Chesley (along with, by some accounts, Charles Colcord), drilling for oil on farmland owned by Creek Indian Ida E. Glenn, created the first oil gusher in what would soon be known as the Glenn Pool . The discovery set off a boom of growth for the area, bringing in hordes of people: lease buyers, producers, millionaires, laborers, tool suppliers and newspeople. Daily production soon exceeded one two zero , zero zero zero barrels.

The oil field was the richest the world had yet known, making more money than the California Gold Rush and Colorado Silver Rush combined and making Oklahoma known around the world for oil production.

 '''Jenks''' is a city located in Tulsa County, Oklahoma in the northeastern part of Oklahoma. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of nine , five five seven and is growing by about one zero % per year. Jenks is a suburb to the south and west of Tulsa and lays between the Arkansas River and highway US seven five . In Jenks houses sell as nearly as fast as they can be built. In the year two zero zero three alone, twenty-six subdivisions were in the planning or development process.

City

Riverwalk Crossing on the Arkansas River, Jenks.
Jenks is not just a suburban bedroom community. Despite its growth, Jenks is a town known for its antique small-town charm. Along Main St., small boutiques, antique stores, and salons in historic buildings are very popular and draw visitors from all over. Growth is largely fueled by the popular public school system in Jenks which is one of the top school systems in the state. The Jenks school district encompasses significant portions of southwest Tulsa, and in fact many of the Jenks schools are located in Tulsa. The high school, though, remains near downtown Jenks.

In two zero zero four , the new Oklahoma Aquarium opened along the Arkansas River in Jenks which started a boom in riverfront development. Two new hotels and the new Riverwalk Crossing center are being built or have been built on the river near the aquarium. A pedestrian bridge links the Jenks riverfront area with the Tulsa Riverparks system on the other side of the river. Commercial development on the river is now spreading into Tulsa as well. 

Jenks is home to Tulsas general aviation airport Jones Airport which is the state's busiest airport and -- measured by number of takeoffs and landings -- one of the busiest in the world.

 Baseball commissioner Bart Giamatti announcing Pete Rose's voluntary banishment from baseball amid accusations of betting on baseball games. Eight days later, Giamatti was dead.
'''Angelo Bartlett Giamatti''' (April four , one nine three eight  September one , one nine eight nine ) was the President of Yale University, and later, the seven th commissioner of Major League Baseball in the United States. Giamatti is best remembered for overseeing the banishment of popular baseball player Pete Rose from the sport for his gambling infractions (detailed in the Dowd Report) in one nine eight nine . 

Personal life
He grew up near Mount Holyoke College, in South Hadley, Massachusetts, where his father, Valentine Giamatti, founded the departments of Italian and Spanish languages and literatures. He also collected translations of Dante's Divine Comedy. His mother, Mary Claybaugh Walton, was the daughter of Helen (Davidson) Walton and Bartlett Walton, who attended Andover and Harvard College. His paternal grandfather, Angelo Giammattei (so spelled) emigrated from Italy through Ellis Island in about one nine zero zero . Bart graduated from South Hadley High School, and while President of Yale, served as a Trustee of Mount Holyoke College.

A. Bartlett Giamatti attended Andover and Yale. He was tapped by Scroll and Key, and graduated ''magna cum laude'' in one nine six zero , marrying Toni Smith that same year. Toni Smith Giamatti taught English for more than twenty years at the Hopkins School in New Haven up until her death in two zero zero four .

Of their three children, Marcus Giamatti, Paul Giamatti, and Elena Giamatti, two have become actors. In the movie ''Sideways'', a photograph of the younger Miles Raymond (Paul Giamatti) with his late father is really a picture of Paul and Bart Giamatti.

Yale
Giamatti stayed in New Haven to receive his doctorate in one nine six four . He became a professor of English at Yale University, an author, and master of Ezra Stiles College at Yale. He spent a brief period teaching at Princeton, but was at Yale for most of his teaching life. Giamatti's scholarly work focused on English Renaissance literature, particularly Edmund Spenser, and relationships between English and Italian Renaissance poets. His work on the genre of pastoral and on the influence of Ludovico Ariosto in England remains influential.

When Giamatti's tenure as Stiles master ended in one nine seven two , he was so popular that his students wanted to honor him with a present. Giamatti told them he wanted a joke gift and they got him a moosehead (from a yard sale), which was ceremoniously hung in the dining hall. As the new master took over, Giamatti told him in a serious tone, I have only one solemn duty to convey to you. Take care of my moose. 

He served as President of Yale University from one nine seven seven to one nine eight six . He was the youngest President of the University in its history. He served on the Board of Trustees of Mount Holyoke College for many years, participating fully despite his Yale and baseball commitments.

Baseball
His lifelong interest in baseball (Giamatti was a die-hard Boston Red Sox fan) came into play when he became President of the National League in one nine eight six , and later Commissioner of Baseball in one nine eight nine . During his stint as National League president, Giamatti placed an emphasis on the need to improve the environment for the fan in the ballparks. Giamatti also decided to make umpires strictly enforce the balk rule. He supported social justice as the only remedy for the lack of presence of minority managers, coaches, or executives at any level in Major League Baseball.

Just a year prior to his now monumental banishment of Pete Rose, while still serving as National League president, Giamatti suspended Rose for three zero games after Rose shoved umpire Dave Pallone on April three zero . Another notable suspension that Giamatti handed out in one nine eight eight was to Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Jay Howell, who was caught using pine tar during the National League Championship Series.
 
Giamatti, whose tough dealing with Yale's union favorably impressed Major League Baseball owners, was unanimously elected to succeed Peter Ueberroth as commissioner on September eight , one nine eight eight . As reflected in the agreement with Pete Rose, Giamatti was determined to maintain the integrity of the game during his tragically brief commissionership.

While at his vacation home in Martha's Vineyard, Giamatti, a heavy smoker for many years, died suddenly of a massive heart attack at the age of five one , only eight days after banishing Rose. Bart Giamatti had only been the commissioner of baseball for one five four days. Bart Giamatti became only the second baseball commissioner to die while still in office (the first was Kenesaw Mountain Landis). Giamatti was immediately succeeded by his close friend and baseball's first-ever deputy commissioner, Fay Vincent. 

James Reston, Jr. notes, in his book ''Collision at Home Plate: The Lives of Pete Rose and Bart Giamatti'', that Giamatti suffered from Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, an inherited neuromuscular disease affecting peripheral nerves.

Works
''The Earthly Paradise and the Renaissance Epic'' ( one nine six six )
''Play of Double Senses: Spensers Faerie Queene'' ( one nine seven five )
''The University and the Public Interest'' ( one nine eight one )
''Exile and Change in Renaissance Literature'' ( one nine eight four )
''Take Time for Paradise: Americans and their Games'' ( one nine eight nine )
''A Great and Glorious Game: Baseball Writings of A. Bartlett Giamatti'' (ed. Kenneth Robson, one nine nine eight )

References

 Details 
Alva was established in one eight nine three as a land office for the Cherokee Outlet land run, the largest of the land rushes that settled western and central Oklahoma. The site was chosen for its location on the Atchison, Topeka Castle on the Hill, a huge, fanciful brick building, modeled after a Norman castle, that towered over much of the town. The Castle on the Hill The Castle burned down in one nine three five , to be replaced by the more staid Jesse Dunn Hall, which was dedicated in one nine three seven by Eleanor Roosevelt. The town council is actively soliciting murals -- one of the most recent is of the fabled Castle -- and trying to attract businesses to attract tourists and to keep people in town, important as the population of Woods County has been dropping since the one nine three zero s. Alva lost two zero zero people between one nine nine zero and two zero zero zero according to official census figures. It has a Wal-Mart Supercenter that is one of the smallest supercenters ever built; the other supermarket in town closed after it opened. There is now a new grocery store in town Alva's Market . The area is generally religious, with one six different churches, all Christian, in town.

 Famous Natives 
Alva is the birthplace of actor Jack Ging.

 '''Capron''' is a town located in Woods County, Oklahoma. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of four two .

 Geography

Capron is located at three six  five three ' four seven  North, nine eight  three four ' four two  West ( three six . eight nine six three zero seven , - nine eight . five seven eight three five one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of zero . three km ( zero . one mi ).  zero . three km ( zero . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are four two people, one seven households, and one zero families residing in the town. The racial makeup of the town is one zero zero . zero zero % White, zero . zero zero % African American, zero . zero zero % Native American, zero . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . zero zero % from other races, and zero . zero zero % from two or more races.  zero . zero zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one seven households, out of which two three . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five eight . eight % are married couples living together, five . nine % have a female householder with no husband present, and three five . three % are non-families. two nine . four % of all households are made up of individuals, and one one . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. In the town the population is spread out, with one nine . zero % under the age of one eight , seven . one % from one eight to two four , three three . three % from two five to four four , two eight . six % from four five to six four , and one one . nine % who are six five years of age or older. The median income for a household in the town is $ two four , two five zero , and the median income for a family is $ two three , seven five zero . Males have a median income of $ two two , five zero zero versus $ one six , two five zero for females. The per capita income for the town is $ one one , one five six .  zero . zero % of the population and zero . zero % of families are below the poverty line.

History
Prior to the opening of the Cherokee Strip in one eight nine three , Capron, Oklahoma was first known as Warren , a small cattle station on the main line of the Santa Fe railroad. It consisted of a store, and an old railroad car left by the Santa Fe. Sometime after the opening of the strip residents wanted to come up with a new name for the growing town. The name was changed to Sterling , but the postal service and Santa Fe would not accept it because there was a town by that name on their line in Kansas. The names of Virgil and Kermit were proposed, but Santa Fe would not accept these names, for the same reason. Therefore, a committee consisting of Mr. George Espy, postmaster, Dr. G.W. Todd, and Congressman Dennis Flynn was appointed to select a name which the Santa Fe and Postal Service would accept. The name of Captain Allyn K. Capron, Jr. was proposed. Captain Capron was a member of Teddy Roosevelt's Rough Riders, and had been killed at the battle of San Juan Hill. The name of Capron was approved by a petition of the residents. The Santa Fe and U. S. Postal service accepted the name and so it stands today.

At one time Capron was quite a thriving community. It had two banks; the Bank of Capron, and the Capron State Bank; three general stores; two drug stores; a hotel; depot; a millinery shop; theater; blacksmith; a weekly newspaper, The Capron Hustler; a monthly newspaper, The Screech Owl; two barber shops; hardware store; lumber yard; two churches, Warburton Memorial Methodist Church, and First Congregational Church; the Driftwood Telephone Company and Hampton's Foot Powder Factory.
 
In April one nine three nine a tornado struck Capron, making a straight line down the main business street. Many of the residents of town did not even know the tornado has struck until the next morning when they went downtown to open their stores and found them gone. Most tornados sound like trains, and since a train goes through Capron about every two zero minutes no one noticed! Most of the above businesses, and the public school building, which was only one zero years old, were destroyed. The majority of these businesses were never rebuilt. However, the public schools were rebuilt.

Capron was always concerned with having a good school system. In one eight nine four a small but enterprising group of Driftwood Township citizens provided for the establishment of the first Capron Public Schools. The school consisted of grades one  one nine five six , additional classrooms and music room; and one nine six four , when a new cafeteria was added to the school. The high school was first accredited in one nine one two . In one nine six eight the high school was closed due to falling enrollment. There were no families in the school district on public assistance in one nine six eight , and the patrons of the district never voted down a tax increase for their school; they wanted the very best for their children. The Elementary School, grades K eight were closed in one nine seven six by a vote of the patrons which carried by only one vote. The vote was contested. This decision was taken to court and eventually upheld by the Oklahoma Supreme Court. Today Capron has two large concrete grain elevators, a rural water district office, United Methodist Church, garage, filling station, and American Legion Post. The Post Office closed in one nine nine four after one zero zero years of service to the citizens of the area. It is hard to believe that any of this once thriving little center of trade ever existed and today lives only in the memories of many of its older residents.

 The City of '''Woodward, Oklahoma''' serves as the county seat of Woodward County, Oklahoma. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one one , eight five three . 

 Geography 
Location of Woodward, Oklahoma
Woodward is located at three six  two five ' five nine  North, nine nine  two three ' five two  West ( three six . four three three zero five nine , - nine nine . three nine seven seven four five ), elevation one , nine zero six feet ( five eight one meters).

The city lies on the North Canadian River, one zero zero miles ( one six one kilometers) east-southeast of Guymon, Oklahoma and eight five miles ( one three seven kilometers) west of Enid, Oklahoma. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three four . two km ( one three . two mi ).  three four . zero km ( one three . one mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . five three % water.

 History 
More than fifty thousand individuals and families settled across the old Cherokee Strip of northern Oklahoma on September one nine , one eight nine three in the greatest land run in American history. The settlers founded cities that day from Woodward all the way to Enid, Oklahoma and Ponca City, Oklahoma. 

On April nine , one nine four seven , the deadliest tornado in Oklahoma history tore through Woodward, killing one zero seven people and destroying one zero zero city blocks. The family of storms, known as the Glazier-Higgins-Woodward Tornadoes, ranked as the sixth deadliest in US history, having caused many fatalities and much damage in other communities in Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas.


 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one one , eight five three people, four , seven eight seven households, and three , two four five families residing in the city. The population density is three four eight . eight km ( nine zero three . five mi ). There are five , five six one housing units at an average density of one six three . seven km ( four two three . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine one . nine eight % White, zero . two five % African American, one . nine six % Native American, zero . six seven % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, three . two six % from other races, and one . eight six % from two or more races.  six . zero six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are four , seven eight seven households out of which three three . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five four . six % are married couples living together, nine . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and three two . two % are non-families. two eight . two % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . four three and the average family size is two . nine eight .

In the city the population is spread out with two six . nine % under the age of one eight , nine . five % from one eight to two four , two seven . seven % from two five to four four , two one . seven % from four five to six four , and one four . two % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are nine two . eight males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . three males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three two , four four one , and the median income for a family is $ three nine , seven six six . Males have a median income of $ two nine , two two two versus $ one nine , one zero two for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one seven , zero four zero .  one three . three % of the population and nine . two % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one four . five % of those under the age of one eight and one zero . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Economy 
Woodward serves as a market and processing center for wheat and cattle that also produces hay and poultry. The area includes the Southern Plains Range Research Station, a United States agricultural experiment station. 

Woodward lies in an oil and natural-gas area. Manufactures include oil field equipment, apparel, crude iodine, and printing and publishing. Clothing factories are a relatively recent addition. 

The Museum of Pioneer History and Plains Indians attracts tourists to the city. Boiling Springs State Park lies to the east of Woodward.

 History 
Although a post office was established on March two seven , one eight six six , Baker City was not incorporated until one eight seven four . In one nine one one the city dropped City from its name, but restored it in the late one nine eight zero s in recognition of its history and to further encourage tourism.

Baker City is also the seat of the Roman Catholic diocese for the state of Oregon east of the Cascade Mountains. While the diocese has been sued by about two dozen individuals claiming that they had been sexually abused by priests, it is not affected by the archdiocese of Portland filing for bankruptcy on July six , two zero zero four .

 '''Halfway''' is a city located in Baker County, Oregon. This town took its name from the fact the post office, located on the Alexander Stalker ranch, was halfway between Pine and Cornucopia. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of three three seven .

History
The area was originally used as hunting territory by the Nez Perce, Umatilla, Shoshone and Snake Indian tribes.

It was explored and mapped by Benjamin Bonneville in the one eight three zero s, and first settled by white people in the one eight six zero s. The smaller national forests now combined into the local Wallowa-Whitman National Forest were created in one nine zero eight . Halfway was incorporated in one nine zero nine .

The town has always been primarily a farming and ranching community. There was a small gold rush to nearby Cornucopia, now a ghost town, and some timber industry in the early two zero th century. Major employer the Idaho Power Company now operates three hydroelectric dams on the Snake River. 

Halfway earned a place in the history of the dot-com experience when it received, and accepted in December, one nine nine nine , an offer to rename itself '''Half.com, Oregon''' in exchange for $ one zero zero , zero zero zero , computers for the school, and other financial subsidies. Since the company half.com was bought by eBay in February, two zero zero one , it has not been made clear whether eBay would honor the numerous financial considerations.

The financial conditions that led to the city accepting half.com's offer returned in two zero zero four , when the company owning a promissary note secured by its fairgrounds and improvements demanded payment of over $ five three zero , zero zero zero . Foreclosure of the eight three -year-old fairgrounds would endanger the future of the yearly Pine Valley Fair and the annual rodeo.

 View across the Nith Estuary, close to the Solway Firth.

'''Caerlaverock NNR''' is a National Nature Reserve covering part of the Solway Firth and the land south of Dumfries, in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. It lies between the River Nith and Lochar Water. It is administered by Scottish Natural Heritage.
It has been designated a Biosphere Reserve by UNESCO.

It shares the Solway Firth with another National Nature Reserve in England....

The Reserve covers an area of five five . zero zero km and consists of saltmarsh, vast mudflats and grazing land. It is an internationally important wintering site for waterfowl and wading birds. Virtually the entire population of Svalbard Barnacle Goose overwinters here, ca. two four , zero zero zero . More than one three zero , zero zero zero wading birds have been recorded in winter. In addition, many thousands of birds stop for bed and breakfast while passing through.

 '''Canby''' is a city located in Clackamas County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one two , seven nine zero .

 Geography 
Location of Canby, OregonCanby is located at four five  one five ' five eight  North, one two two  four one ' two six  West ( four five . two six six zero zero two , - one two two . six nine zero six six three ). This puts it about two zero miles SW of Portland. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of nine . eight km ( three . eight mi ).  nine . eight km ( three . eight mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

Canby is separated from its larger urban neighbors by a beautiful stretch of farmland in rolling hills and fields. Entering Canby from the north brings visitors past the beautiful Willamette River and from the south through the historic community of Aurora.

There are four , four eight nine households out of which four zero . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six zero . three % are married couples living together, one zero . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two five . zero % are non-families. two one . two % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  Community 

Canby is a place where the best of small town living meets proximity to the urban culture and amenities in Portland. It is separated by rolling farmland from the Metro area and maintains an active historic downtown core, home to a revitalized business district and family-oriented community events.

The community features excellent schools, neighborhood and regional parks, and active neighborhood groups. The community values its small-town feel and seeks to maintain this even as growth continues to occur. 
 

See also

Hart's Reptile World Zoo located in Canby, Oregon, is a reptile zoo that has gained national notoriety. Reptiles from the exhibit have been featured in videos for Michael Jackson and Tears for Fears. 

 Name 

Canby is named for Gen E. R. S. Canby, a Civil War general who was later killed in the Modoc War by Captain Jack and his group of warriors.

'''Estacada''' (IPA: ) is a city located in Clackamas County, Oregon, roughly three zero miles southeast of Portland. The origin of the city's name is disputed. One explanation is that the city's name is a corruption of the name of a local resident, ''Esther Katie''. There is no evidence that she existed. The more prosaic explanation is that someone with knowledge of the Llano Estacado region of modern-day Texas threw the name in a hat and it won, but somehow the final ''o'' became an ''a''. Whatever the truth, it is doubtless the only place in United States (possibly Planet Earth) bearing the name ''Estacada.'' As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two , three seven one .

 Geography 
Location of Estacada, OregonEstacada is located at four five  one seven ' two four  North, one two two  two zero ' four  West ( four five . two nine zero zero zero nine , - one two two . three three four five three seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two . eight km ( one . one mi ).  two . seven km ( one . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is three . six seven % water. The Clackamas River flows by the town, which drains into the Willamette River, thence the Columbia. There are four dams in the immediate vicinity of Estacada: River Mill Dam, Faraday Dam (a diversionary dam), Cazadero Dam, and North Fork Dam.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , three seven one people, eight five zero households, and five nine one families residing in the city. The population density is eight seven one . nine km ( two , two five nine . six mi ). There are eight eight six housing units at an average density of three two five . eight km ( eight four four . four mi ). The racial makeup of the city is eight four . eight six % White, zero . one seven % African American, one . four three % Native American, one . seven seven % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander, nine . nine one % from other races, and one . eight one % from two or more races.  one two . seven eight % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

In the city the population is spread out with two nine . six % under the age of one eight , one zero . five % from one eight to two four , two eight . five % from two five to four four , two zero . five % from four five to six four , and one one . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three three years. For every one zero zero females there are nine three . two males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . nine males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three nine , two zero zero , and the median income for a family is $ four six , four four five . Males have a median income of $ three seven , two six nine versus $ two two , two six seven for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one seven , zero four nine .  one two . nine % of the population and one zero . one % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one five . eight % of those under the age of one eight and five . nine % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

History and economy

The city was founded in May one nine zero five as a camp for workers building a hydroelectric dam on the nearby Clackamas River in order to supply Portland with electricity. At the time, the river was relatively inaccessible by road, forcing the Oregon Power Railway Company to build a railway to the vicinity of the river to transport crews to the river for the construction of the dam. After the construction of the Hotel Estacada, the town became a weekend destination on the railroad line for residents of Portland. During the week, the train carried freight and work crews to and from Portland. In the early two zero th century, a trolley line connected the town with downtown Portland. The early railroad history of the city is commemorated in a mural in downtown near the town hall. Nowadays, the railway line has been removed; and there is no rail service to Estacada any more. 

After the building of the dams, the primary economy has been lumber. As this has fallen on hard times, the town has been depressed in recent years; many young people have left. The scenic beauty of the area continues to be a weekend draw for residents of Portland.

Schools

There are several schools in immediate Estacada area. In the immediate environs are Eagle Creek Elementary School, River Mill Elementary, Clackamas River Elementary, Estacada Junior High, and Estacada High School. The high school mascot is the Ranger. 

Media
The local newspaper is the ''Clackamas County News''.

 '''Oak Grove''' is a census-designated place located in Clackamas County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of one two , eight zero eight . The town began to take off at the beginning of the two zero th century and many businesses, homes, and streets were built about this time. Oak Grove owes much of its initial growth to the fact that a street car line went down the middle of the town and the Oregon Trail finished a few miles away in Oregon City. Some of the campfire burn from the wagon trains are still visible on the trees. The Street car line went from Portland to Oregon City but closed in the one nine five zero s. Some of the tracks used to be visible on Arista Drive, but they are still visible on a nature trail and a pillar from an old stop is visible outside the current Oak Grove School. Oak Grove School was originally built in one nine zero seven but it burned down about two zero years later. A school was erected in the one nine three zero s with an addition in the one nine six zero s. In the sixties, another school was built was known as North Oak Grove. Oak Grove school was closed in one nine nine nine and all the students shifted to North Oak Grove which was thereafter known as Oak Grove. The former Oak Grove school is still used by the district as a charter school for gifted students and one for bilingual education in Spanish and English. The Downtown of Oak Grove began to die in the one nine five zero s when McLaughlin was built as a major thoroughfare and directed the business and traffic away. Many stores sit along the street and it is known as a very important shopping area for Clackamas county. One of the famous sites along McLaughlin used to be the Holly Farm. This farm sent holly around the world for Christmas time and was paved over and replaced with the Holly Farm Mall.

Oak Grove often receives attempts by the city of Milwaukie, Oregon to annex it and turn it into a part of Milwaukie. This has always been rebuffed by Oak Grove and the area currently remains unincorporated. The county of Clackamas tried to increase the population density of the area and had plans to raise the population of Oak Grove from one two , zero zero zero to six zero , zero zero zero . This did not go over well with the inhabitants who raised questions about where all the people would go and whether the ground could take all this extra infrastructure since Oak Grove was formerly a swamp.

 '''West Linn''' is a city located in Clackamas County, Oregon. It was named after Senator Dr. Lewis Fields Linn of Ste. Genevieve, Missouri, who had advocated the American occupation of Oregon as a counterclaim to the British. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city has grown to a total population of two two , two six one .

History
Major Robert Moore arrived in one eight three nine having been the senior member of the first attempt to create an American colony in Oregon, the Peoria Party. His title stems from his military service in the War of one eight one two , where he served in the Pennsylvania militia, possibly as a battlefield surgeon. Sometime after journeying around the Willamette Valley and Columbia Basin, Moore bought title to approx. one , zero zero zero acres ( four km ) on the west side of the Willamette Falls, across the Willamette River from Oregon City, from a local Native American chief named Wanax-ha, on which he platted a town known as the Robbin's Nest in early one eight four three . He also filed a provisional claim with the then government of the Oregon Country, not knowing if his unique transaction would be honored by the eventual governing laws. The later Territorial Legislature of Oregon voted to rename it Linn City on December two two , one eight four five as a memorial to Dr.Sr. Lewis Fields Linn for whom Linn County is also named. Dr. Linn was a neighbor and family friend of the Moores from their time as settlers in the early Missouri Territory. For many years Linn City was an intense political and commercial rival to the adjacent town of Oregon City but it suffered a series of natural and manmade setbacks, including Moore's death in September of one eight five seven . A great flood put an end to the pioneer settlement in November, one eight six one disbursing many of the surviving family members throughout the Pacific Northwest. However, the seminal village site was later redeveloped as a locked canal and industrial complex decades later and the descendant companies still function to this day.

The current West Linn, incorporated in one nine one three and merged with the adjacent town of Willamette in one nine one six , includes the former townsitesdevelopments of Bolton, Multnomah City, Sunset City, and West Oregon City.

Early two zero zero zero 's West Linn politics were marked by conflict between no-growth advocates and their adversaries. From the November two zero zero zero to the November two zero zero four elections a no-growth advocate, David Dodds, held office as mayor and was supported by a city council having similar thinking. In the two zero zero four elections, however, this group was swept out of office as Norm King and a like minded city council took control on a platform of easing anti-growth controls. The Dodds-led city government also hired John Ellison as police chief. Chief Ellison was quickly embroiled in controversy as several police officers left the force and accepted employment elsewhere. In two zero zero five , after two and one-half years on the job, Mr. Ellison resigned. 

On September two zero , two zero zero five , voters agreed to annex three parcels of land to the city, totalling one three acres.

 Geography 
Location of West Linn, OregonWest Linn is located at four five  two one ' five five  North, one two two  three eight ' two eight  West ( four five . three six five two zero one , - one two two . six four one zero two four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two zero . five km ( seven . nine mi ).  one nine . one km ( seven . four mi ) of it is land and one . three km ( zero . five mi ) of it is water. The total area is six . five seven % water. West Linn is nestled between the Wiillamette and Tualatin rivers with hills rising, sometimes rapidly, from the river banks. The area near the two rivers was, generally speaking, settled first, with later development climbing the more inland hills. Barrington Heights, is an inland area of expansive mansions, whereas the Willamette District, near the spot where the Tualatin river flows into the Willamette river, features older homes and commercial buildings, some of which are historic.

The Camassia Natural Area, in central West Linn, displays a dramatic landscape sculpted by prehistoric floods and hosting an extraordinary floral diversity including rare plants and uncommon wetland and grassland communities.

As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two two , two six one people, eight , one six one households, and six , two seven five families residing in the city. There are eight , six nine seven housing units at an average density of four five four . four km ( one , one seven seven . four mi ). There are eight , one six one households out of which four one . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six five . five % are married couples living together, eight . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and two three . one % are non-families. one eight . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and four . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . seven two and the average family size is three . one one .

In the city the population is spread out with two nine . zero % under the age of one eight , six . one % from one eight to two four , two eight . seven % from two five to four four , two eight . four % from four five to six four , and seven . eight % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three eight years. For every one zero zero females there are nine nine . zero males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine four . three males.

 Famous figures 
Two famous sporting figures have roots in West Linn. Mitch Williams aka Wild Thing, pitched in Major League Baseball for the Texas Rangers, Chicago Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies, Houston Astros, California Angels, and Kansas City Royals before retiring in one nine nine two . Cade McNown starred in football at UCLA then went on to the NFL to play for the Chicago Bears, Miami Dolphins, and currently plays for the San Francisco four nine ers.

'''Cannon Beach''' is a city located in Clatsop County, Oregon, USA. Originally named Ecola, after the creek that empties into the Pacific Ocean to the north of the community, it was renamed in one nine two two to Cannon Beach (the name of the beach that extends south of Ecola creek for eight miles until ending at Arch Cape) at the insistence of the US Post Office because the name was frequently confused with Eola. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , five eight eight .

 Transportation 
Haystack Rock.
While cars are everywhere in Cannon Beach, they are not the best mode of transportation within downtown. Parking spots can be difficult to find, especially in the summer months of tourist season. Most of the business district is easily accessible within walking distance of any parking spot. Biking is also a popular way to get around, as bikes can be used on not only the beach, but also to get around town.

A shuttle also runs from the north of Cannon Beach to the south, helping tourists get from the business district back to their resort or vacation rental, and vice versa. 

 History 
The first recorded American or British journey to this area was made by William Clark, one of the leaders of the Lewis and Clark Expedition in January, one eight zero five , when a group of Native Americans invited him to view a beached whale at the nearby beach.

The beach received its name after a cannon from the US Navy schooner ''Shark'' washed ashore there in one eight four six . The schooner was wrecked while attempting to cross the Columbia Bar, also known as the Graveyard of the Pacific because of the danger of the bar. The name eventually stuck, and today the town takes its names from that famous cannon. It can be seen alongside U.S. Highway one zero one .

Cannon Beach is an affluent resort town; for a period in the one nine eight zero s, its principal gas station had a sign made from stained glass. Although locals and non-resident house owners have rented their houses to tourists, this practice has been the cause of much conflict. Until one nine eight seven , it was illegal to rent ones house for less than one four days in the residential parts of Cannon Beach. 

When the rules were loosened, in response to the recognition that they were being widely ignored, complaints of litter, traffic and noise over the next five years forced the city council to once again tighten the rules, although over one zero zero exceptions for short-term rentals were granted, at first for a period of five years, but since then most have been renewed, and will not expire until January one , two zero zero five . Wrangling over this practice still continues between renting and non-renting residents, most recently with a special election scheduled for March eight , two zero zero five concerning the latest compromise the city council has hammered out.

 Geography 
Cannon Beach is located at four five  five three ' two one  North, one two three  five seven ' three nine  West ( four five . eight eight nine one five five , - one two three . nine six zero seven three eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three . nine km ( one . five mi ).  three . nine km ( one . five mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one , five eight eight people, seven one zero households, and four one eight families residing in the city. The population density is four one one . five km ( one , zero six six . eight mi ). There are one , six four one housing units at an average density of four two five . two km ( one , one zero two . four mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine two . five seven % White, zero . one nine % African American, zero . eight eight % Native American, zero . three one % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, three . two seven % from other races, and two . seven seven % from two or more races.  one zero . five two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are seven one zero households out of which two zero . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four nine . zero % are married couples living together, seven . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and four one . zero % are non-families. three three . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one one and the average family size is two . seven zero .

In the city the population is spread out with one seven . four % under the age of one eight , one two . three % from one eight to two four , two one . five % from two five to four four , three two . one % from four five to six four , and one six . seven % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four four years. For every one zero zero females there are eight six . eight males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight four . four males.

Males have a median income of $ three one , two five zero versus $ two one , six four one for females. The per capita income for the city is $ two four , four six five .  one two . zero % of the population and eight . two % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, one six . three % of those under the age of one eight and two . one % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 City Landmarks 
Cannon Beach is recognized by its well-known landmark, Haystack Rock, located to the southwest of downtown Cannon Beach, near Tolovana Park. This igneous rock has an elevation of three two seven feet, and is often accessible at low tide, especially in the summertime. There is a small cave system that penetrates the rock and can be seen from the coastline. The rock is also protected as a marine sanctuary.

Near Haystack Rock are the Needles, two tall rocks rising straight out of the water. Together with Haystack Rock, the Needles create a photogenic panorama that is even more appealing during a sunset over the Pacific Ocean.

Downtown Cannon Beach is filled with small businesses. Chain stores such as Safeway and McDonalds have been discouraged from building in Cannon Beach in order to preserve the local economy and small town feel. 

The main drag through Cannon Beach is Hemlock Street, which runs from the north end of town to the south, through Tolovana Park. Both ends of the street connect to US Highway one zero one . The separation of the highway and the town's main street help ensure that the highway doesn't get bogged down with intercity traffic and the town doesn't have endure the trucks and tourist traffic.

'''Dumfries''' (''pronounced dum-freece, not dum-fries'') ('''''Dn Phris''''' in Scottish Gaelic) is a Royal Burgh and town of about  three five , zero zero zero people on the River Nith in Dumfries and Galloway in the south west of Scotland. It was the county town of the former county of Dumfriesshire.







Visiting Dumfries

Dumfries, gateway to Galloway and the Machars, occupies a position in the South West of Scotland not far from the border with England.(around two five miles) It has many associations with Robert Burns who lived here in the one seven nine zero s. The Robert Burns Centre is situated in an one eight th century watermill on the west bank of the River Nith. It tells the story of Burns' last years in the town, shows films, and has a cafe and restaurant.

Above the mill there is an one eight th century windmill tower which houses Dumfries Museum and the Camera Obscura Observatory. The Museum has exhibits from prehistoric times, the wildlife of the Solway saltmarshes, stone carvings of Scotland's early Christians, and many Victorian farm implements. The Camera Obscura, originally an astronomical instrument installed in one eight three six , has a table top screen on to which are projected panoramic views of Dumfries and the surrounding countryside.

Across the one five th century Devorgilla Bridge there is Old Bridge House, Dumfries' oldest house, dating from one six six zero and built into the sandstone of the bridge itself. Dumfries has a large number of public houses, including, on the town's High Street, The Globe Inn, which Robert Burns himself frequented. 

The town has one domestic rail link, Dumfries Railway Station.

Dumfries also promotes a sustainable transport infrastructure with prompt access to all main UK destinations via road, largely through the A seven four (M) motorway and A seven five , the latter of which has been criticised due to large amounts of traffic and prevailing safety concerns.

History
In one one eight six , Dumfries was officially given the rights of a royal burgh. Throughout the first five zero years of its foundation the town was at the forefront of the Scottish Borders until the consolidation of Galloway in one two three four . 

Robert Burns
Dumfries was the hometown of Robert Burns from one seven nine one until his death in one seven nine six . The poet is now buried in St. Michaels churchyard in Burns Mausoleum. 
Celebrity
A number of well-known people were educated at Dumfries Academy, among them James Matthew Barrie, author of ''Peter Pan'', John Laurie, actor (Private Frazer in ''Dad's Army''), and Jane Haining, missionary. Dumfries is also the hometown of former F one racer Allan McNish.

Local Economy

Growth
Dumfries has a long history as the county town of a rural backwater. The rich agricultural land between the hills and the sea has for many hundreds of years been carved up into huge estates controlled by hereditary ruling class interests. Since the arrival of the railways a strong middle class has grown in the town and county. The abandonment of the traditional rural economy over the past one hundred years has pulled the very disadvantaged poor from communities scattered across the countryside into local authority and other social housing schemes, and low grade commercial housing, generally in the towns. The displacement of the whole spectrum of the local rural population by the purchasing power of incomers is moving ever faster at the start of the two one st century. The overall effect of this process is to decrease the sustainability of Dumfries as an ecomomic area, and to increase its dependence on a diesel-powered subsidiary relationship to the north of England and the Scottish central belt.
Decline
In recent years, there has been a significant decline in the strength and vitality of local economy. This decline is closely related to a vast change in regional demographics with a noticable number of inhabitants, many of a young age, emigrating to other parts of the United Kingdom to seek professional employment.  
Regeneration
In a bid to stimulate a development in Dumfries, both economically and in a social context, several strategies have been proposed by the controlling authorities. 

In January two zero zero six , Dumfries & Galloway Council announced that plans to build a  one six . five m leisure facility situated in the town centre would commence in the spring. 

Local Authority

Dumfries hosts the headquarters of Dumfries and Galloway Council. 
Civil Arrangements 

Dumfries & Galloway Constabulary
Dumfries is centre to Scotlands smallest police force . Despite its size it is credited in its participation of one the largest criminal investigations in modern history when neighbouring town, Lockerbie, was devastated by the events that took place onboard Pan Am Flight one zero three on December two one st, one nine eight eight .

Areas of Dumfries

Although serving a relatively small population, Dumfries is divided into several key districts. This segmentation lays basis for a strong community based culture. 

Town Centre
Dumfries High Street hosts many of the historical, social and commercial centres of the town. During the one nine nine zero s, these areas enjoyed various aesthetic recognitions from organisations including Scotland in Bloom. Unfortunately such awards are not an innate reality in two zero zero six owing to an increased degenerative appearance throughout many of the town centre's key areas.

Towards the end of two zero zero five , the town's illustrious Midsteeple was dismantled conceding to safety concerns of its structural integrity. This event caused much controversy within the town on the councils capability to maintain key features. The landmark is now in the early stages of reparation, the costs of which are estimated to be around  one . six m. 

Key Districts

Dumfries has several suburbs, including Georgetown, Larchfield, Calside, Lochside, Sandside, Heathhall, Lockerbriggs and Maxwelltown, formerly a burgh in its own right.


Education

Dumfries has several primary schools, approximately one per key district, and four main secondary schools. All of these institutions are governed by the local council and the Scottish Executive. The secondary schools are:

Dumfries Academy
Dumfries High School
Maxwelltown High School
St. Josephs College


The town has recently acquired a university campus, acting as a subsidary for the University of Glasgow and the University of Paisley. The campus offers a limited number of degree level courses, with the majority focusing on Arts, Business & Social Science disciplines. 

Festivals
There are a number of festivals which take place throughout the year, mostly based on traditional values.
''Guid'' Neighbours
Guid Neighbours ('''''Guid Nychburris''''' in Scottish Gaelic) is the main festival of the year, a ceremony which is largely based on the theme of a positive community spirit. 
Dumfries and Galloway 
The name Dumfries and Galloway is given to one of Scotland's three two council areas comprising the former ( one nine seven five - nine six ) districts of Nithsdale, Annandale and Eskdale, the Stewartry of Kirkcudbrightshire and the Machars. 

Dumfries Lieutenancy Area
Dumfries Lieutenancy

Dumfries also lends its name to a Lieutenancy Area, similar in boundaries to the former Dumfriesshire county.

 '''Seaside''' is a city located in Clatsop County, Oregon. The name Seaside came from a summer resort built by the railroad magnate, Ben Holladay in the one eight seven zero s, Seaside House, located a mile south of the business center. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five , nine zero zero .

 Geography 
Location of xxx, NebraskaSeaside is located at four five  five nine ' three four  North, one two three  five five ' two zero  West ( four five . nine nine two eight five zero , - one two three . nine two two one zero eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one zero . four km ( four . zero mi ).  one zero . zero km ( three . nine mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is three . nine nine % water.

Seaside lies on the edge of the Pacific Ocean, at the southern end of the Clatsop Plains, about two nine km ( one eight mi) south of where the Columbia River empties into the Pacific. The Necanicum River bisects the town and flows out to the ocean at the northern edge of town. Tillamook Head towers over the south edge of town.

 Transportation 
Seaside has one major highway, U.S. Highway one zero one . 

Seaside is served by an intercity bus system. 

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are five , nine zero zero people, two , six five six households, and one , five one one families residing in the city. The population density is five nine zero . two km ( one , five two nine . four mi ). There are four , zero seven eight housing units at an average density of four zero seven . nine km ( one , zero five seven . one mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine three . zero eight % White, zero . three four % African American, zero . nine eight % Native American, one . zero seven % Asian, zero . two nine % Pacific Islander, two . one seven % from other races, and two . zero seven % from two or more races.  six . four six % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two , six five six households out of which two five . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three nine . six % are married couples living together, one two . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and four three . one % are non-families. three five . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one four . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one seven and the average family size is two . seven six .

In the city the population is spread out with two one . four % under the age of one eight , eight . four % from one eight to two four , two six . zero % from two five to four four , two five . one % from four five to six four , and one nine . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is four one years. For every one zero zero females there are nine zero . five males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight six . five males.

Out of the total population, two five . two % of those under the age of one eight and one one . four % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

History
About January one , one eight zero six a group of men from the Lewis and Clark Expedition built a salt-making cairn at the present site of Seaside. The Native American name for the Clatsop village near the cairn was ''Ne-co-tat''. The town was incorporated in one eight nine nine .

Every spring, Seaside hosts the Dorchester Conference, a convention of the Oregon Republican Party. This convention was founded in one nine six four , by then-state representative Bob Packwood as a forum for liberal Republicans, but within the next few years attracted interest from other Republicans, and in the one nine nine zero s was dominated by members of the conservative branch of the party. The conference has over the years attracted visits from presidential candidates, debates between Republican primary candidates, and discussions of wider political and social issues.

'''Warrenton''' is a city located in Clatsop County, Oregon, USA. The city is named for D.K. Warren (Daniel Knight), an early settler. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of four , zero nine six .

 History 
The first settlement within the Warrenton city limits was Lexington, which was laid out in one eight four eight , and served as the first county seat for Clatsop county. The name fell out of use, and this area became known as Skipanon, which is preserved in the name of Skipanon River which flows through the town. A Lexington post office operated intermittently between one eight five zero and one eight five seven ; a Skipanon post office operated without a break from one eight seven one to one nine zero three .

Warrenton was platted in one eight eight nine , and incorporated as a city in one eight nine nine . Built on tidal flats, it relied on a system of dikes built by Chinese laborers to keep the Columbia River from flooding the town.

Warrenton has a charter fishing boat port.

 Geography

 '''Clatskanie''' (IPA: ) is a city located in Columbia County, Oregon. It was named for the Clatskanie River, which empties into the Columbia River within the city limits. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , five two eight .

History

According to some reports, the original name of this town when it was platted in one eight eight four was Bryantville. However, the post office in this location is shown as Clatskanie as early as December, one eight seven one .

Clatskanie comes from a Native American word, ''Tlatskani''. According to the Clatsop County pioneer Silas B. Smith, ''Tlatskani'' was a point in the Nehalem River that was reached from the Columbia River by way of the Youngs River or by way of the Clatskanie River. The native inhabitants applied the word ''Tlatskani'' to the streams they would follow in order to get to that point, and not the streams themselves, for they were not in the habit of naming the streams. The white men who settled here later carelessly applied the word to the streams.

Clatskanie is also the name of a Native American people, whose numbers dwindled from smallpox, intermittent fever, warfare, and intermarriage until they numbered only three people in a one nine one zero poll.

 Geography 
Location of Clatskanie, OregonClatskanie is located at four six  six ' one one  North, one two three  one two ' one three  West ( four six . one zero three one four three , - one two three . two zero three seven zero one ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three . one km ( one . two mi ).  three . one km ( one . two mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

Clatskanie is sorrounded by many small communities, including: Quincy, Mayger, Inglis, Lacoda, Swedetown, Clatskanie Heights, Delena, Alston, Kerry, Woodson, and Marshland.

 '''Rainier''' is a city located in Columbia County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , six eight seven .

History

Rainier was founded on the banks of the Columbia River in one eight five one by Charles E. Fox. The name was taken from Mount Rainier in Washington, which can be seen from the town.

For much of the last quarter of the twentieth century, Rainier was known to the rest of Oregon as home to Trojan Nuclear Power Plant, the only commercial nuclear reactor in the state, which supplied electricity to Portland and its suburbs starting in March of one nine seven six . This reactor failed to be an economical source of electricity, and was decommissioned in January one nine nine three .

'''Vernonia''' is a city located in Columbia County, Oregon. The city is located on the Nehalem River, in a valley on the western side of the Coast Ranges. It is located the heart of the of the most important timber-producing areas of the state, and logging has played an important role in the history of the town. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two , two two eight .

 History 
The community was first settled in one eight seven six by Judson Weed and Ozias Cherrington, both of Ohio. Sometime afterwards, the question of a name for the community came up, and Cherrington suggested the name of his daughter in Ohio, which was adopted. Unfortunately, since he had left Ohio around one eight seven three , he misremembered his daughter's name, which was ''Vernona'', so the town is not actually named after her. Cherrington died of a farming accident in one eight nine four , having never seen his daughter since his departure from Ohio.

Vernonia started to become more than an isolated farming community on July one zero , one nine two four when the Oregon-American Lumber company opened a state-of-the-art lumber mill, which was supported by a railroad line connecting Vernonia to the rest of the country. Oregon-American merged with Long-Bell in May, one nine five three , which itself merged with International Paper Company in November, one nine five seven . International Paper judged the mill antiquated, and closed it on December two zero , one nine five seven .

 Geography 
Location of Vernonia, OregonVernonia is located at four five  five one ' three five  North, one two three  one one ' two one  West ( four five . eight five nine eight four six , - one two three . one eight nine one two five ).

 '''Marcus Giamatti''' (born October three , one nine six one in New Haven, Connecticut) is an American actor. He is the son of former Yale University president and Major League Baseball commissioner A. Bartlett Giamatti and older brother of actor Paul Giamatti who attended Choate Rosemary Hall and then Yale University. He is a graduate of the Yale School of Drama, where he received the Carole Dye Award for Excellence in Acting.

Giamatti started his career on the soap opera ''One Life To Live'', but is best known for his role on ''Judging Amy''. He has also guest-starred on a number of popular series, such as ''The X-Files'' and ''Homicide: Life on the Street''.

An accomplished musician, Giamatti plays bass guitar in several bands in Los Angeles, including the alternative folk-rock group ''Olivea'' and the psychedelic jam band ''Rebel Soul''. He is also a session musician and is a member of ''Musicians Local four seven ''.

 Paul Giamatti

'''Paul Edward Valentine Giamatti''' (born June six , one nine six seven ) is an Academy Award-nominated American actor.

Early life
Giamatti was born in New York City, New York to A. Bartlett Giamatti, a Yale University professor who later became president of the university and commissioner of Major League Baseball. His mother, Toni Smith, was a teacher at Hopkins School. Giamatti's paternal grandfather was the child of Italian immigrants; his other grandparents were American.

Giamatti has a brother, Marcus, who is also an actor. Giamatti attended the elite boarding school Choate Rosemary Hall, was an English major at Yale, and has a Master's degree in Fine Arts from the Yale School of Drama. Following his graduation, he performed in numerous theatrical productions (including Broadway) before appearing in some small television and film roles in the early one nine nine zero s.

Career
His first high profile role was in the film adaptation of Howard Stern's ''Private Parts.'' Paul Giamatti played Kenny Pig Vomit Rushton, Howard's antagonistic program director at WNBC. Howard praised Paul's performance often on his radio program, calling for him to be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. That didn't happen, but Paul's career certainly received a boost. He appeared in a number of supporting roles in big-budget movies such as ''The Truman Show, Saving Private Ryan,'' and ''The Negotiator'' (all one nine nine eight ). In one nine nine nine he played Bob Zmuda (and Tony Clifton) in the Andy Kaufman biopic, ''Man on the Moon''. Paul Giamatti continued to appear in major studio releases such as ''Big Momma's House'' ( two zero zero zero ) and the ''Planet of the Apes'' remake ( two zero zero one ), and co-starred in ''Big Fat Liar'' ( two zero zero two ).

He is most often confused in public as Rob Schneider. When he guest hosted for ''Saturday Night Live'', he had a sketch reflecting this.

Awards
Paul's most acclaimed performances were in lead roles in ''American Splendor'' ( two zero zero three ) and ''Sideways'' ( two zero zero four ). He was nominated for a Golden Globe for the latter but did not win. He was nominated for a Golden Globe and an Oscar in two zero zero five for his role in ''Cinderella Man'' and also won the SAG award for Best Supporting Actor for the same movie.

 '''Bandon''' (IPA: ) is a city located in Coos County, Oregon, on the south side of the mouth of the Coquille River. It was named by George Bennet, an Irish peer, who settled nearby in one eight seven three and named the town after Bandon, Ireland, his native home. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two , eight three three .

 Economy 
Like many towns on the Oregon coast, Bandon had significant fishing and timber industries which came to an end by the one nine eight zero s. Currently Bandon is a center of cranberry production. This crop was introduced in one eight five five by Charles McFarlin, for whom the MacFarlin hybrid is named.
Today however, Bandon's economy revolves around the golfing and tourism industries.

'''Bandon Dunes Golf Resort''', located just north of the town of Bandon, employed more than four five zero in the summer of two zero zero five and, because of the walking only experience, more than three zero zero caddies. All of the resort's three course are ranked in the top one zero zero in the world and top five zero in the United States by Golf Magazine (September two zero zero five edition)  the only resort in the U.S. with this claim to fame. Bandon Dunes was the first course to open at the resort. Opened on May, one nine , one nine nine nine Bandon Dunes was designed by Scotsman David McLay Kidd. Instantly garnering high praise the course features gorse lined fairways and numerous pot bunkers. The resort's second one eight hole course, Pacific Dunes, opened on July one st, two zero zero one . Pacific Dunes was designed by Michigan architect, Tom Doak and sculpted by his design firm, Renaissance Design, Inc. Pacific Dunes also opened to glowing reviews and quickly surpassed Bandon Dunes as the highest rated course on the property. The resort's third course, Bandon Trails was designed by the team of Bill Coore and Ben Crenshaw. Bandon Trails opened on June one st two zero zero five . Bandon Trails departs from its siblings in that no holes are routed along the Pacific Ocean. The course meanders through dunes, meadows, and forest land. Along with being one of Coos County's major employer, Bandon Dunes is affecting nearby North Bend Municipal Airport, two five miles north of the golf resort. The commercial airport recently received funding to expand the terminal facilities.

History
Bandon was founded by the Irish peer George Bennet, who also introduced gorse (''Ulex europaeus'') into the local area, which in the following decades went wild and could be found flourishing in both the town and in the neighboring countryside.

On September two six , one nine three six , embers blown from a nearby slash fire of a logging crew enflamed gorse growing inside Bandon, and ignited a fire inside the city, causing massive destruction. Bandon's entire commercial district was destroyed. The total loss stated at the time was three million dollars, with one one fatalities. Stewart Holbrook vividly described this conflagration in his essay The Gorse of Bandon.

 Chronology of events 
 one five seven nine Francis Drake is said to have sought shelter in the bay for the Golden Hinde and its crew.
 one eight five three City founded and named Marshfield after the Massachusetts hometown of one of the founders.
 one eight six six Cape Arago Lighthouse begins operation.
 one eight seven one Marshfield post office established.
 one eight seven two Coos Bay Wagon Road opens, connecting Coos County with Douglas County's Umpqua River valley, across the Coast Range of mountains.
 one eight seven four Marshfield incorporated.
 one nine zero eight The first automobile arrives in Marshfield via the Coos Bay Wagon Road. (Previous autos arrived by ship at the Port of Coos Bay, or by way of lesser trails.)
 one nine four four Residents vote to name the city '''Coos Bay'''.
 one nine two two A fire ends up burning down a large portion of the business district.
 one nine two five The Egyptian Theatre opens. Originally equipped with one screen (later increased to three), the playhouse operates for eight zero years before closing in December two zero zero five . On Jan. three zero , two zero zero six , its owner sells the building to Coos Bay's urban renewal agency, which plans to reopen the Egyptian under the management of a nonprofit agency.
 one nine two eight KOOS-AM radio begins broadcasting.
 one nine four two Nearby Mt. Emily becomes the first U.S. mainland site to be bombed by the Japanese in World War II.
 one nine six two The most powerful non-tropical storm in U.S. mainland history, the Columbus Day Storm, hits.
 one nine seven two The Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area is established.
 one nine nine nine The MV New Carissa freighter runs aground.
 two zero zero two Three Coos Bay firemen die when the roof of a burning car-supply store collapses. It is considered the worst loss of life for a fire department in modern Oregon history.

 '''Prineville''' is a city located in, and the county seat of Crook County. It was named for the first merchant located in the present location, Barney Prine. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of seven , three five six .

 History 
Prineville was founded in one eight seven seven when Monroe Hodges filed the original plat for the city. The post office for the community had been established with the name of Prine in April one three , one eight seven one , but changed to Prineville on December two three , one eight seven two . The city incorporated in one eight eight zero , and obtained its first high school in one nine zero two .

Long the major town in central Oregon, Prineville was snubbed in one nine one one when the railroad tycoons James J. Hill and Edward H. Hillman bypassed the city as they laid track south from The Dalles. In a period when the presence of a railroad meant the difference between prosperity and the eventual fate as a ghost town, in a one nine one seven election, Prineville residents voted three five five to one to build their own railway, and raised the money to connect their town to the main line one nine miles away.

Helped by timber harvests from the nearby Ochoco National Forest, the City of Prineville Railroad prospered for decades. The profits from the railroad were so abundant that between one nine six four and one nine six eight , the city levied no property taxes. However, with the decline of the timber industry in Oregon, the revenue from the railroad have vanished: in two zero zero three , the railroad reported a loss of $ four zero zero , zero zero zero .
