 '''Brookings''' is a city located in Curry County, Oregon. It was named after John E. Brookings, president of the Brookings Lumber and Box Company, which founded the city in one nine zero eight . As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five , four four seven . As of two zero zero five , Brookings had a population of over six , zero zero zero within the city limits. The total population of the Brookings area is over one three , zero zero zero , which includes Harbor, a CDP, and others. There have been numerous attempts to annex the unicorporated areas into Brookings. While most attempts failed over the years, one large area north of town owned by  '''Borax''' has succeeded and in January two zero zero six the city approved another for a six zero seven -acre parcel in the hills above Harbor. The city also annexed a three . five -mile stretch of Highway one zero one to connect to the new development. These new developments have the potential to add thousands of homes over the next two zero years, although developers expect many of them to be occupied only seasonally.

Due to its location, Brookings is subject to winter (and less frequently summer) temperatures considered unseasonably warm for the Oregon Coast. Temperatures can reach seven zero to eight zero degrees Fahrenheit ( two one to two seven degrees Celsius) throughout the year. This is due in part to the marine influences from its location on the Pacific Ocean, but mostly from its situation at the foot of the Klamath Mountains, whose winds compress and warm the air flowing onto Brookings. This is called the Brookings effect or Chetco effect. Fog is common in the summer.

 History 
While John E. Brookings was responsible for the founding of Brookings as a company town, it was his cousin Robert S. Brookings, who was responsible for its actual design. The latter Brookings hired Bernard Maybeck, an architect based in San Francisco who was later involved in the Panama-Pacific Exposition to lay out the plat of the townsite.

On September nine th, one nine four two , Mt. Emily, near Brookings, became the first site in the continental United States to suffer aerial bombardment in wartime. A Japanese floatplane piloted by Nobuo Fujita launched from submarine I- two five was loaded with incendiary bombs and sent to start massive fires in the dense forests of the Pacific Northwest. The attack caused only minor damage. Fujita would be invited back to Brookings in one nine six two and he presented the town his family's four zero zero -year old samurai sword in friendship after the Japanese government was given assurances that he would not be tried as a war criminal. Brookings made him an honorary citizen several days before his death in one nine nine seven . 

Since the one nine eight zero s, Brookings has attracted retirees, largely from California, who have come to form a sizeable minority of the population. Their political influence is felt in routinely voting against new taxes. It is also home for a number of people who commute to jobs in California--mostly at nearby Pelican Bay State Prison.

 '''Port Orford''' is a town located in Curry County, Oregon. It is located on the southern Oregon coast, at the northern end of what coastal oregonians call the Banana Belt, due to the fact that the weather from Port Orford south is warmer and noticeably different than the weather north of Cape Blanco. The town takes it name from George Vancouver's original name for Cape Blanco, which he named for George, Earl of Orford, a much respected friend. It was later changed to the name of the town close by, possibly also referring to the deep harbor beside the town, that was often used during storms. 

The Port Orford Heads State Park is located on a bluff above town and has three main walking trails ... the Cove, Tower and Headland trails. From each of these vantage points (at the right time of year) you can see commercial fishing boats, orcas, grey whales, california and stellar sea lions and various seabirds. The Headland Trail offers an unrestricted view of Cape Blanco to the north and is a very popular whale watching spot during the Fall. From one nine three four to one nine seven zero , the park was home to one of the first lifeboat stations on the Oregon Coast. The recently opened Museum and Interpretive Center is on the National Register of Historic Places. Take time to inspect the station's refurbished, unsinkable three six -foot motor lifeboat. In the museum, read about the one nine four two Japanese submarine activity off the south Oregon coast. Two of those attacks involved bombing runs made by a submarine-launched float plane. As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one , one five three . 

 one nine nine zero Aerial view of Port Orford

History
Native Americans originally lived in the area.

Oregon Coast near Port Orford

Captain William Tichenor was the first to settle in the area of the town, which was an important early center for shipping Port Orford Cedar. It was the county seat for Curry between one eight five five and one eight five nine ; while it was not formally incorporated until one nine three five , it was the first town to do so in the county.

In October of one nine four one , then mayor Gilbert Gable, frustrated with the condition of the state roads around Port Orford, whose poor condition hampered economic development, suggested that a number of counties along the Oregon and California state border should secede and create the State of Jefferson. This movement came to an end with US involvement in World War II.

The Port boasts the only dry dock port on the west coast where the fishing boats are lifted in and out of the water by operated cranes.

 Geography 
Port Orford is located at four two  four four ' five nine  North, one two four  two nine ' five three  West ( four two . seven four nine seven one three , - one two four . four nine seven nine five two ). It is two eight miles north of Gold Beach on U.S. Highway one zero one .

The city is adjacent to Cape Blanco, considered by many to be the furthest point west in the lower four eight states, and located just north of Humbug Mountain, which is considered the tallest mountain in the lower four eight to descend directly into an ocean.

 '''Bend''' is a city located in Deschutes County, Oregon, United States. The name Bend was derived from Farewell Bend, the designation used by early pioneers to refer to the location along the Deschutes River where the town eventually was planted, one of the few fordable points along the river. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five two , zero two nine . As of two zero zero five , there are about seven zero , zero zero zero people, and still growing. 

Bend is located on the edge of the Ponderosa pine forest on the west as it transitions into the high desert plateau, characterized by junipers, sagebrush, bitter-brush, and little water. Originally a logging town, Bend has become identified as a jump-off point for multiple outdoor sports; such as fishing, hiking, camping, rock climbing, skiing, and golf.

 History 

Historic Tower Theater in downtown Bend

Until the winter of one eight two four , the Bend area was known only to Native Americans who hunted and fished there. In that year, members of a fur trapping party led by Peter Skene Ogden visited the area. John C. Fremont, Dr. John Strong Newberry and other Army survey parties came next. Then pioneers heading further west went through the area and forded the Deschutes River at Farewell Bend. 

Actual settlement did not occur until the early one nine zero zero s with the founding of the Pilot Butte Development Company by Alexander M. Drake. A small community developed around 
the bend in the river and in one nine zero four a city was incorporated by a general vote of the community's three zero zero residents. On January four , one nine zero five the city held its first official meeting as an incorporated municipality, appointing A. H. Goodwillie as the first mayor. Twelve years later, Deschutes County was formed from the western half of Crook County and Bend was designated as the county seat. In one nine two nine , Bend amended the charter and adopted the managercouncil form of government.

The settlement was originally known as Farewell Bend.

Bend, Oregon is home to David Stoliar who was the sole survivor of an attack on the Struma, a ship carrying Jewish refugees from the holocaust. Other native sons include the poet and American philosopher Joel Wright.

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of eight three . five km ( three two . two mi ).  eight two . nine km ( three two . zero mi ) of it is land and zero . six km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . six eight % water.

Just south of Bend is Newberry National Volcanic Monument easily reached on

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are five two , zero two nine people, two one , zero six two households, and one three , three nine five families residing in the city. The population density is six two seven . four km ( one , six two four . eight mi ). There are two two , five zero seven housing units at an average density of two seven one . four km ( seven zero two . nine mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine three . nine eight % White, zero . two eight % African American, zero . seven nine % Native American, one . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero eight % Pacific Islander, one . seven five % from other races, and two . one two % from two or more races.  four . six one % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

Bend is central Oregon's most populated city, with a projected population within its city limits of six five , two one zero in two zero zero five .

 Weather 
Bend's climate is typical of the high desert with cool nights and sunny days. Annual precipitation averages one zero - one three inches, part of which is the average snowfall of three four inches. The winter season in Bend provides typical daytime temperatures in the four zero 's to five zero 's. Nighttime temperatures range anywhere from two two to five one .

A typical central Oregon summer is marked with daily temperatures in the eight zero 's and nine zero 's during the day, and the mid four zero 's and five zero 's during the night. Hard frosts are not unheard of during the summer months. Autumn usually brings warm, dry days and cooler nights, and Bend is known for its annual Indian summer. 

 Economy 
Tourism is one of Bend's largest sectors. Mount Bachelor ski resort brings in tourists from all over Oregon, Washington, and Northern California. The nearby Cascade Lakes are also a large draw for tourists. Recreational activities include downhill and cross country skiing, hiking, rafting, golfing, camping, and fishing to picnicking, rock climbing and general sightseeing.

Bend is also home to the Deschutes Brewery, the largest of several microbreweries in the city. Since two zero zero four , Bend has also hosted a film festival (Bendfilm).

Much of Bend's rapid growth in recent years is also due to its attraction as a retirement destination.

The nearest commercial airport is Roberts Field, one eight miles north.

Bend is the only metropolitan area west of the Mississippi without a public bus system. A measure that would create a transit district on the November, two zero zero four ballot was defeated five three to four one percent.

 Education 
The Bend area is serviced by the BendLaPine school district. There are four high schools (grades nine - one two ), four middle schools (grades six - eight ), one two elementary schools (grades K- five ) and three magnet schools. There are several private schools within the area as well. 
Central Oregon Community College (COCC) along with Oregon State University (OSU) serves the community with both two and four year programs.

 Sports 
Bend is home of the Bend Elks of the West Coast Collegiate Baseball League. The Elks play at historic Vince Genna Stadium. 
Bend is also home of the Central Oregon Hotshots of the International Basketball League.

'''La Pine''' is a census-designated place located in Deschutes County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of five , seven nine nine . The community is in fairly isolated area of central Oregon, consisting of a fairly loose collection of homes and businesses along U.S. Highway nine seven about two three miles southeast of Bend. Most of the residential development is second-home, vacation-homes, and retirement homes, and concealed from the highway itself. Several peaks of the Cascade Range are prominently visible from the community.

La Pine is in the valley of the Little Deschutes River, a tributary of the Deschutes River. The river provides recreational opportunities such as fishing, swimming, canoeing, and other leisure activities.

History
La Pine was founded in the one nine th century with Huntington Road as the main street. The fledgling community quickly grew and prospered until the combination of a failed community water system and rapid growth of Bend caused a slowdown to occur. Today, La Pine is beginning to grow once again, but this time as a bedroom community to Bend, making Deschutes County one of the fasted growing counties in America.

 '''Sisters''' is a city located in Deschutes County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of nine five nine . By two zero zero five the population had grown to about one five zero zero with growth predicted to four seven zero zero by two zero two zero .

Location of Sisters, Oregon

 Geography 
Sisters is located at four four  one seven ' two seven  North, one two one  three two ' five six  West ( four four . two nine zero eight two eight , - one two one . five four nine zero two four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of three . eight km ( one . five mi ).  one . two five miles of Squaw Creek run through the southern half of town.
The main highway through downtown, with a lot of pedestrian traffic, 
is known for its many specialty stores and galleries.

 Recreation 
Sisters is surrounded by the Sisters District of the Deschutes National Forest. Hiking, biking and horse riding trails go from the city limits into the Three Sisters Wilderness. The
 Sisters Community Trails Committee is working to improve the trail network.

 Hoodoo Ski Area is two zero miles west of town.

Golf courses include Black Butte Ranch and Aspen Lakes.

 Schools 
The Sisters area is served by Sisters School District six , one of the most successful and highly acclaimed school districts of its size in the state of Oregon. The district is responsible for the education of approximately one , three zero zero students at four facilities. 
 Sisters Elementary School - Kindergarten through Grade five . 
 Sisters Middle School - Grades six through eight .
 Sisters Senior High School - Grades nine through one two .
 Sisters High School Alternative Programs - Grades nine through one two .

The Sisters Schools Foundation helps to fund programs that have been reduced by budget problems.

 History 
Camp Polk was established as a military post in one eight six five in response to the Paiute Indian wars that
were raging throughout eastern Oregon during the one eight six zero s and seven zero s.
Named after the Oregon county from which the camps commanding officer hailed, it consisted of
a group of cabins along the west bank of Squaw Creek, about three miles northeast of Sisters. The
troops spent the winter of one eight six five - six six there.
After discovering that there was no Indian problem they left. Around one eight seven zero , the area was homesteaded by Samuel Hindeman who also ran the post office. The
post office at Camp Polk was moved to the present site of Sisters in one eight eight eight , and the name was changed to
Sisters after the Three Sisters mountains that
dominate its western skyline.

 Sisters Community Garden

The local newspaper is the Nugget News published weekly on Wednesdays. It is free and available at most businesses in town.

 '''Reedsport''' is a city located in Douglas County, Oregon. It was named for a local settler, Alfred W. Reed, who founded the city in one nine one two . As of the two zero zero zero census, it had a total population of four , three seven eight . 

 History 
According to the ''Oregon Blue Book'', Reedsport was established on the estuary of the Umpqua River on January seven , one eight five two . The post office was created July one seven , one nine one two .

Built on marshy ground, for much of its history Reedsport has struggled with frequent flooding; most of its early buildings were elevated three to eight feet above town. Following a devastating flood in one nine six four , a dike was constructed to protect the lower town.

In the last quarter of the two zero th century, Reedsport has struggled with the collapse of the Oregon timber industry. Although the U.S. Forest Service maintains a local office in the town, Reedsport's historic connection with the timber industry ended in one nine nine nine with the closing of the International Paper plant in nearby Gardiner.

 Geography 
Location of Reedsport, OregonReedsport is located at four three  four one ' five six  North, one two four  six ' four four  West ( four three . six nine eight seven eight nine , - one two four . one one two one four zero ). It is five four miles northwest of Roseburg, where Oregon State Highway three eight meets U.S. Highway one zero one .

 Demographics

The '''People First Party''' (, pinyin: Qnmndng) is a conservative political party in the Republic of China on Taiwan. It was founded by James Soong and his supporters after his failed independent bid for the presidency in two zero zero zero . Soong is currently the chairman and dominates much of its politics. Its title, ''Qnmn'', literally means Close-to-People and has Confucian connotations. 

The official goals of PFP, as regards to cross-strait relationships and diplomacy, is for the ROC to: participate in more international organizations, promote Chinese culture overseas and seek economic and cultural interaction between Taiwan and the mainland. Its views are seen as generally favorable towards Chinese reunification and staunchly against Taiwan independence.

The party maintains a close but tense relationship with the Kuomintang as part of the pan-blue coalition. However, since PFP had, like the New Party, grown out of the KMT, the two parties had to compete for the same set of voters. This dynamic in which both the KMT and PFP must simultaneously compete and cooperate with each other has led to complex and interesting politics.

In several notable cases, this has led to situations in which both parties have run candidates, but close to the election the party with the less popular candidate unofficially drops out of the race. This in turn has led to some notable situations when either the PFP or the KMT is campaigning against its own candidate, which has led to intra-party resentment.

To avoid a repeat of this effect, which led to the election of Democratic Progressive Party candidate Chen Shui-bian to the presidency in two zero zero zero by a low share of votes, Chairman Soong ran as vice-president on KMT Chairman Lien Chan's presidential ticket in the two zero zero four presidential election.

 Soong Chu-yu

'''James Chu-yu Soong''' (  Wade-Giles: Sung Ch'u-y; pinyin: Sng Ch y; born March one six , one nine four two ) is a politician in the Republic of China on Taiwan. He founded and chairs the People First Party, which favors eventual Chinese reunification.

 Early life and education 
Soong was born in Hunan Province in mainland China. His father, Soong Ta, was a career soldier staunchly loyal to Chiang Kai-shek who rose to the rank of Major General in the Nationalist Army. With the Nationalist defeat in the Chinese Civil War, the family fled to Taiwan in one nine four nine . He earned his bachelor's degree in diplomacy from National Chengchi University in one nine six four . During this time, he was remembered for wearing business suits every day to fit his career ambitions.

Soong travelled to the United States for graduate school and received an M.A. in political science from the University of California, Berkeley in one nine six seven and an M.S. in library science from the Catholic University of America in one nine seven one . He earned a Ph.D. in political science from Georgetown University in one nine seven four .

While at Berkeley, Soong met his future wife Viola Chen (  ). They later had a son and a daughter.

 Rise to power 
As he was finishing his doctoral studies, he was recommended by Government Information Office (GIO) Director Frederick Chien to be then-Premier Chiang Ching-kuo English secretary. Soong served as Secretary to Premier from one nine seven four - one nine seven seven and with Chiang Ching-kuo's accession to the presidency, the Personal Secretary to the President from one nine seven eight - one nine eight one and one nine eight four - one nine eight nine . Soong gained his public fame when he addressed the nation following the Carter administration's decision to break ties with the ROC in order to switch diplomatic ties to the People's Republic of China on December one six , one nine seven eight in which he gave a patriotic condemnation of the American position and a ringing defense of the ROC.

Soon afterwards, President Chiang promoted Soong to become the youngest Director-General of the Government Information Office, which he served until from one nine seven nine to one nine eight four . He was accused by his critics of aggressive censorship, including excessive use of libel laws and prison sentences to silence critics, and involvement in the suppression of the Kaohsiung Incident, during which he called Shih Ming-teh the king of pirates. Soong received widespread disapproval in one nine eight one for revoking the press licence of Tina Chou of the Associated Press for her violation of the GIO's orders to refrain from publishing autopsy results of Professor Chen Wen-cheng, who died at the National Taiwan University campus under mysterious circumstances and was suspected to have been murdered by government agents. Soong's supporters point out that, despite this record, it was under Soong (later as governor) that censorship was greatly relaxed as were limits on the use of Taiwanese in the electronic media.

Soong and the rise of Lee Teng-hui

Upon Chiang Ching-kuo's death in one nine eight eight , Soong was seen as instrumental in consolidating the power of the new president, Lee Teng-hui. Soong was part of the Palace Faction (  ) that included Chiang loyalists such as Hau Pei-tsun and Lee Huan and which sought to limit Lee Teng-hui and his native Taiwanese faction's role in the government. During the KMT's central standing committee on the day of Chiang's funeral, when the Palace Faction sought to delay Lee's accession to the party Chairmanship, Soong unexpectedly made an impassioned plea in favor of Lee, declaring that Each day of delay is a day of disrespect to Ching-kuo.  He also made a veiled criticism of Soong May-ling (with whom he was unrelated), implying that she had returned to Taiwan after her stepson's death to try to reassume power.

Soong established himself as one of the few mainlanders who were also loyal to Lee. In support of Soong, Lee coined the term New Taiwanese to describe a person born in mainland China, raised in Taiwan, who calls Taiwan home. Lee moved swiftly to promote Soong to KMT Secretary-General, a position Soong held from one nine eight nine to one nine nine three . In one nine nine three , Lee appointed him Governor of Taiwan Province.

 Governorship 
In one nine nine four Soong became first and only directly elected Governor of Taiwan. He was widely perceived to be an excellent campaigner and his excellent showing in the governorship ended hopes by the DPP of a Yeltsin effect, by which an elected governor would have more legitimacy than the national government.

Despite his Mainlander background, Soong proved to be a popular politician among all ethnic groups on Taiwan, in part because he was one of the first KMT politicians to attempt to use the Taiwanese language in political and formal occasions, despite speaking it rather poorly.

After Premier Lien Chan was elected vice president in one nine nine six , the premiership was to be vacated. Soong felt that as Governor of Taiwan, he was natural successor of Lien, but Lee believed that Soong should serve out his term. Lee appointed Vincent Siew, whom Soong considered a subordinate, and led to their split.

The position Governor of Taiwan was eliminated in one nine nine eight following a National Development Council meeting in one nine nine six , when it suggested the administrative structure of the Republic of China government be streamlined. Soong and his supporters believe this to have been a political move done by Lee to cut off Soong's power base, but proponents of the downsizing called it a pragmatic move to eliminate contradictory administrative territory. Soong tendered his resignation on December three one of the same year, but Lee did not accept.

 two zero zero zero presidential elections 
After losing the KMT presidential nomination to then-vice president Lien Chan, Soong ran as an independent in the two zero zero zero Presidential elections. Soong advocated a gradual union between Taiwan and the mainland by first signing a non-aggression pact followed by the formation of a cross-strait union similar to the European Union. His platform called for the characterization of relations between the Mainland and Taiwan as neither foreign nor domestic. Although widely seen as the candidate most friendly to Mainland China, Soong took particular effort to counter the perception that he would sell out Taiwan. 

The KMT responded by expelling Soong and his supporters from the party. In the final months leading to the two zero zero zero elections, the KMT, then under Lee Teng-hui's leadership, sued Soong for theft, alleging that as party Secretary-General, he stole millions of Taiwan dollars in cash intended for the family of the late President Chiang Ching-kuo and hid the money in the Chunghsing Bills Finance Company. The KMT alleged that Soong wired the stolen money, summing up to one two million US dollars, into more than two zero accounts of his relatives in the United States. Among them, six million US dollars was under his son's name. In defense, Soong admitted the existence of the money but then claimed the money in his son's account was a gift from a senior friend. He later admitted that the money in those bank accouts was in fact all from the KMT, but he insisted that the money transfer was authorized by then-KMT chairman, Lee Teng-hui, which Lee denied. 

The scandal tarnished Soong's image as a clean politician. Initially leading in the polls, Soong narrowly lost the election with three six . eight four % of the vote to Chen Shui-bian of the Democratic Progressive Party with three nine . three %. Lien came in a distant third with only two three . one %. One common belief on Taiwan is that Lee Teng-hui favored the unpopular Vice President Lien Chan over the highly popular Soong in a deliberate effort to sabotage the Kuomintang and was secretly supporting Chen. Others believe Lee feared Soong would help expose the corruption in his regime, and undermine his legacy.

After losing the election, Soong's supporters protested in front of the KMT party headquarters and blockaded the building for a few days. They succeeded in pressuring Lee Teng-hui to resign as KMT Chairman in favor of Lien Chan. Within weeks, Soong and his supporters formed the People First Party (PFP), considered a spin-off from the KMT. The loss of PFP votes was a major factor in causing the KMT to swing toward Chinese reunification thereby causing the subsequent expulsion of Lee Teng-hui.

Prosecutors later dropped all charges against Soong in the Chunghsing Scandal. In two zero zero three , the investigation was reopened, with former President Lee (now expelled from the KMT and the spiritual leader of the radically pro-independence Taiwan Solidarity Union) testifying against Soong in court. However, with the KMT allied with the PFP for the two zero zero four presidential election, the KMT aided Soong in his defense, and KMT Chairman Lien Chan claimed the KMT was misled into filing the lawsuit against Soong. The KMT dropped the charges and collected the money that had been returned and was deposited in the court by Soong.

 two zero zero four presidential elections 
Despite the personal rivalries between Lien, the KMT chairman after two zero zero zero , and Soong, the KMT and PFP pledged to cooperate in future elections to prevent splitting the vote, as they basically share the same electorate. Though losses in the two zero zero one legislative elections made the DPP the largest single party in the Legislative Yuan, the pan-blue coalition retained a narrow majority over the pan-green coalition.

Soong ran as Vice Presidential candidate under Lien Chan in the two zero zero four elections. Some believe that the PFP's lack of experienced candidates in the December two zero zero two mayoral elections in Taipei and Kaohsiung (the PFP supported the KMT's candidates), and the PFP's poor performance the city council elections in those cities at the same time were major setbacks to Soong's chances of being the KMT-PFP candidate for president. There were widespread rumors that Soong agreed to take the Vice-Presidential post in exchange for a pledge by Lien to give him significant power including the Premiership. Many KMT members opposed the linkage as they considered Soong an opportunist and traitor. Soong's supporters cited that he was more popular than Lien, as consistently demonstrated by polls and the results of the two zero zero zero presidential elections. Though both men garnered a combined six zero % of the vote in two zero zero zero (compared to Chen's three nine %) they lost to Chen by a mere zero . two two % of the vote and never conceded.

 Post-Election 

After the two zero zero four Presidential election, Soong actively sought the merger of the KMT and PFP. However, he ceased doing so after the ROC Legislative Election, two zero zero four . Although the pan-blue coalition did well, the PFP did not, and Soong ended talk of a KMT-PFP merger. In February two zero zero five , he signed a one zero point consensus program with President Chen Shui-Bian which brought heavy criticism to Chen. The possibility of DPP-PFP cooperation ended in May two zero zero five , when Soong visited mainland China to meet with Hu Jintao. Initially, Chen stated that Soong was to deliver a secret message to the PRC leadership, but Soong denied this.

In the two zero zero five KMT chairmanship election, Soong, who retains significant following within the KMT, despite initially instructing party officials not to support either Ma Ying-jeou or Wang Jin-pyng, endorsed Wang at the last minute. The endorsement appeared to backfire, however, as Ma defeated Wang by a rather large margin of seven two % to two eight %.

On July two two , two zero zero five , Soong, unopposed, was reelected chairman of the PFP.

 Visit to mainland China 
Soong's visit to mainland China followed quickly on the heels of the trail-blazing visit of KMT Chairman Lien Chan. A few weeks after shaking Lien's hands at the airport and wishing him luck, Soong took his turn at the spotlight. Despite early predictions by critics that the two political peers would try to out-stage each other, the two visits proved to be similar and complementary in many respects.

Soong's whirlwind nine day, five city Bridge Laying tour began on May five th, with a trip to the traditional Chinese capital of Xi'an. There, he visited the tomb memorial for the Yellow Emperor, a near-mythical historical figure from whom the Chinese believe they are descended. He then visited Nanjing, the former capital of the Republic of China, where he visited the tomb of ROC founder Sun Yat-sen. After a brief visit to Shanghai, Soong made an emotional return to his ancestral home in Hunan province. Soong and his family visited and honored the grave of his maternal grandmother buried in Xiangtan in a widely televised emotional ceremony. Choosing to appear as familiar as possible to his mainland hosts, Soong spoke his greetings in the local dialect in each of the cities that he visited.

Beyond sentimental visits, the important political aspect of his tour comes from his visit to Beijing. There, he shook hands with the general secretary of the Communist Party of China Hu Jintao, only the second major political figure from Taiwan to ever do so. The carefully scripted red-carpet ceremony was identical to the previous greeting for KMT Chairman Lien Chan. The key out-come of the meeting was the publication of a shared political platform between the Communist Party and Soong's People's First Party. Finally, Soong lectured at Qinghua University, an echo of Lien's lecture at Beijing University four weeks prior.

Soong's visit was designed to emphasize his belief in common shared roots for the Chinese people, a reflection of his pro-unification sentiment. He specifically chose to honor the historical ancestor of the Chinese people, the contemporary father of the Republic of China, and then his own direct ancestors in that precise order. His public comments addressed this continuous theme as well, receiving rapturous support from his mainland audience. The political consensus borne of the visit between the PFP and the CPC called for practical actions towards establishing links between Taiwan and mainland China, while firmly resisting Taiwanese independence.

 Political ideology 

In the middle of the SARS endemic in May two zero zero three , he bashed the administration for not being able to participate in the WHO which lead to the danger in public health. Subsequently, he promised to the public that if elected, he will push for participation in WHO under the principle Under the Roof of One China. In this Under the Roof of One China principle, he will not challenge the One China policy set by PRC, he added. However, this proposal enhanced the public perception of selling out Taiwan toward him and his opponents questioned how he can protect Taiwan's sovereignty and accept that Taiwan be a part of China at the same time. In order to quelch this negative image, Soong and his running mate Lien made a unexpected change of direction in their cross strait policy by announcing that they would drop unification as the ultimate goal in their cross strait policy in an international press conference during the two zero zero four presidential election race. They further explained that they would not exclude the possibility of final independence of Taiwan. However, his opponents still hold a suspicious eye to Soong's true intentions. His mainland origins also plagued him in the two zero zero four election.

Soong has been a staunch opponent of Taiwan independence. He publicly opposed Taiwanese language education in his early political life and criticized that multi-lingual education would lead to ''Lebanonization of languages'' and create communication chaos in the nation. He also criticized President Chen for staging a referendum. He strongly opposed the major military weapon procurement from the US and actively participated in the anti-weapon-purchase protests. He maintained the purchase would be part of a military race across the strait and would not enhance Taiwan's ability in self-defense.

His base of support includes strong supporters of Chinese reunification, rural voters (particularly in northern and eastern Taiwan, who were grateful for the selective economic development undertaken while he was governor) and urban middle class voters who see him as a cleaner alternative to the KMT. Soong is well known for using his body language, publicly kneeling and shedding tears, as a gesture to plead for constituency support. Though many criticize it to be histrionic, most of Soong's supporters see it to be candid and sincere.

 The '''New Kuomintang Alliance''' (   ; Hsin Kuomintang Lienhsien) was a faction of Kuomintang in the Republic of China on Taiwan, active late two zero th century. Composed of mainly younger mainlanders, this faction was in favor of interparty reform. It accused President Lee Teng-hui of autocratic tendencies and complained that the KMT was too corrupt. In August one nine nine three , days before the one four th KMT Party Congress, the New KMT Alliance broke away to form the Chinese New Party. This move was propelled by the resignation of Premier Hau Pei-tsun, whom New KMT Alliance members had viewed to be a counterbalance to Lee's power.

 ''Rev. Ezra Stiles'', one seven seven zero - one seven seven one , by Samuel King
The Rev. '''Ezra Stiles''' (November two nine , one seven two seven - May one two , one seven nine five was a Congregational clergyman, theologian and president of Yale College from one seven seven eight to one seven nine five . 

Born the son of the Rev. Isaac Stiles in North Haven, Connecticut, Ezra Stiles graduated from Yale in one seven four six . He studied theology and was ordained in one seven four nine , tutoring at Yale from that year until one seven five five . Resigning from the ministry, he studied law and practiced at New Haven from one seven five three to one seven five five , when he returned to the ministry for two two years. He was pastor of the Second Congregational Church in Newport, Rhode Island from one seven five five until one seven seven seven , then at Portsmouth, New Hampshire from one seven seven seven until one seven seven eight , when he became president of Yale until his death. 

He was also a dedicated supporter of the American Revolutionary cause, and an avid amateur scientist who corresponded with Thomas Jefferson and Benjamin Franklin about scientific discoveries. Using equipment donated to the college by Franklin, Stiles conducted the first electrical experiments in New England. He had struck up a close friendship with Rabbi Haim Isaac Carigal during Carigal's six month residence in Newport in one seven seven three , the two meeting two eight times (according to Stiles' records) to discuss a wide variety of topics, ranging from kaballah to the politics of the Holy Land. In addition, Stiles took the opportunity to improve his rudimentary knowledge of the Hebrew language, to the point where he and Carigal were to correspond by mail in Hebrew. 

Stiles' knowledge of Hebrew also enabled him to translate large portions of the Hebrew Old Testament into English. Stiles believed, as did many Christian scholars of the time, that facility with the text in its original language was advantageous for proper interpretation. As president of Yale, Stiles also became its first professor of Semitics, and required all students to study Hebrew (as was also the case at Harvard); his first commencement address in September, one seven eight one (no ceremonies having been held during the Revolutionary War) was delivered in Hebrew, Aramaic, and Arabic. By one seven nine zero , however, he was forced to face failure in instilling an interest in the language in the student body, writing 
: From my first accession to the Presidency ... I have obliged all the Freshmen to study Hebrew. This has proved very disagreeable to a Number of the Students. This year I have determined to instruct only those who offer themselves voluntarily. 
The valedictorians of one seven eight five and one seven nine two , however, did deliver their speeches in Hebrew.

Yale's legacy from this interest of Stiles' includes a portrait of Carigal by artist Samuel King, and the Hebrew words Urim and Thummim (      ) on the Yale seal.

He married twice and had eight children. He owned at least one slave, named Newport, whom he freed on June nine , one seven seven eight .

A book he authored, ''The United States elevated to Glory and Honor'' was printed in one seven eight three .

Named in his honor is Ezra Stiles College, one of Yale's newest residential colleges, and known for its successes winning the Gimbel and Tyng cups. Also noted is its Eero Saarinen design, particularly the building's lack of right angles between walls. The college's mascot is the moose, inspired by the installation in the dining hall of a stuffed moose head in honor of former college master and Yale president A. Bartlett Giamatti. Adjacent to Ezra Stiles College is its near architectural twin, Morse College, named for Samuel F.B. Morse.

 '''Roseburg''' is a city in state of Oregon , USA. This city was named for Aaron Rose, who settled within the current city limits September two three , one eight five one , and managed a tavern. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two zero , zero one seven . Roseburg is home to Umpqua Community College. 

Transportation
Oregon Highway nine nine runs through downtown Roseburg as the main north-south arterial. Interstate five runs along the west side of the city, across the South Umpqua River from downtown.

Oregon Highway one three eight runs northwest from Roseburg to Elkton, Oregon, and generally east from Roseburg to its terminus at a junction with U.S. Highway nine seven , just east of Diamond Lake and Crater Lake.

There is a Greyhound bus station with connecting service to Amtrak passenger rail service. A Central Oregon and Pacific Railroad freight railway runs through Roseburg, and there is a municipal airport at the north end of town.

 Park in Arlington, looking towards the Columbia River

'''Arlington''' is a city located in Gilliam County, Oregon. The account of how this city received its name varies: one tradition claims it was named after the lawyer Nathan Arlington Cornish; another tradition claims that the Southern inhabitants of this city had enough clout to rename the city after Arlington, Virginia, home of general Robert E. Lee. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five two four .

 History 
Originally named Alkali, Arlington came into existence as a shipping place for cattle down the Columbia River. It was incorporated as Arlington in one eight eight five .

Following the completion of the John Day Dam, the original location of Arlington was moved south in one nine six three to avoid the resulting inundation.

Arlington was the birthplace of musician Doc Severinsen, best known as the bandmaster for the American television program ''The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson'' ( one nine six seven - one nine nine two ).

 '''Canyon City''' is the county seat of Grant County, Oregon, about a mile south of John Day on U.S. Highway three nine five . As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of six six nine .

Canyon City was established in the one eight six zero s as a result of the discovery of gold in Canyon Creek, which flows through the town. According to ''Oregon's Golden Years'' (ISBN zero eight seven zero zero four two five four eight ), the discovery led to land between Canyon City and John Day being worth $ five zero zero per square yard ($ five nine eight m ). Panning for gold could yield several ounces in each pan of sediment. At the peak of the local gold rush, one zero , zero zero zero lived in Canyon City, making it larger than Portland at the time.

The town was platted in one eight six two and was chosen as the county seat two years later, when Grant County was split from Wasco County. It was incorporated in one eight nine one .

 '''Granite''' is a town (almost a ghost town) located in Grant County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two four , up from its population of one zero in one nine nine zero and one in one nine five eight . It is also the smallest (according to population) incorporated city in Oregon. 

According to ''Oregon Geographic Names'', the name Granite was established for the town when its post office was established in one eight seven eight ; the name is a reference to Granite Creek, where the discovery of gold on July four , one eight six two drew people to the town.

 Geography 
Location of Granite, OregonGranite is located at four four  four eight ' three two  North, one one eight  two five ' one three  West ( four four . eight zero eight seven seven four , - one one eight . four two zero one six two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the town has a total area of one . zero km ( zero . four mi ), none of which is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two four people in the town, organized into one five households and nine families. The population density is two three . two km ( six zero . three mi ). There are seven four housing units at an average density of seven one . four km ( one eight five . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the city is one zero zero % White, with no African Americans, Native Americans, Asians, Pacific Islanders, and no people who consider themselves to be of other races or from two or more races. One person ( four . one seven % of the population) is Hispanic or Latino of any race.

None of the one five households have children under the age of one eight living with them. six zero % of the households are married couples living together, zero . zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and four zero . zero % are non-families. four zero . zero % of all households are made up of individuals and six . seven % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is one . six zero and the average family size is two . zero zero .

In the city the population is spread out with no one under the age of two four , two zero . eight % from two five to four four , six six . seven % from four five to six four , and one two . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is five seven years. For every one zero zero females there are one one eight . two males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ one five , six two five , and the median income for a family is $ two zero , six two five . Males have a median income of $ one one , two five zero versus $ six , two five zero for females. The per capita income for the city is $ eight , zero two four .  three six % of the population and two zero % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, all of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Occupational and social life 
A one nine three nine interview, recorded as part of the Federal Writers' Project, described the town and surroundings of Granite. The following are excerpts from that interview; the women being interview was Mrs. Neil Niven, Granite's school teacher and a co-editor of the town's newspaper, the ''Granite Siftings'':
:Granite was first named Independence. On July four , one eight six two , the notorious Jack Long discovered gold here and this precipitated a rush. The town was named in honor of Independence Day; on which it was founded. Later, when the Granite townspeople petitioned the United States government for a post office the government insisted they change the name of Independence. In accordance with the government edict the townspeople voted for the name Granite.
:The little town is filled with rich, boisterous lore. Rollicking, rough, and ready, would best describe those townspeople.
:Granite, or Independence, as it first was called, was built in the heart of the Blue Mountains. As you know, many creeks roar down from the mountain springs into the canyons. The mountains are rough, tower high into air and flatten out into rocky, almost impassable flats at other places. This rough country presents many obstacles hard to overcome. The roughness, coupled with the unfavorable climatic conditions are, at times, almost unbearable. The Granite country could be and usually is nature at its best and worst.

 Supplies 
:Supplies were brought in from Pendleton or the Umatilla Landing by freight wagons. The regular mail came through by pack train from John Day. The supplies brought by the wagons could only be wagoned in during the summer months. The rest of the year the roads and trails were impassable. Mail nearly always managed to get through, with the possible exception of the heavy snow season.

 Seasons 
:Each season of the year presented peculiar problems. The fall was the best time for everyone. Then the days were warm and pleasant, fading into cool, brilliant, moonlit, starlit nights. The air brought a fresh, crisp, tang to your nostrils. The smell of the pine needles was always more sharp in the fall.
:Winter covered the mountains with snow. As soon as the snow started falling the men began an almost never-ending shoveling of drifts from the walks we used in town. Ravines that during the summer harbored laboring miners were completely filled with snow. The houses we lived in looked rather like large Eskimo ice houses. The mountain streams were beautiful at this time of the year. They cut a sparkling, almost black line through the heavy crusted snow, they were about the only thing in that country that didn't look frozen. The high drifts, piled higher by changing winds, blocked the trails and entrances to the mines. Often operations were forced to shut down.

 The men and their living quarters 
:The men in the mines wore a regulation miner's hat with a candle on the front bill. Overalls, with hip-boots, and a dark blue, heavy shirt completed his outfit. About the only concession they would make for social life would be a different hat, and smaller boots. They used picks and shovels for tools most of the time in the mines. Dynamite and all the paraphernalia that goes with its use was utilized whenever possible.
:For living quarters the men chopped down trees, trimmed and seasoned them to use in building log cabins. Simplicity and utility were their chief characteristics. A few of the windows in the cabins were waxed paper, but in my time most of us had regular window panes. Furniture was made from rough lumber and produced by the men.

 Young single women 
:When I first went to Granite as their schoolteacher, there were only two other single girls there. A little later another girl, too fat to make any difference moved into town. We three girls, and later the fat one, had a glorious time. Every bachelor there at one time or another asked us for a date.
:At the Never Sweat Hotel we girls started a library. Every evening we would spend at the library encouraging the young men of the town to read books. Precious little reading was done, but many books were taken out of the library. Each girl had a special beau to see that she arrived home safely, but it did not hinder our entertaining the other bachelors at the library.
:The library had the books for an excuse for the miners to come to the hotel, but an old organ helped provide the entertainment. We would dance and sing to the music of that old, out-of-tune organ, and have the best time.

 Chinese 
:When Granite was at its height there were approximately three zero zero zero Chinese working in the mines, or working mines of their own. These Chinese would buy mines after the white man was nearly finished with his operations. Usually the white man was convinced of the fact that he was selling slag dirt. However, the Chinese could still make a living from the tailings or slags. This always struck me as a peculiar but profitable quality.
:The poor Chinese were socially ostracised from white society. However, they had their own lives and led them much as we do ours.

 Local code of ethics 
:The men of Granite had a code of ethics that fulfilled the function of legal law. Oh! There were plenty of infractions of the code, but often these infractions were dealt with by lead logic, rather than by legal evasion. M-h-m, yes, I suppose it isn't right to stretch a horse thief with his boots on, or lead up a sift snitcher, but it served its purpose with remarkable finality to further trespassing.

 Lincoln's election 
:Granite citizens, almost to a man were Southern Democrats. The ugliest name they could call a man was Lincolnite . The worthless Jack Long was no exception. His hate for Lincoln was the most eloquent thing about him. When the dreaded news came that Lincoln had been elected bitterness burned deeply in all Democratic hearts. The few votes he received in Granite cast the finger of black Republican suspicion on many people.
:Jack Long, on one of his glorious sprees, decided he had the courage to find the man who dared to vote for Lincoln. Arming himself with a revolver and knife, he set out on his self-appointed mission. Each man he met an the street he questioned boldly, threateningly. His voice could be heard booming up and down the street.
: Did you dare to vote for Abraham Lincoln? Most everyone answered, No. A man riding by on his horse reined in and said to Jack: I dared to vote for Lincoln. What are you going to do about it? Dead silence fell on the crowd that had quickly gathered. Jack Long broke the silence with Well, that makes one. Where's another?  Someone in the crowd yelled, thought you was gong to shoot the first black Republican you met, Jack?  Well, he answered, you can't shoot a man on his horse.  Accused of being a coward, Jack countered, I'd rather be called a coward than be dead. Republicans were safe after that.

 '''John Day''' is a town located about a mile north of Canyon City in Grant County, Oregon, at the intersection of U.S. Highways two six and three nine five . The town is named for the nearby John Day River, which had been named for a Virginian member of the one eight one one Astor-Hunt party. It was incorporated in one eight eight eight .

As of the two zero zero zero census, the town had a total population of one eight two one , making it the largest town in the county.

According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the town has a total area of four . nine km ( one . nine mi or one two zero zero acres), none of which is covered with water.

 History 
In the one eight eight zero s John Day was home to nearly one zero zero zero Chinese immigrants, attracted to the area by a gold rush twenty years earlier. A trading post built in the area in the one eight six zero s along the Dalles Military Road was purchased in one eight eight seven by two of the immigrants, Lung On and Ing Hay. They converted the trading post into a clinic, general store, and social center for the local community. In the one nine seven zero s that building was converted into a museum and state heritage site now called the Kam Wah Chung  ( nine six nine . five mi ). There are eight four six housing units at an average density of one seven three . seven km ( four five zero . four mi ). '''Bjuv''' is a municipality and town in Scania in southernmost Sweden.

The municipality covers an area of one one five . five km. 
Of the total population of one three , seven zero five , six , eight five six are male, and six , eight four nine are female. 
The population density of the community is one one nine inhabitants per km.

 Geography 
The geography consists of beech trees in its north-eastern parts, hills to the south and , in the north, some plains.

 History 
The city arms depicts a mining torch lighting up a dark area. The reason is that Bjuv has had a coal mining industry since the one eight th century which laid the foundation for the industry. In the end of the one nine th century, the clay industry flourished, based on the coal.

'''Bromlla''' is a municipality and town in Scania in southernmost Sweden. The town Bromlla has a population of about seven , three zero zero .
 
 History 
The name itself comes from a Bromlla, which translated to Bridge Mill, one or more mills used at least from the one seven th to the one nine th century, adjacent to a small river. The city arms depict a bridge over a river, and a water wheel symbolizing the mill. 

The town only consisted of a few houses until it began to grow about one zero zero years ago around a newly established limestone quarry, leading to the establishment of several ceramics industries.

 Industry 
IF makes water toilets and has been doing it for over a hundred years. All over Sweden are water toilets with the IF-insignia.

 Culture 
Bromlla boosts remains from the Stone Age, and even some findings of dinosaurs. More recent remains also attract visitors, among them old churches, mills and some other curiosities that have survived the modernisation. In the municipality are several cultural houses, rural museums and mansions that can be visited.

In the town Bromlla also lays a popular cinema visisted by people from as far as Kristianstad. It was elected Best Cinema of Sweden in two zero zero one by the leading film reviewing program on TV.

Born in Bromlla
 Johanna Sjberg (born March eight , one nine seven eight ), swimmer

'''Burlv Municipality''' is a municipality in Skne County in southern Sweden, just north of Malm. It is the second smallest municipality in Sweden with an area of one eight . nine km. 

The municipal seat is located in the town of Arlv, which has come to form a conurbation with the city of Malm to the south (with a total of two seven zero , zero zero zero inhabitants). 

 Geography 
The municipality has no forests, lakes, or streams, but has an abundance of high-voltage power grids, highways and railroads, as it is on the main line from Malm to northern Sweden. Like the rest of Scania, much land is used for agriculture and there are several old farms, mills and other sights from the last centuries in the vicinity.

 Demography 
The population of Burlv has increased with almost one , zero zero zero persons between one nine eight six and two zero zero three , but it decreased last year. The largest part of the population increase has been due to high birth rates. Moving rates have played a small part, and is rather equalled, where  as is normal in smaller communities  young people move out and families with children move in.

 Towns 
The population is chiefly divided between:
 Arlv, with eight , eight zero zero inh.
 karp, with five , three zero zero inh.
 Burlvs egnahem, with six zero zero inh.

''Arlv'' is an early industrialized town dominated by multi-storey apartment buildings, with a working class character. Its largest industry is Arlv Sugar Factory, to which large amounts of sugar beets are transported from all around Scania. 

In Arlv, the ''Burlv Centre'' is also located. It is a large shopping mall in the region, but considered rather expensive. 

''karp'' and ''Burlvs egnahem'', consist of detached house districts. They have a suburban character from where people commute to commercial centres and work within the metropolitan area of South-Western Scania.

Burlv Old Church
 Culture and history 
Arlv is located in the vicinity of agricultural fields, where the ''Old Church of Burlv'' can be found, in the Burlv Village. One of the oldest churches in Scania, it has mostly remained the way it was built in the one two th century, with its oldest parts concreted out of sandstone.

The coat of arms depict a sugar beet which was the chief industry for a while (E.g. the large ''Arlv's Sugar Factory''), and a star that symbolizes the Hvilan folk high school which was among the first group of folk high schools that were established in one eight six eight . one

'''Bstad Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Scania (Skne) in southern Sweden, where the Scanian town '''Bstad''' is seat with a population of four , seven zero zero .

Bstad has most tennis courts in the country, and has fostered many internationally successful tennis players, such as Magnus Larsson. Every summer Swedish Open Bstad in tennis is held here as part of the ATP Tour. It attracts some two zero , zero zero zero visitors and puts the town in a festive mood for a few weeks.

 History 
The first city privileges were granted in the one four th or one five th century, when the area (all Scanian counties) belonged to Denmark. The first certain date is one five one three when it was re-granted. At the time, the name in print was ''Botstd'', which would translate to Boat City . 

The area was in one six five eight conquered by Sweden, and Bstad was given new special privileges in one six six four , because it was of too insignificant size to recive the full royal charter as one of Sweden's cities. The minor privilege allowed the town to be used for commerce, handicraft and hostelry. The minor privilege was in effect until one eight five eight when it got proper rights as a ''merchant town'', or ''kping''.

 Geography 
The town is located in a sheltered bay with the Hallandian ridge stretching behind it. The town borders the shore, whereafter the terrain raises until the dense vegetation of the ridge takes over.

The marina; Hallandian ridge in background
A street adjacent to the central square


 Hallandian ridge 
Extending through the municipality, marking the border to the province Hallandia, is the ridge of Hallandia, or ''Hallandssen''. It is one of the highest point in the otherwise flat terrained Scania, with a high of two two six meters. 

The ridge reached in the public eye in one nine nine seven , when a tunnel being dug through the ridge caused fishes in the streams to die and cows grazing on the ridge to become paralyzed. The reason was a substance containing the poisenous substance acrylamide used by the digging company to counteract a surprising high level of groundwater in the ridge.

 Other sights 
Image:Mariakyrkan, Bstad.jpg
The Church of Bstad or Saint Mary Church is located in central Bstad. It was constructed in the one five th century. It is a Romanesque church, and contains several wall paintings from various centuries; a madonna image; and a Danish altarpiece, among other things.

 Notable natives 
 Carl Adolph Agardh ( one seven eight five - one eight five nine ), botanist, born in Bstad.

'''Eslv Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in southern Sweden with its seat in the Scanian town '''Eslv''' with two zero , zero zero zero inhabitants. Today Eslv largely serves as a suburb of Malm and Lund.

The city of Eslv received its privileges in one nine one one after incorporating the parish of Vstra Sallerup. Eslv had been a town by its own since one eight seven five . Today the city has a growing population of one five , four zero zero ( one nine nine six ). Eslv was but a small village until the Southern Railline (''Sdra Stambanan'') between Stockholm and Malm was run through in the mid- one eight zero zero 's. Trade flourished around the new station and eventually it also attracted industrial settlings. Among the city's companies are ''Procordia Food AB'' (''former Felix AB''). 

The municipality has several interesting places. There are one one castles. '''Hjulard'''s castle was the place for the Swedish TV classic '''Mystery of Greveholm''' sent by SVT. In the '''Vstra Str''' village there are old rune stones from ca year one zero zero zero . Sweden largest and almost only sugar refinery lies in '''rtofta''' in south of Eslv. In Eslv there are two nature reserves, Allmnningen and Abullahagen. The Stone Mountain, Eslv Church and Hotel Sten Stensson Sten with the locally famous 'Scanish' Steps lie in the middle of Eslv. Maybe the most famous inhabitant of Eslv is the comicer Johan Glans, who has made several TV series.

'''Hrby''' is a municipality and town in Scania in southernmost Sweden. 

The municipality covers an area of four two two . five km. 
Of the total population of one three , seven four two , six , nine zero four are male, and six , eight three eight are female. 
The population density of the community is three three inhabitants per km.

 Geography 
The geography is varied with a little forests, some lakes and streams and farming lands and even wildlife. It is also one of the most meadow filled municipalities in Sweden.

 Culture 
Hrby still has much of the old cultural heritage remaining in the villages. 

Hrby is famous for being one of the transmitting stations specified on old MF radio receivers. The broadcasting signals (radio, TV) are still transmitted from the Teracom transmitting station in stra Sallerup, seven km south of Hrby village.
MF transmissions do not occur from Hrby any more,but from the new transmitter in Soelvesborg, inaugaurated in one nine eight five , at the coast of the Baltic Sea.

On the first Thursday in July every year since one seven four eight , the Hrby Market (Hrby Marknad) is held. It attracts thousands of visitors and is one of the three main traditional markets in Skne together with the markets of Kivik and Sjbo.

The most famous personality from Hrby was the authoress Victoria Benedictsson ( one eight five zero - one eight eight eight ).

'''Hr Municipality''' is a Municipality in Skne County, in southern Sweden where the Scanian town '''Hr''' (pop. seven , zero zero zero ) in the midth is seat and largest urban area. 

It was formed in one nine six nine through a merge with Norra Frosta municipality, Snogerd municipality and Tjrnarp parish. 

Hr credits itself by being different from the rest of Skne: Apart from the agricultural areas most Skne hosts, Hr also has several forests and the lake Ringsjn. Ringsjn is the second largest lake in Skne and covers some four zero km, about three times the size of the town Hr. 

Sunset over Ringsjn

The two main attractions of the municipality that draws visitors from the rest of Scania are the zoological garden ''Sknes Djurpark'', and the ''Bosjkloster Castle'' established in the one two th century. The castle is situated in a scenic location in a cape in the lake Ringsjn; the zoological garden is situated just north of the town Hr. 

One of the ponds of the town Sights in the town proper are few in the little town with its seven , zero zero zero inhabitants, but it has a church that was built in the late one eight th century, which is actually a rather uncommon time for church building in Scania, and some other older houses that may be interesting solely by their architecture. Most houses are one storey houses, or possibly two. There are no larger streets and it seems like a peaceful place. Adding to the picturesque image are the two centrally located quiet small ponds and the thickly foliaged trees and bushes surrounding them, which increasing into thickness until the unite with the forests surrounding the town. 

A car used by municipal workers with the coat of arms
The train station is located on the line from Kristianstad to Malm and making it quick and easy to commute. Also basically situated through the town is a large road leading north and south.

The locally semi-known rock band Subtitle is based in Hr; it is also the only place it is recognized in.

 '''Cascade Locks''' is a city located in Hood River County, Oregon, United States. The town took its name from a set of locks built to improve navigation past the Cascades Rapids of the Columbia River. The federal government approved the plan for the locks in one eight seven five , construction began in one eight seven eight , and the locks were completed on November five , one eight nine six . The locks were subsequently submerged in one nine three eight , replaced by Bonneville Lock and Dam, although the town lost no land from the expansion of '''Lake Bonneville''' behind the dam located some four miles downstream of the town.

Cascade Locks is located just upstream from the Bridge of the Gods, a toll bridge that spans the Columbia River. It is the only bridge across the Columbia between Portland and Hood River.

Cascade Locks is used frequently by hikers along the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) to cross the Columbia River. Cascade Locks is the lowest point along the trail, which runs from the Mexican border in California to the Canadian border in Washington.

Cascade Locks is a few miles upstream of Eagle River Gorge, a popular scenic area that doubles as an alternate route for the Pacific Crest Trail.

As of the two zero zero zero Census, the town had a total population of one , one one five .

 Geography

'''Lomma Municipality''' is located in Skne (Scania), about one zero kilometers north of Malm, in southernmost Sweden. Its seat is located to the small town '''Lomma'''. 

Geography
The small municipality -- the two zero th smallest in Sweden -- borders to Kvlinge, Burlv, Staffanstorp and Lund. As Burlv also is notably small, Lomma almost borders to Malm too.

It is situated by resund, at the inlet of the at the small river Hje . Along the river lies a small-boat harbour. The beaches along its coasts also attract visitors from other municipalities; Lomma's beaches are the principal beaches for people from the beach-less Lund.

 one zero kilometers to the north-east is the university city of Lund, with some nine zero , zero zero zero inhabitants, about the same distance as to Malm (with its two five zero , zero zero zero inhabitants) to the south. Lomma is also considered part of Metropolitan Malm, showing itself for instance by the six , five zero zero commuters that live in Lomma. Travelling to and from Lomma is easy, as a main highway actually passes straight through the town of Lomma, connecting with Lund and Malm, and with other cities to the north. 

Geologically, its terrain is almost completely flat levelled, which is the custom for south-western Skne as a whole. The highest location in Lomma is four zero meters above sea level.

History
The area where Lomma is now is located between two small rivers, and was inhabited by hunters in the Stone Age. The name ''Lomma'' can be traced to one zero eight five , and in the ensuing centuries it established some wealth thanks to merchancy with the episcopal see in Lund. 

Lomma kyrkaNone the less, the area was only a village until Sweden's first cement works was established in one eight seven one . The ground consists of a certain clay stemming from the last ice age, and is available in large quantities in Lomma. A full fledged industry was started in the one eight six zero s, and by the end of the century Lomma had five brick factories. The bricks from Lomma are yellow of appearance and were regarded as the highest kind of bricks during that century. One church built with those bricks is the church in Lomma, (''Lomma kyrka''), a large neo Gothic church that was finished in the one eight seven zero s.

The municipality of Lomma was created in one nine zero zero ; however at the time it was much smaller than today. It got its current size in one nine six zero when it was united with two other municipalities. From that time stems the coat of arms. It depicts an anchor -- showing the importance of the harbour -- and a brick wall, indicating that Lomma once actually had city rights (when it belonged to Denmark, before the Treaty of Roskilde one six five eight ) as well as its brick industry.

Population centres
The two main towns in the municipality are Lomma and Bjrred. With some eight , three zero zero inhabitants, they have almost the exact same population figures, and combined they house nine three % of the municipal population. In comparisment, Bjrred may be regarded as a somewhat more fashionable town than Lomma. 

None of the remaining population centres are significant: of the others, ''Fldje'' is the largest with its two one zero inhabitants. Of note is also Alnarp, where one of the main campuses of the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences is located.

'''Hood River''' is a town in and county seat of Hood River County, Oregon, and a port on the Columbia River. The town was named for the nearby stream, Hood River. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five , eight three one .

 History 
A Post office was established at the site of the present town in September three zero , one eight five zero , and the town itself was incorporated in one eight eight one .

Long an agricultural center, Hood River experienced a boom of growth with its discovery as a gateway to world-class windsurfing in the Columbia River Gorge. The rapid increase in the cost of housing has forced many less affluent long-time residents to nearby communities, some as far away as The Dalles.

Hood River is also the home for the ''International Museum of Carousel Art'' and the employee-owned Full Sail Brewing Company, a major Oregon microbrewery.

It is also the western gateway to the Mt. Hood Scenic Byway and to a major section of the Columbia River Highway.

'''Simrishamn Municipality''' is a municipality in Skne in southern Sweden where the Scania town '''Simrishamn''' (pop. six , three zero zero ) is seat. 

 Geography 
The landscape south and west of Simrishamn is mainly open and very flat farmland, in most places you can see for several miles in all directions. To the north of Simrishamn the landscape is broken up by small forests and gently sloping hills. The coastline directly south and north of Simrishamn is stony to a great degree, but turns into broad beaches with white sand further away.
The scenic Stenshuvud National Park is located by the shore, within the municipal borders, and is one of the geographically more fascinating places in Skne.

 Municipal towns 
One of the picturesque small villages in Simrishamn municipality is Kivik, some one five km north of the Simrishamn village. Kivik is famous for its Market (Kiviks Marknad) which takes place on the third Wednesday in July. This market, with a medieval history, is one of the three main traditional markets in Skne (Sjbo and Hrby being the others) and attracts hundreds of thousands of visitors every year.

Also within the municipal borders, in its south-western part, is the Glimmingehus. This is the best preserved medieval fortress of Scandinavia, and one of the best known locations in the province.

'''Sjbo Municipality''' is a Swedish municipality in Skne in southernmost Sweden where the market town '''Sjbo''' (pop. six , zero zero zero ) is seat.

 History 
It started growing when it became a halt on the railway between Malm (to the west) and Simrishamn (on the east) in the early one nine th century. Today the town can not be reached by rail, but a road through central Skne also crosses the municipality and town, while another large road from east to west also crosses it.

Sjbo is one of the municipality created during the municipal reform in the one nine seven zero s. 

 Refugee controversy 
The municipality reached into the publics eye in one nine eight eight by declaring reluctant to accept refugees, after a referendum gave a majority of six seven % votes. Most other municipalities in Sweden accepted refugees that came from troubled countries such as former Yugoslavia and Iraq.

: ''In the late one nine eight zero s and early one nine nine zero s, there was an immigration crisis in Sweden. The number of asylum seekers increased, and the share of Nordics among newcomers fell from two-thirds to one-third. High unemployment and the fiscal burdens on local governments which were obliged to integrate refugees, and the refusal of the city of Sjobo to accept refugees in one nine eight seven , led to the adoption of a combined immigration and integration system in the Aliens Act of one nine eight nine .'' 
__NOTOC__

The streets are long and straight in Sjbo town
The Old Church of Sdra sum, just north of Sjbo town

 Geography 
The town of Sjbo is flat terrained with many small houses and three long strait streets stretching through it, leading to learger roads.

Within the limits of the municipality lays the main part of Vombsjn, which is the largest lake of southern Skne and notable for being the water source of Malm. Located in north western municipality, some parts belong to Lund Municipality. It offers fishing for perch, pike, pikeperch and eel.

 Activities 
There are at least five (largely) authentic medieval churches from the one two th century in the municipality. They are notable for not having undergone severe restaurations that was suffered by many others churches in Scania once the population began growing in the second half of one nine th century and Helgo Zetterwall was hired to expand on them. 

Anyways, the churches in Sdra sum, Tolnga, Bjrka, Blentarp and Everlv are all interesting. The one in Everlv hosts fascinating paintings in the ceiling. Recently, a sixth church, in Illstorp, also had its old ceiling paintings uncovered. 

Apart from religious activities, there is the annual festival ''Sjbo marknad'' , translate to ''Sjbo fair'', that was first held in one eight six four , and is now held in late July, attracting some one zero zero , zero zero zero visitors; one of the largest country fairs in Sweden. It has carousels and is otherwise noted for its pottery commerce.

'''Tomelilla Municipality''' is a municipality where the is Scanian town '''Tomelilla''' (pop. six , zero zero zero ) is seat, in Skne in southernmost Sweden.

Tomelilla started expanding when the railroad between Ystad and Eslv was inaugurated in one eight six six .

Geography 
Tomelilla is located in the south-eastern plains of Skne known as sterlen, which is an area notable for its beauty, and thus popular among painters as well as covered with summer cottages, country mansions, and so on.

Notability
Tomelilla was made famous by Tage Danielsson ( one nine two eight - one nine eight five ) and Hans Alfredsson ( one nine three one -), who directed and acted in numerous movies that were filmed in and around Tomelilla:

Around Skne, Tomelilla is known for the amusement park ''Tosselilla'' (previously known as ''Tomelilla amusement park''), quite possibly the most visited amusement park in the province.
