 '''Joseph''' is a city located in Wallowa County, Oregon. Originally named Silver Lake and Lake City , in one eight eight zero the city formally named itself for the Nez Perc chief, Chief Joseph. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , zero five four .

 History 
Joseph was deeply affected in the one nine eight zero s collapse of the timber industry, which resulted in high local unemployment, sometimes approaching one seven %. However, beginning in one nine eight two , two local bronze foundries have been opened in Joseph (as well as one in neighboring Enterprise), as well as studios and art galleries specializing in statues. Sales are nation-wide, and include a $ two . four million order for bronze wreathes, armatures, and flagpoles for the National World War II Monument in Washington, D.C.. This new industry has helped Joseph to stabilize its economy. However, one of the foundries is reported to be in the process of moving to La Grande, Oregon.

The city sponsors an annual Joseph Days Rodeoeach July that's been running more than six zero years and one of the top outdoor small rodeos in the nation, a  Blues and Brewsfestival each August since two zero zero one , and an  Alpenfest(Swiss-Bavarian festival staged in the traditional Oktoberfest style) the last weekend of September at nearby Wallowa Lake since one nine seven four .

 '''Antelope''' is a city located in Wasco County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of five nine .

 Geography 
Location of Antelope, OregonAntelope is located at four four  five four ' three nine  North, one two zero  four three ' two two  West ( four four . nine one zero eight five two , - one two zero . seven two two seven eight four ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the village has a total area of one . three km ( zero . five mi ).  one . three km ( zero . five mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are five nine people, two seven households, and one eight families residing in the city. The population density is four four . seven km ( one one six . eight mi ). There are four one housing units at an average density of three one . zero km ( eight one . two mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine three . two two % White, zero . zero zero % African American, six . seven eight % Native American, zero . zero zero % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, zero . zero zero % from other races, and zero . zero zero % from two or more races.  three . three nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two seven households out of which one four . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six three . zero % are married couples living together, three . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and three three . three % are non-families. two nine . six % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one nine and the average family size is two . seven two .

In the city the population is spread out with two two . zero % under the age of one eight , one . seven % from one eight to two four , one eight . six % from two five to four four , three two . two % from four five to six four , and two five . four % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is five zero years. For every one zero zero females there are one zero three . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one zero zero . zero males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ four zero , two zero eight , and the median income for a family is $ three seven , five zero zero . Males have a median income of $ three zero , zero zero zero versus $ three zero , four one seven for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one seven , four four four .  two two . two % of the population and one six . seven % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, six four . three % of those under the age of one eight and zero . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.
 History 
The town of Antelope was the first to be settled in a valley of the same name where many antelope grazed. It became a stopping point for stagecoaches where passengers could rest and even stay over night. By one eight seven one , the town had grown to the point that warranted a post office and one was opened in August of that year. The town grew to become a center for cattlemen and sheepmen and had its share of shootings common in western towns during the one eight nine zero s. Like many other small towns during that period, Antelope was all but destroyed by fire in one eight nine eight . All but one building on the main street was destroyed but that building still stands today. The town was quickly rebuilt. Only a few miles north Antelope a new town called Shaniko became the terminus of a railroad causing the population to gradually fade.

After World War II, the community languished until the one nine eight zero s when followers of Bhagwan Shree Rajneesh, who had started the city of '''Rajneeshpuram''' on a ranch, came to dominate the town. '''Rajneeshpuram''' was the intentional community of the followers of Rajneesh. The ranch, previously known as The Big Muddy Ranch was the commune that the Rajneeshees called home. On Sept. one eight , one nine eight four , by a vote of five seven to two two , the charter was amended to change the name from Antelope to Rajneesh. A short time later Bhagwan was indicted on federal immigration charges. After an abortive attempt at flight, he pleaded guilty and returned to India. Meanwhile, on Nov. six , one nine eight five , the remaining residents, both original and Rajneeshee, voted three four to zero to restore the original name. The ranch is now owned by Young Life and has been converted into a camp, known as Wild Horse Canyon.

 ''Disamb: For the German rock group The Dalles, see The Dalles (band)''

'''The Dalles''' is a city located in Wasco County, Oregon. The name of the city comes from the French word ''dalle'' ( flag stone ), what the French-Canadian employees of the Hudson's Bay Company called the now-inundated Long Narrows of the Columbia River above the present-day city. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one two , one five six .

 History 
Lewis and Clark camped near Mill Creek on October two five - two seven , one eight zero five , and recorded the Native American name for this creek as ''Quenett''. The first use of the name ''Dalles'', according to Oregon Geographic Names, appears in Franchere's ''Narrative'', on April one two , one eight one four .

The Dalles was the end of the land route of the Oregon Trail.

A post office was established within the boundaries of the current city in one eight five one , and The Dalles was incorporated as a city in one eight five seven . It has been the major commercial center between Portland and Pendleton since.

In one nine seven zero the Bonneville Power Administration opened the Celilo Converter Station here, the northern terminus of the Pacific Intertie which sends two zero zero zero MW of electricity to Los Angeles.

Construction of The Dalles Dam in one nine five seven submerged the Long Narrows and Celilo Falls.

In one nine eight four , The Dalles was the scene of a bioterrorist incident launched by the Rajneeshee Cult. It was the first known bioterrorism attack of the two zero th century in the United States. (See Bhagwan Shri Rajneesh.)

Highways I- eight four , US two six , and US nine seven meet at this city.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one four . four km .  one three . six km of it is land and zero . eight km of it is water. The total area is five . two three % water.

There are four , eight nine six households out of which three zero . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five one . one % are married couples living together, one zero . six % have a female householder with no husband present, and three four . one % are non-families. two nine . two % of all households are made up of individuals and one three . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older.  Politics 
The Dalles has a very long running anti-war rally against the Iraq War which started before the war began. The protest is put on by the Wasco County Citizens For Human Dignity. This rally happens every Friday at five : zero zero PM at The Dalles Post Office. 

The Dalles is also home to another long running demonstration against the local porn shop. A group of local churches have rallied together to picket the store daily.

 The jokingly-named Shaniko Jail
'''Shaniko''' is a city located in Wasco County, Oregon, along U.S. Highway nine seven and about eight miles ( one three km) north of Antelope. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two six , a virtual ghost town whose preservation is being spearheaded by investments from Robert Pamplin, a businessman and owner of the ''Portland Tribune'' and Columbia Empire Farms.

According to ''Oregon Geographic Names'', Shaniko was named after August Scherneckau, a settler who came to the area after the Civil War. The spelling of the town's name reflects local pronunciation of Scherneckau's name. The town was originally called '''Cross Hollows'''; a post office by that name was established in May one eight seven nine with Scherneckau as postmaster.

The town's heyday was the first decade of the two zero th century, when Shaniko served as a transportation hub spurred by the presence of the Columbia Southern Railway, a subsidiary of Union Pacific Railroad which built a branch from Biggs Junction to Shaniko. That branch was completed in May one nine zero zero but by one nine one one , another line diverted traffic once served by the Columbia Southern and the town begin to decline. A mid- one nine six zero s flood in Hay Canyon near Grass Valley destroyed part of the Columbia Southern line and led it its abandonment.

 Geography 
Location of Shaniko, OregonShaniko is located at four five  zero ' one one  North, one two zero  four five ' one one  West ( four five . zero zero two nine five five , - one two zero . seven five three one four nine ), at an elevation of three , three four four feet ( one zero one nine m), according to Oregon Blue Book.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one . two km ( zero . five mi ), none of which is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two six people, one four households, and nine families residing in the city. The population density is two one . eight km ( five five . nine mi ). There are three five housing units at an average density of two nine . four km ( seven five . three mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine two . three one % White and seven . six nine % African American.

There are one four households out of which seven . one % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five zero . zero % are married couples living together, zero % have a female householder with no husband present, and three five . seven % are non-families. two one . four % of all households are made up of individuals and one four . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is one . eight six and the average family size is two . one one .

In the city the population is spread out with seven . seven % under the age of one eight , zero % from one eight to two four , one one . five % from two five to four four , four two . three % from four five to six four , and three eight . five % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is six one years. For every one zero zero females there are one three six . four males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are one four zero . zero males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two eight , seven five zero , and the median income for a family is $ three one , two five zero .  '''Aloha''' is a census-designated place and an unincorporated community located in Washington County, Oregon. It was named in one nine one two by Robert Caples, after the Hawaiian word, ''aloha'', although the place name is pronounced instead of . As of the two zero zero zero Census, this unincorporated community had a total population of four one , seven four one . 

Aloha is considered by its residents as one of the few remaining affordable yet desirable housing markets left in the Portland metro area, and is a desirable market for working families due to its close proximity to a number of major Intel campuses, and the Nike world headquarters. While the neighborhood currently consists of mostly single family, low density dwellings, higher density dwellings have become increasingly common due to the Portland metro area's Urban Growth Boundary, and the recent extension of the MAX (Metro Area Express) light rail line along Aloha's northern boundary. Aloha is serviced by two school districts, Beaverton and Hillsboro, which both consistently rank high on school performance evaluations.

History
The Aloha post office was established on January eight , one nine one two . It was supposedly named by Robert Caples who worked for the railroad passing through the area, but the reason for the name was unknown. Another popularly cited source claims that Julius Buck was the first postmaster and that he named the office Aloah after a small resort on Lake Winnebago in Wisconsin. During the application process, the last two letters were transposed by the Post Office Department. However, the local pronunciation has remained Ah-lo-wa rather than Ah-lo-ha. 

Aloha has been, for most of its existence, a rural community. With the increase of suburban development in eastern Washington County starting in the one nine five zero s, Aloha would have become another indistinguishable block of housing when Intel bought land in one nine seven four at the intersection of the Tualatin Valley Highway and one nine eight th Ave, which became the first of several plants Intel has built in Washington County between Hillsboro and Beaverton.

An attempt at incorporation in the early one nine eight zero 's failed at the ballot box. Since then, its location between the cities of Hillsboro and Beaverton have made it vulnerable to annexation battles between the two cities. Agreements in two zero zero five between Beaverton and Washington County have limited Beaverton annexations in the Aloha area for one zero years.

 '''Cedar Hills''' is a census-designated place and neighborhood in Washington County, Oregon, near the intersection of highways two one seven and U.S. two six . Cedar Hills was the largest single housing tract development in the western United States at the time of its creation in one nine six one . 

Originally located in unincorporated Washington County, part of the neighborhood has since been annexed by the city of Beaverton, and in a plan agreed to by the county and Beaverton the remainder is scheduled for annexation by two zero one zero .

Property within Cedar Hills is governed by the Homes Association of Cedar Hills.

As of the two zero zero zero census, the neighborhood had a total population of eight , nine four nine .

 '''Cedar Mill''' is a census-designated place and an unincorporated community located in Washington County, Oregon, mostly north of U.S. Highway two six and west of the Willamette Stone. It received its name from a sawmill on Cedar Mill Creek, which cut Western Redcedars which were the dominant tree in the area; the mill's pond was near the intersection of one one nine th and Cornell Road, which could still be seen into the one nine six zero s. As of the two zero zero zero census, the community had a total population of one two , five nine seven .

Most of the land, as was typical in the Tualatin Valley, was settled in accord with the Donation Land Claim Act of one eight five zero . It became a school district in one eight five six . According to ''Oregon Geographic Names'', a Cedar Mill post office was established in one eight seven four , in the John Quincy Adams Young house, which still stands on Cornell Road and is being renovated to become a Tualatin Hills Park and Recreation District facility.

 '''Forest Grove''' is a city located in Washington County two five miles west of Portland, Oregon. A missionary settlement founded in the one eight four zero s as West Tuality Plains, the name was selected for the community on January one zero , one eight five one at a meeting of the trustees of Tualatin Academy (later known as Pacific University). J. Quinn Thornton was the individual who suggested the name. Pacific University has been the most distinctive aspect of the town throughout its history. Originally a small farm town, it is now primarily a bedroom suburb of Portland. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one seven , seven zero eight .

 '''Garden Home-Whitford''' is a census-designated place (CDP) consisting of the neighborhoods of '''Garden Home''' and the smaller '''Whitford''' area in Washington County, Oregon.  They are located in the southwest hills of Portland, near Beaverton. As of the two zero zero zero census, the CDP had a total population of six , nine three one .

 History 

According to ''Oregon Geographic Names'', a Garden Home post office was established in one eight eight two . Garden Home was an established community when the Oregon Electric Railway was built at the beginning of the two zero th century, which named a depot on the line for the community. Whitford was a station on the same line, located at the present-day intersection of Allen and Scholls Ferry Roads; the name was created by combining the names of W. A. White and A.C. Bedford, New York investors who were directors of the railway.

Whitford station closed when the railway stopped running around one nine two zero , and unlike Garden Home, which became the name of a Portland suburb, Whitford exists today primarily as the name of a Beaverton middle school.

In a plan agreed to by Washington County and Beaverton, Garden Home is scheduled for annexation by Beaverton by the year two zero one zero . Now, the Garden Home area is one of the few places where the City of Portland lies outside of Multnomah County

 Geography 
Location of Garden Home-Whitford, OregonGarden Home-Whitford CDP is centered at four five  two seven ' four one  North, one two two  four five ' five zero  West ( four five . four six one three four zero , - one two two . seven six three eight zero seven ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of four . nine km ( one . nine mi ), none of which is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are six , nine three one people, three , zero four eight households, and one , eight three four families residing in the CDP. The population density is one , four zero eight . five km ( three , six five six . nine mi ). There are three , one seven five housing units at an average density of six four five . two km ( one , six seven five . two mi ). The racial makeup of the CDP is nine one . seven nine % White, three . one seven % Asian, zero . seven five % African American, zero . four zero % Native American, zero . one six % Pacific Islander, zero . seven two % from other races, and three . zero zero % from two or more races.  three . two zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are three , zero four eight households out of which two six . three % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four seven . eight % are married couples living together, nine . three % have a female householder with no husband present, and three nine . eight % are non-families. three zero . six % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . two % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . two six and the average family size is two . eight three .

The population in the CDP is spread out with two one . one % under the age of one eight , six . five % from one eight to two four , three one . six % from two five to four four , two seven . seven % from four five to six four , and one three . one % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Hillsboro''' is a city located in Washington County, Oregon. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of seven zero , one eight six . According to the city records and street signs, the population has grown to seven nine , three zero four . It is the county seat of Washington County.

 History 
The city was founded by David Hill ( one eight zero nine - one eight five zero ) in the one eight four zero s. It went by two other names -- East Tualatin Plains and Columbia -- before it became to Hillsborough in honor of Hill after his death; the spelling was later simplified to Hillsboro. It incorporated in one eight seven six .

 Geography 
Location of Hillsboro, OregonHillsboro is located at four five  three one ' two six  North, one two two  five six ' three four  West ( four five . five two three seven seven six , - one two two . nine four two eight six five ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of five five . nine km ( two one . six mi ).  five five . nine km ( two one . six mi ) of it is land and zero . zero five % is water.

Hillsboro is located in the Tualatin Valley, and the Tualatin River forms part of the southern city limits. The geography of that area is fairly flat. Hillsboro is about one eight miles to the west of Portland, Oregon, with Beaverton, Oregon located in the intervening area.

 Economy 
Many high-tech companies operate in Hillsboro, making it the center of Oregon's Silicon Forest. In particular, Intel's largest site is Hillsboro. Sun Microsystems High-End Operations is headquartered in Hillsboro. Other high-tech companies with factories in Hillsboro include Fujitsu, Epson, NEC, and Tri-Quint Semiconductor.

 '''King City''' is a city located in Washington County, Oregon. Its name was picked arbitrarily by the Tualatin Development Company, Inc., which used a royalty theme in naming the city streets. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one , nine four nine .

 History

Created as a planned adult community, King City was incorporated in March of one nine six six . The city's legal restrictions which forbid minors from living within its city limits for more than a short time have since been subjected to increasing criticism.

Due to controversy in the annexation by the City of Tigard of the Bull Mountain area directly north of King City, a proposal for King City to annex the area instead was made. Since the population and size of Bull Mountain is significantly large (about five , six zero zero registered voters), compared with King City, this would be a noteworthy change in King City.

 '''Raleigh Hills''' is a census-designated place and neighborhood within the metropolitan area of Portland, Oregon, in the United States. It is located in the southwest hills in Washington County, with Beaverton to the west, West Slope to the north, and Progress to the south. As of the two zero zero zero census, the census-designated place had a total population of five , eight six five .

History
According to ''Oregon Geographic Names'', Raleigh Hills was named after Raleigh Robinson, a resident of the neighborhood. A post office named Raleigh was established in the area April one eight nine two , and was closed twelve years later. Southern Pacific's Red Electric Line had a stop in Raleigh from one nine one four until the line ceased operation in one nine three zero . A Raleigh Hills branch of the Portland post office was opened in one nine six eight . In a plan agreed to by the county and Beaverton, Raleigh Hills is scheduled for annexation by Beaverton by the year two zero one zero .

 ''Shine Road'' The name tells the history of this back road in Hemingway, South Carolina
Revenue men at the site of moonshine stills, Kentucky, one nine one one or before
'''Moonshining''' is the making of whiskey surreptitiously and illegally. Because the activity of distilling whiskey unlawfully was usually done at night under the light of the moon, the word became both a verb, meaning making the liquor, and a noun, meaning the liquor that was made. The reason it is done at night, and usually somewhere away from houses and buildings, is that the distillation process requires heat to boil the alcoholic liquor from the mash, so it produces a considerable amount of smoke and steam, which can be visible for a great distance if it is done outdoors in the daytime. The fire can be seen at night if the still is not set up inside a building or somewhere hidden by rocks andor trees, but buildings (and caves) are not considered as safe as outdoor locations, in case of a raid by the law enforcement authorities (or competition).

Some shiners , as they were called, made a firebox out of stones or bricks, to keep the flames contained while concealing them, and to keep the still off the ground. Quite often, a dry creek bed was employed, particularly in Florida. Many stills were mainly made of copper, which is considered helpful in maintaining a good taste in distilled liquor. A shiner would often make his own still.

Selling moonshine or legally-made alcohol in an illegal manner is bootlegging . One person may perform both functions. A U.S. synonym for moonshine is '''hooch''', a word apparently borrowed into English ca. one eight six seven from the Hoochinoo tribe of Alaska, noted for its homemade liquor. '''White lightning''', '''mountain dew''', '''stumpholewater''', '''liquid stumpblaster''', '''mule-kick''', and '''white mule''' are also attested.

History of moonshining in Appalachia

Appalachia, generally the rural region of the United States in the vicinity of the Appalachian Mountains, has a history of small-scale whiskey production as part of its culture.

The production of whiskey in this area predates the federal taxation of alcoholic beverages. For farmers in remote parts of the country, it was a way to turn their corn into cash when grain prices were down. The imposition of a tax on whiskey was considered an unwanted federal intervention and was largely ignored. The Department of the Treasury sent special agents  revenuers  to prosecute unlawful distilling. Gun battles sometimes occurred when revenuers arrived to enforce the tax. Those battles are often referred to as the Whiskey Rebellion.

Revenue man at the site of a moonshine distillery in Kentucky, one nine one one or before. In this image, the fire is burning, the still working, and the moonshiner's coat hangs on a tree.
The grain used to make the mash, which is the mixture of grain, sugar, water, and yeast that ferments to produce the alcohol, is virtually always corn, so the product is corn liquor (also known as corn whiskey ), sometimes called mountain dew because it appears overnight, or simply shine . (The clear, potent (i.e. high-proof) liquor is also called white lightning because of its effect, or kick .) Today, commercial hog chow is often used, because it is readily available, buying it does not attract the attention of law enforcement, and it is primarily corn, but other corn-based animal feeds can be used instead, and differences in the other ingredients in the feed impart slightly different flavors to the finished product. Ordinary white sugar is often the chief ingredient of moonshine mash, in which case the spirit distilled is technically a rum rather than a whiskey.

The federal authorities who police moonshining are traditionally termed revenuers because they historically worked for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (BATF), which was part of the U.S. Internal Revenue Service until July one nine seven two , when it became a separate bureau within the United States Department of the Treasury. When the Department of Homeland Security was created in two zero zero three , most of BATF was moved to the new agency, but alcohol enforcement remained in Treasury, handled by the new Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau.

Handling shipments of moonshine is often called Ridge-Running , Whiskey-Running , or simply running it, by analogy to rum-running, which originally meant smuggling rum by ship.

Franklin County, Virginia is known as the Moonshine Capital of the world.

Moonshine production today
Moonshine continues to be produced in the U.S., mainly in Appalachia and parts of the South. The simplicity of the process, and the easy availability of key ingredients such as a corn and sugar, make enforcement a difficult task.
However, the huge price advantage that moonshine once held over its legitimate competition legally sold has been reduced. Nevertheless, over half the retail price of a bottle of distilled spirits typically consists of taxes. Many of those who buy moonshine do so for the thrill of obtaining and consuming an illicit product and as a defiance of authority. Also, the number of jurisdictions which ban the sale of alcoholic beverages is steadily decreasing. This means that many of the former consumers of moonshine are much nearer to a legal alcohol sales outlet than was formerly the case. Moonshining is far from totally over, but is certainly far less widespread than was the case decades ago.
For individual moonshiners, with purchase of cheap refined white sugar, moonshine can be produced at a small fraction of the price of heavily taxed and legally sold distilled spirits. This alcohol is also used for some for herbal tinctures.

Product safety
Sloppily-produced moonshine can be contaminated with toxins, mainly from materials used in construction of the still. Despite the well-known hazards, it is claimed that stills constructed using car radiators for a condenser are still used. The lead used in soldering these radiators ends up in the moonshine, and in some cases, glycol products from antifreeze used in the radiator can appear as well. Both are poisonous.

Occasionally moonshine is deliberately mixed with industrial alcohol-containing products, including methanol and denatured alcohol. Results are toxic, with methanol easily capable of causing blindness and death.

Methanol and other toxic alcohols can occur naturally in distilled spirits and are called fusel oils. The methanol is concentrated in the first few percent of condensate produced in a batch. The fusel oils are mostly found at the end of a batch or run. Ordinarily these portions are discarded, though if ingested alone or included with the rest of the distilled product it may cause toxic effects. Like commercial beer, wine, and liquor, properly produced moonshine contains small amounts of methanol at levels that are not toxic. A common way to determine the quality control of a batch of moonshine was to see if the moonshiner would dare to drink it.

In addition, moonshine that is over one zero zero proof (i.e. five zero %) is very flammable and easily ignitable. This is especially true during the distilling process in which oxidized vaporized alcohol can accumulate in the air if there is not enough ventilation.

Moonshining worldwide

Armenia
A crude moonshine (samogon) device in an Armenian village.
The Armenian name for moonshine is '''aragh'''; however, the Russian word '''samogon''' is used more often, as aragh is synonymous with regular vodka. The production of samogon is widespread in Armenia. White mulberry, grape and apricot moonshine are especially popular, particularly in the countryside.

Czech Republic
Czech moonshine is traditionally made from distilling plums and is known as 'slivovitz'. Traditionally produced in many garages and cellars, it is particularly popular in the east of the country, Moravia.

Finland
Finnish moonshine is home-made vodka, usually made from any fermentable carbohydrates, most commonly grain, sugar or potato. The most common name is '''pontikka'''. It is said that this name came about due to the poor quality French wine from Pontacq. Other names are '''kotipolttoinen''' (home burnt), '''ponu''' (short from pontikka), '''tuliliemi''' (fire sauce), '''moscha''' (most common finnish-swedish term), '''korpiroju''' (wildwood junk) or '''korpikuusen kyyneleet''' (tears of wildwood spruce) as stills often are located in distant and badly accessible places. '''Pirtu''' refers to Rectified Spirit, currently illegal outside medicinal or technical purposes.

Unlicensed moonshining is illegal in Finland, but it is often considered a challenge or hobby. In practice prosecution follows only if authorities become aware that the product is being sold. Most Finnish moonshiners use simple pot stills and flash distillation. Some have constructed sophisticated reflux or rock stills for fractional distillation, containing plate columns or packed columns, with reflux filling components of Raschig rings, crushed glass, nuts, glass pellets or steel wool.

Iceland
Icelandic moonshine is largely made by hobbyists as a protest against the high liquor taxes enforced by the government. Due to the lack of natural cover and harsh weather conditions, most moonshining activity occurs indoors in a controlled environment. Although potatoes are the most common constituent of Icelandic moonshine, any carbohydrate can be used, including stale bread.

Ireland

Potato-based moonshine made illegally in Ireland, is called poitn (IPA , anglicized as ''poteen'' or ''potcheen'') or formerly ''potheen'' (IPA but in Ireland ). The term is a diminutive of the word ''pota'' 'a pot'.

Scotland
Illicitly produced whisky from Scotland is called '''peatreek'''. The term refers to the aroma (or ''reek'') infused in the drink by drying the malted barley over a peat fire.

Sweden
The most common moonshine ( hembrnt , literally home burnt ) in Sweden is made of potatoes andor sugar. Common nicknames are Skogsstjrnan (forest star), Garagenkorva (a wordplay on garage and Koskenkorva ) and Chateau de Garage (a pun on French wine brands).

Swedish moonshine is often used for the drink Hger, vnster , meaning Right, left , in which you have moonshine in the right hand and soda in the left, and drink one mouth-full each, in that order.

New Zealand
No discussion of moonshine would be complete without a nod of the head to New Zealand, one of the few countries where home distillation is legal. In New Zealand, stills and instruction in their use are sold openly.

Norway
Due to very high taxation of alcohol, moonshining continues to be a popular albeit illegal activity in various parts of the country, especially in rural areas of the Trndelag and northern parts of the stlandet regions and Solr. Moonshine is called Hjemmebrent in Norwegian, and the Mash is called Sats. In the county of Telemark mash is also referred to as Bs. In the old days on Finnskogen they called the mash The Wine of the Forest (Skogens vin), this name was mostly used by the poorer people who didn't have access to distilling equipment. Moonshine is commonly enjoyed mixed with coffee, and sometimes a spoon of sugar, in Norway. This drink is called Karsk in Trndelag and the northern parts of stlandet, and Kaffedoktor (in Solr). While brewing is permitted in Norway, distilling is not permitted, and it is illegal to possess equipment for distilling. All alcoholic beverages above six zero % (NOT vol. %) is considered hard drugs in Norway, and as such prohibited, and heavily punished.

United States
Although home distillation of ethanol for commercial purposes is still illegal in the United States, legislation was introduced in November of two zero zero one to legalize home distillation in much the same way as home brewing of wine and beer were legalized in one nine seven eight . This bill had a single sponsor and did not make it out of committee. Despite the illegal status, home distillation is growing in popularity in the U.S. with ready availability of instructions, materials and support.

Russian Federation
The Russian name for any home-made distilled alcoholic beverage is called '''samogon''' (ru:     ), literally translated as self-distillate . 
The most popular source for ''samogon'' is sugar as it is quite effective. ''Samogon'' of one distillation only is called '''pervach''' (ru: ), literally translated as the first - it is well known for its impressive smell. The production of samogon is illegal but widespread in Russia.
Samogon, oftentimes had a strong repulsive odor but for lack of any other alcohol, was very popular at one time.

Thailand
In Thailand, home-brewed alcohol, most commonly distilled from rice, is called ''lao khao'' (white spirit). It is sometimes mixed with various herbs to produce a medicinal drink called ''yadong''.

Slovenia
In Slovenia, especially in the western part, moonshine is destiled from fermented grapes, which were left from wine production, and sugar if necessary. It is called ''tropinovec'' (tropine, means squeezed half-dried grapes, in the west of the country) or ''nopc''. Because it has around six zero %- seven zero % of alcohol is often mixed with boiled water to make it lighter( vol. five zero %). Tropinovec is rarely drank in large quantities . It is often mixed with fruits (cherries,pears, etc.) to cover the strong odor and taste, or herbs (Anise, Wolf's bane, etc.) for medical treatment.

Moonshine in popular culture
Moonshine is often portrayed in the media in a clay jug marked only with XXX. Supposedly, the moonshiner would inscribe a single X on the jug each time the mixture passed through a still. This image of a jug or bottle marked XXX is used in comic strips and cartoons to depict an intoxicating beverage. For example, Drinky Crow is often shown drinking from one of these stereotypical jugs. Although clay jugs may have been widely used in the one nine th-Century, glass Mason Jars have predominated since at least the early two zero th-century, with plastic jugs also coming into use in the one nine seven zero s. Devotees of Moonshine usually prefer to purchase and consume the elixer from Mason Jars because it is easier to judge quality and lacks the plastic aftertaste.

The one nine five eight movie ''Thunder Road'' was about running moonshine. During Prohibition cars were souped-up to create a more maneuverable and faster car. Many of the original drivers of NASCAR were former Ridge-Runners in the cars they raced in.

Steve Earle's popular song Copperhead Road revolves around a family of moonshiners.

In ''The Great Escape'' ( one nine six eight ), Hilts (Steve McQueen) and Hendley (James Garner) brew moonshine to help celebrate the Fourth of July. It's so strong, upon tasting it, they can only comment Wow! very hoarsely.

In the one nine eight zero 's television show (and two zero zero five movie) The Dukes of Hazzard, both based on the one nine seven five movie , moonshine was a central element of the backstory. The Duke family were covert moonshiners, until the nephews were caught running moonshine out of the county.  Uncle Jesse made a deal with the government to shut down the moonshining operation; in exchange, his nephews were released and were on probation for most of the series. Many of the early episodes center around moonshine made by someone else, usually associates of Boss Hogg, planting said liquor on Duke property in an effort to revoke the younger Dukes' probation. This series plays off of a large number of the stereotypes commonly associated with the Appalachian moonshiners.

Moonshining (along with alcohol in general) is a common theme in American Country music.

 Sherwood, Oregon

'''Sherwood''' is a city located in Washington County, Oregon. It is a residential community in the Tualatin Valley southwest of Portland. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one one , seven nine one .

 History 

Prior to western settlers arriving in one eight five three , the Tualatin Indians inhabited the area.

During the early years of settlement, farmers had to grow nearly everything they needed; twice a year they would undertake the three -day journey to the town of Portland for staples such as sugar, salt, and syrup.

In one eight eight five , J.C. Smock gave a right-of-way on his property to the railroad, and a few years later planned the town of Smockville around the tracks with his wife Mary Ellen Hall. The town incorporated in one eight nine two , at which time the residents felt they needed a more sophisticated name. Since the surrounding area was reminiscent of Sherwood Forest in England, Robert Alexander, a local business owner, suggested the name.

The main industry in the one eight nine zero 's was a brick yard supplying building material to Portland. The buildings in the current day area of Old Town were built during this period. After the brickyard closed in one eight nine five , the economy was based on fruit and vegetable canning and a tannery. Manufacturing is the city's main industry today.

The population of the city in one nine one one was three five zero within a one square mile city limit, which had grown to one four , zero five zero people and four . five sq. miles by two zero zero four . 

 Geography

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of one zero . five km ( four . one mi ).  one zero . five km ( four . one mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one one , seven nine one people, four , two five three households, and three , three zero zero families residing in the city. The population density is one , one one eight . six km ( two , eight nine five . five mi ).  '''McMinnville''' is the county seat and largest city of Yamhill County, Oregon. According to ''Oregon Geographic Names'', it was named by its founder, William T. Newby, an early immigrant on the Oregon Trail, for his home town of McMinnville, Tennessee. As of January two zero zero six ,the city had a total population of three zero , zero eight six .

History
McMinnville was incorporated as a town in one eight seven six and became a city in one eight eight two . County residents voted to move the county seat of Yamhill County from Lafayette to McMinnville in one eight eight six .

A tourist attraction located in McMinnville is the Evergreen Aviation Museum, which houses the Spruce Goose, the world's largest propeller-driven airplane, built by the famed aviator Howard Hughes. The museum, a large symmetrical building with a glass front, holds many airplanes used in America's wars during the twentieth century.

McMinnville is also known amongst UFO enthusiasts for photographs published on the front page of the June nine , one nine five zero edition of the city's newspaper, the ''News Register'', reportedly of an unidentified flying object seen a month earlier. ''The Oregonian'' published the photographs the next day, and within a week they were published in ''LIFE'' magazine. The photographs were taken on a farm near McMinnville by a farming couple, Mr. and Mrs. Paul Trent. Mrs. Trent was the first to see the object - it resembled a classic flying saucer - and she pointed it out to her husband, who obtained a camera from their farmhouse and took two photos before the saucer flew away. A debate has raged for decades between UFO researchers, who claim that the photos are genuine and are among the best ever taken of a UFO, and UFO skepticsdebunkers, who claim that the photos are a hoax. Both sides in the debate have hired photographic experts numerous times to do a professional analysis of the photos, but so far neither side has offered convincing evidence to prove their case. The Trent's background was also thoroughly checked, and to date there has been no evidence brought forth implicating the Trents in a hoax. The whole sequence of events has led to a UFO Festival being held in McMinnville each year.

Another popular festival happens to be McMinnville's main summer attraction: Turkey Rama . This event is a three-day festival held in downtown McMinnville celebrating the on-going tradition of the turkey barbecue. The barbeque was started in one nine three eight by turkey farmers in Yamhill County, when the main source of wealth in the county was largley based on the booming turkey-farming industry. Now, commercial exhibitions have replaced the turkey exhibitions , and so the turkey-judging competitions and turkey races have been eliminated in favor of more turkey-friendly rides, booths, and outdoor entertainment.

Wine
Since the one nine nine zero s, the majority of the vineyards of the Willamette Valley American Viticultural Area (AVA) have centered around McMinnville, thus giving this city a claim to the title of the capital of Oregon's wine industry. In January two zero zero five , a McMinnville AVA was established after an application from Youngberg Hill Vineyards. The new AVA includes one four wineries and five two three acres ( two . one two km) within the Willamette Valley AVA. The city is at the northeastern border of its AVA namesake.

The International Pinot Noir Celebration has been held every July since one nine eight seven on the Linfield College campus.

Geography
 Location of McMinnville, Oregon'''McMinnville''' is located five zero miles from the Pacific Ocean, three zero miles from Portland, Oregon, and two five miles from the state capitol, centered at four five  one two ' four two  North, one two three  one one ' five zero  West ( four five . two one one eight , - one two three . one nine seven three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two five . six km ( nine . nine mi), none of which is covered with water, in spite of an average of four two inches of rain per year.

Demographics
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two six , four nine nine people residing in the city, among nine , three six seven households and six , four six three families. The population density is one , zero three three . five km ( two , six seven five . eight mi). There are nine , eight three four housing units at an average density of three eight three . five km ( nine nine three . zero mi). The racial makeup of the city is eight six . three nine % White, one . three nine % Native American, one . two five % Asian, zero . six eight % Black or African American, and zero . one eight % Pacific Islander.  one four . six four % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race. seven . two six % identify themselves as from other races, and two . eight six % from two or more races.

There are nine , three six seven households out of which three five . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five three . five % are married couples living together, one zero . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and three one . zero % are non-families. two three . nine % of all households are made up of individuals and one one . five % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . six six and the average family size is three . one three .

In the city, the population is spread out with two six . three % under the age of one eight , one four . seven % from one eight to two four , two six . nine % from two five to four four , one seven . nine % from four five to six four , and one four . three % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three two years. For every one zero zero females there are nine three . seven males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are nine zero . six males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ three eight , nine five three , and the median income for a family is $ four four , zero one three . Males have a median income of $ three three , five one seven versus $ two four , four zero five for females. Out of the total population, one four . zero % of those under the age of one eight and seven . eight % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line. The area is slightly conservative. In the two zero zero four presidential elections, George W. Bush won the city five six %- four three %.

City Description
McMinnville has a varied landscape, including low-dropping mini valleys and forest-like patches of evergreens and other trees surrounding the downtown park area and scattered throughout McMinnville.

McMinnville has several parks scattered across the city. The best-known city parks are the Wortman Park and the Downtown Park, which is within walking distance from the downtown business district. In one nine one zero , the city sold $ three , zero zero zero worth of park bonds to finance construction of a band stand and a small zoo featuring bears, deer and other local animals. Near the site of Lower City Park, along the Cozine Creek, there used to be a large flour mill, called the Star Mill. The mill was closed in one nine two one and was damaged by a fire in one nine two seven . The city of McMinnville sold $ eight , five zero zero zero worth of bonds to finance the purchase of the property. The tract ran from Star Mill Way to Cozine Creek and West Second Street, to the Mill pond site. The pond site is now occupied by tennis courts. Wortman Park is a very large park with a small stream running through it and beautiful trees scattered throughout the whole area. In fact, there are so many trees in the park that it sometimes creates an umbrella effect from the weather, keeping the park shady in the summer (though still hot and dry) and only damp or moist when it rains.

Parents of the nearby towns of Amity and Lafyette often send their children to McMinnville's public schools. There are five elementary schools in McMinnville (Cook, Newby, Memorial,Colombus, and Grandhaven), two middle schools (called Patton and Duniway), and one High School (McMinnville High).

McMinnville is a quaint, medium-sized Oregon town with a steadily growing population, and an expanding art and music scene. Much of the town's growth can be explained by its proximity to Salem, Oregon's state capitol, which is only a thirty-to-fifty-minute drive from McMinnville. Portland, Oregon's largest city, is only an hour's drive by automobile.

 '''Braddock''' is a borough located in the eastern suburbs of Pittsburgh in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, ten miles ( one six km) above the mouth of the Monongahela river. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of two , nine one two . The town is named for General Edward Braddock ( one six nine five - one seven five five ). The Braddock Expedition, particularly his infamous crossing of the Monongahela River on July nine  one seven five five at this place lead to his own fatal wounding and a sound defeat of his British troops who had been moving against the French at Fort Duquesne. This battle was a key beginning in the French and Indian War. 

Braddock was probably first settled about one seven nine five . It was incorporated in one eight six seven . The town and its industrial economy began in one eight seven three when Andrew Carnegie founded there The J. Edgar Thomson Steel Works. This historic steel mill remains a part of the United States Steel Corporation. This era of the town's history is best known from the novel Out of This Furnace by Thomas Bell. 

The early population figures were these:  one eight nine zero , eight , five six one ; one nine zero zero , one five , six five four ; one nine one zero , one nine , three five seven ; one nine two zero , two zero , eight seven nine ; one nine four zero , one eight , three two six . Braddock lost its importance with the collapse of the steel-making industry in the US in one nine eight four .

 '''Carnegie''' is a borough located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, five miles ( eight km) (direct) southwest of Pittsburgh. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of eight , three eight nine . 

Carnegie is not situated beside a river, therefore no great steel mill existed there (despite its name). The early manufactories were of the light industry types. Coal mining existed there, as did the manufacturing of stoves. Lead works existed too, but those manufactories no longer exist. 

 Geography 
Carnegie is located at four zero  two four ' two five  North, eight zero  five ' one two  West ( four zero . four zero six eight one nine , - eight zero . zero eight six seven nine five ). It is approximately seven miles southwest of downtown Pittsburgh.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of four . three km ( one . six mi ).  four . three km ( one . six mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

History and culture
Carnegie's population count in one nine zero zero was seven , three three zero ; in one nine one zero , one zero , zero zero nine ; in one nine two zero , one one , five one six ; and in one nine four zero , one two , six six three . 

Carnegie is named after Andrew Carnegie, who donated one of his libraries for the gesture. It was incorporated around one nine zero two - one nine zero three from the boroughs of Chartiers and Mansfield (separated by Chartiers Creek). Later, the borough annexed part of Robinson Township (now Rosslyn Heights).

Neighborhoods include Rosslyn Heights, Cubbage Hill, Irishtown, Forsythe Hill, Library Hill, and Old Mansfield. Many neighborhoods were at one time or another mined for coal. The main industries were a few excuses for steel mills. Carnegie had a rail yard that had connections to several railroads early in the twentieth century. The Wabash Pittsburgh Terminal railroad was one of them. The Pennsylvania Railroad connected Carnegie later. In the one nine seven zero s, Carnegie suffered economically with the closure of the great steel mills such as J  L in and around Pittsburgh and the railroad yard stopped its growth. 

Notable celebrities include Honus Wagner (who, according to local legend, was discovered throwing rocks along the rail line not too far from his home). Mike Ditka also spent some of his early years here (a ballfield on Cubbage Hill was named after him).

Carnegie is ethnically diverse, marked by the number of churches as well as bars in the neighborhood. There are several Catholic churches serving different communities - Polish (St. Ignatius), Irish (St. Luke), German (St. Josephs) and Italian (Holy Souls) - as well as at least two Ukrainian orthodox churches, several Methodist churches, several Baptist Churches and a Synagogue. Another peculiar aspect of Carnegie is the number of local clubs there are (VFW, FOE, AL, Elks, Polish Eagles, Polish Sportsmen, AOH, Ukrainian Club (the Ukes ), plus a number of smaller clubs).

In the one nine two zero s or one nine three zero s, the Ku Klux Klan came to Carnegie to try and recruit members. A riot ensued, and at least one person was killed.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are eight , three eight nine people, three , nine six seven households, and two , one three four families residing in the borough. The population density is one , nine six three . zero km ( five , zero seven six . seven mi ). There are four , two four nine housing units at an average density of nine nine four . three km ( two , five seven one . three mi ). There are three , nine six seven households out of which two two . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three seven . four % are married couples living together, one three . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and four six . two % are non-families. four zero . four % of all households are made up of individuals and one eight . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one zero and the average family size is two . eight six .

In the borough the population is spread out with one nine . four % under the age of one eight , eight . one % from one eight to two four , three zero . four % from two five to four four , two two . zero % from four five to six four , and two zero . one % who are six five years of age or older.  '''Castle Shannon''' is a borough located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of eight , five five six .

 History 

The first families settled Castle Shannon in one seven eight six in pursuit of farmland and timber. The most prominent farm was owned by David Strawbridge, which he named Castle Shanahan. Over time, the farm would lend its name to the area, as Shanahan would evolve into Shannon. 

In one eight seven one , a railroad from Pittsburgh to Castle Shannon was built. Development was stimulated by free two-year passes for the railroad given to anybody building a home. In one eight seven seven , a second railroad was built from Finleyville through Castle Shannon to the West End of Pittsburgh. In one nine zero nine , the right of way through the valley containing Castle Shannon was purchased by Pittsburgh Railroad. This helped lead to Castle Shannon becoming a center for coal mining. The Pittsburgh and West Virginia railroad, still active today, came shortly after.

The First National Bank in Castle Shannon was the site of a much publicized bank robbery in one nine one seven . $ one eight , five zero zero was taken in the robbery, of which $ one zero , five zero zero was immediately recovered from one man shot during the escape. The full sum was never recovered.

Castle Shannon was incorporated as a borough in one nine one nine , formed from parts of Baldwin, Mt. Lebanon, and Bethel Township.

 Geography 
Castle Shannon is located at four zero  two one ' five five  North, eight zero  one ' one one  West ( four zero . three six five one four nine , - eight zero . zero one nine eight five zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of four . two km ( one . six mi ).  four . two km ( one . six mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics

Interstate three seven six , known as the Parkway East by native Pittsburghers, runs through Churchill.  '''Clairton''' is a city located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, along the Monongahela River. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of eight , four nine one . The city was the setting for the movie The Deer Hunter ( one nine seven eight ). It also is home to Clairton Works the largest coke manufacturing facility in the United States.

 Geography 
Clairton is located at four zero  one seven ' four seven  North, seven nine  five three ' one four  West ( four zero . two nine six four one nine , - seven nine . eight eight seven zero nine zero ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of seven . eight km ( three . zero mi ).  seven . one km ( two . eight mi ) of it is land and zero . six km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is eight . three one % water.

 History 
Clairtons existence began when the United States Steel Company acquired the towns site just after the turn of the century as a location for an integrated steel mill. The site had more than a thousand acres of level land suitable for a large industrial complex. In January of one nine two two , the City of Clairton was incorporated as a City of the Third Class with a population of approximately one one , zero zero zero . This incorporation was prompted by industry, which was taxed by the three boroughs -Clairton, Wilson and North Clairton - which were chartered separately prior to the incorporation of the City of Clairton. 

During the next several decades, growth and advancement indicated a thriving city. As the steel mill expanded, the population of Clairton grew. Clairton took on a life of its own, including a business district and educational, religious, and cultural facilities. However, with the decline of the steel industry in the early one nine eight zero s, Clairton began to experience severe problems in its employment and tax base, which spurred a major economic shock to the community. 

In one nine eight eight , the City of Clairton was designated as a distressed municipality by the Commonwealths Department of Community Affairs (DCA). Pursuant to Act four seven of one nine eight seven (the Financially Distressed Municipalities Act), DCA commissioned the development of a recovery plan for Clairton. (Steel Valley Council of Governments- City of Claiton)-users.adelphia.net~svcogClairton.html

 '''Collier Township''' is a township located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the township had a total population of five , two six five .

 Geography 
According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of three six . nine km ( one four . two mi ).  three six . eight km ( one four . two mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is zero . two one % water.

 History 

The earliest settlers of the township were James Ewing and Gabriel and Isaac Walker. James Ewing was born in Cecil County, Maryland, about one seven three zero , emigrated to the west in one seven seven zero , and built a gristmill on Robinson's run. His claim comprised a thousand acres. Gabriel and Isaac Walker were born in Lancaster County, Pa., the former in one seven four four , the latter in one seven four six . The Scotch-Irish brothers emigrated to the west in one seven seven two , and purchased two thousand acres from John Henry. Gabriel located near Hays crossing, on the Pan Handle railroad, and Isaac at Walker's Mills. 

Collier Township was erected on June seven , one eight seven five , comprised of portions of Robinson and South Fayette townships, and a half-square mile of North Fayette. The township is named for Hon. Frederick H. Collier, a county court judge.

 History 
Sketch of Elizabeth and West Elizabeth, circa one eight nine seven .

 one seven eight seven - Elizabeth (formerly Elizabeth Town) was founded by Samuel Mackay, Colonel Stephen Bayard and his wife Elizabeth Mackay Bayard (for whom the town was named).
 one eight zero three - The keelboat used for the first stages of the Lewis and Clark Expedition was built in Elizabeth. (This claim is disputed by the city of Pittsburgh, which makes a similar claim.) (See references below.)
 one eight three four - On April two , one eight three four , a charter was issued to incorporate the Town of Elizabeth as a borough.

 Early industry 
Among the earliest industries of Elizabeth were glass making, safe making, steamboat building, and ship building.

 '''Homestead''' is a borough located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, in the Mon valley, seven miles ( one one km) southeast of Pittsburgh. Settled in one eight seven one , Homestead was chartered in one eight eight zero . In the past, Homestead served as the place where one of the world's most productive steel mills existed. About seven , zero zero zero men were employed in the plant around the turn of the century in one nine zero zero when the population of Homestead was one two , five five four people. The industrious people of Homestead increased their numbers to one eight , seven one three in one nine one zero , and to  two zero , four five two in one nine two zero . In one nine four zero , one nine , zero four one people lived in Homestead.  After the end of World War II, an inexorable decline in the steel-making industry of the United States took place. By one nine seven zero , it had become well-nigh impossible to obtain employment at the Homestead Works, which was not producing much steel at that time. The Homestead Works was demolished afterwards. As a direct result of the loss of employment, the number of people living in Homestead dwindled.  By the time of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of three , five six nine . 

 Geography 
Homestead is located at four zero  two four ' one eight  North, seven nine  five four ' two eight  West ( four zero . four zero five zero six nine , - seven nine . nine zero seven seven eight five ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of one . six km ( zero . six mi ).  one . five km ( zero . six mi ) of it is land and zero . two km ( zero . one mi ) of it is water. The total area is one one . one one % water.

The racial makeup of the borough is four two . six four % White, five one . three zero % African American, zero . two five % Native American, two . eight three % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, zero . two two % from other races, and two . seven two % from two or more races.  zero . six two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , six zero seven households out of which two four . four % have children under the age of one eight living with them, two three . three % are married couples living together, two four . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and four seven . five % are non-families. four two . five % of all households are made up of individuals and one nine . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one six and the average family size is two . nine nine .

 History 
Homestead gained international notoriety in July one eight nine two as the site of a violent clash between locked-out steelworkers and hired Pinkerton guards. When Andrew Carnegie, owner of the local Homestead Steel Works, announced in the spring of one eight nine two that skilled workers would receive a reduction in wages, the advisory committee of the Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers refused to sign a new contract. Carnegie's management locked the workforce out, declaring that the union would no longer be recognized at the steel works. He believed that too many cooks spoil the broth. 

To secure the mill from the disgruntled workers, management hired hundreds of men from the Pinkerton National Detective Agency. When barges carrying the Pinkertons arrived at the mill on the morning of July six , workers and townspeople met them at the riverbanks. Though eyewitness accounts differed on which side fired first, a day-long armed battle ensued which resulted in eleven deaths and dozens of injuries. The governor of Pennsylvania eventually called out the National Guard to restore order to the town and secure the mill. Carnegie successfully destroyed the union in Homestead and, by extension, in most of his other steel mills through the nation. The Battle of Homestead, as the event came to be known, represented a stunning setback for unionization in the highly-mechanized steel industry.

see also: Homestead Strike

 Attractions 

Homestead is home to two local attractions. The first is the Homestead Waterfront, which is home to many restaurants, movie theaters, and many kinds of stores. The second is Sandcastle, a water park. Both of the attractions are built on the former site of the Homestead Works.

 Transportation 

An important state route, Pennsylvania Route eight three seven , runs through Homestead. Interstate three seven six is only a few miles away from Homestead. For public transit, the Port Authority of Allegheny County has several bus routes running through Homestead that go to downtown Pittsburgh and to McKeesport.

Homestead is served by three railroads: the Norfolk Southern, CSX Trasportation and the Union Railroad. All three used to have large operations when the Homestead steel mill was open. Now that the mill has closed only one company, WMELCo, is served by the railroad. The Union Railroad had a large yard to serve the plant, which is now Waterfront Drive.

 '''Oswald Teichmller''' (June one eight , one nine one three - September one one , one nine four three ) was a German mathematician who introduced quasi-conformal mappings and differential geometric methods into complex analysis. His work was published in ''Deutsche Mathematik'', a journal in synthetic mathematics founded by Ludwig Bieberbach and has been neglected for a while for political reasons. Rediscovered few years after his death, the theory of Teichmller spaces (a moduli space theory for Riemann surfaces) was further developed by Lars Ahlfors, Lipman Bers and others. The ''Teichmller representative'' or ''Teichmller character'' is a construction with p-adic numbers. 

Teichmller was a passionate Nazi who joined the Wehrmacht in one nine three nine and died fighting on the Eastern Front.

 '''McKees Rocks''' is a borough located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, along the west bank of the Ohio River, adjoining Pittsburgh. In the past, it was known for its extensive iron and steel interests. Also, there were large railroad machine shops, and manufactories of enamel ware, lumber, wall plaster, locomotive and car springs, nuts and bolts, malleable castings, chains and forgings, freight and passenger cars, tin ware, concrete, cigars, etc. In one nine zero zero , six , three five three people resided here; in one nine one zero , one four , seven zero two ; in one nine two zero , one six , seven one three , and in one nine four zero , one seven , zero two one people inhabited McKees Rocks.  '''McKeesport''' is a city located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, USA, at the confluence of the Monongahela and Youghiogheny Rivers. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of two four , zero four zero . It is the two nd largest city in Allegheny County behind only Pittsburgh. five five , three five five people lived in McKeesport in one nine four zero . The decrease in the population is attributable to the general economic malaise which descended onto the region when the steel-making industry moved elsewhere.

Settled in one seven nine five and named in honor of John McKee, its founder, McKeesport remained a village until one eight three zero when coal mining began in the district. Large deposits of bituminous coal existed.

McKeesport was incorporated as a borough in one eight four two and as a city in one eight nine one . Population in one nine zero zero , three four , two two seven ; in one nine one zero , four two , six nine four ; in one nine one four (US estimate), four five , nine six five ; and in one nine two zero , four five , nine seven five .  '''Moon Township''' is a township located along the Ohio River in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the township had a total population of two two , two nine zero . It is home to Robert Morris University. The township is located one five miles west of Pittsburgh, PA and is one of Pittsburgh's major suburban centers, developed mainly due to its proximity to the Pittsburgh International Airport. Development success can also be credited to major corporations headquarters in Moon like Dick's Sporting Goods, Nova Chemicals, some departments of Aquafresh and GlaxoSmithKline, and FedEx Ground. Robert Morris University also feeds the economy of the town's University Blvd neighborhood. The town will grow rapidly within the next few years due to many new construction projects such as the redevelopment of University Blvd and West Hills Shopping District.

The township is home to Pennsylvania State Senator John Pippy and Pennsylvania State Representative T. Mark Mustio.

 Moon Area School District 

Moon Township is home to the Moon Area School District, which is comprised of youth from both Moon Township and Crescent Townships. Moon graduates over three zero zero students each year, with the majority of those entering post-secondary four-year educational programs.

Moon athletics are among the best in the AAA class, with back-to-back State Baseball Champions in two zero zero one and two zero zero two and State Basketball Champions in two zero zero four . Girls Soccer and Volleyball and Boys Soccer have reached the Semifinals of the State tournaments in the last frew years as well. Moon Area High School football is known as one of the best programs in the state, reaching playoff contention one zero of the last one two years. A member of one of the strongest AAA conferences in the nation, the Parkway Conference, Moon's rivals include West Allegheny School District, home to University of Pittsburgh quarterback Tyler Palko, Montour School District, the recent focus of ESPN's reality show Bound For Glory , and Hopewell School District, hometown of the one nine seven six Heisman Winner and Football Hall of Fame member Tony Dorsett. A member of the WPIAL, the largest high school sports league in the nation, Moon remains a strong competitor year after year.

 The School Board Crisis 

With the aging buildings located on the Moon Township High School and Middle School campus, the school board, several years ago, decided to look into renovation or rebuilding of both or one of the school buildings. While the discussions lasted several years, the school board decided to go through with a plan to build a new high school and convert the current high school building into a middle school facility. With the high price of the project, taxpayers began to voice concern over the project. Several organizations within the community attempted to stop the project before it could begin. In two zero zero five , the battle escalated, as the Democrat-majority school board sued the Republican-controlled township board of supervisors. In Novemeber two zero zero five , the school board's makeup switched to a Republican-controlled majority, with the newly elected officers promising to attempt to stop the school building project.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of six two . four km ( two four . one mi ).  six one . five km ( two three . seven mi ) of it is land and zero . nine km ( zero . three mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . four one % water.
