History
Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament
A major railroad town, Altoona was founded by the Pennsylvania Railroad in one eight four nine as the site for a construction complex. Altoona was incorporated as a borough on February six , one eight five four , and as a city under legislation approved on April three , one eight six seven , and February eight , one eight six eight . The town grew rapidly in the late one nine th century, its population approximately two , zero zero zero in one eight five four , one zero , zero zero zero in ' seven zero , and two zero , zero zero zero in ' eight zero .

The demand for locomotives during the Civil War stimulated much of this growth, and by the later years of the war Altoona was known as a valuable city for the North. It was considered by Confederate General Robert E. Lee as a target during the Army of Northern Virginia's mid- one eight six three entry into Pennsylvania, before being repelled at the Battle of Gettysburg. Also notable is the Union's War Governors' Conference, held at Altoona's Logan House.

Notable is the Horseshoe Curve, a famous curved section of track owned by the Pennsylvania Railroad, now a tourist attraction and National Historic Landmark, and its funicular. The Curve was used to raise trains to a sufficient altitude to cross the Allegheny Ridge to the west, beyond which was the steel town of Pittsburgh and the rest of the western United States. The Horseshoe Curve, because of it being the industrial link to the western U.S., was a primary target of eight Nazi saboteurs who infiltrated the United States early in the war ( one nine four two ) by being dropped off by Kriegsmarine U-Boats.

In the early two zero th century, the Railroad's Altoona Works complex employed at its peak some one five , zero zero zero people and covered three miles ( five km) in length, two one eight acres ( eight eight zero , zero zero zero m) of yards and three seven acres ( one five zero , zero zero zero m) of indoor workshop floor space in one two two buildings. The PRR built many of its own locomotives at the Works, some seven , eight seven three in all, the last being constructed in one nine four six . Things began to decline steadily from that point, and most of the plant is now long gone.

Altoona is also one of the dual seats of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Altoona-Johnstown as the location of the Cathedral of the Blessed Sacrament, which was made a cathedral and rechristened from St. John's Church in one eight five one .

In two zero zero zero , Altoona became sister cities with St. Plten, Austria.

Today, Altoona serves as the corporate home to Sheetz, widely considered by many to be the fastest-growing convenience store chain in the United States.

Geography 
Map of Altoona and some surrounding areas
Altoona is located at four zero  three zero ' three nine  North, seven eight  two three ' five nine  West ( four zero . five one zero seven two zero , - seven eight . three nine nine seven five eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of two five . three km ( nine . eight mi).  two five . three km ( nine . eight mi) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

Transportation 
Altoona is a major center on the Norfolk Southern's Pittsburgh Line. In Altoona, helper engines are added to heavy trains to give them extra power up and over the Horseshoe Curve west of town. The Juniata Heavy Repair Shop Complex, originally built by the Pennsylvania Railroad, is the primary repair and maintenance facility on the Norfolk Southern. Altoona is served by several Amtrak trains daily. On an average day, over five zero trains pass though Altoona. The historical importance to the railroad industry and the current high level of railraod activity has made Altoona a mecca for Railfans for over six zero years. The Altoona Railroader's Memorial Museum and the Horseshoe Curve are popular spots for rail fans to take photos of passing trains.

Blair County, Pennsylvania
 
   
 '''Hollidaysburg''' is a borough located in Blair County, Pennsylvania, on the Juniata River, seven Miles ( one one km) south of Altoona. On the outskirts of Hollidaysburg are the Ant Hill Woods, famous for their colony of ants. Coal, iron ore, ganister, and limestone are found in the vicinity. In the past, the borough had foundries and machine shops, a silk mill, car works and classification yards. In one nine zero zero , two , nine nine eight people lived in the borough. In one nine one zero , three , seven three four lived there, and in one nine four zero , five , nine one zero residents were counted. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of five , three six eight . It is the county seat of Blair County.

From one eight three four to one eight five four , the borough was an important port on Pennsylvania Main Line Canal, located where the eastern branch of the canal connected to the Allegheny Portage Railroad.

 History 

The borough of Hollidaysburg was first laid out in one seven nine six ; by one eight one four it consisted of several houses and a tavern. Hollidaysburg became the main transfer point between the Pennsylvania Canal and the Portage Railroad, a gateway to western Pennsylvania. The canal and Portage Railroad spurred industrial and commercial development in Hollidaysburg in the one eight three zero 's. In one eight three six , Hollidaysburg was established as a borough.

When Blair County was organized in one eight four six , the Borough of Hollidaysburg was designated the county seat. This designation allowed the Borough to prosper when politicians and attorneys became attracted to the Borough.

In one nine zero three , the Pennsylvania Railroad constructed a large switching yard and US Route two two was directed through the Borough.

 Government 

 
The Borough of Hollidaysburg has a Council-Manager form of government. Voters elect a seven member Borough Council who serve four-year terms. The Borough Council is responsible for formulating policies, enacting ordinances, setting tax rates, approving the annual budget, and appointing the Borough Manager.
 
Council is a policy making board and the Manager is Chief Administrative Officer. The Mayor has limited powers. The roles of a Council are to adopt goals and objectives, establish priorities, approve programs, approve expenditures, approve contracts.

 The Historic District 

The Borough of Hollidaysburg established a local Historic District in one nine eight nine and implemented a historic district ordinance. The purpose of the ordinance is to preserve the unique architectural and historical qualities of the borough. This ordinance regulates alterations, additions, new construction and demolition in the distict. 
The Hollidaysburg Historic District encompasses the central part of the Borough. There are roughly four zero zero structures in the District. These structures are classified as Significant, Contributing, and Non-Contributing.

The Historical and Architectural Review Board is responsible for the review and regulation of changes within the district. This advisory board consists of seven members. The process involves making an application to get a Certificate of Appropriateness (COA). HARB Application. This application is then reviewed by the Board at its regular monthly meeting. HARBHPC Meeting Agenda The HARB makes a recommendation to the Borough Council, who reviews the request and makes a final decision at its regular monthly meeting. If approved, a Certificate of Appropriateness is awarded and a zoning permit will be issued for the work. The charge for a COA is $ one zero . zero zero . There can be additional charges per the zoning permit, depending upon the type of project.

 History 
During the late one seven zero zero s, Patrick Cassidy, a native of Newry, Ireland and an American soldier in the American Revolutionary War, purchased a several-dozen-acre parcel of land in Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, now known as Blair County. C. one seven nine three , he constructed a small town on the land, which he named for his home.

A half-century later, Newry flourished as the Allegheny Portage Railroad began to carry passengers from Hollidaysburg across the Alleghenies to Johnstown. Newry's location made it a suitable stop for the railroad and this new influx of visitors stimulated the economy of the town. This prosperity lasted from the one eight three zero s to the one eight five zero s, when the railroad closed.

During the following century, the town decreased in population and quietly shifted from an urban to a rural center until the one nine five zero s, when migration of Altoonans from the north began to increase the size of Newry and gave it a more suburban character.

Businesses and institutions
The majority of Newry's businesses are found along the main north-south road, Old Route two two zero : just north of the town, a small golf course, an automotive garage, a storage company, and a small motor vehicles store; within Newry, several crafts shops and an electronics repair store; and immediately to the south, the largest business in the town, Leighty's, which comprises a convenience store, a computer systems, parts, and repair store, a golf course, a hunting outfitter, a flea market, a flower store, and a bathroom and kitchen remodeling store.

Along South Street, the southmost east-west road in the town, are located a post office, a small apartment building, a furniture store, a used appliances and furniture store, and St. Patrick's Parish, a Roman Catholic parish comprising a small church, a graveyard, a shrine to Our Lady of Lourdes, and an elementary school.

Along Allegheny Street, the northmost east-west street, one can find a Lutheran church, two bars, and the town hall.

 Events 
The two yearly events celebrated by the community, both held by St. Patrick's Parish, are the Lenten fish fries, held in the cafeteria of the school, and the summer festival, held near the end of August on the school playground and in the gymnasium. Both attract visitors from across the Altoona metropolis and greatly benefit the church and school.

Surrounding areas
To the north of Newry, Old Route two two zero leads to Duncansville and then to Altoona and other points north.

To the west, the Puzzletown Road curves to the southwest through a few miles of housing developments and into Puzzletown, where it becomes the Blue Knob Road, continues south-southwest up the Appalachian Plateau, up the mountain of Blue Knob and reaches the town of the same name.

To the south, two two zero leads through Leamersville and East Freedom, near McKee, and intersects with Interstate nine nine ; it leads eventually to Bedford.

To the east, the Catfish Road goes through a few miles of sparse farmland, interrupted by a few houses and a monastery, until it intersects Route three six , which leads north to Hollidaysburg and south to Roaring Spring.

 The '''''Radio Regulations''''' is an intergovernmental treaty text of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the Geneva based specialised agency of the United Nations which coordinates and standardises the operation of telecommunication networks and services and advances the development of communications technology. 

Covering both legal and technical issues, it serves as a supranational instrument for the optimal international management of the radio spectrum.

The ''Radio Regulations'' define:
 the allocation of different frequency bands to different radio services;
 the mandatory technical parameters to be observed by radio stations, especially transmitters;
 procedures for the coordination (ensuring technical compatibility) and notification (formal recording and protection in the Master International Frequency Register) of frequency assignments made to radio stations by national governments;
 other procedures and operational provisions.

The drafting, revision and adoption of the ''Radio Regulations'' is the responsibility of the World Radiocommunication Conferences (WRCs) of the ITU, meetings of which are typically held every three or four years.  Recent WRCs are:
 Geneva, one nine nine five (WRC- nine five )
 Geneva, one nine nine seven (WRC- nine seven )
 Istanbul, two zero zero zero (WRC- two zero zero zero )
 Geneva, two zero zero three (WRC- zero three )

The two zero zero four edition contains the complete texts of the ''Radio Regulations'' as adopted and revised by WRC- zero three , including all articles, appendices, resolutions, and a subset of the recommendations issued by ITU-R (previously known as the CCIR) (those recommendations which have a mandatory nature, as a result of being cited in the ''Radio Regulations'').

The next revision of the ''Radio Regulations'' will take place in Geneva in two zero zero seven .

 '''Tyrone''' is a borough located in Blair County, Pennsylvania, one five miles ( two four km) northeast of Altoona, on the Little Juniata River. Tyrone was of considerable commercial importance in the twentieth century. It was an outlet for the Clearfield coal fields, and it was noted for the manufacture of paper products. There were planing mills, and chemical and candy factories.  '''Sayre''' is a borough located in Bradford County, Pennsylvania, five nine miles ( nine five km) northwest of Scranton. In the past, various iron products were made there. In one nine zero zero , five , two four three people lived there; in one nine one zero , six , four two six people lived there, and in one nine four zero , seven , five six nine persons made their homes in Sayre. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of five , eight one three .

Sayre is close to the New York border and is contiguous with Waverly, New York. 

 History 
In May of one eight seven zero , a Waverly banker named '''Howard Elmer''', along with Charles Anthony and James Fritcher, bought the Pine Plains area between Waverly and Athens. Elmer then convinced Robert Asa Packer to locate a new railroad repair facility on the Pine Plains for the expanding Lehigh Valley Railroad, which was making a push north to connect to the New York state railroads.  '''Bensalem Township''' is a township located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. The township is composed of many communities, including Bensalem, Trevose, Oakford, Cornwells Heights, Eddington, and Andalusia. As of the two zero zero zero census, the township had a total population of five eight , four three four . The two zero zero four population estimate of five eight , five seven five makes Bensalem Township the nine th largest municipality in Pennsylvania. This figure will continue to rise as Philadelphians, and foreigners especially continue to call Bensalem their new home.


 Geography 
Bensalem is the southernmost township in Bucks County and is bordered by Philadelphia to the west and south.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of five four . three km ( two one . zero mi ).  five one . seven km ( two zero . zero mi ) of it is land and two . six km ( one . zero mi ) of it is water. The total area is four . seven seven % water.

The Fall line, which separates the Atlantic Coastal Plain region from the Piedmont region, runs through Bensalem, and is visible around the Neshaminy Mall area.

 Demographics 
Bensalem has a large and fast-growing foreign-born population, which includes concentrations of Indian, Mexican, Russian, West Indian and Korean immigrants.

As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are five eight , four three four people, two two , six two seven households, and one five , one one four families residing in the township. The population density is one , one two nine . eight km ( two , nine two six . seven mi ). There are two three , five three five housing units at an average density of four five five . zero km ( one , one seven eight . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the township is eight two . nine zero % White, six . nine three % African American, zero . two two % Native American, six . six one % Asian, zero . zero five % Pacific Islander, one . six four % from other races, and one . six five % from two or more races.  four . two nine % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are two two , six two seven households of which three zero . six % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five one . six % are married couples living together, one zero . five % have a female householder with no husband present, and three three . two % are non-families. two six . three % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . nine % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . five six and the average family size is three . one four .

In the township the population is spread out with two three . one % under the age of one eight , eight . nine % from one eight to two four , three two . five % from two five to four four , two four . five % from four five to six four , and one one . zero % who are six five years of age or older. The median income for a household in the township is $ four nine , seven three seven , and the median income for a family is $ five eight , seven seven one .  Philadelphia Park Racetrack 
Bensalem is home to Philadelphia Park Racetrack, a one mile thoroughbred horse racing track. This facility opened in November one nine seven four as Keystone Racetrack. The name was changed to Philadelphia Park in one nine eight four . This racetrack was the track where the two zero zero four Kentucky Derby and Preakness Stakes champion Smarty Jones got his start at.

 Government 
In one nine eight seven , the people of Bensalem voted to become a second-class township with a five member council and a mayor. The township also has its own nine -member school board. The current Republican mayor, Joseph DiGirolamo, is in his four th consecutive term.

 Neshaminy Mall 
Neshaminy Mall is located within Bensalem. It was one of the first malls to be constucted in the country. It has four main anchors ''(three department stores and one movie theatre)'' and over one two zero smaller shops and eateries.

 '''Bristol''' is a borough located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, two three miles ( three seven km) northeast of Philadelphia opposite Burlington, N.J. on the Delaware River. Bristol was first incorporated in one seven two zero . Although its charter was revised in one nine zero five , the original charter remains in effect, making Bristol one of the older boroughs in Pennsylvania.  seven , one zero four people lived in Bristol in one nine zero zero ; nine , two five six in one nine one zero ; one zero , two seven three in one nine two zero ; and one one , eight nine five in one nine four zero . As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of nine , nine two three . Current Mayor is Joseph Saxton.

 History 

First settled as Buckingham (for Buckingham, England) in one six eight one , the borough of Bristol, Pennsylvania is one of the oldest settlements in the United States, and is about one five - three zero minutes north of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. It was originally used as a port and dock. Bristol is rich in history, boasting many historic and restored houses that line the streets of Radcliffe and Mill. 

Attractions include: Bristol Riverside Theatre, Margaret R. Grundy Library  North, seven four  five one ' five  West ( four zero . one zero three three eight two , - seven four . eight five one four four eight ).

The Bristol Borough School District is comprised of two public schools: Warren Snyder-John Girotti Elementary School (K- six ) and Bristol Jr. Sr. High School ( seven - one two ).

Bucks County, Pennsylvania
Census-designated places in Pennsylvania
 
   
 '''Doylestown''' is the name of both a borough and the adjacent township located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, three four miles ( five five km) north of Philadelphia. At the turn of the century in one nine zero zero , three , zero three four people lived in the borough of Doylestown, and in one nine one zero , three , three zero four people lived there. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of eight , two two seven , and the township a population of one six , seven four seven . The borough is the county seat of Bucks County.

 History 
Doylestown was first settled by William Doyle in one seven four five , who established a tavern at what is now the corner of Main and State Streets. In one eight one three , the county seat was moved from Newtown because of Doylestown's more central location within the county. In one eight five seven , after much lobbying, the North Pennsylvania Railroad opened a branch line into Doylestown, later taken over by the Reading Railroad. The town was also located on the trolley line from Philadelphia to Easton. As a result of this abundant transportation, central location and its residential and commercial appeal the town flourished.

Doylestown grew steadily through the two zero th century, establishing itself as a home to predominantly upper and middle class families.

 Personalities 
Doylestown is known for being the home of author James A. Michener, architect and archaeologist Henry Chapman Mercer, lyricist and playwright Oscar Hammerstein II, nobel-prize winning author Pearl S. Buck, short-lived pop icon and American Idol runner-up Justin Guarini, anthropologist Margaret Mead, actor Timothy Stack, and pop star Pink (musician), as well as mathematician, portrait artist, classical guitar maker, and renowned professor of Anatomy and Physiology Manuel Martin Avalos. It is also the birthplace of three One Life to Live stars: Erin Torpey (who left the show in two zero zero three ), and siblings Kristen Alderson and Eddie Alderson. It is or was the home of pioneering Digital Film-makers, Stefan Avalos and Lance Weiler

 Culture 
Doylestown Borough is home to three structures designed and built by Henry Chapman Mercer as museums and cultural sites. The Mercer Museum houses a collection known as, Tools of the Nation Builder, and is one of the most important collections of its kind in the world. The Bucks County Historical Society also maintains a research library adjoining the museum. Fonthill (also known as Mercer's Castle ) was Mercer's home and houses his collection of artifacts from around the world. The Moravian Tile Works is an operational factory using the tools and techniques used by Pennsylvania German potters in the one eight th and one nine th centuries. 

The former prison, across the street from the Mercer Museum, has been converted into the James A. Michener Art Museum. The borough also boasts a small music conservatory, writers' and artists' organizations and other cultural activities.

Doylestown is also home to the Polish-American Roman Catholic shrine known as the American Czestochowa, which houses a painting of the Black Madonna of Czstochowa, Poland.

 Geography 
Doylestown is located at ( four zero . three one two seven five six , - seven five . one two eight seven nine nine ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of five . six km ( two . two mi ).  five . six km ( two . two mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

There are three , nine five two households out of which one nine . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three nine . zero % are married couples living together, seven . two % have a female householder with no husband present, and five one . seven % are non-families. four four . four % of all households are made up of individuals and two two . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of one . four km ( zero . five mi ).  one . four km ( zero . five mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.


 Overview 

Dublin is a very small town, extended along a stretch of Route three one three which connects the much larger towns of Doylestown and Quakertown. Almost the entire town can be viewed from three one three with only a few streets diverging from the main road. The town is surrounded by sparse housing developments and a series of dairy farms and nurseries, all of which are part of Hilltown Township and Bedminster Township. Dublin contains a small shopping center, a Department of Motor Vehicles Center, a pharmacy and five restaurants. Several rows of old houses line three one three , some of which date back to the late one seven zero zero 's. The majority of Dublin's population lives in several developments around the main part of town. Dublin has its own municipal government and maintains a fire station. Dublin has its own local police department and relies on Pennsylvania State Police when not on duty.

 Aerial view of Levittown, Pennsylvania circa one nine five nine 
'''Levittown, Pennsylvania''' is a census-designated place (CDP) and suburban community located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, within the Philadelphia metropolitan area. As of the two zero zero zero census, the Levittown CDP had a total population of five three , nine six six . It is four zero feet ( one two meters) above sea level. Though not a municipality, it is commonly reckoned as the largest suburb of Philadelphia in Pennsylvania;  one . Upper Darby Township, Philadelphia's largest suburban township in Pennsylvania, and other suburban townships boast larger populations, yet these municipalities consist of more than one locality;  two  three In New Jersey, both Camden (though wholly urban in character) and Cherry Hill have more inhabitants than Levittown.

 History 
Levittown, Pennsylvania, is a suburban community, planned and built by Levitt Levittown built by William J. Levitt, who is often credited as the creator of the modern American suburb. 

What set Levittown apart from other developments at the time was that it was built as a complete community. Levitt greenbelts, baseball fields and playgrounds, and a shopping center located in Tullytown Borough that was considered large and modern at the time of its construction (and in fact was the largest east of the Mississippi). Residents (who are sometimes called Levittowners) were first expected to comply with a lengthy list of rules and regulations regarding the upkeep of their homes and use of their property; These proved unenforceable over time. In the years since Levitt garden apartments and a number of non-Levitt owner-occupied houses have been built in Levittown. 

Initially Levitt middle-class gas riots in one nine seven nine in the wake of the Camp David Peace Accords that resulted in a second embargo by Arab oil-producing nations. The unrest occurred as lines swelled and tempers flared in the heart of Levittown at an intersection known as Five Points, a location surrounded by six service stations.

A baseball team from Levittown, Pennsylvania, won the Little League World Series in one nine six zero . Levittown American beat an opponent from Fort Worth, Texas to win the honor.
 
The Levittown Shopping Center (known officially as but rarely called the Levittown Shop-a-Rama ), located in Tullytown Borough, began a slow decline in the mid- one nine seven zero 's from which it never recovered with the building of the Oxford Valley Mall. The mall, located just north of Levittown, in Langhorne, Pennsylvania, in Middletown Township, drew shoppers away from the older Levittown facility, given Oxford Valley's much larger size, and enclosed shopping environment. In two zero zero two , the redeveloped site of the Shop-a-rama was reopened as the Levittown Town Center. The completed facility will contain four six eight , six seven five square feet ( four three , five four one square meters) of retail space.

Public pools, built by Levitt  Two of these had spent time in parish ministry at other Catholic churches located in Levittown.

 Municipalities and Sections 
Levittown, Pennsylvania, is not an incorporated place, though efforts in the early one nine five zero 's were made to incorporate. Some Levittown residents feared that incorporation would lead to higher taxes, by robbing the prospective municipality of a commercial tax base.

Levittown's four one neighborhoods (locally called sections ) are found in parts of four separate municipalities: Bristol Township, Pennsylvania (including the sections of Plumbridge, Mill Creek, Indian Creek, Goldenridge, Blue Ridge, Whitewood, Orangewood, Yellowood, Violetwood, Red Cedar Hill, Apple Tree Hollow, Holly Hill, Crabtree Hollow, Oaktree Hollow, Greenbrook, Farmbrook, Dogwood Hollow, Junewood, Magnolia Hill, and most of Kenwood and Stonybrook), Falls Township, Pennsylvania (including the sections of Vermillion Hills, Thornridge, Birch Valley, Elderberry Park, North Park, Will-o-wood, and portions of Pinewood and Lakeside), Middletown Township, Pennsylvania (including the sections of Deep Dale East, Deep Dale West, Highland Park, Twin Oaks, Forsythia Gate, Snowball Gate, Red Rose Gate, Upper Orchard, Lower Orchard, Juniper Hill, Cobalt Ridge and Quincy Hollow), and the Borough of Tullytown, Pennsylvania (including portions of Stonybrook, Kenwood, Pinewood and Lakeside). 

Map of the municipalities, school districts and original sections of Levittown, Pennsylvania. The thick gray lines are municipal borders.

The names of the streets within each section uniformly begin with the same letter that begins the name of the section in question, a plan that offers a good clue as to where any particular street might be located.  X and Z are not used for section or street names. As there are more than two four section names, road is used for street names in sections to the west of Edgely Road, lanes are found in those section to the east. Red Rose Gate, Forsythia Gate, and Snowball Gate are collectively known as The Gates. (These were the only sections without sidewalks so as to lend a more executive appearance to the neighborhoods.) Lakeside sits next to Lake Levittown. Magnolia Hill is on a prominent hill. Mill Creek is found next to a creek by the same name.

Middletown residents are served by public schools run by the Neshaminy School District. Bristol Township public schools are managed by the Bristol Township School District, while residents of Falls Township and Tullytown Borough are served by the Pennsbury School District. Some students attend schools run by Roman Catholic, Lutheran, evangelical Protestant and Quaker organizations, in and around Levittown. Housing costs in the Middletown Township sections on average are higher than elsewhere in Levittown; Costs tend to be lower in those sections within Bristol Township.

 Geography 
Levittown is located at four zero  nine ' one five  North, seven four  five zero ' five nine  West ( four zero . one five four one zero nine , - seven four . eight four nine seven five six ). Levittown lies in the southern end of Bucks County ( Lower Bucks ), between Philadelphia and Trenton, New Jersey; Downtown Philadelphia ( Center City ) is approximately two two miles ( three five kilometers) away. It is part of the Philadelphia metropolitan area (an area also known generally as the Delaware Valley). It is adjacent to and nearly surrounds Fairless Hills, Pennsylvania, a suburban community more modest in scale, but that shares many of Levittown's characteristics. 

Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) regional rail serves Levittown to the south at its Levittown-Tullytown station, and to the north at its Langhorne and Woodbourne stations. Interstate nine five runs to the north and west of Levittown (connecting it with Philadelphia and the suburbs north of Trenton); The Pennsylvania Turnpike runs southwest of Levittown (connecting it with the western suburbs and the New Jersey Turnpike), and U.S. Route one runs to the north, carrying traffic directly into downtown Trenton. The nearest international airport is Philadelphia International Airport (Airport Code PHL), approximately three four miles ( five five kilometers) southwest of Levittown; The nearest Amtrak station is just across the Delaware River in Trenton, just over nine miles ( one four kilometers) to the east.

Though a steel mill once operated by United States Steel Corporation provided employment in nearby Fairless Hills, many Levittowners have historically commuted by automobile or train to Philadelphia, some to Trenton, still others to more distant locales in as many as four states.  Just over ten percent of employed Levittowners both live and work in the community. 

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of one zero . two square miles ( two six . five square kilometers). The total area is zero . five nine % water.

Median rent in Levittown at the time of the two zero zero zero Census was $ six five seven . Monthly homeowner costs, for people with mortgages, totalled $ one , two two seven on average. The community's racial makeup is nine four . three six % White, two . four five % African American, zero . one six % Native American, zero . nine six % Asian, zero . zero four % Pacific Islander; zero . eight six % are other races, and one . one seven % are two or more races.  two . two two % of the population is Hispanic or Latino, who can be of any race.

Of Levittown's one eight , six zero three households, three five . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, six zero . seven % are married couples living together, one two . three % are headed by a woman, and two two . zero % are so-called non-family households.  one seven . eight % of all households in Levittown are made up of individuals living alone, and eight . five % consist of someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. By national origin, Levittowners are Irish ( three one . seven %), German ( two eight . four %), Italian ( one six . one %), English ( one zero . nine %) and Polish ( nine . five %); three . eight % are foreign born. Although accurate current statistics by religious affiliation are lacking, Roman Catholics and Jews are thought to have been somewhat overrepresented among Levittown's original inhabitants, while Protestants are thought to have been underrepresented. Levittown, in addition to nearly three-dozen Protestant (including two Episcopal), three Roman Catholic and two Orthodox churches, and both a Reform Jewish congregation and a nearby Conservative Jewish synagogue, now boasts a Turkish Islamic mosque, a Hindu house of worship, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, and a Korean-language Presbyterian church. Levittown's largest church is likely  St. Michael the Archangel Roman Catholic Church, located on the Levittown Parkway in Tullytown Borough, with more than one one , zero zero zero Catholics nominally within its parish boundaries. As befits the Quaker State, the nearby Middletown, Fallsington and Bristol Friends Meeting Houses serve Levittown. In the Levittown CDP, two five % of the adult population has never been married, eight % of adults divorced, eight % widowed and two % separated. 

Approximately two % of Levittowners live as same-sex unmarried partners, with slightly more coupled lesbians residing in Levittown than coupled gay men than would statistically be expected by mere chance alone.  United Christian Church, a United Church of Christ (UCC) congregation (also affiliated with the Disciples of Christ), a Unitarian Universalist ( UU) congregation, and St. Paul's Episcopal Church serve Levittown with  welcoming ministries.  
 The Bucks County Courier Times, a daily newspaper, is published in Levittown; It was once called the Levittown Times. Its policy is to publish annoucements of same-sex unions.

 Famous Levittowners 
Social critics such as Lewis Mumford contended that Levittown's architectural uniformity (now muted by time in any case) would give rise to social uniformity. Though the community and its residents have been the object of extensive sociological studies, the evidence has not supported Mumford's thesis. Levittowners who have achieved acclaim collectively betray no obvious political or cultural identification:

 Keith Armstrong, a one nine eight six graduate of Temple University, grew up in Levittown and attended Bishop Egan High School (now Conwell-Egan High School), was a former NFL player, and is now the Special Teams coach for the Miami Dolphins. 

 Selma Bortner, printmaker, born in Cleveland June two six , one nine two six , moved to Levittown in one nine five two . 

Anna Burger, Secretary-Treasurer of the one . eight -million strong Service Employees International Union, considered the highest-ranking woman in the history of the U.S. labor movement, grew up in Levittown in the one nine five zero 's.

Bill Fitzgerald, born circa one nine five seven , television newscaster at MSNBC, grew up on Good Rock Road in Levittown in Goldenridge.

Mike Fitzpatrick, the eight th District's Republican Representative to Congress, lives in Levittown's Snowball Gate.

 River Huston, writer, AIDS activist, author of ''Goddess: New Guide to Feminine Wisdom'' and official one nine nine five Bucks County poet laureate, grew up in Levittown, and currently resides in Upper Black Eddy, Pennsylvania.

 Joan Klatcho, photographer, grew up in Levittown, Pennsylvania, and is creator of an exhibit entitled  Coming Home: Levittown Revisited .

 Hal Lefcourt, a political gadfly, one-time defender of the Myers against a sometimes unruly mob, often called the unofficial mayor of Levittown, organized the Levittown Historic Preservation Society.

 Jack McFadden, poet, lives with his family in Levittown, and has been published in ''The Bucks County Writer'', ''CREO'', ''Dogwood'', ''Garden House'', ''The Horsethiefs Journal'', ''Mad Poets Review'', ''Manorborn'', ''Painted Moon Review'', ''Pebble Lake Review'', ''Quercus Review'', and ''Saucy Vox'', and is working on a book-length manuscript. The Mad Poets Society meets at several locations around the Delaware Valley, including in Levittown. 

 Daisy Myers, who is sometimes called the Rosa Parks of the North, author of secure.inyork.comcgi-yncYCHTbooks.html ''Sticks 'n Stones: the Myers Family in Levittown'', published by the York County Heritage Trust, moved with her family to Levittown in one nine five seven , the first African-American couple to purchase a home in the community; She lived there for five years before moving to York County, Pennsylvania.

Michael Schiavo, born April three , one nine six three , was the late Terri Schiavo's now ex-husband, grew up in Levittown.

 Charlotte A. Schatz, painter, sculptor, born January six , one nine two nine , was a one-time Levittown resident, and member of the Levittown Artists' Association. 
 	
Mark S. Schweiker, born January three one , one nine five three , was the former Republican Governor of Pennsylvania (from October five , two zero zero one to January two one , two zero zero three ), grew up in Levittown, in The Gates.

 '''Middletown Township''' is a township located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the township had a total population of four four , one four one . Many sections of Levittown, Pennsylvania, are located in the southern end of the township. The township is served by public schools run by the Neshaminy School District. The municipality surrounds the boroughs of Langhorne, Langhorne Manor, Penndel and Hulmeville; much of the township beyond Levittown uses Langhorne, Pennsylvania as a mailing address. New neighborhoods continue to be built in many parts of the township, such that the population is expected to grow more rapidly than the national average as it has for the past decades. 

Middletown Township is home to a large senior citizen population as a number of specialized communities for older adults are located there. The Oxford Valley Mall, Sesame Place (an amusement park), and a strip of retail businesses along Business U.S. Route one have increased traffic congestion and other problems associated with development in recent years, and represent a challenge for planners and local officials.

 Sports 

In one nine five five the Morrisville Little League baseball team defeated Merchantville, NJ to claim the Little League World Series title. It is one of four Pennsylvania teams to have won the tournament since its inception in one nine four seven .

 Trivia 
 A well-painted and sunshine-filled Morrisville was featured in a TV commercial on how Pennsylvania locals have the right to choose their own Electric company.

 Morrisville was actually considered a location to house the capital of the United States. However, due to a rational argument from southern representatives, it was voted down due to geographical issues.

 :''Also see Dark Ages (disambiguation)''

'''Dark Ages''' (or '''Dark Age''') is a term of historical periodization most commonly known in relation to the so-called Dark Ages of European Medieval history. It was first coined be Petrarch in the one four th century to paint the ecclesiastical dominated Middle Ages in a pejorative light as part of the humanists vision to restore secular Roman culture to Italy. Since Petrarch, the term has taken on other meanings and uses in both academia and popular culture.

There is no general recognized meaning of what a Dark Age is. Traditionally it was used to infer a historical period of low cultural achievement following one of high cultural achievement. The term was particularly popular in the one nine th century when historians focused solely on written materials, or lack thereof, applying Petrarchs original meaning with a broader scope. However, because it infers a value judgment on a particular period, and was originally coined for that purpose, the usage of the term became less widespread in academia in the two zero th century as new fields of science such as archeology have shed new light. Today it is used with severe qualifications particular to each case.

In popular culture the term Dark Ages has been widely used in movies and fiction.

Academically coined dark ages 

These are three periods that are commonly called Dark Ages within academia. The history and use of the term for each case is not without controversy and qualifications, each instance is detailed in the individual articles.

 '''Dark Ages''' of Europe ( four seven six - one zero zero zero ), following the collapse of the Roman empire
 '''Greek Dark Ages''' ( one two zero zero - eight zero zero BC), during which Mycenean civilization vanished
 '''Dark ages of Cambodia''' ( one four three two - one eight eight seven ), which followed the decline of Angkor

 '''New Hope''' , formerly Coryell's Ferry, is a borough located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of two , two five two .

 Geography 
New Hope is located at four zero  two one ' three seven  North, seven four  five seven ' two six  West ( four zero . three six zero three one two , - seven four . nine five seven two zero three ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of three . seven km ( one . four mi ).  three . three km ( one . three mi ) of it is land and zero . four km ( zero . two mi ) of it is water. The total area is one one . one nine % water. Much of this is the Delaware River.

The borough is located at the confluence of the Delaware River and Aquetong Creek, which begins in Solebury Township at Ingham Springs, the most productive spring in Southeastern Pennsylvania, about two miles from its mouth. The name Aquetong comes from a local Indian word meaning place of the pine trees, a reference to the pine forest that the creek runs through at the beginning of its route. Near its end, the creek forms a scenic waterfall near the Bucks County Playhouse, a former mill powered by the flow of water.

The area features low, rolling hills, and much is forested. The compact township contains much of the population.

The Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission operates two bridges over the Delaware River between New Hope and Lambertville, New Jersey. One is a free, two-lane bridge between the two towns. The other, which carries U.S. Highway two zero two , is a modern toll bridge.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are two , two five two people, one , one six zero households, and five zero six families residing in the borough. The population density is six eight four . six km ( one , seven seven zero . nine mi ). There are one , two five one housing units at an average density of three eight zero . three km ( nine eight three . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the borough is nine four . nine four % White, one . one one % African American, zero . two two % Native American, zero . eight four % Asian, zero . zero zero % Pacific Islander, one . eight seven % from other races, and one . zero two % from two or more races.  five . five five % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are one , one six zero households out of which one six . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three five . five % are married couples living together, four . seven % have a female householder with no husband present, and five six . three % are non-families. four one . six % of all households are made up of individuals and seven . eight % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. More informally, the population contains many artists and former hippies. The notably liberal area has a substantial, but subtle, gay community.

Industry

The primary industry of New Hope is tourism. On weekends the streets are crowded with tourists visiting the many restaurants, antique shops, art galleries, or just strolling along the river.

The Bucks County Playhouse is located in New Hope and features a constant stream of plays and musical productions. It is located in an attractive historic building.

New Hope is also a terminal point on the New Hope & Ivyland Railroad. On weekends, an excursion gives tourists a ride on the railroad through scenic Bucks County.

Bucks County, Pennsylvania
 
   
 '''Newtown''' is a borough located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of two , three one two . It sits on the western edge of the Trenton, New Jersey metropolitan area, and can also be regarded as being part of the larger Philadelphia metropolitan area.

 History 
Newtown was founded by William Penn, in one six eight four . Newtown was one of several towns that Penn had organized around Philadelphia, PA to provide country homes for city residents, and to support farming communities.

 Geography 
Newtown is located at four zero  one three ' four two  North, seven four  five five ' five six  West ( four zero . two two eight two zero eight , - seven four . nine three two three three eight ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of one . four km ( zero . six mi ).  one . four km ( zero . six mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water. 

The Newtown Creek, a tributary of the Neshaminy Creek, runs North to South through the center of town.

 Education 
Newtown is in the Council Rock School District. While the district serves many towns in Lower Bucks County, Newtown is home to Council Rock High School North, Newtown Middle School (formerly Newtown Junior High), Goodnoe Elementary School, and the former Chancellor Street School, which now acts as the administrative building for the district. Private schools in the area include George School, Newtown Friends School, and St. Andrews Catholic School. The township is also the site of Bucks County Community College's main campus.

 Trivia 
The Law School Admissions Council is headquartered there. As a result, most American lawyers have heard of Newtown.
The movie Signs, directed by M. Night Shyamalan, was partially filmed in Newtown. Specifically, a scene was shot in the Newtown Book and Record Exchange, a small store on Newtown's scenic State Street. Another scene was shot in Mom's , a small pizza parlor in the middle of town. The owner of the parlor reports that at least one group stops by every day to see the parlor because of the movie.

 '''Sellersville''' is a borough located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of four , five six four .

Geography
Sellersville is located at four zero  two one ' three one  North, seven five  one eight ' three six  West ( four zero . three five eight five six five , - seven five . three one zero zero eight two ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of three . one km ( one . two mi ).  three . zero km ( one . two mi ) of it is land and zero . one km ( zero . zero four mi ) of it is water. The total area is one . six nine % water. It is located in Southeastern Pennsylvania as part of Northern Bucks County which borders Philadelphia County. 

Overview and History 
Sellersville began in the early one seven zero zero 's. It was centered on a major road known as Bethlehem Pike that connected Philadelphia to Bethlehem and the rest of what was then far Western Pennsylvania. The town was very small and its most notable feature was a large inn. The Inn is today called the Washington House because it is believed to have been visited at least once by George Washington during the Revolutionary War. The town grew slowly over the years until the Industrial Revolution. In the one eight six zero 's the North Pennsylvania Railroad was built, running parallel to Bethlehem Pike: this stimulated the growth of light textile industries and brought a wave of population growth. The East Branch of the Perkiomen Creek runs through the town which connects it to an adjacent town of Perkasie. This creek was dammed in the early one nine zero zero s creating a small body of water known as Lake Lenape. Along the length of the lake a park was built on Perkasie and Sellersville lands. In the one nine two zero 's and three zero 's this park housed a carousel, a roller coaster and several other amusements. The railroad brought hundreds of people from Philadelphia in the summer time, and it became a well known vacation spot for blue collar city workers.  

Today the town is still relatively small, sandwiched in between a ridge line and the larger town of Perkasie. The center of town still runs along Bethlehem Pike which is now called the old Route three zero nine . The Washington House still stands and has recently been restored to become a five star restaurant. The creek is no longer dammed and only the carousel in Perkasie remains of the amusements. The textile industry has long moved out of the area and Sellersville has become mainly a residential town for people working in the many urban centers that are only a short commute away. The addition of Grandview Hospital on the ridgeline overlooking Sellersville has provided some local jobs since it is the only hospital in Northern Bucks County. This change in economics has by no means made the town a depressed place and it is the home of mainly middle class families. The town is surrounded on three sides by open country and spread out housing developments. On the other side it has grown into Perkasie to the extent that the border is only distinguishable by a few signs.

 Demographics

History Timeline

 one eight eight three - The United States Postal Service changed the name of the town to Yardley from Yardleyville.  This was to avoid confusion with the New York CityPhiladelphia train line that made a stop here and at Yardville, NJ.

 one nine five five - Flooding caused by hurricanes Connie and Diane wiped out the bridge to New Jersey. 

 one nine six one - Scudder Falls Bridge opens, just outside of the borough.

 two zero zero four - Hurricane Ivan causes worst flood since one nine five five .

 two zero zero five - On the morning of April, four the water on the Delaware River crested higher than after the Hurricane Ivan. The cause was rain and snow melt.

 '''Butler''' is a city located in Butler County, Pennsylvania. As of the two zero zero zero census, the city had a total population of one five , one two one . It is the county seat of Butler County.

 History 

The city was named for Maj. Gen. Richard Butler, who fell at the Battle of the Wabash, also known as St. Clair's Defeat, in western Ohio in one seven nine one . The first settlers were of Irish or Scottish descent and were driving westward from Connecticut. In one eight zero two the German immigrants began arriving, with Detmar Basse settling in Jackson Township in one eight zero two and founding Zelienople the following year. After Johann George Rapp arrived in one eight zero five and founded Harmony, the trickle of settlers grew tremendous numbers. John A. Roebling settled Saxonburg one eight three two , by which time all counties were filled with German settlers.

 Geography 
Butler is located at four zero  five one ' three eight  North, seven nine  five three ' four one  West ( four zero . eight six zero six seven nine , - seven nine . eight nine four seven nine six ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the city has a total area of seven . zero km ( two . seven mi ).  seven . zero km ( two . seven mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

 Demographics 
As of the census of two zero zero zero , there are one five , one two one people, six , seven four zero households, and three , six two six families residing in the city. The population density is two , one seven zero . four km ( five , six one one . three mi ). There are seven , four zero two housing units at an average density of one , zero six two . four km ( two , seven four six . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the city is nine five . five two % White, two . two two % African American, zero . one four % Native American, zero . four four % Asian, zero . zero three % Pacific Islander, zero . five two % from other races, and one . one four % from two or more races.  one . four two % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are six , seven four zero households out of which two six . eight % have children under the age of one eight living with them, three five . zero % are married couples living together, one four . four % have a female householder with no husband present, and four six . two % are non-families. four zero . seven % of all households are made up of individuals and one six . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . one eight and the average family size is two . nine six .

In the city the population is spread out with two three . seven % under the age of one eight , nine . seven % from one eight to two four , three zero . three % from two five to four four , two zero . two % from four five to six four , and one six . one % who are six five years of age or older. The median age is three six years. For every one zero zero females there are eight eight . one males. For every one zero zero females age one eight and over, there are eight three . nine males.

The median income for a household in the city is $ two five , one five four , and the median income for a family is $ three five , eight nine three . Males have a median income of $ three zero , six zero seven versus $ two zero , nine five zero for females. The per capita income for the city is $ one six , four five seven .  one nine . one % of the population and one four . seven % of families are below the poverty line. Out of the total population, two six . eight % of those under the age of one eight and one four . five % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 Claim to Fame 

Butler was home to a large factory for the Pullman Palace Car company. In addition, the modern Jeep was invented in the town, whose site of invention is now occupied by a strip mall.

Now, the AK Steel plant employs many people from the city and surrounding areas.

An abandoned limestone mine near the town serves as highly secure storage for both Corbis, the stock photography company founded by Bill Gates and the US Federal Government.

A book of poetry has been written about this city:
 The Butler Pennsylvania Poems by Charles L. Cingolani.

 Cranberry Township 

''' Cranberry Township''' is a township located in Butler County, Pennsylvania. The township is classified as a Second Class Township and follows the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Second Class Township Code. As of the two zero zero zero census, the township had a total population of two three , six two five . 

 Geography 
Cranberry Township, PA is located in western Pennsylvania ( four zero . seven zero nine nine six N, eight zero . one zero six zero five W). According to the United States Census Bureau, the township has a total area of five nine . one km ( two two . eight mi ).  five nine . zero km ( two two . eight mi ) of it is land and zero . zero four % is water.

 Demographics 
As of the census two of two zero zero zero , there are two three , six two five people, eight , three five two households, and six , five five six families residing in the township. The population density is four zero zero . two km ( one , zero three six . five mi ). There are eight , seven two four housing units at an average density of one four seven . eight km ( three eight two . eight mi ). The racial makeup of the township is nine six . eight zero % White, zero . eight eight % African American, zero . zero six % Native American, one . three five % Asian, zero . zero two % Pacific Islander, zero . one nine % from other races, and zero . six nine % from two or more races.  zero . seven zero % of the population are Hispanic or Latino of any race.

There are eight , three five two households out of which four four . five % have children under the age of one eight living with them, seven zero . four % are married couples living together, six . one % have a female householder with no husband present, and two one . five % are non-families. one seven . nine % of all households are made up of individuals and six . four % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. The average household size is two . eight one and the average family size is three . two three .

In the township the population is spread out with three zero . seven % under the age of one eight , five . four % from one eight to two four , three five . two % from two five to four four , two zero . six % from four five to six four , and eight . one % who are six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, three . four % of those under the age of one eight and five . zero % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 History 

The Township of Cranberry was founded in one eight zero four . The most populated section of the township was originally known as Criders Corners. Its current name is derived from the cranberry bogs which could be found in the area in days past. The township also includes part of the considerably smaller former town of Ogle.
One reason for the township's tremendous growth is its location. Serving as the intersection of Interstate seven six (the Pennsylvania Turnpike) and seven nine and Routes one nine and two two eight , the community is accessible from virtually anywhere. In addition, the completion of Interstate two seven nine in one nine eight nine cut travel time to Pittsburgh under half an hour.

Several detailed histories of the township can be found here.

 Transportation 

Interstate seven nine and the Pennsylvania Turnpike via Interstate seven six run through Cranberry Township. US Route one nine (i.e. Perry Highway) and PA Route two two eight are also important main roads in the municipality. These four roads are connected by a newly-completed interchange: the $ four four . three million, joint PennDOTPennsylvania Turnpike venture, named the Cranberry Connector Project, was local nuissance for several years, but after opening in early two zero zero four has effectively provided direct, non-stop connection between the heavily-travelled roads.
Additionally, the northern terminus of Interstate two seven nine , an important artery that serves as the parkway north to Pittsburgh, is located a few miles south of the community. Cranberry Township is also the location of the northermost bus service lines of the Port Authority of Allegheny County.

 Business 

Cranberry Township is one of the fastest-growing areas in the United States in both population and business. While many residential communities are being built, even more so are retail stores. With a few exceptions such as a standard retail mall, a K-Mart (which closed while the company was in bankruptcy protection), and few specific restaurants, Cranberry Township has virtually every single store or restaurant imaginable for the Pittsburgh area. Here are some of the more notable retail outlets and restaurants located in the Cranberry area:

 Wal-Mart (in the process of being converted into a supercenter)
 Target
 Costco
 Kohl's
 TJ Maxx
 Marshall's
 Starbucks (four)
 Lowe's

 Lane Bryant
 Giant Eagle (two)
 McDonald's (two)
 Burger King (two)
 Wendy's
 Long John SilversA among them is the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review, whose NewsWorks warehouse prints that paper as well as the USA Today for the entire Pittsburgh area.

A favorite after-hours restaurant and casual meeting place for high school and college-age Cranberrians is Eat'n Park, which is on the western side of Route one nine , and is actually located just over the southern boundary of Cranberry Township, in Allegheny County (for some strange reason, it has a Mars, PA mailing address).

Despite Cranberry Township's heavy commercialization, the town still ceases to harbor neither a bowling alley nor pool hall within its boundaries. This seemingly small but significant impediment often limits college-age kids (while living at home during breaks from school) to few means of entertainment. Many return to Eat'n Park night after night, and most are eventually forced to regularly congregate in groups at one's house and consume large amounts of alcohol. For those who have the means, a bowling alley is located in the next town to the North, and pool halls within a half-an-hour's drive south.

 Education 
Children residing in the township chiefly attend schools of the Seneca Valley School District:
Haine Elementary (K- six ) and Rowan Elementary (K- four ), both located in town
Evans City Elementary (K- six ), located in Evans City, PA;
Seneca Valley Middle School ( seven - eight ), Seneca Valley Intermediate High School ( nine - one zero ), and Seneca Valley Senior High School ( one one - one two ), located in Harmony, PA.
Attendance of the three elementary schools are based upon geographic location.
Upon graduating high school, many of the teenagers from the middle-class town attend college. The largest percentage of them attend nearby Slippery Rock University. Penn State University and University of Pittsburgh are also popular schools among Cranberrians. The farthest known post-secondary institution to be attended (immediately following high school) by a Cranberrian in recent years is the University of North Texas, in Denton, TX.

Slang
Adolescents in the area often refer to Cranberry as C-berry . Favored restaurant Eat'n Park is referred to as E or E'n'P. The majority of residents of this prominent western Pennsylvania town tend to be huge fans of the Pittsburgh Steelers ( Stillers ), and many often drink pop, a timeless carbonated beverage.

There are four zero nine households out of which two three . seven % have children under the age of one eight living with them, five four . three % are married couples living together, six . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and three four . five % are non-families. two seven . nine % of all households are made up of individuals and one zero . zero % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, eight . zero % of those under the age of one eight and five . seven % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 History 
Harmony was founded by the Pietist Johann George Rapp and his Harmony Society. George Rapp came to America from Wuertemberg, Germany in one eight zero three in search of land for his followers. He was searching for a place for his followers to worship, farm and put into effect Rapp's communistic religious teachings. In one eight zero four two groups of Harmonists purchased a tract of land in Butler County, Pennsylvania.

They formally established the society in one eight zero five and lived in Pennsylvania for about one zero years before selling the property and moving on to New Harmony, Indiana. In one eight two four they moved back to Pennsylvania, this time to Economy. The settlements were economically successful, producing many goods in a clothing factory, a sawmill, a tannery, and from their vinyards and distillery. A hotel was also run in Harmony. In Economy the group aided the construction of the Pittsburgh and Lake Erie Railroad, established the Economy Savings Institution and the Economy Brick Works, and operated the Economy Oil Company, Economy Planing Mill, and Economy Lumber Company. The society exerted a major influence on the economic development of Western Pennsylvania. But since the group chose to adopt celibacy, they eventually died out when John S. and his wife Susanna C. Duss, the last survivors of Harmony, died in one nine five one .

 '''Mars''' is a borough located in Butler County, Pennsylvania, USA. As of the two zero zero zero census, the borough had a total population of one , seven four six .

Mars is located at four zero  four one ' four eight  North, eight zero  zero ' four four  West ( four zero . six nine six five nine four , - eight zero . zero one two two zero five ).

According to the United States Census Bureau, the borough has a total area of one . two km ( zero . four mi ).  one . two km ( zero . four mi ) of it is land and none of the area is covered with water.

There are six eight seven households out of which two five . zero % have children under the age of one eight living with them, four five . seven % are married couples living together, one zero . eight % have a female householder with no husband present, and four two . four % are non-families. three eight . three % of all households are made up of individuals and two four . three % have someone living alone who is six five years of age or older. Out of the total population, one one . eight % of those under the age of one eight and one four . four % of those six five and older are living below the poverty line.

 History 
The history of Mars is one seeped in the stories of several families... families that continue to be an active participate of the community two zero zero years after its humble beginnings. These individuals gave of their talent and foresight to improve a community for their children and others. In one seven nine eight Isaac Covert purchased one zero zero acres ( four zero zero , zero zero zero m ) on which he built a log cabin, and later accumulated a total of four zero zero acres ( one . six km ). There were several farmers who had purchased land in the Breakneck Valley. On the South side of Irvine Sireet was the Matthew Parks' farm. On the East of Crowe Avenue was the Thomas Kennedy farm, Nor- thwest was the Covert farm, and southwest was the James Davison farm. These farms all met at the corner of Pittsburgh Street and Crowe Avenue, which was the crossroad of the Valencia-Evans City Road and a road from the Old Plank Road (Rte. eight ) and to Perry Highway on the west. 

Two men, Matthew Parks and Thomas Kennedy, built water- powered grist mills on Breakneck Creek. Matthew Parks built in one eight two five near the intersection of the Mars- Valencia Road and Route two two eight . Thomas Kennedy built a mill in one eight two eight in the valley East of Cherry Street. Farmers from the area came to one of these mills to have feed ground for their cattle. 

Frank Johnston, realizing that most farmers came to this valley to have their feed ground, bought a tract of land from Thomas Kennedy and built a general store in one eight six two between the grist mills and the crossroad. It was located east of the railroad tracks, which later came through the town. Other men, seeing the advantage of having a business in this locality, built in this area. Among them were: James Irvine, and William Crisswell, - Livery Stable, T. M. Marshall - General Store, and W. J. Gilleland - Store. 

In one eight seven three , Samuel Parks, son of Matthew Parks, built a home on the property now occupied by Mars Auto Parts. With the help of the Honorable Samuel Marshall, he established a post office in his home. The origin of the name of the Post Office, Mars, has been a controversial topic. Some say that Mrs. Parks was a student of astronomy and suggested the name. Others say that it was named in honor of Samuel Marshall. The latter seems to be the consensus. Mail was brought by stage coach to Wexford, where Albert Parks, son of Samuel Parks, traveled to pick it up once each week. The trip was made on horseback each Saturday, and the boy received $ eight yearly for his service. 

After the post office had been in the home of Samuel Parks for about four years, it was moved down to Frank Johnston's store. A home, store, and post office combined, it was one of the first buildings in Mars. Other old homes in the town were: the James Davison home, a log cabin built between Irvine Street and the creek across from the Reform Presbyterian Church property; and the Samuel Kennedy four-room log cabin on Spring Street Extension, at a spring northwest of the dam for his grist mill. 

In one eight seven seven , Pittsburgh, New Castle, and Lake Erie Railroad organized to build a railroad through Butler County. As the railroad was to come through the farm of Samuel Ken- nedy, he inserted into the right-of- way agreement that a stop must be placed on his farm, and all passenger trains must stop on being flagged. The stop was named Overbrook, as it was close to a brook. However, the name of the railroad stop conflicted with the name of the post office, so that mail for Mars was delivered to the Overbrook stop. This was confusing to the trainmen and an agreement between the railroad and the postal authorities decided on the name Mars, as there was another Overbrook post office in Pennsylvania. 

On October two zero , one eight nine four , five seven of the seven two property owners in the area petitioned the Courts of Butler County with an application for incorporation of the Borough of Mars. The petition was granted March six , one eight nine five . On April nine , one eight nine five , the first election of the Borough of Mars was held with Samuel A. Kennedy elected Burgess; Samuel Crow, President of Council; Arba Jordan, Secretary; R. H. McElheny, Constable; and Joseph Borland, Street Commissioner. The Organization Meeting was held May two four , one eight nine five , at which time the first one eight Ordinances of the new Borough of Mars were approved. 

The new council had several problems such as sidewalks, animals in town, grading streets with horse- drawn equipment, and all kinds of peddlers coming through the town. 

In one nine zero one , Troutman Gas Co. was given permission to pipe gas to the homes in Mars and gas lights on the streets. 

In one nine zero three , a proposition was presented to council on a water system, with two six fire hydrants. There had been several fires and the buildings could have been saved, if there had been fire hydrants. This would reduce the fire insurance rates. However, several of the councilmen felt the town should own the water systems. On February two one , one nine zero five , the citizens voted to build a municipal-owned water system and increase bonded indebtedness to cover the cost. Council also purchased a plot of ground for a reservoir. 

On April two five , one nine zero three , an ordinance was enacted giving authority to install telephones in Mars. On February two seven , one nine zero seven , the North Pittsburgh Telephone Company was authorized to install telephones and has continued to give excellent service throughout the years. 

In one nine zero four , the Pittsburgh, Etna, and Butler Street Railway Company was granted permission to build a track through the town. This transportation system lasted for a number of years, but because of the use of personal automobiles and the improved roads, passengers were finding that they could drive to, their places of employment quicker than by riding the street car. Use of the street car diminished to the point that it was losing money. In one nine three one , it quit operating. 

In one nine zero eight , L. J. Tracy was hired to make a complete survey of the Borough, establish street lines and the necessary sewer grades for the sum of $ four zero zero . In one nine one zero , the Borough Council enacted an ordinance providing for a sewer system at a cost of $ one five , eight zero zero . The system was completed in one nine one one . 

On May one nine , one nine one one , Council authorized the first paved street in town, by awarding the Pitt Construction Co. a bid to pave Grand Avenue. At the same time residents of Pittsburgh Street decided to pave their street. 

The paving of these two streets awoke the entire town to the fact that all the streets needed some attention. A grading and improving program was begun that helped transportation throughout the entire borough. 

In one nine one two , a group of citizens organized the Mars Light Company and erected electric lines to all 'homes. They also erected street lights on all the corners, giving an excellent system of electric lighting. This system was later sold to the Pennsylvania Power Company. 

Because of the advantage of having water and sewer over wells and septic tanks, several people made application for annexing to the borough and were accepted. But sites to build a home are limited and a great number of homes have been built in the township near the borough, but are facing a problem on sewage. Sometime in the near future they are going to be required to build a sanitary sewer system, and they may have to connect with the present system of the borough. 

Police services date to the borough's incorporation, at which time Mars was served by an elected constable. The first regular police officer, Paul Harger, was hired in one nine three one . The present two-man police force is equipped with a radio- equipped cruiser and receives assistance, as required, from the State Police, nearby township police departments, and an auxiliary staff. 

Organized fire protection, a two- wheel hose cart, was established in one nine zero five following a series of disastrous fires. From that beginning the Mars Volunteer Fire Department was organized in one nine three four . That same year, Borough Council voted tax support for the company. This support continues today. 

The well-equipped Mars VFD has been one of the community's most enthusiastic boosters, and at the same time enjoys the town's loyal support. The VFD sponsors a first- aid staff consisting of specially- trained men available two four hours a day for emergency assistance. 

The educational needs of Mars and surrounding communities are served by the Mars Area School District, which currently serves a student body population of nearly three , zero zero zero students.

The growth of the town has been in spurts. In one eight eight seven , there were about five zero persons in the area of Mars. However, by one eight nine four , with the railroad coming through and the oil excitement, it had grown to three five zero persons. With the news that a Borough would be chartered, the growth jumped to seven seven zero in one nine zero zero . With the street cars and paved roads it increased to one , two five zero by one nine two three . Since that time there has been a gradual increase until in one nine seven two there were one , five eight two citizens in the Borough of Mars. 

The Borough of Mars is very efficiently operated, having a total millage tax of one five mills, of which eight mills is for police protection; one  one two mills for a public library and one  one four mills for fire protection. The annual budget is about $ one two five , zero zero zero . The present council is operating on a pay-as-you-go basis, with no large amount borrowed. This is a five mill increase in five zero years. 

The future of the Borough of Mars will depend largely on the economic growth of the surrounding area. The borough itself has very limited space available for additional residential, commercial or industrial expansion. The surrounding three-township area, however, shows every sign of healthy growth. There is every reason to believe that Mars, as the geographic center and largest business community, will prosper from that trend. 

From Life on Mars Centennial Book, one nine seven three
